DESCRIPTION: House of Sallust. A beehive oven with chimney is located in the north corner of the mill oven room. The mill oven room is located northeast of the property entrance. The oven is visible from the street. The oven has received extensive restoration to both the oven and the chimney. The northwest opening of the oven consists of a large arch leading into a forecourt area with passthrough northeast of which is the entry into the oven which could be closed off with a door. Beneath the large arch is a small archway for fuel storage and or ash waste. The passthrough is accessed from the southeast side of the oven front beneath a semi-arched opening. The floor of the passthrough and the forecourt area are covered with bricks and the same is located on the floor in the archway. No decoration or plastering survives on the front of the oven. The oven chimney is located above the forecourt area of the oven for smoke to rise out of the property area. The chimney of the oven has been heavily restored where it consists of masonry construction with a terra cotta exhaust pipe at the top. The rectangular opening at the beehive oven area consists of volcanic stone leading into a floor paved with terra cotta bipedales and the interior of the beehive oven remains intact.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The oven (6083) is located in the north corner of room mill-oven room (6082) is contiguous to (6084) water, other.

DESCRIPTION: There is a large rectangular masonry cooking platform running along the entirety of the northwest wall on east/northwest and west southwest axis. The platform is a tiled surface preserved throughout. At the west/southwest end there is a low step down in the surface of the platform to a semi circular tile and plaster water basin that extends into the adjoining southwest wall. At the base of the basin a small terra cotta pipe drains through the southwest wall to the room to the southwest. In the northwest corner of the platform directly adjoining the basin there is a square masonry oven. Super structure has been restored. Interior semi circular cooking chamber constructed of tile and masonry upper courses. masonry modern construction? The base of the cooking chamber is tiled.

This replaces sheet #1254.
Room 12 is a store room on a northwest/southeast axis of the kitchen (13). An entry from the kitchen into the store room is present on the east wall of the store room at the southeast end. The north wall has suffered a collapse and survives to only about 1 meter in height. The east wall has suffered collapse and survives at its' highest point to approximately 1/2 meters. The south wall has the remains of plaster within a recessed area of a closed doorway. The color is not discernible. Traces of plaster also survive at the southwest corner. The west wall has suffered a collapse at the southwest end. No plaster is visible. The floor is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 13 to the east. Room 16 to the south. Room 11 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 20 is a square room oriented NW by SE. The eastern end of the NE wall frames the door entrance which is about 1.8 meters high. On the threshold is evidence of a channel for a sliding door. The floor paving is compacted earth. The walls to the SE, the SW and NW are heavily reconstructed in modern times; they show large fragments of plaster. On the SW wall at about 2.2 meters above the floor are two square openings which appear to be in line with the two square holes on the opposite wall above the entrance. The holes would hold beams. The NW wall is pierced with a very small opening at about 2.3 meters above the floor and a large rectangular window at approximately 1.4 meters above the floor. To the W the window is framed by a semi-column which protrudes into the room. The storeroom today is covered by a roof which is a completely modern reconstruction. Although the large window and the column make the room an elegant space. The direct connection with adjoining kitchen suggests the possibility that the room was somehow related to the activity performed in the kitchen. Given the large size of the kitchen, food could have been prepared and cooked in the kitchen 19 and stored in room 20.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 19 to NE, dining room 17 to SE, L-shaped garden area 21 to NW and room 28 to SW.

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 8 is entered from courtyard 6 from the SE. The small squarish room is delineated by walls which are mostly preserved. The NW and the NE walls show large fragments of plaster. Today the floor is covered mostly with lapilli and moss on the top of concrete paving. Against the NE wall and along its entire length rests a long narrow bench like structure. It is approximately 25 cm high above the ground and 45 cm wide. This structure may have been used for supporting food containers or other items designed for storage of food and/or drink. In the corner between the SE and SW walls is a rectangular block of stone which could also have been used for support. It is a few centimeters higher than the supporting structure on the opposite side. On the opposite corner between between the SE and NW walls appears shapeless stone feature which seems to be attached to the adjoining supporting structure. Because of its damaged condition it is difficult to ascertain its function. As a whole, the size of the room, the wide entrance door, the supporting structure and the proximity to the kitchen suggest the possibility that the room was used for storing food or drink.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 7 to the SW, courtyard 6 to the SE and dining room 9 to the NE

DESCRIPTION:
Rectangular room northeast/southwest axis. The floor is opus signinum with marble inclusions and central rosette consisting of a pattern of circles in
white tesserae, around which the couches would have been placed. There is a modern roof. The doorway to the peristyle in the southeast corner has plastered jambs, modern lintel and placings for the door in the threshold. The threshold is contiguous with the remainder of the room. The large window in the center of the southeast wall looking out to the peristyle has a modern lintel. There is a narrow rectangular window in the northeast corner. A large square section of painting has been removed in east corner. Third style decoration survives throughout, red on the lower register and white panels above. Unidentifiable scema survive on the southwest, northwest and northeast walls, alternating with circular rosettes of animals that survive on the southwest and northwest walls. There are various ceramic and glass vessels and metal artifacts and animal bones found.
Allison calls it fourth style, but there is little or no architectural imagery or perspective visible and color palette is limited.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle #19 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. We enter this small square dining room, which has a high narrow doorway, from the southwest. There is a white marble threshold with post holes and a modern lintel above. There is a small bit of painted red plaster on both sides of the door jam. All four walls show evidence of a lower red painted plaster register above which is white paint showing remains of gold stenciling and red and green paint which created borders for decorative panels. There is a window centered high in the northeast wall. The walls are preserved to first story height and on the northeast wall in the north corner maybe evidence of molding. In general the room is in disrepair. The floor is lapilli and pile of modern tiles. There is ceiling extant and the view from within the room looking southwest is directly into the impluvium in the atrium and the peristyle.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 26 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is a formal dining room. The principal entrance is from the northeast from the atrium. The entrance is the full width of the room. Engaged pillars flank the opening and the lintels are supported by two Ionic columns. The front pillars were refurbished with one or two layers of thick plaster which extended the pillars beyond the surface of the walls. While we now carved scenic capitols these may have been covered over as well. On each of these capitols the northeast faces have been intentionally damaged, where essential motifs have been removed and the little side columns remain intact. The inner sides each preserve a figural scene. The one on the north corner depicts a relief of a Pan and a Meanad. The eastern corner capitol depicts a seated figure perhaps of Dionysus with a fully clothed female figure standing behind him. The floor of this room was cocciopesto and oddly covered over the bases of the columns. The three walls all preserve their final frescos. The plaster is very thick and at least two layers are discernible. The tree walls also preserve and elaborate molded cornice with dentil decoration. Except for a short door connecting the dining room to a smaller dining room to southeast, the three walls of this room preserve third style wall paintings. These have white backgrounds. The dado is divided into small rectangular panels with small rectangles alternating with large ones. The small ones have shields with fillets. The mid section preserves the vertical lines dividing large panels but no other details are visible. These dividing lines are in red and yellow, some with highly ornate decoration. The upper panel just below the cornice molding shows delicate birds in red paint in small rectangular panels alternating with large rectangular panels containing red griffins flanked by stylized tree motifs and delicate red branches. The remaining fresco plaster preserves no paint except in the west corner. The upper walls preserve beam holes on the northwest wall and southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium to the northeast and the small dining room 5 on the south east side.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of the northeast wall, in the center of a large panel framed by the north corner and the slender decorated column to the southeast is a flirting female figure. In her right hand she holds a platter on which are various fruits, which kinds are indistinguishable.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The painting is contiguous to the floor below. Painting 3104 is to the northwest. Painting 2105 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION:
The oven is on the northeast wall. This oven was made more heat efficient by encasing the baking mound in a smoke chamber. It is bricked to the ceiling. The smoke escaped through a vent on the front wall of this encasing. This oven is unique due to the huge area below the oven available for the storage of charcoal/wood. The structure is laid on a stone base. The lowest corner of the mound is wider and composed of hard stone to resist blows from shovels. The oven opening is faced with lava stones. Quote, "Bakers, Bakeshops and Bread..." Mayeske. For more description of the features and their purposes see page 41.

On the front arch of the oven, Warsher reports a grotesque mask of terracotta. We see only the remains of the figure's mane where the mask was. There is also a carved phallus on the arch, a common atropeic feature on ovens. In the encasing there is a passthrough on the southeast side. A recessed rectangular opening on the southwest side of the mill accesses this passthrough. A second passthrough on the northwest side connects to a preparation room (3201).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Two water basins (3219 and 3218) and lararium (3233) are to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The stable is a raised area now covered with vegetation, which runs along a northwest/southeast axis and is approximately ten meters in length and four to five meters in width. The entrance is on the west corner of a low southwest, irregular, partitioning wall contiguous to the mill room to the southwest (room 6). The southwest wall is approximately fifty centimeters high. On the side of the mill room and on the inside of the stable is ten centimeters high. On the northwest, northeast, and southeast the walls are to the first story height and beyond. On the northwest wall the plaster survives. In the northeast wall in the east portion a few pieces of plaster with red paint survive, with evidence of remodeling in antiquity. A rhomboidal window in the south corner of the southeast wall allows light. In the north corner of the northeast wall a window appears to have been blocked in antiquity. There is a broken dolium in the east corner of the stable. There is no threshold extant and the floor appears to be sloped at the doorway, however, there is a large square volcanic rock on the west corner of the entrance.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill room (3199) is to the southwest. Oven room (3198) is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the kitchen in the west from the viridarium or from the southwest via the atrium. The L- shaped room runs along a northwest / southeast axis and is in poor condition. There are traces of plaster on the northeast wall. There are four or five holes above this plaster for an unknown purpose. On the north corner of the northeast wall is a partial wall approximately 2 meters long on a northwest / southeast axis abutting the northeast wall. The height is approximately 1.5 meters in the middle and its function is unclear. On the east corner of the northeast and the southeast walls is what appears to be the remains of the latrine (3247) with the northwest portion on a northeast / southwest axis which is approximately 1 meter in length. On the southwest wall is an indentation which runs along northwest / southeast axis the length of the wall and is approximately 50 centimeters high. This would suggest delineation of a cooking platform. The walls are to a second story height. The floor is obscured by lapilli and vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The viridarium (6) is to the west/ southwest, the atrium (3241) is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The room is entered from the salesroom to the south on the south wall. The south wall is of opus mixtum. Some plaster is extant. The color is unclear due to the elements. Wall is of brick coining of opus incertum. There is a rectangular window to the street and is centered in the room with a sill two meters high. There is no plaster extant. The color pattern is unclear due to the elements. The north wall has brick coining of opus incertum. There is some plaster extant, likely white. Seven-beam pockets are visible for the second store, which is non-extant. The east wall is of opus incertum and opus mixtum at the entrance opening. Centered on the wall half meter high is a recess whose identification is unclear but could be shrine/lararium. The floor is of stone rubble. The east wall has a recess in the bricks at the level of the pockets on the north wall. Modern tuck painting is evident on the north, west, east walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A different structure property to the east and north. The street is to the west, salesroom is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: At the northwest rear end of house 6 lies a kitchen which includes a cooking platform and latrine. The kitchen is entered by a doorway off of peristyle walkway 15 to the south. The room is slightly L-shaped with a cooking platform immediately on the west wall upon entering. The latrine occupies the northwest corner of the room. The walls are plain with no plaster remaining. no windows are evident. a pipe from an upper story is visible above the latrine. Some terracotta tiles on the floor denote the area of the latrine. At this time the rest of the floor is rubble.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The west wall is adjacent to the street. The north and west walls attach to adjoining properties. Storeroom 16 enters to the east. Peristyle garden 14 and walkway 15 are to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Room 19 is the longest dining room of this domestic building. Oriented to the south west to the north east, the room is entered from a narrow entrance doorway at the south end of the southwest wall. On the threshold lies three shapeless blocks of stone. Along the same wall at the point where it converges with the southeast wall is a column which today only two blocks remain. This column is partially imbedded and forms decorative corner on the outside of the room. Because of the room's very bad condition nothing much is visible today in terms of decorative layers. However the fragments of red paining on the northeast wall and the existence today of a modern protective tarp on the one section of lapilli covered floor ( tarp which likely covers an excavated fragments of mosaic floor) give the idea for the ancient decorated of the room for dining.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Count yard 16 to the south room 18 to the south west, postium 20 to the south east and room 22 to the north east.

DESCRIPTION: Casa del triclinio all'aperto. Large garden occupying the remainder of the insula to the northwest of the house. The garden is planted with grape vines. Traces of plaster survive along the south wall of the garden on either side of the doorway to room six (6). Red lower register. Pressing tank and dolium (3045) lie to the southwest of the entrance to six (6). In the southwest corner of the garden are the remains of two internal walls that only survive at the junction with the southwest wall. The exterior walls of the garden are extensively restored. In the southwest corner there is a large pile of earthen and ceramic debris. Against the west wall there is the poorly preserved remaining reside of a wall surviving only where it abuts the west wall. Eschebach shows several poorly preserved rooms in this area of the garden. Immediately to the northwest are the remains of a small square room with access to the east. Plastered steps up to the floor of the room and the two masonry supports for a latrine against the wall. In the northwest corner there is a poorly preserved masonry altar (3046) and a deep rectangular cistern directly in the western corner of the garden. One rectangular window in the west wall above the cisterns and two plastered windows. Entrance six in the east wall opens out to the street and the palestra in the southeast corner. There is a blocked doorway with modern lintel opening east to the street. High step and narrow doorway to storeroom 14. Eschebach calls the cistern at the northwest corner a piscina. Jashemski says that it was probably originally planted with vines.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms 14 and 6 are to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The dining room has two entrances with the larger opening west on to the peristyle and fountain. A smaller opening is located on the north wall in the north west corner: this is a service entry. On the north wall plaster survives on the lower register and in the north west corner. The wall has had a good amount of reconstruction and conservation work done on it. Colors are not discernible. On the east wall is a small window located in the center of the wall at the ceiling. The wall painting is better preserved and three registers are discernible. It appears that the wall paintings are of the third style with red and yellow on the bottom register and black, red and yellow in the middle register. The base of an architectural can be seen - possibly a column or pilaster base, above which a canopy is visible, scratched into the plaster. To the left of the column base (in the painting) is possibly a herm or podium but the wall painting is sadly damaged. The upper register is visible only in small amounts but on the east wall only red and black bandings can be seen. The south wall has been heavily restored with only the middle register surviving. In the south west corner of the west wall the lower register is partly visible in black and yellow/white; and the upper register is in black, red, yellow and white panels. The west wall is badly damaged with only plaster surviving at the south west end of the west wall. The ceiling has been restored. The floor is covered with modern archaeological materials. The lintel on the west wall is restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 43 is contiguous to room 44 and 45 to north room 42 to the east, corridor 52 to the south and the peristyle (39) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The prep room (8) is a rectangular room situated on a north west/ south east axis. It has a plastered floor. It has an open entrance to the north west with no defined doorway. The west wall has two square plastered interior windows to the courtyard to the west. In the center of the west wall there is a placing for a down pipe from the floor above. In the south east corner is a rectangular hole has been cut into the floor against which on the east wall is a placing for an arched feature which has been cut into the undecorated plaster. Also on the east wall are three square joists for shelves (?) above which are the joist holes for the floor above. In the center of the north east wall is water feature 3107 which drains east through the wall. The channel of 3107 continues along the east wall to the north where it passes through the partition wall that isolates latrine (3108) from the remainder of the room. In the center of the northern half of the room is a cistern and water channel (3107). A low restored ceiling overlies the northern half of the room preserving the original collapsed beams and floor of the room above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 9 to the northwest, room 6 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The room's long axis is west to east with a direct view to the street. Its primary entrance is through the west wall which is of brick and opus latericium. The south wall is of opus incertum, modern tuck pointing restoration is evident. Some plaster is extant. The color and pattern are unclear because of the elements. The east wall is of opus incertum with a secondary entrance of brick and opus mixtum. There are likely two steps up to exit the dining room through this opening. Three beam pockets are visible for a non-extant second floor. The north wall is opus incertum with evidence of modern reconstruction. There is a small piece of plaster and it is likely a red color. The floor is of stone rubble. This is a dining tablinum because of its view, orientation, and finds in the structure.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A differing property is to the north. A salesroom is to the west. An andron is to the south. A cubiculi is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room. The entrance is located at the eastern corner of southeastern wall. The room is rectangular, oriented southwest. On the northeastern wall a window looks out from the eastern corner to the peristyle court. Couches were located at the southwest side of the room along the northwestern wall, southwestern wall, southeastern wall. Plaster preserves the shallow niche for a couch along the southeast wall. The walls are in very poor condition with only small traces of plaster. No point is preserved. The flooring is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: There are two entrances. One is from entrance 5 corridor 1 on the southwest side through a corridor and the other entrance is on the northeast side 6. No roof. No floor. According to Jashemski this establishment was badly damaged in the earthquake of 62 CE. The rubble was removed at that time and the entire area was planted. The southwest wall is badly damaged, no traces of paint or plaster and partly reconstructed. The south wall is badly damaged with some reconstruction, in the southeastern corner of the room there are traces of a lower wall perhaps defining a space. On the northeast wall a lower wall projects into the room. An entrance from house 15 at corridor 6 has a wall that is badly damaged with faint traces of plaster. The northwest wall is damaged and has been rebuilt. Facing the wall on the right hand side are traces of painting, lower register, faint red and upper, faint yellow. On the southwest wall - facing the entrance at 5 there is a triclinium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: corridor 1, corridor 6

DESCRIPTION: This preparation room has two entrances. The one to the west is a large entrance to dining room 30, to the east side no wall remains but it must have opened to the corridor to the east. No ceiling remains, the floor is obscured by lapilli. The room is L-shaped with five features related to a bakery placed (at the time of recent excavation) near the north wall of the room. The walls and partial walls on the west, south and north sides are badly damaged and reconstructed. Traces of plaster show on the south and west walls - possibly white. As one enters from room 30 the wall to the right is badly damaged and reconstructed and shows traces of white paint (?) in the lower and middle register. There is a lamp niche on the far left high up on the wall facing west, badly damaged. There are traces of plaster and white paint and a possible post hole high in the centre of the wall. In the lower right corner in a vertical row there are 3 square post holes with evidence of a wooden plank in the middle hole. Directly opposite 3 similar square holes are found on the wall of the corridor. The south wall is mostly destroyed and there are no traces. the corridor to the east is the exterior wall to the street (east) The west entrance to room 30 is a reconstruction with a modern wooden lintel. High impressions in plaster running across the opening may reflect the ancient roof line.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: large opening to dining room 30 to the west, possible opening to corridor to the east.

DESCRIPTION: We enter from the south west; to the east there is a high step to a food shop. WE walked into a space that was once an atrium; it has now two benches, triclinium masonry (U-shaped). Then we see to the east an elaborated first style painting and a large entrance to a dining tablinum. We then pass an open air rectangular garden area with a northwest/southeast axis. There is a medium size door with a high large threshold. To the north there is a large entrance to a horticultural area. This space is a large room with four U-shaped benches triclinium masonry benches. Three of these have tables. There are open spaces separating each pair of benches. there are high walls both sides of the neighbors. In the east wall that separates the garden there is a high lararium niche. There is a possibility of an even higher up lararium in this wall but it doesn't have the supporting brick. The floor of this room is lapilli. In the entrance to the horticultural space there is a brick demarcation in the floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Horticultural (10) to the north east, room (6) to the south west.

DESCRIPTION: Square tablinum opening out southwest to the atrium. Restored threshold opus signinum pavement with large numbers of white limestone? inclusions. In the center of the northeast there is a large low open window looking out to the small garden/courtyard. Modern lintel on the window in the west entrance. Modern rood. First style decoration in white, green, red, and yellow survives extensively. Traces of plaster molding on the northwest, southwest and northeast walls. The upper register on the northwest/northeast walls may indicate a false ceiling. High in the northwest door jamb is a rectangular slot. However, this slot is not matched by a slot on the opposite jamb.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Peristyle (3) occupies a long rectangular space which is oriented northwest/southeast. The center fishpond is surrounded by a row of slender pilasters. On the northeast/southwest and southeast sides. Today the area is planted with small trees and bushes. In the past it could have been used as either an ornamental garden or vegetable garden. On the southeast side of the peristyle, the pilasters rest on the paved porticus which is covered today by a sloping roof. On the other side of the same row of pilasters, a channel runs along the edge of the central area. On the southeast and northeast side, on the contrary, the pilasters are resting directly on the natural ground and today support a pergola with vines. The northeast wall of the peristyle is articulated with alternating semicircular and square niches. On the bottom of each of the niches is a platform slightly raised above the surrounding areas. The walls of most of the niches are decorated with what appears to be reddish crushed stone framed by a thin blue band. On the southwest porticus are sixteen slender pilasters with Corinthian capitals. The pilasters are decorated with channel-like ornamentation which is interrupted half way up with rectangular panels on all four sides. The pair of central pilasters facing the entrance of the triclinium (8) are approximately 30 centimeters higher than the other pilasters. On the opposite porticus (southeast/northeast), the pilasters are completely enclosed in modern wooden supports.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southwest are rooms (4, 7, 8, 6, 9, 10, 13, 14) To the northwest is atrium (1). To the north is the bath suite (36). to the southeast is dining room (23) and adjoining open area.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the room from the northeast. The room is rectangular on a southwest/northeast axis with a door on the south corner of the southwest wall and the north corner of the northwest wall. High on the southwest wall is a large rectangular window on vertical axis. In the center of the southwest wall is a large semicircular niche. Still extant at the top is a stucco decoration in the shape of a seashell. On the southeast and northwest walls are rectangular niches. On the southwest wall between the semicircular niche and the west corner appears to be a rectangular light well which penetrates the wall at an oblique angle. the opening into the room is much larger than the hole that penetrates the room (14?). All four walls are covered with fourth style wall painting. The floor is in opus signinum and fragments of brick. As reconstructed, the ceiling is quite high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room (14) to the southwest, room (10) to the northwest, and room (2) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Space 2 is a large horticultural area that encompasses the bulk of an earlier property. Cubiculi surround along the northwest and north sides of the garden. In the southwest corner there is a small dolium against the north cubiculi with a large water cistern and three rectangular features of uncertain use. To the south of the water feature there is a cistern head. Jashemski (page 127) says this was used for viticulture with flowers. Planting beds were visible at that time. Traces of painting with red lower register and yellow panels and no longer visible central image survives in the center of the south wall of the garden. Several indentations in the southwest corner of the garden may mark subterranean features such as dolia. Eschebach reports 11 amphorae in this house with the inscriptions LYMPHAE.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: All the rooms of the property are to he west and north of the garden.

DESCRIPTION: This dolium, which is approximately 50-60 am high, is cylindrical and tapers in to a large, wide protruding lip at its height. There are chips along the northwest side of the lip and the dolium if filled with volcanic debris, otherwise the dolium appears to be in good in repair. in antiquity the dolium probably touched the southeast wall. The construction material is red terracotta.
A circular stone cistern mouth partially covered by an arched plaster recess in the west wall. The cistern is filled with debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cistern is placed directly adjacent to the kneading basin (6211) to the south and the preparation platform (6210) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: There is well preserved stairwell to the southeast of the entrance. We enter the room from the portico from the southeast. southeast of the portico is a garden. The portico has five brown columns at the corners. Garden is mentioned to point attractive view from the dining room. No ceiling remains. It was a room with a high ceiling. The floor is lapilli. The room is rectangular shaped. The entrance is as wide as the room. On the southwestern wall there is evidence of a very long niche for a dining couch. There is plaster 'yellow-red-white' on the southwestern wall. The west corner shows the common red paint. The northwestern wall shows a red lower register with white stenciling and a yellow band. The northeastern wall has a a red lower register with a minimal evidence of a white dado with yellow plaster. There are no windows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 is to the south east

DESCRIPTION: Room entered from atrium 25. Room is on northeast side of atrium looking toward atrium to the southwest. Entrance is impressive two step marble threshold with evidence of door jambs on each step. No evidence of ceiling or room. Floor is rubble and dirt. North wall of room is badly damaged. Traces of plaster with a yellow white pigment with molding and a recessed area running half of the also with traces of plater and painting with possible platform. Facing the wall to the right is evidence of deeper recess, maybe a cupboard niche with traces of plaster and paint. See feature 6371. Rear wall on the east side is badly damaged. Wall on south side is badly damaged with traces of plaster with wall paint of red and yellow, possibly three registers. Wall to the west, the right side of doorway entrance is badly damaged.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Direct view onto atrium 25.

DESCRIPTION:
From the northwest we enter this large dining room over a lava stone threshold. The room is somewhat irregular in shape due to the fact that the doorway entrance on the north extends into the room approximately three and a half feet (105 cms) and is formed from a brick column face with painted plaster. The corresponding door jam is a brick column which abuts the southwest wall between corridor 7 and only protrudes into the room approximately 6 inches ( 15 cms). It is faced with painted plaster. The axis of the room, which is mostly rectangular, is northeast/southwest. The large doorway divides the vista onto the peristyle garden to the northwest. Alternating red and yellow panels are divided by architectural white and stenciled outlines transcoursing all three registers with the bottom and top being a continuous white panel. Evidence of a water plant exists on the south portion of the northwest wall indicating 4th style.
High in the center of the southeast wall is a circular window which is plastered. Above the window is an intricate molding of plants and shells. A remnant is seen on the southwest wall. Four open joist holes appear high on the southwest wall above the molding area. There is a 5th but covered joist hole.
The walls are preserved beyond a first story height with the northeast wall being the exception. The floor is obscured with vegetation and lapilli. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Corridor 7 to the northwest
Dining room 9 to northeast

DESCRIPTION: Room 11 is a large rectangular space oriented on a northwest/southeast axis. It is entered by a posticum to the northeast but it could also have been entered from shops Room 9 (2.1.5) and shops Room 14 (2.1.6) and through dining rooms 10 (2810) and 15 (2807) respectively. This space was once used as a passageway for carts to the possible stables (Room 12 and 13) to the southwest. The large opening of the posticum was partly walled later on. This space could be described as a generic courtyard, a definition that is preferable to the "garden" mentioned by Eschebach. In this space a number of amphorae were found but in the previous description of this area there is no mention of the extant location. The courtyard is framed by two large entrances to the southwest (the one to space 12; the other to space 8) and two more entrances to the northwest (Rooms 10 and 15). each of the entrances to Room 10 and 15 is also adjoined by a large window to the west of each doorway. Above each entrance to 12 and 8 is a large rectangular window. The walls to the southwest and northwest are mostly preserved in their first floor height, while the southeast and northwest are today two meters high. The floor is covered with vegetation and a bush is in the center of the room.

DESCRIPTION: Entering the dining room from the northwest through a shop that has a wide opening to the street. We are unprepared to say what happened within this shop. The threshold raises the floor about two inches above the unknown shop floor. The floor is concrete and tesserae. In the north corner there is a large staircase with three large steps apparent and the stairs have evidence of continuing up on the northeast wall. On the northeast wall you see large portions of 4th style painting. The lower register is black, middle zone is yellow, red and white/cream. On the southeastern wall there is a large entrance doorway to the garden almost duplicated in width to the garden windows. The 4th style painting continues on this wall with lower zone black and middle red and cream and yellow with stenciling. On the southwest wall, the 4th style painting continues the same colors. On the top zone appears to be a small architectural rectangular scenic painting. On the northwest wall that opens to the shop, the 4th style painting continues. This room is currently roofed with modern wooden ceiling. It is a comfortable room with cool breezes. There are no features evident except for painting a stairs.

DESCRIPTION:
We have decided that this huge walkaround is an ambulatory passage. Beyond the ambulatory we see the immense peristyle garden (12) and triclinium area at the back. This beautiful walkway seems to slope gently towards the garden (12) in all four areas. Within this ambulatory are 15 columns and an engaged column. The columns are Doric and of a good size. They stand on a stylobate of very early stones that seem to be in good shape. Alongside these raised stones is a water drainage system, recessed in the center and raised on two sides. In the southwest corner we see a drainhole and behind it a cistern opening (well-head) which is temporarily covered with a big stone. There is a rectangular cistern cover in the garden (12), in front of the engaged column.
We see a rectangular-shaped basin with waterproof cement/plaster. The two small rectangular sides form a semicircle towards the center. The water basin is slightly out of line with the atrium.
There is easy access to and from this ambulatory. There are 12 entrances to various rooms on the north, west, and southwest. There are three very large windows along the ambulatory. To one room (47) off the ambulatory there is a long display of cast window sections. At the bottom of this range of windows there is a ledge on which food and drink might have been placed.
We note in the large walls around the garden (12) there are places for lamps in the dining garden area and along the two back walls.

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain sits on the north side of the Via della Fortuna at the northwest corner of the intersection with the Vicolo Dei Vetti. It is constructed of volcanic stone labs. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.94 meters by 1.23 meters and is 0.70 meters deep. There is a rounded lining at the wall/floor junction. The floor lining is no longer extant, revealing stone and tile bottom. The pilaster sits atop the center of the northwestern slab and is decorated by a large-eyed bovine. The overflow is at the top center of the southeastern slab and the drain is near the interior eastern corner. There are deep worn hand recesses on either side of the pilaster and near the interior northern and western corners. Iron clamps joining the stone slabs are "T"d at both ends. There is modern working plumbing.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the processing room from the South by way of area 12. The room has a Southeast-Northwest axis. The processing room was a pseudoperistyle with two columns in the southeast side of the puteus that has been converted for processing fish sauce. The pseudoperistyle is defined by a low wall (Pouteus) which begins against the Northeast wall and runs roughly Northeast-Southwest, turning to the Northwest just before reaching the Southwest wall. The Northwest-Southeast arm extends to just past bedroom 7 where it ends and makes a right angle turn to the Northeast where it ends about 3 feet. The end stone of this third arm has a decorative design and may in fact be a reused stone. Farther to the Northwest, where the 3rd arm turns at a right angle along the southwest wall are three large dolia, each containing the remains of fish sauce (Allec). Along the North wall, running roughly Southwest/Northeast are 2 additional dolia, just beyond the 2nd dolia a doorway with 3 steps leads to garden 10 to the Northwest. In the Northeast corner of the processing room is the latrine. TO the Southeast of the front wall of the latrine is a dolium containing the remains of fish sauce. In the East corner of the processing room is a built-up platform up to the level of a hole in the Northeast wall that extends to the street on the outside. Along the Northwest wall on either side of the doorway to garden 10 is a garden painting. The latrine in the Northeast corner seems to have been inserted into the corner as the painting shows a ground line of plants at the top. It is uncertain if the garden painting extended to the Northeast before the latrine was inserted. The condition all along the wall is poor, though it clearly has dense foliage and birds. Portions of the Southwest wall have plaster, but little remains of decoration. The Northeast wall, as extent, lacks plaster.

DESCRIPTION: Embedded ceramic dolium with ancient repair. Lip does not survive. Filled with earth. DESCRIPTION:
The kitchen is a rectangular room on a NE/SW axis. Floor is obscured by earth and vegetation throughout. The room is entered through a doorway in the east corner with no visible threshold from room 10, and a doorway with stepped threshold and modern lintel in the south corner to room 18. In the north corner there is a doorway to room 14 with a modern lintel and no visible threshold. High in the northwest wall there is a rectangular window and placings for floor joists for the floor above. Patches of undecorated plaster survive. The eastern wall shows extensive signs of modification or reconstruction, with a small window in the east corner. The south wall is extensively restored. In the east corner there is latrine 4385 and in the south corner, cistern 4384. The latrine is separated from the rest of the room by a low masonry wall.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eshebach p105,106; PPM p406,407; PPP 1, p249-252; Clarke 2006, p233-239; Jashemski p134,135.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 is to the southwest, room 18 is to the south, room 14 is to the north-northwest of kitchen 4383.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the kitchen from room 9. It is a small rectangular room with a pounded earth floor on a northwest southeast axis. On the northeast wall a small window opening onto what was probably a small garden. The northeast doorway is very narrow and tall, opening onto a light well. There is a quern in the north corner and a cooking platform wit a dirt pot. No signs of a lip but the edge is built up with stones against the northwest corner and wall. The roof has been replaced. On the northeast and northwest walls of the kitchen there is a lararium with a splendid scene of worship. The background is cream in color.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room #9 to the southwest, room #8 (garden) to the east Room #9 to the southwest, room #8 (garden) to the east None

DESCRIPTION: A great lararium painting appears in the north corner of this kitchen. On the northwest wall there is an arched lararium. The background is cream color and we see a garland at the top and two skewers containing meat, garland and possibly eggplant(?). Inside he lararium niche is a green garland, a raised half shelf. The bottom beneath the lararium is a protective snake next to another altar where there is burning food offerings. To the left is a hamhock which shows how it is tied up. On the northeast side, the lararium painting extends to the window. There is a large garland that extends over these. A gold rhyton is in one hand (of a man). On the ground line, we see a scene of a household sacrifice. The worshippers have shoes on. We can see clearly fourteen worshippers plus feet. A tipica player is piping, standing next to the altar. Two women with veils over their heads with the female sign of worship. On the altar is a sacrifice. The males, both full grown and one boy, most of them wearing tunics and holding their right hand over their hearts. Most are looking at the altar. Some look to the viewer. Beneath this is a picture of a depiction of half cow, next to him looks like a hourse with a backpack. Faint figure of a donkey or camel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking Platform (2542) to the southwest, Quern (2544) to the northeast. None Cooking Platform (2542) to the southwest, Quern (2544) to the northeast.

Where the rim has broken one can see four holes drilled into the rim. This break is directly opposite an iron hook imbedded in the rim for securing the lid. This dolium is straight-sided, with a carinated shoulder rising inward to a slightly flaring rim. It is made of terracotta.â€ƒ

DESCRIPTION: This is a fresco painting in situ in the center of the northeast wall. It is a rondel painted against a yellow panel. Fruit is placed on a shell on a windowsill and we can identify cherries along with some other larger fruit.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining room from a very wide and high doorway, its shape is rectangular and is on a SE/NW axis. This room has some examples of tesserae laid in concrete, most of it is gone. There is plaster and painting examples on all of the walls but they are not very well preserved. All of the walls are completely restored to a high restored ceiling. The back wall shows a panel painted black. The next level at the back is red and the east and west walls are yellow panels. The most interesting painting remains on the East and West walls. There is a border divided into rectagulars, they are blue turkeys, deep red and rllow and repeated. On these panels there are small stenciled flowers. The flowers are cream and deep red. Above this elaborate border is a smal lrectangular panel with blue turkies background, a triangular base and a very tall slender colou. At the same level of the rectangular panels are larger panels of deep red, yellow and black. No other painting can be seen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: preparation room 2642 to NE preperation room 2642 to NE None

DESCRIPTION:
This is the House of Lesbianus. We have determined that it is a restaurant.

This is a short, round, reconstructed masonry fountain edge with evidence of waterproof cement within. Eschebach labels this a fountain. It is directly outside the grilled window to room 3 (4366). A drain remains on the southeast side.

This water tower is on the south side of the via dell' Abbondanza at the intersection with the bicolored di Octavius Quarto. It abuts 2.2.1. The tower is constructed of tufa masonry. The pipe recess on the south west face has the remains of a lead pipet ground level in situ. The pipe recesses on the north west and south east abut 2.2.1. Abutting the tower on the south east is a stone and cement 'bench' that has what appears to be a door post recess and the remains of an iron circular item that is slightly recessed. When excavated this tower had a lead tank top along with the remains of two lead pipes, one in and one out of the tank. To the west of the tower, across the bicolored is a stop cock in situ. BIBLIOGRAPHY: Pompeii in Pictures; Notizie degli scavi di antichita 14 p. 255

DESCRIPTION: The dining room is located on the east side of the house. The room is on a north south axis. One enters the room from the east. The entrance has a fauces, atrium, cubliculian then room #4. It is a rectangular room overlooking the garden with a cistern, large arched lararium niche with cream and red dots. The ceiling is of modern restoration. The floor is concrete. Window half way up the east wall about 8 feet up. The south wall has a large window with a marble lintel. Walls have been decorated since 62. The lower wall (socle) reverts back to the first style. Colors in the lower panels are green, red, peach and yellow. Panels are divided into separate panel sections. Colored set of panels up are predominantly, yellow with red stencil boarder. Griffins inside the panels of the south wall. Central panel on the northeast wall has a small picture of reclining tibicen player. Figure possibly reclines on a kline. On the south wall is another reclining figure of a musician on a kline, holding in right hand what appears to be a harp. Lions on the side panels of the east wall. In all there are seven distinct animals on the side panels (possibly 1 missing?) Top panels are divided into zones of turquoise, red and yellow. Ceiling is of modern construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms #11 & 12 to the west. Rooms #11 & 12 to the west. None

DESCRIPTION:
Located in region 8 between 2 and 3.

This is a public fountain located on the southeast corner of the forum at the northern end of the Via Delle Scuole. It is in Region 8 between insulas 2 and 3 and is oriented in a slightly northeast-southwest direction. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs and has a rounded lining at the wall/floor junction. The pilaster sits atop the northwest slab and is decorated with the face of a gorgon. The fountain has modern plumbing. The interior of the basin is 1.0 meters by 1.20 meters with a depth of 0.69 meters. The overflow is at the top center of the southwest slab with the drain hole below at street level. The major worn hand placements are at either side of the pilaster and on the northeast and northwest interior corners. The drainage from the fountain goes into a drain/sewage line to the northwest. There is a street shrine on the corner near the fountain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The public fountain is at the southeast corner of the Forum between insula 2 & 3 at the northern end of Via delle Scuole.

DESCRIPTION: This space in front of the altar (4274) has been designated as a public space for eating and drinking as it is associated with the altar. It would have been used at neighborhood festivals for consumption of offerings and public feasting. It is close to an impressive opening to the palaestra area. It is part of the modern Via del Castricio (Street of Castricio).

We hav determined that 2.1.3-7 is a food distribution center based upon the inter-connectedness of the various food shops and storerooms on the property. Room 2 has been identified as a storeroom based upon its doorways to the north west and south east that connect the room to the counter shop of room 1. The room is rectangular in shape and sits on the same north west - southeast axis. The room is a step up from the floor level of room 1 and the floor is cocciopesto. A stairway to an upper level sits in the west corner with two steps and a landing remaining. Walls are opus incertum and were originally frescoed. Fresco remains in the north corner showing a red dado with a white central section divided by red vertical lines (Third Style?) There was a door and a window in the south east wall looking out to garden space 13. The window was fairly large and rectangular. The doorsill was granite. Eschebach talks about an iron door from this space to the space beyond (south east). The ceiling is currently open to the sky.

Jashemski 126; Eschebach 86
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the south east of room 1, to the north west of space 13.

DESCRIPTION: This is a fresco painting in situ in the center of the yellow panel located in the northern section of the northwest wall. This is a central rondel with a dark band surrounding it. A window frame or shelf is depicted with some sort of melon or seeded fruit. Behind this fruit and extending to the left there appears to be a basket with two round red fruits.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This painting is directly west of 4251, which is located on the northeast wall.

DESCRIPTION:
This rectangular room, on a north east - south west axis, has been identified as a tablinum. An opus signinum floor has been preserved throughout and there is a modern ceiling. In the center of the north west wall there is a doorway with a partially preserved stepped threshold and a modern lintel to room 3. In the east end of the south wall there is a wide, open doorway to room 13. This threshold preserves placings for a door and has a modern lintel. In the center of the south wall there is a window to room 13. In the north corner of the room there is the masonry base for stairs to the floor above. The exterior face of the base is painted contiguous with the decorative scheme in the rest of the room. Extensive painted plaster survives on all walls in the Third Style - a black lower register, red panels above and all surmounted by architectural elements on a white background. This room serves as a throughway although the extensive decoration suggests a public function to the rear of the sales room. Ruddell suggests that all of these properties were combined as a single wine seller.

Eschebach 86; Ruddell 80; Amadio, B. 'Regio II, insula 1' in Studi di Rivista Pompeiani 2 (1988) 192-195
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the south east of sales room 3, to the north west of space 13 (space for carts)

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a processing basin however it is not possible to determine its exact purpose. It is a wedge shaped basin in the north corner of the room. The outer surface is painted with stripes and what may be garlands or fruit on a black background. From our vantage point in the doorway we cannot determine any further details. To the east of this basin is an extension of the basin with a raised lip.On the southwest rim there seems to be a hole cut through the wall behind this part of the basin. Whether this allows for the flow of liquid in or out cannot be determined.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is northeast of the doorway and below a small window on the northeast wall.

DESCRIPTION: On the southwest wall at the west end is a fine cooking platform. It is square, with the top being cement. Examples of high lips on the platform touching the walls. Larger deep-arched fuel storage space filled with Custodi containers,on the top is what appears to be an ancient grill which could serve to lift cooking equipment off the hot coals, but could be a modern window grate. Construction is masonry and brick.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium (2498) to West. Water Feature (Cistern-2488) to East. Prep Platform (2490) to southeast. None Lararium (2498) to West. Water Feature (Cistern-2488) to East. Prep Platform (2490) to SouthEast.

DESCRIPTION: This is an L-shaped room with a north-south axis. The northern arm of the room is taken up with oven (6191). To the east and wets of the oven are two small recesses of uncertain use. The western recess has a stepped threshold. The eastern is full of volcanic debris with three floor joists high in the north wall. By the entrance to the eastern recess are the fragments of a dolium. Along the eastern side of the room there are two rectangular brick/tile columns aligning with the doorway of the center of the south wall. Only the base of the northern of the two columns. Between the two columns in the center of the room is the kneading machine (6192). The floor is obscured by lapilli. The west wall is continuous with room 8 and preserves part of the vaulted ceiling. There is no extant wall decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 to the west, room 9 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Room 68 (6923) is a storeroom based on the presence of a cupboard niche and a water basin. The room is located to the immediate northwest of peristyle 26. The floor no longer exists. Walls are opus incertum. There is a closed off window and the doorway in the southeast along with one or two lamp niches. The doorway is of average height and has a stone threshold that contains indentations for door hardware. The southwest wall has water basin (6925) on its west corner and above it is either a closed off window of rectangular shape or perhaps a lararium. Indentations in the wall indicate that shelving was present at several levels. The northwest wall also has at the north corner a large cupboard niche (6924) The walls are all of opus incertum and the southeast and southwest walls have slight remains of plaster. The floor is dirt. No ceiling is present. On the southwest wall there appears to have been a second story doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is situated to the northwest of peristyle 26, to the southwest of room 67 and northeast of hallway 73.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular area to the northwest of processing room 72. Its function is unclear because only a strip of the area has been excavated so its original dimensions and function are unclear. Its use in wine processing is indicated by the presence of three embedded dollia: 6905, 6903, and 6904
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 72 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 21 as a dining room based off of a small atrium on the southeast side of the house; its wide doorway with marble threshold and large window opening to the gardens to the southwest. The room is tall, the ceiling of modern cement, the walls are made of opus incentum and covered in plaster, no decoration remains. The floor on the northeast wall is unique. There is a square cut-out at the floor level that appears to have tiles beneath it. The floor at the easternmost corner of the room has a circular indentation and cut-out. The floor is cut stone tesserae with solid white border on the outside of the room, a black border just inside that and a central field of colored stone inlayed into the white tesserae. The door frame on the northwest wall has a marble threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of atrium (23), to the northeast of garden walkways (22 and 32)

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 38 as a reception hall because it spans the space between the outdoor terrace (38) and the large atrium (41) and as it contains paintings of birds and animals. The room is on a north/south axis and is rectangular in shape. There are three doorways. One on the northeast, one on the southeast, and one on the southwestern wall. The one on the southwest leads to the dining complex, which contains the Dionysus frescoes. The room is painted in the Third style in primarily black paint, which is the dominant color. Small medallions center the large central panels. The dado is divided into two registers, with plant and nature scenes at the bottom and Egyptian motifs at the top of the dado. Above the central panel, another register carries the theme forward. A series of post holes on the east and west walls show ceiling height. On the south wall and north wall, we can see evidence of a frescoed room above. The floor is tiled with white cut tessarae, with a black border and a black inset covering the outer edges.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of atrium (41). North of terrace (37). To the west of room 36.

DESCRIPTION: This is the house of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. We enter the preparation room from the northeast. There is a marble threshold containing holes for door posts. The door is narrow but high. Red, yellow and white painted plaster survives on the southeast portion of the entrance. Painted plaster survives on all four walls, but the room is poorly preserved. The floor is covered with lapilli. On the southwest wall are two vertical parallel groups of holes. On the south are three holes and on the west are four holes which correspond with the exception of the lowest one on the west side. On the west corner of the northwest wall is feature 3135, a lararium, which is approximately 1 and 1/2 meters from the ground. Above the lararium is evidence of molding which corresponds to a small extant portion of intricate cornice on the southeast upper wall. The height of the ceiling is indeterminate.
To the west wall are 6 installed dolia in an L-shaped counter. Reconstructed marble counter surface. Evidence of painted wall decoration. There is a lararium on west wall.

DESCRIPTION: This room runs along a northwest/southeast axis and is open to the atrium. Only three partial walls exist. On the northwest wall we find some plaster which appears to have been decorated in antiquity. It is unremarkable now. The floor is obscured with lapili. The is no ceiling extant. There are 3 levels of brickwork on the southwest wall. One level at 3 and a half feet (105 cm), a second at 7 and a half feet (210 cm) and the third level much higher above. The first levels of brickwork extend to the southeast wall.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the atrium from the fauces on the NE side. The atrium is rectangular in shape on a NW-SE axis. The north corner is a door leading to a bedroom. There is Another opening to a bedroom to the east f the fauces. The latter bedroom has a window looking into the atrium. Along the southwest wall in the west corner is a doorway to a bedroom. The southeast of that door is a hallway leading to the back of the house. On the southwest wall, just to the southeast of the hallway, is a tank. Above the tank is a small window looking into the kit chen. In the south corner of the atrium is a large dolium. The walls of the atrium were painted. Only the color of the lower half is identifiable, a faded red. It is not possible to determine the floor. There is no ceiling. Because of the reported find of four fish sauce urcei and the presence of what appears to be a water tank in the atrium, the house has been designated in literature as a fish shop. If so, then the atrium of the house was probably a sales or preparation room. The dolium seems to have contained lime, probably used in the reconstruction of the house as a commercial property.

DESCRIPTION: The square room opens to the south onto porticus (7) and the peristyle (14) beyond through a wide entrance. In the southwest corner is a small door opening to room (5). The walls are decorated with large rectangular red panels framed by ornamental column-like bands. Above the panels runs a black band between yellow bands. Above those are horizontal panels alternating with square panels. All the panels contain ornamental reliefs. Traces of further painting are above but are not well preserved. On the floor a simple, white mosaic frames a long rectangular band decorated with an ivy scroll with fruit and birds inside (figs and cherries). To the north of the band is a square panel containing a grid of four squares framed by a strand guilloche. The squares contain comedy masks (two facing south and facing north). The northeast corner of the floor has been destroyed. The threshold marble is slightly elevated in relation to corridor (7).

On the south corner is a small doorway leading to the andron. The walls on three sides are elaborately decorated in the fourth style. The colors are predominately red and black and blue or green. On the east wall there is a long rectangular yellow painting of a woman riding on a bull. To the right and left of the large rectangular painting was a small painting which has been removed. The threshold of the room shows places where the room could be closed off. The floor of the dining room is higher than the level of the andron.

DESCRIPTION:
It has been identified that 3,2,1 was a domestic house. It has been determined that the last usage of Room 18 was as a dining room. This identification is based on room location within the structure, wall paintings and room size. Dining room 18 is entered from the eastern porticus of peristyle 12 through a large entrance door that almost spans across the entire length of the wall. The entrance door faces porticus 16 and a very small entrance into room 17. The modern-reconstructed walls are reconstructed to their original height and are fully painted. What is inside today is a large back socle supporting 3 large rectangular panels (the two sides are red and the middle is yellow). Only a few traces of architectural structures against a white background are visible in the southwestern corner. On the lower level of the southwestern corner is a recess (couch niche) for a couch (4621). The floor was originally decorated with a mosaic, but only a few white tesserae are visible today. The northern wall is pierced by a high rectangular window is the middle.
Bibliography: Eschebach pp. 102 - 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Couch niche 18 (4621)

DESCRIPTION: The vat in processing room 18 is a very deep rectangular space delimited by mostly preserved walls to the north and northwest. The western wall is preserved for 75 centimeters. At the bottom, in the middle, is a semicircular opening for drainage. The interior walls of the vat are covered with cocciopesto. At the bottom of the western wall and part of the adjoining northern wall and in the southeastern corner the walls protrude inward. Evidence of another drain is visible in the bottom of the eastern wall. However, as the vat is hardly accessible because of its' depth, it is not possible to ascertain whether it is an ancient drain or a modern opening. It is difficult to specify what could have been processed in this vat.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Space 18 to the west. Processing room 16 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The fish pond is a long rectangular structure which covers the entire central area of the peristyle (3). It is ornamented with alternating semicircular and square niches on the northeast and southwest sides. At about 20 centimeters above the ground is a rectangular slab of stone which divides the space of all the niches vertically into two irregularly high spaces. The lower area could be used as fish receptacles above which could be used as support for statues. Dividing the fish pond in quarters are three arches of bricks each supporting a rectangular marble slab which could be used as a walkway to traverse the fishpond. The interior walls of the fishponds are pierced with three drains which are placed in different sections and heights. A large fragment of plaster is visible on the northwest wall.
Close to north wall are four rubble mill bases. No paving stone extant. Bases are in close proximity to each other
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (1808) to the north. None Oven (1808) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that address 3 - 2 - 1 is a domestic structure and although we do not have access because of structural problems, based upon Eschebach, we have named Room 13 on our plan as a diaeta. The small square room sits immediately to the south of a large garden (12) containing a masonry triclinium (24). The scavi maps indicate potentially a bench or a niche on the northeast wall of the room. Walls are of opus incertum and currently back up to the unexcavated area of the site. The views from this room to the garden indicate that Eschebach is probably correct. Further evaluation of Eschebach's identification has call ed into question whether or not he is correct in calling Room 5 a kitchen. If he is wrong, the masonry mass on the northeast wall may be a cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the direct north of Diaeta 14 and to the southwest of dining peristyle gardens 12 and 24.

DESCRIPTION: This small room may have acted as a small passageway between rooms 4 (counter room) , room 7 (dining other) and room 6 (store room ), but may have also been used for drinking and eating goods for sale from the counter room. The room is on a north/south axis with the main entry way on the south wall onto the atrium, with secondary walls on east, west and north walls. From the counter room, rooms number 5 and 7 are visible. On the south was is a large doorway with the remains of plaster in the southeast corner, otherwise no plaster on this wall. On the west wall towards the southwest end is a small marrow doorway. No plaster remains on this wall. On the north wall a doorway is located on the west end. No traces of plaster survive on this wall. On the east wall a door is located a door is located on the southeast end, and traces of plaster with traces of yellow pigment. The walls and ceiling of this room have been heavily reconstructed. The lintels are of modern concrete construction. The floor appears to be of basic plaster construction. DESCRIPTION: One enters the press room from the north through the wide door. The walls were stuccoed and painted, but little remains. In the east wall near the southeast corner is a large window overlooking the processing room (3). The floor is made of opus signinum and slopes slightly south to north so that the grape juice flows into the rectangular vat located in the northeast corner of the room. The vat has a central wall dividing the vat into 2 unequal parts. The entire west part of the room is taken up by the horizontal beam press (not extant). A low wall runs north/south along the side of the vat for approximately four to five feet beyond the south end of the vat, at which point it turns sharply west and extends to the west wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation room to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Ten dolia arranged in two lines of five along the northeast/southwest sides of the room. The dolia are embedded to the depth of the base of the rim. The rim survives on four of the dolia of the northeast side and four of the dolia on the southwest side. Several of the dolia have been repaired in antiquity with lead joints. On the northeast line, the second dolium to the south is stamped - "ROTIC.SC(?)." The third dolium to the south has an illegible rectangular stamp. On the southwest line, the second dolium from the south is stamped - "EROTIC. . ." . Both dolia then appear to be manufactured by the same person or workshop.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Channel 2957 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION:
It has been identified that 3,2,1 was a domestic house. It has been determined that the last usage of room 3 was a dining hall. This identification is based on the size and painted decoration. Dining hall 3 is entered to the south, from an anteroom(Other Foyer 2.) The high entrance door occupies the southeastern corner of the southern wall. The walls are presented to their entire original height and have been partly restored in modern times. The walls are mostly decorated with large white architectural elements against a black background. On the eastern wall are traces of collanated structures with red decorative elements and showing the use of perspective on the upper structure. The upper section of the eastern wall is pierced by a high, rectangular window opening on to the street. No traces of original flooring remain.

BIBLIOGRAPHY

Eschebach

pp 102 to 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Other Foyer 2 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular raised floor and lower course of walls on this structure are extensively restored. There is no visible decoration on the floor. The room is on a northeast/southwest axis. The only surviving wall to the northwest is extensively restored. Eschebach says that this was a room with two windows. There are no traces of these remains. There is no visible threshold. There is a large couch niche (2969) on the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining garden room (4) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Earlier excavators report a lararium in this room. This recessed arch may be the lararium. In the niche are roof tiles, the neck of an amphora, and a gutter tile.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: (2966) below the lararium

DESCRIPTION: To the south of the stairway at the level of the third step is a small hearth. The hearth is roughly rectangular in shape on a north/south axis. In antiquity the sides and probably the top were stuccoed and painted. Remnants appear on all four sides.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Planting rows (2971) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: High on the northwest wall in the upper register are 3 fish. The fish to the right (northeast) is perhaps a red mullet. The 2 to the left (southwest) appear silver or bluish in color (probably can be identified by an expert). The fish appears to be lying on a table but the ground line is not flat.

It is a u-shaped bench triclinium (masonry) with a smaller center table. the side goes along the horticultural space, the medius is engaged to the wall to northwest and the imus is free standing but connects to the northwest wall. there is a center table.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: benches triclinium masonry: to the southwest #2990; to the south #2988; to the southeast #2987

DESCRIPTION: Immediatly adjacent to the south east door leading into Room 4 is a large dolium embedded into the ground. The dolium extends above the ground. The dolium has a slightly flaring body to a carinated shoulder turned inwards to an out-turned horizontal flat rim.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of the dolia, 5027, 5028, 5029, 5030, 5031. To the south west of dolia 5032 and 5033.

DESCRIPTION: In north wall. Small built-in basin with signinum. Directly beneath lararium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 1834 to west and south 12 to south 1834 to west and south
