DESCRIPTION: Located to southeast of storeroom (16) is storeroom 17, entered through a narrow door. This room is vaulted with a large light well in ceiling. The room is roughly rectangular on a southeast to northeast axis. The room was surfaced with plaster that appears to be painted in solid red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 16- storeroom to northwest 16-storetoom to northwest None

DESCRIPTION: Square room opening North into a peristyle and garden. Traces of plaster survive in the corners without any additional traces of decoration. Large plastered window in the center of the east wall opening into 14 subsequently blocked. Plaster lined couch niche in the southeast corner. Threshold with doorjambs for a door to close off the room from the peristyle.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None Peristyle (3) to the north and garden (4) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room on an east/west axis. In the northeast corner of the north wall there is a doorway with a threshold. In the center of the north wall there is a window looking out onto the peristyle. Cocciopesto is visible on the floor by the doorway. The ceiling is restored. Fourth style decoration is visible on all four walls with a black lower register and red above with motifs of erotoi, dea, leopards and deer. The central scene on the south wall is 50% preserved, with 3 surviving figures, one complete with a landscape behind. Myth needs to be identified. Center of the east wall does not survive. Only the lower right corner of the west wall scene survives, showing the lower half of a seated figure. The ceiling has been restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle garden (11) to the north. Peristyle garden (11) to the north. None

DESCRIPTION: The processing room lies in the middle of the structure approximately one half way between the entrance to the house and the garden though not on a direct axis with the entrance. One enters the room from the southeast. If this is as is supposed, a room for treading or pressing grapes (torcularium), there would not have been a door per se but probably wooden steps. The room is rectangular in shape, on a southwest/northeast axis. The floor has not been excavated, nor can the original height of the walls be determined. The walls were stuccoed and appear to be painted, probably red. The floor level was above the level of the room to the southeast (Room 5 - 2791). The identification of the room as a processing room is based on the construction of a masonry foundation for a terracotta vessel located on the outside of the southeast wall. A lead pipe, still in situ, drained the liquid (must) from the room into the terracotta vessel (small dolium) embedded in the masonry and floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 (2791) is to the southeast. Room 5 (2791) is to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular room is situated on a northwest/southeast axis. It is entered from the northwest by room 4 and opens onto room 6 to the southeast. The walls are preserved to the first story. No plaster is extant. The floor is covered with cocciopesto. The kitchen shows evidence of a cooking platform to the southwest and a lararium to the southeast. The ceiling is no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 to the northwest; Room 5 to the northeast; Room 6 to the southeast Room 4 to the northwest; Room 5 to the northeast; Room 6 to the southeast None

DESCRIPTION: On the northeastern wall of room is a large rectangular niche. The walls are plastered and the shelf shows traces of cocciopesto. The niche was probably used as a lararium as the Pompeian shops are usually provided with this kind of religious feature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter (2815) is to the West. Counter (2815) is to the West.

DESCRIPTION: In the west corner of the northwest wall of the kitchen are two masonry supports for a wooden platform, probably for cooking or food preparation. The west support abuts the southwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine (2746) to the northeast. Latrine (2746) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The lararium is a small, semicircular niche pierced into the middle of the northeastern wall of the kitchen. The inner walk of the niche shows traces of red painting. At the base of the niche is a large, tiled ledge that juts out from the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking Platform (2830) to the southwest. None Cooking Platform (2830) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The floor between the cooking platform and the latrine shows demarcation by a threshold in terra cotta on a northeast/southeast axis. One enters to a slightly sloping floor of a latrine. The latrine shows two masonry supports for the seat. You can see the drain on the northeast wall at the floor going outside. The latrine is located in the northeast corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Masonry supports for a cooking platform (2779) are to the northwest. None Masonry supprots for a cooking platform (2779) are to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is the so called complex of Championnet. It is also referred to as the House of the Geometric Mosaics. This is identified as a double house (entrances 14, 16) and part of the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14 TO 20. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. This room (12) has been identified as a preparation room due to its proximity to the kitchen (10) and other preparation rooms (9 and 11) in the house. We enter from corridor (13) which leads from the peristyle and the eel pond ( ) to the atrium. There is no threshold. This doorway is in the western corner of the room, painted white with a red vertical stripe defining the corner. Fragments of similar painted plaster remain in the north corner but it is more poorly preserved. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation room 12 is to the southwest of preparation room 11 (7012) and is to the southeast of corridor 13.

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: This shop is reported by many people, including Eschebach to be a popina, which is a term for a food shop. It has a large entrance to the northwest with evidence of the ability for closure. There is a large step up. Eschebach reports the remains of an imprint of a wooden counter. We see a lapilli floor. The shop has been decorated with red paint on the walls in Pompeiian red. The room is open to the sky. On the southeastern corner there is evidence of a cubiculum with door opening to it at the southeast corner of the shop. On the southeast wall, center, there is a water basin feature. The owner of the shop was Athictus, as shown in two programata (CIL IV 7523, 7545). We have a lararium on the northeast wall; a rectangular shrine with a ledge and cream background with red border in stencils. On the southeast wall, two steps up to a small door. We see a contiguous room with a highly unusual oven. On the southeast wall there is an opening to the atrium to the house and to the east of the opening there are stairs to a second floor. The southwest wall has a rectangular lararium, high up, with a ledge although no paint or plaster remain. There are four niches, plastered and arched, above the lararium. This shop has an entrance (2.2.3) to the street, but this project combines this shop with structure of house as entrance to house (2.2.2).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium to the south; Passage entry to the southwest; Room with oven to the east. Atrium to the south; Passage entry to the southwest; Romm with oven to the east. None

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: This lararium is on the southeastern wall. It is rectangular and has a ledge which is mid-wall height. It is plastered in cream and Pompeiian red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water Feature (2820) to the southeast; Lararium (2822) to the southwest. None Water Feature (2820) to the southeast; Lararium (2822) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The large vineyard lies to the north-northwest of the amphitheater. One can enter the vineyard from a doorway (posticum) on the southeast side wall. The vineyard shape is defined by a wall on all four sides; just inside the entrance to the to the east is a masonry triclinium (2950). In the northwest corner is a preparation building (2), where the grapes were crushed and the wine made. To the southeast of the building and abutting it is another masonry triclinium (2951). Today, the vineyard has been replanted, following the pattern of ancient roots discovered and plotted by Wilhelmina Jashemski. According to Jashemski, in antiquity there were over 2000 vines arranged in rows. In addition, there were 58 trees (probably fruit and nut trees).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Building (2) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter a large vineyard (Foro Boario) at II V, formerly II VIII, through a columned aedicular lintel which duplicates the entrances of the palestra to the south east. As we enter, we see rows of grapevines propped up by wooden supports and a double (wide) lane (north-south path) separating the vines on the west from the vines on the east. Immediately to the south east, against the wall, we see an outdoor masonry triclinium. Jashemski reports this triclinium at 1.medius 485 cm; 1.imus and 1.summus 450 cm; table 60 cm x 130 cm. The 3 corners - 2 to the north and one to the east - have poles that support a pergola that has a grapevine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Masonry triclinium (2951) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: There is a u-shaped masonry triclinium facing north-northeast. There are masonry couches with traces of plaster on the internal face with no extant description. The surface is obscured by vegetation, however, there are possible traces of opus signinum. The southeastern area slopes sharply to the external side. Against the northwestern arm is a rectangular platform that has been added, with traces of an opus signinum surface. Between the arms of the couches is a rectangular table of which the surface has not survived. The walls to the west and south bear traces of plaster in which two registers are discernible. Five amphora were reported by Jashemski along the extant face of the lectus summus. She identifies these as supports for a pergola. They are no longer extant. A modern pergola has been planted.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest corner of 2949 Masonry triclinium (2950) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, NW/SE axis. Floor obscured by lapilli and vegetation, especially at the SE end. No decoration. Undecorated cement restoration on SE wall. Wide doorway at West end of the SW wall. No threshold visible. Catillus (2893) in N end of the room. The base and a neck rim of amphorae were found in the floor of the room, no in situ, dressel 2/4 rim.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 14 is the SW.

DESCRIPTION: The niche is a rectangular niche cut into the east wall. The niche has been inserted later into the structure and the construction of the niche has reused roof tegulae. A relieving arch has b een put in the wall to take the stress of the wall above the niche. Red plaster survives at the bottom of the north and south end of the niche. Most of the plaster is gone.

Large rectangular dining room, Southwest and Northeast axis. Traces of plastered floor survive against triclinium (2928) and benches (2917) and Northeast and Southwest walls. Doorway with modern lintel and tufa stepped threshold in Southeast wall to room 45. Room 47A inserted into the Northwest corner of the room. In center of Northeast wall, a blocked plastered doorway to 51, modern lintel. The wall above this is restored with 2 thresholds (?) and one blocked doorway in the floor above. Along base of Northeast wall, is a gutter, constructed of roof tiles that drains into street to the North via a terracotta pipe. The adjoining plaster floor is contiguous with the facing of couch 2918. The Northwest wall survives only to half its height (?) with undecorated plaster. In the corner of Northwest wall, a drain runs from the down slope of dining couch 2918 out to the street to the North. Southeast wall with undecorated plaster throughout and molded top, leaving a large high opening out to the garden. The roof and supporting pillars above are modern. Southwest wall has undecorated plaster with 2 rectangular holes for shelves (?) Plastered window with modern lintel high in Southwest corner. Rectangular joist hole in center of the wall for the floor above. The wall above is modern
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 47A to Northwest, Room 45 to Southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Just to the east, almost blocking the entrance is the basin for a mechanical kneading machine. The rim of the basin is very thick and penetrated by four holes for the insertion of wooden stakes. In the bottom of the basin is the fixture for the insertion of the iron pivot (non extant). The stone used for the basin is tufa.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room with east west axis. Traces of plaster survive in the northeast and northwest corners. No sign of decoration. Doorway western end of south wall opens to peristyle (room 9). Collapse of southern end of west wall look through into garden. South wall survives only to about two and a half feet, therefore unclear if window was facing south to the garden. Size and position to garden suggests dining room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: garden (room 8) to the west. Peristyle (room 9) to the south. (room 11) to the west. garden (room 8) to the west. Paristyle (room 9) to the south. (room 11) to the west. None

DESCRIPTION: Room 5 is square and is entered from room 4 to the northwest. Opposite the entrance on the southeastern wall is a window looking out onto room 6. The window ledge is tiled. In the northern corner of the room beginning about 50 centimeters off the ground is a recess about 50 centimeters wide and 50 centimeters deep. The walls of this recess along with the four walls of the room show evidence of plaster. The room is preserved to the first floor height. Lapilli covers the ground. The ceiling is no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 to the northwest; Room 6 to the south; Room 7 to the southwest Room 4 to the northwest; Room 6 to the south; Room 7 to the southwest None

Room 15 is a rectangular dining room on a northwest/southeast axis based upon a wide entrance looking directly towards dining peristyle gardens 12 and 24, directly to the northeast. Garden 12 contains a fountain that would be easily seen by the diners. Currently braced with metal and wood supports and scaffolding, wall and floor construction is impossible to see.

DESCRIPTION: The hearth leans against the northwestern wall of room two. It is situated between the entrances into room nine (shop) and room one ( fauces). It is a U-shaped brick structure in the middle of which is a hole for the fire. The open end of the U FACES South. The top layer of the hearth is tiled.

The long and large cooking platform extends along the southeastern wall of Room 13. The top surface is covered by scattered fragments of tiles which are interspersed with moss. There is no evidence it was plastered.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular cupboard niche is located in the northwest was at the west end of the room. This niche has been created by closing up a doorway between Rooms 4 and 1. The original height of the niche is not discernible. Yellow plaster survives on the southwest and northeast walls of the niche with red banding in the corners. The full height of the niche is not discernible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The niche in Room 2 is located in the west corner of the room on the northwest wall. Northwest of the couch niche 1600.

DESCRIPTION: Inside the northeast and southeast walls is a gutter surfaced with a waterproofed stucco. The gutter beginning in the north corner runs northwest/southeast until it reaches the east corner where it turns at a right angle towards the southwest. In the south corner it empties into a drain located beneath the large puteal. In the east corner to the west of the gutter is a construction of unknown use that slopes strongly from west to east, opening towards the gutter.

A five foot wall partially separates the cooking platform from the latrine. The entrance is SE of the corridor on the NW. The SW wall shows four narrow windows to the street. The latrine receives water from the cooking platform side to the E. The latrine slopes to the SE.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the cooking platform 2928 and water feature, basin, 2942 to the East

DESCRIPTION:
There are alternating semicircular and rectangular bays (alcoves) ten in all "which contained raised planting beds. The semicircular bays were covered with pumice and each had a band of Egyptian blue along the sides and top. The central bay had four bands of Egyptian blue."(p87)
The location of these bays overlooks the fishponds; they all directly face the marble summer triclinium. The area of the bays is shaded by an elaborate pergola (in 2011) laden with green grapes. I think these bays could have been used by large or small dining groups. One person could lie down, or two people could sit and be served with a portable table.
The five rectangular bays show no pumice or Egyptian blue tessera. They are all stripped and are being prepared for redecoration. The fifth bay from the N aligns with the marble summer triclinium. This is the "central bay" to which Jashemski refers.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: fish pond 2937 to W

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 5 opens to the north off atrium 2. This room is oriented southeast/northwest. it shows a very large entrance leading into a rectangular space which is divided into 2 unequally-sized parts by a low wall running east-west direction for half of the length of the room. It is not clear how the small space (B) at the back could have been used, as it is not possible to define the original height of the dividing wall. Was it low enough for supporting, for example, lamps or statuettes? Or was it high so that two separate spaces were created? The northeastern wall of the room doesn't run parallel to the opposite wall, since it is interrupted by a L-shaped wall against which the above-mentioned low wall rests. The three preserved walls are approximately 1.8 meters high with some traces of reconstruction. The floor today is covered with lapilli. Traces of wall plaster are visible in the northern corner of the room and onto the northeastern corner of the L-shaped wall. A square stone platform is placed on the northwestern side of space B (it's function is not certain). A pile of broken terracotta bricks lays in the northwestern corner of the room next to the square stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 to the south. Latrine 10 and preparation room 9 to the north. Kitchen 54 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Visitors entering from the Nocera gate will see the first door to the north of the gate. There is a high step to enter the doorway. One enters that small room just inside the entrance. On the north is a large space which leads to the garden/peristyle. On the southeast wall is an oven. On the west wall there is a locked modern door. The floor is pounded concrete. There are two small high windows on the southwest wall placed diagonally. The higher window is to the south of the lower window. There is a remnant of plaster on the southwest wall below the windows. The ceiling is of modern reconstruction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (4), the dining garden is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular tufa altar with lipped and sculptured top. The northeast and south sides are undecorated. The west side is decorated with a club carved in relief. The altar abuts directly against the northeast wall in the garden. Above the altar is an arched recessed lararium niche. Undecorated plaster survives. Four holes have been cut into the plaster floor in the niche. Three of the holes abut directly against the rear wall. In front and below the niche a tile has been embedded, extending out in front of the altar. The tile is plastered. No trace of decoration.

The latrine is in the northern corner of the room. What is hardly visible today are two shapeless stone fragments, which slope down toward the middle of the room and frame a rectangular space which is now covered with lapilli. On the top of the framing fragment toward the northwest wall is a large terra cotta tile with high edges above which a modern drain pipe running along the northeast wall to its entire height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the south room 3 which contains preparation platform on the opposite side

DESCRIPTION:
In the House of Obelius Firmus in the large kitchen 33, there is a good-sized latrine in the south corner. Remaining is a floor and a seat support. No drain is visible, but the area appears to have been separated from the rest of the kitchen by a masonry wall.

Bibliography: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of cooking platform 4422 and basin 4424, to the south of cooking platform 4421 and to the west of lararium 4423.

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 2 is located in this small food and drink shop perpendicular to the sales room 1 (4887) on a north west / south east axis. Entrance to the room is a doorway near the north east corner of the sales room. The walls are of opus incertum, with the axis of the room arch mimicking the arch of the arcade. Some red painted plaster remains in the arch. The floor is grass today and the original is unidentifiable.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North east of sales room 1

DESCRIPTION: Mill 6085 is the most northeast of the three mills within the mill oven room. The mills is surrounded by volcanic paving stones. The mills base is circular but has been restored. No lead covering remains. A partial catillus is seated upon a meta, both of which are constructed in volcanic stone. The typical two holes for the turning apparatus survives in the catillus but no metal survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill 6085 is contiguous with mill 6086 to the west and the oven 6083 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: The long arm of the masonry counter abuts against the north wall and lies on a axis with the room (north/south). The short arm of the counter lies at a right angle to the long arm and extends to the east a short distance. On the north end of the long arm is a step shelf with three steps. Just south the stepped shelf, embedded in the long arm of the counter is amphora. On the east side of the stepped shelf, below the top and second shelf, is a small cavity rectangular in shape which may be used as a storage area. To the south of the embedded amphora at the rear of the long arm and where the short arm extends to the east is a large round opening for placement of a kettle. The opening extends down to a platform area that extends further to the south. The part of the platform below where a kettle could be placed, probably is where a fire was built. The part of the platform that extends beyond the long arm of the counter has a lip on three sides. The area could also be used for a brazier or other vessels of food. The exterior of the counter was plastered and appears to have been painted. It is difficult to determine the materials of the top of the counter, plain plaster or tiles. The stepped shelves extends beyond the corner of the long arm towards the east. Below the small rectangular cavity in the northeast corner, the lip curves inward towards the west. The portion of the end of the step shelf to the south forms a lip that extends down slightly. This lip extends to within a couple of inches of the south end of the step shelf. The purpose of the lip and extension are unknown.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Square cooking platform with arched brick built recess below, well preserved. Tile cooking surface above. Against wall to the east are three masonry supports for cooking vessels. Behind supports against east wall at junction of the two, the plaster wall decoration is preserved. The platform is immediately adjacent to the shop entrance to the Vicolo del Citarista to the south. Above the platform, high in the east wall is a square window opening onto the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 1819 - Masonry support to west. 1817 - Counter to south. None 1819 - Masonary support to west. 1817 - Counter to south.

DESCRIPTION: Semicircular, arched lararium. Plaster lined with no extant decoration. Located in the eastern end of the south wall beside counter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 1817 - counter to north. None 1817 - counter to north.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the kitchen through the doorway to the northwest. It is L shaped with the northwest/southeast is the long axis; northeast/southwest is the short axis. The designation as kitchen derives mainly from its position since there are no extant features associated with them. (Fiorelli, p.61 identifies this room as a kitchen). In the north wall in the back of the room is a window looking out onto the street. To the southwest is a doorway leading to a small bedroom (7). If the kitchen was decorated in antiquity, nothing remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Small bedroom to the southwest. Small bedroom to the southwest. None

DESCRIPTION: On the northwest side of the pillar in the north west wall below a painting of a garland are 2 cornucopia in a heraldic placement flanking an elaborate caduceus. At the top of each cornucopia is a lid on each side of which are items by food, such as cherries, perhaps figs, pomegranates and eggs? Each cornucopia is similarly decorated.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation platform 3003 is southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Space 2 is a very large rectangular room which is oriented northwest to southeast. The floor of the room, which today is covered with vegetation and lapilli, is about 5 cm above the adjoining mil/oven room. The threshold is covered by one rectangular slab of volcanic material, which shows a fracture. The walls are not completely preserved to the northeast and northwest, while the walls have been restored to the southwest and northwest in their entire height. A number of holes of different size, shape and height appear on these restored walls, but at this stage, following modern construction, it is difficult to assess their function. The processing room contains a latrine and preparation platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: mill/oven room 1 to northwest

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that address 3-2-1 is a domestic structure, and although we do not have access because of structural problems, based upon Eschebach, we have named room 14 on our plan as a diaeta. This very small square room sits between diaeta 13 and dining room 15, with a door opening to a dining peristyle garden, rooms 12 and 24. Walls are opus incertum and back up to the unexcavated area. This room sits in the southwest quadrant of the house.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 102
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of diaeta 13, to the west of dining room 15, and to the southwest of dining peristyles 12 and 24.

DESCRIPTION: The square stone altar is about one meter high and 2/3 of a meter wide. The altar is in the central court of the Room 3 towards the northern corner. The stone alter is interspersed with long rectangular bricks. The altar is placed on a straight axis between the fauces and Room 4 (where the priest probably started the ceremony).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Room 17 open at the back of Room 15 to the south. It is a small rectangular room along a southwest/northeast axis. Excavation reports mention stairs to the southwest of the entrance but what is visible today is only crumbled foundation sloping down to the northeast. The heavily restored walls (south east and southwest) preserved to the first story. The northwestern wall of the storeroom has been reconstructed to about two meters high. The ceiling is no longer extant. The floor is covered with lapilli. No evidence of plaster remains
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room (2814) to the northwest. Room 14 to the southeast. Counter room (2814) to the northwest. Room 14 to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: We enter the old atrium from a northwest entrance. There is a marble impluvium and a beautiful reconstructed compluvium. On the north wall is a 4th style wall painting (2926) and an apparent cornice. The floor is white and black mosaic tesserae. At the northwest entrance of the atrium are three marble steps. There are entrances to a dining room and a dining tablinum on the northeast wall and a third door leading to a corridor. On the southeast wall are two doors. On the southwest wall are three doors. The southwest and the northwest doors lead up to small rooms, and the west door leads to a blocked fauces. Along the north wall is the main entrance to the atrium and two doors lead to a storeroom (22).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: rooms 23 and 24 to the east, and room 22 to the northwest

DESCRIPTION: The mill platform base is a modern reconstruction with a parged modern concrete collection surface. The meta is extant with no cracks or missing material. There is no catillus.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill is one of four in the room. It is the mill closest to the oven, the kneading base and the cistern head.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a possible cooking platform. We have determined the usage of this room is a kitchen based upon the location on the east side of the passage way (9), south of the peristyle. We believe that we have identified various features designating it as a kitchen. This cooking platform consists of a rectangular section in the northwest corner of the room. Although it is a badly preserved, we see evidence of low walls separating it from a rectangular apsed wall in back that abuts the heated wall of the bath. Approximately four feet high, there is scant evidence of a cooking platform on the top surface.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 102, 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Unidentified bulging feature is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of the room a rectangularly shaped vaulted space is constructed into the northwest wall. In the northwest wall of the storage space appears to be three (3) sockets to accommodate wooden beams. No evidence of stucco or painting remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cistern (2935) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of the room is a cistern. A stone puteal defines the central opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Storage space (2934) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Running along the neighboring wall to the south east there is a free standing bench triclinium masonry. It has a large rectangular table in the middle. In an effort to understand it we had eighteen staff members comfortably seated on these benches. Between this bench and the next bench triclinium there is a small pillar. (remains)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 2990 bench triclinium masonry to the northwest; 2989, to the north bench triclinium masonry; 2987 bench triclinium masonry to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: On the arcaded row of shops along via di Sepulcri shop 15 contains a masonry counter with built in dolia which identifies it as used for the purchase of foodstuffs. The salesroom is rectangular in shape on a north east / south west axis. The floor is currently grass. A stone threshold with inserts for wooden doors is extant, which would have closed the shop off from the arcade, but the bracket no longer exists. The walls are of opus incertum. No trace of decoration remains. In the south west corner of the room a masonry pile suggests a stairway to an upper level. The L - shaped counter (feature 4888) is attached at the north west corner of the room.

There is a long couch niche along the northwest wall of the room extending from the northeast corner of the room. Two couch podia are inserted into the niche. Traces of undecorated plaster survive on the face of the larger - westernmost- podium, and along the junction of the podium to the wall behind. Traces of plaster also survive on the vertical end faces. The smaller - easternmost- podium has traces of undecorated plaster on the face and vertical end faces. Undecorated plaster survives on both the east and west ends of the niche.

Along the north wall to the east of room (5) is a series of eleven planting rows on a north/south axis and abutting the north wall. The rows extend into the garden to the south and end on line with the south end of room (5).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hearth (2972) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The preparation platform abuts the Northwest Wall and the low wall to the southwest that divides it from triclinium 2994. The platforms rectangular in shape on a southwest/northwest axis. There is evidence for a stucco covering but none for painting. However, the low wall to which it abuts on the southwest shows evidence of stucco and red paints. The platform sits on a floor raised above the level of the floor raised above the level of the floor of the room. The floor on which the platform sits was covered by covered by beaten cement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium ( 2994) to the southwest lararium to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Abut in the southeast wall to the northeast of the imus of the triclinium ( 2993) is a rectangularly shaped preparation platform on a southwest/northeast axis. The surface mean the southeast walls seems to be higher than the rest of the surface but this maybe a result of the preservation. The platform was stuccoed but there is no sign of painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium (2998) to the southwest prep platform (3000)to this North west.

DESCRIPTION: Located in the south part of house, one enters from the small atrium (2). The room is rectangular in shape on a SW/NE axis. Identification as a dining room rest primarily on its size and orientation to the atrium (2). If it were decorated in antiquity, nothing remains today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 2 - atrium to the northeast. 2 - atrium to the northeast. None

DESCRIPTION: This is an L-shaped counter with one dolium in the northeast/southeast arm of it and two dolia in the northeast/southwest arm. There does not seem to be a hearth as reconstructed. As reconstructed, there is a marble top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Found along the northern 1/3 of the kitchen, separated from the remainder of the kitchen by a small partition wall, is a small square latrine. Joists for the floor above the latrine are found in the east and west walls. Against the east wall there is a U-shaped bench supporting a no longer extant seat. The bench is built out of masonry and bricks, below the seat is a drain now filled in with earth. The floor is plastered and slopes down toward the drain in the east. Undecorated plaster is found in the north and west walls. The ceiling is high above and restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking Platform (2289) to the south. None Cooking Platform (2289) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Located in northwest corner of the house with peristyle 20 is a large oecus (45). On the north side of the oecus is triclinium 57. One enters the triclinium through a wide doorway on the north side of the room. The room is rectangular in shape on a north-south axis. The room in antiquity was elaborately painted but little remains to judge what was there. The room opens onto oecus (45) on the north wall opposite. Easily seen from the triclinium is a painting of the Judgment of Paris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 45 oecus to north 45 oecus to north None

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular built in cupboard niche. Evidence of painting on the back wall. Traces of red and black paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None paristyle (room 20) to the south. None

DESCRIPTION: Opening onto the north porticus of peristyle 20 is a small entrance into the storeroom. I n the northwest corner of the room is a built-in cupboard (1844). Evidence of painting on north, east and south walls. Red framed square painting, rectangular in shape.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 20 peristyle to south 20 peristyle to south 1844 in northwest corner

DESCRIPTION: In the northeast corner of storeroom (16) is a water basin. It has a semi circular construction about waist high faced on the interior with what appears to be water proof opus signinum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: The water basing is coated in the center of the southeastern wall of the possible food and drink shop. It is raised masonry, circular, with a masonry rectangular base partly evident on the eastern side. It is about 18 inches high with about a 9 inch rim. The southeastern wall behind has stucco painted red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium(2821) to the northeast; Lararium (2822) to the southwest. None Lararium(2821) to the northeast; Lararium (2822) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: This is a large altar made of tufa with a pounded stucco surface. The walls, three that surround the altar, show evidence of red and yellow paint, It was here that ritual items were found. Museum sheet pending.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION:
It has been determined that this space in the House of Trebius Valens is an L-shaped ambulatory. This space encloses the northeast and southeast sides of the dining peristyle garden (12). The spaces created are wide to accommodate strolling and/or dining. The northeaster ambulatory has three columns with a third imbedded in the south corner of dining room (11). A low wall is preserved between the columns, which is broken away just before Room 11. Four columns run across the southeast side with an entrance to the dining garden peristyle (12). At the center is a low wall between the others. No flooring is visible. The walls are opus incertum and highly restored. At the eastern end of the southeast wall is a small arched doorway and two small round windows to the baths (6 & 7). West of this is the andron (9). Towards the southern corner is is the wide entrance to dining room (18). The central part of this southeast wall is a wide, open window of the tablinum. The western corner of the southwest side opens with two steps remaining through an external doorway. At the west end of the northwest wall is a small doorway to a small room (17). Adjacent to this is a narrow passage (16) on the southwest side of the dining garden peristyle (12). Remains of plaster can be seen on all walls and columns.

BIBLIOGRAPHY

ESCHEBACH 102, 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space lies to the northeast and southeast of the dining garden peristyle (12) and to the northwest of dining room (18), tablinum (19), and baths (6 & &).

DESCRIPTION: Dining Room 31 is oriented northeast to southwest. The large rectangular room is entered from the southwest porticus of peristyle 22 through a large entrance, which is framed on either side by Doric columns which abut the masonry walls on each side. These columns are mostly painted with red colors and the lentil of the entrance door, which is almost 4 meters high. The floor is paved with a coarse earthen material. The southeast wall shows traces of painting. On the opposite side, the northwest wall, shows a rectangular recess close to the entrance. The whole room has been completely reconstructed in modern times. The entrance is fenced and inside scaffolding is being used to support the walls and ceiling. On the three walls two pairs of square openings aligned centrally. Because of their position (not very high from floor), it is not possible to ascertain their function.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Porticus of peristyle 22 to northeast, rooms 10 and 11 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The preparation platform is an irregular shape located in the middle of the room behind the counter. It consists of two heights indicative of seats or storage. Platform has been heavily restored with a marble fragment surface and traces of plaster remaining. The north face of the masonry platform is the side with the lowered surface at the northeast end of the north segment. Traces of the wall plaster are present here. The east face of the platform consists of two heights because of the shelf/possible seat, and the south face segment is significantly shorter than the total length of the north face. The west face of the platform has been fashioned with a right angle inserted (see drawings and photograph.).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The preparation platform is located northeast of the counter and in the middle of room 2

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: This lararium is on the southwestern wall high up. It is rectangular in shape and has a ledge and no evidence of plaster. Very high up on the wall, above the lararium, are four plastered arched niches.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water Feature (2820) to the southeast; Lararium (2821) to the northeast) None Watern Feature (2820) to the southeast; Lararium (2821) to the northeast)

DESCRIPTION: Along the northeast wall of the impluvium (18) is a dining tabularium with a very large entrance. A large modern cardboard rectangle, either a cover for the impluvium or a covering for a floor mosaic in the center of the floor in the next room (18). In the northeast wall is a large rectangular window with a small window above it to the orchard beyond. The floor features white tessera with black borders. There is some evidence of painting - the lower register black with yellow and red above - but little remains. The ceiling is modern reconstruction. The southeast wall is mostly missing in the center.

Embedded directly to the northeast of the doorway between rooms 4 and 5 we find a large dolium. The dolium extends above the ground. It has a slightly flaring body leading to a carinated shoulder turned inward, above which an outurned horizontal room.The rim is partially broken.

Th dolium shows that it had been repaired in ancient times, both on the shoulder and on the lip.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Centrally located on the southeast wall between 5026 and 5032. To the southeast of dolia 5027, 5028, 5029, 5031.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular cooking platform rests against the N end of the structure aligned with the NE entry to the room. The opposite short side is in line (on axis) with the semi-column framing the protruding northern section of the NW wall. The preserved cooking platform appears badly damaged. The top is covered today with rubble; it slopes down toward the interior of the kitchen. The SW and SE borders of the platform show fragments of plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the SE Kitchen 19

DESCRIPTION: On the N wall as we stand in an area adjacent to the summous of the masonry bench triclinium we see a small raised podium on the floor and we see an aedicular lararium niche. Beige white plaster is still apparent on the back on half sides and the floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Feature 3000 preparation platform to SW
Triclinium 2994 to SW
Triclinium 2993 to S

DESCRIPTION: This space is identified as a fish shop, midway along the arcade on the north side of via di Sepulcri. This is a small enclosed space on a north west / south east axis and is comprised of what appear to be three fish tanks. Tank 1 (4892) is outside the south west opening of the shop in the arcade space. Tank 2 (4893) fills the north western two thirds of the shop space. Tank 3 is along the south east wall and may not be an actual tank.The shop space is very small. The north west corner is fronted with two courses of brick separated by two courses of cut stone. The rest of the walls are opus incertum, and preserve remains of a plaster coating. The floor space along the south east wall has a large block positioned in the middle abutting tank 2. The north east corner does not appear to have been excavated. No floor is visible, no ceiling remains. To the south west of the large block, the floor is not visible but appears quite deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Tank 2 is to the north east of tank 1 and to the south east of shop 21.

DESCRIPTION: According to Eschebach, an ara compitalis lay to the right of entrance 2.4.1. Nothing remains today, except perhaps the rock foundation.
A water basin is attached to the northeast corner of the cooking platform. All that is apparent is the bottom part of the dolium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2928) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room with east-west axis opening east to peristyle (66). Doorway at east end of north to (63). Black and white mosaic floor covered over. Traces of plaster survive on south wall. 4th style paintings with Endymion and Selene on west wall, Adonis and Aphrodite on south wall, no longer extant. That of the north wall, showing Io, Argos, and Mercury (4th style) is preserved in the Naples museum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
63 bedroom to north
66 peristyle to east 63 bedroom to north
66 peristyle to east None

DESCRIPTION: One enters the shop from the street on the south side. Immediately to the west is a counter with three sides. The north side is flush against the north wall and contains three dolia, possibly four. Just to the east of the entrance there's a large stone which Riddell (sp?) indicates was a stove. To the east is a doorway leading to a small room under which Fontana's tunnel can be seen. Directly across the street from the shop is the temple of Aesculapius.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None Small room to the east.

DESCRIPTION: In the south corner of the house is a rectangular shaped triclinium. The identification is based primarily on a comment by Fiorelli description that when excavated there was a triclinium present (no longer extant). Fiorelli also mentions the present (no longer present) of a puteal implying a cistern. The triclinium appears to overlook the garden (room 9) to the east.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None Garden (room 9) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room with two openings onto the Vicolo del Menandro, on the northwest wall. The west entrance has stairs going up, second entrance to the shop. The lararium niche no longer extant. Newly reconstructed counter on the northwest wall with dolium with step shelf which does not match the original archeology report. Entrance to the house in the southwest corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None Room number two to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: (Counter) beautifully reconstructed counter with a marble top and a dolium in the southwest arm with a step shelf in the north corner along the street. Reconstruction does not match the archeological report. Hearth is missing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Located on the northeast side of the house, dining room entered by narrow doorway onto portico of the garden. The room is roughly square and was elaborately decorated with painted walls and stucco reliefs, some of which are extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Room 9 Portico of the garden to the west
Room 6 Storeroom to the south Room 9 Portico of the garden to the west
Room 6 Storeroom to the south None

DESCRIPTION: Room 13 is entered from Room 11 to the northeast. A square pillar to the southwest seems to divide the cooking area from the adjoining Room 14 (courtyard). Opposite the pillar, to the northeast, is a very large square window looking out onto Space 11. The area contains a cooking platform to the southeast which extends along the whole length of the wall. The walls appear to have been reconstructed. The pillar suggests the presence of some kind of roofing which doesn't exist any longer. Because of its location, the kitchen was easily accessible from a number of rooms (Room 10, 11, 14). Through Room 14, the kitchen could have been entered by a door from the street (2.1.11) There is evidence of stucco and painting on the southern corner of the southeastern wall over the end of the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 to the north; Room 11 to the northeast; Room 14 to the southwest. Room 10 to the north; Room 11 to the northeast; Room 14 to the southwest. None

DESCRIPTION: The serving room is rectangular in shape and on an roughly east/west axis across the full width of the north part of the house and extends into the street. The serving room, as is the rest of the house, is a lower level than the outside street. One enters room ten from the north by way of a step on axis with entrance four. In the west end is an L-shaped bench (2785), the long arm abuts the west wall while the short arm abuts the south wall and extends slightly beyond the entrance to counter room (2793) to the east. At the east end of the room abutting the south and east wall is a rectangular bench (2786) on an east/west axis. The interior walls of the room including benches and step were once covered with stucco and were probably painted ( traces remain). There is no indication that the northeast and west walls extended beyond a few inches of the level of the street. Floor is indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room nine (2783) to the south, room one to the south. Counterroom nine (2783) to the south, room one to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining room from the northwest door from the counter room (2805) selling food and drink. There is one threshold 2 1/2 inches up from the shop floor and another raised threshold matches the floor of the dining room. The floor is concrete and terracotta fragments. In the north corner we see two steps that would have to curve to the northeast wall. There is a wide doorway to the garden (2808) on the southeast wall next to it. To the south is a window and there is little remaining of the southeast wall. The southwest wall is intact with a quarter showing plaster. The northwest wall in the corner shows the small portion of red and cream plaster. The northwest wall to the counter room is about half missing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room (2810) to the northwest; Garden (2808) to the southeast Counter room (2810) to the northwest; Garden (2808) to the southeast None

DESCRIPTION:
This is a negative feature.

On the northwest wall we have identified a niche as a latrine based on its location in the kitchen (5) between an unidentified block of masonry that is protruding from the center to the northwest wall and what appears to be a low wall of a storage area. There is no evidence of original wall or floor surfaces.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the room through a doorway in the south corner. A low wall abutting against the southeast wall running southeast to northwest separates the front part of the room from the cooking platform. One approaches the cooking platform through a break in the low wall at the southwest end. As extant the walls show little sign of plaster, primarily at the base of the northeast wall. No evidence of decoration remains. The floor and the height of the walls are indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (14) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Processing room 18 is entered from corridor 20 to the east. The rectangular space is occupied by a vat at the back opposite the entrance. The room is oriented southwest/northeast.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor 20 to the west. Processing room 16 to the south and room 19 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform rests against the southwestern wall of kitchen 54. The preserved structure is approximately 40-50 centimeters high and shows an irregular shape. In fact, while the southeast and southwest edges run parallel to the adjoining walls, the northeastern edge is slightly diagonal in relation to the corridor 28 leading into latrine 10 to the northwest. The front edge to the northeast curves to form a convex shape. The top of the cooking platform is covered with irregularly shaped terracotta tiles for almost the entire length of the structure.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southwest of kitchen 54 and to the northwest of corridor 28.

DESCRIPTION: The middle mill is located between the most easterly and most westerly wall surrounded by volcanic stone paving. The base of the mill is circular and has been restored. The meta of the mill is located on top of the mill base but the catillus is missing. The meta is constructed from volcanic stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill 6086 is located east of mill 6085 north of meta 6088 and west of mill 6087.

DESCRIPTION: The L shaped counter sits in the northeast part of the room. The short arm, without embedded amphora, sits just inside the threshold and lies on a southwest/northeast axis. The short arm ends just before the northeast end of the opening to the shop thereby leaving about a two foot opening between the northeast end of the short arm and the northeast wall of the room. The long arm joins the short arm at a right angle and runs on a northwest/southeast axis into the interior of the room about 80% of the depth of the room, At the southeast end of the long arm is a hearth which open to the northeast. as reconstructed the surface of the L-shaped counter is made of cement and fragments of white, gray and red marbles. The L-shaped counter shows no evidence plaster or decoration. The service area is on a higher level than the floor of the room and runs in a semicircular direction from the east corner of the hearth to the northeast wall about a foot from the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: A large dining room with three entries. The dining room looks north on to the peristyle with fountain and piscina. On the north wall is the longest entry. Red and yellow plaster survives at the northwest corner and at the north east corner. All of the walls in this room survive only to the first story. The lintel is not original on the north wall. On the east wall in the north east corner is a service entry. At the south east corner on the east wall is a second service entry; the lintel has been restored. In the south east corner and along the east wall the plaster survives but the color is indiscernible. The south wall survives to a low height with the remains of plaster (which is red and yellow) in the south west corner. The west wall survives also only to a low height but is covered in plaster with red and yellow dado still surviving on the lower register. The floor is covered with mesh - possible mosaic beneath.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 37 is contiguous to the peristyle to the north (room 39); a small unnumbered space to the west ( also discernible on to the peristyle); room 38 to the south and rooms 27 and 36 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: An L - shaped masonry counter sits in sales room 1, attached to the north west threshold. It contains buit-in openings for three dolia in total, one located on the north west short end of the L facing the arcade and two centrally located on the long arm of the L. Today one terracotta dolium remains in the western most position on the long arm of the L.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south west of room 2.

DESCRIPTION: Negative Feature: 30 wine amphorae; with the inscription "QTR" The location of the amphorae is not specified.

On a southwest area in the room we see a masonry triclinium. The triclinium has a left side, a top middle and a right side. There is a two-piece table/mensa in the rectangular open space. The dining slope is very apparent but there is no painting remaining on the benches, but there is evidence of plaster on the right bench. The top couch is narrow, perhaps too narrow for reclining. Looking at the wall (behind the garden triclinium) on the west of the triclinium there remains a patch of yellow plaster next to a large cupboard recessed niche.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The large cupboard niche (2774) to the northwest; A lararium (2775) to the southwest; Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east. The large cupboard niche (2774) to the northwest; A lararium (2775) to the southwest; Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: On the southeast wall is a large curved cupboard niche. On the back wall there is evident yellow paint stucco inside. This could have contained cooking/eating/drinking utensils.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium ( 2773) to the southeast; Lararium ( 2775) on the same wall to the southeast. Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east. Triclinium ( 2773) to the southeast; Lararium ( 2775) on the same wall to the southeast. Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: On the north corner of the northwest wall is a painting. To the left is a green parrot. To the right, sitting on a box are four apples. One has been cut and three seem to have twigs and leaves attached. The painting is framed by a thin red line, all set within the rectangular panel defined on top and bottom by a continuous red line. It is framed on the left by two vertical green lines and on the right by a vertical red line in the north corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Painting (2839) to the southwest. None Painting (2839) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Negative feature sheet. Identified as a dining room based on the location, size, and wall paintings. Back of the room is filled, walled, and terraced.

In the north corner of the northeast wall there is a built-in niche which was used for inserting the couch. This feature was covered by a layer of plaster which is preserved only on the upper part. Along the lower part is a stone structure (like a low platform) which is interrupted by the adjoining northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 8 is entered from the east corner of the southeast wall corridor three which connects open spaces two and six on either side of the room. The rectangular room lies along the northeastern/southwestern axis. The southwestern side of the dining room was pierced by a large window looking out onto the peristyle which is ornamented with a pool. The corners of this pool are occupied by columns which are not in situ any longer. The room is covered by a modern wooden roof sloping down towards the peristyle. The floor was decorated with opus signinum (orthogonal grid pattern of white squared tesserae).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (three) to the southeast; peristyle (six) to the south west; kitchen-latrine to the north. Corridor (three) to the southeast; peristyle (six) to the south west; kitchen-latrine to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The triclinium is located behind and to the northeast of the atrium. The room is roughly square and has two entrances.: one from the southwest, the second larger one from the southeast. The latter overlooks the large fountain. The floor appears to originally have been of a smooth beaten cement. A lower ceiling has been reconstructed such that it covers the northeast side of the room. In antiquity and as reconstructed today, the entire room had a ceiling a little higher than the lower one. In the center of the anterior faÂade of the lower ceiling, in stucco, was a small arch. In the north corner, the lower two thirds of the northwest wall has been so constructed as to connect directly with the northeast wall thereby covering the north corner. The walls were stuccoed and elaborately painted. On all four walls the lower zone is painted to represent a series of large panels of colored marble. The upper zone is difficult to describe as very little remains. Above the lower zone on all four walls is a light green band decorated with figures of soldiers and a cart; Achilles and the Trojan war including Achilles dragging the body of Hector. Above this band is a much larger band showing large human figures depicting Hercules and his expedition against Laomedon.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room eight to the southwest, room 16 to the southeast (2813) Room eight to the southwest, room 16 to the southeast (2813)

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular garden has a northeast/southwest axis contiguous with dining garden (4) to the southwest and kitchen (7) to the southeast. In the southwest corner water feature (2980) extends into the garden a square basin and drain from the floor above. Undecorated plaster is present in south corner of the room. In the east corner there is a square plastered water basin into which a terra cotta pipe drains through the wall to the east The exterior face of the basin is plastered with yellow paint. In the west corner there are traces of plaster decoration on two registers. Altar and lararium niche (2982) in the west corner. East floor Jashemski does not refer to any aspect of the garden.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms (4) and (7) are to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a rectangular room with NW/SE access. It is inn the southeast corner doorway to Room 4. There is no threshold. There is a window at the west end of the south wall with modern lintel looking toward Atrium 2 to the south. Extensive wall painting on the southeast, southwest and northwest walls has survived. This is second style painting with red panels and green borders. The floor is obscured by lapilli.
