CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 to the Southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is against the southeast wall of the kitchen and runs northeast/southwest. The surface of the platform on its northeast as extant was made up of a single roof tile. The southwest surface is not extant, but may have been another roof tile. Beneath the northeast roof tile is a storage area. The cooking platform, including the storage area, rests upon the foundation that rises about a foot above floor level.

One approaches the triclinium from the southwest by way of corridor 6. The entrance to the room itself is from the north corner from corridor 6. The dining room is rectangular in shape, on the southwest/northeast axis. The floor is a beaten concrete fragments of white and blue marble randomly dispersed. The room was stuccoed and painted as extant along the bottom of the southeast wall. it appears to show some sort of vegetation. in the center of the southeast wall is a large window looking onto garden number 13. the heights of the walls are indeterminate. If there was a window in the northeast wall, it's no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 13 to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the room from the northeast. The room is square in shape with a door on the east corner of the southeast wall and the south corner of the window on a vertical axis. In the center of the southwest wall is a large semicircular niche; on the southeast and northwest walls are rectangular niches. On the southwest wall between the semicircular niche and the west corner appears to be a rectangular light well that penetrates the wall at an oblique angle. the opening into the room is much larger than the hole that penetrates the room (14?). All four walls are covered with fourth style wall painting. The floor is in opus signinum and fragments of brick. As reconstructed, the ceiling is quite high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: contiguous with room (6) to the southeast, room (14) to the southwest, and room (2) to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: The east wall contains a beehive oven on a picium. When looking at the cooking oven, one first sees a raised platform to the north next to the beehive oven. This provides space for preparation. This podium extends beneath the beehive oven but does not extend all the way to the wall. The oven has a post and basalt surface. At the top of the beehive there is a mantle type platform around and above the beehive. there is a large recessed arch above the platform over the beehive oven.

We have identified this feature (4616) to be a lararium. It has an arched, shallow, high plastered recess with poorly preserved base. No visible decoration survives in the plaster.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 102, 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Basin (4617) to the north, platform 4615 to the northwest, and latrine (4614) to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This feature is identified as a couch niche. It is a well-preserved rectangular niche toward the eastern corner of the northeast wall. It is plastered and painted as a continuation of the lower band of the walls.
ESCHEBACH PAGES 102 AND 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This niche is east of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION:
This replaces sheet #32.
The dining room is on a northwest/southeast axis and is entered off the small garden from the west. A second door is located on the north wall in the northwest corner. The north wall has suffered a collapse over the doorway in the northwest corner. Plaster with white and red paint can be seen in the northwest corner. The rest of the north wall is covered in plaster but the colors are not visible. The east wall is entirely covered in plaster although the southeast corner has lost some of this. There are two holes located on the east wall, one at the northeast end and the other at the southeast end. These are located approximately 2 meters up the wall. The south wall is covered in plaster but no colors are discernible and there is a beam hole located in the southwest corner approximately 1.7 meters up the wall. The floor has the remains of black and white mosaic tesserae although it is mostly destroyed. The west wall contains the large opening onto the garden in the middle of the wall. A marble threshold is present inn this entrance with door pivots at both the south and north ends.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 15 is contiguous to the peristyle (8) to the west and Room 16 to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This sheet replaces sheet #31
The latrine is located within the kitchen(13), recessed into a niche in the northeast corner of the space. Above the latrine is a rectangular window beneath which the latrine was located on the east wall in the northeast corner and is on an east/west axis. Little survives of the latrine. No seat niches or marks in the wall plaster can be discerned. No plaster survives in this area at all.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (6061) to the south. Room 12 to the west. Room 16 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: At the north west end of kitchen 10 is a ruined masonry cooking platform with arched recess storage. The top no longer reflects a tiled surface. The platform is in a ruined state. It abuts the south west wall of the room immediately adjacent to latrine room 11.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: north west of platform 5119

DESCRIPTION: The horizontal beam press is no longer extant, but the holes for its parts remain. A square hole for the pier is located at the back and is used to anchor the south end of the beam. In front on the north side of the low wall that runs east to west are two holes to support the beams that anchor the north end of the beam. To the north of and located between those holes is a larger hole, square in shape, into which a weight could fit to help add pressure to the beam as it squeezes the grapes placed in a basket beneath the beam to the rear.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Treading vat? to the east

DESCRIPTION: Square sales room, opening N/NW to the street. Undecorated plaster on S/SE wall, with blocked door way from earlier phase. Rectangular recess adjoining the counter at N end of E wall. Doorway in the center of E wall to room 41 blocked in the modern period. Floor is obscured. A stove is recorded in SW corner, but is no longer present (Ruddell.) In the S end of E wall are holes for floor joists. Counter (2913) is in the center of the room facing the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 41 to the E.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen lies in the southwest part of the house. One enters the kitchen through a door in the northeast corner from the east. The floor is at a level lower than room 2. To the southeast is a latrine and abutting the latrine to the southwest is a cooking platform. The walls are stuccoed and somewhat elaborately decorated. The layout of the kitchen is indeterminate. The floor seems to be of a beaten cement. High on the southwest wall above the cooking platform there are two openings that may have been windows in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 to the northeast. Room 2 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed.

The cooking platform with the square addition on the north side covers two thirds of the room. There are no tile surfaces, no shelves, and no signs of a window. The surface is like that of the floor. Under the platform there are two half moon storage recesses.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to latrine

DESCRIPTION: The large arched cupboard plastered with red & yellow with amphora in situ. Lower level stenciling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Shelf Niche (2702) to the southeast; Amphora (2704) to the northwest; Cupboard niche (2703) to the southeast; Amphora (2705) to south. Shelf Niche (2702) to the southeast;Amphora (2704) to the northwest; Cupboard niche (2703) to the southeast; Amphora (2705) to south.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the rectangular kitchen from a southwestern door. The floor is cement and broken tesserae, and the floor to the northern side of the cooking platform becomes soil. There is evidence of plaster on the southeastern wall, which is painted white with signs of red. The kitchen is open in the southwest to the hallway (2) where it opens with a huge window to the street. The cooking platform is unusual in that it has two components: the southwestern wall component is lower and has a tiled top; the northeastern component is higher and wider with a tiled top. Over the soil portion, next to the platform on the northeast wall is a small, indented, oblong niche which was probably for a lamp. There is no ceiling or window over the platform; the street window in the hall would have provided ventilation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Storage Room (2801) to the northwest; Dining Room (2802) to the northeast, Hall (2) to the southwest Storage Room (2801) to the northwest; Dining Room (2802) to the northeast, Hall (2) to the southwest None

DESCRIPTION: High on the southwestern wall, in the southern corner, is a small lararium. On page 85, Eschebach reports that the lararium was dedicated to Venus, and contained a gold pseudo-alabaster statue of Venus.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None L-shaped counter (2798) to the north None

DESCRIPTION: Water feature other (6084) is circular in shape with flat walls on the body and a handle located on south side of the vessel which probably replicated on the opposite side but has broken off. The interior of the water feature appears to be bowl shaped but is obscured by lapilli. The water feature is constructed of volcanic stone and is likely to be located in its original position in the north corner of the room in front of the oven.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The water feature is located northwest of the oven 6083, in the northeast corner of room one (1), and is east of the mill 6085.

DESCRIPTION: The mill 6087 is located in the northeast corner of the room, northeast of the threshold and west of mill 6086. The mill is surrounded by volcanic paving stones and is circular in shape and has been restored. The meta is located on top of the mill base but no catillus survives. The meta is constructed of volcanic stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill 6087 is contiguous to mill 6086 to the east and entry to the property to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: This is a sanctuary with a large dining room. We enter the room from the southwest behind the altar and altar space. We see a threshold of one half foot with evidence of a door. There is marble and terracotta emblema on the floor. The northeast wall has a storage platform. This platform could be used as a dining bench or as an altar. Two pitchers were found on the platform as well as a sacrificing tool, the hand of Sabatius. The northeast wall, southeast entrance and northwest entrance show plastered walls in red and yellow. The northwestern side of the dining room extends into an open rectangular room which shows red and yellow 3rd style painting with red and white stencil work. The southeast wall has a door opening to a room and an other southwest door opening to the sacred alter space.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Sacred Space (2841) to the southwest; Room 6 to the northwest; Room 7 to the southeast. Sacred Space (2841) to the southwest; Room 6 to the northwest; Room 7 to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain is on the east side of the Vicolo dei Vettii in front of 6.16.28. It is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. There is a round lining at the wall/floor junction. The pilaster is centered atop the northeastern slab and is decorated with a male head in relief (river god?). Eschebach suggests Oceanus or a lion-Griffin (1983:p.13). The overflow is toward the interior southwest corner at the top of the southeastern slab. The drainage hole is below the overflow at street level. The fountain has modern plumbing. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.92 meters by 0.75 meters east-west and it is 0.675 meters deep. There are worn hand recesses on either side of the pilaster and near the interior northern and eastern corners of the basin.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
Eschebach, De Ã–ffentlichen Lauf Brunnen Pompejis: Pompeii, Herculaneum, Stabiae. Amici di Pompeii (1983:p.13)â€ƒ
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This public fountain is located on the east side of the Vicolo dei Vettii in front of 6.16.28.

DESCRIPTION: In the back room of a structure that we have identified as a workshop production facility we found a small frescoed room off the kitchen. The room is almost square and is entered by a doorway in the north corner. It appears on the northeastern wall that there was immediately adjacent to the entry door another doorway that was filled in some time in the past. Wall construction is opus incertum. A rectangular niche, with plastered fresco is high on the southwest wall. No floor or ceiling remains. Based upon the curvature of plaster in the lower south corner it is feasible that this rooms was used as a latrine. As that is the evidence we call it a store room based upon its proximity to the kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To southeast of Kitchen, room 4 and the southwest of Tablinuem 9.

DESCRIPTION:
This sheet replaces previous Sheet 1135.
Garden 21 is an L-shaped open area with orientation NE/SW. The corner between the NW and SW walls is occupied by a masonry triclinium. The floor is today covered by overgrown vegetation. Along the NW side a colonnade porticus is supported by four columns and a pillar. The columns frame a low wall which delineates a water channel running along the entire L-shaped section; however, it is interrupted in the corner which joins the two sides. In the corner between the NE and SE wall there are two platforms of different heights, the function of which is not certain. The NE wall shows traces of plaster on its entire length. Against this wall and very close to the masonry triclinium rests a square pilaster which is about 40 cm high. The NW wall above the masonry triclinium is entirely preserved; it is decorated with red plaster and at approximately 2.5 meters high two small rectangular openings appear on either side of a rectangular window looking out on the adjoining property. This section of the wall continues running to the SW but it is not well preserved. It shows traces of plaster. The area delineated b y this wall contains two wells which are today covered/protected by a fence. At the end of this area next to the triclinium is a small structure which appears that could have been used as a support. The garden area delineated by the colonnade porticus is today ornamented with planters and a vine-covered pergola.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Porticus 18 and kitchen 19 to SW, posticum of 30 to SE

DESCRIPTION: A masonry rectangular platform with curved north end against the west wall of the room. It is partly preserved with a modern cement surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
The cistern (6212) is directly to the south and south of the cistern is the kneading
basin (6211).

DESCRIPTION: Entering from northeast door of the atrium, there is a marble threshold. The room is rectangular with an east-west axis. The floor is in good shape with black and white tessera. What is unique about the floor, it is raised on the north and east sides covering about a third of the room. The first step on the rise is marble. Northwest is a huge window overlooking the peristyle with a small window above to the east. Another large window with a smaller above looking at the orchard. All four walls retain half of their decorations, bottom dado red with green plants. The walls are divided into sections with red paint, architectural elements and beautiful blue paint. Upper part has dragons, porpoises (leaping), griffon. There have been many pictures removed. The ceiling is a modern reconstruction.

This public fountain is on the east side of the Via del Vesuvio, southeast of the Castellum Aquae. Access is restricted due to current excavations across the street in Region V. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The pilaster is in the center top of the southwestern slab and is decorated with a "pilgrim's flask". Pilgrims flask is the name by which Italians call the image. Image of the decoration is a flask with crossed leather (?) straps. The overflow is in the center top off the southeastern slab, presumably with the drain at ground level below. Basin dimensions unknown at this time. The fountain has modern plumbing.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
This public fountain is located on the west side of the Via del
Vesuvio and southeast of the Castellum Aquae. It is in front of 6.16.19.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. This is a rectangular wall painting located on the northwest wall near the north corner of the entryway (fauces) of the House of the Vettii. The painting depicts a Priapus dressed in Phrygian clothing: drape, hat and boots. His left shoulder is leaning upon a pedestal with a thyrsus propped up against the wall. We observe him leaning on his left arm, weighing his huge phallus on a scale, the opposite side of the scale holds a large bag of money (?). His expression is nonchalant and suggests that he knows his phallus is larger than the opposing bag of (weights/gold/?) Immediately below the weight scales is a woven basket containing fruits; pomegranates, grapes, pears and other fruits. The perspective creates a three dimensional view. BIBLIOGRAPHY: JASHEMSKI II pp 153-155, Eschebach pp218-219.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Wall paintings 4666 and 4667.

DESCRIPTION: Broken catillus, no visible Meta. Two broken halves of a hand mill were found in Rooms 8 & 10.
Near the imus of triclinium is a smashed dolium half.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium, masonry (2890) to Northwest.

DESCRIPTION: On South side of triclinium we can no longer see a shallow basin which collected rainwater from the couch of triclinium.

This house is not completed.

This is a fair-sized latrine with a receptacle for an oil lamp on the north wall. Practically everything in this small, rectangular latrine has been redone in opus incertum, plaster and brick. On the north wall is a long open recess over a low-level stone platform. On the east wall there are lines of stone demarcations. There is a large ceramic slab propped against a wall.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to shop store and cooking platform

DESCRIPTION: This is a pond whose shape includes one straight wall and one elliptical wall. The overall shape echoes the shape of an arched niche. There is a fountain in the center whose function probably provides a cooling spray of water.
The counter is in the northwest part of the room. It is rectangular in shape and lies roughly on a northeast/southwest axis. As extant today, only the foundation remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Room 6 is entered from the western corner of the northwestern wall. The step by the entrance adjoins a large square stone slab, under which there runs an L-shaped water channel. The long side of the water channel runs along the entire length of the northwest wall, while the shorter section runs on the corner of the southwestern wall and is provided with a drain hole opening off the street. To the north of the entrance on the northwestern wall is a large window that looks out onto Room 5, (dining room). Below the window, the entire wall is covered with plaster and some traces of white painting. More traces of painting appear on the southern corner of the southeastern wall: A red band which could have framed a panel. Fragments of plaster are visible on the southeastern and northeastern walls. On the southwestern wall, next to the water channel, there is a cistern which is now covered by two stone blocks. The southern corner of the room is delimited by an L-shaped low wall. This was probably a covered room, as a row of 16 joist holes are on the southwest wall. They may have supported the ceiling of this room. Eschebach describes this space as a storeroom, (repositorium) though its location in a large area, the paintings, and the possible arrangement of a garden with the water channel, suggest that the walled space may have been used as a dining room with a nice vista onto the garden. High up in the southeastern wall, above the longer wall, delimiting the dining room is a glass window which appears to be modern. The ground is covered in vegetation. In the southern corner of the southeastern wall there is evidence of a door which was walled up and covered with painting. The southeastern wall is preserved at a two-story height, while the southwestern wall is preserved at a one-story height. In the southeastern wall there is a stone block supporting an upright stone block that juts out from the wall. It is difficult to ascertain the function of this.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 (dining room) to the north; Room 2 (corridor) to the northwest Room 5 (dining room) to the north; Room 2 (corridor) to the northwest None

DESCRIPTION: When facing the cooking platform on the South wall there is evidence of a quarter circle basin on the R back corner of the platform. It shows evidence of a cutout drain to provide water to the contiguous latrine. It is connected to the shelf on the back of the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the cooking platform 2928 to N and latrine 2943 to SW to the east. Basin 2929 to N

DESCRIPTION: In the N corner of NE wall is a rectangular niche on a vertical axis. Probably used to accommodate a wooden cupboard. As extent, there is no sign of plaster or decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: counter 2913 to the SW

DESCRIPTION: Small square room added in final phase into the large shop room 45. Floor is obscured and N and W walls survive to only half height. The E & S walls contains 2 square windows, both plastered and with modern lintels (Decoration or discoloration to plaster to window in E wall). Doorway to Room 45 in N end of NW wall without threshold. Plaster survives on all 4 walls, continuing the decorative scheme of room 45, with black lower register, and alternating red and yellow panels above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: NW to room 45

DESCRIPTION:
This is a large rectangular space that includes a rectangular fountain (4547). It also includes a defined rectangular room. There are ten columns (perhaps there are two more engaged columns against the back wall). This peristyle space has a pond with a straight wall and a circular wall, with a circular fountain in the centre for water spraying. There is one opening in the northwest side.
ESCHEBACH PAGES 102 AND 103

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that late usage is a food and drink shop (Small). It is a single, large room on a northeast/southwest axis. The neighbor to the west is the fauces of a large, old atrium house. To the east side is a corner shop. There is no sign of a door system at the large front opening, but there are 10 stones forming the threshold. This is a good size square room. The floor is greenery and lapilli. The walls are opus incertum, without a sign of paint. The front has the distinctive older style big blocks. Distinctive about this shop are two basins, one on either side of the front of the shop.

Bibliography: Eschebach p381

DESCRIPTION: One enters room 2 from the SW by way of room 1. The room was originally an atrium but at some point was converted into a dining room with two bench masonry triclinia. One triclinium lies on the SE side and the other on the NW. To the NE of the SE triclinium is a dining tablinum, room 12. To the SW of the NW triclinium is room 3. Room 3 seems to be a bedroom converted to contain a latrine in the W corner. To the NE of the NW triclinium is a small preparation platform separated from the triclinium by a small low wall. On the NE wall above the preparation platform is a lararium. Walls of the room were stuccoed and painted but little sign of the painting remains. The floor is indeterminate. To the NE on axis with the entrance to the room is the andron 4 leading to the back of the house.

DESCRIPTION:
The dining room is behind the peristyle. It has a roof with wooden beams, cemented stone, and roof tiles. This room is defined because of the roof plus two columns. Within the columns and under the roof are three triclinium plus a small circular table. We cannot access this room, the pictures will demonstrate why, but on either side we see structures connecting this room with the peristyle wall construction. The two outside columns are engaged at the back wall.
On the back wall of the room/house are painted a mixture of squares and rectangles painted in vibrant colors; dark red with beige, turquoise with cream, mustard with beige. In conjunction with the thicker black outline of each grouping this creates the illusion of embossed "stones" in a header/stretcher pattern from a distance. We see on a northwestern wall there are two niches for pre-prep areas or a lararium (one arched and one squared). There is a small bit of floor that contains the triclinium, which is covered in vegetation, stone, and soil.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 102, 103

One enters the counter room through entrance 6 to the northwest. The entrance is wide with approximately one half on the northeast being blocked by the counter. The entrance way has a stone threshold behind which the counter sits. The room is roughly square in shape with the counter taking up most of the northeast part. The service area behind the counter is on a higher level than the rest of the room. The floor of the counter room is at a lower level than Room 15 (2807) to the southeast. The height of the walls is indeterminate. The floor seems to have been made of stucco and fragments of terracotta and stone. As extant, there is no evidence for stucco on the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 15 (2807) to the southeast. Room 15 (2807) to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 24 is a very small square space delimited by continuous large rectangular and low blocks of stones along the northwestern and southeastern sides. On the eastern side runs a wall which is approximately 40 centimeters high in the direction southeast/northwest. On the southeastern side a wall, which is today preserved at height of two meters. In the southern corner, where the southwestern wall and the southeastern wall are interrupted is an irregularly shaped stone block which forms the paving floor of the adjoining corridor 49 and steps down into the central space of storeroom 24. Because of the badly preserved condition of the whole area, it is not possible to ascertain whether the room was entered from the southern corner as is possible today. The floor shows evidence of paving stones. The southwestern wall includes a group of terracotta tiles which runs along the whole height of the wall. This row of tiles seems to appear like part of a frame of a larger opening. In fact, a farther row of terracotta tiles runs perpendicular to the previous one at approximately two meters high. It is evident that a very large door opened onto the adjoining cubiculum 23, but it was blocked in at a later stage.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Storeroom 22 to the north. Cubiculum 23 to the northeast. Space 25 to the southeast and corridor 49 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Kitchen 54 is entered from corridor 28 to the northeast and corridor 7 to the southeast. It's a small rectangular space which is mostly occupied by the cooking platform to northwest. There is no evidence of a doorway both onto corridor 28 and corridor 7. It seems likely that what is numbered space 7 in the house plan are all referring to is part of the kitchen 54, which would have been entered from the eastern corner of corridor 49.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: "corridor" 7 to the southeast, "consider" 28 to the northeast, store room 8 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Preparation room 8 is a small rectangular room oriented northeast/southwest. It is entered from corridor 28 to the southeast. the floor is covered with lapilli and overgrown vegetation. The walls to the southeast, northwest and southwest are preserved for almost 2 meters. The northeastern wall shows a few traces of plaster. the southeastern side of the doorway is framed by about a 70 centimeters high wall. Because of its small size next to the kitchen, the room could have been used for food preparation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor 28 (with the adjoining kitchen 54) to the east/southeast. Preparation room 9 to the southwest and space 38 - triclinium 37 to the northeast. To the northwest is building 6-1-4.

DESCRIPTION: The couch triclinium masonry is one solid piece of masonry covered with concrete. It has a typical small round table in the middle. This piece shows that 9 people could easily dine. One solid slab trivlinium. This is in room 4565 which is a dining garden. The eastern leg of the triclinium is shorter than the western leg.

We enter this dining room from the northwest from the preparation room (2787) through a large and high doorway. It is a square room with a very large window in the southeast wall to the garden/water area. It is contiguous to a hallway (Room 4) that ends with a kitchen. The floor is covered with lapilli. Of the four walls of the dining room, the north wall shows third style decorations in Pompeiian red and ivory and the lowest zone is a peach color with Pompeiian red splatters throughout all areas of the lower zone. There is no ceiling. The west wall has minimal plaster and the south wall has a huge window. The window is surrounded by a peach and Pompeiian red frame. The east wall again shows the splatter on the lower zone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 (Preparation Room 2787) is to the northwest. The garden/water feature (room 6) is to the southeast. The hallway (Room 4) is to the northeast. Room 2 (Preparation Room 2787) is to the northwest. The garden/water feature (room 6) is to the southeast. The hallway (Room 4) is to the northeast. None

DESCRIPTION: 44 embedded amphorae were found along the eastern edge of the garden. Della Corte and Spinazzola mentioned as reference but no citation provided. Spinazzola states that the amphorae were used for storing wine. Della Corte, by contrast argues that they were used as water containers for the worship of Isis.

This house is not completed. This feature is identified as a dolium. It is reconstructed, presumably in situ. It is a rounded vessel,and no lip or rim remains. It is pink fabric with a buff slip.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dolium is to the northwest of the staircase and to the west of dolium (4519).

DESCRIPTION: This dining room is rectangular and has a marble threshold. There was a door on the south wall. Post and lintel door. Black and white tesserae on the floor. Large window on east wall. South wall has robber hole. Nicely decorated in the third or fourth style. There is an arched ceiling.

This masonry support for a cooking platform is on the northwest wall with space for plenty of storage between the two supports. This would have had a marble or wooden platform that does not exist. The northern (second) support abuts a short wall that would separate the support from the latrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine (2870) is to the northeast. None The latrine (2870) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The biclinium lies on the northeast end of room 16 (2813). The couches lie on the northwest and southeast sides of the euripus which extends back to the aedicular fountain. Each couch slopes back and down from the euripus. The left couch has on its southwest and southeast sides a lip. The right couch has a lip on its southwest and northwest sides. The euripus extends to the southwest to just in front of the zoothecula. The walls of the euripus were painted in blue. The aedicular fountain at the back is composed of two columns in front with Corinthian capitals supporting tympaneum. The back part is a large niche. At the bottom is a base perhaps for a statue. The niche is decorated to appear as a rocky faÂade with a design in dark blue arula and red tesserae at the top of which are sea creatures. On the back wall on either side of the fountain is a painting in red with flowers at the base. A large panel painting on the right to the southeast is of Thisbe and Pyramus. The panel painting on the left or to the northwest is of Narcissus. The Euripus which extends to the southwest is bordered in marble and was probably opened to the sky in antiquity. Columns on the northwest side impinge upon this marble border. Two small bridges cross the Euripes, one just in front of the biclinium, and the second in front of the doorway to the triclinium (2811) to the northwest.

The triclinium composed of three couches takes up most of the room in which it lies. It is on axis with the room and faces out almost full width through a room (2) and a garden (3), with the fish pool. The only portion of the triclinium not covered in marble are the top surface of the couches. The marble front facade of the northeast ends of the left and right couch rises slightly higher than the level of the couches creating a small lip. To the front and at a lower level of the three couches is a platform for food dishes. The rectangular space between the couches functions as part of the water display. The rectangular space extends to a depth below the level of the floor of the room and slopes southwest to the northeast. At the base of the southwest end of the central area is a semicircular hole for water flowing from the stairs above to enter. Water flows down the sloped floor of the central area where it exits through a semicircular hole at the northeast end flowing and then under the floor and out to the garden. As excavated, there appears to have been a narrow space between the triclinium couches and the wall on the northwest, southwest, and southeast sides.

Masonry biclinium in northwest corner of garden. The structure is poorly preserved. Arched storage recess below north couch, partially obscured by debris. Above the couch, in the west corner, is a square plastered lararium niche and to the southeast of the couches Mau has a pool.

At southern end of the base of the east and west walls there is a lead pipe that drains through wall to east and west. The basin preserves opus signinum lining in places, a marble top and plastered exterior. The triclinium stands below a pergola consisting of 4 columns placed in 4 corners of clinia. The columns are plastered and painted blue with red trim at base of capitals. Traces of the white plaster molding survives on capital of the northeast column. The two northernmost columns have brick-built plastered painted pilasters on northern face that perhaps served as bases for statuary. The exterior face of the clinia preserves traces of red paint on the plaster with no other visible decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Dining room (13L) opens to the south through a large opening onto the peristyle (18L). It is a square room. It is decorated with wall painting on the northeast and southwest walls. The northeast wall represents white panels framed by red bands. The central upper panel contains a high platform supporting containers for liquids. The reminder of the painting is too deteriorated to determine content.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle (18L) to the south Peristyle (18L) to the south None

DESCRIPTION: The niche is located in the East corner of the room. It is low, with a decorative, painted nothed area above. The guest of honor overlooks the serving room, street counter, programmate, & entrance to an unexcavated structure.

DESCRIPTION: Shallow, rectangular niche in the northeast corner of the room. The niche is painted in accordance with the decorative motifs of the rest of the room with burgundy lower register containing vegetation. White border with red panels above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mosaic (2018) to the south. None Mosaic (2018) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: In the center of the eastern half of the room there is a mosaic insert around which the clinia would have been placed. The mosaic consists of black, white and red borders around a central rosette depicting a boat with pygmies in a Nilotic landscape containing fish, crocodiles, a smaller boat, a larger animal (hippopotamus ?) with a shrine and palm trees. The pygmies in the smaller boat hold fishing rods and are fishing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Niche (2015) to the north. None Niche (2015) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Based upon the size and shape of room 83, as well as the fact that, as the most excavated of a series of three rooms, ti appears to be the most likely location for the torcularium, (olive oil press) as described in Jasemaki Volume 22, 598.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: No contiguous

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the House of Pomponius as a domestic house. We have determined that the last usage of this room (3) is as a dining room. This identification is based on its location, opening to the atrium and the remnants of some nice wall painting. There is also previous research regarding this. The entranceway on the northeast side of the room opens onto the atrium has no evidence of a door jamb. There is concrete but no evidence of plaster on the doorway. The floor appears to be small pieces of terracotta set in concrete. There is no evidence of a ceiling. Some reconstruction on the walls. On the northeast wall traces of concrete and stucco/plaster with yellowish background paint but no identifiable paint. Appears to be First Style architectural. The ceiling was at least at 2.5 meters, although it is nearly four meters in heights which could indicate many options. The entrance is in the north corner of this wall with round holes on either side of the entrance at about 2.5 meters high. In the lower southeast corner of this wall is a recessed niche for a couch [Feature Number 6519]. The southeast walls has traces of stucco with yellow architectural style panels (Style 1), the southwest wall with eight equally sized panels in the middle region with yellow stucco plaster painted in the First Style. A long vertical niche cut into the wall approximately a meter and a half is cut into the wall at a little over halfway from the southwest corner. It is finished in stucco and intersects the panels. A large rectangular window sits in the upper register above the niche at approximately 3.5 to 4 meters above the floor. The northwest wall has evidence of stucco and plaster in the First Style. In the middle is a large window opening to the fauces.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Entrance on the northeast side of the room opens to the atrium. Window opening to the fauces on the northwest wall.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 9 - 7 - 20 as a house. We have determined that the last usage of this room is a dining hall. This identifications is based on the room location in the structure. It has a very large doorway overlooking an arcaded peristyle (22). There are no specific features associated with food and drink in this room. However, there is a large modern pediment ceiling. The ceiling reaches a large second story because it has a rectangular window at the peak of the west wall. The west, north, and south west wall as well as the east walls between the large door opening show brilliant red, yellow, white and black panel paintings intercepted by still extant square paintings. The dado at the base is the usual black with green aloe. The floor is mosaic showing only black and white tesserae. The room is on a north-south axis. The ceiling was barrel vaulted as extant white molding.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southwest is Room 24 which contains a water basin with drains to the peristyle garden (22).

DESCRIPTION: The first feature is a large cooking platform. Moss covers to the top-tiled surface. The southern end of the platform contains a small oven. The cooking platform contains two semi-circular floor recesses for fuel. The cooking platform is on the east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven 4074 is to the west. The preparation platform 4073 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: On the north wall is feature 23-4073. It is two stone struts able to hold a serving or cooking platform.

This room has been identified as a dining room based on its location, characteristics and features. This is a rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis. The entire northeast wall is open and the space is an ala from the atrium. There are no other doors. No windows are preserved. The room is in very poor condition. There is no original floor level visible. No ceiling remains. The walls are opus incertum with brick at the southern and western corners. All three walls are covered with remains of plaster and preserved paint. The preserved paint is mostly red and appears to go midway to the remaining wall heights. A couch niche (4112) is in the center of the northwest wall. This is a large curving niche with the paint well preserved. The identification of other rooms in the structure is difficult due to the extensive damage caused by bombing and incomplete excavation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium (room 12) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a tavern. We have determined that the room is a dining hall based on the fact that this room is a very large rectangle. This is the largest room in the structure. It is entered at the southeast side. No ceiling survives, but there are three post holes on the northeast wall. Near the entrance at the north end of the northwest wall there are two decorated terracotta moldings with waterspouts inserted in the wall. The floor is irregular with dirt and lapilli covering the original surface. the irregularity of the floor is probably due to bombing. An archaeological trenc is located along the southwest wall and evidence of a black mosaic floor is visible in the baulks. The northwest wall separateds the dinig hall from a latrine (6-4100).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 6-4100 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We entered the large entrance at southeast side into Counter Room. A second entrance is on the southwest side. The room is oriented northwest/southeast. The shop is located facing the street with a fountain to the southwest. Evidence of paved floor. Evidence of two layers of fresco with red paint on outer layer. On the northeast wall is a lararium. The northwest wall has a large door out through the eastern side and three steps of a staircase are present at the west side. Northwest wall is preserved to a height above ceramic lined holes floor beams of second floor. Northwest wall is stone and brick. Southwest wall with doorway to the street; northwest side is brickwork with fresco, and the south side of the doorway is masonry with cut recess and shaped counter is projecting from the eastern wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Southwest of dining room.

DESCRIPTION: In the corner of Room 14 stretching along the southeast wall is a cooking platform. The platform is made of masonry construction; has arched storage underneath; and a top of terracotta tiles. Although partially ruined today, most likely the cooking platform was rectangular in shape.

We enter storeroom(4) from the southeast. The room is on a northwest/southeast axis off the atrium(2). The room lies off the west corner of the atrium. The general condition of the room, relatively speaking, is fair. White painted plaster is extant on all walls. There are six holes on the southwest and four holes on the northwest walls, and five holes on the northeast wall which suggest beams for shelving or storage. The height of the doorways is approximately four meters, and the ceiling is high, but indeterminate. The floor is obscured with lapilli. There is a white marble threshold at the entrance and it appears to house grooves for secure closure.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 is contiguous to the west of the atrium(2) and Room(12) in the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This brick cooking platform is located in the south corner of counter room 1, immediately adjacent to the open threshold to the street on the south west. The counter is made of flat rectangular bricks, mortared in between. There is a storage insert opening on the north west side of the cooking platform at floor level. Unusually, rather than an arch this storage area appears to be square and topped with wood. A modern wood insert is in situ today. The top of the cooking platform contains a C-shaped raised support structure with arms to support cooking pots above the fire. On the north east end of the cooking platform the top of the platform was a tiled surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform is located to the south of counter 6704

DESCRIPTION: Situated on the floor, near the N end of the N.E. wall is a square stone well cap with a round cut out seen in the middle of it. The cap is currently covered with a broken meta that does not appear to belong here. The wall is indented above the well, to allow easy access.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Situated on the North end of the N.E. wall.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this fresco detail is food and drink related because it depicts a bowl of pomegranates. This is not in very good condition, however, a footed bowl appears filled with fruit and is positioned on the shelf. This detail is located on the north wall towards the upper west side. It appears to be placed in an opening against a blue back ground.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is west of feature 14-4063.

DESCRIPTION: This is a large water basin on the east wall between two preparation platforms. It is three quarters of a circle, made of stone and cement. The wall behind and above it shows evidence of space for drainage. The interior is round and on the east wall, there is a small drainage hole. On the front, there is a large hole that opens to the kitchen floor.
This is a rectangular platform, one half the height of the cooking platform and joined to the cooking platform and the east wall. It is made of cement and stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Too cooking platform (4007) and to water basin (4008)

DESCRIPTION:
This tomb (8) has been identified as a triclinium tomb and preserves a triclinium within the enclosure. Although the condition of the three benches is poor and overgrown with vegetation, they are still visible. There is a bench along the south wall. The east and west benches seem to be set in from the east and west walls. These three benches form a "U" centered on the south wall. It is possible they were set in the wall and the space has filled in with debris or they were very wide benches. These appear to have been constructed in opus caementicicum.

Bibliography: V. Campbell pg. 174-175
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The south bench is centered directly south of the entrance and the east and west benches. The east bench is southeast of the entrance and the west bench is southwest of the entrance.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined this fresco is related to food and drink because this detail depicts a straw basket filled with figs. This basket is depicted as resting on the shelf at upper section of the east side of the north wall. The basket is in front of a blue background. It is located on the east of the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is east of feature 4002.

DESCRIPTION: This is an exceptionally large cooking platform. It has a tiled surface covering most the top. It has a large lip, along its back edge against the north wall and the east wall. There are three semi circular openings along the front of the platform, to the floor; used for fuel - charcoal or wood. There is no cooking equipment in situ.

This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined this space to be a dining room based on its proximity to the atrium. No threshold is visible. The room is rectangular in shape. The extant walls are opus incertum with no remaining plaster or paint. On the south-west end of the southern wall there is evidence of a niche for a dining couch. The niche is painted orange. The floor is no longer visible because of vegetation. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to room 18
VIDEO_COMMENTS: video on Bruno iPhone, L. Ludwicki to transfer

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined this space to be a dining room based on its proximity to the atrium. The room is rectangular in shape with its wide doorway on the south-east side. No plaster or paint remains on the walls. There is an upper window located on the eastern end of the south-east wall. The floor is no longer visible. The ceiling no longer remains.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video on Bruno iPhone, L. Ludwicki to transfer

DESCRIPTION: Feature 4044 is a long rectangular room in the north corner of the kitchen. It has a narrow doorway right off of the back street entrance at the north corner of the kitchen. The axis of the room is northwest/southeast. The small size of the room and the location lead us to believe that it is either a storeroom or a posticum. In the northeast wall there is a small square high window opening to the street. The walls are frescoed and appear to have been painted red. Wall construction is opus incertum. A large block of tufa protrudes from the bottom of the south corner wall to the threshold, which appears to have been stone and clay and divided the room from the kitchen. The floor is not visible. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 is located to the northwest off of kitchen 2.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 3 (feature 4045) as a storeroom. We have determined that the last usage of this space is a storeroom. This identification is based on the location off kitchen 2. There are multiple amphora (feature 4046) in eruption material about 1.5 meters above floor level. The room is small with possible slit windows into the kitchen. These walls have been reconstructed. The entrance is on the northwest side, with a low door. The room is unexcavated with possible traces of plaster and painting on the southwest wall. The five postholes on the southwest wall suggest a roof or shelf. The wall above the postholes continues on. It appears there is a door jam.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The feature is located in the south corner of kitchen 2 (4046) with the door on the northwest side.

DESCRIPTION: This is a brightly decorated room with red and yellow panels over a black dado (Fourth Style) that we have identified as a cubiculum. It opens up from the southeast on a northwest-southeast axis. The southeast wall also contains a rectangular window. The reason we took this room is a painting on the west end of the southwest wall that shows a scene of food. The floor is clay with marble inserts. The doorway has two marble pieces on either side that show placement for door hardware. Decorated cornice molding surrounds the room and it has a cornice arch on the southwest wall. A lemon and a pomegranite appear to be located within the arch. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is northwest of room six.

DESCRIPTION: It has been determined that this is a storage room in the House of Pomponius. This identification is based on the features in the room. This space is a small square room on the northeast - southwest axis. The one doorway to this space is located on the western corner of the southwest wall. The western corner of the room is opus mixtum, while the rest of the room is opus incertum. The condition of this room is poor. It is not fully excavated. No ceiling remains. No original floor surface is visible. The full floor surface of this room is occupied by three deep vats ( feature 6526). Although the exact nature of these vats is not evident, it was determined that these vats may have held amphorae.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room opens to the ala (8) just to the southwest. There is a corridor (12) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a tavern. We have determined that this room [2-4097] is a dining room. The room is a small rectangular dining room with a doorway on the southwest to the counter room and a doorway on the southeast wall to the atrium. There are no food and drink features identified. There is no ceiling and the floors are mud and lipili. There is a window on the northwest wall. Third and Fourth Style plaster appears in patches on all the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium [room 3, 4108] is to the south. The counter room [1-4095] is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is the Villa Arianna. We have determined this space to be a small rectangular dining room based upon its decoration and panoramic view. Feature 4708 is a frieze depicting a man holding a silver cup. This frieze is located on the southern end of the southeastern wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In dining room 5
PHOTOGRAPHER: Larry Ludwicki

DESCRIPTION: Within a kitchen (4710) in the Villa Arianna, along the eastern wall is a food preparation platform. Extant remains begin to the north of the hearth (4712) and ends approximately a meter south of the entryway. The platform appears to have been constructed of bricks and opus incertum Extant height is only about 21".
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Food preparation platform (4713) is along east was of kitchen (4710) and to the north of hearth (4712)

DESCRIPTION: This space has been identified as a storeroom in the Tavern of Tertius. It is a rectangular room on a southwest-northeast axis. The identification as a storeroom is based on location and character of the room. The room is presently in very poor condition. The only doorway is in the north corner of the northeast wall. The northeast, southeast, and northwest walls are not preserved above one meter; the door appears to have been narrow. There is a window in the center of the southwest wall. The southwest wall preserves some plaster and three large post holes horizontally places to the west at the level of the window top. No flooring is visible and no ceiling remains. The southwest wall is fairly tall. Two beam holes are visible; one in the west corner of the room and the other fairly close to the south corner. The highest area of the preserved wall preserves a window cut in the center of this room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is adjacent to entranceway [21] which is to the west of the room The doorway of this room opens to the area leading to the atrium [space 3] which is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this feature in room 3 as a cooking platform. This is based on the location and character of the remains. It is in very poor condition but large stone blocks and rubble were used to construct this platform. The location in the west corner of the atrium places this directly below the small window and near the lararium [4104].
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This cooking platform is located very close to lararium niche [4104] and is adjacent to the door into shop [1-4095].

DESCRIPTION: A long narrow passageway leads to the latrine located along the southwest wall of the narrow latrine. We have identified this feature because of the two mounds of stone on the southwest wall, the slope of the mounds, the window above the latrine, and the terracotta drain. This drain is in a recessed area of the outside wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the latrine room [6-4100]

DESCRIPTION: This is at the entrance of the latrine room no longer present but listed in the Naples Archaeological Museum inventory # 112285 "Cacator cave malum."
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the storage room to the north and the dining hall to the south.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified Oplontis A as a villa. Room 7 is a kitchen. We have identified this room as a kitchen due to its location in the villa, for it is a large room where many slaves could work, and it is close to the dining rooms. We have identified a very large cooking platform (4007), two preparation platforms (4009 and 4010), and a water basin (4008).
The floor is pounded mud and concrete. The walls are very high. There is one high window on the north wall above the cooking platform for venting smoke and a large high window opening to a corridor wall. The walls were plastered and painted, but the paint is badly preserved.
On the west wall is a low doorway to a storage room (100). It is in a barrel vault. On the south wall is a high and wide doorway to a hallway. There is a very high reconstructed ceiling.
Sources include Jashemsky, Clark, and Scavi guide.

We have determined that this is a storage area due to its small size and location. It has been conjectured that this would have held food storage or food preparation items. This is a small rectangular space on a north south axis. The only entrance is on the west wall at the northwest corner. The north, east, and west walls are preserved to a great height and support a reconstructed ceiling. The south wall is a partition wall and is not preserved to the ceiling. The construction is opus incertum. A small portion of plaster is preserved along the bottom of the north wall and the south door jamb. The south door jamb preserves a band with paint. This storage area is presently filled with stacks of roof tiles, bricks, and other construction debris. No original floor is visible although there is a stone threshold at the door. Overall the condition of this space is poor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is to the west of the ritual space (27) and to the north of the niche containing the altar (27-4019)
