DESCRIPTION: We have decided that the property at VI.10.3 was primarily a shop with a small house attached behind. Counter room 1 opens directly to the street on the southwest and contains a large L-shaped counter with inserts for dolia. Also included in this room is a small square platform at ground level directly to the northeast of the counter that has been identified in some sources as a hearth. The room itself is squarish on a northeast - southwest axis divided in two by one arm of the L-shaped counter. The northwest - southeast stretch of the room is divided by a short crumbling wall on the southeast side. The northeast wall had doorways on its north and east corners with an opus incertum, plastered painted wall between them. The entrance to the street is to the southwest and had a large stone threshold with channels with inserts for a folding door. Plaster remains on the walls and appears to have been painted red. A single post hole directly behind the street opening indicates the presence of an upper storey. The floor is rubble and no ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northeast of Via di Mercurio and to the southwest of atrium 3.

DESCRIPTION: Within a kitchen (4710) in the Villa Arianna, along the southern wall is a cooking platform with three arched storage areas . This platform runs almost the entire length of the southern wall except for the hearth at the eastern end of the wall. Three large brick-fronted arched recesses below platform held fuel. Platform itself is possible brick also.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This cooking platform (4711) is west of the hearth (4712) along south wall of kitchen (4710)

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 6.10.6 as a house. We have determined that the last usage of room 17 is a dining room. The room is located overlooking a damaged, colonnaded garden. This room is a good-sized, rectangular room. Evidently a bomb struck these back rooms so only three-fifths of the walls remain; the south wall and the west wall. The southeast wall has a small painted area. The southwest wall shows a relieving arch with no plaster. There is some rubble where there was once a wall. There is a tufa threshold made of blocks. There is no northeast wall when you look down on the pasticum. Currently there is no ceiling. The floor is pounded mud, and lapilli. There is a door on the west end of the northwest wall. The room is on a northeast/southwest axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to a stairway on the northwest that leads to an outside door (17).

DESCRIPTION: This central fresco panel in the southwest corner of the room on the west wall of the dining room #2 appears to be a human (male) that floats. The figure has a billowing cape. His head is turned to the south. In his left hand he holds a plate of food. With his right hand he appears to be using tongs to grasp food on the tray. The figure is defaced by what appears to be pick marks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: No other food and drink features are apparent in the room. This figure #4707 is the main image between the west and south windows.
PHOTOGRAPHER: Larry Ludwicki

DESCRIPTION: This space in the Villa of Diomedes has been identified as a small preparation room. This identification is due to the location , size and shape of the space. This room is on a north-south axis. The space is in fair condition. The only entrance to this room is a small door at the south end of the western wall. There is a small window on the north wall at the very northwest corner of the room. The west wall of this room is a partition wall dividing what had earlier been a large room. The decoration in this room continues the red panels seen in room 34. The preservation in this small space is a little bit better than the preservation in room 34 and remains of details, particularly of a cream colored dado, are still visible. No original flooring is visible. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the east of the vestibule 34 and it is to the south of peristyle 21.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified address IV-10-11 as a house and we have determined that Room 10 is a dining room. This determination is based upon the large size of the room, the decorated plaster, and its sightlines to the impluvium in the atrium The axis of the room is northwest to southeast with a stone thresholded opening in the southeast corner. Construction of the room appears to be very old being made of large tufa blocks and overall tufa stone. Small remnants of plaster remain on all four walls and it appears to have had a surface similar to cocciopesto flooring with a cement-like background with terracotta pieces inset. The southeast wall, next to the doorway was a plastered wall with a window opening to the ala. The southwest wall had a high window with a slit opening to the street, rectangular in shape, and another smaller window also with a slit near the west corner also opening to the street. Two postholes indicating an upper story were placed horizontally just above those windows. Two other postholes below the window course may have been used for wall attachments. The northwest wall has at its western end, at floor level, an arched recess, plastered over but filled with rubble that may have been a drain. One large posthole remains in the northwest wall near the north corner. A large portion of this wall is reconstructed. The northeast wall has little plaster remains and one low posthole. At its far east end, the door jamb has holes indicating door attachment. The floor today is lapilli and no ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opening to the west off Atrium 3.

DESCRIPTION:
A large rectangular dining room with the entrance doorway West of the atrium. The room is on a North/South axis. Plaster remains on 3 walls but entirely not on the West wall. Plaster is red and orange in color. No decoration schema can be readily determined, although North wall appears to have red and yellow blocks. Entrance to the dining room is on the Southeast corner of the East wall and extremely tall, about 4 meters high. There are numerous metal repair clamps along the North and East walls. Slight stenciling is found along the lowest south wall plaster. On the East wall, North corner of the room, there is a cutout niche (covered) that is approximately 30 centimeters deep, 2.5 meters wide, that appears to run to the height of the ceiling.
The floor is covered with lapilli.
The door jamb contains two insets on each. The lower is circular 10 centimeters across and 20 centimeters deep. The upper two are rectangular and across from each other.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium is to the East. West wall runs along the street.

DESCRIPTION: Midway on the southwest wall sitting on the floor of the room (possibly built into the floor) is a gray granite vessel. Its shape is cylindrical. It stands about 50 cm. high. It has no protruding lip but does have a lifting knob on one side. The vessel may have been used for mixing liquids or storing other materials.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: below and to the west of lararium (6533) and to the west of dolium 6530 and dolium 6529 and puteal 6531

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. This space (17) is a lararium. This lararium is located along the northern perimeter of the atrium
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: directly north of the fauces. This small space creates a tiny room dedicated to the lares. All the features of the lararium are cut into the north-east wall. There are stones along the threshold but with no finished surface. To the north-east of these stones no flooring is visible. The features of the lararium are set on large gray stone bases that stretch across the entire north-east wall. Plaster remains on all walls with traces of yellow paint on the north corner of the north-west wall and the east corner. Two squared altars stand side by side along the north-east wall. Three arched niches are cut along this wall above the altars preserving traces of red paint. The altars are framed with flanking pillars supporting a decorative architrave in the center of the north-east wall. This irregular niche is cut more deeply on the north-east half. There is a modern covering over the space.
BW_ROLL: Larry Ludwicki
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video on Bruno iPhone, L. Ludwicki to transfer
PHOTOGRAPHER: This is directly north of the fauces and near the north corner of the atrium.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Oplontis A as a Roman villa. We have determined that the last usage of Room 21, the dining hall was for parties and receptions. This identification is based on: 1) the room location in line with the atrium entrance of the villa; 2) the large window in the south wall overlooking garden 20; 3) the great columned opening in the north allowing access and viewing of the large unnumbered garden space; 4) the source identification in guide books. Beginning with the north opening two extremely large fluted columns delineate the threshold with masonry mimicking the fluted pattern on the two side walls. The threshold is marble with a step up from the garden. In between the columns and walls there are three floral patterned black and white mosaics with marble inserts that each show door fasteners to close off the room. The west wall has a large threshold opening on its northern end with remains of the same type of mosaic patterning and slightly larger inserts for doors. The west wall is opus incertum below and opus reticulatum on the surface. The door jambs and wall corners throughout are of flat brick courses with stonework between. There are series of openings scattered within the opus reticulatum indicating something attached to the wall. These continue on the south and east walls as well which are of the same construction as the west wall. The east wall also has a doorway and mirrors the west wall. The floor is mosaic in black and white and today there is a modern ceiling covering the space. The room is undecorated and, based on field reports, was under construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to south of room 20, to the west of room 17 and corridor 6 and to the east of garden 34, room 30 and corridor 3

DESCRIPTION: In counter room 1, an L-shaped counter runs along the street to the southwest and turns into the room to the northeast. The two arms of the L are of roughly equal size. In the arm of the L that stretches to the northeast (into the room) are two round inserts that probably held ceramic dolia. The street- front leg of the L stretching from northwest to southeast has a protruding angle at its top surface angling out over the large door threshold. The counter surface is marble tiled (reconstructed). On the inside of the leg of the L that runs from the northwest to the southeast is a large square opening for storage. Unusually, the counter surface stops just to the south of the open door leaving an approximately 60 cm. gap to the southeast wall of the counter room. The counter does not appear to be plastered.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the northeast/east is preparation platform 6516.

DESCRIPTION: There is a cooking platform on the south wall and against a small divider wall on the east. The modern workers have placed a wooden pallet over the platform, which is holding plaster bits. What we can see is some small portions of plaster on the bottom front wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cooking platform is on the south wall west of the latrine (4049) and east of the lararium (4057).

DESCRIPTION: This kitchen latrine has an arch on the wall above it. It is rectangular and very deep. The wood seat is not here. There is a cement bench adjoined to it on the south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is on the east wall east of the cooking platform (4048) and the lararium. It is south of the water basin (4058).

DESCRIPTION: This water basin is on the east wall, adjoining the latrine to the south and the outside door to the north. These are three walls that define the basin and a pipe that would drain water to the outside of the house, into the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
(4049) latrine is to the south
(4048) cooking platform is to the west

DESCRIPTION: It has been determined that this is a feature. In the northwest corner of the room is a stack of possibly eight amphorae. Six of these are large, wide amphorae stacked upside down. Two tall necked amphorae are also in situ in the lapili, with one additional long, thin amphora lying on the top of the stack. The pile of amphorae is opposite floor cuttings in the north corner of the room.

We have identified the Villa of Diomedes as a domestic villa. We have determined that the last usage of this room (35-4079) is a dining room. This identification is based on the location of the room with an opening in its north corner to the peristyle garden (21). The room is located on the southwest side of this peristyle garden, and the characteristics of the room, which include a large window on the south wall opening to a garden (currently unexcavated). This window is filled in with tufa blocks and mortar. On the west wall there is a threshold and doorway into room 36. The doorway is on the northwestern end of this wall. Today the wall is reconstructed to waist height for most of its length. The entrance on the north wall is centered and opens to peristyle (21). There is no evidence of a threshold and the entrance is partially reconstructed. There is no ceiling extant and the floor is lapilli and pounded mud, with traces of concrete on the south side. On the north wall are traces of stucco and concrete and modern reconstruction but it appears to be a high ceiling. On the northeastern side, upper register, are traces of a red painted border. On the eastern wall there has been reconstruction with evidence of concrete, stucco, and plaster. About 2.5 meters up there is an opening that runs almost the length of the wall, but this was filled in in antiquity. On the south wall is a large window (filled in in antiquity) that opened to a large garden which is presently unexcavated. There are traces of stucco on either side. Traces of stucco and red paint remain in the lower register on southeast side of the wall. On the western wall there is an entrance with a threshold to room 36 on the northwestern end of the wall. There are traces of a door jamb on the threshold. There are no traces of plaster on this reconstructed wall. Today there is a large opening waist high which has been reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: An entrance to room 36 is on the western side and an entrance of the peristyle garden (21) on the northern side.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified IX-7-25 as a house-shop. IX-7-24 is the front counter room. This counter room opens to the north to the street. It has one dolia hole in the north side of the L-shaped counter and two in the south. Food and drink features within this room are the counter (an L-shpaed counter with three openings) for dolia. Another feature is a lararium (13-4109) with two components on the east wall above the counter. On the souther wall of this counter room we see another lararium (4110) which opens to the counter room and the atrium (room 12). Characteristics of the room are its small rectangular size and the tall height of the counter. There is no ceiling. On the east wall there are painted plaster remnants with stenciled red rectangles. The floor is cocciopesto and in some areas mud. This counter room is totally open to the street. There is a high threshold consisting of three tufa stones with a cut-in for the door and a door socket. There is a large doorway to the atrium (room12). The doorway to the atrium has a threshold for a door.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The fauces (room 25) is to the E and the atrium (12) is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The northwest lararium above the counter is a recessed square without paint. Beneath the square is a recessed rectangle with white paint on the sides and a white marble remnant on the bottom.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The counter (4108) is to the east and south.

DESCRIPTION: This feature has been identified as a lararium. It is located in the southeast wall adjacent to the doorway to the atrium (room 12). This is an arched opening with an apsidal back. It is in poor condition without much trace of the back wall. The floor of this niche is a flat ceramic piece, probably reused roof tile. Some plaster remains in the arched area with a yellow painted surface preserved. Although the upper portion seems to be missing which creates an unintended opening with the atrium, there does seem to be an intended opening at the lower section. This opening appears to be a pass-through with a platform extending on other side of the wall in the atrium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 4109 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This feature has been identified as a couch niche. It is a large cutting into the center of the northwest wall of the room. The back is a curved profile. This niche preserves its plaster and paint over sixty percent of the feature. There is a red background decorated with delicate lines and a floral pattern done in yellow and green. Three small sections appear to have been chiseled out of the painting.

We have determined that this is a storeroom for food and drink due to its location and close proximity to the atrium. This is a rectangular space on a north/south axis. The space is partitioned down the length of the room, with the west section adjacent to the corridor wider than the east section. Presently, this space is gated and locked but can be seen from a doorway along the corridor (3) which opens to space 4, allowing a view through a door at the northwest corner of the west wall of space 22. A second view is through a door in the northeast corner of the north wall of room 22. This door opens onto the ritual room (number 27). A third view into this room is possible through the door from room 25 which opens through the south end of the east wall. The partition is reconstructed of wooden beams and plaster panels. The space is presently filled with amphorae. The walls are reconstructed to the original height with a rough opening at the upper portion of the south wall. There is evidence of plaster on the east wall. The ceiling is reconstructed. The original flooring is not visible. The general condition is fair.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the ritual room to the north and the atrium to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this space as a Ritual Space in the Villa of Oplontis A. It is Room 27. On the plan we have adopted from Jashemski. This is determined to be a food and drink space due to the altar feature (27-4019), located in a large niche in the center of the west wall. This room is a rectangular space, aligned along a north/south axis. This large room is richly decorated, although in poor condition. There is an entrance to the room along the west end at the southwest corner. There is a large, high entrance in the center of the east wall, as well as two small doorways along the south wall into storage space 22. Another doorway along the west wall is located in the north corner, and opens to room 2. In the east end of the north wall is a doorway into room 20. The main entrance to this room is the large doorway on the east wall, which is flanked by two large windows. These windows look out to Area 32, an open peristyle. The smaller square windows are centered over the two windows and doorway. The eastern wall has some plaster preserved at the bottom and two sections at the upper end of the room. Remnants of frescoes preserve Fourth Style decoration. A line of these holes are still visible, related to the peristyle ambulatory.
The west wall of this room has a large niche occupying the center of this wall. This large niche is decorated with Fourth Style frescoes including a dark red dado below high ochre panels and white Fourth Style patterns at the upper wall. The ceiling is vaulted over the niche. There is some molded decoration at the tops of the walls.
Although the lintel to this niche is reconstructed, there is a large section of carbonized wood in situ at the south end. The Fourth Style decoration continues outside the niche to both sides and is visible. Traces continue on both north and south walls. The lower panels outside the niche are red instead of ochre. The floor of this room is mosaic, white background with a black border defining the rectangular space of the room with floral dot pattern filling the inner rectangle. The niche is also defined by a black border. The ceilings are reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is located to the west of the peristyle courtyard number 32. Storage room 22 is to the south. Room 26-4017 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Eschebach tells us there was an altar in this space with a bench. Very little remains. What does remain is a simple masonry block along the sidewalk.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the SW of unexcavated Door 6.

DESCRIPTION: Serving room 4624 is roughly square, with a door to the northeast in its north corner, opening directly to the fauces area(1), but more importantly, going straight across the fauces, to shop 15. There is a window in the southeast wall to the street outside, and likewise a high, smaller window on the southwest wall. Area plans suggest that room 3, directly northeast, may have had a door stepping up from this room. Walls are of opus incertum with heavy reconstruction. Room contains a long bench(4626) on the southwest wall, and a well or cistern(4625) in the north corner, strangely enough in front of the door. floor is gravel and weeds!
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
to features in the room... Bench 4626, Cistern 4625.
to other rooms in structure...southeast of serving room 3, to the southwest of fauces 1 and shop.

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room. There is a N.W. - S.E. axis. One enters the room along the N.W. side. There is a marble threshold, that rises from the atrium. On the N.E. wall, is a broad doorway with a marble threshold, leading into the dining hall, space 29. This marble threshold has post holes for doors. This room is well preserved. The tesselated floor shows a black geometric pattern on white tesserae. The 3 walls preserve 4th style painting. 7 picture panels have been removed. The high square window is located in the center of the S.E. wall, this goes up to the ceiling. There is a restored wooden ceiling, situated directly beneath the window. This is feature 3711, which is a small fresco of a lobster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is room 3, there is an atrium situated to the N.W., dining hall. Room 29, opens to the N.E. and room 33 is on the other side of the S.W. wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room, which runs along a N.W./S.E. axis. We enter the area from a large doorway situated on the S.E. wall, from the sales room. There is a modern wooden lintel and no threshold. Supports for the doorway are made of brick. Evidence of plaster survives on the: S.W., N.W. and N.E. walls. There is evidence of red lower register, this survives on the N.W. and N.E. walls. There appears to have been a door which was blocked in antiquity to wards the Western end of the S.W. wall. 9, large rectangular floor joist holes are situated both on the N.W. and S.E. walls. There is a small window on the North portion of the N.E. wall, which would have been at the top of the 1st story. There is no ceiling, the floor is obscured with lapilli and vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room 1, situated to the Southeast and room #4, to the S.W..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader it Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Oplontis A as a villa. We have identified this room as a dining room. It is contiguous to the large portico to the south and to dining room 23, to the southwest and a storage room (4017) to the west and to a short corridor on the east. We enter this rectangular dining room through a very large door from the portico. There is a marble threshold with door posts. There are no particular features but there are characteristics associated with a dining room. The room is small. Mosaic floor seems to indicate placement for one bench. There is a decorative mosaic rectangle filling most decorations, with cream background with reds, aqua, yellow, and blue motifs in three horizontal zones. On the west wall is a door (iron gate, padlocked) to a room storing approximately one hundred amphorae, (storage room 4017).

Situated against the East wall is seen one rectangular, high concrete support strut. There are two struts, a shorter and wider strut jutting out from the South wall (positioned close to the door). The platform, supported by these struts is not present.

We have identified entrance 9 as a house. We have determined that room 2 is a kitchen due to its location within the structure. This kitchen has a wide entrance with a low doorway on the southwest wall, opening to the colonnade. We see a door to a storage room (3) on the southeast wall in the entranceway. There is a door across from this entrance, on the northeast wall, that opens to the street. This is secured by two doors or two sets of locks, evidenced by two sets of holes in the door threshold and circles for pivots. Features in this room include a cooking platform, a lararium, latrine, and water basin. Characteristics include a pounded mud floor, walls include very limited patches of plaster. There are windows, high up on the northeast wall. They are very unique in that they have large rectangular openings with a narrow opening to the street. On the northeast wall there is a small recessed arch over the latrine. On the southeast wall there are five post holes in two rows. Beneath these holes are two additional holes on the same level as the lararium. The northeast and southwest walls are pedimental in shape, suggesting a ceiling over the kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the peristyle (12) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This cooking platform is along the northwest and northeast walls of the kitchen and is "L" shaped. The section of this platform along the northwest wall is about 3.5 feet deep and about 2.5 feet high. There is an arched storage space for firewood below this section. Remains of ceramic tile can be seen on the upper surface. At the northern corner of the room the platform turns to the east, it is the same height bas the other section, but only about 1.5 feet deep. It goes continues at this depth for about 3 feet and then the section at the eastern corner of the room is only about a foot deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform is the the northeast and northwest of a small platform (3927).

DESCRIPTION: This "U" shaped counter runs along the East wall of room 1, with the bottom of the "U" facing via di Fortuna. There are 6 openings for dolia in the tiled surface. The interior base of the counter is masonry with traces of plaster. The surface is tiled in marble. Only 1 of the dolia has an extant lip (that in the SE corner). At the outside end of the "U", on the Southwest end, is an indentation for a hearth, rectangluar in shape. At the North end of the eastern "U", against the wall is dolia(6459). The exterior of the counter is all tiled in marble. The counter is a reconstruction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bench 6461 & counter 6460 to the West. Dolia 6459 is situated to the North

DESCRIPTION: This is a broken clay dolium partially built into the N end of the counter (6458). Dolium is short and squat round in shape. Narrowing at the neck and flaring to a wide lip. The lip is cracked on the West side, with another break in the same area lower down. The Dolium is filled with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the North of counter (6458). To the East of the Counter (6460) and bench (6461)

DESCRIPTION:
Entrance on North East floor is dirt-debris and weeds. No ceiling to room. Entrance is badly damaged. No sign of entrance hall.
North west wall is badly damaged, evidence of 3 post holes high on wall. Facing the wall to the left at eye level there is a lararium, recessed niche. Traces of plaster and paint on wall, presumably a lararium painting. South West wall is badly damaged with traces of plaster. Facing the wall on right side a recessed area leads to a vertical shaft to space above. Inside the shaft evidence of plaster in situ.
South east wall badly damaged with traces of plaster. Facing the wall on upper right there is a small niche for possibly a lamp?
Evidence of a second floor with traces of plaster and painting above kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Kitchen is entered from room 12 to the east

Downshaft in wall of the kitchen is unusual.

DESCRIPTION: This platform shows a meta and the catillus is in place. The meta had been broken apart but largely restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None listed.

DESCRIPTION: Low cement bench/step directly inside entrance 6.8.7 sits at the south end of the masonry counter 6460. Bench runs the width of counter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: counter 6460 to north, counter 6458 to dolium 6459 to east.

DESCRIPTION: Opening directly from counter room 1, this is a small rectangular storeroom on a north/south axis. There is no ceiling. Floor is of obscured by dirt and lapilli. Walls are opus incertum and heavily reconstructed. There is no wall in the south end of this room. On the east, the wall contains a plastered niche housing remnants of a terracotta drainpipe. Remnants of plaster also remain on north wall. Dolium 6466 appears to be embedded in the northeast corner of the room in front of the niche. Currently a stray meta sits in the centre of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: north of counter room 1

DESCRIPTION: One enters the kitchen from the South, via corridor (7) on an E/W axis; off the atrium(3) and then from a corridor (7), perpendicular to (6) on a N/S axis. The Southern wall is badly damaged. There are no traces of plaster or paint. The East wall has a small platform attached to it's North base, which may have formed part of a latrine. The North wall is damaged, with no traces of plaster or paint. Attached to the corner of the North wall and running along the North wall, is a masonary cooking platform. On the West wall, the cooking platform is attached at the Northwestern end. High up on the wall, at the Northeast; there is a circular opening. No traces of plaster or paint remain. The floor is obscured by debris and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (7) is situated to the South.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick and Fran Capo

DESCRIPTION:
This is a small, rectangular room situated on an E/W axis. There is a small doorway, in the W end of the N wall; and it opens to the garden. The floor is obscured by lapilli. The N and E walls are poorly preserved. There is no extant wall finish or decoration. Situated, high in the S wall are the floors for the floor joists for the upper story.

In the center of the W wall, there is a well preserved drain pipe, made of terracotta. It is extending down from the floor above. At the base of the pipe, situated in the S.W. corner is latrine (6303). Eschebach and PPM, identify this as a kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 14, is situated to the N.W..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Cavila

DESCRIPTION: There is low masonary support in the S.W. corner of the kitchen. Adjoining to the masonary support in the W. wall is a terracotta drain from the floor above. Adjoining the support in the S. wall, there is a low recess in the base of the wall. Possibly, this is the drain situated beneath the seat of the latrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the S.W. corner of the room

DESCRIPTION: This small diaeta runs along a N.E.-S.W. axis and looks onto garden no. 27. There is no existing decoration on the floor, which appears to be beaten cement. The S.E. portion has no wall and the S.W.,N.W. and N.E. walls located on the interior contain plaster painted in 4th style, with panels of pompeian yellow and red seen along the lower register and white with architectural features seen above. Figures such as faces, stenciling, and columns are faint but visible. The ceiling is made of modern wood.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
It is contiguous to room 10, situated to the S.W. and 27 to the S.E..

Anything unusual - there is a central rectangular panel missing on the N.W. wall. It's been said, it's in the Naples museum and contained writing implements, an inkwell and the name of "Marcus Lucretius."
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick and Fran Capo

DESCRIPTION:
This bench is indicated along the Northwest side of serving room 14.

*** The source is earlier plan.

In the front shop (4632) obviously moved, is the basalt part of a kneading basin. It has three internal holes for sticks to knead the dough, and it seems to have a circular depression in the center for the central kneading stick.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In shop 15 (4632)

DESCRIPTION: There is a small rectangular area for storage, containing an indentation for a shelf on the East end of the SouthEast wall. The inside of this recess contains plaster, that's painted red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 3719 is located to the South, at floor level, along the same wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video team leaders are Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: In the South corner of the S.E. wall is a low arched niche, which is approximately 1.5 to 2 feet in height, situated underneath the arch. The concrete rubble is in a mass. Plaster is evident on the wall, surrounding it.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 3718 is located to the North, at a higher level along the same wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video taken by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room, situated on a N/S axis. The North wall only survives in fragments. There is extensive restoration of the upper coorses in the E/S/W walls. The plaster survives on the E/S/W walls. It is divided into 2 registers, but there is no visible decoration. Situated, high in the center of the E. wall, there is a lined window, that is blocked in modern restoration. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout the room. The doorway, seen at the N. end of the West wall with a stone threshold and a placing for the door.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 3 is situated to the West
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leaders are Wernick and Capo.

DESCRIPTION: Situated in the corner, between the North and East walls, there is a short masonry (brick tile and rubble) ledge positioned at knee height, which may have formed part of a latrine. There is no apparent evidence of a water supply or pipe drain. The structure is poorly preserved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a cooking platform situated to the West

DESCRIPTION: We enter room 11 from the door on the Northeast, the doorway is low and narrow with modern wooden lintels. This small rectangular room lies on a N.E./S.W. axis. There is plaster painted red and possibly yellow exists on the facing of the doorway and N.E./S.E. and on the N.W. walls. The walls are preserved above a 1st story height. The room contains two basins nestled along the East side of the N.E. wall and in the South corner is a kneading basin. All of these items, are broken but are identifiable. Seen high, centered on the S.W. wall is a small rectangular window into the viridarium, with a modern wooden lintel and lead lintel situated at the top. This is evidence of plaster seen on the inner frame and there are fragments of ancient glass in situ, at the North lower corner. On both the S.E. and N.W. walls, at approx. the same height as the lower sill of the window are large holeas, one on each wall. Eleven circular holes, situated on the N.W. wall, line up approx. 4 ft. above the aforementioned hole. On the N.E. wall, at approx. the same height is a hole into the next room, possibly f.or light or air. It is above the 2 basins. The floor is obscured with vegetation and debris. No ceiling exists. Modern graffiti that is written in pencil exists on the door facing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To prep room 12, situated to the N/N.E.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: This large basin is badly broken. Approx. two-thirds of it remains from the bottom to the lip. It is made of a terra cotta and shares the rubble and lava stone support with basin 3803. This feature is located in the East corner of the room. Rock and plants are present in the bottom of it.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to basin 3803, situated to the N.W.. The kneading bowl is 3802 and the quern situated to the S.W. is 8313.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Terri Bruno

DESCRIPTION:
This is a small dining room. One enters along the Northwest wall and the room is on a N.W./S.E. axis and it is a rectangular space. The doorway is a tall wide, opening; almost the entire width of the room in the N.W. wall. Through this entrance, one can see the garden. (10) The room is in very poor condition. Although plaster remains on the walls, there is no trace of paint. The flooring is not visible and no ceiling remains. 8 pairs of joist holes are cut along the N.E. and S.W. walls, at about 8 feet high.
In the Eastern corner of the N.E. wall, there may be evidence of a niche into the wall rising up about 10 inches in height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is situated to the S.W. of room 8. Room 10 is situated to the N.W..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno

DESCRIPTION: We are outside the entrance 20, looking at the wall that separates us from the baker's mill room. North of this entrance is a long bench filled with stones. Fiorelli suggested the clients of Q. Bruttius Balbus, the owner of the adjoining home could sit there. We suggest that the clients of the bakery/restaurant could eat their bread products here.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the opposite side of the N.E. mill room wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: This is a long rectangular masonry cooking platform with extensive restoration. The surface does not survive. In the center there is an arched tiled recess for storage. In the base of the south face and and east face there are traces of plaster. Fragments of plaster survive inside the recess and in the northwest corner traces of plaster survive at the junction of the north and west walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the northwest corner along the north wall.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, north south axis. Floor obscured by lapilli throughout. Wide open doorway in south wall to peristyle . marble threshold with placing for door. Plaster survives on north, east, and west walls. East and west walls extensive decoration survives. Third style(?). Black lower register with yellow trim with alternating with alternating red and yellow above, separated by white borders. Traces of plaster molded cornice survive on the northern half of west wall with plaster decoration continuing above. Fragment of cornice on southern end of west wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle garden 14/15 to south

DESCRIPTION: This house is not completed. This feature is not identified or completed.

Long rectangular couch niche along the eastern half of the south wall. The dimensions of the niche are poorly preserved due to collapse and modern restoration. At the east and west ends the plaster of the niche survives on teh interior, red color.

Room 21, which is slightly smaller than the corresponding room across the atrium, mirrors the artwork with respect to panel designs. However the lower register appears to have been painted black. We enter this room through the open wall southwest of the atrium and entrance from the street. There is no threshold outlined. The floor appears to have been cement. The painting in the room has a low black dado which contains some stencilled patterns in gold. Alternating large panels, possibly fourth style, of red and yellow occur on the northwest, southwest and southeast walls, separated by portions of white which appear to have features of architectural motifs which extend from lower through middle to top registers. The moulding, which is decorated in floral designs, appears to have been painted red and blue alternately and exists on all three walls - full length on the southwest wall, in patches on the northwest wall and approximately half the length of the northeast wall. The lintel is modern and concrete.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Partially preserved tile floor slopes North to drain into the sewer that extends along the north wall. At the North end of the West wall are placements for a seat and a step that would have extended over the sewer. The seat and step extend to a square masonry platform and step in the North/East corner. as the masonry step and platform are the same height as the seat and step in the West wall, we would suggest that they are apart rather than a separate feature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Against the North wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular storage room. One enters into it, through a doorway in S.E. wall. The axis of the room is N.W./S.E.. The room is in poor condition. No flooring is visible. No ceiling remains, either. The walls are rubble and mortar construction, preserving some plaster on each wall. On the S.W. wall, the plaster has a horizontal incision about 4 feet high, across the entire wall. The N.E. wall may have also had this detail, as the plaster only reaches that height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room #2 (kitchen) is situated to the S.E.. Room #4 (corridor) runs along the N.E. side of the room.

DESCRIPTION: This waist high aedicular niche is situated on the N.W. back wall. It shows a minimal amount of plaster in the arch and shelf. The back of the shelf has been destroyed, the wall stones are visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Beam holes are situated on the S.W. wall, to the S.W. of this feature.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining room from room 10 through a very wie doorway with the remnants of a marble threshold. This typical Roman rectangular dining room has walls with about one third remnants of plaster. A good sized door to the west opens onto the tablinum 15 and through to the atrium 2. We see seven post holes and a high window in the north wall. This dining room, if we look out the broad entrance, overlooks a garden across room 10. Probably the final use of room 10 was as a large bronze workplace however.

DESCRIPTION: This good looking cooking platform has a small remaining front lip. A good recessed storage area is present. We see a small round window. We are surprised to see about one third of a large arch from the north wall over the cooking platform. Several tiles remain on the platform.
This feature may have been a cooking platform. It is in the south east corner of room 6. Presently this is just a pile of rubble.

This cooking platform is heavily reconstructed. It fills the east side of the room extending from the north to the south wall. Made of masonry construction. There is arched storage below. The platform has a lip and a tiled surface. On the front of the platform is a small round hole near the top left as you face it.

DESCRIPTION: Latrine is located in the southwest corner of the kitchen. It is divided from the cistern on the floor by a masonry wall. No trace of tiled floor remains but walls show evidence of a seat placing on thw west and south. Floor appears to slope and the space is narrow.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the west of cooking platform 6454

Rectangular masonry platform with no discernible surface or exterior finish. Abuts directly against water basin 6421 to the south.

Square masonry platform above which there is a plaster lined basin abutting directly to the corner of the north wall. The south side of the basin does not survive. DESCRIPTION: Entering from entrance 6.4.10, immediately to the east is kitchen 2. One is attached by its length to the west wall of the kitchen. The easternmost of the pair appears to have a sight L-shape with the bottom of the L attached to the south wall.

DESCRIPTION: Low arched niche only partly visible above the lapilli that cover the floor. Traces of red painted plaster survive on the interior of the niche. The niche is located at the north end of the west wall.

This lead lined basin is a reused catillus which has been placed upside down. The bottom coating of lead is intact. Above this a mortar and ceramic tile coating went up the side of the basin. The area behind the basin is not excavated.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is in the northwest corner of the room. It is west of the keading basin (3871) in the center of the room. It is across the room from the oven pass through.

DESCRIPTION: This basalt kneading basin is very wide, only one place is visible on the side for the wood or metal fittings. The bottom of the basin shows a round plug for the fittings of the inner machinery.

DESCRIPTION: This niche cupboard is in the southeast wall of prep room three. It is in the center of the wall and is a deep rectangular space. There are drilled channels that supported three shelves. This has been reconstructed with a wooden top and a re-plastered back surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This niche cupboard is directly east of the oven pass through (3873). It is southeast of the kneading basin located in the center of the room (3871)

DESCRIPTION: The storeroom is a situated square on a North West to South East axis. A door is located in the North corner and is of extremely low height, giving the impression that this would have been a servants room. Plaster remains on the South East and South West walls in light/small quantities. On the South West wall, at head height, there is a square window opening to the street. A second doorway is located in the corner of the North wall and is greater in height than the other door. In the South corner of the room, a ceramic pipe runs through the wall and is visible through cracks in the plaster. On the South West wall is a rectangular window that opens at waist height to address 9.6.2 and a square indentation in the wall is seen above the window. It indicates a possibility of a second level to the house. The West wall, seen directly across, appears to be reconstructed and there is no matching indentation. The floor is ground dirt. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The rooms is situated in the South West corner of the structure address, 9.6.3. This room is to the East of room 15. This room is South West of the kitchen (12).

DESCRIPTION: This low rectangular platform stands about 20 centimeter tall in the middle of the northeast wall of the kitchen directly touching the cooking platform to the southeast. Very little remains of the platform, other than some plaster work situated on the northwest edge.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Directly adjacent to the cooking platform (#3932) and across the room to the northeast of the latrine (#3933)

STRUCTURE_ID: Temple of the Genius of Augustus
DESCRIPTION:
It has been determined that this feature (7-9-2) is an altar within the Temple of the Genius of Augustus. The following factors have influenced our decision: The temple is located in a prime north-east site in the Forum. It is located in a large rectangular room with no flooring surface and the walls are a mixture of brick, opus incertum, and partial plaster.

The altar sits in the middle of a court and stands on a low plinth. It is covered with marble slabs and is approximately 137 cm in height and 112 cm in width. The front width of the platform is 179 cm; 22 cm in height. The south-west altar scene is a brilliant depiction. We see a man with his head covered and we think it represents Caesar Augustus, with his right hand holding a patera over a tripod ladened with sacrificial food and drink.

There are 4 figures behind the officiant: one is a boy child holding items germane to the sacrifice. Directly behind the tripod is an older gentleman stripped to the waist, looking at Caesar Augustus and is possibly Marcus Holconius Rufus, patron of Pompei. Immediately to his left is the bull whose head is at the same level as the officiant. The victimarius dressed in half-toga (sarong) is leading the bull through the scene by the nose. This young man might be a son of Marcus Holconius Rufus. The prominence of the figure, his handsomeness, and his important role in the sacrfice suggests his future status in the city. Above the figure is a drape, with a garland pendant below the drape. A flute player standing behind and between Marcus Holconius Rufus and Caesar Augustus is playing his instrument in order to distract spectators from the noise of the sacrifice.
On the north-west side we have a decorated patera and the garland above is filled with fruit. There are two ritual objects: one a dipper; the other a pourer.
On the north-east side of the altar is a memorial wreath dedictaed to Augustus, flanked by large laurel branches.
On the south-east side we see a wreath of fruits and nuts, a shawl on a hook, a chest, and a decorative spiral. The small chest has an open cover and could be filled with fruit.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Eschebach (pp. 308, 309)
Dobbins & Foss (2009, pp. 163, 164)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Contiguous in room 2, 4001.

4402 is contiguous to room 1, 4400, in the north-west.

DESCRIPTION: The south wall has 3 columns and 3 benches. Along the west wall there are 2 very large entrance columns framing the opening for the ramp. Benches are on either side of the columns of the west wall. Two large columns on the north side preserve evidence of fluting. There are 2 benches on this wall. All 7 benches preserve painted red plaster. Several benches, on seat portion, show inch 2 to 5 cm of modern cement reinforcement.

This is a rectangular room with an east/west axis. The floor is obscured by earth and lapilli throughout. All four wall are extensively restored. On the east wall there are two doorways to rooms 15 and 16. There is no visible threshold and there are modern lintels. High in the eastern half of the south wall there are five restored rectangular holes for floor joists. In the western half of the south wall there are two doorways to 18 and 19 with modern lintels. Doorway 19 has no visible threshold. Doorway 18 on the center of the wall has a basalt threshold. In the center of the west wall. The threshold continues underneath the cooking platform to the north. Cooking platform 6491 extends along the north wall from the northwest corner. Two square brick columns are inverted into the north wall. Between the columns are two rectangular openings for windows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 18 and 19 to the south. 15 and 16 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This large dining room runs along a north east/south west axis, almost. One enters the dining room through a large doorway which has a large portion of a wide lava stone threshold in situ. There is a deep groove on the south west side of the entrance and a ledge of the same height on the north east side, however there is no lintel. The room gives the feeling of space in that it is high with no evidence of beam holes. The walls (south east wall in particular) rises beyond a second storey height. Red painted plaster with panels delineated by stencilling is faint but evident on all walls. It appears that some painted plaster or paintings have been removed intentionally from the centres of the north west and north east walls and possibly the south east wall at the doorway, on the east side. there was a lower register of dado which had a filigree design alternating with panels of water plants. In the centre of those with the stencilling, there were circular medallions of some sort. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to atrium 13 to the south east.

DESCRIPTION: Narrow rectangular room. north south axis opening south to corridor 37. Floor obscured by lapilli throughout. No visible threshold. No visible decoration or finish on the north, east and west walls. All three walls have extensive restoration. At the base of the east wall there is a load bearing arch to cover a drain (?) beneath. Against the center of the east wall there is a small square tile and cement base. The upper two thirds of the east wall are restored including three small holes equidistant along the wall. The two southern most holes extend through the wall to the street. High in the center of the wall there is a rectangular window through the wall to the street. To the east with plaster interior faces and tile lintel narrowing to the east. There are no cooking features in this room. Its identification as a kitchen is based on te dimensions and the presence of a water supply.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 37 to the south

DESCRIPTION: One walks into this small dining room through a doorway in the north corner. The evidence we use is positional. The doorway is wide and the floor is lapilli. There is no ceiling. The walls are stone and brick. There are no signs of roof posts but we do see evidence of a ceiling (post holes) in the front room to the northwest. No windows are evident. The room looks into the atrium 2 to the north which also leads us to believe it is a dining room. There is one small patch of plaster on the southwest wall but no paint. In the south corner we see a square platform bout one third of a metre square.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 is north

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular stone preparation platform. There is a square level with a ceramic surface and then the platform steps up at the eastern end to a higher surface. This is in poor condition and located at the northwest corner of the kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: west of preparation platform 3284, directly opposite the entrance

DESCRIPTION: This niche is a low couch niche identifiable by a small concavity in the lower portion of the wall. Some plaster remains on the surface.

Due to its proximity with the as yet uncompleted Central Baths, it is probable that this shop, one of eleven which surround the Central Baths of insula 4, was a large food and drink shop. It is entered by one step up through an open store front from the northwest. The floor is rubble. The reconstructed walls are extant to a first floor level. There is no remaining plaster.

This feature is probably a preparation platform in the mill oven room (9). It is located along the northwest wall directly north of the doorway to room 8. This is a square platform , one large tuff block forming its southwest side, with what might be opus incertum forming the northeast half. This is preserved only to the height of the large block.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform is to the northeast of over (4588) and to the west of mill (4598).

DESCRIPTION: Small tufa altar. Moulded base and lip with a scroll decoration with recessed top. No inscription. The rear face is undecorated.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6326 to the north; 6334 to the south; 6335, 6327, 6328 to the west

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular stone preparation platform with modern cement extending from the east corner along the north wall.
This rubble base has some damage. It is surrounded by lava stones.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill (3862) to the north, mill (3865) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular storeroom runs along a northeast/southwest axis. One enters from the northwest. The room is in a total state of disrepair with piled rocks, rubble and vegetation obscuring the floor. There is a large portion of the southeast wall missing, from which one can see the street. Some red painted plaster remains on this wall in the east corner. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: contiguous to storeroom 31 to the northeast and latrine 33 to the southwest. Corridor 28 is to the northwest

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room. It lies on a S.E./N.W. axis and is situated directly off room no. 1, with a door in the N.E. wall. There is a window on the N.W. wall, it is opening into the other Dining room (3). The room is in poor condition, despite efforts at heavy restoration. No flooring is visible. There is a reconstructed ceiling. Moulding is preserved on the N.E. and S.W. walls, suggesting a barrel vaulted ceiling. All 4 walls preserve, painted plaster. All 4, are in poor condition, they maybe in 3rd style. One can see a red dado. The central zone also has red panels. Although, some decorative details can be seen, it is impossible to discern any subject of figurative designs. Some panels may have been yellow. The door jamb, situated on the North side has 3 deep holes drilled for some kind of door fittings.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is situated to the West of the principle entrance. One goes through room one and enters the door, situated on the N.E. wall. Room one is directly N.E. of this room and room 3 is directly N.W. of this room.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 5-4-1 as a bakery based on the presence of mills and an oven. Room 4 is a kitchen based upon its location directly behind what we consider some public eating areas, the presence of a latrine(4595) and what appears to be the remains of a cooking platform(4594.) The room is rectangular sitting on a northwest/southeast axis, with a door to passageway 13 in the north corner and a door to serving room 3 in the east corner. A round window would vent the cooking platform high up on the southwest wall. The south corner of the room contains the latrine(4595.) the walls are opus incertum but heavily reconstruted. The low doorway in the east corner is re constructed. Ancient postholes above this doorway suggest that the doorway could have been higher. Some fresco remains on he southwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
To other features in the room: latrine 4595, platform 4594.
To other rooms in the structure: [The room is] to the northwest of serving rooms 2 and 3, to the southwest of dining room 5, to the southwest of passageway 13.

DESCRIPTION: Circular basalt basin directly against the oven 6417 to the north. Used to contain water for the preparation of bread. Conical interior with no visible lining.

Circular basalt kneading machine. At the base of the basin there is the placing for a partly preserved iron blade of a kneading machine. In the east and west sides of the basin there are two holes in each and in the north and south side there is a single hole in each. Beneath the hole in the north face there is a small indentation in the external face of the basin.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6420 is to the north

DESCRIPTION: This is an oscan inscription is in white stone on the pebble surface of the east end of the ramp (1-3948). The translation is Oscan - "Oppius appidius oppi filius trebius mezius trebii filius aediles - ovius epidius son of ovius and trebuis mettius, son of trebius, aediles"(Cooley, 2004). This inscription refers to donors.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is an inscription in the ramp (1-3948) and is white in color.

DESCRIPTION: This circular table is centered in the space of the north triclinium. It is circular and is constructed of opus incertum and was covered with a thick plaster layer with ocra, red and black paint splashes. This plaster is on top and around all sides.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This table is centered in the space inside the north triclinium (4-3939).

DESCRIPTION: This table is centered in the space of the south triclinium. It is circular and is constructed of opus incertum and was covered with a thick plaster layer. This plaster is preserved in a small section on the eastern side of the table. The plaster is painted with ocre red and black splatters.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This table feature is centered in the space inside the north triclinium (4-3939).

DESCRIPTION: In the southeast corner of room 2, tucked under an external staircase there is a masonry cooking platform. It is rectangular in shape and in a very ruinous condition. No surface top remains but there is a small amount of plaster on the southwest corner that shows original construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is placed in the southeast corner of room 2.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a preparation room. It is a small rectangular space on a N.E.-S.W. axis. One enters the atrium from the N.E. side of the room. No original top flooring exists. In the N.E. corner of the room there is a cutting through the floor. In the N. corner of the room there is a well. The well is topped with a ceramic putile (13-3960), the putile is in situation.
On the S.W. side of the room is a low doorway to a store room (14-3934).
This room is a step up from the atrium. There is a grey stone threshold.
The walls are preserved to about 2.5 meters. The upper portions have been reconstructed. The walls preserve traces of plaster, over an opus incertum construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This preparation room is S.W. of the atrium and is S.W. of room 14-3934. It is N.W. of the kitchen (12-3930)

DESCRIPTION: This space was noted as a triclinium by Eschorbach. But in the bombed state of this house, there is no evidence pointing to the function of this room. This space is northwest of the fauces in the western corner of the house. It is a rectangular space on a northwest - southeast axis. The entrance to this room is in the eastern corner along the northeast wall. All that remains are minimal traces of walls. Near the doorway plaster is observed on a partial standing wall. At the corner of the northeast wall a curved plastered section steps back into that wall. (situated at wall bottom)

In the south corner of room 4, which has been identified as a kitchen in baker 5-4-1, is a narrow area set off by a low wall on the northwest side, with brick and paved sloping floor and masonry seat supports that we have identified as a latrine. Drainage of the waste would be towards the street outside, making this identification more secure.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of cooking platform (4594).

DESCRIPTION:
Room axis is East/West. One enters the room from the east. The threshold is of stone and raised. There are cuttings for door jams. The east wall shows traces of painting. There is a lower register in red with a thin white border. Above this there is a yellow register. The north wall has better preserved painted plaster. Four registers are visible. The lower register is red as elsewhere. The registers above are yellow. There are two large yellow panels whose style is indiscernible. There are traces of plaster molding high on the wall. The West wall has a large opening looking out on the portico (14) and the garden (15). There are traces of painted plaster similar to the other walls. The south wall carries better preserved painted plaster and molding, similar to the North wall.

View of portico (14), garden (15), lararium through the opening in the West wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: ALA (9) to the east, room 13 to the West.

DESCRIPTION: Square masonry platform in the South/East corner of the room. The surface does not survive. No recess storage.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: South/East corner of the room.

DESCRIPTION: There is an arched masonry cooking platform stretching along the East wall into the Southeastern corner of the room. The surface of the platform is nonextant, although the masonry arch for underneath storage is still present. Pieces of clay on the top suggest the surface may have been tilted.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In Southeast corner of room.

DESCRIPTION: Poorly preserved cooking platform is the Northwest corner of the atrium with arched storage recess beneath and tiled surface. Western masonry support abutts the plaster on the West wall and survives to the height of the tiled surface. Only the base survives to indicate the location of the Eastern support. The floor is obscured by lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest corner of atrium.

DESCRIPTION: This house is not completed. This feature is not identified or completed.

In the southeast corner of the room is a masonry platform. Short end is attached to south wall. Drainpipe coming from floor above is located next to this platform. No top surface. Only masonry remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In southeast corner of room.

DESCRIPTION: This small storeroom runs along a northwest/southeast axis. One enters from the northwest. The room is in a total state of disrepair with piled rubble, rocks and debris. There is a large portion of the southeast wall missing from which we can see the street. Some red painted plaster remains on the same wall next to the hole. There are some pieces of support high on the northeast wall. There is no ceiling extant. The room is approximately four feet wide.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: contiguous to storeroom 30, to the southwest and to kitchen 29 to the northeast and corridor 28 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small dolium. It is located about midway across the southeast wall. It is partially submerged (about two thirds) below ground level and stands at a sight angle. This is complete except for several small chips missing from the rim.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the east of basin 3926

DESCRIPTION: Round terracotta dolium is embedded into the earth in the northeast corner of room 3 (6464) Visible portion of the dolium stands about knee high and tapers to a neck with a flared lip. On the lip is a metal attachment which may have connected a lid to the lower part. A round stone piece currently sits inside the dolium and may have been the lid to a similar feature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: sits in northeast corner of room 3 (6464)

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular counter delineates south wall of room 5 (6467) Counter contains one dolium, water feature 6473 and a hearth. Pot is located centrally in the eastern two thirds of the counter. With rectangular opening for the hearth contiguous to the north. One corner of the counter fits around a brick entrance pillar to room 5. The exterior eastern and southern edges of the counter are covered in brick where they face rooms 4 and 2
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the east of water feature 6473

DESCRIPTION: Low to the floor, immediately to the northwest of the door, located on the southwest wall is a very low masonry rectangle that would have been a prep platform. It is immediately to the southeast of the cooking platform (4129).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
to the southeast of cooking platform 4129
to the southwest of prep platform 4132
to the west of latrine 4135

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a counter. This structure is built into the Southwest wall, running its entire length. It is approximately 2 1/2 feet high from the ground. The front face is reconstructed opus incertum. The top surface id cement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Due west of cistern 4625 in serving room 4624.

DESCRIPTION: This is a stone basin. The exterior is straight sided, with a rounded interior space. The diameter is about 4 ft.. This basin is complete and has 2 notches situated; in the rim about 8 inches apart. A drilled drain exists, at the bottom. This basin is in situ, situated in the South corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This basin is located to the S.W. of the dolium, 3808
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION:
This dining room runs along a N.W.-S.E. axis and is located N.E. of the entrance to the house. The room is poorly preserved. There is a small entrance on the N.W. side of the S.W. wall and a large doorway, which is completely open on the S.W. wall and provides a look into the garden, situated just beyond the passageway. The floor appears to have been black pavement with white tesserae sprinkle about, and is now covered with debris and overgrowth and two column pieces. Evidence of painted plaster remains on all 4 walls, of primarily the colors of red and yellow. The N.W. and S.E. walls have been capped with terra cotta tiles in modern times, and the N.E. wall, which is the highest wall, is not capped but appears to have been repaired and partially reconstructed at some point in time. There is no ceiling extant.

As an aside, it appears that 3 medallions or circular panels have been removed from the Eastern end of the Northwest wall and the East and South ends of the Southeast wall, approximately 1.5 meters from the floor level.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the floor plan by Esch, it is contiguous to room 21 situated to the S.W. and room 22 to the East, and 12 is to the West
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: One enters the room through a door, situated on the Northeast wall that divides this from an adjacent room. A terracotta puteal (well head) that is from an earlier atrium. On the N.W. wall, at the level of my chest, you see a terracotta pipe that extends back (39 c.m.)). Some wall shows remains of a lararium, and adicular niche and some plaster remains. Seen, on the S.W. wall at 5 and one-half feet (approx.) we see 6 large beam holes an estimated 5 feet higher, its probably a candle niche. The S.E. wall, that is heavily repaired; shows 4 candle niches with irregular placements.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 6 is situated to the N.E..

DESCRIPTION: Enter from room 6, Hallway. One enters the room from a doorway, on the South end of the S.E. wall. There is a rectangular storage room with a compacted floor of dirt and lapilli stone. 2 walls have indications of plaster with indicators and preparation for repairing. There are post holes, present, for a relatively low ceiling. The N.W. 2/3 wall is extant to 2 feet high and the West 1/3 of the wall is 10 feet high. It could serve as a pass through to the kitchen. In 2013, the room is filled with roof tiles and 1 large piece of particle board. The room is situated on a N.W./S.E. axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 6 (Hallway) situated to the Southeast. Room 7(kitchen) is situated to the S.W..

DESCRIPTION: In a ruined bombed - out structure, all that remains is evidence of a masonry cooking platform to identify room 2 as a kitchen. The room appears to be L -shaped at an east west axis. With the cooking platform located to the south tucked under an external staircase. Little of the walls remains, but the wall to the southwest has some red plaster. It appears that the doorway to the room would have been in the northeast corner. The floor is rubble. Identification of the room is based on Eschebach.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to the east of fauces 1 and to the south of atrium 3.

DESCRIPTION: Finally, before the oven; room 13, there is a single catillus, perhaps from rubble base 3794, or perhaps it is there to replace an existing catillus.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill (3795), situated to the N.E., there is a well (3792); situated to the S.E..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: A small round split quern, that is made of lava stone is situated next to the kneading basin and under the window of the S.W. wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to 3802, to the S.E. and basins 3803 and the kneading basin 3804, seen to the N.E..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room situated on a N/S axis. It is bombed out. Only the East wall survives with substantial collapse -apparent- and some evidence of modern restoration. It is poorly preserved, at the Northeast, and Southwest corners. No trace remains of the South or West walls. The Northeast corner is filled with earth and debris. The remainder of the floor is obscured by earth and vegetation. Eschebach, identifies this as a kitchen. Eschebach, also refers to a lararium painting, no trace remains of it; nor is it found in other literature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 7 is situated to the North. Garden 6 is to the South.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Carlos Avila

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular cooking platform is located in the South East corner of room 12. It runs lengthwise along the South East wall, constructed of masonry, the platform is today covered with moss with no visible tiling or decoration. The cooking platform is approximately knee high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Feature 3935 (prep) is situated to the North East of latrine (3933), seen to the South West.

DESCRIPTION:
There are 7 programmata outside the bakery mill room CIL, IV, 3674, 3678, 3680, 3683, 3703, 3702 and 5065. On the evidence of CIL, IV, 5065 Della Corte established Papirius Sabinius as the more logical owner of the business. The workers are supporting Papirius Sabanius as Aedile. The workers' names are (male) Pyranus, Calvus, T. Genialis, and (female) Statia, Petronia, and Olympian ica.
The writer of the programmata is Infantion.
In 2013, we can see one programmata in beige with large red letters.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: At the rear of the N.E. mill room wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: In the south corner of the southeast wall of room 12, it appears to be a latrine. Identification is based upon 2 large ceramic pipes running through the wall in the southwest corner and the fact that it is adjacent to the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Immediately to the southwest of the cooking platform (#3932) and across the room to the southwest of platform (#3935)

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room on an East/West axis. There is no ceiling. Floor is obscured by overgrowth. Doorway is located in the Southeast corner, opening to atrium room (4). The threshold was stone but little remains. All four walls show remnants of plaster, pinkish-red in color. No windows are evident, but a probably reconstructed opening leads to the adjoining property at 6-11-17
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (4) to the East.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is a small rectangular room in the Southwest corner of the property. There is a cooking platform (6445) in the Southeast corner of the room. The walls are ruined. No ceiling remains. The floor is overgrown. Trace evidence of plaster on the South wall. There is one brick on the South wall that appears to have two rusty metal attachments on it. Access to the kitchen would be from room (8).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of room (8)

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room; North South axis. The north wall survives only at ground level but consisted of a central pillar separating two doorways to the east and west. No visible thresholds. High in the South wall there is a chimney with a tiled lintel sloping up to the exterior beneath which along the south wall would have been a cooking platform of which no trace remains. The western third of the room was divided from the rest of the room by a plastered partitioned well. The floor in this area of the room was tiled and sloped down to the latrine (6394). High in the South wall there is plaster with no visible decoration and a circular hole - modern collapsed. No plaster on east and west walls. The eastern two thirds is obscured by lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (1) to the North.

DESCRIPTION: Boyce described a fragmentary painting of the lares above the cooking platform. No evidence remaining.

Entering the house to the east into area one, to the left is the entrance to room five. Entrance faces south. Badly damaged, under roughly five feet of rubble and debris. On the east side there is a wall, badly damaged with no traces of plaster or paint. The interior north wall is badly damaged, with traces of plaster and paint high up on wall. Reconstruction visible on north wall. Possible post holes. On the west wall basically nothing is left, very badly damaged. Possible projection from wall. Wall on the south had entrance. Possible evidence of wall, few blocks remain. No floor visible, covered by rubble. No ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is entered from room 1 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is a large ceramic dolium. It is complete except for a round drilled whole approximately 3 inches in diameter. This hole is located just beneath the rim. This dolium is presently located in the Western corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is N.W. of basin 3807
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Terri Bruno

DESCRIPTION: The processing room lies between the Mill room (5) to the S.E. and the oven room (13), in the SouthWest. The room is in a state of disrepair and is filled with debris, rubble and undergrowth to a depth of approx. 5 feet. Seen on the S.W. wall are 7 brick lined joist holes. On the N.E. wall, there are 12 brick lined joist holes, under which there is a small window, jutting out to the street. Only a fragment of plaster remains on the S.E. wall. The heights is undetermined, however, in the Western corner; we see indications that this was a high wall. No ceiling is present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the mill room (5) at the S.E. with the Oven room (13) being situated to the S.W..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Terri Bruno

DESCRIPTION: We enter the dining room 5 from a small entrance in the north wall from atrium 2. The room is rectangular and lies along a northeast/ southwest axis. The north and east walls are preserved to a second storey height while the south wall, which contains a large opening providing a view into the peristyle, is approximately two metres high on the west end and 2.5 to 3 metres high at the east end. The west wall is slightly lower that the north and east. Remnants of painted plaster remain on all four walls in red, yellow and white. An odd finding, high on the west wall, is a portion of ancient glass window pane, in situ, placed horizontally and perpendicular to the wall - perhaps an ancient shelf? The floor was cement with fragments of marble. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 to the north, garden 6 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Stone kerbs are above the street (which is not named on Eschebach). We see painted cement and a street shrine. It can be seen as a short aedicula shrine and was decorated in antiquity. Eschebach reports a painting of two snakes alongside the altar and a basket of offerings above. The paintings are no longer extant though the whole lower portion of the wall is painted pinkish-white
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Via Stabiana to the west, north corner of 9.1.1. and 9.2.12, feature is across the street and west of 9.1.34

DESCRIPTION: This is the kitchen. It is a square space on a raised platform one step up from corridor 5. It is on an east/west axis. The rubble remains of a cooking platform (3274) are in the southeast corner. The north and east walls are stone construction with traces of plaster. The south wall is a partition between this room and the latrine (7) There is no west wall. No flooring is visible. It is all in a very poor state of preservation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 7 lies to the south, corridor 5 lies to the west

DESCRIPTION:
Shelf (bracket)
The Northeast and Northwest walls of storeroom 6 contains holes to support wooden shelves. The Northwest wall has two holes at the higher level and one one hole lower near the west corner. The Northeast wall has three pairs of 2 holes each at staggering heights. See drawing for dimensions.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In storeroom 6 (4599)

DESCRIPTION: There is a large masonary cooking platform, located in the N.W. corner of the kitchen and it extends approximately two-thirds of the length of the North wall. No storage niches are present. There is a raised ledge, situated at the East end of the platform
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is situated to the East
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Taken by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: This is a Dining Room. It is a rectangular space, situated on a N.W.-S.E. axis. One enters this room from a wide doorway, almost the entire length of the N.E. wall.
