This room is in poor condition. There is some evidence of Opus sectile in a red pebble matrix, situated near the Northeast wall. No ceiling remains. The walls are preserved from 8-15 feet in height. The short wing walls situated on the N.E. side are partially covered with plaster with some evidence of paint as are the N.W. and S.W. walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is situated N.W. from room 3. It is S.W. of the atrium.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION: This is a tablinum/dining room. It is roughly on an east/west axis. This rectangular room has wide openings through both the east and west walls. Due to its location between the atrium and the garden portico it has been identified as a tablinum and dining room. This is in a very poor state of preservation with the stone walls preserved only below the ceiling level. Brickwork flanks the doorway on the western side. All walls retain the remnants of their plaster covering with traces of fresco. The dado is visible in some places and seems to be a third or fourth style painting. On the north wall there is a small section of blue painted panel just above the dado. The midsection is divided into large panels with wide red borders on the north and south walls and blue or green borders on the west wall. No flooring is visible. There is opus signinum visible only in the threshold on the east entrance. There is also a small piece of marble threshold in the east entrance with a cutting for a door.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 at its east side, the garden portico 6 is to the west, the passage 4 lies to the south

DESCRIPTION: We enter the storeroom from the west through the posticium 18. The room is square on a southeast/northwest axis. The threshold appears to have been just volcanic rock. The doorway, which has basically completely deteriorated, has a cut edge on the east side. The western portion is all but missing. Traces of red painted plaster appear on the east, south and west walls. On the east wall are two or three holes for shelf support. On the south wall is a rectangular small window, above which are five indentations which appear to have been for second storey support. On the west wall there is one hole. There is also a hole for an unknown reason from which something has been removed. It is about two m high in the southeast corner and today we can see to the outside through this hole. The east and south walls are preserved up to the second storey. The west wall is not as high and the north wall, where we enter, is only about two m at its highest. No ceiling is extant and the floor is obscured with rubble and vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: posticium 18 to the north, kitchen 3270) to the west

DESCRIPTION: Small shop no food and drink

This is the south triclinium located in front of the temple portico. This was an outdoor dining area. No ground surface is visible. The triclinium constructed of large benches of opus incertum covered with a level of cocciapesto and an outer surface of plaster conserving red paint. This painted plaster is preserved along the lower side of the southern couch as well as the southwest corner of the western couch. Plaster is also preserved on the northern end of the eastern couch. There is preserved plaster on the outer wall of the eastern couch and the southern couch.

The outer base of the temple is also plastered and painted red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is south of the ramp (1-3948) and surrounds the table (4-3958).

DESCRIPTION: This is the north east triclinium located in front of the Temple Portico. This was an outdoor dining area. No ground surface is visible. The triclinium is constructed of large benches of opus incertum covered with a level of coccia pesto. The benches have an outer surface of plaster painted in red paint. This painted plaster is preserved on the inner walls of the eastern couch. There are also smaller remains at the counter of the north couch and on the inner northern corner of the west couch. The couch ends facing the south - towards the ramp (1-3948) - also preserve plaster with red paint; as does the western outer edge of the couch. There is some plaster on the outside wall of the east bench. The ground level has a lower cut, exposing more of the wall height than on the south triclinium (4 - 3940).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is contiguous to ramp (1 - 3948). This feature surrounds the table feature (4 - 3957).

DESCRIPTION: This is an entrance ramp situated at the counter of the western wall. It extends outward from the portico into the central area of the dining forecourt. It rises from about 7 centimeters above present ground level to approximately less than 1 meter in height at the portico entrance. It is aligned with the temple on an east-west axis. The construction of this ramp is opus incertum with a cocciopesto layer and pebble surface. There is an oscan inscription across the east end of the ramp. On the south side of the ramp there are 3 blocks along the edge which appears to be insitu.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The ramp is in the central space between the triclinia north (3939) and triclinia south (3940). It is on the west side of the portico in the exterior space (4-3955).

DESCRIPTION: There were furrows and root cavities visible at the time of excavation.

Rectangular room. north south axis opening from a narrow corridor which continues to south to peristyle 14. Vaulted concrete ceiling with the placing for the planking throughout. Partially preserved tile floor in the south, east and north half of room. Slopes north drain into the sewer that extends along the north wall. At the north end of the west wall are the placings for a seat and a step that would have extended to a square masonry platform and step in the northeast corner. As the masonry step and platform are the same height as the seat and the step in the west wall we would suggest that they are part of the latrine rather than a separate feature. There are no visible cooking features in the room but its position in the house, dimensions and latrine suggest possible function as a kitchen. No visible threshold. Modern lintel above. In the southeast corner the surviving section of floor has a raised ribbing running parallel to the east wall approximately 5 cm from the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle 14 to south

DESCRIPTION: L-shaped room with the arm north/south and the base east/west. The room extends around a northwest side of a no longer extant oven. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Only the lower courses of the walls survive with extensive restoration. In the north end of the west wall is a doorway to room 3 with a partially preserved stone threshold. At the western end of the south wall is a doorway to the salesroom 1.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 1 to the south, room 3 to the west

DESCRIPTION: Eschebach p 174 identifies this property as a bakery and the plan shows an oven. No traces remain.

This is a latrine in the west corner of the kitchen. It is placed within a small arched apse which is cut into the northwest wall. The seat extends outward along the southwest wall. The apse may have been faced with ceramic pieces one of which remains in situ. The drain cuts under the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: dolium 3231 and cooking platform 3229 to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: Long rectangular couch niche blocked by rubble and modern restoration. The niche extends along the north wall from the junction with the west wall to the center of the north wall. Plaster survives on the interior face and on the base to support the couch there is no visible decoration. It is not clear if this was used in the final phase or if the refill is modern. The couch may have been plastered in its final phase.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the northwest corner of the dining room.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, East/West axis. Floor obscured throughout by lapilli. North/East/West walls survive only in the lower courses with extensive modern restoration. At the West end of the North wall there is a narrow doorway with stone threshold with placements for door. Wide doorway in the West wall, overlooking the garden, and stone threshold with placing for shutters. South wall survives to a higher level with signs of collapse and modern restoration. At the East end of South wall there is couch niche 6315.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden peristyle (31/39) to the West, and atrium (41) to the North.

DESCRIPTION: Arched, plastered lararium niche with moulded edge. White plaster with burgundy trim. On northeast wall of the kitchen 16. Burgundy extends to ledge. White plastered background with traces of original figures. Below the ledge is the remains of a painted lararium with burgundy border, badly damaged. Traces of a serpent in red and yellow on right side. Yellow figure discernible on left side. According to Boyce p 167, on the back wall of the niche was painted a genius holding in his right hand a patera over a flaming altar, a painted Lar and a coiled snake with a beard facing the altar
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: in northeast corner, 6329, 6334 to the south; 6328, 6327 to the west; 6335 to the southwest

DESCRIPTION: Large masonry L-shaped cooking platform in the southwest corner of the room. The longer arm abuts the west wall of the room. The exterior faces of the platform are faced with undecorated plaster. The surface is lined with cement - modern restoration. The platform is separated from latrine 6328 to the north by a partition wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6328 to the north; 6335, 6329, 6326 to the east

DESCRIPTION: Latrine located in the northwest corner of the kitchen. Separated from cooking platform 6327 to the south by a partition wall. The floor is separated from the rest of the room by a step up. Tile floor survives throughout and slopes down to the west to a drain that extends through the wall to the west. On either side of the drain abutting the west wall are two masonry supports for the seat. The form of the supports is: two low supports for a step that extends into a recess in the south wall. Plaster survives on the north, west and south walls with pink colouring on the south and west walls. Plastered moulding survives at the base of the south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6327, 6335 to the south; 6334, 6329, 6326 to the east

DESCRIPTION: On the Northwest wall, there is an arched recess for storage situated below the cooking platform used for storing supplies. A second arched recess area is located beneath the oven under the southwest part of the platform. Both recessed areas have cement floors. The surface is tiled. No rims are extant and no lips are extant. The recess located under the oven in the South corner of the room, possibly contained charcoal and wood.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cooking platform is contiguous to the oven located in the South corner (3706) and the well located to the Southeast (3707)
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo & Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: On the floor situated by the Southeast wall of the kitchen, is a large rectangular stone with a 3 sided metal barrier, covering a well. This is ideally located for a kitchen
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Situated next to the oven (3706) and cooking platform (3705) which are situated on the S.W. wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
On the east end of the north east wall, there is an indented couch niche. The top of this indentation is curved. It is plastered.

A rectangular room, north/south axis, floor obscured by lapilli throughout. Plaster survives on all four walls with red lower register, white above. At the north end of the east wall are signs of redecoration with undercoat exposed beneath the later layer of red plaster. High at the north end of the east wall are three holes for floor joists. A further hole is in the centre of the east wall and matches four holes in the west wall. In the centre of the west wall there is a window to the street with modern lintel. High in the west wall above the north wall there is a restored window with a modern lintel. In the centre of the east wall there is a door with a modern lintel and no visible threshold to mill room 45. To the north of the doorway there is a rectangular opening to the oven with modern lintel serving as a baking area to the oven. To the south there is a small square opening in the wall with modern lintel looking into the mill room. In the centre of the west wall and in the north wall there are shelves 6420. Against the west wall there is the shaft of a tufa column and in the centre of the southern half of the room there is a kneading machine 6419.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 45 to the east

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is a long narrow room which lies parallel, on a northeast/southwest axis, to the garden 12 on the north and to room 9 to the west and rooms 10 and 11 on the south. At the southwest end of the kitchen is a cooking platform or a food preparation structure. high above this structure in the wall is a circular window. The garden wall, which defines the north boundary of the room, has remnants of red painted plaster. The east wall contains doorways into the aforementioned contiguous rooms. There is no ceiling extant and the floor is covered with vegetation. In the southwest corner above the platform is a curved painted portion of the wall (niche?)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: storeroom 9 to the west, rooms 10 and 11 to the south

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is composed of rubble and mortar. Traces of plaster can be seen on the southwest face low on the western corner which abuts the northwest wall. The surface is obscured but it appears that some reconstruction cement runs around the edges. The structure is located in the north corner of the room with the longer edge streetside, abutting both northeast and northwest walls. The structure is approximately three feet high and deep and four feet long.
This is a mill with a circular platform, but not the necessary equipment.

This horticultural area (6) consists of the irregularly shaped space at the back of the temple. Modern walls limit what we can know of the actual area. The axis of the space is in a north south direction. The ground has new modern gravel and dirt, but original excavation reports (see citation) speak of grapevines and planting furrows. The back wall of the temple appears to have had two steps with a later addition of the wall above them. The bottom step today is of undecorated tufa masonry. The facing of the second step shows remains of plaster with red paint. The temple wall above shows plaster remains of white paint. The area today contains many large stone blocks that were originally part of the the temple, likely the frieze.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to space (5) to the south west back wall of the temple to the west, and to space seven to the south west.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular storeroom runs in a north south orientation. The storeroom appears to be cut out and dug below room three. At the north end of the depression there may have been stairs leading down; only one now remains. The east wall is created unevenly from the large block structure of the temple wall. The west wall is also unevenly constructed with masonry jutting out on the west wall. The south wall is narrow and flat and could possibly require further digging downward. Construction is of masonry, opus incertum on the three interior walls. Floor is composed of lapilli rubble. No roof covers this below the ground spot.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is centrally located on the east wall of room three. The location is directly to the east of the preparation feature (#3953).

DESCRIPTION: This space is a sacred space. The large rectangular space runs on a north south axis. It is accessed by an open masonry threshold, from the west. The wall construction is of large tufa blocks in the Samnite style. The floor is cocciopesto and is partially intact. The ruined floor areas are covered by lapilli. In the centre of the room is a P-shaped preparation structure (#3953) of more recent opus incertum, construction. There is no remaining plaster on any of the interior walls of this room except for a small amount on the base of the north east wall. The storeroom (#3951) is located at the east end of this room in the middle of the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to the east of room two (#3949) and to the west of the horticultural area, six (#3946).

DESCRIPTION: Reconstructed concrete cistern head square exterior, round interior, approximately 2 feet high. Located in the north west corner of kitchen room 7.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north west of feature 6439 cooking platform

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room with a north/south axis. Accessed from a corridor east running the length of the house. The dimensions and layout of the room are unclear as it is completely filled with debris. In the west wall there are two arches abutting the wall. Beneath the northern arch are the rubble remains of cooking platform 6358. Amongst the debris against the south wall is a carrot-shaped amphora and a fragmentary dolium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: corridor to the east, room 18 abuts to the south, stairs 20 abut to the north

DESCRIPTION:
This is the sales room of this establishment. The room has a SW-NE axis. One enters from the street on the S.E. side through a doorway that is almost the entire width of the space. There is a 3 block threshold of pompeian stone with a channel, cut the entire length of the 3 blocks. The condition of the room is very poor; very little plaster remains on any of the walls. The room is constructed mostly of rubble and mortar, although the doorways were composed of brick.
There is a doorway in the N.W. wall, at the Western end. A large window is in the wall, seen North of the doorway. The floors are not visible and there is no longer a ceiling. The remains of the bottom of the staircase is situated in the West corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is located N.W. of the street and adjoins the Kitchen atrium (room 2), seen to the N.W..

DESCRIPTION: Feature number 3745, abuts the Southeast wall situated at the South end, as we enter the doorway and abuts over half of the S.W. wall with a gap for a grill, situated in the center; therefore what appears to be 2 structures was actually one structure joined by a missing grlll. The entire structure was approximately 10 feet in length and approximately 2-3 feet high at it's highest point. The building material, are random bits of rubble, marble and terra cotta. The structure is in disrepair. However, traces of painted plaster can be seen on the Southwest and Southeast walls, and over the Southernmost structure, we see; indications of a shelf situated approximately 4 feet above the surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Situated contiguous to feature 3747, to the Northeast

DESCRIPTION: This platform may have been used as a low hearth, or for preparation, however, its use is not known. The feature is in disrepair and appears approximately 9 inches high on the N.W. end. The front face of the platform is badly broken and the S.E. face is crumbling. The structure abuts the N.E. wall, for approximately 2.5 feet. The material composition is rubbble.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is situated N.E. from the cooking platform, feature #3745.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room North/South axis. The floor obscured by earth and vegetation throughout. In the east wall there are three doorways to cubiculi (2) and (3) and fauces. And in the West wall there are three doorways to cubiculum (5) corridor (7) and dining room (6). All four walls are plaster but there is no visible decoration. High in the North wall there are 9 holes for floor joists. The placements survive at the North end of the East and west walls. In the Northeast corner of the room there is a cooking platform (6443).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms one, two, and three are to the East. Rooms five, six and seven are to the West.

DESCRIPTION: Standing about a metre high, the mortar appears to be embedded in the lapilli floor. It is made of waterproof concrete and two iron hardware pieces show repair of cracks on the top surface. The shape is cylindrical, tapering towards the floor. It has two protuberances across from each other that are shaped like an upside down 'U' which may have been handles. Mortar is currently filled with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to east of counter 6462

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room on a north/south axis. The preparation room is entered from room 8 to the north of corridor 4 to the east. Bricked columns and pillars delineate the entrances. There is a stone threshold to corridor 4. Floor is obscured by lapilli. Only the west wall is at full height. The east wall is knee high. At the south end of the room is located counter 6468. The room has no ceiling. A misplaced meta is located in this room. in front of the counter in the southwest corner is a red coloured tiled pad.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: dining room 8 to north, corridor 4 to the east, counter room 2 to the south

DESCRIPTION: This room has been identified as a processing room. This identification is based on its location, which is at the back of the house, and the pass-through to the over (4588) and other features. It is a rectangular space on a northeast/southwest axis. There seems to be no separation from the area identified as the stables to the northeast (16). That space (16) is paved with large black stone, but this space has no flooring. There are two stone preparation platforms (4629, 4630) along the northwest wall, perhaps the supports for a long worktable. Along the southwest wall is a narrow, long platform (4631) the length of the entire wall. The three walls are opus incertum with remains of plaster, but no paint. There is a high window in the southwest wall. Another is in the northwest wall, however, there are ceiling beam holes below it on this wall as well as on the southeast wall. No ceiling remains. The pass-through to the oven is at the eastern end of the southeastern wall. The doorway to the space is beyond the oven to the eastern corner of the space.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The space is to the northwest of the oven (4588) and to the southwest of the stable (16).

DESCRIPTION:
I entered rm. 10 from corridor 11, to the SouthWest. The room runs on a Northeast-Southwest axis, and is in a state of disrepair. It appears, that the S.E. wall incorporated at least 3 of the columns on the N.W. end of the peristyle (12), to enclose the room.

One capital, can be seen atop the 2nd column. Evidence of plaster, painted red can be found on the: N.W., N.E. and S.E. walls. The walls rise to a height of 3 meters. The floor is obscured with lapilli and vegetation. The N.E. wall appears to have been reconstructed above the height of the others. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to corridor 11 and garden 12
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leader if Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION:
This room is situated along a S.E./N.W. axis, as we enter from rooms 13 and 14, on the N.E. wall. The room has been determined to be a kitchen, supported by evidence from a bibliography, and a ledge that could have been a cooking platform in the South corner of the room, of the S.E. wall.

The room lies to the East of the primary entrance of the address. The general condition of the room is poor. The floor is obscured by debris and overgrowth. Plaster remains on the S.E. and S.W. walls and on the N.W. walls, with a small niche situated approximately 1.5 meters high on the West wall and a possible water feature with plaster in situ, on the Northwest wall, containing cocciopesto and plaster in a surround for some sort of container and an arch above, which reaches approximately 1.5 meters in height. Beam holes appear on the S.W. and N.W. walls at about 2 meters, and the ceiling is no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to rooms 15 and 14, to the East.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video team leaders are F. Capo and L. Wernick

DESCRIPTION: Situated in the North corner, is a good sized couch niche with signs of black plaster and a stenciled black border, inside the niche. Seen, slightly off center, at the floor level; inside the niche is a stone rectangle, that more carefully demarcates the niche's location.
The painting was not found. This is a negative feature sheet.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small space identified as the kitchen. It is in extremely poor condition. It's a rectangular space on a N.W./S.E. axis. There is a doorway, on the S.E. wall, that's terminating on the South side, with a column. From this low doorway, one enters the room w.here the Southwest side seems to have been only a low partition, instead of a wall. The room has plaster and a cut hole in the middle of the N.W. wall. No paint is preserved on any of the wall plaster. No features are preserved in this room. It may have had a rubble cooking platform. The room is presently filled with rubble. No flooring is visible and no ceiling is preserved
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The storage space (16) is situated to the S.W.. Space (10) is to the N.E..
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION: Remnants of a water trough remain low on the S.E. half of the mill room and run from the Southern corner adjoining the corridor to the East edge of the window. Only the outline remains, as the lip is gone, however, it apparently extended approximately one foot into the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to mill 3793, lararium 3791, and a 3792 well head, all of which are located N.W. of this feature.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno

DESCRIPTION: Square room with doorway in centre of south wall to room 30. Floor is obscured by lapilli. Plaster survives on all four walls with red lower register and white above. High at the south end of the east wall are holes for three floor joists for the floor above. Against the north wall are four large rectangular buttresses possibly supporting storage. They are plastered with red lower register and white above contiguous to the plaster on the adjoining walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 30 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Boyce 49-50 describes a lararium painting tht is no longer extant. In the centre is a blue omphalos, around which coils a huge scaly serpent with crest and beard and , on each side of it, stands a Lar clad in bright violet Phrygian cap, blue sleeveless tunic and red pallium which flies out behind his head, and holding rhyton and situla. Each Lar stands between two laurel trees. Across the top of the painting is stretched a heavy garland.

The entrance is facing west off atrium 4. No visible remains of ceiling. Floor obscured by lapilli. Traces of plaster remain on the entrance opening with red and yellow paint but it is very damaged. The wall to the north is damaged and there is some reconstruction. Plaster with traces of paint remains - a lower red dado with border, a large middle register and an upper register (?) - faded red and yellow on wall. The wall to the east is badly damaged - there are traces of red plaster on both corners at the lower level. The wall to the south shows traces of plaster in two registers, red paint and possibly the remains of a third border. 5 round post holes are high on the wall. Ancient metal clamps are in situ in the lower register and in the middle of the wall to the west - badly damaged traces of plaster and red paint. Facing wall to the the left is a recessed area with a modern wooden lintel. There are traces of plaster with yellow and red paint and an opening at window level to the adjacent room 7.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: entrance on the west goes directly to atrium 7

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room east /west axis. All four walls are poorly preserved with no traces of decoration and has modern restoration. Floor is obscured by lapilli and rubble. At the east end of the south wall there is a doorway with a stone stepped threshold. At the north end of the east wall there is a doorway with a stone stepped threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 3 is to the east and room 8 is to the south

DESCRIPTION: one enters dining room 5 from a door on the NE wall. The doorway has modern supports and is in bad condition. Plaster remains on both sides of the doorway as we enter into the room. The floor, though obscured, appears to be coccio pesto. Wall paintings have been removed from the center of the SE, SW,and NW walls. The painting style is indiscernable, however, may have 3rd or 4th according to traces on the NW wall. It appears there were red panels above a low dado which looks black or white. There are two windows inthe room, each high and supported with wood and metal inserts. One is on the SW and the other on the SE wall. There is a ledge just over the windows which continues the full length of each wall which would indicate a second floor. Additionally, eight joist holes high on the NE wall support a second storey idea as well as another higher window above those. No ceiling is extant. There are three holes spaced vertically on the SE wall aligned with the southern most portion of the window on the SE wall, and on the western most border of the window above is one whole of the same height and shape on the SW wall. It is an after thought but should be noted that each of the aforementioned windows angle to let light into the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to fore room 4 to the NE.

DESCRIPTION: This is the kitchen. The room is aligned on a northeast/southwest axis. It is a narrow rectangular room with an entrance from the front shop at the west. This entrance is a very low doorway at the south corner of the west wall. There is a second low doorway in the north wall. There are windows in the north and west walls (one in each wall) In the west corner of the room is feature 3253, a cooking platform. The flooring is not visible. The walls are in a poor state of preservation but extant to the height of two storeys. Only the west and south walls preserve plaster. There is no roof. There are two tall arched niches in the south wall, west end. These are filled with ceramic tile and mortar with the insertion of ceramic pipes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a latrine 9 at the east side of the room separated by a stone and ashlar wall. A shopfront 11 is to the west. An atrium (room 3 of House 7) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform runs along a northwest/southeast axis and fills the entire wall on the northeast end of the room. The platform is approximately 40 cm high and 50 cm deep. The surface is obscured by moss and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: dolium 3231 sits in situ on the north corner of cooking platform 3229. Latrine 3230 is west/southwest

DESCRIPTION: Situated in the north corner of room 4 on top of cooking platform 3229 between the northwest and northeast walls are the remains of a dolium which is small and made of terracotta. The shape appears to be cylindrical but only fragments remain. The height is indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform 3229 beneath. A latrine 3230 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is an L-shaped stone preparation platform. It is preserved only to a very low height. It is located in the north and east walls and is in very poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: preparation platform 3283 lies to the west

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 5 as a potential dining room in this bakery 5-4-1. There is a wide opening towards passageways 10 and 13, directly opening to horticultural area 11, which would have given diners a nice view. The space is rectangular, on a northwest/southwest axis. This was a very old structure in the city, with walls of opus incertum, heavily restored. A drain pipe visible in the southwest wall indicates that there was an upper floor above. Modern reconstruction suggests a large window on the southwest wall originally existed opening to the street outside. the walls are undecorated and the floor is gravel and weeds. The southwest end of this space has two doorways, one with stairs to the floor above, and one leading to storage room 6(4599.)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of storage room 4599, to the southwest of horticultural area 11 and passageways 13 and 10 and to the northwest of kitchen 4.

DESCRIPTION: This hearth in atrium 2 is square and approximately one metre by one metre and 30 cm high. It is located about 40 cm from the entrance to room 7 and one metre from the southeastern corner of the atrium. It is made of volcanic rock and plaster remains on the surface. Itabuts the east wall.

This is a storage feature, (cella penaria). It is comprised of rubble construction, about 4 ft. in height. It has a flat surface, at the top. The sides and front are in poor condition. The arched interior has remains of plaster facing. This opens to the N.E. and it occupies the Western most corner of the house. Generally, it is in fair to poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is the Western most corner of the house. It faces the partition to room 9. A latrine is located on the S.W. wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION: This is a narrow room on an east/west axis. Entered from the west from room 8. The room is divided in half by a masonry arch. The doorway is a step up from the peristyle, with a concrete lintel indicating restoration. There is no ceiling. Floor today is covered in dirt but may have been tiled. Entering the room we see a concrete base for a cistern. Immediately to the right in the southwest corner is latrine 6455. Above the latrine and door on the west wall is evidence of a past roof line (a channel with inserts cut out of the masonry) On the northwest end of the wall, below the channel is a square post hole. No plaster remains. The south wall is heavily reconstructed, with two post holes on each side of the dividing arch. On the east wall is located cooking platform 6454 with a small square window above. The north wall contains three post holes, two to the west and one to the east of the arch. The easternmost hole is above the cooking platform. There is probably one more hole next to the arch obscured by modern reconstruction. Wall has some faded pinkish painted plaster remaining. On the north and south walls close to the cooking platform are four or five small round holes which may have held shelves or hooks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 8 to the west

DESCRIPTION: north end of the east wall contains a figure of a partially clothed nymph. In her left hand she is holding a branch with cherries. In her right hand a platter/bowl containing cherries.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: north east corner

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform lies at the west end of the kitchen and consists of two separate structures which abut the west and south corners of the kitchen. The wall which is in between shows evidence of plaster painted red in antiquity as does the wall behind the western structure. The floor plan indicates that the two were connected in a U shape, however these two appear to be individual. The structure is in disrepair, each side consisting of a pile of stones with no visible surface and at their highest points about 50 cm. Each pile runs along a northeast/southwest axis on the west side of the room.
Small shallow plastered kneading basin in the top of a masonry plastered support contiguous with basin 6414 to the south. The basin now contains part of a catillus of a no longer in situ mill.

Circular beehive oven. Well preserved tiled floor. Brick interior face preserved throughout with tiled superstructure. Basalt stoke hole. In front of the oven there is a basalt and tiled platform with openings to the east and west. In front of the platform is the arched facade to the oven facing south to the mill room. Traces of a strip of iron on the basalt stone in front of the stokehole.

We nter this dining garden from a tablinum 7 which is open. The garden is a rectangle. Immediately to the west wall is a stairway and a low entrance to a storage room 3849 with a low door to a good sized storage area under the stairs. This west wall also shows two cubicula. Eschebach reports that there was a large animal painting on the south wall. There is also a very high lararium or lamp holding area on this wall. It is arched and has a shelf. The dining grden is paved with some opus sectile appearing. The garden is contained by a low wall with four columns showing red plaster at the bottom. Within this wall is a large masonry summer triclinium 3842. We see a round table with six arched niches at the base. The lectus immus has an extension that Mau says is for children, but could also be a miniature serving platform. Within the low wall and around the triclinium is pounded mud. This dining garden is certainly open to the sky. The east wall shows some red plaster on the lowest level, and the entrance to the kitchen is also on this wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: tablinum 7 to the north, kitchen 10 to the east, storage room 17 to the west

DESCRIPTION: One enters the kitchen from the northwest from an andron 7 or from the street entrance doorway on the northeast (9.5.13). The space is delineated on the northwest and southeast by remnants of walls or partitions and the edge of the street entrance. Surrounding walls extend to second storey height. Evidence of some plaster remains above the cooking platform which abuts approximately half of the northwest wall and half of the northeast wall. The kitchen platform is about two and a half feet from the ground and is poorly preserved, but intact. There is no ceiling extant. The floor is covered with vegetation and debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 13 to the west, room 12 to the south, room 9 to the north

DESCRIPTION: On the center of the southwest wall of kitchen[4595], we see masonry remains at floor level. They are immediately adjacent to the short wall of the latrine(4595), probably on its longer side and adjacent to the southwest wall on its shorter side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: [Contiguous to feature...] latrine 4595.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this bakery from door (4). There are stones demarcating the entrance from a wide sidewalk of mud and lapilli. The rectangular shop room with walls to a second floor. On the north wall is a rectangular window and on the lower zone is some orange plaster. The east wall also has orange plaster on the lower zone. The south wall has some remaining orange plaster and a door in the northwest corner leading to the mill room (3861). The floor is covered by lapilli. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Street, and mill room (3861) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We enter dining room4 from the atrium to the southwest. The room is square and is north of the street entrance. An outline of an old threshold remains and the floor appears to have been cement with cocciopesto material mixed. The painting in the room has a low white or black dado which contains some stencilled patterns in gold - with a bird on the northwesternmost section. Alternating large panels (possibly fourth style) of red and yellow occur on the northwest, northeast and southeast walls, separated by white portions which appear to have features of architectural motifs which extend from lower through middle to top registers. The moulding, which is decorated with dart and thistle, exists in fragments on all three walls about two feet above the highest register. The lintel is modern and concrete. Six large square beam holes are high on the northwest and southeast walls. Plaster survives to a second storey height on northeast and southeast. No ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 to the south

DESCRIPTION: A squarish room with an east/west axis. Room is entered from salesroom 1 to the east and provides access to cubiculum 3 to the west. There is a plastered lararium with a terracotta shelf on the west wall. On the southwest corner of the west wall red plaster trace remains. North wall is solid masonry. The east wall is reconstructed to waist height with a stone threshold for the doorway and a mound of stacked tiles which could be the remains of a staircase to the upper floor or the remains of a hearth (per Eschebach). South wall is reconstructed masonry. West wall has its own step up to the cubiculum. Floor is obscured by lapilli. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a salesroom 1, located to the East, and cubiculum 3 to the West

DESCRIPTION: This is a preparation room. It is a rectangular space on a north east/ south west axis. There are 2 doorways on the north east wall. One enters this room from the atrium just to the west of entrance 16. Evidence for storage and preparation remain in this room including a dolium and a square cutting in the south corner of the room. The room is in poor condition. The flooring is not visible. No ceiling remains. There is some plaster on the south east wall. There are several cuttings in the north west wall going horizontally at about five feet as well as three others in the north corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the south west of entrance 16 it is directly south east of the cubliculum (bordello) (room 25).

DESCRIPTION: This house is incomplete. This description is incomplete. The painting decorates the eastern wall of lararium in space 23.

We walk through corridor 8 and turn south into a corridor to the furthest triclinium. We enter via a lava threshold into a good sized dining room. This dining room has a broad door overlooking the colonnaded garden. Earlier reports identify a window on the south wall - no longer extant. On the north wall is a good sized bench niche. The floor is modern lapilli. On the north wall is a narrow doorway to the adjoining dining room 3280. The separating wall is just waist high. On all of the walls are small patches of cement and plaster and some red and yellow paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: dining room 3288 to the north, garden 11 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is the kitchen. Its alignment is east/west. One enters from the andron 8 through a door in the south wall at the southwest corner of the room. There are two preparation platforms - 3283 is in the northwest corner, platform 3284 is along the full length of the eastern wall. The stone walls have no plaster remaining. The floor is not visible. the walls are preserved only to a low height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: andron 8 to the south,

DESCRIPTION: Dining room is on an east-west axis, with the door opening off of tablinum (7) to the south. There is no ceiling. Floor is lapilli with no sign of extant threshold in the doorway. Room is identified as a dining room by its large size and the fact that it has two windows, one looking at at the atrium, one looking at the garden behind. Looking at the north wall, one finds remnants of red and white plaster. In the middle of the north wall there is also evidence of a ceiling cornice molding in white. Wall is heavily reconstructed, with two holes above plaster level which could have held joists for an upper story. Turning right and facing the east wall, again heavily reconstructed, you can see just a trace of the white cornice molding at ceiling height. In the southeast corner of the room, still on the east wall, is a very small square window with a reconstructed lintel. Directly below the window is the best preserved plaster in the room, showing a bright red lower register with a light pink plaster above. The south wall, which contains the door, is ruin and reconstruction. The west wall is the same.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Tablinum (7) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We climb two steps from the atrium 3 to a small corridor 4. To the east are the remains of a garden wall fountain with water. To the west is a cubiculum 5. To the north is a medium sized doorway to a dining room. One enters the room from a narrow doorway in the south corner of the west wall. The floor is now mud but at the entrance is a concrete mixture. This is a typical Roman square room. There are walls to a modern ceiling and a concrete lintel. On the southeast wall is a large window opening to the garden topped with a concrete lintel. A portion of this room can be seen from the entrance. The window is set low and is high and emphasizes the garden view. All four walls show evidence of third style painting - yellow, white and red with a red dado indicating a re-design at some point. No features are evident in this room. Remnants of a corner cornice and a cornice between the window and the door.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: garden 7 and fountain 8 are to the east, cubiculum to the west

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room with a north/south axis. Originally a single room with 18 but subsequently separated by a partition wall (west) containing doorway to 18. Doorway in the south wall to kitchen 16 with stone step threshold and a modern lintel. Plaster survives on the east wall and the northeast corner where it is pink in colour. Plastered moulding survives at the base of the north wall at its junction with the west wall. High in the north wall between rooms 17 and 18 there is a window to the garden with a modern lintel. At the top of the wall there is a possible window in the second storey. At the east end of the north wall there is preparation platform 6331. Floor is obscured by lapilli throughout.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 18 to the west; room 16 to the south

DESCRIPTION: This square mill room has a typical bakery floor around the rubble bases of basalt stones. Away from the bases, the floor is pounded mud and lapilli. On the north walls is the entrance to sales room (1). The east wall is built to the second floor. The west wall shows three large piers. The first large opening leads to preparation room (9), the second to hallway four and the third is a small wall and a space for storing grain. Behind the west wall rises to a second floor and shows little plaster. The rubble blocks are an appropriate size for the mill bases, so there is probably little reconstruction. At the south opening is a complete mill but the catillus is probably not original to this meta. On the west wall we see a broken catillus and a carved basin.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Sales room (1) to the north, Preparation room (9) to the southeast, Hallway (4) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a conical hand quern. The rim is partially preserved. Possibly not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6329, 6326 to the north; 6328, 6327, 6335 to the west

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a fragment of a rotary hand mill. Possibly not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6334,6329,6326 to the east; 6327 to the west; 6328 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This large outdoor triclinium, with a table in the middle is medius 4.10 m; immus 3.86 m; summus 3.12 m. It is a mixture of stones and brick as is the table

This is a miniature beehive oven located on the Southwest portion of platform 3705, located in the kitchen. It has a square opening, to the kitchen. It is constructed of mortar and cut stone slabs. It is constructed of mortar and cut stone slabs. The base is cut stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a platform, extending from this oven (3706), situated along the Northwest wall. There is a stone slab, covering a well (3707) located immediately Southwest of this oven.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leaders are Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: A toilet situated on the Northwest wall is adjacent to a large cooking platform. A ceramic, vertical pipe system is visible, running from floor 2 to floor 1. The drain to the street is situated below the pipe. The ceramic fill, supports the toilet seat for two persons.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The toilet is contiguous with the cooking platform (3705)
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo & Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION:
This house iso not completed. This space has been identified as a storeroom at front of the "House of C. Vibi". This space, which is a stairwell, was clearly used as a storage space as well. This identification is based on remains of two large dolia in situ (4518 and 4519). The space is almost a square. The entrance door is in the center of the northeast wall. This is a high doorway of brick. The walls behind the northeast wall are of opus incertum, with tuff and also large cut stones in courses by the stairway. The south side of the southeast wall is mixed with alternating courses of brick and cut stone. The stone staircase rises to the south along the southeast wall. There is a small landing and it would have continued to the south through an opening into the wall to the adjacent room. The walls are preserved beyond the beam holes to the second floor and continue to rise on the northeast/southeast and southwest sides. No floor or threshold are visible. One dolium is located in the northeast corner of room (4519) and a dolium (4518) stands to the northwest of the stairway.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The storeroom is to the southwest of the atrium and to the southeast of dining room 11.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room, north/south axis. Floor obscured by lapilli and earth. The south wall consists of a wide open doorway to the street to the south with fragmentary stone threshold. In the centre of the west wall is a wide doorway to the street to the west with a fragmentary stone threshold. At the north end of the wets wall there is a doorway with a stone stepped threshold which Eschebach says accessed stairs to the floor above. At the west end of the north wall a terracotta downpipe is embedded into the wall and drains out through a square hole at the base of the wall. In the west wall there are two holes for shelves. Undecorated plaster is on the north wall and in the southeast and southwest walls. Several small holes for 3 to 4 sets of shelves are located along the east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 3 to the north

DESCRIPTION: The 4th style painting decoration of this room includes large yellow panels in the central zone. Above this wall, the painting depicts open spaces with figures enclosed in delicately framed rectangles. 2 of these figures flank the feature which is a depiction of a large lobster against a blue background. It is located on the S.E. wall, situated just below the window.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick and Fran Capo.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that Room 82 is the western most in a series of three processing rooms just outside the pool and residential area. The room is rectangular, no excavated doorway is visible. The room is only partially excavated, but appears to contain one very large basin partially excavated in the floor of eastern portion of the room. Also at the northeastern corner, appearing to be inside the large basin, is a smaller, square basin, also with cement walls. Some traces of plaster remains on the walls, but it is impossible to say how it was decorated. No roof remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room: Situated immediately to the west of Room 83 and to the north of Room 81. No unexcavated access exists.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 83 as part of the production area of the villa. We have determined that the last usage of room 83 was a processing room. Set off from the residential area of the villa there is a series of three rooms, this is the middle one, partially excavated. This room is narrow and rectangular, with traces of painted plaster that appear to be of the "zebra striped" pattern. The floor is clay, with a doorway and threshold off of passageway 81. The floor is excavated in a slope to the west and exits through a low arch into a possible drain into room 84. Plaster remains on the inside of the arch indicate its existence pre-excavation. Although modern holes are cut into the east and west walls, these do not appear to have existed in antiquity. Visible brickwork on the south wall suggests a window, mid-wall height, currently looking at the unexcavated area. We believe that this room is the most feasible of these excavated rooms to contain the torcularium (olive oil press), as suggested by Jashemski. No ceiling exists.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opens to north of passageway 81.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is on a north south axis. We have determined that room 32 - 4062 is a kitchen. This identification is based on the fact that this room has a very low doorway and is in the part of the house with consistently low doorways. We see there is a food and drink feature which is an L-Shaped cooking platform (4064) which has no recessed-to-the-floor storage nor tile surface. The characteristics that identify this room as a kitchen is that the square room contains an L-shaped cooking platform that is in the east and south wall that covers a third of the room. There is no modern ceiling and it could have been unroofed earlier. The walls are without paint. The floor is pounded earth. There are no windows. There is a recessed area in the north west corner, it's function undetermined.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Continguous to a possible small recessed latrine or a preparation room (31-4063) and corridor (29).

DESCRIPTION: In the domestic Villa of Diomedes, we have identified room 46 as used for dining. Its location on the upper level of the villa with a wide opening looking west, perhaps to the sea, indicates that usage. The room is on an east-west axis. The entire south end is open. There is also a very small narrow doorway in the southwest corner of the south wall opening to an adjacent dining room(36). The walls are of opus incertum and were frescoed. Some restoration occurred in 1977 on the south, east, and west walls. As to decoration of the walls, all that remains today is some red-tinted plaster. The floor was cocciopesto, but very little remains. No ceiling remains. There is also no remaining threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south is dining room 36. To the west is terrace 44.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Villa of Diomedes as a domestic structure and room 22 (frigidarium) is part of the personal bath complex. The area is triangular in shape and contains a large rectangular tub (open to the sky) and a colonnaded walkway running north and east with six columns. The area inside the columns would be open to the sky. Two high large square recesses in the northeast wall suggest that a portico or awnings may have covered the tub. The reason we are identifying this room in this database is the presence of a cooking platform in the northernmost corner of the walkway around the tub. The room was brightly painted. The floor appears to have been black and white mosaic. Opening off the triangular frigidarium are four doorways: one leading to the remaining rooms of the bath complex, one leading to the kitchen, one to a dining room, and one off the peristyle. The main entrance to the frigidarium is in the south corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen room 24 is to the east. Bath complex 25,26,27 is to the southeast. Dining room 28 is to the south and peristyle 21 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Tucked into the dead-end northwestern corner of the colonnaded walkway surrounding the frigidarium tub is a cooking platform. The platform is created of brick masonry and is fitted up against walls to the north and west. The platform stands a little lower than 68 centimeters high and has a horizontal triangular-shaped opening for storage underneath. The top of the cooking platform is terra cotta tile. The narrow northwest end of the platform top has a masonry support in an inverted U-shape built up on it. The front of the cooking platform appears to have had a smooth masonry edging (a small portion remains). The mosaic tile floor continues underneath and the frescoed walls appear to have been in place before the cooking platform was constructed.

The painting appears to be 1.5 meters from the ground. It is a square fresco with two men, the man closer to the eastern side is dressed in yellow with a blue cloak and appears to be holding a cup. The man in the brown tunic appears to be holding some type of drinking vessel. This fresco is located on the southeast wall, with a red border and a white background.

This is a square fresco, situated approximately 1 1/2 meters off the ground. It is located on the southwest wall, northern side of the entrance. There is a red border with a white background. There appears to be four people, one in blue with a drinking cup. The painting is damaged.

We have identified this room 3 as a dining room. We have identified this feature (6520) as an Olive Crusher [trapetum]. The Trapetum is located in the centre of the room and appears to have been placed by early excavators. The general condition of the feature is good. There does not appear to be any restoration, neither ancient nor modern. The crusher/press is circular and has an approximate diameter of 1.5 metres. There is a base with a platform (circular) with metal rod in sit at the centre. There are 2 half-dome circular presses with a square space at the centre for a beam to crush the olives as it rolls around the circular basin.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature sits in the centre of room 3 (6518)

DESCRIPTION:
This is an L-shaped counter, with one side facing the street. The "L" of the L-shaped counter is positioned with a southwest side (which faces the street) and a southeast side (facing a side interior wall of the shop). The front side of the counter facing the street has a marble floor molding with cut marble inlaid above. At the south corner of the L, the counter facing the street protrudes slightly before recessing to the southeast side of the counter. A painted decoration appears on the front of the southeast side. The northeast end of the counter today is undecorated but appears to have been previously plastered.

The inside of the L is masonry covered with plaster.

The top surface of the counter is pieced marble. There are three holes along the long southeast countertop of the L. In the center hole some terra cotta is visible. These are unusually narrow as they appear to fit an amphora rather than a dolium.

At the west corner of the counter there is a series of at least six marble-covered display shelves that are the width of the counter itself. The rise of these stepped shelves creates a partial arch, open below, creating a storage area.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north of cooking platform 6705.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a house. We have determined that the last usage of room 5 was as a dining room. This identification is based upon room size, evidence of room decoration, and the entrance off the atrium (room 3). The room is on a northeast -southwest axis and is entered from the south corner from atrium 3. No threshold remains in the doorway. The doorway is wide with plaster remaining on its east jamb. Midway up there are two large circular openings indicating door attachment. The southwest jamb of the doorway is of opus testaceum construction. The remainder of the southeast wall shows evidence of painted plaster with a red dado running along the bottom. The southwest wall also has painted plaster remains. At mid-wall height directly to the west of the doorway is a small square window which appears to have been a doorway in antiquity. The window directly abuts caupona VI.10.1 suggesting the two properties were connected at one time. In the northwest corner of the room is a small square masonry platform (feature 6512). The remaining two walls, the northwest and northeast, both contain decorated plaster remnants. Opus incertum construction between large tufa pillars suggest the room may have been open to these sides at one point in its history.Floor is lapilli and no ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the room opens to the south/southeast from atrium 3

DESCRIPTION: A circular cistern lined with opus signinum sits in the northern corner of the impluvium basin [4187]. The cistern is full of debris and is capped with a tufa puteal. It was originally a kneading machine or basin. Holes survive in the northwest, southeast, and west faces. The lip of the cistern rests directly on the earlier opus signinum pavement of the atrium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Basin 4187 and prep table 4180 are to the south. Mill 4184 is to the north. Mill 4183 and lararium 4185 are to the west. Mill 4182 is to the southwest. Oven 4188 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The room is unexcavated but clearly visible are pieces of amphora. There is one amphora fairly intact and one dolium fairly intact.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
They are lying facing the west wall on/within the eruption material.
In the southern corner of the kitchen (4047).

DESCRIPTION: The small, low rectangular platform is of block masonry construction. It is suggested in some sources (Eschebach) that it may have been a hearth but no evidence of a cooking surface remains today. It is attached to the counter at the east inside corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the southwest/west is counter 6515

DESCRIPTION: We have identified VI.10.3 as a shop house structure. We have determined that the last usage of this room (6517) is a dining room. This identification is based on past research. The entire room appears to be on a lower level. It is based on the northeast corner of the house at the back. There is a possible entrance on the southwest corner that enters into a possible garden on the southwest side of the room. There is a possible threshold and stone door jamb. There is no evidence of a step into the room from the garden. There is a drop of approximately 1 m. from the garden to the floor of the dining room. The southwest wall is badly damaged with a possible threshold to the southwest corner. There is no evidence of a floor - today it is rubble. To the southern side of the southwest wall there is a possible pilaster opening to the garden. This wall appears to have been filled in during antiquity. On the southern corner of the southwest wall at about 2.5 m. above the floor is a post hole that is matched by another possible post hole at the same height on the northeast wall. The northwest wall is reconstructed and patched up in modern times. There is a round hole at about one third of the way from the southwest corner (approximately 2 m. above the floor). There may be small traces of stucco. On the northern side of this wall is a narrow arched entrance to an apparent corridor or storage room. The door is 2.5 m. above the threshold, which is higher than the sloping floor. On the northeast wall there is a large entrance which is a step up from the street. To the south of the entrance is a small window whose ledge is approximately 3 m. above the sloping floor. At approximately a half metre to the east and below the window is what appears to be a post hole. There is modern reconstruction but no apparent stucco. The southeast wall is reconstructed with concrete with some possible traces of painting and stucco. To the eastern side there are three large post holes at approximately 4 m. On the western corner of this wall there is one single round post hole at approximately 4 m. The ceiling is not extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room apparently opens to the garden on the southwest wall. On the northeast wall it pens to the street at VI.10.18. On the northeast corner it opens to a storage area or corridor

DESCRIPTION:
This is House of the Geometric Mosaic in the so called complex of Championnet. This is identified as a double house (entrances 14,16) and part of the complex referred to by Eschebach as the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14-20,. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. This room (9) has been identified as a prep room due to its location adjacent to the kitchen (10). We enter this small room (9) from a wide entrance off the corridor (14) from the kitchen (10), The floor is covered by grey gravel obscured by vegetation. The three walls are brick and opus incertum and appear heavily reconstructed. There is no plaster remaining. There is no ceiling extant.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This prep room (9) is to the northeast of kitchen (10) and to the northwest of corridor (14).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified house 6-10-6 as domestic and we have determined that room number 15 is a dining room. The room is located immediately to the southwest of a large garden, contains a large doorway opening to that garden and had elaborate pointed surfaces. The doorway is along the northeast wall and has a wide stone threshold. Walls on either side of the doorway are of a brick and stone construction in an alternating pattern. On the north corner wall there is a square posthole midway up the wall. The remaining three walls, the northwest, southwest, and southeast are all of opus incertum construction with traces of pointed plaster. The northeast wall appears to have had a high window opening. Painting on the southwest wall shows evidence of the First Style, and the southeast wall has two very high postholes indicating an upper story, and two lower postholes at the midpoint. There is a low doorway in the east corner of that wall. The floor is red cocctopesto. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Room 14 is to the southeast and peristyle garden is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION:
From the street we enter the atrium Tuscan style displuviate through a long vestibulum facing northwest. As we look into the atrium, which runs along a northwest/southeast axis, we see an impluvium in disrepair with a broken marble cistern cover on the northwest side. The room is rectangular. The general condition of the room is poor, however some plaster remains on all walls. In the east corner of the room is a lararium which is highly decorated. There is evidence of red paint on the wall with a white lower register on all the walls. Over the lararium the paint is well preserved in third style displaying reds and yellows with intricate stenciling in gold and possibly a bird atop a standard. Plaster symbolizing faux columns is extant next to the entrances to the adjoining rooms on the northwest and southeast.
The ceiling is high but indeterminate. The floor is covered with lapilli. There are doorways on all walls except the southwest wall which adjoins the neighboring property. High on the northeast wall near the east corner appears to be small window into a small dining room (9). There is a large window on the north end of the northeast wall which allows a view into the atrium from the dining room (7).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northeast is room (7), (8) and (9); northwest (3) and (4); southeast (1).

DESCRIPTION: This is a square fresco approximately 1.5 meters from the ground. There is tavern activity, possibly gaming, with a table and a man in red with a blue cloak possibly holding a drinking vessel. There are four men around a table. It is located on the southeast wall with a red border and a white background.

This painting is on the north west wall on the eastern side of the entrance at VI.10.19. The fresco is 1.5 meters off the ground with a red border and a white background. Two figures are shown standing. A man in a brown tunic is pouring a drink with his left hand into a cup held by a man with a yellow tunic, possibly a blue cloak and spear. The serving man is holding what appears to be keys in his right hand

This painting is on the northwest wall, eastern side of the entrance (VI.10.19). The fresco is 1.5 meters off the ground, with a red border and white background. It is badly damaged, and appears to be two donkeys with a wine cart.

This tomb (number 8) is located on the south side of the Via delle Tombe (entrance 23). It has been identified as the tomb of Gn. Vibrious Saturninus. This is classified as a triclinium tomb. It is a rectangular enclosure entered up a very large step to a marble lintel before one steps up to the level of the enclosure. The entrance is situated at the center of the north wall. The enclosure walls are constructed of opus caementicium with the lower levels preserving opus reticulatum of yellow stones. The walls would have been with plaster which is preserved best on the west corner of the northern wall. Traces of plaster are also visible in the southwest corner and northeast corners. Although the interior space is overgrown with weeds, the three triclinia are still evident (4656). The north wall raises to a gabled center with considerable reconstruction. The exterior facade was primarily opus reticulatum. There is a niche in the center of the pediment containing a replica inscription. The inscription is CIL X 1033. Bibliography: V. Campbell pg. 174-175
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This tomb is directly to the west of tomb 7 (entrance 22). It is along the south side of the Via delle Tumbe.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this contains a feature that is an L shaped counter. It is a Food and Drink shop. It has a good sized L shaped counter. The foundation base is rubble and modern cement. There is a marker indicating this. It was reshaped , reconstructed in 1985. The short end of the L faces the street. There are traces of red plaster on the bricked peirs. This portion of the counter is faced with reused marble. The long side of the L sits on, what appears to be remains of a rectangular hearth. The floor of the heart contains shaped and cut tiles. The L shaped counter is placed on the S.W. wall.

It is determined, the large room to the back of the counter room is a large open space, and therefore seems to be where food would be eaten rather than being an area for storage and food space. The room is L shaped and runs on a S.E./N.W. axis, with the bottom of the L turning to the N.E., on the N.W. end of the room.

The room is reached by stepping up on a threshold, situated on the S.E. end of the room. A wall would have extended for approximately a quarter of the space from the S.W. side, to the step. The long S.W. wall contains slight occasional traces of plaster. Situated, directly behind the small wall, on the S.W. side, the remains of a ceramic pipe descends through the wall from the floor above. Through discussion, it was considered; a possibility of the pipe leading to a latrine, but this was not confirmed by the available evidence.

Situated, high toward the top of the wall are post holes indicating an upper story was present. A round hole seen half way up the wall may have indicated something was attached. For the next item, there was a door that was blocked off in antiquity. All walls are constructed of opus incertum.

Moving to the N.W. wall, it appears to be closed off from the property, situated behind in antiquity. Scattered bits of plaster remain, but nothing that can provide a clear idea of how the room was decorated. To the N.E., we have the stepped wall that provides the bottom portion of the L.

The furthest portion to the N.E., is simple opus incertim, while the S.E. shows some old block construction, also. As the wall rejoins the long portion of the L, there is an indentation for a well (3982) and a lararium ( ). The lararium is situated directly to the N.E., as you enter from the steps and had a rectangular construction with a canted roof, comprised of a 30 degree angle leading up from the N.E. to the East. The back of the shrine is made of terracotta and the picture that had originally been on it, has been cut out. The floor is composed of rubber lapilli, with no roof present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is situated to the N.W. of the counter room (1).

DESCRIPTION: Inside processing room 82 in the northeast corner is a small square basin inset into the floor of a larger basin. This basin is rimmed with concrete and the depth is not excavated. The rim of the basin rises slightly over what is the excavated level of dirt.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the northwest corner of the basin 4038.

DESCRIPTION: The feature in this room is a bench/couch niche. This feature is located on the southeast wall and takes up the eastern half of the wall It is large, tall, and high. The red stripes on a beige background are apparent. The dado is black, unlike the rest of the room where it is white. The indentation for the bench is deep. It appears to be square in shape rather than curved.
This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined this feature 4690 as a latrine in preparation room 21. The latrine itself is not visible as it is overgrown.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: located in room 21 in south-east corner

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this room as a dining room due to its size and location This is a large, rectangular space with an east to west axis. the room is almost square, with an opening niche along the southeast end of the south wall. There is no ceiling preserved and the upper walls are heavily reconstructed.The walls all have preserved plaster revealing a high black dado and solid cream-colored walls situated above the black dado. Any fresco decoration on this cream surface has either perished or was never completed. This matches the circumstances of the other surrounding rooms, situated south. The floor is mosaic. It reveals a white field with a black border. There is a wide doorway at the center of the east wall with a view out pass a hallway to the portico and pool. This room has a wide marble threshold. There is a smaller door in the entrance niche at the southeast corner of the south wall. This has a marble threshold. This doorway passes through to another square room which is to the east of Room 89. There is a large square window centered in the west wall with a view to the large garden to the north of this villa entrances, southwest of the window. The overall condition of this room is fair.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room: This room is to the east of the front gardens to the north of the villa's main entrance. There is a corridor to the east of this room.

DESCRIPTION:
Extending in a westward direction from the northeast corner of the processing room is a partial cement border of a water basin. The basin itself is currently filled with dirt. But the floor below to the west is about thirty centimeters down. The basin contains a second basin (our feature number 4037) directly inside its north east corner.
As this area is not fully excavated we cannot tell the full dimensions of the basin.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Other features, the floor below etc., surround the basin 4073

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 8 as a dining room based upon its large door opening to a colonnaded peristyle in its south east wall. The room is on a north west, south east axis and is brightly painted with cream based Forth Style decoration. The central paintings in almost all panels have been removed. Two small rectangular panels on both sides of the southeast door remain. One is of a sacro-idyllic landscape but the other is of a painting of fish (our feature 4051). The dado is painted bright red with floral and animal paintings. Some volcanic material still remains in the room. The floor is clay with marble inserts and the visible threshold is marble with cuts for door hardware. A second much smaller door is in the east corner of the northeast wall. No evidence of the ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The feature is located to the northwest of peristyle 12 and to the southwest of Room 6.

DESCRIPTION: In the southwest corner of the room on top of one quarter of the cooking platform [4072] is a small, well-preserved, beehive oven. The top surface could also be used for cooking.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cooking platform is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the Villa of Diomedes as a domestic villa and we are identifying Area 21 as a front peristyle with a walkway around it. This peristyle opens directly off the street to the north. It is situated on a northeast-southwest axis. The central portion of the peristyle is enclosed by 14 columns, red below and white above and, per Jashemski, would have been a decorative garden with a fountain. Various dining rooms, bath complex, cubicula, and tablinum open off this peristyle. We are identifying this peristyle by the location of a food and drink painting [4070] now found in the Naples Archaeological Museum. The walls were painted frescoes but no trace of painted decoration remains today except for some red and yellow patches. The peristyle was open to the sky and the walkway today is covered with grass. There are stairs leading to the subterranean level located in the north corner of the peristyle. A wide room [tablinum] leading to a series of dining rooms is located on the south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle is to the south of doorway 24, to the north of tablinum room 40, with a series of other rooms opening on each side.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 9-7-20 as a house. We have determined that the last usage of this room 25-4065 is as a dining room. The identification is based on the location of this room looking out on the atrium. This is a good size N-S-E-W rectangular room with large patches of painted walls on all 4 walls. The dominant color is beige-white with red stripes. There is minimal detail to the painted walls. The floor is pounded earth. There is no ancient ceiling but there is a modern cover over most of the room. There is a large rectangular window in the north wall which overlooks a possible garden (29). The doorway is located in the southwest corner of the wall, and is of moderate height. Above there is an indication of a higher lintel. The east wall centrally divided by the window shows an indication for a good size dining room bench. This niche is painted in beige, red, and white.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the north of an atrium (26).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified VI.10.6, the House of Pomponius as a house. We have determined the last usage of this room (5) as an atrium (6523). The identification of this feature as a well is determined by its shape, depth, and proximity to the impluvium. The well is positioned on the east corner of the southeast edge of the impluvium. The well is oval shaped. The well is approximately 2.5 meters long x 2.0 meters wide. This is edged and lined by large rectangular masonry rock. There are traces of concrete lining. At 2.5 meters down there appears to be a channel which could connect to the impluvium on the northwest edge. The well appears to be six meters deep. There is a large rectangular piece, possibly from a wall, which is sitting at the bottom of the well.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is located in the east side of the atrium. It is southeast of the impluvium, with possible drainage through a channel from the impluvium.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is identified as a lararium in the atrium of the Tavern of Tertius. This is a shallow, square niche with a marble bottom. Painted plaster is visible on the sides and upper surface of the niche with red paint on cream paint. This lararium is associated with the cooking platform [3-4103] which is nearby in the western corner of the space. This lararium, about two meters off the floor, is on the southwestern wall, and is at the same level as the small window in the west corner. Below the marble bottom of the niche can be seen remains of a shelf protruding front the wall. This section of the wall has plaster preserved around the lararium.
