Red paint is visible beneath the protruding shelf.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This lararium is located near the western corner of the space, near the cooking platform [3-4103].

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a tavern and this long room as a latrine room. There is evidence of a latrine which is a feature of a latrine room. The room is a long and narrow room on an northeast/southwest axis. There is no ceiling. All walls show small patches of red plaster. The floor is of mud and lapili and appears uneven. There is a window on the southwest wall over the latrine. There is no evidence of a floor.

We have determined that this is a market space primarily due to its location on the forum as well as its large size. It is on a northwest/southeast axis. It is rectangular in shape and is divided into two rooms by simple pillars of opus latericium. Room one (to the south) is one step lower than room two. The floor is made of a stone and ceramic mix in a clay basis and although we do not have levels it appears the floor slopes from the near (southwest) of the building to the front (northeast). The southeast wall of the building was bombed in World War 2 and have since been restored. The southwest/northwest walls are well preserved. The southeast wall in room one is reconstructed. The southwest wall is in both rooms one and two as well as the northwest wall in room two. These two walls preserve three courses of support holes for shelves where the walls are visible. These rooms are currently used for artifact storage for items found in Pompeii. The northeast facade, facing the forum, consists of a series of nine opus latericium pillars flanking eight large openings. Only the third entrance in room one moving north from the east corner preserves traces of a double swinging door. In room two the second entrance from the east corner moving toward north also has traces of a double swinging door. Directly to the southeast in the forum is located the mensa ponderaria.

This tomb presently identified as the Tomb of Scaurus is located to the south side of the Via Della Tomba, west of the Villa of Cicero. This identification is in question and the alter tomb directly east of it may have been originally the Tomb of Scarus. The attribution is based solely on an inscription.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: V. Campbell page 162-165

This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. This space (20) is identified as a kitchen. We have concluded that this portion of the house (nine rooms at the western end of the north-west side of the house) was a late addition to the earlier house. This space is identified as a kitchen due to the presence of a platform we have identified as a cooking platform (4691) It is a rectangular space with a wide opening entrance at the southern corner. The space is on a north-west/south-east axis. It is in extremely poor condition. No flooring is visible due to overgrowth. The walls are opus incertum with traces of plaster remaining on the south-eastern wall at the east corner. Nothing else remains of this room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the north-east of space 21. it is the northern corner of this wing of the house.

DESCRIPTION: In the west corner of dining room 5 (6511) is a rubble and concrete platform, low to the floor and square with plaster on the two visible sides. On the southeast side of the platform we can see remains of painted plaster indicating that this platform was placed here after the walls had already been plastered.

We have identified this space as a dining room in the house of Ianipendius D. Caprasius Felix. This identification is based on the size and location of the room. It's decoration and feature support this identification, as does the orientation and and character of the entrance way. This room is in poor to fair condition. Only small traces of plaster flooring remain. This room is rectangular with a southwest - northeast axis. The entrance to this room is in the east end of the southeast wall, which appears to be a wide opening onto space 41 (possibly an atrium). The southeast wall is constructed of alternating courses of brick and cut stone. The other walls are opus incertum. Except for the southeast wall, the others are plastered and painted. The condition of the paintings is poor, but a low dado is visible with cream colored panels above red borders and thin yellow spindly details. This painting is third or fourth style. No ceiling remains. In the north corner of the northwest wall there is a couch niche (4068).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of space 41 and to the northeast of room 39.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the House of the Geometric Mosaic in the so called complex of Championnet. This is identified a double house (entrances 14,16) and part of the complex referred to by Eschebach as the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14-20. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. This feature (7010) is a very large preparation platform in the kitchen (10). It is heavily reconstructed in opus incertum and preserves no fuel storage or upper surface, which has been replaced by terra cotta pieces and cement. It runs along the northwest wall from the north corner over half the length of the wall and its width takes up about half the length of the northeast wall. It has been rebuilt to about waist height.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This preparation platform (7010) is northeast of preparation platform (7011).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this room as a preparation room in the House of Ianipendius D. Caprasius Felix. This identification is based on the character and location of the space, adjacent to the kitchen (32). The entrance to this room is through a low door opening to an L-Shaped corridor which leads east to area 29 and west to area 26. This is a rectangular space on a south east and north west axis. It is a small room constructed of opus incertum. It is in poor condition, with plaster seen only on the south east wall. There is a small window in the center of north east wall looking out to area 29. No ceiling remains. There is no visible flooring. The floor is pounded earth.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is adjacent to the kitchen (32) which is to the south west. Space 29 is to the north east.

DESCRIPTION: This L-shaped cooking platform, located along the east and south walls takes up one third of this square kitchen. This platform is interesting because of it's structural omissions, such as there are no tiled surfaces, recessed storage areas for fuel, shelves, lips or windows above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corrider 29 is to the north east. Preparation room 31 - 4063 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: In the Naples Archaeological Museum [inventory number 8634] is a wall painting of a cup with olives, tray with fish, and two partridges. "Pompeii in Pictures" reports that, according to Mau and Breton, this painting was located in this peristyle.

This couch niche is a low niche with a curved profile. It is set into the west corner of the south west wall of the dining room (40). The floor of this niche is a plaster floor which is partially preserved plaster and paint. The painted decoration appears to be a broad black horizontal band, with black and red vertical lines above and below it.

This feature is a group of three vats located in storage space (6525). There are three vats of various sizes. They are all rectangular. The largest of the three vats is on a northwest-southeast axis and goes across almost the entire length of the southern part of the room. The next largest vat is in the east corner of the room, and the smallest vat is located in the center of the northwest wall. The vats are opus incertum and were all plaster lined. All vats are submerged below floor level. It is thought that these vats had held amphoras.

This feature is the counter itself located within the counter room. Within the room, the counter is located halfway on the northwest wall running east to west in the center of the room, the 'L' continues to the South. There are two stepped shelves in the Northwest corner. There are two small circular openings for dolia in the counter. The counter has a small portion of painted plaster under the step shelves. This counter does not have a top of reused marble that we often see. rather, it is a rough stone surface.

Rectangular room facing south. Window high in east wall. Traces of plaster survive on north, south, and east walls. Floor obscured by lapilli. Identification as dining room based on size and width of doorway overlooking large room with two columns subsequently subdivided. Room #6 was examined as a possible kitchen (in view of small size and proximity to dining room), however, no indication of use survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room #4 to south and room #6 to west. Adjacent to street to the east. Room #4 to south and room #6 to west. Adjacent to street to the east. None

DESCRIPTION:
This is the so-called House of Championnet, also known as the House of the Geometric Mosaics. We have identified this area as a separate entity which one enters through entrance 13. We have identified this space (4) as a dining room due to its size and position in the house. We enter the room from the atrium (2) via a door on the east wall with no threshold. /the remaining walls are a mixture of opus incertum brickwork and ashlar blocks of tuff define the doorway. There is no wall to the west overlooking the peristyle garden 12. This seems to have been removed and the red cocciopesto and white tesserae mosaic floor extended over the ambulatory (14) around the columned peristyle garden (23) to enlarge the room. A door remains in the north wall that may have been blocked in antiquity. Plaster remains on three walls but no paint. No ceiling remains.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium (3) is to the east, the curc buildings facing the forum to the north, ambulatory (14) and the peristyle garden (12) to the west. Tablinum is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that space number 1 in the Imperial Villa is an ambulatory. This colonnaded space is very long and is bordered by 43 columns with a gutter on the west side. A recess in the north end of the colonnade is brightly painted and is today protected by a modern roof. The east wall was painted in Fourth Style paintings of which few remain. The southern end of the east wall contains the doors and windows that allow entrance to the remaining rooms of the Imperial Villa. Today the floor surface is of gravel and is completely open to the air. The modern reconstructed museum building is situated above this building and a row of terra cotta drains have been placed above to assist the escape of the water.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The ambulatory is tot he west of Rooms 2 and 3.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room (13) is entered from the courtyard (12) to the southeast. It is a medium-sized rectangular room oriented southeast/northwest. The threshold is framed by a marble rectangular stone to the northeast. Evidence shows of the opening for the bolt to be inserted. To the southwest of the threshold a low rectangular piece of stone leans against the southwest wall of the doorway frame. The floor is paved with a polychrome mosaic which is badly preserved. What is visible today is a u-shaped section which contains irregularly-shaped marble panels of white, pink, red, and black, on a white background. This section is framed by a large white band and two black thinner bands. In the middle of the floor is a larger rectangular panel which is framed by a two-strand guilloche in red, yellow, white, and black. The decorative motif in the middle is completely destroyed. On the northeastern side, the floor slopes down toward a pipe pierced at the bottom of the wall. The walls of this very well-preserved room are decorated with fourth style painting. The lower zone in black motifs: the ones best preserved show female figures holding trays. On either side of this figurative panel is a vase framed by a garland. The middle zone contains three large rectangular panels containing in the middl figurative emblema. The only best-preserved ones are on the northwestern wall. They represent from left, a semi-naked boy riding a horse, a female figure with traces of a child and a man, and a similar semi-naked boy on a horse. Fragments of architectural structure are evident on the border framing the panel in the northwestern and southeastern corners. in the upper zone, individually-placed female figures decorate, but in this section, the wall painting is badly decayed. On the top of the upper zone runs a stucco cornice which is only partly preserved along the northwest and northeast walls. On the very top of the northwestern and southeastern walls below the reconstructed roof are two large rectangular windows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Courtyard (12) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Based upon the high level of decoration and its location immediately behind a counter room with a cooking platform, we have identified room 2 as a small serving room. The room is on a northeast/southwest axis. The room is entered through a doorway on the southwest side which has a cement threshold. Another doorway on the northeast wall, with no threshold, continues to serving room 3. Today the room is behind a locked, iron and barred door which is rusted shut. The walls visible from that door are all frescoed with remains of red and white painting with designs visible from the door unidentifiable. The floor appears to be of clay. Modern wood beams hold up a renovated cement ceiling. On the northwest wall around elbow height is a rectangular indentation identified as a lavarium by Boyce (180). He described a painting that cannot be seen today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
To the northeast of counter room 1.
To the southwest of serving room 3 adjacent to the northwest with serving room 4.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have identified this room (15) as a garden. This is based on the fact that it is in the back (south) corner of the property open to both the peristyle and to the summer dining room (16) via a window. There is no front wall demarcating this area from the peristyle. The space is square. Overgrowth prevents discerning the floor surface. In the southern corner along the outer wall is a niche running across the western wall and into the eastern wall to other small openings on the eastern wall on either side of the window. In the south-east wall close to the south corner is an infilled plaster lined niche which does not reach the floor. The upper part of the eastern wall is heavily re-constructed. There is opus incertum construction on the western wall. Undetermined material is extant on the south wall and a mix of opus mixture and infill on the east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle (14) is to the north-west, summer dining room (16) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: A small rectangular painting of three fish and two clams is located on the southeast wall, directly to the south of the large door entrance. The background of the panel is blue with a red border. One fish is orange and two are gold.

This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined that this space (21) was a preparation room with a latrine (4690) in the south corner, for the adjoining kitchen (20) This is a small rectangular room. The floor is no longer visible due to overgrowth. The walls are opus incertum, no decorative elements are extant. The ceiling no longer exists.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen (21) to the east
VIDEO_COMMENTS: done by Steve Jenness on Twyla Howse's phone, L Ludwicki to transfer

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this unexcavated space as a diata. this attribution is based on the visible remains which symmetrically match diata (78) at the opposite south end of the colonnade. One can see the window on the south wall of this diata as well as the exterior molding above the curving portion of the north wall. The exterior of this space has a cream background and floral dado and a simple pattern of ashlar blocks painted with thin red lines.

Square room to the north of doorway 4 opens off entryway to the house. Kitchen contains a long masonry platform the width of the north-wall with two-third of surface tile and the other northeast one-third contains masonry cooking hearth with supports. A rounded tile lip runs the length of the platform. To the southwest of the cooking platform are two masonry supports of either side of the sewer opening to the street. Above the opening is a ceramic pipe feeding into the sewer from the higher level. A window is located immediately above the cooking platform on west wall. Another window is located on the east wall close to the entrance. Walls appear to have some remnants of utilitarian plaster, with red dado along west wall to approximately one meter. Floor is rubble. Rough cut hole above cooking hearth area along north wall at approximately 4 meter elevation. Possible blocked up doorway where east wall meets cooking hearth, as evidence as limestone jambs, bits of plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 3 is located at the front entrance of the structure to the north of the vestibule rooms 1 and 2. It is located to the west of atrium of 5 and to the south of dining room 15.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room opening up onto peristyle 9. Room axis is northeast/southwest. Large double-doored doorway with tufa stone threshold opened onto peristyle. Immediately to the west of the main entrance way is another smaller doorway leading to adjoining dining room 15. Walls show evidence of high fresco decoration which Eschebach calls Fourth Style, although it is no longer visible. The floor has areas of cocciopesto.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Immediately to the northwest is dining room 15. Northeast wall abuts street Vicolo della Fullonica. Southeast wall abuts kitchen room 10 and storeroom 12. Southwest opens to peristyle 9.

DESCRIPTION: Square central image poorly preserved on middle of east wall. A large central fish is still clearly visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mosaic 6142 and painting 6140 a and b to south, paintings 6139 a and b to north.

DESCRIPTION: In kitchen room 10 are two attached-to-wall masonry supports identified as being for a cooking surface. The northwestern support is worn down to just a few centimeters from ground level. The northeastern support appears to be intact (possibly some reconstruction). See drawing for measurements.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the south wall of storeroom 12 and directly southwest of latrine (6135) centrally located along north wall of room 10(kitchen).

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east west axis. Doorway in the center of the east and west walls opening to atrium 6 to the west end parallel to the east. An obvious addition to the southwest of the west wall was made in antiquity, narrowing the west doorway. No extant decoration on walls. Floor obscured by lapilli. Eschebach identifies this as a dining room (as did the PI in 2001)However, note the through way of the two doors.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 6 lies to the west, room 11 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular basin lined with opus signinum. The upper course did not survive along the east and southeast. Opus signinum survives on the base of the exterior face as part of the terra cotta floor of room 15.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation platform (feature 1556) to the east with vat (feature 1558) against east wall. The basin is in the center of the west wall of room 13. None Preparation platform (feature 1556) to the east with vat (feature 1558) against east wall. The basin is in the center of the west wall of room 13.

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 3 opens to the northwest. Opposite corridor 5 is a small square room whose western and northwest walls are mostly preserved in their height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining garden 2 to the west; corridor 5 to the southeast and kitchen 4 to the northeast.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on this Feature Sheet.

DESCRIPTION: This large rectangular garden is to the northwest of the portico and is surrounded by high walls on the northeast and southwest and low wall on the northwest which contains four steps up to a higher level for what Jashemski denotes as a flower garden. On the southwest wall there five beam holes on the upper register and five beam holes approximately halfway up the wall on the west end. High in the middle portion of the wall is a deep rectangular window. Two holes are on the southwest wall to the south. On the northeast wall there is one visible hole high in the wall. Jashemski and others describe furrows as excavated in 1865. Today some depressions are extant suggesting the furrows run in a northeast southwest pattern. In the south portion of the garden near the southwest wall are a cistern cover or puteal. Today the garden is covered with grass and bay laurel bushes surround the perimeter, five each on the southwest and northeast and three on the northwest wall. This garden runs on a northwest and southeast axis. On the east corner of the northeast wall a rose bush grows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 20 to the south. Dining room 26 to the south east.

DESCRIPTION:
Reference: Eschebach 1993, 90-1.
Eschebach: A U shaped counter once laid in the North corner of the room. The counter opens to Northeast where the salesman stood.

At entrance to the shop, you can see a U-shaped counter. The entrance to the counter is on the northeast side. The counter arm on the southeast side has 3 dolia. A heavy layer of concrete covers the U-shaped counter. The southwest arm faces the street. The arm on the northwest side contains 2 dolia but are aligned by stone and brick. The counter is restored. The height is approximately 1 meter. Each arm is approximately 2 meters long.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Shelf (3186) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Lararium is located in the east corner in this atrium which is southeast of the atrium entrance. It is a large square aedicular shrine. The platform rests on a base approximately 1.5 meters from ground. Base is topped with a double band of decorative stucco molding and the two sides of the base are frescoed with red paint on a white background, preserving what may be paintings of an aedicular shrine on each side. The west corner supports a column, doric in style, with yellow and red marbleizing paint. North and south corners have pillars topped with double rows of stuccoed moldings and abaci. Molded cornices above and both sides have pediments that are also plastered mold decorated. The interior of the lararium preserves a curved back platform in the southeast wall. This brick with fresco coverings and paintings appear to be 3rd Style. White upper structure is brick, the base is mixed brickwork and stonework, including an area with exposed opus reticulatum on the southwest side.

We have determined that this structure was most likely a high-level residence and that room 6 is a dining room. This is based upon its location immediately to the northeast of grand atrium 2, the high open door to that atrium, as well as elaborate fresco decoration in the room itself. The door to the atrium is on the southwest wall with a stone threshold with hardware insets. A smaller door enters the ala on the southeast wall. Fresco remains on all four walls, with some imagery identifiable. Small birds are visible on the north, east, and south walls. Fresco colors appear to be a red bottom register with green and yellow dividers above, with a white background. Two high paintings appear to have been removed from the northeast wall. The lines of small holes indicate the presence of cornice molding. Room is rectangular on northeast/southwest axis. Portions of the floor are concrete with the insets. The remaining floor and ceiling are modern.

Bibliography: Esche. p. 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Continuous Relationship to Other Features: To the southeast of dining room 5 and to the northeast of Atrium 2

Continuous Relations with Other Rooms: Northeast of Atrium 2; adjacent to Room 5.

DESCRIPTION: The shop is opposite the Stabian Baths, with an altar to the south. The sidewalk is very wide. The stop is a step up from ashlar masonry which shows a door indentation across counter space indoor entrance. A large U-shaped counter is immediately apparent on the southeast wall. The flooring is lapilli. There is no roof or windows. Doorway (large) to a dining room and preparation room are to the northeast. The wall on the southeast is painted with holes for two layers of shelving. Height of walls are extant ti first floor. You can see three holes for top shelf and three holes for bottom. Southeast wall is propped up with scaffolding.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 and 3 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is located in the north corner of the house. One enters the kitchen from Room 5 from the southeast. The room is roughly square. There is a little platform abutting the southeast, southwest and northwest walls. On the northwest wall in the north corner is a large niche lararium. Below the lararium on the floor a short distance from the northwest wall is a construction that may have been a hearth or altar. The room was plastered and painted a red color. On the northeast wall just outside the entrance to the kitchen is a lararium. The height of the room and the type of floor are indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 to southeast.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on this Feature Sheet.

DESCRIPTION: On the northwest wall in the north corner is the niche lararium. The interior is stuccoed and painted. On the back wall is a painting showing the Deity "Abundance" reclining on a bed (according to Fiorelli).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hearth to the southeast. Preparation platform to the south and southwest.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on this Feature Sheet.

DESCRIPTION: On the east wall just outside the doorway to the kitchen is the niche lararium. The interior was painted though the decoration is unknown because the back wall is not extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hearth and Lararium to the north.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on this Feature Sheet.

DESCRIPTION: This is the house of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. In the north corner of the northwest wall is a small couch niche which is approximately 1 and 1/2 meters in length and runs on a northeast southwest axis. No evidence of paint.

Between Via _______ and Via ______ at the tip of the triangle is a public fountain. It is rectangular. The block that distinguishes the location is devoid of a distinguishing feature pattern. There is a step on the southwestern side. Inside the fountain is a drain in the southeast side which empties onto the street. Stones (large and irregular basalt) are located (3) out of (4) corners. The north corner is missing a stone. These were to avoid traffic damage. In the center of the southeast side is a channel for overflow. Indentations of metal clamps that held the sides of the fountain together are still visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water storage (6023) to the northwest and crossroads shrine (6025) to northwest

DESCRIPTION: Poorly preserved square base of a rubble cooking platform inserted against the plaster of the south wall of the dining room.

This is a narrow, rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis for food processing. The entrance to the room was a door on the southwest wall. Only a small cutting in the masonry at the south corner indicates a door. This room is aligned with the front entrance. Flooring is not visible. The southwest wall is not preserved. The northwest and northeast walls are preserved to a great height, but the southeast wall is very poorly preserved. The northwest, northeast, southeast walls preserved plaster coating with fresco visible on northeast and southeast walls. Although poorly preserved, there are traces of red paint. Feature number 3185, a low vat, is located along the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is directly toward the southwest side of this room. Room 3 is to the southeast side.

DESCRIPTION: This feature consists of 2 large, high steps (brick and rock) which run along a northwest/southeast axis and join in the west corner of the southwest wall upon entering the room (1). The portion which runs along the northwest wall consists of 2 volcanic stones which join from the wall, the most northern of which shows evidence of a metal fastening. The surface suggests that the entire structure was plastered in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter (3184) is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: We enter shop by stepping up from pavement on Via Stabiana, one shop away from the corner of Via Abbondanza. The entrance is a wide door. The threshold is one step up from the sidewalk. Southeast wall is resplendent with a penis and a scrotum in a rectangular frame at shop lintel, height. The outside walls are brick interspersed with opus reticulatum. On the northwest side of the doorway entrance is a quern. There is a ceiling to floor recess on the northeast wall, approximately 1 meter wide. At northwest of entrance is a cooking platform, which is relatively tall. To southeast of entrance is a feature-preparation platform. It is the same height of the cooking platform. The floor is lapilli-covered. Plaster on the northwest wall corner has red paint and darker paint. No windows or ceiling in this room. The shop is on the northeast side of the street.
The triangular area between Via ____ and Via _____ there is an arched stone structure with one window type opening. This is a public well behind a public fountain and a bakery.

One enters the dining room through a door on the south corner. The room is rectangular in shape on a northwest to southeast axis. The floor on a level higher is of beaten cement in a simple repetitive mosaic design of small pieces of white marble. The window now appearing on the southeast wall is probably modern. The height of the roof is unknown. All four walls were stuccoed and painted in the fourth style. On the southwest, northwest and northeast walls, in the center between thin decorative columns is a rectangular painting with black backgrounds each showing a motif of drinking parties. There may have been another on the southeast wall where the window is located. The other panels of the room have in their centers floating figures with red backgrounds. Below the panels on all four sides in the lower register is an alternating pattern of triangles painted in black.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous with room (11) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This room is determined to be a kitchen due to its features, location and size. A marble threshold leads into a tile-shaped brick surface - remnants of a herringbone terracotta bricked floor. The major portion of the kitchen is unroofed. In this large space facing southwest is a small doorway leading to a tetrastyle atrium. In the southeast there is an open passageway showing signs of being covered, leading to a preparation room (6891) In the center of the east facing wall another door leads to a storeroom with stairs leading to the second floor (6911) The final door on the east has a raised threshold, slave sized, narrow and dark which leads to a storeroom (6892) Above this small doorway is a large window in the second floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to peristyle 26 and passageway 25 to the north and rooms 13, 12 and 10 and passageway 11 to the east.

DESCRIPTION:
On the northwest wall in the center of a large panel formed by two thin decorated columns is a rectangular painting on a southwest to northeast axis showing a scene from a drinking party (Greek symposium?). The diners recline on couches beneath a large awning or perhaps tent - one couple per couch. Between the two couches is a tripod table on which sits a cup and ladle. To the right a slave pours water or wine into a large bowl. The couple on the right recline on their left elbows, the male gestures towards his right. The woman holds a drinking cup. The couple on the second couch exchange a
kiss. To the left appears to be two servants, both facing away from the couples. One servant drinks from a cup. Behind the couch is another standing, possibly a slave.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Floor below; (3103) to the southwest; (3105) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: According to Eschebach's floor plan room 11 was provided with what looks like a cooking platform along the Northwest wall, as the lararium suggests the function of the room as a kitchen.
According to Eschebach's floor plan room 11 was provided with what looks like a preparation platform along the Northwest wall, as the lararium suggests the function of the room as kitchen.

Room 10 is entered from Northeast off room 14. The room has another opening; a large low window looking out onto room 15. The rectangular room is on a Northeast/Southwest axis. The Northwest and Southwest walls show traces of red painting and large fragments of plaster. They are also largely collapsed. The southern section of the Southwest wall is largely collapsed.
The Southeast wall (with the window) is mostly covered with dead vines. The ceiling is non-extant. The walls framing the entrance to the Northeast exist now only as small blocks of stone resting on a heap of soil in the northern corner of the room. The floor is covered with overgrown vegetation and heaps of soil.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 15 is to the Northeast. Room 11 is to the Southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Latrine is immediately adjacent to exterior southeast wall of the house and is part of room 10 (kitchen). Identified as narrow space with sloping floor, with window immediately above. No masonry remains or wall decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bordered on northwest by masonry support 6136.

DESCRIPTION: The dining hall is located in the west corner of the house. One enters the room from the atrium from the northeast. The room is rectangular in shape and is on a southwest/northeast axis. There is a large doorway to room 5 on the southeast wall. As reconstructed, the ceiling is very tall. The floor is entirely in black and white mosaic. A simple design runs around the periphery, while the interior appears to be white tesserae. Stucco remains on each of the walls although the the paint has disappeared.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium, room 2, is located to the northeast. Room 5 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, northwest axis, floor obscured by lapilli. Traces of undecorated plaster in southeast corner. Wide open doorway in west wall to the street outside. Stepped threshold with placings for door. Doorway in the east end of the north wall provides access to the atrium of entrance 5. There are no files recorded in Eschebach nor any indication of food and drink however Nina identifies this as a taberna.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 3 to the north

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This a cooking platform. It abuts the partition on its southeast side which separates it from the latrine (3153). The cooking platform is a low stone feature without outer surfaces preserved. The northeast side wall is devoid of outer surface. A series of four hole across the northeast wall provided shelving above the platform. There is a small vertical window in the northeast wall above the platform.

This is the house of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This is a small square lararium on the west end of the northwest wall, approximately 1 to 1 and a 1/2 meters from the ground. It is approximately 50 centimeters wide and 20 centimeters deep. Poorly preserved plaster is extant on the middle portion on the northeast side with no evidence of paint.

This is the house of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. Room 14 runs along a southeast axis. One enters the dinning room one of two ways: from the northwest one gains access through the main entrance off the peristyle. The small service entrance maybe accessed from the north side of the northeast wall. Plaster exists on all four walls. There is evidence of blue, red and gold paint. The floor is obscured with debris. The height of the walls is indeterminate. There is no ceiling.

This is the house of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. We enter this dining hall from the southeast across a marble threshold to floor of opus signinum. This large rectangular room has a decorated northwest wall with evidence of plaster remaining on three walls and the entrance side walls. No evidence of bearing support for ceiling. No roof now exists. On northwest wall we see third style wall covering which includes Hercules in red toga contemplating seven nymphs engaged in music making. Two of the nymphs each hold a lyre. Garden fences and small shield as border 1 meter from floor. We appreciate the care taken with the paintings' portion and sense of mystery and something special happening. This northwest fresco is thankfully protected by a 6 foot overhang. On the south portion of the southwest wall approximately 2 meters above the floor is a framed portrait of one couple, male/female, (14 inches by 14 inches). The male face shows features and expression. The woman shows only two eyes and part of the hair. The painting has a blue background. The picture is protected by tile overhang.

House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This is a vaulted storage niche. It is located directly south of the oven. This niche is barrel vaulted. it has a plaster floor. The walls and vault are also plastered with vestiges of red paint. The exterior face is arched brick and stone work.

The lararium is located on the southwest wall of room 11. It is semicircular, almost 10 centimeters deep. The walls are partly covered with a thin layer of plaster behind which was another painted surface which was covered with dados of green and red paint on a white background. The arched vault was covered with a terracotta border which was later covered by the plaster revetting the entire wall of the room. The ledge is deteriorated but shows some plaster along the inner ledge.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2875) and preparation platform (2876) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The altar in the sacellum has the customary scrolls (lips) of the platform top. The lips are Northwest and Southeast. The altar shows plaster without painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Podium in Northwest (2885)

DESCRIPTION: To the northeast of the southwest corner of the oven (3081) appears to be a meta flipped over onto its top and encased in masonry all abutting the oven (3081). The hole in the top of the meta has been sealed with tile and plaster. The use is unknown, but may have been for water or perhaps fuel for the fire or ashes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (3081) to the southwest; basin (3082) to the northwest; kneading basin (3085) to the north; kneading machine (3084) to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: In the middle northeast wall is an interesting reuse of two catilli or mills. The first is cemented to the wall, the second worn catillus is cemented to the first and to the ground. The one on the wall is lined with plaster/cement. The second more worn catillus is lined with perfectly fitted terracotta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (3081) to the southwest; mills (3086, 7, 8, 9) to the west; water basins (3083, 82) to the southwest; kneading machine (3084) to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: This a minority report. We enter this storeroom from the southwest over a threshold which shows evidence of a door with locks. It is a long rectangular storeroom on a northeast/southwest axis. The floor is now covered with dirt which covers a white tessera floor. The 4 walls show much evidence of plastering in cream/white with no designs. The northwest wall has 4 definite square shelf holes that would have held 2 shelves, one above the other about a half meter apart. The southeast wall has an identical shelf arrangement at the northwest wall, with 4 definite shelf holes. This is a high room with possibly modern tile ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room (2861) to the northwest; dining room (2862) to the southeast; peristyle portico (5) to the southwest

DESCRIPTION: A U-shaped drain runs along the east wall from the latrine to drain through the east wall. The second arm of the drain runs diagonally across the room to the north west where it joins a terra cotta pipe and outflow from the water feature in room 6. The two arms of the water feature enclose water cistern with a puteal consisting of a reused catillus that has been refinished with plaster. A marble puteal as been subsequently placed over the whole.

In the north east corner of the room, separated from the remainder of the room by a partial wall is a latrine with a plastered floor sloping east into a drain (3107) against the east wall of the room. The drain undercuts the seat of the latrine and the base of the partition wall at its junction with the east wall of the room. There is a masonry and tile seat of the latrine with a plaster lip and facing. The latrine drains through a tiled channel sloping east through the wall to a cistern outside to the east. Placings for a wooden seat survive in the north east and south west walls. There is a low ceiling, a modern restoration of the original.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water feature 3107 to the south

DESCRIPTION: One enters the small dining room through a doorway in the south east. The floor is on a higher level than room 11 to the south east requiring a step. It is of beaten cement with no discernible decoration. The room itself is rectangular in shape on a south east to north west axis. The walls are painted and stuccoed in, essentially, Third Style. The ceiling is vaulted on a south east to north west axis. In the north corner are the remains of what may have been a small cupboard abutting the north west and north east walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 11 to the south east

DESCRIPTION: We enter the dining room from the northeast. The room runs along a northeast- southwest axis. There are two modern windows high on the southwest wall. There is a door on the south corner of the southeast wall to the adjoining room. The entire room is of modern use and decoration for the custodii. The only thing which is original is the step from the atrium into the room (northeast).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (3) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: It is a low rectangular plastered platform against the earlier second style painting of the east wall. The platform is surmounted by a high plastered terra cotta lip on all three sides and a matching support in the center of the platform. The lip and support will have supported two grills and fire placings. There is a gap in the lip on the southeast corner to clear out the ashes. Traces of white plaster survive.

The platform is L shaped against the southwest and northwest walls, abutting the northeast wall in the kitchen and there is a lip against two edges. There are storage areas in two sections underneath the platform for fuel for the hibachi-style burner. On the modern plastic protectors that hang in the doorway and prevent entrance, the conservators identified kitchen implements. These are, listed from top to bottom, iron triangular shaped hibachi-style stand for food receptacles; a casserole dish on display on the stand with a convex space and flared rim; a terra cotta basin with spout; the stems or bottoms of amphorae for light grinding; a circular shaped weight; and thin wall jug with anthropoid features.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium #3076 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The shrine sits directly behind the fountain and is connected to the south wall of the well. As extant it is a block. it is a crossroads shrine. Eschebach reports that Nazois has a drawing of the shrine. Some evidence of white stucco/paint exists on the west side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fountain (6024) to the southeast; well (6023) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Midway down the east/west axis of the house is room 11, a large rectangular dining room. The access to the dining room is a doorway at the northwest corner of the north wall. The room was frescoed. Traces of red paint remain. Construction of the north wall consists of eight courses of brick with opus incertum above. The door threshold in the north wall, west end, is of tufa stone with a channel for the door so the door opened to room 11. There are no windows in the room. The room identification is based on size, shape, and view towards garden (9) through the doorway. The axis of the room is east/west.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 14 is contained in the northeast corner of room 15. The south wall abuts room 16. There are trace remains leading to room 13.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. You enter the L-shaped kitchen from the south. The longer portion of the room is on a northeast/ southeast axis. In the western corner of the southwest wall is a bench. On the northeast wall is a large cooking platform (3139) which is in poor condition. Centered over the cooking platform is a large window to the street. On either side of the large window are two smaller windows. There are remains of a low plastered bench along the northwest wall with a small drain embedded at the most northwest corner. A small patch of plaster remains on the northwest wall approximately a meter from the ground. Adjoining the cooking platform along the northeast wall (north side) there remains plaster painted in yellow with red above. On the east portion of the southeast wall is a large window connecting room 19 to room 20. The walls are extant to the first story. The floor is obscured with lapilli and debris. On the west side of the southwest wall there is a small recess with a lip whose function is unknown.

This is a roughly rectangular shaped dining room, and axis is east west. Identified by size and location as a dining room. Plaster evidence on walls shows the same red-below-white pattern as we have seen elsewhere in the service-type quarters of this house. The west wall appears to be a modern reconstruction for the most part. A narrow doorway is located on the west wall. The floor is rubble. No windows evident. Small niche in center of north wall approximately 2.10 high.

Two rectangularly-shaped blocks situated at the bottom center of the east wall. Surrounded by single lentil all set amid irregularly shaped stones.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: CindyFloor is lapilli rather than rubble.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the horticultural space from the northeast. (See Jashemski's description) The north corner holds the saccellum and the northwest wall leads to a two-step entrance of an open garden and a single room structure. The wall of the maritime Venus fresco in 2. 3.3 forms the remainder of the northwest wall. The southwest wall is high with vegetation growth. In front of the wall in the southwest corner is a possible casting of plant root. The whole southwest corner is covered with modern tree cuttings to make way for modern vineyard. The modern vineyard contains 293 staked vines. The southeast corner contains an entrance for modern farm equipment. It may indicate a large entrance in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Saccellum (2881) to the northeast; room (14) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the horticultural area from the northeast, immediately coming to a lararium niche on the wall northwest of the entrance. On the northwest wall rebuilt to a second floor we see an entrance approached by four steps and a large threshold. The threshold is of pounded stone and a high window wall above the door on the second floor. We look in through a locked gated door. The room is square with walls in place one and a half floor high. The first thing we see is an alter with customary scrolls (lips) of the platform top. The lips are northeast and southwest. The alter shows plaster without painting. Behind the center alter is a podium which is higher than the alter. The podium is divided into three sections by masonry struts and two columns. On the northeast and southwest walls at about eight foot level there is evidence of molding with a top ledge. The panel walls show faint yellow and white paint. The podiums northwest section may have once held a painting. There is a round section removed. The central and most important part of the podium may show an indicular frame. There is no painted evidence what gods were worshipped. Custodi have placed two platforms of four sections of laid out broken wall fragments. If they are restored and replaced, we may have more information.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Sacellum to northwest (17).

DESCRIPTION:
This feature is a dolium. Although in pieces, it appears to be complete. This is a large dolium. Although not visible, this type is known to have a narrow base rising to slightly flaring sides. The shoulder turns inward, rising to a broad rim with a flat topped lip. This dolium is of a thick pink fabric with a buff slip. The base is in situ in the west corner of the storeroom (8).

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is located due west of the doorway in the northwest wall, leading into atrium 2.

DESCRIPTION:
A circular basin inserted into a masonry platform consisting of
a partially restored terracotta bowl used in conjunction with an adjoining cistern and preparation platform for the preparation of bread. The lip of the platform/ basin is partially restored in cement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cistern (6212) is directly to the north next to which is the preparation platform (6210).

DESCRIPTION: From atrium, southeast side, enter a doorway of average width, approximately one meter, without a lintel. We determined this is a dining room because of the repurposing of the old house to an inn/hotel. The room is close to the southeast entrance of the inn oriented northeast/southwest. General condition shows very little plaster. The floor is soil and missing ceiling. Based on the presence of a large window on the southwest wall facing the atrium, and impluvium, we interpret this as a dining room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: In the second panel to the southeast of painting 3105, framed by a slender column to the northwest and a large decorated band to the southeast, is a floating figure of Mercury holding a rabbit by the legs in his right hand.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The painting is contiguous to the floor below. Painting 3105 is to the northeast. Painting 3103 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that three small holes through the plaster on the southwest wall were cut to hold a shelf. Those holes are approximately three meters high and are aligned horizontally across the wall. The two end holes are located roughly forty centimeters above two more holes which may have held the brackets for the shelf.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature would have been on the wall going from above the counter (1-3992) and the preparation platform (1-3994).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Oplontis Villa A as a domestic villa structure. We have determined that the last usage of this room 23, is a dining room. This identification is based on : a) room location within the structure - off peristyle (24) with a view of a garden (59) ; b) the presence of designated food and drink features (wall paintings) ; c) certain characteristics to include walls, doorway, and the floor; and d) previously identified as a salone. Feature description : 1) the features in the room are wall paintings ; 2) the paintings are located on the north and south walls ; 3) the condition of the paintings is good to excellent with some damage ; 4) the paintings are set within the entire wall ; 5) the paintings are of food and drink objects. The ceiling and upper walls are reconstructed with a partial row of plaster molding, partially reconstructed in situ, approximately three quarters of the way up. The floor is white mosaic with a black border defining a central space. The room appears to be square. The west wall has a large entrance with a marble threshold of two low steps. Evidence of door jambs in the marble threshold step (western). Inside the room looking west at the western side on the north end, three quarters of the way up there is evidence of a repaired cornice/molding. There are traces of restored wall painting of a possible shield and traces of paint in the upper register running above the doorway. On the eastern wall, the cornice/molding is restored about three quarters of the way up. The entire wall is painted in second style with architectural features. There are two painted Corinthian columns. There are four painted doorways. Two appear to be slightly ajar. In the center of the wall there is a painted scene with a red painted border. The scene cannot be identified. Above is a painted theater mask, flanked by two painted vessels. A painted garland hangs from the top of the fresco.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the western side of the room there is a large entrance on to portico (24) with a view of a garden (59). On the south side an entrance opens on to a joining corridor.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined this space to be a dining room because of its proximity to the atrium. No threshold remains. The room is rectangular in shape. We enter facing south. On the east, south and west walls fragmented plaster remains. The dado appears red on the east, south and west walls. Slight remnants of yellow wall paint are extant on the south and west walls. The floor is no longer visible due to the vegetation. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to room 19.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: video on Bruno iPhone, L. Ludwicki to transfer

DESCRIPTION: The remains of a cooking platform which is in poor condition and today piled rubble and tiles cover the west end. The feature runs along a northwest-southeast axis on the southwest wall of the atrium. At its highest point the structure appears to have been approximately 20 centimeters high.

The couch is on the southwest wall. At the top on the south side of the niche there is a space for a triclinium knob. It has white plaster with a double red line at the west corner. The niche is very apparent in the room.

The kitchen is located in the south corner of the peristyle (room 5). The room is rectangular in shape and is on a southeast/northwest axis. One enters the room from a doorway in the north corner. In the south corner of the room is the masonry foundation for stairs to the upper floor. On the northeast wall is a lararium. Abutting the southwest wall to the northwest of the stairs are the rubble remains of a possible cooking platform. As reconstructed the ceiling is missing. The type of floor is indeterminate. The wall was originally stucco but no sign of painting remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle (room 5) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION:
Room 15 kitchen is located near the northeast corner of the house. The kitchen contains a cooking platform on the east wall and a latrine in a small room immediately adjacent to the north of it. The kitchen is l-shaped, with a doorway in the southwest corner. No evidence of windows outlets remain, although at this point a ceramic pipe appearing to come from an upper level is visible over the cooking platform.

There is no trace of plaster on the kitchen walls and the floor appears to be lapilli. The latrine is entered by a door on a northeast abutting wall off the l-shaped room. There is plaster along some of the north and east latrine walls, and the latrine floor is cocciopesto. However, this appears to go on the side of the building only.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 14 is contained in the northeast corner of room 15. The south wall abuts room 16. There are trace remains leading to room 13.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the north side of Via del' Abbondanza near the intersection with the Via dei Teatri. The fountain sits basically in front of 7.14.13 and 7.14.14. It is constructed of volcanic stone slabs and has interior dimensions of 0.97 meters by 1.24 meters and is 0.73 meters deep. Only the floor appears to be lined with opus signinum. It has an added lining to round off the wall/floor junction. The pilaster is centered on the northwest slab and is decorated with a helmeted figure (man or Minerva). This fountain has no modern plumbing. The overflow is in the center top of the southeastern slab. The drain is at the center botton of the northeastern slab.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is located on the Via del' Abbondanza, on the north side of the street in front of 7.14.13 and 7.14.14.

DESCRIPTION: There are three stone bases for the preparation platform along the central axis of the room used for mixing the dough prior to placing the bread in the adjoining oven. Each of the stone blocks preserves architectural molding indicating reuse from a different structure. There are no other features in the room. There is access to oven (3081) via the window in the north corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None listed

DESCRIPTION: We enter this bakery/restaurant from a door in the southeast - a large entrance. As we look into the room we see a square bread sales room. In the north corner are steps to the upper floors. Red painting is above the first step and plastered first two steps. The floor is plastered mud. No roof is extant. In 2011 steel scaffolding fills the room. A door on the eastern corner is low and perhaps to a bedroom. This sales room has full vision of a wonderful bakery oven. As we walk through the large entrance we see the work area of the baker/miller. This is a rectangular room with a northeast/southwest axes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill room (3080) to the northwest. Room (2) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room situated on a northeast/southwest axis. The floor us obscured by lapilli. In the center of the southeast wall is a doorway with a stepped threshold to the mill room (3). Plaster decoration survives in the west corner with first style decoration. Along the northwest corner of the room is a bench (3098) and in the east corner of the room is a vat (3099). In 2011, the room is filled with metal stairs and scaffolding.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill room (3) is to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: Abutting the southwest wall to the northwest of the stairs are the rubble remains of a possible cooking platform. The platform appears to be rectangular in shape and is located on a northwest/southeast axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a lararium (2867) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the space from a long corridor to the northeast. On the northwest a long wall separates the space from the other section of the structure. At the top of the wall there is white plaster. Three/fourths of the way up, the south wall of the gladiator barracks is visible. There is a small northwest wall quadrant that backs up to the barracks. A southwest wall also backs up to the barracks. The south wall is adjacent to the triclinium dining garden (2889) in (8.7.6.). The south wall ends in line with the neighbor's triclinium. There is an east wall which connects to the south wall and separates an unroofed space. The area in one spot shows a peach plaster along the bottom of the northwest wall. A garden is reported along the north wall and southwest wall in an L-shape and communicates with the garden triclinium area in the adjoining property.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (8) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The masonry preparation platform has a top surface constructed of broken bricks. There are no fuel arched beneath. A small window is directly above the preparation platform. The platform is located on the east wall in the southeast corner of the room abutting the south wall. The latrine (6030) is located to the north of the cooking platform and the two are divided by a wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The preparation platform is south of room (17) which has entrance (23) in it. It is east of corridor (20) and east of room (19).

DESCRIPTION: The open space between the amphitheater to the southeast and the vineyard to the northwest was probably denoted at least partially to the sale and the consumption of food and drink. The basis for this conclusion derives from the painting "Riot in the amphitheater" presently located in the archeological museum in Naples. The painting, while it shows men fighting, also shows what are clearly temporary structures, tents or awnings used for the sale of items. That food could have been served in these temporary structures is strengthened by the fact that the vineyard to the northwest had a triclinium just inside the wall that no doubt served spectators. Although the painting shows only the space described above, there could have been temporary structures in the area between the amphitheater and the palestra to the southwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Vineyard to the northwest and palestra to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The altar is a rectangular masonry structure against the west wall. There is no exterior facing that survives. The surface is modern restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium 3043 is is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this space as a dining room within The House of the Working Painters. This identification is based on the location of the room off the peristyle, the size of the room, and the quality and character of the printed decoration. The shape of this room is almost square and so the axis of the room relating to the doorway is NE/SW. There is one doorway to this room located along the SW wall toward the South end of the room. This is a high, wide doorway. The room is in good condition. It appears the floor was plastered and painted red. This is preserved throughout most of the room. The walls are conserved to the height of the ceiling molding, and was probably a one story room. No ceiling remains. The color scheme in this room consists of a black decorated dado and red panels above in two registers. The middle section is divided into panels by spindly, columnar motifs. The panels are decorated with small floating figures (putti) and garlands. The NW, NE, and SE walls have central framed pictures. The upper register is divided into squares and rectangles with small figures, animals, and birds. The arched areas on the upper portions of the NE and SW walls have pictures of food; features 5-4056 and 5-4055.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the NE of the peristyle and to the NW of the kitchen (2-4047).

DESCRIPTION: This is a feature in Dining Room 11 -4054. It is the painting located in the arched portion of upper SW wall. This is a rectangular panel in the center of the arch. It depicts an eel an a squid on a platform. The sea creatures are painted realistically; the platform is brown and beige and the background is blue. It is not completely intact in it's restored condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is accross the room from the painted feature, 11 - 4056, ehich is in situ on the NE wall. It is above the doorway on the SW wall.

DESCRIPTION: There is a lararium niche in the south wall above and to the east of the cooking platform and the post hole. It is rectangular with no remaining decoration, except for a portion of the red painted ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This lararium is to the South of the cooking platform (4048).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this feature 20-6544 as a masonry triclinium based upon its location in the center of the garden directly on an access with a large dining room 18 and the remains of masonry construction. There is also evidence of a serving table in the center. The open side of the triclinium is on the southeast side. The couch to the southwest has been badly damaged with just its base remaining. The northwest couch is attached to the southwest and northeast couch, and is badly damaged. The couch on the northeast side is also badly damaged. There is a square tufa stone small dining table in the center of the triclinium.

A square, partially plastered insert in the tufa bricks of the southwest wall, about 100 cm. from the floor is all that remains of this lararium. The lararium appears to have had a slightly arched top surface and was originally painted but few traces remain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the west of features 6529, 6530, 6531 and 6532.

DESCRIPTION: The tile floor sloping south to the latrine and drain are in the southeast corner. Long rectangular room with a doorway to the peristyle (room 11) in the east wall. To the south of the doorway is an arched window providing access to a basin lined with opus signinum in peristyle. Basin (feature 1557) in the center of the east wall. There are traces of red decorations with white upper register surviving along the west wall. Shelving supports survive on the north wall for a single tier of shelves. A possible drainage channel survives against the east wall north of vat (feature 1558) with opening to the east at the floor level. Three vats (features 1558, 1555, and 1553) found along the east wall with preparation platform (feature 1556) to the west of vat (feature 1558). Red lower register and white upper register survives on the east wall above vat (feature 1554) to arched plaster lined lararium niche. There is a stepped cooking platform (feature 1552) south of vat (feature 1553) against the east wall. There is a arched storage recess with a tiled surface and lip. Latrine (feature 1551) in the southeast corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle (room 11) and garden (room 20) located to the west. Peristyle (room 11) and garden (room 20) located to the west. None

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 7 lies on the northeast side of the house opposite the north corner of the peristyle, room 5. The room is rectangular in shape on a roughly northeast/southwest axis. As reconstructed, the ceiling is quite tall and the floor is of a beaten cement of terra cotta fragments and large irregular shaped pieces of marble. One enters the room through a wide door from the southwest. The walls are covered in stucco and richly painted in fourth style. The northwest and southeast walls have large panels with a central rectangular panel, probably of mythological scenes. The small panel on the southwest wall is missing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle, room 5, is to the. west.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the room from the mill room from the southeast. This is an elaborate oven room with a massive enclosed oven to the northeast and two water basins are along the southwest wall (3219 and 3218). There is a lararium (3233) in the southwest wall. The northwest wall has a doorway (to room 8) which leads to the street. See Mayeske, page 41, "Bread, Bakeshops) sic. The side space opened to a passage to another room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north is the preparation room (3209). To the northwest is a latrine (3205). There are six holes in the curb outside the external doorway. The stable (3200) and mill room (3199) are to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this small dining room from the northwest through a low doorway. There is a pounded pavement with a mixture of stone. This small square dining room has a window in the southwest wall overlooking a garden space (room 14). There is evidence of plaster on all the walls. There is no ceiling. The window and doorway are reinforced in modern times. The doorway looks out into a doorway (room 18).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden space (room 14) is to the southwest. Corridor (room 18) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The dining hall is located in the west corner part of the house. One enters the room from the atrium from the northeast. The room is rectangular in shape and is on a southwest/northeast axis. On the southeast wall is a large doorway to room 5. As reconstructed, the ceiling is very tall. The floor is entirely in black and white mosaic. A simple design runs around the periphery, while the interior appears to be white tessarae. Stucco remains on each of the walls, although the painting has disappeared.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (room 1) is to the northeast. Room 5 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the latrine from the oven room six from the southeast. This is a small narrow latrine with a few terracotta tiles on the floor. The north wall is approximately 1m high and adjoins a room which was for stairs. The gradient of the northeast suggests that the height of the room would be determined by the height of the stair. Evidence of plaster is extant on the southwest, northeast walls. The drain is not determined, however there may be a hole in the north corner.

This is a large open area, opening to the East with a wide doorway to the East opening to the street, at entrance 22, possibly for the use of carts. To the South the area opens to a series of small rooms, possibly used as stables. To the North of the doorway is a possible latrine.
In the center of the room are stairs going North to the floor above. To the West of the base of the stairs is a preparation platform (6116). Beneath the stairs is a water basin. (6117) In the Northeast corner and North are the doorways to three dining rooms. In the Northwest the room opens to the garden and a small tiled latrine. Adjoining the latrine is a doorway to a store room. (26) And out-of-situ marble cistern head is in the room. The floor is
obscured by lapilli. In the Southwest corner is a narrow corridor leading to the
atrium area.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 26, 27, 28 to the North. 40, to the Northwest. 29 to the East. 33, 34, 35, 36, to the south. 38 to the Southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
The entrance faces N.W., off corridor with a large garden (6), situated in back of the house. There is no floor, however one sees: grasses, weeds and dirt. There is no evidence of a roof. The N.W. wall is badly damaged. There is reconstructed evidence of plaster and perhaps painting at the left of the entrance opening.
The S.W. wall is badly damaged. Traces of plaster seem possible here, there is painting and a window. There are 3 sides only- situated above eye level, facing and looking out on to the street.
The S.E. wall is badly damaged, only traces of plaster remain here. The N.E. wall is badly damaged. The facing wall to the left, finds traces of plaster that is very faint and a trace of paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Looks out onto the corridor to the N.W.. The entrance hallway and large garden is seen to the right, it's not visible from the room.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The Video team leader is Carlos Avila

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room situated on an E-W axis. The Northeast and West walls survive with a modern restoration effort. The North end of the East wall has a rectangular buttress. The buttress East and North walls contain preserved traces of plaster. The Southwest corner and South wall are no longer extant, so the entrance to the room cannot be defined. The floor is obscured throughout the room by vegetation, earth and debris. The room is identified as a storeroom by Eschebach. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 is situated to the South.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Carlos Avila

DESCRIPTION: We step up slightly into a large rectangular room, the view is of a dining room. Because of this position and the view to a horticultural room. (This room is not a perfect rectangle.) The South East wall is shorter than the garden room wall. The walls are bereft of plaster and painting. These are very old walls, whereas the entrance piers are made of brick. The old walls are made of opus incertum. The room is raised to 6 inches above the garden room. The threshold is marble. There are no features in the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 9 (#3929) is to the North West of this dining room.

DESCRIPTION: There were furrows and root cavities visible at the time of excavation.

This space is a forecourt at the western entrance side of the temple. No original ground surface is visible. Presumably, this was an open space with no walls except for the exterior western wall of the temple portico. Excavated post holes attest to a pergola covering (not discernable). This space would have been used for dining. Flanking both sides of a central ramp are 2 triclinia (3939 (north))(3940 (south)) covered in plaster and painted couches. There is a circular table (3957 (north)) (3958 (south)) in the centre of each space.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is located west of the portico (2). It is outside of the temple.

DESCRIPTION: small shop no food and drink
small shop no food and drink
small shop no food and drink
shop with l-shaped counter with 3 dolia built in to left of counter. 3 shelves for display linked to 14 numerous rooms.

We have determined that this is a market space primarily due to its location on the forum as well as its large size. It is on a northwest/southeast axis. It is rectangular in shape and is divided into two rooms by simple pillars of opus latericium. Room one (to the south) is one step lower than room two. The floor is made of a stone and ceramic mix in a clay basis and although we do not have levels it appears the floor slopes from the near (southwest) of the building to the front (northeast). The southeast wall of the building was bombed in World War 2 and have since been restored. The southwest/northwest walls are well preserved. The southeast wall in room one is reconstructed. The southwest wall is in both rooms one and two as well as the northwest wall in room two. These two walls preserve three courses of support holes for shelves where the walls are visible. These rooms are currently used for artifact storage for items found in Pompeii. The northeast facade, facing the forum, consists of a series of nine opus latericium pillars flanking eight large openings. Only the third entrance in room one moving north from the east corner preserves traces of a double swinging door. In room two the second entrance from the east corner moving toward north also has traces of a double swinging door. Directly to the southeast in the forum is located the mensa ponderaria.

A small cooking platform is identified on the south wall, in the southeast corner. We identify this by the small arched fuel storage area and a cooking surface. There are no refinements to the cooking surface. Most of it is obscured by floor ruble.

This is the House of M. Pupius Rufus. We have determined that this feature is a cooking platform in the kitchen (20) based on its size, shape and construction. The platform is hard to see due to overgrowth of vegetation. There is no lower space for wood.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: in room 20 on north-east wall, preparation room 21 to the west

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this exterior space as a garden on the east side of the Villa of Oplontus A. This is the long narrow space bordering on the east side of the pool. This identification as a food-related garden is based on Jashemski, who noted a lemon tree in this area. Presently this is a level area which may have been an open space with a covered colonnade, or an area with statue bases, to the east. This area with the statue bases is presently planted with two lemon trees and other trees and two bushes. Remains of volcanic rock debris are visible attesting to the west side of the colonnade. Each statue base has a drain passing through from east to west.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The garden is situated to the east of the pool and to the west of a long horizontal border of volcanic rock.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. One enters this L-shaped room from the long end (southeast) with a northwest southeast axis. Immediately on the northeast wall is a large cooking platform above which is a small narrowing window to the street. Centered along the northeast wall there are four holes which suggest support for shelving. A second window on this northeast wall is higher and wider than the first. The northeast wall curves eventually forming the northwest wall of the room. Within this curve, adjacent to the aforementioned window, is a modern lintel which has apparently replaced an arch contiguous to the large oven(3150). This structure along with the curved wall forms an irregular space which could have been used for kneading. The area did not receive a separate designation as a room due to the lack of a pass through to the oven. The major portion of the northwest wall is the large oven which projects directly into the space. Another archway which adjoins the northwest wall and extends to the southwest of the short end of the L-shape provides entrance to the remaining spaces which are also designated by smaller arches. The large, low, wide arch (3144) on the southeast wall possibly for grain storage is plastered. The arch which is the southwest most portion of the room houses a well (3152) and has a hole above in the arch itself for passage of water. On the northwest wall just north of the well is entrance to room 29. There is a large water basin north of the oven. The archway and oven wall are mostly brick and volcanic. The height of walls appear to be preserved to first story height and the floors obscured with lapilli and broken bricks. There is no ceiling extant.

House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. The entrance on the southeast has a small low doorway. When you enter from the southeast going northwest you immediately see a rectangular opening to the oven entrance on the east end on the northeast wall. The floor is lapilli the walls are mud and rubble with low grade concrete coating on parts of the wall. The ceiling has the barrel vault. There is a skylight opening on the northwest end of the barrel vaulted ceiling. To our surprise we found a catillus ( round upper mill stone). The lava catillus is in the north corner. There are no mills in this kitchen. Why is the top of the mill found here? Betty Jo speculates this was once a bakery, but the usual 3 to 4 mills were removed to provide more space. There is no sign of a kneading machine in this house.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 28 (3142) to the south east.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. The large water basin is located in front and to the north of the oven. The water basin is made out of stone covered with cocciopesto lining. The basin features two handles (bassos). The depth of the basin cannot be determined because of the soil and ash filling approximately half of the vessel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Beehive oven 3150 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION:
WE have determined that this is a dining hall in the house of Obellius Firmus. This identification is based on the size, location and structure of the room. This is a large rectangular hall on a northeast, southwest axis. This room had openings on three sides. along the northwest wall is a large doorway to the atrium. This talldoorway has a tuff threshold with bronze holders for the door jams in situ. The northeast wall has a large doorway into the tablinum (48). The threshold on this wide doorway has several pieces of white marble in situ. There are round cuttings visible for the door jams. The southeast wall has a window the full length of the room, with a caste of a wooden screen. The window looks out to the peristyle. No flooring is visible. The walls are opus incertum, with a door in the northwest wall framed with large masonry blocks. at least three levels of plaster remain visible on the soutwest wall, and plaster is visible on the other walls, however no frescoes survive.
