The upper portions of the walls have been reconstructed. No ceiling has survived.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschenbach 451, Jongman, W."M. Obellius Firmus, Pompion Duovir" Talant 10-11, 1978, 62-65
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle is to the southeast. The atrium is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a large chest (displayed under glass and locked) in the Southwest corner of the large atrium. It is a black rectangular chest constructed of wood and multiple wrought iron straps that are attached with hundreds of rivets. The wrought iron was weakened by the heat of the volcano eruption to the point of collapse of the right Northeast corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Chest 4431 is located in atrium 2, West of the impluvium.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular masonry platform inserted into the southeast corner of the atrium. The platform rests against plaster to the wall to the south. Poorly preserved rubble structure, however fragments of in situ tiles surface as well as loose tiles originally from the tile surface of the platform are visible.

House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This small rectangular room is the latrine. It is located directly north of the kitchen door. It is aligned on a northeast southwest axis. There is a stone threshold. No other flooring is visible. The northeast wall has a low stone platform going from the north corner going half way across the wall. This supported the toilet seat. Cuttings in the southeast wall supporting the other side of the seat. The east corner of the northeast wall has a cut drain at the base of the wall. The walls of stone work preserving only small areas of plaster. The northeast wall has small high vertical window. The northwest side is preserved on to the height of a low partition, approximately one meter but an indentation in the northeast wall suggests it may have been twice as high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is contiguous to the cooking platform 3143 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This wonderful pedimental sculpture has been placed in a modern frame, at the appropriate height above portico entrance. The central area of the pediment is occupied by two large figures. To the left is Dionysis who is holding in his left hand a bunch of grapes, his right arm is stretched out and his right hand is holding a goblet. He is smiling and has abundant curls. He wears a short girded tunic. To the right is a reclining female figure, who may be Ariadne or Aphrodite. The female figure's head is now missing. Her right hand is on her abdomen, her left hand holds her veil. To the left bottom of Dionysis, beyond his goblet is his pet panther, stretched out to receive a wine sprinkling. To the right of the female figure, at her feet is a putti holding a fan in his right hand, and his left hand rests on one of his wings. Between the central figures is a Thrysus. The temple is totally covered on top by plexi glass.
There were furrows and root cavities visible at the time of excavation.

We have determined that 8, 5, 1, 40 is a corner shop, based upon its location at the Via Abbondanza and proximity to the forum and a number of large houses. Eschebach suggests that this is a taberna. The room is rectangular with a slight addition for an additional entrance (40) and probably missing stairs to above. The axis of the room is northeast-southwest with the northeast containing a wide doorway with a number of varied door placement indentations. The sill and the doorjamb have door markings that do not match up and, in addition, the west wall directly behind hasother markings for the same thing. The northeast wall contains a lararium with a stone area above and the southwest corner has an exit to the neighboring street that can also be secured, with a basin (4447) adjacent to the north. Walls are all opus incertum with mixed limestong and tufa reconstruction. The floor today is dirt. The northwest contains remnants of frescoes.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Eschebach 379

ANYTHING UNUSUAL?
No
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room contains waterbasin 4497

DESCRIPTION: This is a well located in the North corner of the preparation room (13-3959). The well is stone lined. It is visible to a depth of 1/2 meter. The well is covered by a ceramic putile. This is in situ and level. It is decorative with a base molding and rim. The putile is intact except for chips missing from the rim and base.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This well is located just to the North of the doorway leading to the atrium (2).

DESCRIPTION: A large rectangular masonry platform takes up the full north east wall of kitchen room 4. It has a tiled surface and is made of opus incertum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Immediately below lararium 4144 and to the south east of oven 4142.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Geometric Mosaics in the so-called complex of Championnet. This is identified as a double house (entrance 14, 16) and is part of the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14 to 20. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. This room, in association with entrance 14, is identified as a dining room. It is a rectangular space on a northeast, southwest axis. It is wide open to the atrium (2). This room and its adjoining space, room 4, were undergoing renovations at the time of destruction. The shared entrance to room 4 at the eastern corner of this room appears to have been heavily damaged due to earthquakes. The floor toward the east corner of the room buckled and rose so that it was necessary to cut out this section of the floor. This left a space now filled with gravel, occupying the east corner of this room and south corner of room 4. We see fragmentary remains of the top level of flooring done in white cocciopesto over a layer of red cocciopesto. There are two chunks of this white stone in this room as well as a third chunk in room 4. We have identified this stone as the source for the small fragments composing the cocciopesto floor. The entire southeast side .......... (insert end of sentence). One bottom of a brick column is in situ near the eastern end of the opening. Earlier floor plans included an additional column toward the south end of this opening. Corners and doorways are brick and the northeast, northwest, and southwest walls are opus incertum. Three holes in a line are cut into the mid-level of the northwest wall. No ceiling remains. No plaster or fresco remains. The room is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the southwest of the adjoining room (4). It is to the northwest of the atrium (2).

DESCRIPTION: Cooking or preparation platform to right inside entrance. Water pipe visible behind. Next to sleeping room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: No other features. ?Stairs to left of front door? Sleeping room behind. Sleeping room behind No other features. ?Stairs to left of front door?

DESCRIPTION: In the residential Villa of Diomedes, we have identified room 45 as a dining room. Although smaller in size than other dining rooms in this structure, the room was decorated and had a large opening looking south. The southwest corner has a doorway with slight remains of a stone threshold. The southern end of the room has an opening constructed of tufa block and may have had door hardware attached to it based on what appears to be a round hole about 50 centimeters up. The north wall has a doorway opening with a marble threshold opening to tablinum (40). That threshold does show evidence of door attachment. The walls are of opus incertum and show faint evidence of panel decorations. On the north wall, high up, there is a post hold opening which could indicate a roof or an upper floor. No floor decoration remains. The floor is now dirt and gravel. The room is currently without a roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the north of walkway 44 and to the south of tablinum 40.

DESCRIPTION: As we face this large work area we will describe the ovens of the baker first. On the Southwest wall we see an elaborate oven of masonry faced with bricks. Mortar is of lime and sand in this oven. A beehive shaped baking mound was encased in a smoke chamber to enhance heat efficiency. The oven is bricked to the ceiling. The inner beehive is enclosed. Standing on top of construction stairs we see that the beehive portion of the oven has just the open space and vent at the front of the beehive. This is a rare chance to see the top of an oven. The whole of the mound structure was laid on a brick base. The bottom course of the mound is wider and has hard stones to resist blows from shovels. The oven opening is rectangular. The South part of the oven has a large rectangular pass through open space to the preparation room. Beneath the lava stones is a small rectangular area usually used to hold kindling, dried brush wood, bark of flax plant, or charcoal. This is probably an ash pit for raking out the ashes. As we look at the brick lined arch to the oven we see a rectangular recessed area which probably contained a phallus/penis. On the North face of the oven is a rectangular niche. In front is a water basin on each side. There is no oven door extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kneading machine (3084) to East; water basin (3082) to South; water basin (3083) to the North; kneading basin (3085) to the Northeast; mills (3086, 7, 8, 9) to Northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We see a round lava stone container; the metal socket is in place. This allowed the machine to knead dough. The vertical shaft is not in place that would have turned the arms; still to be seen are round holes on the sides for wooden shafts which could be turned by men or animals to pull and push the dough.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (3081) to the southwest; mills (3086, 7, 8, 9) to the west; water basins (3082, 2083) to the southwest; kneading basin (3085) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Mill (3086) is only a rubble base.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (3081) to southeast; mill (3087) to the southwest; mill (3088) to the west; mill (3089) to the northwest; kneading basin (3085) to the east; kneading machine (3084) to the southeast; water basins (3082, 3083) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Mill (3087) has a rubble foundation; meta of hard porous lava is in place, plastered surface surrounding.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill (3088) to the west; mill (3086) to the northeast; mill (3082, 3083) to the east; kneading basin (3085) to the east; kneading machine (3084) to the southeast

DESCRIPTION:
We enter this room from the west from the atrium, through a relatively wide door with a moderately high lintel. We move to the small rectangular kitchen avoiding a short northwest wall. the floor is lapilli and dirt. The walls show minimal signs of red plaster. The southwest wall shows plaster painted white with two red stripes and a window for the smoke to escape. There is no roof but there are indications of post holes for a roof. The post holes do not match as far as height.

Previous reports state that there is a latrine here. We could not find evidence of a latrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium (2) is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Two deep recesses which form a "V" at the corner of the northwest and southwest walls appear to have been supports for a latrine. Each recess is approximately ten centimeters deep and ten centimeters high. Each is twenty to twenty five centimeters in length.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hearth and shelves 3195 on the northeast and south east walls.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is on the south end of the southwest wall. The cooking platform is large and has two recesses for wood or charcoal. The room has a barrel vault ceiling. The cooking platform abuts on the southwest wall which features a small skylight opening on the southeast wall above the platform. The platform has a small portion of front lip. The platform features rear shelf from the wall. The platform back abuts on the southwest wall. The platform features a tiled surface. There is no roasting pit.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 3164 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: One enters this rectangular dining room which runs on a northwest southeast axis from the southwest. There is a marble threshold with tracks for secured doors. The height of the southwest wall is indeterminate. The northwest and northeast walls and east side of southeast wall are preserved to the first floor. The northwest wall shows indication of reconstruction marked by terracotta tiles below which some plaster survives. In the eastern corner of the room on the northeast and southeast wall faces traces of plaster survive. The floor is covered with lapilli. No ceiling is present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 19 is to the south. Room 27 atrium is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular plastered vat is embedded into the floor in the north corner of the room. Above the vat on the north and east walls, there is a placing for an unidentified lid or cover. Remains of a partition wall, poorly preserved, divide the vat in two. At the base of the east wall, there is a small terra cotta out pipe that drains through the wall into channel(2957) in processing room (3). In the northeast corner of the east wall, a large semicircular recess from the vat into the wall may be from collapse.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Olive/grape press (2955) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The wine channel is narrow, raised, and plastered and runs along the southwest wall of the room from the northwest. At the west end there is a drain from the vat in the pressroom (4). In the external face of the channel, three lead pipes (the fourth of which is no longer visible,) drain into the adjoining dolia. The channel was used to drain the wine from the press room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dolia (2954) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Eschebach pp. 389-90.

The room is rectangular and runs along a northeast/southwest axis. There is a wide doorway at the northeast end of the northwest wall. No visible threshold survives, and the northeast and southeast walls are extensively restored. The southwest wall is almost completely modern. The floor is completely obscured by earth and vegetation. Some structural debris is in the northeast corner. There is an opening at the west end of the northwest wall which is modern collapse.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (14) to the northwest.

STRUCTURE_ID: House of A. Cossius Libanus/House of Sallust
DESCRIPTION: Masonry triclinium facing south. Cocciopesto surface survives on north and east surfaces. Marble faced basin in center of couches. Wall painting survives on north and east face. North is red with traces of small (3) central tondos. Brick column stands to the southwest of the couch supporting roof now removed. Traces of post supports survive in north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North of garden 21, cistern in garden to east, cistern in garden to south, and guttering along garden colonnade. None North of garden 21, cistern in garden to east, cistern in garden to south, and guttering along garden colonnade.

DESCRIPTION: Shop with L-shaped counter. 1 dolia built-in and back room connecting to 17 & 18

This space has been classified as a garden. The area is not fully excavated so only the South West end and the North West parts of the space are visible. The original space was almost square. One would enter from the atrium (1) through a door in the Northern corner of the North East wall. This North East wall also had a doorway towards the Eastern end accessing room (3). Only the South West and North West walls are visible. The floor surface is not visible. No roof remains. The condition of the space is very poor. The North half of the North West wall is brick. There is a large window in the Northern half of the wall looking into room (5). The Western end of the North West wall has a small high window looking into the house 9.6.5 room (13). This wall preserves plaster and paint with a large red panel towards the center of the wall. There are 5 small holes above the window corresponding to the partition wall which would have held small roofing beams creating a roofed storage area. This storage area has 3 pairs of holes in the South West wall, presumably for shelving. The interior of this space was plastered. Possible hinge or bolt hole on Southern wall of storage area. The Southern corner of the garden is occupied by a large lararium. The South West wall between the lararium and the storage area was plastered and painted with red panels. Other than the brickwork on the North West wall, the walls are incertum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is contiguous to the atrium which is North of this garden.

DESCRIPTION: Irregularly shaped platform with tiled surface. Plan is preserved but sides are eroded with stones missing. No recesses for wood storage. Walls not high enough preserved to indicate window. Platform clearly built after walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine located down corridor and to right. Latrine located down corridor and to right None

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular/squarish dining room with door in northwest corner into garden and small door in northeast corner comes to small room (12). Neither doors nor window in west wall are preserved to their full heights. There is a window on the south wall (intact) presumably connecting to house #28. A sign on east wall records restoration in 1977. Remains of faded wall plaster preserved on south wall; no visible remains of original floor covering.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room in southwest corner of house looking west through door and window into garden. Dining room in southwest corner of house looking west through door and window into garden. None

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified Oplontis Villa A as a domestic villa. We have determined that the last usage of this room (#65, feature #4032) is a dining room. This identification is based on the room location within the structure. It faces east with a wide entrance and view of the large pool. There are no clearly obvious food and drink features.
The characteristics that suggest a dining room are the mosaic floor, large entrance with view, possible serving passage on western side, elegant wall paintings, and niche on western side and previous research indicates a salone. The floor is mosaic, white with black border, defining space within the dining room. The ceiling is all reconstructed. Along the western side of the room, there appears to be a separate area defined by the wall structure, mosaic floor, and niche attached to the western wall. This area to the west is clearly accessible to the main room.
On a north/south axis there are two large openings on the north and south walls, each with well planned views of planted areas and garden paintings. The entire room was purposely planned with views on all sides. A base molding of stucco painted to look like marble, reconstructed around the room. In total there are five entrances to other rooms.
The east is a large monumental opening, reconstructed, with evidence of a marble threshold with door jambs. The interior of the east wall is reconstructed, partial plaster remaining but no wall painting. Traces on the south portion of the east wall is a base molding painted to look like marble. The south wall has an entrance to (63), area 63 appears to be a corridor for servants because it is painted with white and black stripes. The center of the south wall is a large opening with a marble ledge. Evidence of door jambs are present to close off.
This opens to a recessed rectangular enclosed area with elegant garden paintings on the three walls and of a painted fountain with birds. The color scheme is gold, yellows, red and blue. On the west side of the south wall it is divided by an attached pillaster defining a secondary space. On the far west there is another exit for corridor (63). In the lower register there remain marble panels which have been reconstructed. The wall above has been stuccoed but there are no traces of paint.
The western wall has two large openings to a garden (56). They flank a central large niche jetting out to the room. On the south side of this wall below the window are black and white marble panels. In the center of the wall is a large niche on a base of marble projecting into the room. It has been reconstructed with traces of unidentifiable paint. At the top of the ceiling there is a reconstructed stucco cornice /molding in red, blue and white. The window opening to the north has another marble ledge with evidence of door jambs.
The north wall on the northwest side has an opening to a corridor (67) for slaves, with black and white striped paintings. This passageway connects to the central dining hall. There is a large pillaster separating this room into sections. In the middle of the north wall there is a large opening with a marble ledge. This looks directly onto (68). Room 68 was painted with elegant garden paintings of fountains and birds. The color scheme is gold yellows, red, blue and green. The view to the north through room (68, 69, 72) is of a fountain in room (74) identical to the fountain on the south wall of 65. The wall is restored with stucco but no paint. On the west side of the north wall there is an entrance to room (15).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the west portico #60. To the south is passageway #63. To the north east is passageway #67. There is an entrance to room 75 on the north west side.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as Oplantis A. We have determined that Room 69 is a dining hall. This room is the central dining hall of the pool complex. This dining hall dominates the east wing of the villa. This dining hall could hold three to five complete sets of triclinia benches. You would approach this room from the existing colonnade on the east side. There are no food and drink features. There are characteristics that determined this to be a dining hall including the size of this huge rectangular space. On the east side, the room is totally open to a view of the pool and lemon trees beyond. On the north wall there is a door opening to a room where diners could await their time to dine. Centered on the north wall is a huge window with a marble ledge, overlooking a garden with garden paintings. This garden room has a large window aligned with the first, that allows a view through another dining room, through a third window to a second garden room with the same painted garden walls. There are also small, high windows on the north and east walls of the garden room.

From almost any location in this dining hall, you can see five distinct garden decorations, bird baths, peacocks, plants and flowers. Main zones are yellow background, lower and border zones are red backgrounds. Lower red zone is tall.

In the dining hall, there is another door on the north wall located on the west end. This leads to the slaves' corridor, with black and white stripes. On the west wall, there is a huge window overlooking a garden or orchard area.

On the south wall, the two doors flanking a centered window duplicate the same arrangement as on the north wall. These open to slaves' corridor, garden room and waiting room. In this garden room there are four bird baths and one large flower pot. The ceiling is a modern covering shaped like a pediment. The floor is covered in beautiful marble squares and triangles. One third is still extant. There is incomplete molding around the base of the west and north walls. The walls were plastered but no colors are visible now.

This small rectangular painting is located on the west end of the southwest wall in cubiculum (7) in the center of the middle register. We have identified the painting as a table with an amphora laying on its side on the far left, with a shelf perhaps holding loaves of bread in the center, and maybe a cornicopia or a rhyton on the far right.

This is feature is a dining room, 5 - 4054. It is the painting in the arched portion of the upper north east wall. This is a rectangular panel in the center of the arch. It depicts a large rope-handled basket of fish which is tipped on it's side on the top of a platform. The fish are spilling on to it. An unidentified object is at the lower right foreground of this picture. The fish and container are in realistic colors; the platform is brown. The background in faded blue and cream. Approximately 80% off this painting is intact.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is across the room from the painted feature 5 - 4055 in situ on the SW wall.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this room 3 as a dining room and determined its last usage was as a dining room. We have identified this feature as a couch niche. This couch niche is located in the lower part of the NE wall on the east side. The condition is fair, with some reconstruction in modern times. The approximate size is 1.5 meters wide by .5 meters high by .25 meters deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
This feature is situated in the lower east corner of the NE wall of the room
(3-6518).

DESCRIPTION: Possible traces of a basin in the northern corner of the room. The existence of a basin is suggested by plastered floor and plaster inserted against the wall plaster of the north and east walls. No indication that the south and west sides of the basin survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 4193, and 4194 to the southeast. 4192, 4191, 4190 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the Villa of Diomedes as a villa. We have determined that the usage of this room is a kitchen. The room is located within the villa facing the northwest exterior wall and is east of the frigidarium [22-4086]. There are several food and drink features [23-4072, 23-4073, 23-4074]. The room is a slightly distorted trapezoidal shape on a southeast-northwest axis. On the southeast wall we see stairs with a storage area underneath. The floor is pounded earth. This is a big kitchen. The ceiling is non-existent. The walls are opus incertum without a sign of plaster. There is a door at the southwest end of the cooking platform which leads to a latrine. There is no set pattern so probably this unroofed kitchen needed some light.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to the latrine on the west, and frigidarium [22-4086] to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: On the western half of the northwest wall is a painted niche. The painting at the northern half of the niche is a mythological scene on a black background. A goddess (?) enthroned on a wheeled cart is pulled by two goats. A figure behind her follows with arms outstretched and a heavy male figure is in front of her. The goddess appears to be holding a drinking cup in her left hand.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A painting (3192) is above. A painting (3191) is to the north. Niche (3193) is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: At the northern end of the northwest wall, the fresco is well-preserved. The panel closest to the north corner preserves the traces of a winged figure on a yellow background. To the west of this panel, is an architectural design featuring a doorway with three shields with faces above. A band above the three shields shows food including fruit from a basket and a boar. On the small column on the north side of the painting window opening is a mask at the top and three dead ducks suspended with ribbon. Other animals appear in this panel including a bird on a ledge and a leopard perched on the roof. To the north corner is an upper panel with a seated female feeding a peacock.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Niche (3190) and painting (3192) are to the west. Niche (3193) is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is approached from room 11 to the north. The room is roughly rectangular in shape on a south eat to north west axis. The room is quite small as most of it is taken up by the cooking platform. To the north west are stairs to the upper level. The walls were plastered but no sign of paint remains except on the north west facing of the cooking platform. The ceiling of the kitchen is indeterminate, if there was one.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 11 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. The large cooking plate form which is in poor repair has a raised ledge on the northwest side. It has a tiled surface. It is about 0.8 meters high. it is located under a large window.

The room is small and square with an entrance at the east end of the north wall. The floor is obscured by lapilli, and there is no extant wall decoration. The north and west walls are preserved to a foot and a half. Eschebach refers to a cistern identified as a pile of rubble and the adjoining west wall in room (8). Eschebach refers to a non extant lararium (2899) and a cooking platform (2900)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (8) to the northwest

DESCRIPTION: This large rectangular pressing vat runs on an northwest/southeast axis. The masonry walls with opus signinum top are contiguous with the opus signinum lining of the tank. The tank is filled with earth and vegetation. The southeast end of the tank abuts directly against the exterior wall of the peristyle garden. Against the southeast corner is an intact partially submerged dolium. A puteal has been added to the rim of the dolium encircling the east and south sides constructed of tile and surfaced with opus signinum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining couch to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION:
This dining room other opens out into the atrium on a north-south axis with a large opening on the south wall. A second doorway is located in the southwest corner of the west wall. A small window is atop the north wall. Yellow, red and white painted plaster is present on all the walls but but does not have scenes on the walls. A molding was present on top of the walls, and traces remain today, but the ceiling is a modern reconstructed one. The lintels are modern concrete. The threshold on the south wall is marble and indicates bifold doors. The ancient floor is not visible.
The room is located northeast of the primary entrance and was accessed from the counter room (2) through room (5) to the east of room (7).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (7) contiguous to (6) to the north; (8) to the east; (4) to the south; room (5) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The function of the room is defined by the L-shaped counter, one arm of which begins on the northwest wall and runs parallel to the street. Midway in the large doorway the counter turns on a 90 degree angle to the northeast and ends approximately two and a half feet from the northeast wall. In the west corner on the northwest end of the counter is a display counter with four steps. Underneath the counter is an arched opening for storage. At the northeast end of the arm running northeast/southwest is a large hearth opening towards the northeast. The hearth extends above the height of the counter and is wider than the width of the counter arm. The northwest and southeast arms of the hearth extends towards the northeast wall for approximately 18 inches. Inside the hearth is a low shelf. Extending beyond the raised portion of the hearth is a platform. this platform also forms the floor of the hearth. The exterior of the counter including the hearth and step shelves was covered with plaster and painted red, parts of which are still extant.

This room is a small rectangular kitchen. The doorway is in the middle of where the ruined NW wall would be. To the E of the doorway the wall contains traces of painted plaster: red in color and on the lower part with very faint painted decorations above. Along that east wall, you first see a preparation(feature #3935) platform low to the wall. Continuing to the south end of that wall,the major cooking platform (12-3932) touches the wall. The southeast wall also shows traces of red plaster and a ceramic drain runs down the south corner of that wall and a second drain is to the southeast immediately to the adjacent cooking platform.
The cooking platform runs from the east corner 3/4 of the way along the southeast wall towards the south corner.
Immediately adjacent to the cooking platform, based upon the evidence of the wall pipe is latrine.(feature # 3933)
The southwest wall shows only faint evidence of plaster with no color remaining.
On the southeast wall at the top are 5 posthole openings showing evidence for an upper level.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to the south of room 13 and to the northeast of storeroom 14.

DESCRIPTION:
This dining room is in the northeast wall opposite the peristyle. We have determined it is a dining room. Diners would look at the peristyle, but not see the Atrium.
The general condition of this room is bad, some plaster remains on the walls and the floor is not visible. It has a wide doorway, which looks out on the peristyle. The door to the peristyle is very wide and only one side of the door exists.
There are no features in this dining room other than some white plaster on the southeast wall and the northwest wall. No ceiling is extant. This area has much green foliage.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 9 Atrium southwest

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular platform, at the N corner, along the NW wall of the kitchen (11-3969), is of rubble construction. It is preserved to it's full height in the N corner where a ceramic tile surface is preserved. Along the NE edge the remains of the partition are visible. A small trace of plaster coating remains at the lower eastern corner of the platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This cooking platform is located N of doorway 7 and NW of the vat (11-3971)

DESCRIPTION:
This is a rectangular Vat located in the center of the northeastern wall of the Kitchen (11-3969). The northwest side of the Vat is made of ashlar, with the exterior plastered. The southwest and southeast sides of the Vat are made of rubble construction. The Vat abuts the northeast wall, but the rubble construction is not flush with the rest of the wall and it abuts to the eastern end of the wall.
The Vat has not been emptied and the interior is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This Vat is situated southeast of the cooking platform(11-3970), and is along the southwest wall of room #13 (13-3972).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified structure VI-10-11 as a house and room 14 as the kitchen. This identification is based upon the presence of a cooking platform. The room is roughly square in shape and has a low opening to the southwest to preparation room 13 and to the northwest to passageway 23. On the southeast wall next to the cooking platform we see a small trace of red painted plaster. The walls are in a fairly rough shape of remaining architecture. The floor is rubble and the room is open to the sky. There is a step up in the doorway to corridor/passageway 23.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation room 13 is to the southwest, corridor 23 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: A terracotta cylindrical dolium sits directly to the north of the kneading basin 4532. It is close to the southwest wall and just off center toward the northwest of the room. The dolium stands about 70 cm. high and is much more narrow in girth than the second dolium in the same room (6529). The lip is about 20 cm. wide and the neck of the dolium provides for an opening about half of its total girth. There appear to be some isolated etchings on the dolium but these may be modern graffiti. The sides of the dolium are at a right angle to the floor and turn in towards the top. There is a decorative band around the top of the cylinder.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the west of 6531 and 6529, to the east of the other 6533 and 6532

DESCRIPTION: Identified as a home structure. We determined that this room is a dining room. This identification is based on the location within the structure. It would overlook the atrium (however this portion is not excavated) there are no features in this room. The conditions of this room suggest it is a dining room. It is rectangular in shape the walls are plastered and painted on all four walls. Door is very high in north end of northeast wall opening to atrium. Northeast wall has picture framed in yellow and red but subject cannot be ascertained. Other three walls also show centrally framed picture spaces. Southwest wall has high windows (12 meters up) and evidence of molding at cornice level. Floor is lapilli. No ceiling remains but evidence of post holes for roof on northwest and southwest walls.

We have identified Oplontis A as a villa. We have determined that this is a serving room based on its location within the structure; adjacent to a dining room and near the kitchen and its large size. A large, high door opens on the north wall into a small corridor which opens to the kitchen. There are no particular features in this room. There is a modern ceiling. The walls are painted in third or fourth style, which shows an interest in updating this room, visible from two aristocratic dining rooms. The floor is cement and shows remnants of opus sec tile. As noted, doors open directly onto a dining room an a corridor with a door to kitchen.

It has been determined this is a domestic house shop. It is known as the House of Fabius Amandio. Room 8 has been identified as a dining room due to its form, location and decoration. The room is entered by a tall narrow doorway at the western end of the northwest wall. This doorway provides a view to the garden and fountain (6). The room is one step down from the garden with a black basalt threshold. The nature of the decoration within this room is indicative of its function as a dining room. The floor is opus signinum with lines of white tesserae forming triangular patterns. There is a central mosaic tableau. This is a black on white pattern of squares and lozenges comprising four octagons. The position of the central mosaic indicates the triclinia would have been placed along the northwest, northeast, and southeast walls. Fresco is preserved on all four walls; however, only the lower portion of the walls preserve the painting. What remains appears to be yellow fields divided by thin red bands. The detailing suggests this is third or fourth style painting. There is a line of beam holes across the upper southeast wall. There is a rectangular niche in the southwest wall near the west corner of the room (6970). The ceiling is modern reconstruction as are the upper sections of the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the east of the garden (6). It is to the northeast of the dining tablinum (9).

DESCRIPTION: This is a low rectangular masonry preparation platform with modern cement reinforcement which abuts directly onto the West base of the stairs which rise to the North. It is approximately 170 centimeters long from East to West, 25 centimeters high and 1.20 meters long on the North/South axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6117 is to the North.

DESCRIPTION: This is a deep square basin in an arched recess beneath the stairs, open only to the West. Access is restricted by a low plastered wall. The basin is lined throughout with opus signinum, and there is not apparent exit/ingress for water.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6116 is to the South.

DESCRIPTION: The low preparation platform abuts completely the southeast and southwest walls. It extends a small distance along the northwest wall. It appears that the platform was stuccoed, but there is no evidence of decoration.

House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This is a well. It is within a niche with a vaulted ceiling which is pierced by a round whole directly above the well. The hole is capped at the upper level by a stone well head. The well is plaster lined. There appears to be a drain at the northeast side. The well head is well cut stone. The niche is plastered . No paint is preserved. The archway of the well niche is stone vousoirs.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This well is located to the west of the storage niche.

DESCRIPTION: The masonry triclinium is located in the northeast part of the garden. Each of the three couches abuts a wall. In the south corner of the southeast wall and embedded in the wall is a column made of tiles stuccoed and painted. The northwest wall is an extension of the northwest wall of the garden. The couches were stuccoed and on the interior faces of the couches was a series of erotic Nilotic scenes. On the interior of the summus still extant are pygmies. On the northwest wall near the north corner are the remains of a garden painting. The surface of the couches slopes down toward the walls. In the center of the couches is a large rectangular masonry table on a southwest/northeast axis. The table was plastered but no evidence of painting remains. The triclinium appears to have been roofed.

In this large house and large kitchen 33 we find a niche in the southeast wall, midway to the ceiling, holding a lararium. Extensive fresco remains surround an arched niche. The niche is centered in an aedicula shape. The pediment is pointed red with yellow molding and a round medallion centered within the pediment. Within the niche we see the figure, probably the genius of the household, holding a patera. Surrounding the figure are many multicoloured dots which probably represent flowers. A tiled shelf protrudes below.
BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the east of the two cooking platforms 4421, 4422, to the northeast of the water basin 4424, and to the north of the latrine 4420.

DESCRIPTION: This is a fish tank in shop 20 (4891) along the arcade, north of the via di Sepulcri. This tank is almost square in shape and occupies two thirds of the north west shop space. The bottom is not excavated. The south west side is the large cut masonry block across the entryway. A similar large block is located along the southern half of the south east side. This block also has a cut drain channel near the southern end. The remaining sides are plaster coating (opus signinum) over what may be a brick structure, covered at the top surface with cement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Abuts the south west wall of the shop 20 (4891) This is on the arcade to the south west.

DESCRIPTION:
At the north end of the room there are horizontal grooves that extend across the north wall for about one and a half feet, and southward on the east and west walls. The height is approximately three and a half feet from the floor.
BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Shelf 4427 is below shelf 4580 within room 49.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is located to the southeast of the open air triclinium. There is no way of separating the northeast/southwest axis along the southeast wall. No part of the kitchen has a ceiling. At the southwest end between the stairs to the southwest and the cooking platform to the northeast is the latrine. To the northeast of the latrine is the cooking platform with dual storage areas beneath. To the northeast of the cooking platform is the water feature. The water feature is not connected to the cooking platform. The floor is indeterminate. The southeast wall was stuccoed or probably painted, although no paint remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining garden (4) to the to the northwest. Other garden (8) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Entered from the NE corner, the rectangular dining room (20) is on a NW-SE axis, immediately to the SE of the fauces. Entering from the atrium, there is a cement threshold with indentations showing the presence of a door. Much of this room is rubble from the bomb that hit the property next door. With walls only remaining on the NE and SW sides, the ruined NE wall is of opus incertum and undecorated. The SW wall, on the street side of the building, shows traces of 4th style painting with white fields and red trim all around. The floor is rubble. This room was identified as a dining room because of it's view through the atrium and tablinum to the peristyle beyond. It also is of a slightly larger size than a cubiculum would be.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 20 is to the SE of fauces 1, to the SE of atrim (2), and to the S of cubiculum 19.

DESCRIPTION: We walk through a large threshold from the peristyle area. This is a dining room by virtue of its shape, by virtue of its shape, by virtue of its view to the peristyle, and by virtue of the small patches of plaster on 3 of the walls. On the south corner there is white, red, and a small segment of yellow. There is a small high window in the wall to allow breezes. The floor is covered with weeds and stones. In the northwest corner there are a pile of stones. This is a large house. The room leads to a large peristyle. In order to move to the primary entrance you need to move to an area between this room and the tiblinium. The northwest section of the north wall has an ancient partition which contains the high window. The ceiling is no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of kitchen (5) sits a rectangular masonry structure in fairly ruinous condition. The structure is unusual in that the storage area under the platform counter is square, lacks the typical arch, and is located at the north end (rather than the usual central placement). The top shows remains of a tiled surface, but very little is extant. The cooking platform's short end abuts the northwest wall and the longer end abuts the northeast wall. The platform stands about knee high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The platform is northwest to the latrine (3985)

DESCRIPTION: The stable is located on the east side of the house. The room is rectangular in shape on a north/south axis. It is approached by two entrances: An east entrance opening on to the street and a south entrance onto hallway (5). High on the east wall to the north of the street entrance is a window opening onto the street. The roof of the stable is in line with the top of the window based on beam holes in the east wall. In the southeast corner there appears to be the remains of a water trough. The room was originally stuccoed but there is no sign of decoration. Still present are the skeletal remains of (5) equids - whether horse, mule or donkey is unknown. Along the west wall appears to be plaster casts of trees or posts which may have been used to tie up the animals. At the head of the equid found in the northwest corner there is an upside down terracotta pot. When found, one equid lay in the northeast corner, one in the northwest corner, two in the middle of the room, and one at the entrance to the east doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room (5) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: According to Pompeii in Pictures, a wall painting, now in the Naples Archeological Museum, was located on the north wall of this room. The painting is of meat, game eggs, and produce. On the right panel is a silver cup. On the left panel is a bag of money (Naples inventory number 8643).
With oven, recessed storage. Great rectangular niche above oven opening once housed penis. Betty Jo says not a cooking platform - just an oven.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Between FS # 183R basins and FS # 182R Kneading room. None Between FS # 183R basins and FS # 182R Kneading room.

DESCRIPTION: There is a large L-shaped counter along the northwest entrance and turning southeast. It has a reused marble top. There are three circular holes in the counter (two on the east end and one on the north). The dolium lip on the north side of the counter is visible in the counter top. The two dolia on the southeast leg do not show lips. On the north side of the counter there is one small and one large storage area. On the east side of the counter there is another large storage area for the use of the salesperson.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 4109 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this feature is a preparation platform. It is located in the west corner of the room. This platform has two blocks, the higher one is in the corner and the smaller lower one is to the south of the large one. These form a step-like platform. The platform is opus incertum covered with a gray mortar. There is some ceramic tile and brick inlaid into the surface. It is in fairly good condition. It is only missing a small section of the lower step.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: this platform is west of the counter (#1 -3992)

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that this space is a dining room. It is a square room on a northwest-southeast axis. This room is entered through a doorway on the eastern end of the southeast wall. This room opens to the atrium (#2). There is a white marble threshold, at this entry.
Although the walls are preserved to over four meters, the room is in poor condition. The original floor surface is not visible. There is no ceiling remaining. The walls are opus incertum. Plaster is preserved on all four walls and painted surfaces can be seen along the bottoms of the southeast and northeast walls. These areas show red paint. So little paint remains, it is difficult to discern the style. There are lines in red and yellow on the upper northeast wall which may indicate fourth style. The only remaining upper molding is a horizontal band situated along the upper northwest wall at the north end.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of the atrium (#2), and it is northwest of space #6.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular bench consisting of a single piece of tufa, immediately to the east of the sales room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the northeast of bench 4156.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This tiny room runs along a northwest southeast axis. It is rectangular in shape and appears to be a preparation room. There is a modern lintel. The lower register is plaster painted red on all three walls and the upper register is painted white plaster. On the east side of the northeast wall there are two small holes probably used to support a shelf. The walls are preserved almost to a first story height. One large hole exists on the white plaster of the southwest wall. The floor is obscured with lapilli and pumice.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 26 to the northwest and dining room 34 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular mosaic insert with marble insets into the cocciopesto floor. Border of black and white tesserae surrounding multicolored marble inserts into cocciopesto. Surrounding hexagonal hole for table base or mosaic emblemata or a similar feature. The feature is placed so that the dining couches can be arranged around the northwest, northeast, and southeast sides. A small doorway leads southeast to dining room 14, while doorway with double doors to the southwest looks out onto peristyle 15.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Other features: Paintings 6141 (a & b) are to northwest, 6140 (a & b) to southeast.
Other rooms: Peristyle 9 is to southwest. Dining room 14 is to southeast.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the House of the Vettii. We enter from the east into the fauces (Room 1) through a large doorway. The threshold is made of massive blocks of basalt set into a cocciopesto black floor with large white tesserae arranged in a grid pattern. The threshold remains, with holes for door posts on both ends. Fourth style painting remains on four walls. These frescoes are fragmentary. They include features 4665 on the west wall, and 4666 and 4667 on the north wall, all of which are paintings. Looking from the floor to the ceiling on the north wall, the dado depicts a Nilotic motif. The center panels depict several individual scenes. Above the friezes is plaster molding, and above this is a garden scene. On the south wall the friezes are fragmented. The ceiling is a modern reconstruction.
BIBLIOGRAPHY: Jashemski II pp153 - 155, Eschebach pp 218-219
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Wall Paintings:
4665 (Priapus)
4666 (Sheep
4667 (Deer)

Atrium 8 connects to the fauces.

DESCRIPTION: Mill (3089) has a rubble foundation and a meta in place made of solid porous lava; only fragmentary evidence of plaster surround.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill (3088) to the southwest; mill (3086) to the east; mill (3087) to the southeast; oven (3081) to the southeast; water basins (3082, 3083) to the southeast; kneading basin (3085) to the east; kneading machine (3084) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: See feature sheet 3-3090 for full record. This sheet provides video documentation number only. Needs to be reconciled.

The latrine is at the southwest end between the stairs to the southwest end and the cooking platform to the northeast. There is no evidence of a roof. The walls were stuccoed, although no sign of paint remains. The floor slopes from the northeast to the southwest and joins in the west corner a gutter that runs southeast/northwest all the way to the northwest wall of the house.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2979) to the northeast; water feature (2980) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: To the northeast of the latrine is the cooking platform. The cooking platform is constructed of masonry. Above the platform on the back wall are the remains of plaster, but no paint remains. The cooking platform is bordered on the southwest and northeast by a wall the height of which is unknown. The cooking platform has two semicircular storage spaces that extend to the floor. The surface of the cooking platform is made up of a cement and fragments of stone but with large pieces of terra cotta embedded in no discernible pattern.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine (2978) to the southwest. Water feature (2980) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the triclinium (9) from the hallway (8) to the west. The room is rectangular in shape on a northeast/southwest axis. The doorway is rather wide. In the northwest wall near the entrance is a niche for a cupboard. In the north and east corners, near floor level, are couch niches. The east niche is longer than the north niche. The walls show evidence of having been plastered, but no paint survives. In AD 79, the niches in the east and north walls had been plastered over. Evidence for this in both cases is the surviving plaster. The floor is indeterminate, as is the height of the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (8) to the west

DESCRIPTION:
In this very large home we have a very large kitchen, based upon the presence of extremely large cooking platforms (4422 and 4421), a large water basin (4424), latrine (4420), and painted lararium (4423) niche. The kitchen is L-shaped, with the long arm of the L on a northeast-southwest axis. A high door opens on the northeast to corridor 32. The walls are opus incertum, with parts still showing faded fresco (except for the lararium (4423) on the southeast wall, which still retains its imagery - see feature sheet 4423). There is a triangular lamp niche in the northeast wall to the north of the high doorway. The floor is dirt, the ceiling is modern. There are two high windows above the cooking platform (4422) on the southwest wall. Unusually, there is a lot of open floor space in this kitchen, as well as large cooking features.
BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
To the southwest of passageway 32, to the southeast of second atrium 39.
Cooking platform 4421, cooking platform 4422, basin 4424, latrine 4420.

DESCRIPTION: Room (8) is identified as a dining room based on it's size and position overlooking the atrium. The rectangular room is accessed by a stone threshold from the atrium on the south east side of the room. The dining room has a northeast and southwest axis. The walls are of opus incertum. The floor is coccio pesto. Faint traces of plaster can be seen high up on the northwest wall and a post-hole type opening is to be found in the upper north corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (8) is to the northwest of atrium (1), to the west of room 9 and to the east of room (7).

DESCRIPTION:
This is a small rectangular space which may have served as a storage room. The entrance is at the western corner, along the SW wall, off of the kitchen (3969). The room is on a NW-SE axis. This space is in very poor condition and is being braced with modern scaffolding.
The NW wall is only preserved to a maximum of 1.6 meters (approximately). The NE wall is preserved to 4 meters and the SE wall is preserved at a higher level. These walls are opus incertum, with plaster preserved on NE and SE walls. The SW wall appears to be a later addition.
No floor is visible and no ceiling remains.
There is a series of 4 holes along the NE wall, at about 3 meters height, which may have held a joist for a low ceiling or a shelf.
There is an opening on the SE wall which may have been a small window looking into the next house (?).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room sits to the NE of the kitchen (11-3969) and the vat (11-3971).

DESCRIPTION: In the south corner along the southwest wall is a small lararium. This is a small rectangular niche with a sloping top. Traces of plaster remain along the top (sloped) and southeast side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This lararium is just south of the small window on the southwest all. The brick archway in the southeast wall is directly east of the lararium. The vat (3971) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a kitchen with a cooking platform in the southwest corner. It is a small rectangular room. There are traces of light beige and orange paint on the southeast wall. The northwest wall that borders the street is totally missing. The entrance is shored up in the shape of a barrel vault. The ceiling is gone. The floor is pounded ground.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This kitchen is to the back of the atrium behind the dining room. Room (7) is to the northeast of the kitchen.

DESCRIPTION: As you enter the kitchen, you see a cooking platform in the southwest corner. It is rectangular in shape. The top is covered with soil and weeds. We cannot see a lip. Some tile and brick are discernible from the front. There is a triangular receptacle, to hold wood.

We have identified the space in the east corner of the kitchen room (five), as a latrine. This is based upon the wall curvature in that corner, as well as the possibility that the pieces of the terra cotta, that we see in the corner, were part of a water pipe coming from the floor above. The space today is covered with fresh and loose stones, but was previously identified by Eschebach.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is to the south east of the cooking platform (#3984) in the east corner of the kitchen room (five).

DESCRIPTION: On the northeast and southwest walls of dining room 30
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: situated above the central panels is a narrow register with a light blue background with light structural shapes that could be a balustrade. Seen
COLOR_ROLL: Lee Payne
PHOTOGRAPHER: scattered across are groupings of two cherries which appear to be on tree branches. See photo for further details.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the Imperial Villa as a villa structure. We have determined that the last usage of this room was as a daieta. This room is located at the southweset corner of the Imperial Villa. This has a prestigious location next to the reception room and the large dining hall. There are no food and drink characteristics visible. It is a good-sized room. The ceiling has been replaced. One quarter of the room has a barrel vault over a raised dais. About one-third of the walls are decorated in Third or Fourth Style. The colors are beige, white, red, green, and turquoise. On the north wall there are two doors, one close to the raised dais on the northeast wall and the other at the juncture of the northwest wall. There are two good-sized windows, one on the west side overlooking the ambulatory, the other overlooking a peristyle garden on the south. The floor is currently mud but shows a diamond-shaped tile pattern. Their pattern is repeated on the raised dais. The rectangular room is on an east-west axis. Currently this room has barred windows.

In the very center of the sales room sits an extremely large, rounded dolium with a narrow neck and a broad lip on top. The dolium is made of terracotta and stands about 70 cm. tall from the current floor. There are some large cracks on the northwest side of the dolium and several small fractures around the lip but there is no evidence of repair. It is partially embedded in the ground. It is currently filled with lapilli and modern rubbish.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the west of puteo 6531 and to the east of 6533, 6532 and 6530

DESCRIPTION: The L shaped counter occupies the S.E. part of the room. The short arm of the counter takes up about the width of the doorway and is found on a S.E./N.W. axis. Situated at the Southeast end is a 2 step counter. The 2nd step serves as a square shaped shelf. The combination of the step and shelf, in effect, creates a covering for a cupboard that extends from the S.E. end of the short arm to the S.E. wall. The long arm of the counter meets the short end at the right angle and extends to the interior of the room, about three-fourths of the way in. The long arm lies on the N.E./S.W. axis. Seen on the N.E. end of the long arm and at a lower level, is a hearth. The hearth faces S.E.. The platform for the fire is defined by a 'U' shaped RIM. The width of the hearth, is evaluated as being wider than the width of the long arm of the counter. As reconstructed, the surface of the platform, but not the step or the hearth, is made of cement and broken pieces of marble. As extant, the counter does not have any evidence of stucco decorations.

This is a rectangular room on a northwest/southeast axis. There is a doorway (no distinct threshold) in the north corner to the mill room (3). On the north, east and west walls undecorated plaster survives. In the center of the east wall a red bordered vignette depicts Venus flanked by two eroti. In the north corner there is a rectangular window to the oven through which the loaves would have been passed for baking. In the center of the southeast wall there is a window to the street. Animal bones lie in the floor against the west wall beaten earth floor. In the center of the room are three stone blocks for preparation platform (3093).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill-oven room (3) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is situated on a northwest/southeast axis. It has a plaster floor. Plaster decoration survives on all four walls. There is a smooth red lower register, coarse white upper register. Only the lower course survives in the southeast wall. The doorway to the mill room is in the center of the southwest wall with a plaster door jam and modern lintel. There is a rectangular window high in the northwest wall with a modern lintel. Placings for floor joists survive high in the northwest and west walls above which is the decoration of the floor above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill room (3) is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular masonry bench runs along the entire northwestern wall of the room. It has a plastered surface surviving in place and abuts directly against the plaster on the northwest wall of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Vat (3099) is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Mill (3088) is complete. It has a rubble foundation, a lava catillus of hourglass shape with square sockets in place on top of the meta. This mill also has a circular metal fitting to catch the flour.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill (3087) to the southeast; mill (3086) to the southeast; mill (3089) to the northeast; kneading basin (3085) to the east; kneading machine (3084) to the southeast; water basins (3082, 3083) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is at the intersection of the Vicolo dei Gallo and the Vicolo dei Gigante. It is actually on the north side of the Vicolo dei Gallo, in front of 7.15.1. It is constructed of either a fine limestone or marble. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.90 meters by 0.90 meters and is 0.90 meters deep. The ancient floor lining is missing. The pilaster is on the northeast and runs the entire height of the slab and the projection above as one piece of stone. Modern reattachment of the pilaster possibly moved it to the southeast of the original location. The pilaster is decorated with a standing rooster with wings outstretched and the spout coming through the base of a large vessel beside it. The overflow is in the center of the southwest slab with the drain directly below (approximately 0.13 meters above the bottom of the exterior of the basin). There is an opening for the pipe to enter the pilaster on its northwestern face. There are worn hand recesses on the northeastern side of the pilaster and in the interior north corner. It has no modern plumbing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The fountain is located on the northern side of Vicolo deo Gallo in front of 7.15.1.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the House of the Vettii. We have identified this room as a cubiculum/small reception room facing the atrium. It is east of the atrium, south of the main entrance, and the entry is on the western wall. The floor is cocciopesto with white tesserae. A flower pattern at the entry is still on the floor. The center is a circle pattern and inside the circle are two squares. The walls are covered with frescoes, and the dado design is faux marble. The central frieze on each wall has a central panel flanked by vertical panels with birds and vessels. The upper frieze has fish and crustaceans. North, east and south walls features holes for support beams for something (not a floor). Above the upper frieze is a plaster molding (architrave). Above the molding is another panel of friezes on all walls. The ones on the north and south sides are topped with a pediment. Remains of a plaster ceiling can be seen in the northeast corner of the room.
BIBLIOGRAPHY: Jashemski II pp 153-155, Eschebach pp 218-219
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cubiculum/small reception room (#2) is immediately south of the fauces. The doorway on the west faces out to the atrium.

DESCRIPTION:
Previous sheet #1135
Masonry triclinium in space 21 is a U-shaped structure with the northeast side shorter than the opposite side to the southwest. Facing southeast, the masonry triclinium occupies the corner between the northwest and southwest walls of the garden. The couches are covered by a thick layer of cocciopesto on the very top surface. The inner sides of the couches are occupied by a rectangular band of which the inner edge is delineated by a row or band of vertical terracotta tiles. This band, which is about 30 cm wide, was probably used for resting plates. This same band on the Southwest couch also forms the top of semicircular receptacle which is underneath. Both the outer and inner sides of the three couches show traces of plaster. The central area is occupied by four bands covered with marble which frame the fountain in the middle. The northeast couch, whose top, covered with cocciopesto, is mostly preserved, does not slope outward as much as the adjoining couches. As the northeast couch is directly attached to the wall, it is not clear how the area was shaded or protected from the elements.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 21 is to the South.

DESCRIPTION: The L-shaped counter shows repurposed marble on the top. Five dolia are seen, recessed into the platform. Four have a ceramic lip. All of the dolia are filled with lappilli about 12.5 centimeters from the top. As part of this L-shaped counter, there is a stone and tile hearth. On the long exterior side to the southeast of the counter are traces of red, painted plaster. The counter is located in the south corner at the front of the store front.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The prep platform (3994) is to the northwest. The shelves are to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This room is determined to be a dining room because of it's slightly irregular rectangular shape, the room's location, the room's large doorway, and the painted plaster walls. There are two entrance piers with no discernible threshold at the northwest entrance to the room. This room would have overlooked the peristyle and interior peristyle garden, but these peristyle's are now gone. The entire Eastern side of this house is now piled bomb debris. The floor is now pounded earth with green weeds. On the northeast wall remains red and white plaster which continues on the southeast wall and the southwest wall. The southwest wall has moldings and portions of a cornice. The wall continues two and a half meters above the molding. In the west corner of the southwest wall there is a low doorway to a small room (11). There is no ceiling remaining to this room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is continuous to Preparation Room (11) to the west and room 9 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Directly to the S.E. of the doorway in room #3, on the N.E. wall, is an indented area, fully plastered, that appears to have been cut out for the placement of possibly a cupboard. The indentation was plastered over and appears to have 4th style wall painting on it. The niche looks like it is approximately 4 feet high by 3.5 feet wide (see drawing for exact measurements). The niche abuts the E. corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This niche is in the E. corner of the room, next to the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as the Villa of Diomedes. We have determined that the last usage of this space was as a large dining garden/peristyle. This rectangular garden/peristyle is located in an immense lower garden area (59), surrounded by a colonnade. Jashemski describes five trees in the garden and other plantings. But the distinctive feature of the garden is the swimming pool located at its center which is overlooked by the dining garden. The pool is rectangular on three sides and crescent shaped on the fourth side. On the northwest and southeast corners are half-circular apses. This peristyle/garden, located west of the pool, is central to the atrium villa concept. There are no specific food and drink features. However, the size of the dining garden/peristyle suggests a prestigious dining area. The east and west colonnade are interrupted by doors. The floor is now heavy grass. One of the six columns shows a fluted Doric surface. There are four columns on the north-south walls. No flooring remains. The two columns located on the west side of the garden enclosure have traces of fluted plaster decoration remaining; white upper register, red lower register.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the swimming pool area (59) to the north east.

DESCRIPTION: The feature appears to be a square fresco, approximately one and one half meters from the ground. It shows painting in blue, white, red, yellow, and brown. It's damaged. There are four people sitting at the table eating and a small serving person/child standing, in yellow, on the table. This person appears to be serving a dish or pan. There is painted hanging food above the people consisting of sausages, meats, and unknown food objects. Located on the southeast wall; it has a red border and white background.

This is a large commercial kiln in a workshop at the northern end of the arcade. The shop is a complex of rooms, this space (2) to the northeast of space 1, contains this feature. The kiln is roughly square, opening to the northwest side. The fire chamber opens through a brick arch. The opening is in a shelf-like projection of opus incertum with a brick top surface. The walls of the firing chamber are opus incertum on the sides. The interior is not visible since it is in a locked space. The walls stand to what may be closed to their full height. A modern roof is covering it. The kiln is in the vaulted space, making the venting an open question. Overall, the kiln is in good condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This kiln is to the northeast of room 1 and at the northeastern extreem of the shop at this level.

DESCRIPTION: The south wall bottom low register follows the other four walls with yellow, red and blue architectural features (Style One). This wall is reconstructed, the wall painting (Style Two) is damaged and partially reconstructed. As part of the reconstruction, etched into the new plaster are designs tracing what may have been the original wall painting. As in the north wall, there are panels in the mid section with five panels visible. The entrance way to the corridor to the south replaced the last two. The first panel from the east wall appears to be painted architecture. The second panel has a painted bird, possibly a peahen. In the third panel from the east wall there is a painted presentation of green grapes sitting on a ledge, and possible apples. The fourth and central panel has a pedestal raised on four possible struts. Sitting on the pedestal is a single layer cake with red sides, a white top, and fruit or flowers sitting on top. The remaining panels are cut by the entrance. Above the second panel from the east wall, there is a badly damaged glass bowl, juxtaposed with the glass bowl on the northern wall. In the center panel above, sitting on top of the architecture, is a glass bowl also juxtaposed to the north wall. The bowls appear to be identical. Above the doorway is speculated that there was also a glass bowl juxtaposed to the glass bowl in the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This wall has an opening on the west side and a doorway to the corridor along the south.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is identified as an altar. It is directly in front of the Temple of the Capitoline Triad in the Forum. It is a large rectangular structure on a northwestern/southeastern axis. It stands on marble paving stones. It is heavily restored: constructed of bricks and dark volcanic stones. No cladding remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The Temple of the Capitoline Triad is to the northwest; the Temple of the Public Lares is northeast.
PHOTOGRAPHER: Larry Ludwicki

DESCRIPTION: This is a small dining room. The entrance is the entire width of the northwestern wall. This had a moderately high doorway. The lintel over the door space supported six beams to the southeastern wall to form a low ceiling. The walls are in poor condition,but preserve plaster and fresco decoration on northeast and southwest wall. On the southwest wall a decorative plaster molding is also preserved. A fine red line is visible below the plaster molding. The entrance is flanked with small projections that are pillar-like and preserve fresco with paint visible on the lower portion. On the southeast wall three poles supported a low shelf.
This feature is the remains of the couch niche. Fine plaster preserves the concave space located at the south end of the southeast wall.

A rectangular room (courtyard) situated on a northwest/southwest axis with low plastered walls along the northwest and southwest. There are large plastered drains/troughs along the interior face of the low walls and larger plastered drains/troughs along the northeast and southeast walls. The floor of the courtyard is plastered. In the northeast wall there are two square plastered windows to the east. The southeast wall has undecorated plaster and a window with a modern, restored lintel. The southern corner of the room is separated from the remainder by a partition wall. The space is of uncertain use but is decorated with red panels with a lower register of plants on a red background. There are small mythical (?) xenia with an architectural molding above. Two feline rampant on either side of a vessel with fruit on either side. There is a vaulted ceiling. The use of this space is unclear (possible ritual use?). The low wall on the southwest side of the room is recessed from the wall creating a narrow rectangular area containing altar (3112) abutting the southwestern wall of the room. Along the southwest wall are two lararium scenes: one earlier scene of two lares and one or two other figures over lying the altar and snakes has been replaced with a more elaborate lararium painting with two registers; a lower register altar with pine cone with two snakes, one on either side of the altar. The upper register has twelve Olympian deities. In the north corner a lead pipe as well as a plastered drain drains fro the water feature to the east where it joins feature 3107. In the north corner there is also a doorway with a modern lintel and a threshold with placement of door which leads top the stable (room 9). In the northwest wall there is a square window with traces of a plaster jam and a modern lintel looking it to the adjacent triclinium (room 10). In the west corner is a steep threshold through a plastered doorway into the mill room (room 3) with modern lintel. The room opens directly to the latrine (3108) to the north.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms 7 and 9 are to the north. Room 8 is to the east. Room 3 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of the room abutting the northwest and northeast walls are the plaster remains of a wooden cupboard. The cupboard is too deteriorated to determine any details except that is was probably rectangular in shape but one cannot determine the axis.

Rectangular dining room located East of the ala. The window and room face garden room 40 to the North. The room has a North/South alignment, with a doorway with a marble threshold to the North, East wall. Room has paint remaining on three walls only, excepting the East wall. Plaster colors extant are red and yellow and some traces of white border on the yellow plaster on the South wall. The floor is rubble, mostly lapilli. However, some white and black tesserae (rare) remain. There is a large window located waist height from the ground. The room also has a marble door jamb with placings for attachments of a double door. There are circular pivot holes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is bordered on the garden room number 40, on the East by ala 8, to the West by room 5, and to the South by atrium 4.

DESCRIPTION:
The room under the stairs is identified as a kitchen by Eschebach, although no evidence remains. Because of the presence of a latrine, we agree with Eschebach. The room is located on a passthrough between the two halves of the house. The room is rectangular on a North-South axis.
On the East side of the room, all evidence is located. To the North are the remains of a staircase going East, then North to the upstairs, and under that staircase we suggest the cooking took place in an arched alcove. Next to the alcove is where the latrine is located on the South and East corner of the room.
There is some plaster evidence on the four walls. The lower register was painted red. The upper register appears to be painted white. Plaster evidence appears under the stairs in the archway. The floor is rubble. No windows are apparent.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the North is hallway 38. To the East is room 36. To the South is the next structure. To the West is the passageway (andron) leaving to atrium number 4.

DESCRIPTION: The storeroom is oriented East-West with an entry from the Southwest corner on the South wall and is located Northeast of the primary entrance. The condition of the room is poor and has been heavily reconstructed. The floor is not visible and the ceiling is reconstructed. A window is located in the center of the North wall, at the top, but not at full ceiling height. Immediately below the window is a possible drain to the adjacent property to the North. Four beam holes are located on the North wall; two at Northwest end, one in center, and one at East end. A beam hole (modern?) is located at ceiling level of the East wall with a corresponding beam hole (modern?) at the ceiling level of the West wall. In the South wall traces of plaster survive from the Southwest corner to the middle of the wall - the color is indiscernible and the plaster is in poor condition.
