The entry at the Southwest end of the South wall has the lintel restored. There are 2 beam holes present. The top of the wall is at the Southwest end. The West wall is possible window or collapse. At the upper part of the wall, 4 beam holes are present: 2 at the South west end and 2 at the Northwest end.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 6 (storeroom) is located at the Northwest end of the property with rooms 5 and 7 to the South, and the L-shaped peristyle garden to the Northeast (room 21) and room 30 to the East.

DESCRIPTION: Entering off the Tablenium at the northeast this small rectangular room appears to be a kitchen based upon its location at the back of the house. In the western most corner of the room there is a large masonry block that we suggest to may have been a cooking platform. The room has plaster on the southwest wall, we see evidence of a high decorative molding above. There is a plastered rectangular niche that may have been a lamp holder. No floor or ceiling remains. Walls are opus incertum with restoration above the niche. A second door on the southeast wall opens to store room 5.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To northwest of store room 5, to southwest of area 6.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this home from the southwest through the 7th doorway from the Nocera Gate. The wide entrance shows signs of plastered walls. We see a large rectangular room probably a previous atrium. In the center there is an impluvium with a puteal moved to the center of the impluvium. The room lies on a northwest/southeast axis. On the west wall a wide and tall room with a threshold. The northwest wall has a red bottom zone. The northeast wall has two tall door openings. On the north corner there is a high window with an arched top. Looking at the compluvium, which has an incredibly small opening, the masonry around it shows designs. In the east corner, there is a cooking platform. On the southeast wall there is an entrance with a tall door with a double window. In 2011, this room is used for storage of small terra cotta materials and amphorae.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (1) to the southwest; room (11) to the south; room (3) to the west; room (4) to the north; room (5) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as a villa. We have determined that room 36 is a dining room on a northeast-southwest axis. This is one dining room in a dining room complex. The room is on the upper level. It has a very large doorway overlooking space 44. This rectangular room contains no food and drink features, however, the characteristics of the room suggest that it is a dining room. The size would permit dining couches. Currently there is no roof, although it is protected b a modern structure. On the south wall at a high level, we see a portion of a high window. On the east wall we see a large window to a smaller dining room (35) and a narrow doorway in the north corner. Tufa stones serve as a threshold. There is another doorway to an adjoining dining room (46) on the northwest wall. The floor is pounded earth. On the northwest wall between the two dining rooms, at a high level, there is a long rectangular opening, perhaps for lighting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is contiguous to a small dining room (35) to the east and another room (46) which overlooks the bay.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a kitchen in the house of Dido and Aeneas based on the evidence of a cooking platform in the north corner as well as a latrine in the northeast corner. This is a square room oriented in a northeast, southwest alignment. It is northwest of the tablinum (office), the atrium, the shop, and the street. The original floor surface is not visible due to the pounded earth, lapilli, and green weeds that are now present. Remnants of stairs are visible in the west corner of the room. No ceiling remains and there are very few patches of plaster on the walls. There are no windows, but there is a door on the southeast wall, leading to the tablinum (6).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The kitchen is contiguous to the tablinum (6) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that in the west corner of the southwest wall of dining room (3) there appears to have been an indentation at floor level rising about 60 centimeters that may have been a niche used for couch placement. This is determined based upon the appearance of the plaster in a downward curving fashion. In addition the lowest level of painting, the dado, appears to set this indentation off when viewed from a distance. Wall construction behind was of opus incertum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The niche is on the west corner of the southwest wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is the tomb of Numerius Istacidius Helenus. The enclosure is overgrown. Marble slabs covering referenced libation tubes (CIL X 1029). Tomb is on the south side of the Via delle Tomba. BIBLIOGRAPHY: CAMPBELL pp 171-172

We enter this kitchen from a hallway from the atrium. This doorway is very narrow and low. Looking from the center of the room we see a barrel vault extending into the room over the narrow door on the north wall. On the south wall in the south east corner we see the remains of a cooking platform. The storage area of the cooking platform only protrudes partially above the present floor level. Currently there is no ceiling. There are three walls with no signs of plaster. The only remaining plaster is within the barrel vault. The floor is filled with large blocks of rubble and is highly irregular.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the atrium (3) is to the west

DESCRIPTION: At the Roman Villa Oplontis A, we have determined that room 31, (partially excavated) is a dining room based upon its size and its location with a view across water feature 16 into the dining room 15. The south wall is the unexcavated wall, with the remaining three walls, the east, north and west, all showing remains of highly decorated painted plaster. The north wall has a small doorway opening to room 18, which is part of the bath complex. The large entrance to the room is on the north wall and is only partially excavated. The threshold from the that doorway contained a black and white, floral mosaic pattern, with a small step down over a marble sill. The sides of the doorway, at floor level, had cutouts for door hardware. The opening itself is very high. The mosaic floor was white with two black border stripes. The paintings on the walls contained a lower red dado with panels above with a yellow background and a black and red trim. Architectural elements are visible on the north and east walls but no central images remain. Above that is a pattern of painting, also with the yellow background and red trim, in diamond shapes, with what appear to be central medallions. No ceiling remains. The fresco remnants stop at the height of the large entrance with plain stonework above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of water feature 16. To the east of room 18.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Oplontis Villa A as a domestic villa. We have determined that the last usage of this feature 4019 is as an altar. This feature is described as: 1) an altar/lararium within room 27; 2) it is located on the eastern side in a recessed area facing the west; 3) the general condition is restored and modern. The base is heavily reconstructed; 4) The approximate size is 2 m. by 1.5 m.; 5) its attributes are as a lararium. It contained possible shelves to hold religious objects. The shrine is attached to the eastern wall. The exterior of the base of the shrine is painted. There is a red border with a painted, marbleised border. The centre is a large red circle with a yellow-orange border. The front of the base is damaged and reconstructed with no trace of paint. The exterior north side of the base is reconstructed and badly damaged with traces of red paint. On the surface of the base sits a domestic shrine which is badly damaged. It appears to have been reconstructed in both modern times and in antiquity. The space is defined by two walls at the north and south side jutting out possibly half way into the space. Today there appear to be to ledges along the inside of the space. One of the ledges appears to serve as a shelf for ritual objects.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: in a recessed area on the eastern wall of room 27.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a small space walled off from the identified cooking area to the South wall of room 37. The space is approximately 50 by 70 centimeters. The walls are covered in plaster in red paint up to about 1.5 meters. The floor is rubble.
On the East wall of the latrine, about 1.6 meters from the floor, is a horizontal volcanic stone and possible opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the North is hallway 38. To the East is room 36. To the South is the next structure. To the West is the passageway (andron) leading to atrium 4.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. Entering through to a very large dining hall from the southeast past an old peristyle with nine columns and two engaged columns that are on the next house wall. The outside entrance of the room is wide and formally decorated with plaster molded to copy marble slabs in a a second style form. There is no discernible threshold. The floor shows some evidence of a white marble chipped floor adjacent to the northwest, northeast and east corner. No ceiling is evident. On the walls is a second layer of concrete with finish coat of paint. In the east corner there is a small low doorway with a low lintel that provides egress to room twenty five. The doorway is through the northeast wall and has a basalt threshold. No dining dining features are evident except for the scale of the room and its location. The location provides a view of the ancient peristyle. On the peristyle columns there is evidence of red paint and doric capitols.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 25 is to the northeast and can b accessed through a small doorway.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This is a dining hall on a northwest southeast axis. There is a wide entrance on the southeast side and small doorway on the end of the southwest wall connecting to dining hall 24. The floor of this hall was cocciopesto with stone threshold. The walls of this hall are decorated with frescos in a first painting style. Alternating panels of red, yellow and green are divided by yellow borders, which are delineated in raised plaster. This first style decoration has a dado and wide band and the rectangular panels of the medium zone. The upper zone is also divided into rectangular panels. This room is on axial alignment with the primary entrance. Overall this room has excellent preservation on the northwest and southwest walls. The roof is reconstructed as a sloping roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dining hall is contiguous to 24 to the southwest and opens to the peristyle court 23 to the south east. There is a stairway in room 23 which located outside the eastern corner of 25.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. In the northeastern corner of the northwest wall running on a southwest-northeast axis, is a deep couch niche which is approximately one meter in length fifty centimeters high fifteen centimeters deep. The support is modern. There is no evidence of paint.

This is a rectangular room on northwest/southeast axis. The doorway with modern lintel is in the north corner opening to the atrium (2). The roof is modern. In the center of the northeast wall there are two high rectangular windows separated by a stone pillar. The square hole in the center of the pillar matches a similar hole in the east jamb. The room is currently used as a storeroom for finds and it was not possible to enter. The floor appears to be solid. The walls have plaster in some places. Sodo says that the room was decorated and white panels and that there was a scene of a colloquy.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (2) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room southwest/northeast axis. First style decoration survives on the northwest and southwest walls. The west corner of the room has been isolated as a separate room entered from theÃŠsoutheast by the construction of partition walls. The partition walls abut directly against the first style plaster decoration indicating their posterior construction. Fragmentary floor of opus signinum with traces of geometric decoration in white tesserae, against the southeast wall. In the center of the southeast wall there is a doorway with modern lintel to Room 10. The southeast and northeast walls are extensively restored and the roof is modern. Cooking platform (3026) in the north corner. Latrine (3025) in the north corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 10 to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: This small mill stone on a platform would provide flour for the household. it is located midway in room 16 along the north east /south west axis. The base and a small part of the catIllus are all that remain. The platform for the mill has space enough surrounding it to be either animal or slave driven (see measurements) it is circular with a small nicely preserved meta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the north west of water basins 5118 and 5117

DESCRIPTION: This lararium is located near the eastern end of the southeast wall of dining room 9 in the village of the mosaic columns. It is a deep, squared niche. Plaster remains on all surfaces. A small squared (and plastered) hole is cut through the wall in the upper eastern corner of the back surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is southeast and opposite the couch niche (5125) and directly south of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: This lower kitchen is entered from a stairway in the southern corner of the kitchen (10) it is presently inaccessible but is known to contain two cooking platforms.

Cooking platform along the southeast wall. Two well-preserved masonry supports for a no longer extant surface. The eastern support abuts directly against the undecorated plaster of the southeast wall indicating its subsequent construction. The original floor is poorly preserved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine (3019) is to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: The hearth is located near the northern corner of the room. It is square in shape, but the original height is indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium is to the northwest. The preparation platform is to the south.

DESCRIPTION:
Central circular rosette in the south wall of the room poorly preserved.
Possible fish depicted diving (?) down in the center of the image.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6142 mosaic and 6141 painting to the southwest.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Cindy.Comment-to the east of central rosette is a better preserved smaller rosette depicting seated figure with blue background.

DESCRIPTION: Small space off dining room number 10 situated north of dining room. Store room is southwest/northeast and is rectangular. There is a low doorway for access. Walls show evidence of plaster including what appears to be First Style tan, orange and red painting on southwest wall. Space is approximately 300 x 100 cm. Door height is approximately 150 cm. Floor is rubble. There are no windows. The space is under stairs that rise from room 8.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opens to the northwest of room 10. Room 12 is to the southwest. Staircase in room 8 is immediately to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Cooking platform extends across entire width of room 15 on its' eastern most wall adjacent to the Via della Fullonica. Cooking platform is rectangular and waist high (approximately 90 cm) with arched open storage below. In the open storage area are seen remains of a plastered floor. Cooking platform is masonry with a brick arch and has a rounded terracotta lip across the front top surface. A low (approximately 10 cm high) 25 cm square limestone block may be seen along the south wall, approximately 50 cm from the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Back of cooking platform is on east wall of kitchen, room 15. The north wall of the cooking platform abuts latrine room 14 and the south end of the platform is on the kitchen wall that abuts room 16.

DESCRIPTION: The hearth and shelf structure runs along a northeast southwest axis and the short arm abuts the northeast wall and the long arm abuts the southeast wall. On the northeast end we find a cooking platform which is small and almost square with a terracotta cooking surface which is partitioned on the southwest end and adjoins the remaining shelf. Underneath the cooking platform is an arched opening for kindling and is plastered on the southeast wall. The other portions of the structure are volcanic rock and the shelves, which are badly deteriorated today, extend the approximate distance along the southeast wall on the southwest end on the structure.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The room is located in the north corner of house. One enters the room from northwest through entrance #5. In the south corner of the room is the door to room 3. Eschebach's map shows a U-shaped counter in the north corner of the room. Nothing remains today. Neither the height of the room or type of floor can be determined, covering no longer extant. No stucco remains on the walls. Floor is obscured by vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 3 to southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. We have identified this space as a cubiculum/small reception room with a door facing southwest onto the atrium. The back half of the floor has a raised platform. Most of the original floor covering is missing. Frescoes on all walls are extant with the patterns echoing that of room 9 across the atrium. The dado is a red background with white vertical and horizontal lines creating panels of various sizes. Images and panels appear to be plants and abstract plant images. The central frieze is a pale background divided into panels by colored frames. Images within include birds, fowl, garlands, vines and a variety of symbols supported on pillars of organic trees or trunks. Above the central frieze is a painted molding separating the central frieze from the upper frieze. Mythological creatures and human-like figures adorn the space.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
This cubiculum/small reception room (18) is on the north side of the atrium and east of dining room 17.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: JASHEMSKI II, pp 153-155, Eschebach pp 218-219.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining room from the atrium on the north corner of the northeast wall through a narrow passage way over a white marble threshold with tracks for doors. A second access is a lower doorway on the northwest wall which leads to the dining room. Evidence of painted plaster is on northwest, southwest and southeast walls. On the southwest wall at the south end is evidence of yellow paint which has been covered in antiquity with plaster perhaps for redecoration. There are couch niches: a small one on the northeast wall just inside the doorway and much larger longer one which extends from approximately the middle to the south end of the southwest wall. the floor is obscured with lapilli however the doorway in the northwest wall suggests a cocciopesto floor in antiquity. There is no ceiling and walls are preserved to approximately first level height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room 5 to the northwest, atrium, and room 3 to the south east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small dining room one can enter from the atrium from the northeast through a very tall doorway with a marble threshold with cuttings for double doors. The flooring was cocciopesto with white tesserae. Both the southeast and northwest walls have doorways have doorways on their northeast ends. These are both low doorways. The door on the northwest wall connects to the formal dining room 6. The floor of room 5 is at a slightly lower level. All four walls preserve most of their frescoed surface. Crown molding remains in part on both the northwest and southeast walls. The wall decoration preserves shadowy traces of painting which suggests that this room matched room 6. The only difference is that these frescos go up to the ceiling level.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 6 to the northwest. The atrium to the northeast and room 4 to the south east.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a stone vat. It is located on the northwest wall and is a long, narrow rectangular form. This is very poorly preserved. At the northwest side, it abuts the wall and has two horizontal cuts in the wall toward its west corner. The walls of the vat remain along the southwest, southeast, and northeast sides and a low brick and tile surface remains at the northeast end of the vat. The ceramic tiles are embedded in plaster and were covered with a plaster having a terracotta matrix.

This is a rectangular preparation platform. It is located along the south half of the southwest wall to the south of the entrance. This platform is constructed of stone and preserves the remains of a plaster top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform 3173 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the small dining room through a doorway in the east corner. As wit dining room 12 next door, one must step up from room 11 at least one step. The floor is of beaten cement with no sign of decoration. As extant, the floor seems to have a high point in the middle creating a slope towards all four walls, possibly due to the eruption. The room is rectangular in shape on a north east to south west axis. The ceiling is barrel vaulted running south east to north west. The walls are stuccoed and painted in the Fourth Style. On the north east wall is a niche lararium
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 11 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the north side of the Via del' Abbondanza. It is near address 9.11.1. This fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The interior dimensions are 0.89 meters by 1.23 meters and it is 0.70 meters deep. It has an added lining to round off the wall/floor junction. Only this lining and the floor are covered in opus signinum. The pilaster is in the center of the northwest slab and is decorated with a patera or plate in relief. The overflow is centered at the top of the southeastern wall and the drain hole is below, about 0.10 meters above the street level. Worn hand recesses are visible on either side of the pilaster, as well as near the interior of the north and west corners.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is located close to 9.11.1. It is on the north side of the Via del' Abbondanza and immediately across the street (the south side of Via del' Abbondanza) is water tower #4724.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain 4824 is in front of 7.1.33. It is on the west side of the via Stabiana near the intersection with the via degli Augustali. It is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. There is a rounded lining on the wall / floor junction that appears to be coated with opus signinum. The interior dimensions of the basin are 1.18 m. by 0.91 m. and it is 0.75 m. deep. The pilaster sits atop the south western slab and it is decorated with a bust of a woman with a bird on her right shoulder (possibly Venus with a dove?) The overflow is in the centre of the top north east slab and the drain hole is in the east interior corner. There are deep hand recesses on either side of the pilaster and near the south and west interior corners. This is near water tower 4825
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: on the via Stabiana in front of 7.1.33

DESCRIPTION: We enter the preparation room from room 8 to the southwest through a low door. The room is along a northwest/southeast axis. Evidence of painted plaster exists on the northeast, northwest and southwest walls. All walls are preserved above a first story height with evidence of beam holes high on the northwest wall and one high on the south portion of the southeast wall. Five other holes indicate possible shelf support on the lower portion of the northwest wall. In the north corner of the room is an L-shaped preparation platform, the long arm of which runs along a northwest/southeast axis abutting the northeast wall. The short arm runs along a northeast/southwest axis and abuts the northwest wall. The height of the platform is approximately one meter. The floor is covered with lapilli, which however, portion of hydraulic cement are visible. A major feature of a contiguous room shares the southeast wall on the lower portion on the south end: the passthrough into the oven (3197) in room 6.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The oven room (3198) is to the south/southeast. Hall (room 8) is to the southwest. The northwest parallels and is contiguous to the street.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information provided for this feature sheet.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the counter room from the street to the southwest. There is a high step from the sidewalk and a threshold made of volcanic rocks (three large and one small). There is a deep groove running the length of the doorway and holes for door posts and one small piece of metal. The shape of room is determined by the partition indicators on the north and east corners. In antiquity the room appears to have been plastered and painted red and white. Immediately inside the door is an l-shaped counter, the long arm runs on a northeast/southwest axis. The short arm, which parallels the street, is on a northwest/southeast axis, and abuts the brick column of the outer wall on it south end with a large pile of hardened rubble in the inner corner of that space today. The northwest and southeast walls are primarily extant to just under a first story level. Against the eastern of the southeast wall are the remains of two dolia (3209 (southwest) and 3210 (northeast). Reports indicate that a third dolium was extant to the southwest previously. The surface of the counter is marble pieces which are probably of ancient reconstruction. The floor is covered with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The preparation room 2 is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The storeroom is entered from the northwest from the kitchen thru a low doorway. The dirt floor slopes upwards from the entrance. The walls show signs of ancient plaster. We see amphora to move water on the southwest wall. The location indicates this was a food and drink storage room. The ceiling of the room currently extends to the second floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen # 20-3156 to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
This is an ala (wing) in the house of the Vettii. The ala is located to the south of the main atrium. The ala has three walls; east, south and west. A black dado with a Nilotic motif goes around the lower register of all three walls. The black panels are incised, creating individual sections and simulating masonry. The middle register is comprised of six yellow panels divided by red framing. Moving from east to west we see the following: a circular vignette, a rectangular vignette, then a circular vignette, another circular vignette, and another rectangular vignette depicting chickens/fowl. The upper frieze is fragmented, the ceiling is reconstructed. The floor is black cocciopesto with large, white tesserae in a grid pattern. The remnants of a later wall are present along the floor to the north.
BIBLIOGRAPHY: Jashemski II, pages 153-155, Eschebach pp 218-219.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 8

DESCRIPTION: High on the center of the northeast wall is a niche lararium. The interior and exterior were covered with plaster and painted. There is no sign of any figures in the painting. The shelf of the lararium extended into the room to the southwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a floor below. Painting 3115 is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: On the northwest wall in the highest register, where the wall begins to pitch to form the barrel-vault, is an upright rectangular panel, framing a small round shallow basket but appears to be hanging by strings from the upper part of the frame. The string is tied with a bow to the basket handle. In the basket are eight pieces of fruit, perhaps cherries.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Painting contiguous to the room below. Lararium (3114) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This public well (or cistern?) 4820 is outside the south east corner of the Basilica on the vicolo de Championnet. The super structure, made of tufa masonry, is possibly modern as is the square metal covering on the top. The arched opening leading to the superstructure has been partially filled in, creating a very small access. The Basilica should have a cistern nearby to harvest rain water off the building - could this be an opening to the cistern instead of a well?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: on the vicolo de Championnet abutting the south eastern corner of the Basilica

DESCRIPTION: We enter the atrium from the southwest. We are on the northwest/southeast axis. The atrium is Tuscan style. The impluvium is made of twelve or. forte en volcanic stones and is ancient. The atrium was plastered in antiquity. and painted with red lower register and white upper register. On the southwest wall, west side, remains evidence of a cooking platform. The height of the wall on the southwest, southeast and northeast appear to support a second story. The north end of the northeast wall and the northwest wall height is lower. The floor is obscured by lapilli. No ceiling is extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 11 is to south east. Room 4 is to northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter a rectangular dining room from an entrance doorway off the atrium in the northwest corner of the room. The southwest wall is largely opened as a window to the peristyle portion. The floor shows evidence of a white tessarae pattern. The northwest wall has no remaining paint. The northeast wall has a red lower zone with plants. Above are two panels in white framed with yellow stencil bordered in red. A tondo is visible on each panel. The left northwest border is a male with a piercing look whilst on the right (northeast) the border is not clearly discernible. On the southeast wall we have a red lower zone, and a middle zone with three panels. The middle panel has garlands on a white background with columns in frames of green and red. The center panel fresco is not discernible. The left and right panels have cupids. The southwest wall is partially a window with no paint on the walls. The threshold of the atrium on the southwest corner of the northwest wall has third and fourth style painting on the wall. The rectangular room has corners on a north/south axis and an east/west axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium (room 2) is to the west. Storeroom (2866) is to the southeast. The peristyle portico (room 5) is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: There is no roof. The southeast wall is approximately five meters tall and has three windows. There is evidence of a small indentation for an oil lamp and a rectangular one for a lararium. This area has a mud and lapilli floor except for examples of paving stones placed around the mills, which are placed basins. We see one basin and meta, a catillus next to it, a strange meta consisting of one lava stone and one basin, and a complete but damaged mill consisting of meta, catillus and basin. These are placed along the southeast wall. There is also a kneading basin along the same wall. This room abuts a stable room which is on the northeast wall. There is a cistern on the northwest wall. There is a lava water basin on the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The stable (room 10) is to the northeast. The oven room (6) is to the northwest. Storeroom (2) is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room north east/south west axis opening south west to atrium fifteen. Stone stepped threshold to the atrium. Modern lintel to doorway. Modern roof and plaster floor. In the east wall there is a blocked rectangular window or recess. Undercoated plastic survives on the north west, north east and south east walls with holes for shelves. In the north west corner there is a rectangular plastered recess or blocked doorway with modern lintel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium fifteen to the south west

DESCRIPTION: A one seater latrine located in the Northeast corner of room 18 adjacent to a dividing wall located beside the preparation platform. The latrine is masonry construction with a limestone seat. At the rear of the latrine seat is an opening for waste disposal; the front of the latrine is also opened. The East wall in the Northeast corner is of masonry construction but appears to have had a waste disposal pipe inserted indicating it serve both an upper floor and the latrine in room 18.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is contiguous to room 17 at the North; room 19 at the West and corridor 20 at the West.

DESCRIPTION: The dining room is located in the Northwest part of the house. One enters the room from a doorway in the East corner of the Northeast wall. The room is rectangular in shape on Southeast/ Northwest axis. In the South corner of the room is a doorway leading to a storage area under the stairs. As extant neither the height of the room nor type of floor is determinate. Stucco and remains of painting are extant on all four walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fauces ( 1) to Northeast; store room 2872 to Southeast, room 9 to the Northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Room 11 is entered from the Northeast corner of room 15. It is a small rectangular room on a Northwest/Southeast axis. The Northeast and Southeast walls are mostly collapsed. The Northwest/Southwest walls are preserved to a a second story height. The roof is not extant. These walls show joist like holes scattered along the walls. The Southwest walls shows large fragments of plaster. The floor is with a thick layer of vegetation, debris and two large heaps of soil to the Northwest and Southeast. The room contains a lararium in the Southwest wall and 2 possible platforms (cooking and preparation) along the Northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 is to the Northeast. Room 12 is to the Southeast. Room 15 is to the Northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Latrine recessed into the southeast wall of the room. The rear of the latrine has a steeply sloping terra cotta tile draining into channel below. The channel is completely filled. The terra cotta tile of the floor drains into the latrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2906) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Entry from Shop 14 from the kitchen is to south in corridor. General condition is bad. No ceiling or walls. Floor shows indication of rocks and stone. Without walls there are no windows. It has a wall foundation on east and south only. The cooking platform indicated by Eschebach's map.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room (4-2908) to southeast and room 1 to the north

DESCRIPTION: We enter the room from a doorway on the southeast wall. This small room has been determined dining-other due to its location which is northwest of the counter room. Entrance 16. The orientation of the room runs along a northwest-southeast axis. The general condition of the room is poor; however, every wall on all four signs of plaster which is original. Evidence on the southwest wall and the northwest wall suggest that the room had been replastered. There are colors on the lower register of red and white painted plaster and stenciled work in yellow and red. The floor is covered with lapilli and ash. The ceiling is absent and the entrance door is notably high. Above the doorway on the southeast wall are four beam holes which were used for support of the second story.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room (1) to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 6 is located in the back of the house abutting the northeast wall. One enters the room from the southeast. The room is roughly square in shape. The height of the ceiling and the construction of the floor are indeterminate. As extant the floor has been excavated down below the original level of the room. The walls lack any evidence of plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a square room, opening in the southeast to atrium 2. There is a wide doorway with a preserved marble threshold with placings for a door and a modern lintel. In the east corner there is a partially blocked window to the adjoining property and high in the northwest wall, there is a window to the street to the north. The upper registers of all four walls are modern with a modern ceiling. Extensive plaster survives on all four walls which are decorated in the fourth style with a yellow lower register and white above with red trim. A mosaic floor survives throughout. Work of opus signinum with marble inserts and a white square pattern at the entrance to the room face a central rosette (6965).

Bibliography: Eschebach page 38.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This lararium is in the northwest corner of the large atrium with gigantic corinthium columns. This shrine is square with two top pediments facing east and south. The base is high and has a semicircular opening with a pedimental shelf which could hold various sacramental objects. There are two columns (one of which is engaged) and one rectangular engaged pilaster holding up the roof. The two back walls are bordered in turquoise with a red outlining. The two back surfaces which are higher than the main surface (creating a ledge) have evidence of paint also.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Within west corner Atrium 2, west of impluvium.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a small, square plastered altar. The plaster is contiguous with that of the wall and floor. The surface of the altar is formed by a roof tile with overlying plaster in red (?). The altar abuts directly against and midway against the west wall of the room and the two lararium paintings. There are two lararium paintings: one from an earlier phase with two registers. The upper register has two lares and two (?) other figures with altar and snakes low. A second later painting has two snakes on either side of an altar with twelve Olympian deities above.

Square holes for two tiers of shelves survive on the north east, south east and north west walls. Two holes survive at each end of the north west wall and the north east wall whilst only one hole survives in the south east corner. Two holes survive in the south corner.

The entrance to the store room is located in the South corner of the dining room (2871). The height would have been determined by the scope of the ancient stairs. The room is rectangular in shape on a Northeast/Southwest axis. Plaster on the Northwest and Southeast walls with red paint remaining, indicates that the room was decorated in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room (2871) to Northwest; dining room (2873) to the Southeast.

DESCRIPTION: In the Counter Room, we find the lararium on the northeast wall behind the counter. It is a small arched recess approximately 1.5 meters from the floor. Some remains of the original plaster still remain along the arch. The structure appears to be original. The width is approximately 20 centimeters. The depth is approximately 10 centimeters. Red and white paint survives on the north side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter on east and southwest

DESCRIPTION: Square room with door way to atrium in the south east corner. There is a modern lintel, and an ancient threshold in the west corner. There is a rectangular window to storeroom thirty. There is a modern roof, plaster floor and decorative plaster survives on the walls. The room is inaccessible and the walls are not visible as it is used as a finds store by the custodian. Traces of red painted plaster in the south west corner. Recess for cupboard in the north west, finds of glass and ceramic vessels and amphora suggest its used as a storeroom.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium is to the south east

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room north west/ south east axis. Opus signinum floor with low stepped threshold to atrium fifteen in the west. Modern roof. Doorway to atrium in the south west corner with modern lintel and plaster surviving on the internal faces of the door jambs. In the north west corner there is a large window with plaster upon the jambs and bases. The southern jamb preserves a circular indentation in plaster. Modern lintel. Undecorated plaster survives on all four walls. Two square holes for shelves survive in the south west corner and the center of the north west wall. The lines for the intervening shelves are preserved in the plaster on all four walls. The room was found to contain ceramic vessels, 2 lamps and amphora.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium fifteen is to the west

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this room as a storage room, based on evidence of shelving and small size. This is a long and very narrow room opening to the ambulatory 11 (4573) at its south end. The floor is rubble and the walls are plaster with no evidence of paint. On the north wall and the north end of the east and west walls are grooves, which probably supported an upper and lower shelf. On the west wall, 5 feet 8 inches from the floor, are two holes approximately 2 by 4 inches, that may have held lamps. On the south wall, above the door frame, is a rectangular niche approximately 6 inches by 24 inches tall.
The ceiling slants upward from north to south because it supports a staircase.

BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to ambulatory 11

DESCRIPTION: L-shaped counter facing southeast and southwest entrances. Southwest portion of the counter has two cut dolia which are notably shallow. The base of the counter is preserved stonework and the counter top is modern restoration in marble pieces, with a piece at northwest end with what appears to be a modern inscription(?). Southeast exterior side has preserved traces of fresco with red paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Southwest of lararium on northeast wall

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is situated to the south of entrance 1. The semicircular built-in structure on the lower level faces the western couch of the masonry triclinium. The vault is covered with bricks as well as the outward semicircular vault of the opening. The three walls inside are covered with plaster. The platform, on top, shows a pattern of irregularly shaped and colored tiles.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Masonry couch triclinium (2733) is to the southwest. Water pool (2735) to southwest. Water basin (2739) to south. Hearth (2734) to east.

DESCRIPTION: Entered immediately to the north/east off street entrance 8. Room appears, by masonry supports to be divided in thirds, the rear third being the latrine, the front 2/3 being kitchen. Kitchen is a narrow rectangular room on a north/south axis. The northeast 1/3 of room contains a latrine draining to the street. Two deliberate holes are inserted into east wall across from latrine south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: West wall is on the street Vicolo di Modesto. South door opens to entry way 1. East wall abuts rooms 3 and 4. northeast wall is shared with neighboring. property VI.5.7.

DESCRIPTION: A pair of masonry supports are located in the west wall of the kitchen (room 2) immediately off the west doorway to entryway (room 1). Supports are low (see sketch for dimensions). With the southern of the pair appearing to be missing about half of its length. The northeastern-most support appears to be full length. Space between the two supports is about 60 cm.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Located on the west wall in southwest 2/3 of the room. Latrine (6149) is about 50 cm. to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Located in the northwest area of the room, the latrine is defined by a sloping floor, masonry support and a niche in the wall for the insertion of a seat. The niche in the wall turns the corner from the southwest to northwest walls and ends at its masonry support about 1/3 of the way down the wall. Latrine is raised from the kitchen floor by about 10 cm. Walls are of plain masonry. Floor is currently covered with plastic which indicates previous archaeological work and protects terracotta slabs. There is no sign of windows. There are two man made holes in the east wall suggesting attachments.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Located in kitchen (2) along the northwest walls. Masonry platform supports area to the northwest and is bounded by the kitchen to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room, east west axis. Doorway in east wall opens to the garden to the east. An earlier doorway leading west had been blocked. No extant decoration on the walls, floor obscured by lapilli. Piece of remaining masonry in northeast door sill suggests the door must have opened into room if a door existed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Open air triclinium 6 lies on the northwest side of the hotel. It included U shaped masonry couch. According to Fiorelli and Jashemski, the dining space was shaded by pergola; but there is no evidence to support their statement. The triclinium faces the entrance 2 to the south. The very badly preserved conditions do not allow us to define any type of possible decoration of this dining space, except for traces of painted red and possible green painting along the northwestern wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden to the west. Storeroom 3 to the north. Triclinium 6 to northeastern corner.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on Feature Sheet

DESCRIPTION: This is a garden in the Villa of the Mosaic Columns. It is a roughly rectangular space, opening up from its entrance to fauces 12. This well documented space is constructed of walls of opus incertum which shows scant traces of plaster. Post holes along the tops of the walls suggest the presence of awnings or a roof. There is a door that leads to area 3 to the east, as well as a high and wide entrance to the northwest. Standing at the end of entrance 2, you can see the placement for the four famous mosaic columns, culminating in our fountain 5106. No evidence of floor or upper level remain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is northwest of area 3, northeast of entrance 2, east of area 5.

DESCRIPTION: Around atrium section of Macellum, now grassy, is a large u-shaped travertine gutter. It would have circled whole grassy area originally, but only segments remain in situ today to north, east and west. Gutter was used for water drainage by whole Macellum commercial space and particularly for the fish market, which it surrounds.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fish market is in center of grassy area with gutter running around its perimeter. None Fish market is in center of grassy area with gutter running around its perimeter.

DESCRIPTION: Niche remains in east wall of triclinium. Plaster remains on both inside and outside of recess and all along east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION:
On west wall to south, fresco section shows platter with fish in center and a whole top section (has) approximately 10 fish. One appears to be a lobster. To north of platter, a crustacean resembling a crab appears to depicted.
No drawing required.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To south of fresco with chicken in center. blank To south of fresco with chicken in center.

DESCRIPTION: Small one-room shop with wide opening onto forum. Structure is partially stone and partially brick, and has small sections of plaster remaining on south wall. Sections of original floor remain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North of room 5. North of room 5. blank

DESCRIPTION: Small rectangular 1-room shop with wide entrance onto forum. Southern section of threshold remains. Structure is combination of brick and stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: South of room 6. South of room 6. blank

DESCRIPTION: Large U-shaped display counter follows circuit of large rectangular sales room. Counter is of stone masonry construction with terracotta tile in seemingly random sections on top surface. Counter divides in center in east section, providing space for people to pass through. Two drains with terracotta/brick border are in situ on north and south front sections of counter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room (currently used for contemporary storage). Evidence of plaster on south wall. Wide entrance overlooks fish market area.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: East of 30. West of 32. East of 30. West of 32. blank

DESCRIPTION: A small rectangular room containing counter with dolia (possibly for oil) and water basin. Plaster on walls. A marble threshold with grooves for doors to close up shop at night.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: small back room exists with window looking into room 1. small back room exista with window looking into room 1. None

DESCRIPTION: Front room of shop is rectangular in shape and retains stone threshold with groove to allow wooden slats to fit in to close up shop. To rear/south, opens into room 2.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Connected with room 2 to south. Connected with room 2 to south. blank

DESCRIPTION: (subterranean level) Possible dining room. Large apsidal recess to the west with lararium niche at center; evidence of plaster with decorative frieze on all walls, vaulted ceiling; vaulted doorway to E; recessed space to N; two symmetrical brick-layered pipes connecting to street on west wall with large trapezoidal window. To south, square opening to kitchen; recess for bench on north wall, arch on south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen to south; hallway to east Kitchen to south; hallway to east None

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii (room 19). This room is identified as a cubiculum/small reception space. It is a small room decorated in fresco. This feature is one of a group of seven and is a small vignette located at the northern end of the northeast wall. It has a red border on a white background. There is a blue ground with a bird depicted facing to the right. There is a fruit (peach?) in front of the bird. It is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is to the east of feature 4694 which is on the northwest wall and it is to the north of feature 4696 also on the northeast wall.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room with plaster remains on southeast wall and west wall. Entrances to north, south, and west. To the north the floor plan and remaining structure bordering on the garden is difficult to discern.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opening to portico garden (11) to north. Opening to atrium to south. Opening to portico garden (11) to north. Opening to atrium to south. blank

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular shaped room with a wide entrance, doorway to north. Plaster on all walls. The beginning of an arch at the top of the east wall. A large window near the top of the west wall. Upper sections of wall have probably been reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To north lies room 14 (function unknown). Shares east wall with staircase leading down to underground level. To north lies room 14 (function unknown). Shares east wall with staircase leading down to underground level. blank

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular built-in platform against east wall. Recessed arch for food storage at base. South section of surface has terra cotta tiles well preserved. North section has additional structure that could have been a grill or oven. Top ledge of plaster around rill on north and east walls is well preserved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room with two openings (one to east, one to north). A cooking platform in northeast corner with oven?/grill? Evidence of plaster on west wall. A staircase would have risen over the room from north to south.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: south of room 1 south of room 1 None

DESCRIPTION: Alcove area containing large vat for holding liquid and cooking platform. Decorative plaster work with brick-like painting in red and white. Evidence of mosaic floor in front (north of vat); well-preserved in one small section.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: West of dining room (4) West of dining room (4) None

DESCRIPTION: An L-shaped counter with base in east opening and extending west. Two small dolia in counter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: counter located in wide east opening of room None counter located in wide east opening of room

DESCRIPTION: The south side of this dining/summer room opens to the peristyle garden. The modern restored roof has collapsed on the east side of the room. Remains of a rectangular yellow wall painting remain, it is probably the remains of the famous painting of the wedding of Hercules (rear north wall). The small altar noted by Jashemski is no longer remaining at the site.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North of ? , south of Ala #7, west of tablinum, northwest corner of peristyle garden North of ? , south of Ala #7, west of tablinum, northwest corner of peristyle garden None

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room. The floor has been dug out revealing an earlier phase of construction. The room has undergone extensive modifications. The wall from the north corner extending to the west includes two brick-built columns into which a wall has subsequently been built, and the excavated area reveals a smaller square room from an earlier phase. Along the northwest and south walls, traces of red painted plaster survive. To the north there are alcoves contiguous with this room, however, they seem to have served a distinct function. DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. We enter the rectangular dining room from atrium 26 from the southeast. We cross a white marble threshold which has post holes and tracks. There is a high modern lintel and plaster on both sides of the door jam with evidence of red and white paint. The room runs along a northeast southwest axis. In antiquity it appears that the walls were painted with a reddish color framed by darker red panels and stenciling. Evidence is most prominent on the northwest wall. However all four walls suggest the same motifs. On the southwest wall is a large window which gives view to a large peristyle of the Corinthian style. In the corner of the southwest- northwest walls there remains a pillar constructed of brick covered with painted plaster to match the walls and extending to first story level. In the north portion of the northwest wall is a large deep niche (3149). The walls are in disrepair; however they reach first story height. The floor is obscured with lapilli and there is no ceiling.

DESCRIPTION:
The garden takes up the entire southeast of the property. One enters the garden from the northwest through room 7. The shape of the garden is roughly square although in the north corner it extends along the north east side of the house for a short distance. On the northeast wall is a large aediculate lararium, in front of which is a small altar.
In the northwest corner is a small rectangular pool whose axis is east/west. The garden is surrounded on all sides by a tall wall. The interior of this wall and the exterior of the southeast wall of the house is stuccoed and painted. A small portion of which is still extant in the northwest corner. On the exterior of the southeast wall of the house is a low masonry bench running parallel to the southeast wall from its northeast end. Just before it reaches the southwest end it stops. The rest of the distance to the doorway of room 7 was taken up by a small dolium. To the southwest of the doorway inside the garden, sitting on a masonry base, bordered with stone is a large dolium. to the southwest of the dolium is a doorway opening to the northwest to room 4.
From the doorway to room 7 toward the southeast into the garden was a paved walkway about a quarter of the way into the garden, to the southwest of the walkway is the remains of a column base. If there were a matching column to the north, it is no longer extant.
Paralleling the southeast wall of the house is a stone walkway. On its southwest and northeast ends the walkway turns 90 degrees to the southeast. The walkway on the southwest end parallels the northwest wall until it reaches to the south east wall. There appears to have been two rooms, one behind the other in the southwest corner. In the rooms only a small portion remains. The walkway on the northeast end runs southeast until it reaches the southeast end of the masonry triclinium where it turns at 90 degree to the southwest and extends to where it meets the central walkway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 12 and room 7 plus room 4 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The dining room opens to the southwestern corner of the peristyle (15). In the middle of the southern wall is a window opening onto room 11. On either end of the threshold entrance are rectangular holes for doors on rectangular marble. The doorway was partially blocked in its final phase. The walls are painted with a red lower register. Above this are small rectangular panes (with a green background) and framed with black feston and poutti-like vertical panes. On the top of the panels runs a narrow ornamental freeze. Above this is a larger frieze running around the room depicting centaurs chasing maidens. On the west wall the central panel represents Perseus holding the head of Medusa and sitting next to Andromeda. The other two central panels are not well preserved. On the southeast wall a small panel represents a building with a marine landscape. Above the red frieze at the top are large panels with traces of architecture mostly destroyed.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the large dining hall (69) to the east from the triclinium. At the entrance were two columns resting on rectangular bases, dividing the entrance into a large central one and two small ones on each side. The room is quite large: rectangular in shape on a northeast-southwest axis. The floor was covered with a black and white mosaic. Central area of mosaic too damaged to tell, but seems to have been bordered by squares alternating with meander designs. In antiquity the walls were elaborately painted with large central mythological scenes on two if not all three sides. On the east wall is a scene of Ariadne abandoned by Theseus. Included in the scene are Dionysiac motifs, including Pan and an aged Silenus. On the north wall is shown Orestes and Pilas with Iphigeneia. The sitting male figure with bluish clothing is King Toantes (?).

The cooking platform on the northwest wall is much larger than those on the southeast and northeast walls, perhaps suggesting that the northwest section was a cooking platform with the northeast and southeast sections being preparation.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room with an east/west axis. The western end of the southern wall has a doorway to portico (7) to the south. In the southern end of the western wall, there is a doorway to (8) with a threshold preserving placings for door. On the threshold for the doorway on the south wall there is a geometric pattern in white tesserae in diamond pattern and two lead placings for a door or gate (date unknown). Cocciopesto flooring with large marble inserts. In the center of the eastern half of the room there is a mosaic insert around which the clinia would have been placed. The mosaic consists of black, white and red borders around a central rosette depicting a boat with pygmies in a Nilotic landscape containing fish, crocodiles, a smaller boat, a larger animal (hippopotamus ?) with a shrine and palm trees. The pygmies in the smaller boat hold fishing rods and are fishing. Walls are decorated in third or fourth style with burgundy lower register with plants and red, black and yellow panels above, burgundy border above that with miniatures of bords and sea creatures with white background with vegetation and architectural details above. Inserted into the eastern center of the north wall is a rectangular window. At the eastern end of the north wall is a plastered niche (2015).

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room with east/west axis with blocked doorway opening to the west to the Via Stabia. Three blocked doorways in north wall to room (1) to the north from earlier phase. DESCRIPTION: One enters the mill-oven room (2) through room (1) on SW part of the room. As one enters, on the right (to the south) no longer extant was a low platform and next to it, in the south corner was a small dolium (2 negative feature sheets). The the left (N) of the entrance no longer extant was a platform. Along southeast wall is the oven. Between the dolium and the oven was the entrance to the preparation room (3). East of the oven was the entrance to room 5, probably a preparation room or store room. Along the northeast wall was the entrance to room 6, probably a stall/stable. In the corner of the room were stars to the upper floor. In the middle of the room were arranged 4 mills, two flanked the opening into the stables. To the west of the mill [1874-2] was a cistern. Today none of the mills exist in situ, only portions of the mill foundations exist reconstructed. Portions of four catilli and one meta lie scattered in the room. On the north wall, to the west of the stairs is the entrance to room (7). If the mill room were decorated in antiquity, none exists today. In the northwest corner of the room is the back portion of the oven for room (11). The four mill installations are all surrounded by a stone floor most of which is extant.

DESCRIPTION:
Rectangular garden accessed by stairs in northeast corner down from corridor 55. Masonry cutter runs from the southeast corner to the east. Opus signinum floor (?) inserted into south wall above the gutter with square recess at east end. Function is unclear. Below there is a square recess with a terracotta drain above. The opus signinum floor is perhaps an insert during reconstruction of the south wall. Along the west wall there are rectangular holes: function is unclear. High in the south wall there are sporadic holes (for a mezzanine?). In the north wall there are rectangular holes. Some of the holes appear to be manmade; others may be collapse.

Maiuri found circular holes throughout the garden, each of which contained a root cavity. Jashemski identifies this as a vegetable garden. Weeding hooks and an iron brazier were found in the subterranean storerooms. The garden is separated from a lower area to the east by a low wall. The lower area is called a "heliocaminus" by Maiuri, arranged around a square, shallow plaster basin. O n the southwest corner of the basin is a circular masonry platform. To the north of the basin is the doorway to the subterranean storerooms. No traces of decoration survive. It is not clear if the bath suite in the floor above extended over the lower area of the garden.

DESCRIPTION: The room is entered from the northwest through the doorway leading down by four steps to the courtyard (room 11). The door opens into a vaulted, small anteroom, which gives access into the dining room to the west and to the garden to the south. At the back of this long rectangular room is a masonry triclinium to the west. To the northwest of the entrance is a built-in cooking platform with an oven below. Along the southern wall there are five rectangular horizontal windows looking onto the garden; nine small opening high along the north wall. The south and west walls were decorated with a large, red lower register and yellow panels above on the south wall. Three unequally spaced elements are built into the wall. They may have been used as hooks, but their function remains uncertain. In the middle of the northern wall two smaller windows open into a bedroom of the adjoining house.

DESCRIPTION: This public well is at the southeast end of the triangular forum. It was surrounded by a circle of Doric columns, of which four are extant. The modern metal cap on the wellhead prevents observing the interior. Parts of the entablature is extant.

DESCRIPTION: The cenaculum is located at the back southeast of the atrium (2). One approaches the cenaculum by way of stairs (7) to the south corner of the atrium. Ascending the stairs one approaches the cenaculum from the southwest. The room is rectangular in shape on a southwest, northeast access. On the northwest side overlooking the atrium are six columns. The end columns southwest, northeast are engaged*. The capitals are in all cases ionic. Since the cenaculum has been totally reconstructed there is no way to determine the nature of the floor, ceiling or decoration. *In antiquity, there seems to have been two railings (iron bars) connecting the columns. This is evidenced by two holes on both sides of the interior columns and a single set of holes in the end columns.

DESCRIPTION: A small rectangular room on a north/south axis. Northeast from the main entrance near the middle of the house. As one walks into the dining room through a large doorway from the west, one sees three columns with capitals that overlook the garden triclinium (19). The room is decorated in the fourth style. Lowest dado typical black with aloe plants on all four walls alternating with a yellow upright images and a yellow boarder. The second segment of the decoration is alternating red panels with white architectural details and gold stenciling. The back wall to the northeast, the first gold panel has a medallion with a face of a garlanded woman with earrings, chubby cheeks and a wistful smile. To the east of the gold anels is a thin panel of 2 1/2 pine cones with green and red garland of flowers. A large central panel has a picture obliterated. White densiling was around the picture. Next to the east another thin panel is obliterated. The final panel to the east is yellow with a medallion (Dionysus) with grape garland in their hair, holding perhaps a thrysus. The east wall shows the same yellow, white, red, white and yellow patterns as on the north wall. However, the medallion in the northwest corner is faded. The thin panels are white architectural features. The red panel is gone. Traces of yellow panel on the south wall is indeterminate. Sloping ceiling of modern construction approx. 15' feet high, sloping to the south. Traces of tessarae are found on the floor. The doorway threshold is gone.

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain is on the south side of the Via di Nola in front of 9.8.1. There is a public altar/street shrine on the corner near the fountain. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. There is a rounded lining at the floor/wall junction. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.95 meters by 1.26 meters and it is 0.75 meters deep. The pilaster sits atop the center of the southeastern slab and is decorated with a flower. The overflow is in the center of the northwestern slab with the drain near the northern interior corner. Worn hand recesses are on either side of the pilaster and near the interior southern and eastern corners. Note that the overflow projects from the northwestern slab.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This public fountain is located in front of 9.8.1.

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain is in front of 9.7.17 on the Vicolo di Tesmo at a T intersection. It is oriented northeast/southwest and is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The floor lining is missing with only terra-cotta tiles on the floor. The interior basin dimensions are 0.99 meters by 0.63 meters and it is 0.70 meters dee[,. The pilaster is atop the northwest slab and is decorated with the head of bull/ox in high relief. The fountain has no modern plumbing. The overflow is on the center top of the southwestern slab, with the drain hole below at street level. There are worn hand recesses on the interior northern and western corners of the basin.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This public fountain is located in front of 9.7.17 on the Vicolo di Tesmo.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the so-called House of Championnet, also known as the House of the Geometric Mosaics. This is identified as a double house (entrances 14 and 16) and is part of the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14 to 20. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. This rectangular room (25) has been identified as a dining room due to its position in the house and the view. We enter through a wide doorway in the southwest wall from corridor (28) along the remains of the peristyle. There are remnants of a threshold. A farther door to the serving room (26) is found in the north corner of the northeast wall. This has a fragmentary threshold of rectangular tiles separated by strips of marble of which fragments remain. The walls are brick and opus incertum. Fragmentary plaster remains on the northwest and northeast walls and southeast walls, with no traces of paint. No ceiling remains.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Serving room (25) is to the northeast and corridor (28) is to the southwest of dining room (25).

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the south side of the via dell' Abbondanza. It is in front of (north) of 1.9.1. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.90 m. by 1.30 m. and it is 0.70 m. deep. The pilaster centred on the north east wall and is decorated with a patera or plate in relief. The overflow is in the centre of the south east slab with the drainage hole below at street level. It has an added lining to round off the wall / floor junction. Opus signinum is only on the lining and the floor of the basin. BIBLIOGRAPHY: Pompeii in Pictures 1.9.1
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In front of (north) of 1.9.1 and the south side of the via dell'Abbondanza

DESCRIPTION: A large rectangular vat with low walls, on a southwest/northwest axis, blocks entrance to Room 4 from the northwest. The southwest wall of the room forms the southwest wall of the vat. The exterior walls of the vat were plastered and painted. The interior walls and the floor were covered with opus signinum. There was also an ovolo which seals the area where the walls and floor meet to prevent leakage. In the south corner at floor level is a drain to drain the vat. A second drain, at the floor level in the southeast wall, appears to drain into the cistern. The vat may have held water, perhaps used in preparing the picked grapes for crushing in Room 2.

A spear lies on the chest of the pig between his two front legs. The painting is framed by a thin red line all set within a rectangular panel defined on top and bottom by the continuous red lines and by the double vertical lines to the northeast and a red vertical line on the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
In the Villa, it is determined that this is a Dining room (R-49) because of the presence of a large open doorway to the garden (82), situated to the Northwest. The floor separators, divide the room into 3 differing parts. There are 2 couch alcoves and a square open area situated between these two. The room also has a storage cupboard niche (6926). Also, elaborate paintings, accompanied by a high arched ceiling. The room is shaped in an L-shape with a cupboard and a protrusion that is stopping the room from being totally square. The floor is of a black and white color, there are brown colors also and it is composed of cut tesserae. There are 2 couch alcoves and seen around a central panel are plain white surroundings. The 2 couch niches are banded by straight geometric tesserae. The square part of the floor is composed of dark tesserae colored X's with a black banding seen situated around the floor. Most of the walls contain intact painting that is architectural in style with perspective shown with use of columns and pilasters. Also, there is an architraves situated above.
A tholos is depicted in a circular medallion, seen on top of the East wall. Arches are framed with carved cornices, the one above a Northeast niche is intact. The southeast arch is framed, but appears to be identical. The door frame is large, with the sill not being visible due to the presence of a plaster cast of wooden folding doors that would have been there at the time of the eruption, (see Northwest wall). A second low door is present from corridor 40, seen to the Southwest. There are door hardware attachment holes, present in a small portion of the marble door sill.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the Southeast of area 81 and to the Southeast of area 48

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified the structure of Villa of the Mysterias as a Villa Rustica type of structure. We have determined that the useage of the room is a diaeta (room chamber).

The location in the structure is in the southwest corner of the villa. There is no evidence of food and drink features. The floor gives indication that this room was used for food and drink because the mosaic is divided into two large rectangles separated by a narrow rectangle with black olive leaves on white background. The larger rectangle on the south side is white small tessarae with regularly spaced groups of four black tessarae around one white one. There is a simple double black line border. The rectangle on the north side is smaller and fits into the narrower space of the room. This one has white background with a pattern of single black tesserae. There are three large windows; two on the west wall and one on the south. All three overlook an "L" shaped garden. All have large white marble sills. The only door is on the east wall on the south end. The doorway shows evidence of door hinges. There is a small rectangle of mosaic floor along the threshold with a more ornate desig of leaves and flowers.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Reception Hall 31

DESCRIPTION: This feature is the painted dado. It is black with thin white lines dividing it into panels. Each panel originally had a depiction of fruit and/or birds, although out of the original fifteen panels only ten are discernible. Going counterclockwise, starting at the door panel A on the northeast wall is a bird at the right, looking to the left where there are two pieces of fruit. The second panel on the northeast wall, panel B, is a bird on the right , looking to the left where there are two figs and a third piece of fruit. The central panel, panel C, on the northeast dado depicts one small bird to the right, looking left. There are perhaps 3 pieces of unidentifiable fruit. Panel D on the northeast wall is in poorer condition than the previous three ( A B C), but fruit can be seen in the center. Panel E is on the north corner of the northeast wall: two birds facing each other are eating a leafy branch in panel E. Panel F is located in the north corner of the northwest wall. There is a bird to the right, facing left eating olives. Panel G is located in the center of the northwest wall and appears to be a large group of figs. This panel H is located on the southwest wall. The painting to the east is no longer visible, but this one is preserved. Panel H has a long-tailed bird, facing the left with two pieces of fruit. Panel I is located in the south corner of the southwest wall, although in poor condition. It is a cluster of fruit, possibly grapes. Panel J is located in the south corner of the southeast wall. All that can be seen are two birds, facing each other at the center of the panel. It is not clear what they are eating

This is a rectangular room on a northeast / southwest axis. Traces of a plastered floor are visible at the junction with the walls. The remaining floor is obscured by earth. The doorway at the west end of the northwest wall has a stone threshold and a modern lintel. The window in the north end of the northwest wall has a modern lintel. In the center of the southeast wall there is a square window with a modern lintel looking over vineyard 6. In the east and northeast corners of the room, final phase plaster decoration survives with a red lower register and yellow above with red trim, 3rd or 4th style. This overlies an earlier phase of decoration that is also visible in the north and west corners with red lower register, white above.

Bibliography: Eschebach page 87; Amadio, B. 'Regio II, Insula 1' in Rivista di Studi Pompeiana 2 (1988), 192-5.
