DESCRIPTION: Located on the north wall close to the northeast corner is a small remnant of a fresco above the central panels. It is polymorphous in shape. The subject matter is Egyptian in theme, with a landscape with structures, nature, people, and a highly decorated altar with food offerings. The altar is T-shaped with a solid stone base. It is surrounded with yellow draping hung like a garland or tent. The draping appears to be attached to column like structures on both sides of the altar. On the top surface of the altar are three offerings. They are small and far away, but it appears to be one taller vessel (perhaps a bottle for drinking?) and two smaller objects that could be food stuffs. There is a tall man dressed in an Egyptian kilt who may be the officiating priest. Behind him are these other figures in the distance who appear to be doing something related to the water in the background.

DESCRIPTION: (Courtyard) Room 9 is located in the Southeast part of the house. The room is rectangular in shape on a Northeast-Southwest axis. One enters the room from the Northwest by way of Room 7. On the Southeast wall to the Southwest, a wall runs northwest-southeast to about halfway into the room, dividing the room into unequal parts. In the North corner is an oven. In the east corner, along the Northeast wall, there was once a fountain and built-up basin (according to Eschebach). On the Southwest wall there is a doorway to Room 11. The floor seems to have been of cocciopesto and there is evidence along the Northeast wall where floor and wall meet, there is an ovolo. Along the Northwest wall from the oven running in a westerly direction, the floor slopes toward the Southeast as evidenced by a built-up area using roof tiles. It seems that the floor of the room may have generally sloped toward the area of the fountain. The walls of the room were stuccoed in antiquity, but no decoration remains. The wall that runs at a 90 degree angle to the southeast wall has two small windows in it, looking into the large part of the room. In the south corner of the Southwest wall is a window into Room 11.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain iis at the southern end of the Via delle Scuole at the intersection with the Vicolo della Regina. The fountain is in front of 8-2-20/8.2.21. The fountain is constructed of brick and rubble faced with large-inclusion opus signinum on the interior and exterior. The interior dimensions are 0.99 meters by .89 meters. There is a lining to round off the wall/floor junction and interior corners have rounded protrusions. The pilaster is offset on the southeastern wall and decorated (possibly) with a recessed patera or plate. There are worn hand placements visible to the east of the pilaster and near the northeast and northwest interior corners, as well as mid-wall on the northeast and southwest slabs. The drain is at the west corner of the fountain. There is a street shrine at the intersection of 8.3.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is northwest of 8.2.21 and 8.2.20.

DESCRIPTION: The biclinium lies in the western corner of the garden. The longest arm is on a northwest southeast axis, perpendicular to room #2 to the southeast. The short arm is on a southwest northeast axis, parallel with room #2. To the northeast there is a low wall running northwest to southeast that joins the shorter arm of the biclinium on the northeast and abuts a pillar to the southeast. How high this wall was is indeterminate. In the area formed by the benches off center towards the south was a well head that may have also been used as a table base for the biclinium. On the southeast end of the long arm there is a water channel extending to the south that parallels the southeast end and extends to the south/southeast allowing for water to drain off when cleaning the biclinium. The floor in front of the area of the biclinium is indeterminate. The height of the original ceiling is unknown. The entrance to the biclinium from the southeast, judging from the remains of a threshold, was capable of being closed off. The southwest and northwest walls were stuccoed and painted. On the southwest wall there is a window to room #1. The decoration on the southwest wall shows garlands at the top of two panels. The decoration in the panels are difficult to discern, but may have been a garden scene, although to judge from the decoration on the northwest wall there may have been a small panel within each larger panel. The decoration on the northwest wall is divided into three sections with an overall erotic theme. The western most section shows a framework of vines with birds at the top. In the upper left hand corner appears to be a cluster of phalli. A large phallus is in the center with two smaller phalli below. All three incorporated within the outline of a larger phallus. In nearly the center of the panel there is a smaller panel which seems to show a sacro-idyllic scene. Below this where the wall is indented, is a painting of a statue of Venus holding a mirror and to the right of the statue of Priapus. The center panel also has a framework with a smaller central panel showing a bedroom scene with sexual activity. The third and smaller panel is too damaged for description.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None Room #2 to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: We enter into the kitchen from the atrium to the northeast of the kitchen. It is a relatively small door with a modern lintel, not too high with no indication of a threshold. This kitchen shows evidence of plastering with no painting. On the northwest wall there is a raised cooking platform in the north corner. There is a rectangular on the southwest wall , an open rectangle within the platform. The open rectangle possibly could have contained a grill. The plaster continues to the bottom of the rectangle.

DESCRIPTION: This water tower is on the northeast side of the Vicolo di Eumachia street at the intersections of the Vicolo del Balcone Pensile. It is at the western corner of 7.10.7. The other pipe recess is on the northwest face close to the west corner. There is a heavy calcium carbonate accumulation down the northeast face of the tower. There is some calcium carbonate scaling inside both recesses. On the southwest side of the tower there is infill between the tower face and the brick wall of 7.10.7.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This water tower is located on the Vicolo di Eumachia at the intersection with the Vicolo del Balcone Pensile. It is at the western corner of 7.10.7

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room on a northwest/southeast axis. The plaster floor has been preserved throughout. In the center of the northwest wall there is a doorway with a modern lintel and no defined threshold. In the center of the northeast wall, there is a large window looking northeast to room (9). Extensive modern restoration is apparent in addition to the modern lintel. Third style painting survives extensively with white panels with green trim and garlands. Green and yellow architectural elements and black lower register are present. The figurative and landscape center pieces survive on the southwest wall, including a depiction of tropheum. High in the northwest and north, molding and the molding for a vaulted ceiling survive, above which is a placing for joists. They match two surviving joist holes in the south corner. In the northwest corner the plaster continues above the height of these joists, indicating a false ceiling. The room is modern. There is a cooking platform (3007) against the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (5) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: A west facing dining room with a wide entrance to the west. Flooring is black & white tessarae. Outer boarder is black tessarae with a regular linear symmetrical pattern of white tessarae. Counter boarder on the outside is a reverse swastika with a flora pattern of one stem and leaves in each corner. Inside this is a large circle with eight pie triangles inserted with diamonds. The southeast corner has a door to the atrium (2). There is also an east lower door, leading to a cubiculum (12). The walls rise to the restored ceiling with fourth style painting evident on all four walls. The most complete panel is on the northeast wall. Other walls do not have much left but appears to repeat the pattern and the colors. The bottom panel is red with gold stenciling with one yellow flower with leaves in green. This panel is divided from the upper panel with a white boarder. Central to the wall is a red panel bordered by yellow in a sloppy panel with a white stencil boarder. The figure is a seated woman wearing white with her arms raised from the elbows. Something is on the floor to the left of her but it is indeterminate. The central panel is framed by cream color columns, followed by twin green boarders contained within each. The architectural section to the left of the central panel is all yellow. The one to the right is mottled red with yellow and a mostly yellow bottom with red on the top. Ceiling is reconstructed at about 10' high. In the architectural panel are balconies with deep perspectives with a bird on the balcony. There is a portion of a hunt scene with a dog on the right chasing a deer or rabbit into a net. On the east wall is a miniature picture of a bust of a woman with a lovely face and necklace.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None Atrium (2) to the southeast, Room 14 to the west, Cubiculium (12) to the east.

The original height of the ceiling in indeterminate with modern construction but was probably considerable. The walls were stuccoed and painted apparently in fourth style, though details are hard to determine. In the south corner of the southeast wall is a round hole in mid-height, most likely not ancient. In the north corner of the northwest wall there is a narrow niche from floor to ceiling of unknown purpose.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the south side of the via dell' Abbondanza near address 2.3.5. It is near the intersection of the via dell" Abbondanza and the northern end of the vicolo di Guilia Felix. The basin is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. It has an added lining to round out the junction of the floor to walls. The ancient pilaster is missing and there is a modern one in its place, with modern plumbing. The overflow is at the center of the northwestern slab and the drain hole is at ground level directly below it. There are worn hand recesses on either side of the pilaster, particularly to the northeast, as well as at the interior south and east corners, again, particularly on the east. The basin's interior dimensions are 0.90 m. by 1.24 m. and it is 0.70 m. deep.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined this structure known as the Villa of the Mysteries as a commercial and residential establishment. This room has been identified as a serving room (44) due to the size and location. One enters this room through a doorway in the southwest wall and passes directly to the south into dining room 43. Both doors have marble thresholds with door post holes. This is a rectangular space on a northeast - southwest axis. It is a small room and appears to be a late partitioning of the larger space with partition walls at the northwest, northeast and southeast. Only the bottom sections of these walls remain. These walls are painted black with a thin red band separating the dado from vertical panels above. The mosaic floor is black and white cut stone tessarae set diagonally. A black border flanked by white stripes is set in alignment with the walls of the room. The central field has dotted lines of single black tessarae, while the border defines the northeast, southeast and southwest sides. The northwest edge is seen in the contiguous room (46). It is thought because of the pass through to the dining room (43) that this space would have been used as a passage and space for a serving area. This area is now under a modern ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of dining room 43 and to the northeast of reception area 42.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a crossroad shrine. It is attached to a water fountain (4275). It is situated on the corner of Via di Castricio at house 1.13.10. It is opposite a large public entrance to the palaestra area. This is a large rectangular altar; approximately half of the surface is missing. The platform would have been a long rectangle. The fountain shows a matronly woman with a wide open mouth wearing a braided hairstyle. No plumbing currently exists. The basin is large, rectangular and deep and is drained by a round hole at the base of the front of the fountain.

This is the so-called House of Championnet. It is also known as the House of the Geometric Mosaics. We have identified this section as separate entity which one enters through entrance (13). This establishment has been identified as a restaurant and so this room was ____________. Room #5, which is located directly off the atrium (2) adjacent to the fauces (1) is a square space with a doorway on the west corner of the southwest wall. This small space preserves rough remains of cocciopesto flooring although it is in very bad condition. All the walls preserve the remains of plaster and fresco. Although these are in poor condition, they preserve remains of a dark dado with white panels above. Traces of wide bands separate the white panels at the center of the northwest and southwest walls. The construction is opus incertum. No ceiling remains. Overall the spaces in poor condition.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is to the southeast of the fauces (1) and to the northeast of the atrium (2).

DESCRIPTION: This water tower is on the south side of the Via dell'Abbondanza immediately across the street from public fountain 4723. It is at the northwestern end of the Vicolo di Paquius Proculus at its intersection with Via dell'Abbondanza. The tower abuts 1.6.1 on the southwest face of the tower. The tower is made of brick and has deep pipe recesses on the northeast, northwest and southwest faces. All recesses have a build up of calcium carbonate. The northwest and northeast faces also have calcium carbonate outside the recesses. The northwest face has remnants of iron nails at 1.97 meters and 2.10 meters from current sidewalk. Currently, the Vicolo di Paquius Proculus is closed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This water tower abuts 1.6.1 on the tower's southwestern face. It is across the Via dell'Abbondanza from public fountain 4723.

DESCRIPTION: This painting in Dining room 2 is part of a suite of five remaining paintings. This painting is on the southwest wall. No border remains, but an elegant black cooking pot with a handle is shown on a cooking platform with shelves.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified space 4304 as a space for public eating and drinking. This feature (4305) is a wall painting in situ. CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is on the wall above the shrine 4303, and is to the southeast of fountain 4306.

It is most likely not in situ. The latrine is located near the east corner of the northeast wall.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed.

This structure is also known as "House of Theseus", "House of the Seven Skeletons", and "House of the American Admiral". It has been determined that this early house may have been used as a commercial property or solely as domestic. We enter this preparation room from the ambulatory. It looks like it had a small doorway and four walls, although it may have had a low wall on the ambulatory side. The floor is strewn with boulders, vegetation, and lapilli. This is a square room and there is some plaster evident with faint beige and white paint on the walls. The wall to the ambulatory is low and would have been useful for sliding prepared food through to the ambulatory. On the other hand, this room could have been used as a cubiculum (or guest bedroom) because it has a low doorway to the adjoining dining room. This is not uncommon in some houses and businesses.

Eschebach 257

No

DESCRIPTION: MINORITY REPORT: This is a rectangular room on a northeast southwest axis. This room is locked within a locked structure. On the east side of the fauces overlooking the atrium is a dining room. The door is high and it overlooks a light well past the atrium. We enter and see all four walls in place and a restored ceiling. The floor is cocciopesto. There is a window on the rear northeast wall about 12 feet high. All four walls are decorated in fourth style. The northeast wall has a black lower panel, as does the southwest wall. The southeast and northwest panels are cream/peach in color. There is a red boarder on the northeast, west and southeast walls, and half in the west wall. It is not apparent in the niche. The next panel, shows gold stencils with architectural elements. On the southwest wall is a framed picture of a bird. There is also a winged lion. There are two deer. The top panel is different with a yellow band with minimal architectural elements. Two couch niches are seen on the southeast and northwest walls. The two niches extend almost the length of the walls. They are sloped at the top and painted. The architectural elements on the southeast, west and northwest walls depict temples.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (2) to the southwest Atrium (2) to the southwest None

DESCRIPTION: The masonry triclinium lays of the west side of the horticultural. The triclinium abuts the wall and fauces to the east. The right couch on the northwest side is fitted into the corner and abuts the west wall and the north end of the north wall that projects from the west wall. The left end couch does not abut the west wall. The left north middle couch abuts the west such that there is a narrow path behind the triclinium that extends almost to the right couch. The couches slope back from the inside. On the inside edge of each couch is built-up to form a ridge. The ridge on the right hand couch beginning at the point where the middle couch meets it turns slightly to the northwest direction where it continues into the west wall. The ridge then continue to the north and then to the east at the east end of the right hand couch. The path behind the triclinium does not extend completely to the right couch, but is blocked by a rectangular structure attached to the middle and end of the right couch. The right and middle couch are slightly higher than the left couch. The triclinium surface is of cement with crushed terracotta. The sides were covered with plaster and were probably decorated. Some red paint remains on the end of the right couch.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: The water feature lies to the southeast of the cooking platform, abuts the north and east walls, and lies at a level lower than the surface of the cooking platform. The water feature is divided into two parts. To the northwest is a niche, possibly for the storage of some sort of water container. The northwest wall of the niche is shared with the southeast corner of the cooking platform and rises above the cooking platform to an indeterminate height. To the southeast of the niche is a tiled surface that slopes down and toward the back wall where there is a drainage hole in the wall that extends to the outside street. The anterior tile has a high lip. The anterior tile in front of the niche may also at one time have had a similar lip. To the front of the water feature and at a lower level there seem to be remains of a step.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2707) to the northwest. None Cooking platform (2707) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: A large rectangular garden on a northeast/southwest axis. Along the east wall, to the north opening to a portico with a large plastered water basin with three terracotta drains at the base of the north and northeast corners. Adjoining the basin to the north is a circular, plastered cistern head. To the south of the water feature, central to the east wall, there are stairs to the floor above. Below the stairs is a plastered water channel running from the water basin, diagonally, through the wall, under the stairs and joining a terracotta channel that runs along the east wall to the eastern corner of the room. Traces of faded pink plaster lie at the junction of the channel and the eastern wall. In the angle of the channel, beneath the stairs, there is a low masonry platform with a central hole. At the eastern end of the south wall, a masonry cooking platform (2624). To the west of the cooking platform there is a masonry triclinium (2623). Traces of undecorated plaster survives on the wall to the south above the cooking platform and couch. Jashemski reports 49 root cavities, four of which were large trees at the edge of the garden. Large roots near the south wall were olive trees. Olive pollen was found in the area of #2623. A large root cavity near the north wall was a fig tree, carbonized figs were found in the area. Fragments of planting pots were found along the north wall. Carbonized beams were also found in the garden. In the southwest corner, a limestone block, which Jashemski says may have been an altar. At the southern end of the east wall, there is a square window with a modern lintel overlooking the atrium. To the west of 2630 there is an unidentified masonry feature with a rectangular hole.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 14 to the northeast Room 14 to the northeast None

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the south side of the via dell' Abbondanza between address 2.1.2 and 2.1.3. It is southeast of the Gladiator School and southwest of the House of the Moralist. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. It has an added lining to round out the wall to floor junction. There is opus signinum only on the lining and floor. The pilaster is located on the southeast slab and is decorated with a bull's head. The overflow is centered at the top of the northwestern slab with the drain hole at street level directly below it. The pilaster has no working modern plumbing. The basin interior dimensions are 0.89 m. by 1.23 m. by o.71 m. deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is located in front (north) of address 2.1.2 and 2.1.3.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is outside the northwestern corner of the triangular forum. It is in front of 8/7/30. It is on the south side of the Vicolo delle Pareti Rosse near the intersection with the Via dei Tretri. It is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. It has an added lining to round the wall to floor function. Interior dimensions of the basin are 0.95m. x 1.17m. and it is 0.69m. deep The pilaster is on the southeastern slab and is decorated with what appears to be the face of a Triton. Worn hand recesses are on either side of the plaster near the east interior corner and about 0.20m. out from the south corner (because of the slab joint). The overflow is in the top center of the northwest slab. The drainage is at the center bottom of the southwestern slab. There is no modern plumbing operating.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is located at the northwestern end of the triangular forum in front of 8.7.30.

DESCRIPTION: This is a commercial establishment with a shop, vineyard, and processing spaces. We have determined that this is called the House of the Wine Handler or also the House of the Isis Lararium. This space has been determined to be an Atrium (2) due to the position of the room in the house and the presence of an impluvium and cistern, It is a large square room with alae entered through a "fauces" (3) on the southeast wall. Also on this wall is a narrow door a shop (1) and a door to dining room (4). On the southwest wall there are doorways to rooms 14 and 13. A Lararium (5007) is between Room 13 and the ala. On the northwest is a wide entrance with a large threshold to Room 12. On the northeast wall there are doorways to Rooms 5 and 6, and the ala. An impluvium remains surrounded by shaped stone edging. The floor consists of lapilli and weeds. The walls have no signs of paint and no roof remains. A well head is located north of the impluvium.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified structure 1,3,5-6 as a food and drink shop, large, based upon its size, location near to theaters, the presence of a counter and its architectural details. The room is rectangular in shape and sits on a southwest to northeast axis. There is a door in the west corner on the southwest wall and a second door midway in the northwest wall, which has a step up into room 3. The existing arched area only covers the back northeast quarter of the room. The walls are opus incertum with traces of fresco on the northeast and southeast walls. There are traces of red, white and green paint on the fresco. The floor is lapilli.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular shaped room on a northeast southwest axis. A small doorway in the center of the southwest wall to the atrium with no threshold and a modern lintel. Plastered floor can be seen along the northeast wall, also poorly preserved plaster is seen on the southeast wall. Plaster survives on all four walls with a pink lower register and white above. This overlies earlier plaster decoration in the northwest wall with a red lower register and white above. At the north end of the northwest wall, a spherical hole looks through the wall. In the center of the northeast wall is a square window with a modern lintel looking through to a small garden to the east. High in the southeast wall there are four holes for possible joices. In the middle of the southeast wall are two smaller holes. Diagonal to and above the east hole there is a small circular hole through the wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is an altar tomb dedicated to Naevoleia Tyche, tomb 7. It is determined that this enclosure tomb is comprised of large tufa blocks. There is a door to the enclosure on the southeast corner with the tomb on the west. Entrance to the chamber/tomb is in the rear (south). The arched chamber has a bench on three sides: northwest, northeast, southeast, with two arched niches (loculi) under each bench. Above on the northwest wall are two additional arched loculi; two more loculi on the southeast wall; and one rectangular niche on the northeast wall. There is an upper arched window on the southeast wall. Virginia Campbell observed two columella on the west side, no longer visible. Campbell also reports three glass cinerary urns, four terracotta urns, and 18 lamps. BIBLIOGRAPHY: CAMPBELL p 172

DESCRIPTION: This water tower is a little more than ten meters north of public fountain 4824, on the northwest corner of the intersection of Via Stabiana and the Vicolo degli Augustali. DESCRIPTION: A large open ala, the walls of the southern and eastern corners of the room are no longer extant making the shape of the room unclear. Fontana's aqueduct runs through this area and is probably responsible for its destruction. A section of wall in the southeast corner survives, possibly demarking a large doorway at the south end of the east wall to the atrium. There may also have been a large opening in the southern wall to corridor #13. Lower register of plaster survives in the northeast and west walls. Black base, yellow above with black trim and red above. High in the northwest corner, there is fragments of stucco molding. Traces in indeterminate plaster and tile of the western end of the north wall. Inserted into this is a circular recess. Below this inserted into the northwest corner of the wall and overlying the earlier plaster decorations is a large masonry platform with a tiled surface that opens to an oven (2605).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room #13 (hall) to the south, room #4 (atrium) to the east. Room#13 (hall) to the south, room #4 (atrium) to the east. None

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a commercial structure known as the House of the Wine Handlers. It is also known as the House of the Isis lararium. This space is identified as a vineyard based on the presence of eight large dolia. While unexcavated by Yashemski, it was presumably a vineyard and is presently planted with approximately 100 grape vines. The vines are in eight rows going the length of the space in northwest/southeast alignment. In addition to the planted vines, there were eight dolia near the eastern corner, seven of which remain intact (4985, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90, 91 and 92). Dolium 4985 is the only one seen in fragmentary remains. Room 10 occupies the eastern corner of this large space. The walls are opus incertum and preserved in fair condition at their lower levels. One enters through a doorway near the center of the southeast wall. This space is at a slightly higher level than space 12. The walls have only one window preserved near the center of the southwest wall. It is a small high square window.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is to the northwest of processing area (12). It is a corner house with roads on the northwest and southwest sides.

CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is located at the northend of a line formed by dolia 4990 and 4991.

DESCRIPTION: This is the Villa Arianna. This space (6) has been identified as a dining hall. This is a very large rectangular space on a northwest-southeast axis. The entrance to this room is the entire width of the north-west wall and originally extending past the modern partician. This is evidenced by the remaining flooring which is a black mosaic with a random scattering of colored marble pieces. Two white stripes mark the perimeter of the room. There was a doorway at the west end of the south-west wall into room 5 as evidenced by the side of the threshold stones which are grey with cuttings. The front part of the room steps out wider than the rest of the space. The north-east and south-west walls are not fully preserved at their north-west ends. Although the walls are highly reconstructed there is brickwork visible at the bottom and partly up the wall and where the room narrows. The north end of the north-east wall also reveals grey stone opus reticulatum. A great deal of the lower portion of the fourth style frescoes remain. There is a high clad with a red background interrupted by painted niches with black backgrounds. Enough of the central zone of each wall remains to see that large panels depicting mythological scenes are featured on each wall. These include Dionysus at Naxos on the south-east wall
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hippolitos on the north-east wall
BW_ROLL: This room is to the north-east of space 5. The present walkway is the north-west side of the space.
COLOR_ROLL: Larry Ludwicki
PHOTOGRAPHER: Ambrosian on the south-west war and Zeus and Gamymede at the west end at the south-west wall. The south-east and south-west walls preserve enough of the painting flanking the mythological scenes to see windows looking out. Each window has a small pointed vignette below its sill. The vignette below the window painted at the south-end of the south-west wall feature 4709 depicts figs and a cup. The painting does not survive at the upper portions of the walls. The ceiling with a small centered vault was painted and is under reconstruction. The room is in fair to poor condition.

DESCRIPTION:
The commercial property1.13.13 is a wine handling facility and we have identified Room 10 as a storeroom, based upon its small size and position in the house with direct access only from the kitchen. The room is rectangular on a northeast/southwest axis. entered from the southeast by a small low doorway. Centered on the southwest wall is a small rectangular window opening to the horticultural area 11. The walls are opus incertum and no trace of plaster exists. Above the door on the southeast wall a series of 8 postholes indicate where the ceiling would have been, The room is currently open tot he sky and the floor is covered by lapilli and weeds.

Bibliography: Jashemski 96-97; Eschebach 70
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Storeroom 10 is to the northwest of kitchen (room 8).

DESCRIPTION:
Along the east and south east walls of storeroom 4299 are placings for five shelf supports. A further placing survives in the south west corner, although the restoration of the west wall of the room obscures any placings that may have been there.

Eschebach 86; Ruddell 80; Amadio, B. 'Regio II, Insula 1' in Rivista di Studi Pompeiani 2 (1988) 192-195

This structure is located at the second north entrance from the Nocera gate. We enter and pass a northwest room. There is a storage room to the south. Continuing, another northwest room was probably used for food storage or preparation.
This space is a garden dining peristyle. As we look at the northwest wall, we see a plastered surface behind the triclinium; it is an orange and red wall. Facing west, there is a window to the preparation room. The northwest wall is high. A third of the space is utilized by a triclinium. The space is delineated by a clear stone narrow border which separates the dining garden peristyle and the garden with the altar.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Other garden (8) to the northeast; kitchen (7) the southeast; room 5 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Colonnaded hallway to peristyle garden. With northwest entrance, two southwest entrances and one southeast door to cubiculum/dining room with lararium above. On southwest are four columns with a balustrade and arches spring from columns. On southwest wall to the west of the first southwest door about six feet up is a lararium with ledge.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room (2727) to the west; cubiculum/dining room to the south; garden to the east. Dining room (2727) to the west; cubiculum/dining room to the south; garden to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Masonry U-shaped triclinium. The western arm preserves red plaster facing. The surface of the couch is plastered and slopes down towards the three walls. The southern and eastern couches are less well preserved. Between the arms is obscured by vegetation, lapilli and earth. Drawings from Jashemski and PPM do not show any feature between the arms of the couch although Oliva's drawing in PPM has a circular capstone. At the northern end of the western arm a drain has been cut into the surface of the couch which drains into a terracotta drain at the base of the N face of the couch. The water will then have drained across the opus signinum floor to the drain into cistern 2518. Above the western arm of the couch there is a large window to room 9.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Above the eastern arm is lararium 2516. NW is cistern 2518; N is cooking platform 2519. None Above the eastern arm is lararium 2516. NW is cistern 2518; N is cooking platform 2519.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is located in the SE corner of the horticultural space #3. One enters the kitchen from the NE. To the SE is a vaulted niche with two masonry supports for a cooking platform. Each abutting a wall. In the SW corner of the kitchen is a latrine. To the NW of the latrine is a small storage space. On the SW wall is a large window. The floor is indeterminate. As extant, the ceiling seems to have been vaulted, but higher than the vault over the cooking platform. The walls were stuccoed and probably painted in antiquity, but no decoration remains. The vaulted ceiling supports a stairway to the upper floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Horticultural area #3 to the N. Horticultural area #3 to the N. None

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is on a northeast-southwest axis. It opens through a wide doorway in the left half of the southwest wall to atrium 2. There is no visible threshold. Extensive restoration of the upper courses of the wall is evident. Undecorated plaster survives in the north and northeast wall. In the center of the northeast wall is a rectangular window to the street with a modern lintel and bars. The floor is unlevel beaten earth and plaster. Along the northern side of the room there is a pile of earth and debris contiguous with platform 4270.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 is to the southwest.

To the Northwest of the counter is the entrance to room 2. To the West is the kitchen (3). To the Southwest is the entrance to room 4. The floor is cocciopesto. The walls were stuccoed and painted, however, the decoration is indistinct. On the Nortest wall is a lararium. On the Southeast wall in the S corner is a rectangular window. Height of the ceiling is indistinct although as reconstructed it may have been considerable. In the South corner of the Southwest wall there seems to have been constructed a niche running at least to the height f the window of the Southeast wall.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular dining room on northeast/southwest axis along northern wall of house, west corner. Entrance to room is a medium-sized doorway in southeast corner. View to the doorway is through a columned atrium. Walls are heavily plastered with bright red paint on the lower register and possibly white or yellow above. Some traces of yellow border design on the red. No windows are obvious. Floor is rubble. South door jam contains inset for door closure. Deliberate blind opening approximately 240 cm above ground level in center of north wall.

This is a commercial establishment with a shop, vineyard, and processing spaces. We have determined that this is called the House of the Wine Handler, also known as the House of the Isis Lararium. This lararium is situated on the southwest wall between the entrance to Room 13 and the ala. It is a large aedicula shrine. The pediment shows mosaic in lapis lazuli blue and yellow and red stones, and white shells. The large rectangular opening has modern restoration at the top, two painted sides and back. The base does not remain, The decorations are unique and show red flowers, which may be roses, and at least 12 red figs. A sistrum of Isis is seen along with 2 caducei, 2 sistula buckets, and green foliate infill. It is currently in a state of deteriorating repair.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This lararium is on the southwest wall between the ala and Room 13.

DESCRIPTION: The triclinium is located at the front of the house in the north corner. One enters the room from the southwest. The room is rectangular in shape on a southwest to northeast axis. There is a doorway in the south corner leading to room 4. The height of the room is indeterminate, but judged from the stucco on the northeast wall it was vaulted. The walls are stuccoed and elaborately painted in the 4th style with central panels on the southeast, northeast and northwest walls. In the east corner along the southeast wall is a couch niche with low ridge to support the dining couch. The floor is entirely of beaten cement with a simple design of white marble tesserae surrounding a central square panel of blocks of colored marble. In the west corner of the northwest wall abutting the northwest and southwest walls is a low hearth. High on the northwest wall are two windows. One near the northeast corner and the other toward the northwest corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (4) to the southeast; Atrium (2) to the southwest. Room (4) to the southeast; Atrium (2) to the southwest. None

DESCRIPTION: Triclinium is located to the south of the stairs leading up to the second floor. Constructed of masonry the three couches are approximately of the same length. To the front of the left couch, running the entire width is a step. The interior of all three couches have a series of shallow arched niches, six in the left couch, four in the middle couch, five in the right couch. The left and middle couch have a rim running around the edge. The right couch has a rim on the northwest side but a low wall on the northeast side. In the center of the couches is a rectangular table on a northeast/southwest axis. The northeast end of the table is defined by two projections with an open end. Underneath the table is an opening to what appears to be a cistern. The surface of the couches appear to be modern reconstruction. The table was apparently covered with masonry of which a little remains. In the southwest corner, next to but not connected with the left couch is a shallow rectangular water trough parallel with the left couch.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Pool (2734) to the southwest; cooking platform (2736) to the northeast; water basin (2739) to the southwest; hearth (2734) to the east. Pool (2734) to the southwest; cooking platform (2736) to the northeast; water basin (2739) to the southwest; hearth (2734) to the east.

DESCRIPTION:

The center of the east-southeast wall is a large, open doorway with a stepped threshold to the street, to the south. The threshold preserves placings for a door. There is a modern lintel. Extensive decorated plaster survives on all four walls. The lower register is red, with white above. The upper registers of all four walls are modern reconstruction. High in the center of the southwest wall is a square window with a modern lintel. At the east end of the north wall is a high doorway to Tuscan Atrium 2. No visible threshold remains, and there is a modern lintel. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. In the center of the room facing the street is a counter 5004. DESCRIPTION:
We have determined I-13-11 is a house and room 9 is one of three dining rooms. Room 9 is a dining room based upon its high door and high ceiling and view towards garden 4. The room is large and rectangular and sits on a southeast / northwest axis. The door is in the east corner of the northeast wall. No door sill is visible. The floor is lapilli today, so no original floor is visible. The walls were constructed of opus incertum and traces of plaster remain on all but the southwest wall. Frescoes appear to have a red lower level and be capped with a white upper. and centrally located on that wall is what appears to have been a blocked, arched window which may have been turned into a lararium or a lamp niche. Also on the same wall above the window or niche is what remains of a cornice decoration. The room today is open to the sky and with the current restoration, it is impossible to know if there was an upper floor.

Bibliography - Eschebach 70

On the northwest wall, this wall directly abuts the vineyard garden of I-13-9

DESCRIPTION: One enters the dining room from a large unexcavated garden area (8) to a rectangular shaped dining room through a large doorway from the southeast wall. The room runs on a northwest/southeast axis. A large tile threshold with a cistern with a single stone cover. There are walls restored on a high level, no ceiling and the floor is pounded dirt and weeds. On the southeast corner is a low rectangular window that looks into room #10. On the west wall evidence or plaster and a couch niche can be seen. The lower panels appears to be a cream/gray color with traces of red. The next panel is cream with red lines. The other walls show minimal traces of plaster and no paint. The wide doorway might indicate a pleasant garden scene.

DESCRIPTION: A square room with a portico along the north side with 2 square plastered columns, red lower register, white above. Between the columns and the walls there is a low masonry wall heavily reinforced with traces of plaster. To the west of the western column inserted into the wall is a partially buried dolium. In the center of the west wall there is a preparation platform (2540). In the center of the south wall there is a lararium niche (2536). In the southeast corner a small shrine building has been inserted secellum (2537). In the center of the east wall there is a low bench with plaster and opus signinum top (2539). At the northern end of the east wall there is a wide doorway opening to room #9. There is a masonry and tile threshold. The southern half of the garden is taken up with a large masonry triclinium (2535). The triclinium is below a restored wooden pergola with 6 uprights over which vines grow. To the north of the eastern arm of the triclinium is a dolium (2538). Undercoated plaster is found on all four walls.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a rectangular cupboard niche inserted into the south wall of the room. The base is earth and there is a modern lintel. Undecorated plaster survives on the rear and west interior faces, preserving placings for at least two wooden shelves that are no longer extant.

Bibliography: Eschebach, page 38

This is the House of the Vettii (room 19). This room is identified as a cubiculum/small reception space. It is a small room decorated in fresco. This feature is one of a group of seven and is a small vignette located at the eastern half of the southeastern wall. It has a red border on a white background. There is a blue ground with a gray bird facing right towards a branch with leaves and a piece of fruit, perhaps a peach. It is in good condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is to the east of painted feature 4698 and to the south of feature 4696 which is on the northeastern wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small crossroad shrine composed of a single tufa block, plastered. It is situated at the corner of 1-14-8 in the small street leading to the Garden of the Fugitives. It is in poor condition, but evidence of a three-sided lip around the top of the altar remains. Plaster on the altar and the wall behind it is fragmentary and little trace of paint remains.
The space surrounding altar (4172) would have been used at festivals for the consumption of offerings and neighborhood public feasting.

The latrine lies to the southwest of the cooking platform. The wall to the west, which the cooking platform abuts with extends more than half way into the room and serves to define the space of the latrine. In the doorway, just inside the latrine area, seems to be the remains of a wall running north/south roughly which may have narrowed the actual entrance to the latrine. No evidence of facilities remain in the latrine. The walls indicate that the area of the latrine was stuccoed, but no decoration remains. The floor is indeterminate. Post holes on the south wall indicate the level of the ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2560) to the northeast. None Cooking platform (2560) to the northeast.

It is intact except for a quarter of the rim, which is missing. This dolium is straight-sided, with a carinated shoulder rising inward to a slightly flaring rim. It is made of terracotta.

DESCRIPTION: This processing room is entered from the oven room which is to the northwest. The room is in a state of disrepair, but runs along the northeast/southwest axis. On the northeast wall is evidence of a vaulted ceiling and on the southeast a low wall appears to be added in antiquity to repurpose the room. Small patches of plaster are evident. The floor is obscured with rubble and debris and on the northwest wall there appear two holes that may vent the oven. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room (6) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Due to its proximity with the as yet uncompleted Central Baths, it is probable that this shop, one of eleven which surround the Central Baths of insula 4, was a large food and drink shop. It is entered by one step up through an open store front from the southwest. The floor is rubble. The reconstructed walls are extant to a first floor level. There is no remaining plaster.

This is a small dining room that is located directly Southwest of the vestibule 17, at the entrance, #24. One enters from a door, from the atrium, 15 into the Eastern corner of the room. This doorway is cut into the S.E. wall. The room is in very poor condition with only traces of plaster covering ushlar masonry and stone walls. No paint survives. The walls are preserved to about 7-10 feet in height and there is no ceiling. The floors are only preserved to a cement layer. The S.E. wall has a self niche, # 16-3718 and a couch niche # 16-3719.

DESCRIPTION:
We enter this large rectangular storage room through a low doorway situated in the West corner of the N.W. wall. There is no threshold, but there is a modern wooden lintel. As we enter, the room on a Northeast-Southwest axis, we notice the N.W. and S.E. walls jut into the room, slightly for approximately one-third of the length of the room. Seen, on the N.E. wall and the S.E. wall, is red and white painted plaster remains, in small areas in the East corner of the room is a modern utility pole.

This room is in disrepair, with walls preserved to an indeterminate height but restore
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The door leads to Peristyle area (8), on the Northwest
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION: Situated, at the East corner, there is a large square niche built into the Northeast wall, for a dining bench. There has been an effort to plaster the lower part in the same color red, as seen elsewhere in the dining room.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terry Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: The structure and room's primary access is north/south. The room is entered from the northwest corner of the north wall. Plaster is extant on north, south, east and west walls. Unsure of fresco style. Window on the south wall with sill 1.5 m above the floor - looks out on the vicolo. Floor is stone rubble. North, south and west walls are opus mixtum. This is a dining room because of its size and the view to the atrium 9.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the street is to the south, adjoining property to east, north is cubiculum 8 and atrium 9

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, north/south axis, floor obscured by lapilli and weeds. Walls have signs of extensive restoration. Across the north wall are stairs to the floor above accessed from entrance 1 to the northwest. In the centre of the west wall is a wide open door with a step to the street outside. In the centre of the east wall is a wide doorway to 14. In the southwest corner is a masonry support for a preparation platform 6124. In the southeast corner is a cooking platform 6123.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: street to west, rooms 13 to the northwest and 14 to the north

DESCRIPTION: Small square room immediately to the east of salesroom 12. No decoration on walls. Door opening is from a small area on the northeast wall. No floor remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: salesroom 12 to east; entered from area 10 on the northeast and to the northwest of room 5 and to the southeast of rooms 14 nd 15.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rctangular cooking platform with tiled surface and two arched recesses. Above in the east wall is a large window to the street. Fragmets of undecorated plaster survive on the northern and southern ends of the face.

DESCRIPTION: This is a narrow alcove between the cooking platform and the south wall in the southeast corner of the room. The floor is completely obscured by lapilli. As any drain or floor is completely obscured by lapilli its identification as a latrine is based on location and the drain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: cooking platform 6197 to the north

This room is the sales room for a large bakery. Access to this room is in 2 places from the street with the principle on the S.W. ,#10, and a 2nd entrance on the S.E. wall, #11. Entering from the S.W. doorway, one would step up on a raised threshold where one could face a Z shaped sales counter, feature #3737. This long rectangular room is on a S.W.-N.E. axis. In addition to the 2 street entrances, there is a door on the Western end of the N.W. wall. There is also, a doorway on the N.E. wall, leading into the bakery work area, #8 with a basalt threshold. The overall condition of the room is very poor, wall plaster survives only on the Eastern end of the S.E. wall.

The S.W. wall, situated in the South corner of the room has a cut opening, that runs all the way through to the exterior. The gray pompeian basalt threshold of door 11, steps up from the street and preserves cuttings running the entire length, this may be for a screen closing. The walls rise only to 4-10 feet, there is no original flooring that is left intact.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Room 2 is situated to the N.W.. Room 8 is situated to the N.E.. The bakery sits on the corner, A.D. 5. This room is contiguous to roads on the S.W. and S.E.

A contiguous feature is an exterior program, to which was located on the exterior of the S.E. wall.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick & Fran Capo

DESCRIPTION: This is a storage room aligned on a N.E.-S.W. axis. The room is very poorly preserved, no walls rise any higher than about 8 feet. There is no floor visible. There is no ceiling. There is no plaster visible. Because of its proximity to the sales counter, it suggests that it would serve as a store room. The entrance to this room is at the Southern end of the S.E. wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is contiguous to room no. 1, situated to the S.E.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick and Fran Capo.

DESCRIPTION: Situated to West of the cooking platform is an interesting water feature. The top has a ceramic container on the N.W. wall. At the top, there is a hole in the wall of the water feature indicating that it served as a conduit , from the garden to this water feature. We see 3 descending layers (steps). This was a helpful way to get water into the bakery for the bakery and the animals. The Northwest wall shows evidence of thick plaster. There are remnants of tile(s), they are embedded in the top front of the water feature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Located S.W. of the cooking platform is feature #3740, (water feature)
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Taken by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: This long rectangular room runs along a N.E./S.W. axis. We enter the room, from a low doorway, situated on the N.E.. There is a two step doorway, on the North corner of the room, which leads to room #7. Remnants of the plaster, remain on all low walls, particularly at the S.W. end of the room. Evidence of yellow, red and white paint remains, on the walls. Situated high on the S.W. wall is a tall, thin rectangular window, abutting the adjoining exterior wall, to the Northwest. The walls of the room are high up. No ceiling exists. The floor is covered with moss and debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to Room 7, on the Northwest and room 5, to the North.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION: This feature number 3722 is a rubble and mortar basin for the mill. The top is smoothed with cement and the structure sits just North-Northwest of the 3 basins, that are aligned with the S.E. wall. The basin is near the Northern corner of the N.W. wall. The structure is approximately 1.5 feet high on the exterior at it's highest point, and it is circular. The inner height is slightly less. The width of the ring surface from the outer portion to the inner portion, is approximately 8 inches, appearing like the rim of a tire. The center contains rubble and debris.

Feature 3723 is located to the N.E.
Feature 3721 is located to the S.E.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of Vettii. We enter this small atrium from the formal atrium where, on the east wall, we see a double stairway to the second floor. Rooms 22 and 23 are also storage areas - also room 21.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a platform located in the Northern corner of the room. The platform is about 2 feet wide by about 5 feet long. There is a level surface of about 18 inches high. In the very corner of the room, the platform rises about a foot more and abuts the corner walls. Within this raised area, there is a concave opening, that is preserved. This suggests that this was a stand for one or more doliums. This platform is in very poor condition. The flat surface and curved sides are ceramic.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform lies NW of the sales counter at the other end of the room. It is directly, situated to the NW of the doorway to room #8.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernick

DESCRIPTION: From the mill room, we look into the next room and what is the West wall of the structure. Our passage is currently blocked by a catillus. The oven room is filled with an oven that bears a plaque of restoration in 2005. As we enter this oven room, we are standing in a hallway which leads directly to a preparation room, #12. Looking at this partially destroyed oven, we see wht seems to be an unexcavated area blocking access to the area that would allow the baker to work. We cannot get close to the oven, beehive or the enclosed area of the oven. The outside arch exists in only about one-fourth of its arch shape. There is an opening situated West of the preparation room. There is no oven opening to the East processing room. The interior of the oven is all rubble, with a large basalt post and lintel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The Northwest side of the oven is contiguous to a large processing room (3799). The hallway leads to the West, it connects to a hallway and an oven passageway, to a preparation room. (3800)
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Terri Bruno.

DESCRIPTION: This is a bombed out property. It is a rectangular room, situated on an E-W axis. All 4 walls of the kitchen are poorly preserved. There is a doorway at the W. and at the S. wall, with a stone stepped threshold to 27. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. In the center of the room from the N.W. wall, there is a masonry partition or other feature. There are plaster fragments in the W and N walls. Situated high up, are the remains of the East wall, where there are 4 holes for floor joists. This is identified as a kitchen by Fiorelli and Werscher.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 27 is situated to the South
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The video team leader is Cavila

DESCRIPTION:
This is a rectangular room with an E-W axis. The room, on the whole, has poorly preserved walls. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. There is a wide doorway and a W. wall, with a stone stepped threshold, looking out to 27 (a garden?) The doorway, situated at the W and of the S wall, heading to atrium 21, has no visible threshold. There is white plaster with red trim and a blue border survives in the N.W. corner. There is a couch niche 6343, at the E end of the N. wall. Plaster survives at the N. end of the E. wall, with a pink colored hue.

All of this is part of a bombed out house.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To room 27 to the West and 21 to the South

DESCRIPTION: This is a Dining Room. It's a restaurant space situated on a NW-SE axis. One enters this room from a doorway in the N.E. wall, by the North corner. The room is in poor condition. Part of the pompeian stone threshold remains. No flooring is visible and no ceiling remains. The walls are preserved from 8-10 ft. in height. Some plaster remains on the walls. However, very few; painted surfaces survive. On the S.W. wall, situated in the West corner, the wall steps back for about 2 ft., forming approximately a 6 in. deep niche. This room is positioned off the atrium, suggesting it's use as a Dining room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is S.W. of the atrium. It's S.E. of room #4.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: The team leader is Terry Bruno

DESCRIPTION:

The facing wall on the lower left, there are traces of plaster with very faded paint. On the North wall, the facing wall situated on the right side is a doorway entrance. It is a badly damaged, it's reconstructed in the far left corner. There are traces of plaster with light yellow paint. Up high, there is a possible round post hole.
Whe West wall is badly damaged, the facing wall on the right side, shows traces pf plaster. The square window is high up in almost the center of the wall. The South wall is badly damaged. There are large areas of plaster with faint traces of paint. Six possible post holes are seen, when facing on the upper left side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The entrance to corridor number 21 is to the North

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular cooking platform with tiled surface preserved throughout. Arched recess storage area beneath. In the southeast corner there is a tile hearth, partially preserved, and showing a brick stamp.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east/west axis, with doorway at the west end of the north wall with marble threshold and placings for a gate. Immediately to the east of the doorway is water basin 6429. Against the west wall are stairs to the floor below. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. Extensive plaster survives on the north, east and south walls with a pinkish hue. At the east end of the north wall are two holes for floor joists matching holes in the south wall. High in the eastern half of the south wall are two windows that narrow to the street to the south. In the centre of the south wall is cooking platform 6430. Directly abutting the platform to the west is the masonry base of a partition wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 19 to the north

DESCRIPTION: Low rectangular platform against the centre of the south wall. Masonry with fragments of a tile surface. No visible storage or lip. Abuts directly against the south wall. To the west of the platform are the fragments of a partition wall only the base of which survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: water basin 6429 to the north

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room on an east/west axis. Doorway at the east end of the south wall opens to atrium 9. Marble threshold with placings for a door. Fragments of a mosaic floor survive along the north wall and most extensively in the northeast corner with a white interior enclosed by a black border. There are wide modern windows in the south, west and north walls - it is not clear if these existed in antiquity. Fragments of plaster survive on the east wall nd adjoining corners as well as the northwest and southwest corners. The plaster is red in colour with traces of borders but the colour is not discernible. Two tall rectangular blocked windows (?) in the east wall.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, north/south axis. The entire south wall is absent to provide access to atrium 4. The floor is obscured by lapilli. DESCRIPTION: The central feature of Room 8 is the great oven. There is arched brick in the outer opening. The basalt stone demarcates a floor space under the oven, for ashes. On the North side of the oven, there is no typical opening to the prep room. On the Southeast side, the oven is closed from the mill area. The oven has probably been restored. The bottom platform of the oven supports the arch leading to the oven, and on each side of the oven is provided a raised preparation area.
