DESCRIPTION: The latrine runs along the NE and the SE walls of the kitchen. There is a small step up from the kitchen into this area. In the eastern corner of the NE wall, is a badly broken terracotta pipe. Oddly, there is a painted plaster area in the latrine with red and gold portions. The SW portion of the latrine is delineated by the NE cooking platform support which runs approximately half the distance of the space toward the NW wall. There is a small lightwell high on the SE wall above the latrine. There are no tiles evident today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to cooking platform 3907 to the SW.

DESCRIPTION: This is a large prep room, one enters from the northwest wall at the northern corner. The room is on a southwest/northeast axis and is rectangular. There is a low door and a slight step up into this room. Due to it's proximity to the service corridor (11) this appears to be a prep or storage room. This room is in very poor condition. The southwest wall is quite tall with a small high window for light. Presently this wall is braced with wood and metal supports. There is some plaster on each f the walls, however, no paint remains. the floor iis not visible. The ceiling no longer remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the southwest of dining room 7 and southeast of corridors 13 and 11.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small dining room. it is rectangular with a northeast southwest axis. One enters the room through a doorway from space 9. The doorway forms the eastern half of the wall. The doorway forms the eastern half of the wall. The northern half of this wall is n very poor condition and is made from a red volcanic stone. The room is in very poor condition. Coccio pesto flooring can be seen near the doorway.; The northwest , southwest and northwest walls still have some painted plaster, however, large central tableaux have been cut out from these walls. The painted decoration preserves traces of a high dado and large panels above. This room has had various attempts at conservation, including metal butterfly clamps on the southwest, southeast and northwest walls. No ceiling remains, the upper portion of the southwest wall is red volcanic stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is located northwest of dining hall (6) it opens to space 9 leading to the atrium (8).

DESCRIPTION: This oven is a large beehive oven. It takes up two thirds of the room space of room (6). The oven appears to be in good shape, and was placed in the room, which had previously been plastered. From the ground level the oven structure extends vertically about six feet above which the ceiling is vaulted for six additional feet. The ledge of the oven is composed of lava stones which lie low from the ground. Four or five pieces of terra cotta remain on top of this ledge on the southwest and west. A large passthrough from room (3) to the northwest is lined with a terra cotta drain tile. The opening to the oven is composed of lava stones, which appear to be three stones. The inside of the oven is covered with ash on the bottom, but the spaces around, which form the inside of the brick oven appear to be in good shape. There appears to be a stone slab under the ash towards the eastern corner. The central circular top of the oven on the exterior is in place. Two holes which can't be observed from inside this oven seem to be venting on the southeast wall into room (8). There are some holes on the southeast and northwest walls toward the north end, but the function is unknown. Modern structural supports for ceiling in wall are in front of the oven today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It's contiguous to feature (3876) (basin) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is a preparation room. It is a square room. There is a wide opening at the northwest side of the room to the mill room. There is a small doorway on the southeast side of the room to another prep room (room 3). The northwest wall is left open with brick and stonework piers at the north and west corners. The southeast wall is also brick and stone masonry up to the height of the doorway lentil. Above the height of the lentil is a rubble mortar wall, the same as northeast and southwest walls. Some plaster remains on the southwest wall, no paint remains. The floors are not visible, however, the paving stones of the mill room extend to the inner side of the north corner pier. A basin fashioned from a catillus is located in the western corner of the room (3874). This room is in very poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is located to the southeast of the mill room. It is northwest of prep room (3).

DESCRIPTION: Due to its proximity with the as yet uncompleted Central Baths, it is probable that this shop, one of eleven which surround the Central Baths of insula 4, was a large food and drink shop. It is entered by one step up through an open store front from the southwest and northwest. The floor is rubble. The reconstructed walls are extant to a first floor level. There is no remaining plaster.

This is a mill/catillus made of local stone. It is almost completely missing, there are several small fragments from the upper rim/portion and base. The form of this has the fittings block extends from the rim to the base. The rim preserves the notch in the center of the fitting block. The condition is good!.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is N.W. of the pillar and S.W., across the room from the oven.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Lisa Wernick and Fran Capo.

DESCRIPTION: A dining room with entrance in the West wall in the southwest corner. There are two niches in this room (6032 and 6033). The north wall has red and yellow plaster surviving a the bottom and a band of stucco work at the top of the wall. The east wall has a large niche (6032) cut into the wall in the north east corner running to the south. The doorway in the east wall has a threshold in place with pivot marks and a stop join surviving; it is of volcanic stone. In the southeast corner of the east wall , red plaster survives. The south wall is plastered with red plaster but has suffered a collapse. The west wall has suffered a severe collapse but in the northwest corner is a niche (6033). Small traces of plaster remain in the south end of the niche. The floor is covered with lapilli. There are signs of modern conservation in the pointing of the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 is contiguous with Room 1 to the south, Room 5 to the southeast and in the west of Room 6.

DESCRIPTION:
One enters the dining room hallway 2 through a small door in the SE corner. The room is rectangular in shape on a SW-NE axis. In the center of the SW wall is a doorway leading into garden 6. The floor and the height of the walls are indeterminate. The walls were plastered but only little remains today. No decoration is extant.
Post-earthquake rectangular pillar effectively creates a rectangular recess between the low wall on the NW wall and the SW wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 6 to SW hallway 2 to SE.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the triclinium (7) from a doorway in the north corner. The room is rectangular in shape, with southwest/northeast axis. Though not extant today, early excavations show a small pillar, rectangular, abutting the southeast wall, on line with northeast end of the west wall. Neither the floor nor the height of the walls are determinable. Walls shown no evidence of plaster today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to hallway 6 to northwest.

DESCRIPTION: See feature number 11
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 to the west. Corridor 12 to the north. Space 19 to the east. Corridor 21 and room 27 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Kitchen 18 is entered from corridor 12 to the west and corridor 20 to the southwest. It is a small square room which is provided with a large preparation platform against the north wall. Adjoining the preparation platform is a latrine to the west. The preserved walls on the eastern, western and northern sides are approximately 2 m high; roof is missing. The floor is now covered with lapilli, with no trace of original paving. Traces of plaster are visible on the lower zone of the western wall. A small rectangular window opens on the top of the northern wall above the preparation platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Back entrance 17 to the west, space 19 and corridor 20 to the south

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a painting in the House of the Vettii. This is a small detail on the wall directly east of the entrance from the fauces. It is a small vignette at the bottom of a narrow section of wall. It is in a red field on a yellow panel. A figure is depicted holding what may be a cup. It is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is directly east of the entrance from the fauces and it is south of the doorway to room 19.

DESCRIPTION:
Triclinium - rectangular table which had receding semicircle cut into its east end. Couches faced with opus signinum and show evidence of having been painted red. The top of the table was inlaid with marble, the center circular, the others square. There is no evidence of a small table attached to the north wall (as described in Jashemski). The triclinium is currently under a blue tarpaulin.

Medius 4.60m; imus 4.65m; summus 3.75m

Rectangular table 2.00 x 1.45m
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dolium 16-2894 to south east

DESCRIPTION: Dining room with entrance from the west wall in southwest corner, window opening on to corridor and peristyle on the east wall in the southeast corner. The dining room is visible from the main entrance at 10 through the atrium. There is a closed doorway with marble threshold on the south wall in the southeast corner. North wall has remains of white plaster with red bands in the northeast corner. This plaster continues on the east wall to the window. On the south wall white plaster remains at the bottom of the wall. Some conservation has been carried out to the wall at the southeast end. The floor is badly degraded but would have been crushed stone embedded in plaster or cement. The doorway to the dining room on the west wall is the highest preserved wall but the lintel has been restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 is west of room 4, south of room 10, south east of 12, east of room 9 and west of room 7

DESCRIPTION:
This sheet replaces #1264.
Kitchen 13 is entered through Corridor 18 to the southern corner. It is a small rectangular room oriented southeast/northwest. The only totally preserved wall it to the northwest. On the same wall is a long rectangular window above the cooking platform. This looks out into Dining Room 11 of the house at 6,2,27. The floor is covered with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor 18 to the south. Storeroom 14 to the northeast and Room 12 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform rests against the southwest wall of Kitchen 13. This wall is almost all gone. The long rectangular top surface shows very few remains of terra cotta tiles on the western half. On the eastern section the tiles are covered by a thin layer of grayish porous material. Underneath the surface is a large, semicircular opening for the storage. The outer arch of the storage space is supported by a row of vertical terra cotta tiles.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 13 to northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The niche for the insertion of the dining couch in recessed into the northwest wall of the Dining room 4. It is approximately 1 meter high. The back wall is partially plastered in red. Based on evidence visible today the northeast side wall of the niche continues into the northeast wall of the Dining Room. At the southwest side wall of the niche, on the contrary, the recessed area is fully evident in the northwest wall
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Room 4 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: In the south/southeast corner of the garden there is a raised area. Eschebach reported an open air triclinium. In 2011 the area is obviously higher than the rest of the garden. There is a large tree where there might have been a table.

The preparation platform lies in the corner between the southeast and southwest walls. It is in very bad condition today. What is left is a low structure sloping down toward the middle of the room. The top is covered with moss with very few fragments of terracotta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to south of room 2 which contains latrine to the north

DESCRIPTION:
This is a small, square room has been identified as a foyer. It has a doorway to dining hall 3 in the center of the north wall. There is no threshold to this doorway. There is a doorway at the southwest corner to atrium 2. This doorway has a tufa threshold with placings for a door and a modern lintel. Fourth-style painting survives along the southeast with yellow panels and a plaster corner. High in the east corner is a rectangular plastered window tapering to the east, subsequently blocked. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout.
BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining hall is to the northwest. Atrium 2 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: It has one bench opened to the room, one bench along the northwest wall and a bench attached to the preparation room wall. This u-shaped bench triclinium does not have an extant central table.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bench triclinium masonry: to the south #2988; to the southeast #2987; to the east #2989

DESCRIPTION: This feature (4682) is in room 2 of the House of the Vettii. It is a circular vignette showing a bird, facing right, beside an apple and is situated to the right of the central panel in the central frieze on the south west wall. BIBLIOGRAPHY: JASHEMSKY II PP 153-155; ESCHEBACH PP 218-219
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: this feature (4682) is on the south west wall in the western corner

DESCRIPTION: On the north eastern wall of the garden 5105 is a large , half domed mosaic fountain. There is a triangular pediment at the top with plaster over it. Exterior side wall construction is opus mixtum originally covered by plaster. Interior walls of the dome and fountain area ae constructed of tiny tesserae mostly in blue and white floral patterns crowned by a nude portrait of a woman, presumably Venus. There is a sea serpent or snake behind her. In mid center is a rectangular niche, covered in a leaf tesserae pattern, with a striated vessel from which water would have poured. It would pour down several steps leading to a half round basin of water proof cement. Inserts on either side of the top of the steps indicate a shelf-like projection at the top of the stairs.

Located along the northeast wall, about a third of the way down from the southeast wall of room 3, is an underground wine cellar. The entrance to the cellar is defined by a low wall on an east/west axis and is a lower level than the level of the vineyard. One descends the stairs from the east. Approx. eight steps down the steps turn at a right angle towards the southwest. At the southeast end running the entire width of the cellar is a low wall that together with the cellar walls create a deep vat. About one fourth of the way from the entrance of he cellar is the remains of the wall. The walls of the cellar were lined with opus signinum. The ceiling of the cellar is vaulted its entire length interrupted only in the front middle and back by the three vent holes. Near the midpoint of the southwest wall is a large opening into a cavity of unknown use. It may have been merely where the wall has caved in as it may have been covered by the plaster of the wall. At the bottom of the stairs the cellar opens to the southeast and runs in a northwest/southeast direction. The cellar appears to run all of the way or almost so to the southeast wall of the vineyard (room 2) There appears to be three openings to the cellar in the floor of the vineyard to allow light and air into the cellar and evacuate gases from the fermenting wine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Agricultural area (2732) to the west; Processing room (2738) to the northwest. Agricultural area (2732) to the west; Processing room (2738) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The latrine lays in the northern corner of Room 5. It is completely covered by lapilli, vegetation and modern plastic hoses. However the southeastern stone edge is still visible. No drain is extant due to vegetation/lapilli layer.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2768) to the south. None Cookinbg platform (2768) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the dining room with a marble threshold through a large wide door. This is a rectangular dining room with a northwest / southeast axis. The floor is plastered but tesserae are not visible. On the entrance wall (southeast) no plaster remains. On all three remaining walls we see good evidence of Fourth Style painting. The bottom zone is divided into burgundy rectangles. The walls have burgundy, ivory, yellow with Third Style perspective that Vitruvius would not like. The ceiling is modern which indicates there was no ceiling after the eruption. On the northwest corner there is a brick engaged column that would have been covered in plaster. The northeast wall near the corner shows evidence of an earlier door. You could see a peristyle from the dining room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (5) to the southeast is a peristyle and a wide corridor. Room (5) to the southeast is a peristyle and a wide corridor. None

DESCRIPTION: Room 1 opens to the northwest by descending a flight of two steps. The rectangular room is on a northwest/southeast axis. Two thirds down the room to the southwest is a masonry couch triclinium. Above the middle couch to the south there are two semicircular niches. The top niche which is larger than the smaller niche; it has a shelf and shows traces of white painting on the upper curve of the niche. This suggests that the niche was probably used as a lararium. The other smaller niche which is about 70 centimeters above the middle couch is deeper than the larger niche above the ground. Perhaps it was used to hold lamps. To the south of the larger niche is evidence of a walled up window. On the same wall to the west there is another large niche resting on the ground. There are traces of yellow paint on the southeast wall and red painting on the eastern corner of the northeast wall and in the northern corner of the northeast wall. On the north and east and southwest walls there is evidence of plaster. In the northern corner of the northeast wall there is a U-shaped frame of a window that was blocked up. On the southwestern wall there are irregularly shaped holes located in different points. The function of these joist like holes is unknown. The walls have been heavily reconstructed to the first floor height. The floor is now covered with overgrown vegetation, however Jashemski argues that the area was planted with olive trees and possibly vines because traces of wine were found in the dolia. The ceiling is no longer extant. The dolia were found in the eastern corner of the room. Today in the southern corner is an unburied dolium but there is no evidence if it was there in antiquity.

The lararium lies above the triclinium (2773) on the southwest wall. The lararium has aedicular shape with a ledge. It's a good size. On the north side of the lararium there is ivory colored paint placed with strong touches of red and pink apparent. Perhaps this replicates the scattering of roses we've seen on other lararia. The lararium is not centered over the triclinium but is slightly south of the center. Next to the lararium on the west is a rectangular window. Beneath the window and lararium a curved opening probably for a lamp.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium (2773) to the northeast; Large cupboard niche (2774) on same wall to the northeast; Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east. Triclinium (2773) to the northeast; Large cupboard niche (2774) on same wall to the northeast; Two dolia (2776, 2777) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: A low bench (for dining?) abuts the northeastern wall, southwest of the entrance of the shop. The bench is rectangular in shape on a southwest/northeast axis. As reconstructed, the surface of the bench is square tiles. There is no evidence of stucco or decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Kitchen (9) lies in the western corner of atrium area two. The room is not accessible today because of a modern locked door. It is being used as a store room. However, on the western side are the remains of a cooking platform and a possible latrine that are visible. This is confirmed also in the description of the house by Eschebach and in PPM. On the wall opposite the entrance door is a small rectangular window looking out on peristyle six. A modern wooden roof is sloping down southwards.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (2) to the northeast; dining room (8) to the east; peristyle (6) to the south. Atrium (2) to the northeast; dining room (8) to the east; peristyle (6) to the south. None

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is located in the south corner abutting the southeast and southwest walls. There is an arched storage area beneath which had a shelf raised above the floor by approximately 6 inches. The surface of the cooking platform is divided into two parts. On the northeast side there is flat surface made up of flat stones embedded in cement with a lip along the southeast wall whose surface slopes toward the front. The southwest portion of the cooking platform, and the larger part, is built up higher than the first part. It is possible that the entire cooking surface had been built up and that the northeast portion has fallen away. A wall on the northeast side separates the cooking platform from the latrine. The walls were stuccoed but no evidence of painting remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine (2125) to the northeast. Latrine (2125) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: We enter kitchen through a door in western corner of the atrium/reception area. This is a narrow rectangular space on a northwest/southeast axis. This is a kitchen with elaborate decorations. Perhaps open to public. Floor is lapilli. Newly plastered with lower register of yellow. Upper register of white. Southeast wall show red stenciling on sides and pale green color in areas. Cornice molding on southeast wall. The reason for kitchen designation is presence of two arched niches. No ceiling. In the room between the two arches is a place for cupboard niche higher tan both arched storage niches. Amphora were left in situ. Ceiling no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium/reception (2) to west Atrium/reception (2) to west None

DESCRIPTION: The feature in this kitchen that identifies the space is the cooking platform, which is located against the southeast wall. The platform is unusual in that it has two components: the southeast wall component is lower and has a tiled top; the northeast component joins the southeast component and is higher and wider, with a tiled surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: We enter the square storage room from the southwest, through a very small entrance from the hallway (2) which connects the counter room (2796) and the kitchen (2799). On the northwest wall there is a very large window to the counter room. The storeroom shows some plaster on the northeast and southeast walls and there is evidence of floor with some broken tesserae.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room (2796) to the southwest; Hallway (2) to the southwest; Kitchen (2799) to the southeast Counter room (2796) to the southwest; Hallway (2) to the southwest; Kitchen (2799) to the southeast None

DESCRIPTION: Room five is a square room which opens from Room 2 (corridor) to the west and faces the entrance (2.1.13). The northwestern wall was decorated with paintings, of which some traces of red and yellow are extant. On the opposite wall to the southeast is the door and window which open to Room 6 (garden). The floor is covered with packed earth, under which there is evidence of cocciopesto. Further traces of red paint also appear on the lower zone of the northeastern and southeastern walls, while plaster covers the southern corner. To the east of the large window there is another window which is smaller and has a shelf that is covered with tiles. The ceiling is no longer extant. The northwest and northeast walls are preserved to the first floor height. Up to the northwestern wall is a square joist hole, roofed by a large tile, the function of which is difficult to ascertain. The large opening and location of this room, from which the street was visible (through the entrance), and the large window to the west along the same wall, make it likely that the room was used for public dining.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 (corridor) to the west; Room 6 (dining room) to southeast; Room 4 (kitchen) to the west Room 2 (corridor) to the west; Room 6 (dining room) to southeast; Room 4 (kitchen) to the west None

DESCRIPTION: The masonry triclinium is located in the center of the horticultural area, Room 5 (2791). The triclinium faces to the southwest. The left couch is slightly longer than the right one. Around the interior edge of all three couches is a raised lip. All three couches slope slightly down from the inside out. The interior walls of the couches contain niches for storage; four niches in the right couch, three in the middle couch and five in the left couch. In the center of the couches is a large rectangular masonry table lying on a northeast / southwest axis. The table according to Jashemski had a variegated marble top, no longer extant. As extant, the exterior of the couches and table lack any plaster. As reconstructed, the surface of the couches is made of a hard cement with fragments of terra cotta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Altar (2793) to the southwest. None Altar (2793) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room (8) lies in the eastern corner of the hotel. The large entrance faces a semicircular stone structure at the back of space (2). On the opposite wall is a large square window opening onto courtyard (13). To the west of the entrance remain traces of red painting on the wall. They also appear on the northeast wall. The floor is today covered by lapilli. The ceiling is gone. To the eastern side of the entrance are remains of the ancient wall, made of terracotta slabs. The dining room is rectangular and along a southwest/northeast axis.

DESCRIPTION: Room 3 is located to the southwest of entrance 1 and opens onto space 2 to the west. The room is today closed by a modern locked door which allow us to give a full description of the space inside. However, from some space holes at the entrance it's possible to see a low wall at the back. This wall could surround a tank for processing grapes since PPM describes a grape pressing structure in front of the masonry couch triclinium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Entrance 1 to the east; Space 2 to the west and south. Entrance 1 to the east; Space 2 to the west and south.

DESCRIPTION: In the southwest of triclinium 3024 is a rectangular fish pond on a northeast-southeast axis. The pond is quite deep and as extant no longer shows evidence of stucco.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium to the northeast. Furrows to the northwest and southeast. Well to the west. Water feature to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: On the northwest wall in the west corner is a painting of four bunches of grapes, two of which have branches attached. The painting is framed by a thin red line, all set within the rectangular panel defined on the top and bottom by a continuous red line. It is framed on the left by a vertical red line and on the right by two vertical green lines.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. We have determined that this is a dining room, slightly smaller than room 13, opening on the to peristyle. There is no apparent threshold. The floor is vegetation and a few stones. The room is rectangular, the walls opus incertum and plaster. Again, the view is of the ambulatory and peristyle. The doorway opening to the south onto the space leading from the atrium has lost one-fifth of its wall, so the doorway itself is no longer visible.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room (5) shows a double entrance. The bigger one opens onto space (2) to the southwest. This entrance was closed by a door, as the stone threshold and the three door jams on it show. The rectangular room is on a northeast/southwest axis. The walls were decorated with 4th style painting. The lower part of the walls were painted with a black register. This register on the northeast wall shows traces of green, white and yellow plants. On the same wall, above the black zone, is a green and yellow band framing the middle part of the wall. No trace of painting has survived except two red bands which were used as frames. On the other part of the wall runs a frieze framed by marble molding which continues running onto the two adjoining walls. The walls are preserved in their height but the wooden ceiling is of modern construction. There are a few traces of cocciopesto floor by the main entrance. On the southern corner is a smaller door opening onto the kitchen (4).

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that this is a dining room outside of the major bath complex. This is because of the room's location close to the swimming pool. The walls give indication of a new, trendy way of pleasing elite people. We have identified a kitchen in a direct line with this structure.
There are two entrances. Both have definite areas of white marble. The northeast door has walls on either side over the six-foot level. The south entrance is wider and shows a long, wide strip of marble edging a step. At the southeast we see a mangled part of the room. From the interior, the wall of this part is curved. A huge mass of volcanic material fell on this wall. Steve identifies pyroclastic flow material, probably from flow 6, because on top of this material we see a collapsed arch. This could indicate a ceiling for this dining room. The floor is uniformly stone and red brick pieces in random patterns. There are four highly irregular walls. What we see is a mixture of brick and opus reticulatum. The northeast wall is straight until it reaches the corner where the circular part of the room begins. The northwest wall is a mixture of brick and opus reticulatum and in three places the brickwork protrudes. In the center is niche 4601. The southwest wall has an interesting pattern with three brick protrusions. A smaller protrusion in the center reminds us of the the niche in the northwest wall. Is this room covered or uncovered? There is an ancient drain in the wall which protrudes onto the outside.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: SAP Inventory no. 40686

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is at the intersection of the Vicolo dei Soprastanti and the Vicolo delle Terme. It is on the south side of the Vicolo del Soprastanti, outside the northwest end of the forum. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs and the floor of the basin reveals terracotta tile. The pilaster is on the southeast side and is decorated with the head of a dog/wolf. There is no modern plumbing. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.72 meters by 0.94 meters and is 0.47 meters deep. It has an overflow on both the northeast and southwest slabs, as well as a diagonal overflow on the southwest side of the pilaster. The drain hole is at ground level of the southwestern slab. Northwestern and northeastern faces of the basin are supported by stone and concrete rubble. There are worn hand recesses on the interior east corner and one near the north corner. Another worn hand recess is approximately at the center of the northwestern slab and another is on the southern interior corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is located on the Vicolo dei Soprastanti, outside the northwestern end of the forum. It is next to 7.7.26

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified 7, 2, 48 as a commercial restaurant. We have determined that the last usage of room 12 is as a kitchen. This identification is based on its location within the structure and the size. Kitchen 12 is entered from a large rectangular entrance door to the south off corridor 15. The well presented walls of the rectangular room were originally painted, but only a few remains of red and white plaster remain on the lower sections. The western section of the northwestern wall contains a shallow rectangular recess, which may have housed a structure for storage or cooking. No traces of the original flooring are visible. The kitchen looks out onto space 9. The entrances between kitchen 12 and space 9 are in line.

DESCRIPTION:
We have decided that this is an oven and it is the normal structure for breadmaking. It is in the northwest corner of a good sized room. It has an interior beehive oven and a large stone slab at the outer rectangular entrance. Beneath the stone slab is a rectangular space that stored wood or charcoal. There is a large, brickfaced opening to the oven. Above this is a somewhat usual phallic symbol. The phallic symbol is a normal decorative element of an oven. It suggests good luck for breadmaking and the phallic symbol brings good luck and happiness. On the left of the oven is an arched opening where the bread was passed through. On the right is a large arched opening where the baker would put bread to be removed by slaves and put on the preparation platform.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is made up of volcanic stone slabs. It is on the east side of the Vicolo del Labirinto at the intersection with the Vicolo di Mercurio. It sits in the street at the northwest corner of 6.13.17. The floor lining is no longer extant, revealing terra cotta tiles placed upon the street stones. The interior of the basin is 1.18 meters by 0.76 meters and it is .73 meters deep. The pilaster, which was originally centered atop the northwestern slab, is missing. The overflow is at the top center of the southeastern slab, with the drain hole at the street level below. There is a slightly worn hand recess on the east side of the pilaster; the west side is broken. There is a slightly worn recess about 0.39 meters south of the western interior corner and another one near the northern interior corner of the basin. There is no modern plumbing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fountain is on the east side of the Vicolo del Labirinto at the intersection of the Vicolo di Mercurio. It is in the street outside of the northwest corner of 6.13.17.

DESCRIPTION: The masonry couch triclinium is in the middle of Room 15 and is situated slightly to the west in the room. It is U-shaped with the eastern couch about 50 centimeters longer than the western couch. The inner walls of the couch are decorated with ground-level semicircular niches (five on the eastern couch, three on the southern couch, three on the western couch) for storing plates. Along the outside of the couches runs a low bench. In the middle of the southern couch and in the corner of the southern and eastern couches were pillars. The pillar in the southern couch is the only one remaining. The benches on the eastern and western couches continue out and enjoin a large rectangular structure. They are slightly higher than the benches connected to the triclinium couches. The large sunken rectangular structure contains an embedded pillar in the middle of the southern side. This pillar may have supported a table which suggests the idea that the whole area may have been used as a garden. Today the masonry triclinium is shaded by a vine pergola.

DESCRIPTION: N/W S/E axis of rectangular room originally open air dining area. The lararium 2516 has two terracotta gables to protect it from the elements. Opus signinum floor survives along the western wall between the dining couch 2517 and the cistern 2518. The remainder of the floor is obscured by lapilli. Room located at rear of the property. DESCRIPTION: This large rectangular room is on a roughly north/south axis. It contains a masonry couch triclinium in the middle of the room situated slightly to the west. It is planted with modern olive and fruit trees and grapevines. Along the eastern wall appears a small rectangular recess which seems to have contained a flight of stairs but the overgrown vegetation doesn't allow us to go beyond this as an hypothesis. The surrounding walls have been heavily reconstructed in modern times and vary in height. The south and east walls are restored to one plus stories high. The east wall varies between over one story to the east to waist high in the west. At the base of the southern wall runs a low bench-like structure which seems to have been used for supporting the entire wall. Along the northern wall, to the northeast, there are traces of red and yellow painting. The is a small rectangular niche in the northeast corner of the eastern wall about 1.5 meters above the ground. In the northeast corner of the northern wall there are four joist holes about two meters above the ground. On the eastern wall there is also a high rectangular window. Along the western wall towards the kitchen there are traces of red and yellow painting on the lower part of the wall. Near the kitchen there is also a large built-in shallow semicircular niche. It has a narrow ledge and there are traces of plaster. South of the niche is a large rectangular stone that juts out of the wall and is about two meters above the ground, the function of which is uncertain. There is a recessed area to the east of the entrance of Room 5 which, according to the floor plan was actually a doorway to Room 2. Today it is blocked up. According to the floor plan there are stairs in the southern end of the eastern wall. The stairs no longer exist. In the southeast corner today there is a small glass building showing thirteen plaster casts of victims of the 79 A.D. eruption (men, women, children). According to modern literature the bodies were found in Room 15.

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that this space was a public space with seating for outdoor eating. This identification is based on the feature that is a continuous bench on three sides of this space. The space is located along the suthwest side of the bath complex. It is an open space entered from the plaza to the southwest. The large paving stones from the plaza continue into this space. This space forms an inset area and the bench is in a horse shoe form. The niche continues the exterior decoration of the baths consisting of large molded plaster panels with multi-colored first style blocks in the plaster above. There's a large window in the northeast wall looking into the bath, two small windows are cut into the southeast wall. The walls are a mix of opus reticulatum, opus incertum, and lots of restoration.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is located to the northeast of the large plaza and is southwest of the bath building.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this is VII-1-47 as a domestic structure (house). We have determined that the last usage of Room 36 is a triclinium. This identification is based on the room location within the structure, large size, central marble emblem on the floor, a large entrance and lavishly-painted walls with figurative motifs. Room 36 is entered from the southeast corner of the Atrium 21 through a large entrance door with threshold showing traces of door hinges on either size. The floor is marked by a central, square emblem formed of marble square slabs of different colour. The dining couches would have been placed along the three sides of the room facing the middle emblem. From the northeast corner of the room, guests would have had a clear view of the Atrium 21 with its fountain and cartibulum. The northeast wall is fully decorated with paintings showing up a black lower band. In the middle, the central part of the wall is decorated with a figurative emblem while the upper sections show architectural motifs with open doors and awnings. The same design is found fragmentally on the northwest and southeast walls (look for references to mythological stories in the emblems). On the other section of the northwest and southeast walls are rectangular openings. Bibliography: Eschebach p246-247 and Jashemski 169-171

We have identified that VII-1-47 as a domestic structure (house). We have determined that the last usage of Room 34 is a triclinium. This identification is based on the room location within the structure, size, floor paintings and location of the single door and single window. Room 34 opens onto the southeast corner of Atrium 21 through a fairly narrow door entrance with a raised threshold step. The northwest wall is pierced by a large window, looking into Peristyle 15. The walls show fragments of painting and the floor shows traces of opus signinum. The southwest wall includes a long, rectangular recess. On the opposite wall, the central section shows a semi-circular recess. The room was decorated with a painting of 'Aeneas Wounded on His Leg' (now in the National Archaeological Museum in Naples). The room is now used for the display of three casts (a man and two women that were found in Skeleton's Alley).

Bibliography: Eschebach p246-247 and Jashemski 169-171

The garden lies at the back of the house to the SE. It's roughly rectangular in shape on a SW/NE axis. One enters the garden via andron 6 to the NW. In the NW wall to the W is a large window opening into triclinium 7. On the SE wall is a large aediculate lararium from which the house gets its name. On the SW wall is a small niche lararium. In the NW wall to the NE is a small window into kitchen 8. In the same wall to the NW is a light well in the area above the kitchen. Along the NE wall today are whole and broken amphorae. It is not obvious that they are in situ. However, along the NW in the NE corner are two small and one slightly larger dolia, apparently in situ. In the S corner is a cylindrical dolium likely a puteal for cistern apparently in situ. The floor is indeterminate (if there was one). The walls were plastered in antiquity, but the decoration except the lararium is gone. As a garden, it probably did not have a roof.

DESCRIPTION:
This is an enclosure tomb on the south side of the cemetery road, with a house-like facade. It is the tomb of G. Munatius Faustus. The facade is built in opus incertum and covered in stucco. There is a moulded cornice and pediment with moulded raking cornice, and a marble dedicatory inscription in the center of the pediment. A large doorway goes through the center of the facade with steps approaching from the road. The white stucco facade has red painted borders around the pediment and moulded cornice and this also has red graffiti across the facade. No remains of a door are visible. There are remains of plaster still visible on the north west, south west and north east walls. The south west wall is capped with a brown cement which in the southern half of the wall is part of the vaulted roof of tomb 7, the next tomb to the south west. The door frame ,like the threshold, is framed in dark, large volcanic blocks. Behind the facade is a walled enclosure for funerary banqueting. No flooring is visible. The facade has a peaked roof, reconstructed with roofing tiles.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Campbell, 30 pp 244 - 245
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This tomb is to the south east of the cemetery road. It is adjacent to tomb 11, which mirrors its facade and is to the north east.

DESCRIPTION: In the large garden a large masonry square poorium with brick columns supporting a cover in each of the four corners. One column remains embedded in the north corner and a second column lies on the surface in the west corner. South and east columns are heavily eroded. The surface is paved with opus signinum that has been laid over at least twice earlier with opus signinum. The floors are visible on the northern tip of the platform. The eastern face preserves plaster facing overlaid with earlier plaster. Along the north and west sides of the platform there is an "L" shaped tank. The southern edge does not survive, destroyed by construction of the fontina aqueduct which also destroyed the east corner of the platform. In the center of the north arm is a circular stone column, lined with plaster. The base of the tank is filled with earth and debris. All faces of the basin (tank) are plastered with no decoration. Embedded in all the long walls are a line of the upper halves of amphorae. In the center of the north wall there is an upper register of two embedded vessels. Collapse has exposed or destroyed several of the embedded amphorae. The function of this is unclear. However, the amphorae suggest nestings for fish and this tank was used for fish breeding. The square podium in unclear, the position next to the tank in dicates its position is deliberate and its structure suggests a function related to the tank such as dissection of the fish.

Note: on the database this space is considered as part of the kitchen 10; however the dividing wall to the east against the cooking platform clearly delineates the space from the adjoining area.

The orientation of the room is east west to north south. The walls show large fragments of plaster, particularly the southern wall is completely covered with red paint. The wall is more damaged and shows traces of a possible window to the southwest. The floor is today entirely covered with lapilli. Given the large size of the kitchen, which could include also space for the preparation of food (especially in the area delimited by the cooking platform to the west and latrine to the east. Space 11 is likely to have been used for storage.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 10 to East, space 4 to West, space 8 to South.

DESCRIPTION: Low rectangular masonry platform with broad tile rim around the entire platform, square on the outside border surrounding an elliptical opening. The base of the elliptical opening is masonry. Placing for charcoal or brazier. The platform is against the northeast wall, sited between the north corner and the window to Room 9.

The niche is inserted into the southeast wall of Dining Room 15 at approximately 1.4 meters above the floor. It is a trapezoidal shape and its walls are covered with plaster. The back wall shows two small circular holes which are on the some axis and about 40 centimeters apart from each other. The function of these holes is difficult to ascertain- maybe for supporting hooks? On the bottom of the niche is a well-preserved marble shelf at the front edge. The back area of the shelf is covered with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Room 15 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: On the SE side of the atrium is a masonry bench triclinium facing o the NE. The imus abuts and parallels to the SE wall and the medius abuts and parallels the SW wall. The summus extends towards the NE into the room. In the middle of the benches is a rectangular -shaped table on a SW/NE axis. As extant neither the benches nor the table show evidence of stucco or painting. On the NE end of the imus there is a low platform possibly used for placing a container of some sort.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Triclinium 2993 to NW
Preparation platform 3000 to NE

DESCRIPTION: Garden 10 contains 16 furrows: 7 to northwest of the pool, 9 to the southeast, used for growing trees of various kinds such as hazelnut, peach, plum, and apricot. On each side a small pathway running southeast-northwest separates the furrows into 2 groups.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the center triclinium 3024, and fish pools 3030 lie in the middle of the furrows. Water feature in the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
This space is in the House of Trebius Valens. It is identified as a dining room (or repositorium by Eschebach). It is a rectangular space on a northwest/southeast axis. The entrance is located in the center of the southeast wall. No threshold is visible. No flooring is visible. The walls are opus incertum. Plaster and fresco remain on all walls. The lower frieze is black. There are white panels above this with red border lines. The room is in poor condition, although restored to full height with a reconstructed ceiling. There are two large rectangular windows on the southwest wall. Near the center of the southwest wall is a visible brick column of the original colonnade It is embedded in the wall. A round window is placed over the center of the western window. These dining room windows open to a view of the peristyle garden and outdoor triclinium.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 102, 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of the "ambulatory" (16) and to the northeast of the peristyle garden (12), and the outdoor triclinium (24).

DESCRIPTION:
This sheet replaces sheet #30.
Kitchen 13 is entered from posticum 16 to the south. The medium-sized rectangular room is oriented northwest/southeast. It contains a cooking platform on the eastern side of the space. It also includes a latrine(14) to the north of the cooking platform. The northern and western walls are preserved to about 2.30 centimeters high. On the top of the northern wall above the cooking platform is evidence of five rows of rectangular terracotta tiles which are interrupted in the middle with what looks like a window. On the small wall a farther window opens to the northern end. It is about 1.7 centimeters above the ground. On the northern wall is a large fragment of plaster was a few traces of red color. The eastern side of the southern wall rests against the pillar-like door frame of the back entrance(21). This wall which is not well-preserved slopes down towards the entrance into the kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Posticum 16 to the south. Store room 12 to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
This replace sheet #1253.
Cooking platform is a large structure in the southeastern corner of kitchen (13). The surface is covered with large irregularly-shaped terracotta tiles. Along the eastern and northern sides the edges are raised a few centimeters above the central area. They are delimited on the exterior sides by a row of vertical terracotta tiles. At the bottom of the exterior side of the cooking platform to the south are two deep semicircular niches which were used as ovens. The oven to the north next to the latrine is blocked by the structure supporting the platform. The cooking platform is oriented to south/north-east/west.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the eastern side of Kitchen 13. Latrine to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the House of the Vettii. We have identified this space as a cubiculum/small reception room. The entrance is on the north side of the room facing onto the atrium. There are frescoes on all walls, not extant in upper area of the room. Original floor is not extant. The dado is a red background with vertical and horizontal white stripes creating separate panels. Dado imagery is possible; olive foliage and abstract foliage decor. The main frieze features a light background divided into panels of various sizes with images of floating figures. There are also winged individuals surrounded by vines, urns, light stands and fowl.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Jashemski II, pp 153-155, Eschebach pp 218-219
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This cubiculum/small reception room is next to a stairway in the southeast quadrant of the house, and its doorway on the north faces out to the atrium.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform is a small rectangular platform along the southwest wall abutting the north wall with an arched fuel storage niche beneath. The platform is in poor condition and the arched opening has begun to collapse. Because of the condition it is not possible to know what exactly the surface is covered with. A marble sill has been inserted into the floor within the arched opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The cooking platform is located along the south west wall of room 8, the kitchen, south west of the arched niche located in the kitchen space.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular kitchen, NW/SE axis. Doorway in SE to Room 47, square plaster window with modern lintel high in SW wall to Room 45. Traces of undecorated plaster in NE/SW walls, two holes at the N and S ends of W wall for joists match to holes opposite on the E wall. At the S end of E wall are 2 smaller holes for shelves? Along SW wall, starting in the S corner, is a large rectangular masonry preparation platform (2920) that abuts directly to cooking platform (2920) to the NW. The floor is obscured. Modern roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Door to S/SE to Room 47.

DESCRIPTION: Enter the room from the southeast side of room 25. We go through a small room, then SE into the dining room. There is a marble threshold which is broken into two pieces. The mosaic floor is gone. On the NE wall is a large window overlooking the orchard. Centered directly above the large window is a smaller window. On the SE wall is another set of windows, duplicating the east wall. They also look onto the orchard. The N wall shows evidence of red wall painting with a black dado along the bottom edge. The room was roofed in modern times.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 25 to NW

DESCRIPTION: Sodo refers to a dining scene painted in this room. Location in room unknown. Not possible to enter room.

We enter this garden from corridor 5 to the northeast. At the end of this corridor we see a wall. About a third of the wall is preserved with full-sized amphorae. To the northwest of this wall there is a latrine. There is a southeast entrance to a rectangular garden. The walls of the garden are high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (5) to southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The mill 6088 is a meta stone which is not in situ and is located in the southeast corner of the western half of room one (1) and was possibly part of a small hand rotary mill. The meta is circular in shape with an opening in the center at the top for the mill furniture. The meta is approximately 60 cm in height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill 6088 is located south of mills 6086 and 6086 and is located in the southeast corner of the western most half of room one.

DESCRIPTION: Storeroom 4 is entered from a very narrow corridor to the southwest between a flight of stairs and the oven. The orientation of this room is southwest to northeast. The threshold is marked by a block of volcanic stone which is about 30 cm high above the floor of the adjoining corridor, while the top of the stone is on the level of the storeroom. The floor is today covered with lapilli. The walls are preserved at different heights. The northwest wall contains a rectangular recess which is about 25 cm deep. Because of the location next to the oven and mill room, the room might have been used for storing wheat or bakery products.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: mill room 3 to southwest with oven to northwest

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular room is on a northeast/southwest axis. A doorway is in the east corner with modern lintel. The northeast wall is extensively restored. Traces of undecorated plaster on the northwest wall. There is a hole in the west end of the southwest wall through to adjoining room. The southwest wall is restored. The southeast wall is restored. The opus signinum floor throughout is partially obscured by moss. There is an opus signinum threshold as well. The large masonry cooking platform and hearth extend along the entire northwest wall (2984). A Base of a poorly preserved semi circular feature is in the south corner of the room and the Function is unknown.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (6) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Replicate almost exactly the 2988 feature. One side of the triclinium bench opens to the room; the other is connected to the neighbors wall to the northwest and the other ruins along the wall to the horticultural space. The end of the bench connected to the horticultural wall shows concrete and bricks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bench triclinium masonry: to the south west 2988; to the northwest 2989; to the west 2990

DESCRIPTION: On the NE side of the dining room is a masonry bench triclinium opening to the SE. The imus abuts and parallels the SW wall and the medius the NW wall. The summus extends into the room to the SE. In the middle of the benches is a large rectangular masonry table on a SW/NE axis. In the N corner where the medius and summus meet both abut a low wall. As reconstructed the summus appears at a slightly lower level than the medius but this may not have been the case in antiquity. As extant neither the benches nor the table show evidence of stucco or painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Triclinium 2993 to SE
Preparation platform 3000 to NE

DESCRIPTION: This is a dolium in store room (5) located as the second dolium from the entrance. This is embedded in the ground almost to the shoulder. The body is a large, rounded form curving in to a broad neck and rim which flares outward and slightly downward. The stem appears to be intact.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is north west of dolium 5026. It is against the south west wall of this room.

DESCRIPTION: The bench/couch niche is located in the east corner of the room along the northeast wall. The niche is approximately 50 cm in height and has been recessed into the wall and the red painted plaster interior survives. Some conservation has been applied.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The niche 6100 is located in the east corner of the room 2 (6099 - Dining Room)

DESCRIPTION: The preparation room is a rectangular room off the kitchen room 8 and also accessible from the corridor room 6. The room survives in poor condition with the remains of the plaster present south corner of the southwest wall (no discernible color). The southwest wall has the remains of red plaster and close to the entry to the kitchen is a channel cut into the floor for waste disposal. Traces of plaster remain on the northwest wall. The floor is covered with lapilli and the walls are at low height with exception to the southeast wall which survives to about 2.5 m with 2 beam holes inserted at east end of southeast wall and approximately 2 m and 2.25m height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 7 is contiguous to Room 8, the kitchen, to the northwest, Room 6 to the north and room 3 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a couch niche located along the northern half of the northwest wall of dining room (9) in the Villa of the Moasaic Columns. This is an unusually long niche. It is low and shallow with a curved top. Plaster remains over most of it with red lines visible in the middle area.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The couch niche is across the room and to the northwest of the Lararium (5026). It is northwest of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: Large square cooking platform in NW corner of the room (47A), large recessed storage, partially filled with debris and earth. Surface of platform is plastered and a large plastered partition extends south across the platform, dividing the platform in two. The half of the platform to the W of this partition is raised above the level of the surface of the rest of the platform. There is a buttress lip along the N wall (placing for a grill?)

DESCRIPTION: The entrance to the Herculaneum Gate is approached by the via di Sepulcri. An arcade is located on the north east side. To the west of the arcade is a paved area that is approximately double the size of the street and may have been used for carts or animals. There are twenty nine shops covered by the arcade and one outside. Shops with dolia, fish tanks, and pottery are evidenced along the arcade. The arches of the arcade show brickwork and a combination of other materials. There is some evidence of a paved flooring in the space but it is presently covered in vegetation, as it perhaps was in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north side of the via di Sepulcri, along shops 15 to 29.

DESCRIPTION: Masonry dining bench extending along Southeast and East walls of room 47. Benches have 2 arms extending Northwest to the center of the room. Between the arms of the benches are two square masonry tables of opus signinum work. The benches and tables are plastered throughout in red. The plaster is contiguous with that of the adjoining floor. The couches are too narrow for reclining and must have been used by seated diners. The surface of the Western most of the two tables is broken away and the plaster facing of the arms of the benches has collapsed in places. There appears to have been extensive modern restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Masonry triclinium to Northwest (2918)

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room NW/SE axis. NW wall has a poorly preserved doorway at W end opening to corridor and atrium 18. Above this door is a square plaster internal window. There is extensive first style decoration with red border and yellow or white background. On the NE wall undecorated plaster survives with placing for shelf supports. High in the center of SE wall is a window with a modern lintel and undecorated plaster. The SW wall has undecorated plaster and placing for shelf support. There is a poorly preserved window at S end which might be collapse. Also a poorly preserved door at W end of S wall which might indicate collapse. The upper courses of the walls are restored and the floor is obscured by earth, debris and vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor to Atrium 18 to NW

DESCRIPTION: The northwest wall has fourth style painting with a black dado, green leaves, and red central space. Above the cornice are two pomegranates and the bottom third of a basket. A fish is hanging from the basket. A golden apple is below the basket.

The room is on a northwest/southeast axis. We enter from entrance (10) from the southwest. The entrance floor is soil. To the south, there is a toilet enclosure with four slotted windows. There is an additional window on the south side of the toilet. The toilet is separated from the kitchen by a plastered wall. Moving to the second large part of the area, there is a large cooking platform. The cooking platform area has a roof The third part of the complex was probably used for storage. There is a window over the cooking platform. In the third area, there are two large high windows. There is a high
wall separating the work area from a hallway to the old atrium. There is a large window in the wall to the adjoining room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (17) to the north and room (28) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform runs the entire length of the southeast wall with two recessed, arched niches underneath for storage of wood, coal, or kitchen equipment. There is evidence of tiles on the top of the cooking platform. The wall is plastered in this area, and there is a window above the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water feature, basin (2929) to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This is a narrow, long rectangular basin extending along the southern side of the room. The poorly preserved lip of the basic rises above the floor while the interior is embedded below. The base of the basin is obscured by earth so that it is impossible to discern its depth. No visible lining survives although traces of plaster survive above the basin on the wall to the south.

Bibliography: Eschenbach pp. 102 - 103

DESCRIPTION:
In the house of Trebius Valens we have identified room 5 as kitchen. This is a rectangular room with an east-northeast - west-southwest axis. The floor is of earth. In the center of the southwest wall there is a doorway with a modern lintel opening to the corridor to the west. All four walls show extensive restoration and consolidation, especially in the upper courses to a modern ceiling.
High in the northeast corner is a rectangular window tapering to the northeast. Undecorated plaster survives in the north, east and south walls. In the center of the northwest wall, a plastered brick buttress stands against the wall, in front of which is a low masonry support. To the west of the buttress there is a square platform (4615) and the blocked oven of the adjoining baths (6 and 7). To the east, there is a latrine (4614) , and a high narrow masonry platform, separated from the latrine by a partition wall, the lower courses of which survive. Along the southeastern wall there is a rectangular basin (4617), above which in the south corner is a lararium (4616).
BIBLIOGRAOHY ESCHEBACH PAGE102
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor 9 is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This large dining hall looks south on to the peristyle garden and fountain. It has a single large entry at the south end and there are three arcoated niches with semi-curricular tops in which a stucco shell has been created. On the west wall the arcoated niche is present in the middle of the wall; the wall is decorated with red and yellow and black plaster in large panels. The room filled with archaeological equipment and therefore not entirely visible. The niche in the middle of the west wall was painted with blues and greens whilst the upper semicircular area contains a large seashell in stucco with a stucco banding beneath. The upper area of the niche is painted in reds and whites. On the west wall near the south entrance to the room are two emblema scenes but the southern most has been removed while the second is in bad condition. It is possible to see an upper register of yellow banding on the wall painting. On the north wall plaster survives only on the lower register in yellows and reds in the northwest corner. Again the arcoated niche is in the center of the wall and is as described fort he west wall: however the stucco work banding beneath the shell is better preserved with possible details of bead and reel decorations visible. On the east wall the plaster is much better preserved and three registers are visible in whites, yellows, reds and black. The semicircular niche is again in the middle of the east wall but is badly preserved. The wall paintings are fourth style in this room. Around the arcoated niche on the east wall it is possible to see the remains of a marble sill at the south east corner and the remains of a pilaster surround on the lower half of the arcoated niche.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 47 is contiguous to room 48 to the west; room 39 (peristyle and fountains) to the south and room 46 to the east. North of room 47 is the exterior property wall.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, northwest southeast axis. The northwest wall is no longer extent, doorway in the center of the south east wall opens to vineyard (1). Above the door is a modern lintel and two rectangular joist holes. Above is a modern roof. All three extent walls preserve traces of plaster , red lower register with white above. The north east wall is extensively restored, but preserves a trace of molded top above which is a modern pillar roof. Step up in the north west, with single step to higher level floor to the northwest. The base of the south east wall, in the east corner, a terracotta drain, drains out from the processing room to the vineyard. Stone stepped threshold to the doorway in the south west wall. In the north corner of base of what was the north east wall is the terracotta out pipe into the processing room. The floor is earth, into which are embedded two lines, against either length wall are five submerged dolia (2954), in total 10. The south west wall features a large poorly preserved window into the press room (4) with modern lintel. Below window is low rectangular step or bench. Extending west to the end of south west wall, along it, is raised plastered, narrow channel. At the west end is a drain into the adjoining room. Above, approximately two feet, the channel, a long horizontal facing has been cut into the plaster wall. Parts of four roof tiles are still extent in this placing to provide a sloping cover, protecting the channel below. In the external face of the channel, three lead pipes, the fourth is no longer extent, drain from the channel into the dolium below. The channel was used to drain the must from the vat of the press room (4) into the preparation room and dolia. Channel feature number 2957
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 4 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Poorly preserved U-shaped counter of which only the lower courses survive in the North of the room, facing the street to the North/Northeast. Adjoins a rectangular plastered recessed storage cupboard niche in the wall to the BE. Ruddell refers to a dolium, but nothing is visible.
The niche is a rectangular niche in the northeast corner of the room. A small amount of red and white plaster survives a the bottom of the southwest corner of the niche.

Large "U"-shaped masonry dining couch, sloping out to N/NW/W/NE. The couch is plastered throughout with opus signinum on upper surface. The couch plaster is painted red throughout. Between the arms of the couch is a solid masonry circular table, plastered and painted red. The W corner of the couch slopes down to a drainage channel through the wall to the street to the N.

DESCRIPTION: The latrine is located in the southeast corner. The latrine is in a very badly degraded state. Two niches survive for the plank. 1 in the south wall and 1 in the east wall. The floor is cocciopesto. The floor is collapsing in the southeast corner.

DESCRIPTION: Eschebach 389-390
Eschebach 389-390

There was a triclinium (medius 4.60 m, imus and summus 3.20 m) attached to the south wall. On sides of triclinium, which were finished with painted plaster, two amorini were painted on a red background. The one on right trying to ward off a pheasant that attempts to peck at a bunch of grapes held by the amorino, the other amorino drinking from a bowl while pushing back an animal, perhaps a leopard. Triclinium table, rectangular in shape with an incurving semicircle in front (1.40 x 0.90 m), had a top decorated with circles, squares and triangles of colored marble.

In the west corner of the garden to the southeast of the kitchen is a well. The aboveground structure is topped by a rectangular piece of volcanic stone. Depth is indeterminate. The well head, except the top stone, seems to have been stuccoed and possibly painted.

DESCRIPTION:
It has been identified that 3, 2, 1 was a domestic house. We have determined that the last usage of Room 2 was as a foyer. This identification is based on the location of the room within the structure and room size. Foyer 2 is entered from the northern side of Atrium 3 and leads into Dining Room 3 to the southeast. The heavily reconstructed walls are partly preserved. No traces of wall painting and flooring remain. The space is currently used for the storage of roof tiles.
ESCHEBACH PAGES 102 AND 103
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Hall 3.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular masonry preparation [platform, no storage; poorly preserved plaster surface. Against SW wall there is a thick buttressed lip with plastered top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: cooking platform 2920 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: On the northwest wall above the level of the rectangular niche are the remains of painted decoration. In the west corner, one is able to detect a bunch of grapes; to the north is a seascape showing what appears to be a large crocodile above which is a boat with three individuals. Farther to the north a large individual is shown from the waist up, and behind him there appears to be another boat.
To the south east of the entrance to the food shop 15 sits a narrow masonry bench which could be used by customers of the shop

This feature is on the exterior of the shop (4891) along the arcade. The feature has been identified as a fish tank.The tank is rectangular across the front of the shop (south west wall / opening) It is of opus incertum on the north west, south west and south east sides which abut the long masonry blocks across the south west opening. Remains of plaster (opus signinum) are visible on the walls of the north corner of the tanks and there are two drainage cuttings across the masonry blocks which form the south west wall of the tank.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This shop is to the north east side of the arcade, to the north west of shop 19.

DESCRIPTION: In the NW corner of the garden is the kitchen. One enters the kitchen through a door on the SE corner of the room. The room is very small, rectangular in shape lying on a N/S axis. In the SW corner, taking up about half of the W wall is a masonry structure which was probably the cooking platform as extant the center part of the structure is missing. There could have been a wooden top to allow for cooking. To the N of the cooking platform is a small area for a latrine. The walls were once plastered, but no decoration remains. The floor seems to be a beaten plaster. As extant on the S, W and N walls there are small holes that let in light. It is unknown if these are ancient windows. Ceiling has been reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 9 garden south. Room 9 garden south. None

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room, narrowing to the east end. Room is entered from the atrium. Travertine threshold remains in situ at entrance. Remnants of plaster remain on east, south, and west walls some of which retain evidence of red color.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is contiguous with porticoed atrium (5) to north. Room is contiguous with porticoed atrium (5) to north. None

DESCRIPTION: Medium-sized rectangular room. The ceiling is rather low and appears to be a modern reconstruction. The ancient ceiling was probably higher. This ceiling is exactly the same height as doorway. All the walls appear to be ancient, however, they've been painted over recently with white paint. There is a small square window centrally located on back east wall with modern bars blocking the view. The doorway is centrally located on west wall directly opposite the window. DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain 4733 is on the south side of the via di Castricio in front of (north west) 1.16.4. The fountain is made of volcanic stone slabs. The ancient floor is eroded thus it is not possible to discern if it had opus signinum lining. The pilaster is in the centre of the south east slab and is decorated with a patera or plate in relief. It has no modern plumbing. The overflow is offset at the top of the north western slab with a drain hole directly below. Interior dimensions of the basin are 0.82 m. by 0.82 m. and it is 0.635 m. deep. There are worn hand recesses on the north east side of the pilaster and near the east and south interior corners. There is a large gouge in the stone to the east of the over flow.

Floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. High in the southwest wall are two lararia (4456, 4457). Against the centre of the north wall is a low masonry platform base for stairs. In the centre of the east half of the room are the fragmentary remains of a hearth (4455). Against the west wall is a shallow rectangular tufa basin, not clear if in situ. In the south corner is the plaster-lined recess for a couch niche or bed. High on the southwest wall are the placings for the joists of the floor above. A trace of white plaster with lower red section can be seen in the lower section of the northwest corner of the room.

Bibliography: Eschebach p205

In the east corner of shop VIII, 5, 10 is a preparation platform acting as one of the indicators, along with two basins, that Eschebach was correct in suggesting that this was either a grocery or drinks shop. What we see today is a low rectangular solid stone, fairly small in size, excavation in the east corner, along with the presence of a drain pipe from the upper floor, suggesting we may have a latrine instead.

Bibliography: Eschebach p381

DESCRIPTION: This water tower is on the northwest corner of the Via del Vesuvio at the intersection with the Vicolo di Mercurio. It is on the southeast corner of 6.16.3. This water tower is constructed of tufa masonry and is 0.88 meters northwest of public fountain 4828. It has pipe recesses on the northwest, southwest and northeast faces. There is some calcium carbonate within the northwest pipe recess, but a much heavier calcium carbonate accumulation is found on all other sides of the tower, especially on the southeast. The tower and fountain (4828) are near a fullery that is currently being excavated.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This water tower is at the southeast corner of 6.16.3. immediately northwest of public fountain 4828.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room, opened to south to large window. Nice remains of painted wall plaster on west and east, not so preserved against north end as well as poorly preserved fragments of plaster beneath segmental arch of vault. The floor is exceptionally well preserved but dirty. White tesserae create octagonal and diamond forms. Octagons displayed pieces of colored marble all in a darker matrix ( matrix not mosaic) (See PPM Vol. 8). Toward back, that is north of room is rectangular panel bordered by stripes, black and white tesserae, with white central mosaic in which larger pieces of colored and veined marble displayed. Circular discs in center. Squares and triangles of various shapes. Unique features are the furniture niches which are cut into the east and west flank walls. West is clearly visible, but east obstructed by large wooden frame. The niche is deeper and taller than most and has protruding bench like feature within. The two niches are not opposite. West wall niche is further south than mate in east wall. On west wall, above niche, is a patch of plaster that has been removed in a regular shape suggesting that the painting was taken. Smaller hole through existing painted wall in northwest. Note: not discussing features of paintings. Found in PPM.

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain is located at the intersection of the via di Castricio and the via di Nocera. It is on the southeast corner of address 1.13.10. It is constructed of smaller volcanic stone slabs than is usually seen for the fountains in Pompeii. There are 8 slabs. There is an added lining to round the junction of the floor to walls of the basin. There is opus signinum on the lining and floor of the basin. The interior dimensions of the basin are 1.11 m. by 0.68 m. and is 0.60 m. deep. The pilaster is not attached at the top center of the wall, but is part of the central nouthwestern slab. The pilaster is decorated with the head of a woman with a diadem (possibly Juno or a nymph). On the northwest side the slabs appear to have been joined by butterfly clamps which also appear to have been used on the south west side. There is no overflow. There is a drainage hole in the north corner with the bottom of the opening approximately 0.21 m. above the current ground level. A deep hand recess is near the southern interior corner of the basin. Adjoining the fountain to the north are the remains of the lower portion of a street shrine. There is a large buildup of stones on the west side of the fountain.
BIBLIOGRAPHY: Pompeii in Pictures

This public fountain 4822 sits at the intersection of the vicolo della Regina and the vicolo dei Dodici Dei. It is on the south eastern side of the vicolo della Regina in front of 8.2.29. It is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The pilaster is seated atop the south western slab and is decorated with a bull or ox head. There is an added sloped lining at the wall / floor junction of the basin that is covered with opus signinum. At the top of the north eastern slab are five iron pins in situ. There are three iron pins in situ on the top of the south eastern slab. This fountain has no modern plumbing. The overflow is centred on the top of the north western slab. The basin has two drainage holes: one 0.15 m. below the overflow and one at ground level of the north western slab. There are worn hand recesses near the western interior corner and south of the pilaster (possibly a knee?) The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.70 m. by 0.92 m. and it is 0.65 m. deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: on the vicolo della Regina outside 8.2.29
