It has been determined that this early house may have been used as a commercial property or solely as domestic. This space is identified as a dining room; it is a very large rectangular room with a northwest - southeast axis. This attribution is based on size, location, and features. The room has undergone restoration, particularly the upper walls and the modern ceiling. The ceiling is restored sloping down to the northwest. The room is filled with modern materials stored throughout the room. Cocciopesto flooring can be seen in the western corner of the room and the rest of the room is either obscured with modern materials or under dirt. The main entrance to this dining room is a large doorway along the southeast wall. There is no evidence of a threshold. A lower secondary doorway passes through the eastern end of the northeast wall, also without a threshold. The walls are predominantly Opus Incertum and the doors are flanked by large stonework or brickwork.

DESCRIPTION: Room is entered from hallway 30 on the northeast wall of kitchen. There is another entrance on the southeast wall from room 27. There is no roof and the floor is obscured by lapilli. There are seven features identified in this room The entrance on northeast wall, viewed from the interior is damaged and reconstructed with some faint traces of reddish color in plaster. At the stone threshold there is one step down from corridor 30 with evidence of a door jamb. Facing the southeast wall to the lower right side is feature 6405, a preparation platform. Above the doorway and preparation platform and to the right of the doorway is a round hole. In the northeast corner of the room is a cooking platform (6401). There is a lararium (6403) on the southeast wall to the left of the doorway. Facing the southwest wall we see damage and reconstruction with a trace of plaster and faint red paint. Facing the wall to the lower right on the floor is evidence of a latrine (6404) (with a stone projection that may have held a shelf), with drainage on the floor under the wall to the right. Facing the wall about in the middle is an arched recessed niche, high up. It is connected to a pipe opening, allowing running water to reach the floor level water feature (6406). The recessed niche is above feature 6405 called a preparation platform. The pipe-like opening has one side and is open on the other side. It is a long narrow recessed space. The northwest wall is damaged and reconstructed, with no trace of plaster. Facing the wall, there is a long, large cooking platform with a restored tile surface. Facing the wall to the left there is construction with possible evidence of a latrine. Facing the wall to the right is a recessed area from floor to ceiling that possibly held a furnace for the baths. There are seven features in the room. There is apparent water from possible pipe through niche into basin below.

Entrance is off corridor 30 to the east.

CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is to the northeast of the atrium. Room 3 is to the northwest. Room 4 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Latrine 6368 is on south wall in the eastern corner. Latrine appears to be in close relationship to cooking platform and what may be an arched recess to a sewer (?)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the east wall at opposite end of the doorway that goes to the street. East of cooking platform 6367 and southeast of cooking platform 6366.

DESCRIPTION: This room is a narrow corridor aligned northwest-southeast along the southwest side of the house. There is an entrance at the southeast end, as well as a passage to the next room (4) at the northwest. A large stone vat (3755) is located along the southwest wall occupying the northern portion of the room. This room is in poor condition. The walls are only preserved to about nine feet in height. Very little plaster remains over the rough cut stone and mortar. No finished flooring is visible, no roofing remains. The vat suggests that this area held life fish or was used for processing related to the activity in room 4.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is northwest of corridor 2. This room lies to the southeast of room 4.

DESCRIPTION: This feature appears to have been a support to hold a dolium or basin. It is low and abuts feature 3759 (the vat) and 3757 (preparation platform). Although it is broken off it appears to have been one height in antiquity and was lined with cement, which was painted red. it intrudes into the space of the platform which is next to 3759.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to vat 3759 and to platform 3757.

DESCRIPTION: A square altar, small, is directly below lararium. The altar was faced with fired beige/light coral plaster, which appears in several places on the room's walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 3759 above on northwest wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is a niche-shelf. It is a recessed area about 1 foot deep and about 4 feet wide. The height can not be determined since the wall has not been preserved to its full extent. There are traces of plaster on the southeast side of the niche. Otherwise it is just rubble and ashlar masonry of the wall. No evidence of shelf holes or brackets remains. At the upper level of the northeast wall two cross section pieces of column drum are reused in this all.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is along the northeast wall of the house. Latrine (3825) is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: In the southwest wall there is a cupboard located in the middle of the wall. This is a cupboard about 10 to 12 inches in depth. It retains most of its plaster covering. The etched seam continues through these cupboards. Two small cut holes are at the base of the back wall and appear to be deliberate. Small bracket holes are aligned toward the front of the cupboard on both sides, suggesting shelf supports. The back wall preserves a series of small holes. The northern most one still containing the metal fitting. One horizontal line of these holes is about halfway up the cupboard and a second group of lines up approximately a foot above these. This is in poor condition with restoration at the top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: #3753 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room. The wide doorway to the atrium (1) takes up almost the entire north wall. Only the lower courses of the wall survive with modern restoration. The floor is obscured by lapilli, debris, and weeds. The adjoining room (8) to the west is possibly a latrine and the function of room 7 is also unclear. Both rooms 7 & 8 are filled with debris. Eschebach says there is a kitchen and a latrine, but there is no visible evidence.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The kitchen is a small rectangular room with a north/south axis directly to the south of entrance 1. Lower courses of the walls survive with extensive modern restoration. The floor is obscured by lapilli. The adjoining room 25 to the southeast contains a latrine under the stairs, accessed from entrance 2.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 20 to north.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is the painted area beneath the barrel vault on the east wall. A large rooster is painted facing the center area from the north corner and is shown eating grapes. To the north of this rooster is a basket of pomegranates. Another pomegranate is located toward the south side of the painting. there are also other objects that cannot be identified but may have to do with food.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mills (3265, 3266, 3267) to the W; painting (3254) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: In the south west corner of the tomb chamber projects the head of an amphora which has been identified as the head of a libation tube by Campbell.

This public fountain 4823 is in front of the temple of Aesculapius at 8.7.25. it is on the west side of via Stabiana. It consists only of a volcanic stone pilaster decorated with an incised patera or plate. It has no modern plumbing and no basin. The pilaster is embedded in the curb stones and extends all the way to the street level. On the back of the pilaster a vertical pipe recess is visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: in front of 8.7.25 (temple of Aesculapius)

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room. The south wall is absent to allow an opening to the atrium to the south. Only the lower courses of the north, east and west walls survive, with modern restoration. The bulk of the north wall consists of a wide, low window looking into the garden to the north. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Against the center of the west wall there is a modern or restored square basin or pit (?) with a tile and cement lip. The function and date is unclear.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium (4) is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is a Catillus in poor condition with both ends broken. It is black basalt. It is not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Two other catilli sit next to this one (3265 and 3266) along the north wall.

DESCRIPTION: We enter room 14 from 'corridor' 5. Room 14 is southeast if the 'corridor'. There is a marble threshold. The doorway is topped with a modern concrete lintel and is medium height. The room is a Roman square room and the floor is a mixture of mud and Lapilli. The wall which opens to the corridor holds a large window overlooking the garden and corridor. the window is closed to 2/3 height with a corrugated iron sheet. Two of the vaults show plaster with white and red paint. There is a modern ceiling. This room contains paint, boards, concrete, tubing for use of custodians.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjoins corridor 5 to the north; Rooms 11, 12 and 13 to which there no access, to the south; Dining Room (3256) to the NW; Dining room (3258) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: At the far northwest corner of the house is a small rectangular room. The room is extremely narrow. There was a low ceiling as evidenced by a series of holes at a height of approximately at six and half feet along the two long walls. The room is orientated in a east west direction. Plaster is present on the lower half of the three walls. The doorway to space 3 constitutes the fourth wall. There are no windows. The floor is rubble. The room has been identified as a kitchen solely based upon Eschebach's description.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The northwest walls abut the adjoining property. The south wall abuts room (5). The doorway opens to space (3).

DESCRIPTION: This dining room is a square room with a northeast/ southwest axis. The entrance is on the southwest wall and is a wide opening. No threshold or flooring is visible. In general the walls are poorly preserved with plaster repairing on the southwest , northwest and northeast walls. The construction of the southwest wall at the south corner is opus vittatum. The southeast wall has used ceramic and brick mixed into the stonework. There is a fairly large window in the northeast wall with a view to space (6). There is an arched recess (niche 3241) in the northern corner of the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (3249) to the southwest and room 6 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This long cooking platform runs approximately 8 feet (240 cm) along the southwest wall on a northwest/southeast axis. The northwest portion abuts the partition which delineates the room from the street entrance (22). The platform is made of lava rock and mortar. It appears to have been plastered in antiquity as evidenced on the lower north face. This platform is low although the height could be raised with lapilli and/or the surface could be missing a layer or two. On the east end of the northeast face is a poorly preserved arched recess. The unusual feature of this platform is its inclusion of the base of an arch which is build into the wall and covered with original plaster. Therefore a small section of the southwestern abutment incorporates the jutting arch. This platform is poorly preserved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous with feature 3887 (lararium) to northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform appears to be in relatively good condition. It runs along the northwest/southeast axis. This is a large cooking platform approximately six feet in length (180 cm), five feet deep (150 cm) and three feet high (90 cm). The surface of the cooking platform is covered in moss however terra cotta tiles form the surface beneath. The platform itself seems to be made of stones, brick and mortar, the front of which can be seen on the southwest face. There are two concreted arched recesses for wood storage. Plaster painted red is evident on both southwest and northwest faces. The platform abuts the northeast and southeast walls. There is evidence of a lip along the three sides which was made of lava stone covered with terra cotta roof tiles. Most of the northwest face is covered with painted red plaster.

This house is domestic. This is a dining space opening from the atrium (ala). This ala, or wings, on the southwest mirrors an ala across the atrium on the northeast side. This space is in poor condition with reconstruction of the upper walls. This space is walled on three sides and still has a great deal of plaster and paint on the lower portions. The painting is either third or fourth style. The central zone preserves rectangular spaces and on the southwest walls one can see roundels which presumably would have contained portraits. This same wall also has two large restored holes which may have been for tunneling in. Up a molding remains in part on all three walls. Joist holes go across the entire length of the southwest wall. The floor is white mosaic with black bands around the periphery.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Space is southwest of the impluvium and in the atrium (2). Room 19 is to the northwest. Room 18 is to the southwest

DESCRIPTION: The room is on a northwest/southeast axis and is narrow and actually contains part of the corridor the the back of the structure. The room contains a vat (3819) in the southern corner of the southwest wall. In the west corner of the room there is a portion of a terra cotta pipe from above and a drain common to the northwest wall. The room is sloped towards the street. Only fragments of plaster appear on the southeast and southwest walls. The northwest wall is faced with brick. There is a piece of plaster low on the northeast and a deep groove in the northeast wall toward the entrance of the room. The floor is obscured with lapilli and debris. The walls are of indeterminate height, but high on the southwest and northwest walls. The ceiling is not extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 to the southeast and room 3 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Connected to the vat (3818) is a long rectangular preparation platform.l
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Vat (3818) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: On the west wall of this salesroom is a possible fish tank 4. It is rectangular and is partially coated with opus signinum. It is about knee high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Prep platform (3817).

DESCRIPTION: This platform consists of a bricked arch with storage beneath and a tiled surface. The west and east end of the cooking platform show traces of plaster and the west end is directly attached to latrine 6502. These two features are located at the west end of the south wall of kitchen room 2 (6501).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: East of latrine 6502.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining room from the atrium. There is a stone basalt threshold. This is a rectangular room with a north/south axis. The floor is pounded mud. Today we see pounded mud and lapilli. There are a few sections that show cement. On the east wall, a section is covered with plaster. The north wall has on the high zone signs of a window and beneath this window there seems to have once been a pipe (?). There are also traces of a red border. On the west wall we see one/third plaster. There are faint indications of a red border on one part of the wall and yellow rectangle. On the south wall we see plaster that is undecorated. The plastered remnants on three walls are held in place by modern metal butterfly hooks. We see no sign of a roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the atrium (4) and to the entrance hallway (1).

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room with a doorway at the south end of the west wall to room 5. It has a modern lintel. The floor is obscured by lapilli. The south and west walls show signs of restoration. Undecorated plaster survives on all four walls, but most extensively on the north and east walls. High in the east wall there is a square plater window opening to the street. In the south wall are two poorly preserved holes for shelves (?). There are also several randomly spaces holes in the north wall. Eschebach identifies this a as a kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 is to west.

DESCRIPTION: To the northwest of entrance seven of Vicolo della Fullonica is a large rectangular room with two doorways. One leads to the south (atrium 1), the other leading to the east into a passageway (2). No door sill evidence remains. On the east wall is a large window, just above waist height, that opens to room 3. Plaster remains on the west wall at the bottom. Other then that the wall are bare opus incertum. No flooring remains. A little bit of red plaster remains in the northeast corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North and west doors are contiguous to adjoining properties. South wall is contiguous to rooms 1 and 5. East wall is contiguous to spaces 2 and 3.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room with a side doorway to the garden at the west end of the north wall, with a marble threshold and placing for a door. The remainder of the north wall consists of a low open window looking over the garden. Traces of plaster survive on the base of the window. At the north end of the west wall there is a doorway to dining room 18 with a modern lintel and no preserved threshold. The partially preserved floor consists of marble chips inserted into cocciopesto. The ceiling of the room is modern restoration. Extensive 4th Style decoration exists on the south and west walls. Fragments of 4th Style decoration survive on the west wall. The central images survive on the south and east walls and are identified by Bianco as hermaphrodites.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 14 is to the north. Dining room 18 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular pedestal of two layers of tufa blocks comprise the superstructure of tomb 2.The tomb is located adjacent to the city gate to the north east. The top of the tomb is formed of a brick pillar topped with an egg shaped finial. The burial chamber is below ground and entered from the north west side. A series of six steps takes you to the burial level. Inside the burial chamber room 1, is located our feature4921 the neck of an amphora.

There is a large entrance to the shop on the southwest side from the Via Stabiana. It is a roman square room. The threshold is high with no signs of flaking. There are two catilli in the south corner on a lapilli floor. There is a smaller doorway on the northeast wall. The height of the wall is not ceiling height. There is evidence of pink plaster on all four walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (3249) sits to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION:
We enter the atrium in the southwest from the shop (3248) and look through to the hallway which is to the east. The southwest entrance
is blocked by an out of place catillus. The floor is uneven lapilli. The walls are over 3 meters high with minimal plaster which is pink.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The shop room 1 (3248) is to the southwest the dining room 3 (3240) is to the northeast. A hallway is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room north-south axis. Floor obscured by lapilli. Undecorated plaster survives on the south wall, the southwest corner, the northeast corner, the base of the north wall and northeast corner. In the north wall at the east end there is a poorly preserved window looking into atrium of VI-3-3, In the center of the north wall there is a small square hole. At the north end of the east wall there is a possible window of collapse? High in the center of south wall is a poorly preserved window. In the northern half of the west wall there is a doorway opening down to the salesroom to the west. The threshold consists of two masonry steps going down to the level of the sales room. There are no signs of a physical door in this place.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: One enters room 12 off andron 11 passing through room -3 to the north. The kitchen is rectangular on an east-west axis. On the western end of the room is found latrine (feature 6267) and on the east end of Room is cooking platform (6266). The room is divided between the two by a short divider wall. Some plaster remains on the walls and post holes on the south wall provide evidence of an upper story. On the east wall up high is an opening that may have been a window. No flooring remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen's west wall abuts Room 8. The opening on the north abuts space 13 and passageway 11. The south and east walls abut adjoining property.

DESCRIPTION: This is a large dining room. It is positioned at the back of the house with alignment to the front entrance (2), gives a sense of great formality. This large space used for dining or meeting gave its occupants a view to the peristyle garden (10) and to the tablinium, atrium and entrance. The room is now in poor condition, no flooring is visible, no ceiling remains. The walls remain to great height in some sections but no paint can be seen on the plastered surfaces. In addition to the very wide opening in the center of the northwest wall a small door opens onto corridor (12) in the northern corner of the room along the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is in the southeast section of the house. It is southwest of corridor 12 and northeast of room 18.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room. The west side is completely open to planted peristyle 34. No ceiling. Floor is damaged, with traces of conglomerate floor with pattern of white tesserae. North wall is badly damaged with traces of plaster with red and yellow paint. The east wall, rear wall, is badly damaged, with fragments of plaster. The south wall has no plaster remaining, is badly damaged. On the floor facing the dining room on the far right is the possible opening of round shaped stone on the floor with circular opening nearby, evidence of underground cavity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room opens completely west to a portico facing a planted area, small garden, with a planting wall surrounding it #34.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. This feature is a dolium in the eastern corner of the storeroom. This dolium has a base that flares up to slightly flaring sides, with a carrinated shoulder and then a flaring rim supports a wide, flat, horizontal lip.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium of located east of dolium (4518) and southeast of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: This tomb sits immediately to the north west of the very arge tomb of Eumachia. The tomb consists of a grand masonry pedestal topped with a house-like structure, fronted by four plastered and fluted columns with three statue niches behind with statues extant. The bottom base of the tomb has four niches with the middle two containing a columella. To the north west of the tomb, in what is today a grassy area, sits an altar partially reconstructed with a masonry top. This altar shares a wall with the tomb of Eumachia to the north east. The altar and rectangular tomb share an open space leadig to the street. It is hard to judge how much open area belonged to this tomb.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Directly south west of Eumachia's tomb.

DESCRIPTION: Circular masonry support for a mill, poorly preserved surface4. Moedern cement on exterior face. Neither the catillus nor the meta survive, although a fragment of a basalt catillus lies on the base.

Lararium painting. A white background with garlands above. From the south there is an unidentifiable figure. A lare facing north with his rhyton in his left hand. The other lare is not extent. A child standing next to a female figure with a staff. The lower half of the painting is completely destroyed. Above preparation platform 6423 and water basin 6421.
Wide shallow terracotta kneading basin with iron ties indicating repair in antiquity. Contiguous with 6413 to the north. The basin is embedded into a masonry plaster support.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
6413, 6414, 6415,6416 and 6417 to the north.
6409, 6408, 6411 and 6421 are all to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Shallow plastered kneading basin on top of plastered masonry. Support contiguous to kneading basin 6415 to the north. The terracotta kneading basin 6413 abuts directly to the south.
The cooking platform has no hint of a front lip but evidence of a side lip is present. The archway below is partially filled with lapilli and could have served as storage.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Not applicable

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. It has been identified that 7-2-20 is a domestic house. It has been determined that the last usage of Room 23 was for food and drink storage. This observation is based on the location within the structure and the presence of designated food and drink features, which are a water basin 4546, a cistern 4545, and lararium 4577.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach

We have determined that the House of Obellius Firmus is a residential property. This atrium is a grand space with a Tuscan impluvium of tufa. The impluvium has four grandiose fluted Corinthian columns at the corners. This space is on a Northwest/Southeast axis with alignment to the fauces (1) and tablinum (48). The great height of this space is also reflected in the very tall doorways of all the spaces opening to this atrium. The layout is fairly symmetrical with three doors opening on the Northeast side mirroring the three doors on the Southwest side. There is an ala near the South corner matching one to Eastern corner. A lararium (4432) is located in the Western corner. A large chest (4431) presently stands along the Southwestern side. There is a doorway from the South ala to room 47 which reflects the doorway from the East ala into space 8. The walls are primarily large stone masonry with some opus incertum, most of which is reconstruction. Small areas of plaster remain on some of the walls. No fresco remains. The floor are cement with random patterns of white stone. No ceilings remain. A channel running towards the Southeast is cut into the floor of the impluvium, terminating at a round white marble table top fountain sitting up on the Southeast border of the impluvium. In the impluvium, in front of the round table, are two stands for a small table. A larger rectangular table is presently positioned directly to the Southeast of the impluvium. This has white marble claw-foot legs mounted on dark greenish-black bases on top of the white marble blocks (some of these are modern reconstructions). The table top is a grey marble slab.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Eschebach, P. 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This atrium is to the Southeast entrance of the fauces (4) and Northwest of the tablinum (48).

DESCRIPTION: The latrine in kitchen 10 is in the west corner of the northwest wall. Evidence for the structure is supported by the four large terracotta pipes which appear to come from the second floor. On the southwest wall which runs from the northwest to the southeast evidence of plaster remains as well as on the northwest wall near the drain. A small window to the north on the northwest wall opens to the street near entrance 27. The floor is obscured by ash and debris however some rock appears to have made a channel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform 3239 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This is a cooking platform. Only slight traces of this platform remain including the southeast end where an outer edge can be seen abutting the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 3238 to the southwest

DESCRIPTION: There is a rectangular masonry platform on northeast/southwest axis with an elliptical extension to the northwest extending along the southeast wall of room (7) and (8). A circular wellhead is inserted into the center of the platform. The plaster lining base is obscured by earth. Adjoining the well to the east is a square plaster-lined basin. A narrow drain runs on the basin down into the adjoining well. A terra cotta pipe drains into the basin from the garden to the northeast. Undecorated plaster survives on the exterior face to the northeast. A terra cotta drain survives against the southeast wall of the basin into which runs a placing for a terra cotta down pipe from the floor above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (2979) is to the southwest. Latrine (2978) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: \N

A large square niche inserted into the wall of the insula is present at the crossroads. There are traces of plaster which survive on the sides and top rear. There are no visible decorations, and the niche is arched and the external face of the arch is finished with a brick arch and tile lip. The niche is two feet above the street level. There are traces of plaster with red paint surviving at the base of the wall. the masonry base of the niche is poorly preserved and covered by earth, but may have originally been painted.

Extensive painting along the entirety of the west/southwest wall. Plain plaster on which a lararium scene has been painted. From south, garlands above with lar depicted below with raised right hand, left hand pointing downwards but only preserved in fragments. Facing poorly preserved picture of lar of which only right arm and part of head survive. The lar is facing a tripod around which is an encircling snake. Garlands continue to the west corner with a third figure with raised left hand holding a cornucopia. In the west corner a fragment of red grapes.

Rectangular room southeast/northwest axis. Doorway in the west corner of the southwest wall stepping up to to room 3. F plastered floor preserved throughout. The southwest northwest and northeast walls preserve first style decorations with extensive surviving architectural molding and yellow lower register. High in the northwest corner modern (?) opening through the wall in to adjoining property. Cooking platform (3041) occupies the entirety of the southeast wall. Traces of red marble finish survive on the wall plaster in the southeast corner. The roof is modern.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 3 is to the west

DESCRIPTION: This is a long rectangular dining room. On the south east wall we see a plastered lararium niche. On the south west wall we see a water pipe with a few holes but well situated. There is a small window that overlooks a stairway in another room. There is a larger than usual couch niche on the north wall. There is no evidence of a floor and the ceiling no longer exists. We suggest that the location of this room would indicate a slaves' dining area. Walls were frescoed but little trace remains.
This is a minimal catillus; less than a fourth of this catillus remains. It sits in the south corner about one third of a meter from the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Catillus (3244) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Currently open area at the northwest end of room 17, latrine is identified by terracotta floor tile sloping down towards the cooking platform to the south. Additional evidence within the west wall of the latrine is a terracotta drain pipe that runs within the west wall directly above the latrine. The latrine would be located on the west street wall of the room and would have drained out to the street, although no evidence of a drain in the floor remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is located in the northwest corner of room 17 immediately to the north of the cooking platform 6271.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room east/west axis. At the east of north wall there is doorway to Atrium 4 with stone threshold. The threshold preserves placing for a door. At the north end of the east wall there is a doorway to Room 8 with stone threshold. in the center of the west wall there is a doorway to Room 6. The floor is obscured by lapilli. On the south wall there is extensive preserved plaster with dark lower register, red and yellow panels above. High in wall a fragment of molded cornice survives. The door jambs in the doors in the north and east walls contain recesses for bars or locking mechanism for the door?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 to the north, Room 8 is to the east, Room 6 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: on the south wall of kitchen (12) running between the east wall and the wall dividing the room from the latrine is a largely reconstructed masonry cooking platform. current surface appears to be plain asphalt and masonry is flush to the floor with no storage below. Cooking platform is about knee high from the floor, perhaps a bit higher.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the cooking platform is east of latrine (6267) in the southwest end of kitchen (12).

DESCRIPTION: Latrine is a square area on the southwest end of room 12. identification is solely based upon Eschebach as there are no remains of a tile floor or drain. some plaster remains on the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is in the southwest end of room 12 immediately adjacent to the wall separating it from cooking platform 6266 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a fountain pool. This is basically rectangular with alternating rectangles and semi-circular recesses. The walls of the pool are painted blue. the top surface is capped with white marble. In the center of the pool is a column supporting a column base which was part of a fountain. At the S.W. end of the pool water, that is cascading down from 7 marble steps. Adjacent to the S.E. side of the stepped fountain is a deep square tank which Jashemksi suggested may hold fish while the pool was being cleaned or used to cool drinks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the central inside columned area of room 26.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular masonry base of a water feature. Fragments survive of a tiled surface. Against the extension of the basin to the north is a terracottta downipe. At the junction of the southern end of the basement and the west wall there is a hole for a drain?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6449 is to the East.

DESCRIPTION: Two masonry supports against the east wall of the room. Plaster facing survives on the northern face of the northern platform contiguous with the plaster on the east wall. Fragments of the same plaster survives at the southern face. The southern masonry support consists of a single stone block and there is no extant plaster. in front of the block, traces of a base of the support are visible on the floor. No evidence for the table survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6451 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this kitchen from Hallway 7. There is no discernible threshold and a very low entrance. There is a northwest/southeast axis for a long rectangular space. On the northeast wall we see a low cooking platform (3853). On the northwest wall we see a low lararium, deep niche with some orange paint remaining. On the northeast wall above the platform we see three large square post holes and a partly filled in lararium. No post holes are visible on the opposite wall. Further on the northeast wall to the southeast we see two large round post holes (?). On the center of the northeast wall you see a large patch of red painted plaster and the remains of a partition wall placed in front of the plaster. The southeast wall shows red plaster. The west wall has remains of a stair and the landing above. It was plastered but no color remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hallway (7) to the west

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform (3853) is a low rectangular one. The top was leveled. No front lip is present. On the northeast corner there is a large stone abutting the edge as build in protection. Above the rectangular platform are three large post holes ( perhaps for a protective awning ). Above the northeast corner is a partly filled lararium which may be used as a lamp niche. There are two storage areas under the platform. The north corner is square and the northeast storage is oval. On the northwest wall is another feature - a deep lararium niche.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: lararium (3855) to northwest

DESCRIPTION: This lararium is on the low zone of the wall. The floor is shaped - a roof tile is serving as the floor of the lararium. The curved edges face upright. The lararium is plastered with signs of coral paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (3853) to southeast

DESCRIPTION: This is a second style wall painting. A section of the painting shows a walled structure with towers at the corners. To the bottom of this section there is a pygmy carrying two vessels on a stick over his shoulders, these may contain food or water. This is in the center of the northwest wall. The lower right side of the same wall has a little pygmy holding sticks and is about to become crocodile food.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: These features are on the northwestern wall to the northwest of room 36 to the west from the doorway to this room.

DESCRIPTION:
The room's primary access is from north to south and is entered from the south from the mill room via 2 doorways. Floor is of stone and lapilli rubble. North wall is of opus incertum with evidence of significant modern reconstruction. A small bit of plaster is extant in the northeast. The color is likely red, but faded due to the elements.
The west wall is of opus incertum with a handful of tufa blocks with heavy reconstruction in modern times. Very little plaster is extant, likely first style of white and red color. The south wall is opus incertum.
The east wall is opus incertum and shows evidence of several phases of modern reconstruction. East wall contains preparation pass-thru opening to the front of the oven.
Eschebach references a stair directly west of the pass-thru opening. Evidence for this is not extant. Along the east wall is 1/3 of a mill catillus, fragment not in situ and does not match the 3 surviving mills. Along the west wall is a low incertum edifice, possibly a wall or preparation platform base. No windows are extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A differing property / structure is to north and east. The street is to the west. The mill room is to the south and the oven abuts the room to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The mill is roughly centered in the south edge of the room. The base is of modern reconstruction/repair. Material collection surface has been parged with modern concrete. Meta and catillus are extant. Catillus is damaged and missing 40%. There is no evidence of repair in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Just inside the primary (south) entrance of the room. It's axially due east of the lararium in the west wall. One of 3 extant mills.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room E/W axis. Floor obscured by earth and vegetation. The West and off the north wall, there is a doorway to the atrium with a basalt stepped threshold. At the west end of the south wall, there is a doorway to the area beneath the stairs from entrance 18. At the south end of the west wall, there is a plastered window that narrows to the room to the west and the circular hole (modern collapse?). There are traces of undecorated plaster surviving on the west wall. At the base of the west wall, there is a water basin (6451). Directly to the north of the basin, there is a terracotta downpipe embedded in the wall from the floor above. Undecorated plaster survives on the north wall, and high on the wall are placings for a floor above. Plaster survives on the east wall with a pink hue. In the center of the east wall, there is a square window looking out at the street outside. At the north end of the east wall, there is a square hole and at the south end of the east wall, there are 3 small holes of an uncertain function. At the base of the east wall, are masonry supports (6449). The south wall has extensive modern restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 7 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: feature 6367 is a very large cooking platform with the remaining of flat top surface. Facing platform to the left is a raised edge. The remainder of a raised rim. Below platform is a large arched recessed area.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opposite cooking platform 6366. It is on the south wall to the west of latrine 6368.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east/northeast - west/southwest axis. Plaster floor subsided to the center of the room. Doorway in the east corner of the southeast wall with stepped threshold to atrium. Modern lintel. Traces of plaster on all four walls. The northwest wall has two registers, white above. Large locked doorway or recess at the eastern end of the southeast wall. In front is a low plastered step facing the southeast corner of the room. Against the southeast wall is cooking platform (3020). To the east of the cooking platform there is ceramic debris including a roof tile, the lower body of an amphora and the base of a dolium. In the northwest corner of the room, divided from the remainder by an undecorated partition was/is a latrine (3019). In the north corner of the room is a large masonry podium with two plastered steps leading to wooden stairs to the floor above (no longer extant). The upper sections of all four walls are modern restoration and the roof is modern also.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 4 to the southeast

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a house. This room is a dining room. We determined this by its location adjacent to the ambulatory (11), the presence of intricate wall painting, and its large doorway. This is a rectangular room with a north-south axis and one very large doorway on its north wall. There is one small doorway on the west wall, in the north corner on the west wall leading into cubiculum 16. There is no evidence of original floor (the floor is stone and cement fill) except for one stone block on each end of the entranceway and a cement lip creating a threshold area, which has three rectangular blocks forming the lip. On either side of the entranceway there is approximately 2 feet of the north wall that is not visible to us because the entrance is gated. The other three walls are fully painted in second style fresco. The upper portion of the walls is modern with a modern roof.

BIBLIOGRAPHY ESCHEBACH PAGE 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opens into ambulatory 11; small doorway on the west wall to cubiculum 16.

DESCRIPTION: The floor contains a floor mosaic done in a couch pattern. The flooring material is dark green and is inlaid with large pieces of a variety of marble. The marble inlay includes numidian giallo antico and pavonazetto with the emphasis of the marble pieces in the center.

We have determined that in this very large house room 30 (4426) is a storeroom based upon its size and location. It is entered from a small, narrow corridor 31 to the northwest and sits directly adjacent to the second storeroom 29 (4425). Doorways are in the northwest and southwest and both are small and arched. Walls show fresco remains, with opus incertum construction behind. Floor and ceiling are modern. Kitchen 33 is located northwest of these storeroom which suggests it would be useful for food storage.

Bibliography: Esche.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Southwest of hallway 32, kitchen 33, corridor 31, and northeast of storeroom 39.

DESCRIPTION: The lararium takes up a portion of the northeast wall, and the southeast face of the archway which is incorporated into the room. there is a small alter which is in situ and joins both walls in the eastern corner. There is painting in the whole lararium and alter, which appears to be fourth style surrounded by a red border and containing approximately 5 lares and a faint water plant painting. A garland is visible at the top of the northeast painting. Plaster garlands which are in poor shape are on the northwest and southwest faces of the alter. Plaster molding surrounds the bottom of the alter. Today a tile has been inserted into the wall in an effort to protect the lararium. Situated directly above are two raised lips along the top of the alter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to feature 3886 (cooking platform) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small rectangular storage room. It is on northwest/southeast axis. One enters from the corridor (12) through a doorway on the southwest wall. This room is in very poor condition. No floors are visible. No ceiling remains. The walls are rumbling and no plaster remains. A pile of rocks from crumbling wall is in the northern corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the northeast of corridor 12 and northwest of room 14.

DESCRIPTION: This is a medium size dining room, almost square. One enters via a doorway through the western corner of the northwest wall where there is a stone threshold flanked by two pieces of white marble. Door post cuttings can be seen on all piece of the threshold. The room is in poor condition. The floor can be seen in some areas and is cocciopesto with lines of white tesserae. Plaster is preserved on all four walls, however very little painting remains. No ceiling remains. While one would have a view through the door to the atrium, there are no other doors or views.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Thisr oom is to the northwest of room 11. The door opens to the atrium (2). Space 8, the tablinium lies to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: On the far northeast corner of the room. A recessed area cupboard niche with evidence of a shelf. Damaged but with plaster and traces of yellow and red paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In northeast corner of room in north wall.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. It has been determined that this is a rectangular room used as a dining room because of its size and view over the atrium 27 to the south. The axis of the room is northeast to southwest. Extensive restoration and consolidation exists on all four walls. High in the northwest wall are two square windows with modern llintels. In the south corner, there is a doorway to atrium 27 with no visible threshold. The floor is obscured by lapilli and vegetation. Undecorated plaster is visible on all four walls.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 258-259
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 27 to the south

DESCRIPTION: In the southwest corner of the room a raised preparation platform is of masonry and stone surfaces, somewhat obscured. it is in the corner along two walls, with curved wall out into kitchen and next to doorway from room 27 and next to water feature 6406.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water feature 6406 and 6422 and 6404 to the northwest. 6401 and 6403 to the east. 6402 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This vat extends the width of room 4 along the northwest wall. it is deeper than the floor level of room 4. There is waterproofed cement painted red which extends approximately 3 feet in height on the back wall and on the southwest and southeast walls. It is preserved to a lower height and is irregular. On the northeast wall there is no evidence of paint, only cement, with a hole in the middle. The southeast wall is made of rubble and mortar and the finished opening is no longer extant. One patch of red waterproofed cement exists on the face of the protruding wall off the southwest wall and the height is consistent with the delineation of red inside the vat. It should be noted that with the proximity to the adjacent structures and with commentary from Eschebach that this may have been a latrine before it was repurposed. An indentation for a large pipe runs from the ground to the top of the surviving southwest wall. The floor of the vat is obscured with lapilli and debris. Walls are preserved to a high but indeterminate height. No covering exists above. On the exterior portion of the vat on the eastern region is a terra cotta tile which provides an indentation for feet.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to dolium holder 3758 and other preparation platform 3757.

DESCRIPTION: This dining garden lies at the southeast of the entrance. It is in very poor condition as it is filled with ash, debris and vegetation. There is no doorway today; however, on the north corner on the raised entrance is a piece of white marble with an indentation which indicates some sort of closure. A short brick northwest wall exists in the western corner. Southwest and southeast walls exist; however, the room is otherwise completely open. In antiquity there was probably a small wall on the northeast which separated the garden from kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen 4 to the northeast and atrium 3 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This feature appears to be a three part base to a working/cooking platform. The three large blocks line up along the northeastern side of the space. The eastern most block is aligned with the walls of the room; however, the other two blocks are turned at a slight angle. It is assumed that these blocks formed a table top support.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: These three blocks are in the northeast third of the southeast rectangular section of the L-shaped room.

DESCRIPTION: A masonry platform with a large arched storage below is located in the southwest corner of room 7. The platform is attached to the west and south walls and is rectangular in shape. The top shows remnants of tile surface and the arch is made of brick. The platform stands at approximately waist height in the room.

A niche in the southwest wall extends along a northwest - southeast axis and occupies approximately two thirds of the wall. In antiquity there appears to have been at least two layers of plaster and paint in bright yellow is exposed where the top layer is missing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A second cliche niche (3167) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This niche on the northeast wall is square. with no evidence of paint or plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A second couch niche (3166) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
The dining room is entered from the southwest from the portico. The dining room entry is wide but very low and unpresupposing. The floor is lapilli. The is no evidence of a worked floor. The room is almost square in plan. The walls have small areas of white plaster. There is a large window opening on the northwest wall that provides a view of the hortis area. There is no ceiling. This suggests to us this is an eating area for slaves.
In 2012, there is a pile of stones and bits of floors in the south corner, piled up the wall to about 1.5 meters high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Portico (southwest), window of an elegant dining room, southeast, and the horticultural area (northwest).

DESCRIPTION: This dolium lies to the northeast of dolium 3209 and abuts the protruding column which forms the northeast/ southeast definition of the room. The dolium is approximately 50-60 cm high it is cylindrical, the upper portion tapers and narrows into a large wide protruding lip at its height. The northwest half of the lip is missing and the dolium is filled with volcanic debris and lapilli. The construction maternal is red terracotta. The letters N.A are inscribed on the northwest face, however these may not from antiquity.
Mayeske:1971 Dolium not extant. Evidence from earlier studies Mayeske,1971 suggest that a third dolium was south of dolia 3209 and 3210 in antiquity.

We enter this tiny dining area from the northeast (a la Pliny, a diata, a dining and reclining room prevalent in larger villas). It is a small rectangular northeast/southwest oriented room. Present condition of the space shows no plaster, lapilli floor and no ceiling. Central door on northern wall permits a good view of a garden and water feature. We can see nine fluted Doric columns surrounding the garden/pool.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the northwest is a columned garden and water feature(Room 11). To the southwest a hallway and steps (no room number).

DESCRIPTION: This room is decorated on the three walls that we can see with second style fresco paintings. The paintings on all three walls are divided into 3 zones on upper, middle and Dado. The Dado is a continual black frieze with some decorations. The middle zone contains red, rectangular panels separated by white columns and blue parts. There is a center panel on the south wall with three figures. In the upper sonze the wall seems to open up so that we can see colonnaded architecture against the blue sky. There are some other decorative elements such as vases, theatrical masks and shields.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Painted walls within dining room 15.
DIGITAL_IMAGE: 10 Comments: No stick, no slate - picture through bars.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Video taken through gate. Blocked access.

DESCRIPTION: Square tile and masonry platform with plaster finish. Traces of the decoration survive on the northern face and appear to continue the scheme of the adjoining triclinium with unidentifiable red features on a blue background. A circular marble element is inserted into the plaster decoration. The plaster on the east face is contiguous with that of the adjoining couch. The plaster does not survive on the west face. The surface is modern cement. It abuts the lectus summus (southern arm) of couch 3024 to the east.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cistern (3027) to north, couch 3024 to the east, fish pond 3030 to the west, water feature (3033) to the west, cistern to the west (3031).

DESCRIPTION:
In this space we see the stone masonry remains of an open air triclinium. The imus medeus summus are apparent. I see no plaster. A triclinium slope is discernible and can still be seen. It is contiguous with the preparation platform. This space is well within the city walls.
The triclinium imus is north, the medeus is east and the sumus is south.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 3050 Preparation platform to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
On the Eschebach plan of the house a cooking platform seems to appear at the back of the room along the north west wall.

Eschebach defines the room as a kitchen.

Rectangular room north east/south west axis. Holes for 2 sets of shelves in the north west and north west walls. The room contains amphora. Presence of the shelves and amphora indicate this room was used for storage; however traces of early decoration survive. The walls have undecorated white plaster; however traces of first style decoration and architectural molding survives on the north west and south east walls. Plaster floor with geometric pattern in tessera. The room is accessed from the south west level of the floor in the adjoining atrium. In the south corner there is a rectangular plaster window or collapse into room eleven. Roof is modern.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium fifteen to the west

DESCRIPTION: Two square hole for shelves survive at the west end of the north west wall. The north east section of the wall does not preserve the placings. Two further supports for shelves are useable on the east wall.

Square holes for two sets of shelves survive in west corner in the north west wall. Contiguous with these holes are the lines of two tiers of shelving cut into the plaster decoration of the wall. Shelves ran along the north west and south east walls of the room.

Masonry cooking platform which runs the length of the north wall of kitchen room 3. Platform is about 50 cm high (see drawing) and has a lip of rounded tiles running the full length. There is a tiled surface on the southwest two-thirds of the surface of the platform. Remaining one-third to the northeast is untiled masonry with cooking supports. Cooking platform has a medium sized window above on the northwest part of the west wall opening to the street. Portions of cooking platform appear to be reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Covers full length of northwest wall of room 3. Latrine is about 20 cm to the south of the platform along the west wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is an L-shaped room with a north/south axis. The longest arm of the room consists of a tiled latrine sloping south to a drain beneath the latrine. The drain is filled with earth. In the southwest corner there is a tile recess extending from the latrine into the wall. At the base of the center of the west wall, almost at the junction of the latrine and cooking platform, there is a terracotta down pipe that drains through the wall to the street to the west. As well as tiles, the floor is covered with a fragmentary preserved layer of opus signinum. The northern half of the west wall consists of a cooking platform (6160). The floor of the east arm is obscured by lapilli. The doorway opens east to a peristyle (2). Traces of undecorated plaster survive on the north wall and plaster extends beyond the southeast corner suggesting the south wall may be a later addition. Above the platform in the west wall there is a small window to the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A peristyle (2) is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This preparation platform extends along the southwest wall of room 4 and abuts the wall which provides the boundary for vat 3759. It is approximately 3 feet high at its highest point and 3 feet deep. However, the depth at the western end decreases to approximately 2 feet as it is interrupted by the space for feature 3758. The structure is made of a mixture of stone, mostly volcanic and terra cotta on the surface. The surface is missing on the western half. On the surface of the prep platform is a nearly crescent shaped rock structure extending from the back wall to the middle of the preparation surface. An indentation which mirrors the structure abuts the southeast wall, which delineates the space between rooms 3 and 4 and rises to approximately 6 feet from the floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to dolium holder 3758 and to vat 3759 in room 4.

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that this space is a dining exedra at the southeast extremity of the houes. This is a garden exedra in alignment with the tablinum, impluvium and fauces (entrance 4). This is an almost square space behind garden (12). Built into the back part of the house, it is opus incertum with large blocks forming the front corners. The back wall at the southeast of the space has four holes cut in at about eye level, possibly lamp niches. this would have been an open air space with a good view of the garden peristyle and house. This would not have been floored or covered.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:

Esch 451
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of the garden (12)

DESCRIPTION: The couch niche is in the southwest corner of the dining room. Yellow ochre and red plaster are extant. The niche is large as compared to other dining room niches we have seen/observed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The feature is in the southwest corner of the room.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room on an east/west axis with a doorway to room 1 out the west end of the north wall with stone threshold and modern lintel. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Only the lower course of the south wall survives. The north, east, and west walls show signs of extensive restoration. On the south, north, and east walls there are fragments of plaster with no visible decoration. In the southwest corner there is a low plastered preparation platform (6297).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 to the north

DESCRIPTION: This partial catillus sits in the south corner of the shop. It was either moved or blown in here; more likely it was moved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A minimal catillus sits to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The third in a series of large square rooms opening off of space 1, dining room 5 has a larger sized doorway on the south wall. The room does not have a door sill and just has a lapilli floor. Above the door is located a small square window for light. On the east and west walls of the room are located two large holes on each which are paired across from each other and probably held a beam at ceiling height. In addition, 11 smaller holes are located on the north wall where joists for an upper story would have been positioned. The east and west walls show painted plaster remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North wall abuts the adjoining property. The east wall abuts dining room 4 and the west wall abuts dining room 6. The south wall is contiguous to space 1.

DESCRIPTION: A small room accessed next to the cooking platform in room 7, dining room 8 has been identified by a niche in the west wall. The room has plaster on its north wall and the plaster carries onto an indentation above the couch niche which could have been a lamp rest or a lararium. The room is mostly square with a lapilli floor and no windows. There is a tufa and tile door sill extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North, south and west walls abut the adjoining property. The east wall abuts kitchen 7.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed.

This structure is also known as "House of Theseus", "House of the Seven Skeletons", and "House of the American Admiral". It has been determined that this early house may have been used as a commercial property or solely as domestic. We enter this ambulatory from the atrium to the northwest. There is a marble threshold between the surrounding walls. We see a tablinum (dining) on the south side of the rectangular peristyle. We see a rectangular fish pond for the restaurant delicacies, then 12 columns. The peristyle is totally surrounded by an ambulatory on all four sides. The 12 Doric columns all have their capitals missing. There is a cistern between the first two columns of the atrium. There is a partial cistern.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Eschebach 257

ANYTHING UNUSUAL?
No

You see the rubble basin with a meta on top. There is no sign of a metal sheath. This mill is closer to the southeast wall however the animal could have still moved around it. It is in the southern corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is next to (east) of a catillus (3220) which is out of place. Mills (3227 3207) and kneading basin (3222) to the northeast. Water basin (3225) and cistern (3216) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the room from the storeroom (2) from the southeast, or from room 4 from the northeast. All walls are low and show evidence of plaster painted red and yellow. The room is basically square but runs along a northwest/ southeast axis. In the east corner of the room abutting the northeast and south walls is a low preparation platform (3224). There is a large stone which may or may have been used in the room, located parallel to the southwest wall. The floor is obscured with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: store room (2) is to south east. Room 4 is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The axis of this room is southwest/northeast. Entering the room from the southwest one goes through a wide opening almost the entire width of the space. The northwest wall may have also been open. The 2 corners of the room along the southeast wall are brick pillar construction. The corners of the northwest wall are constructed of stone. Five folio (3211 to 3215)are embedded along southeast wall and there is a square cistern (3217) on the northwest wall just south of a doorway into room 3. Along the northwest wall at the north of the doorway into room 3, there are the remains of a stairway. Remains of fresco remain on southwest wall (door pillars). Plaster and paint are also on the northwest and southeast walls. Yellow paint can be seen on both and red painted bands Re visible on the northwest walls. No flooring is visible. Preservation is overall very poor. Two rows of three square holes run horizontally high above the Delia along the southeast all. These were for shelves.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room to the southwest. Preparation to the northwest, room 5 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: The room's long axis is generally north/south. The cistern head and basin are on the west wall. The primary entrance to the room is from the south. The wall extant is almost one meter high and may have been a low wall in antiquity. There is an entrance to the oven room to the north wall. The floor is of stone rubble. Minimal plaster remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation room is to the west. Ala/corridor is to the east. Oven room is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is located in the western end of the northwest wall of dining room 5. It is above the large rectangular white panel, centered on a white field beneath a hanging ribbon. This image depicts a shallow-footed bowl, perhaps glass, with five rounded pieces of fruit visible in the bowl. The bowl has an out-turned rim. The fruit and the bowl are painted in yellow. This painting mirrors one opposite in the south end of the southeast wall, which is badly faded away.

Square masonry tank in the southwest corner of room 10. Divided into two by masonry partition wall. The walls are extensively restored. No traces of exterior finish no trace of lining survives in either tank. The bases of both tanks are obscured by lapilli. Eschebach says that these are fish tanks.

We have determined that in this very large house, close to the kitchen 33, we have two small rooms entered through a short, narrow passage 31. The room 29 is roughly square, with walls of opus incertum, with a high square window on the southwest wall. You enter the room from room 30 to the northeast through an arched doorway. Walls show remnants of plaster; floor and ceiling are modern. It was suggested by Dr. Mayeske that this room may have stayed cooler in the summer, providing storage for food for kitchen 33 to the northwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Southwest hallway 32, kitchen 33, southwest of storeroom 30.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 42 as a dining hall based on the size, location and decoration of the room. This large rectangular room is on a Northwest and Southwest axis. It can be entered through a tall doorway in the center of the Northeast wall or a smaller doorway at the South end of the Southeast wall. The doorway on the Northeast wall has a raised grey stone threshold with bronze fittings for the door posts. The threshold for the South doorway is multicolored and has white stones in cement. The floor level is slightly higher than the Northeast stone threshold. This is a cement floor with large white stone tesserae in lines forming a diamond pattern. The room is in generally poor condition with significant reconstruction. Large sections of plaster are preserved on the Southeast and Southwest walls but no fresco remains. However, large plaster moldings divide the wall in sections with molded plaster above and below an upper frieze. The plaster molding can also be seen at the Northern corner of the Northwest wall. A high ceiling is reconstructed, as is the very tall doorway into the atrium (2). The walls appear to be opus incertum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the Southwest of the atrium (2) and across the atrium from the matching door to room (4).

DESCRIPTION: Latrine is in the west/northwest corner of the room separated from the remainder of the room by an undecorated partition wall that abuts directly against the undecorated plaster in the northwest wall indicating that the partition wall is a subsequent addition. The latrine is entered from the south/southeast over a stepped threshold. The floor is plastered and slopes towards the latrine drain in the north/northwest. The drain is filled with earth and debris. U-shaped bench along the north/northwest wall is plastered over a tile surface. The U encircles the seat and drain area. The bench continues into an arched recess in the west wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (3020) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small kitchen. There is an entrance at the east corner of the northeast wall. There is another entrance at the south corner of the southwest wall to the shop. The floor is not visible. The walls are in poor states of preservation with only some plaster in a few places remaining. There is a small window in the northwest wall. Only traces remain of a cooking platform (3237) along the northeast wall. The latrine (3238) is located near the north corner of the northwest wall. Four sections of ceramic pipes are visible in the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The porticus entrance 27 is north. Shop (entrance 29) is southwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this small square dining room from the northeast through a relatively low doorway. Evidence of plaster with 3rd Style wall painting is extant on all four walls and is best preserved on the northwest and southwest walls. On the north corner of the northwest wall is a large window between two pillars which were integrated into the wall in antiquity. High on the northwest wall, west end, is a small square window which is enclosed in what appears to have been an arch in antiquity but was blocked in. These windows provided light and air circulation, the larger providing a view into the garden. The ceiling is high, with concrete beams and terracotta tiles with plaster, which appears to be reconstruction. The floor is indeterminate but may have been beaten cement. The axis is northeast/southwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 9 is to the northwest and room 7 is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: store room 16 is accessed directly from kitchen 17 to its west. the doorway is narrow. the space is rectangular on an east west axis. plaster remains on the south wall where we also see a pair of linteled windows looking onto peristyle 14. Above the second window and to its south are three holes which may have held beams for an upper story. The floor is rubble. The lower window is the larger of the two and begins at about chest height on a five foot six inch person. The second window is smaller and although higher than the top lintel of the lower window, is located diagonally t o the upper right when facing that wall inside the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the south wall abuts peristyle 14. The west wall and doorway abut kitchen 17. The north and east walls abut adjoining property.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular platform is located immediately within the doorway of room 17 along the west wall. Solid masonry construction makes up the cooking platform with no open storage spaces. The top may have been tiled at one time because there are scraps of terracotta material remaining. The platform is about knee height and about 5 feet long.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The platform is approximately 2 feet from the doorway of room 17 stretching along the west wall towards latrine 6270 at the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This feature has been identified as a basin. It is one of two flanking the doorway of the shop. This is a circular stone basin preserved to about two courses of rough opus incertum. Since we see no plaster lining, it has been concluded that this could be a stand for a dolium. This feature is located in the northern end of the northeastern wall. It is positioned in line with the wall projecting into this room as well as the room next door, shop 11.

Bibliography: Eschenbach p381
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 4500 Basin

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain 4826 is on the north west corner of the intersection of the via del Vesuvio and the via della Fortuna. It is at the south east corner of 6.14.17. The fountain is constructed of limestone slabs. There is a rounded lining at the floor / wall junction. The pilaster sits atop the centre of the north western slab and it is decorated in high relief with a portly male figure leaning on a wineskin (? This is probably Silenus and the spigot is in the place where a wineskin is usually seen) The tap or spigot is positioned under the figure's left arm. The overflow is at the centre of the south eastern slab and the drain is in the south western interior corner. There are deeply worn hand recesses on either side of the pilaster, near the centre of the north east and south west slabs and on the northern and western interior corners. The modern plumbing is not presently functioning. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.95 m. by 1.19 m. and it is 0.69 m. deep.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: on the via della Fortuna at the south east corner of 6.14.17. It is south of a street shrine and water tower 4827

DESCRIPTION: Room is entered at the North West corner of room 13. No threshold remains Floor is covered with lapilli and debris. there is no ceiling. North wall is badly damaged with traces of reconstruction and no traces of reconstruction and no traces of plaster. South west wall is badly damaged with some reconstruction and traces of plaster. A large opening appears to and may have been an opening prior to 19 A.D. North East walls are badly damaged and facing the wall to the left is the door opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is contiguous to and entered fro room 13 to the east

DESCRIPTION: The room's primary axis is north/south with two half meter diameter windows on the north wall. One of these windows/pass throughs' sill height is one meter. The other is roughly two meters. There is a high window on the south wall with a sill roughly 2.5 m. high. Room is entered at the southeast corner over a raised threshold. Ten centimeter drain tile is extant in the southwest corner of the room. Minimal plaster is extant on north, west and south walls. One meter dolium is in the room but is not in situ. Floor is stone rubble. Likely opus signinum in northwest corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 is to the south. Preparation room is to the east. Processing room is to the north. Another structure/property is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is a very large ceramic vessel. The lower wall rises almost vertically from the flat bottom. The shoulder is carinated. The rim is missing. The dolium is similar to dolium 3213 to the southwest. There are at least two large cracks but the body is complete. Some of the shoulder and all of the rim are missing. The interior is filled with lapilli and not visible. The dolium is half embedded in the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is the fourth dolium from the south corner. Dolium 3215 to the northeast. dolia 3213, 3212 and 3211 to the southwest. Cistern 3217 to the northwest

DESCRIPTION: The trough runs axially east to west and is engaged with the north and west walls. It physically abuts the street entrance opening and stands nineteen centimeters above the stone threshold. Some opus signinum is extant. There is evidence of modern reconstruction on the trough.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a water basin in the west wall of the room, just south of the trough.

DESCRIPTION: At the south west end of structure 10 we find a very long rectangular room. The room is entered up a step at a threshold of broken masonry in the south east corner of the room. We suggest that adjoining this room may have been a garden giving an attractive view from the triclinium. The floor today is rubble and weeds. No ceiling is extant. There are remains of red plaster on the north east wall as well as the possible outline of a couch niche in the west corner of the north west wall suggesting a highly decorated space for dining. the walls are opus incertum and heavily restored. This was the only identifiable space in this house. Eschebach suggests that one of the rooms on the south east side, either 4 or 5, may have been a kitchen but no evidence if it remains today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the north west of rooms 4 and 5

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room on a east/west axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Fragments of plaster survive in the northeast and northwest corners of the room. It is pink in color? The entire west side consists of a wide open doorway to the street with a partially preserved stone threshold stepping down to the street to the west. The threshold preserves placings for a door. In the north end of the east wall there is a doorway to the dining tablinum (room 2). In the center of the east wall there is a lararium (6225) directly in front of which is a cistern (6227). The southern half f the east walls opens directly to the rear of the property.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms 2, 3, and 4 are to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular vignette, blue upper, brown lower. In the center is a poorly preserved image of fish on a platter (?). Brown border along bottom edge - table?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 3056 is to the east and 3062 to southwest. Chests 3062, 3063, 3061, 3060 below.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular cooking platform in the north corner extending along the northwest wall. The platform abuts first style decoration on the northwest wall. Two large masonry supports with undecorated plaster facing support a platform with terra cotta lip formed of roof tiles and tile surface. The platform is modern restoration from 1984. Opus signinum floor beneath.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine (3025) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the dining hall from the peristyle (3054) which was located to the south. There is a marble threshold and an extremely large entrance way. This dining hall is rectangular and is oriented on a northwest-southeast axis. As reconstructed, the first barrel vault is in place over the back 3/4 of the ceiling. The south corner of the ceiling is higher and flat. There is a floor mosaic (3069) in the triclinium couch pattern. There are seven pieces of reproduction furniture using modern components. All the wood is natural and modern. There are four 3-legged tables with lions'-heads feet. The room to the northeast shows a cast of a heavy door which shows a room to the northeast. On the walls there is a black dado interspersed with yellow and red columns on the bottom. Puti and ladies are represented above the dado and there is a middle zone of a dramatic punishment of Dirce who was]forcefully led to hear death tied to a bull. The middle zone has columns interspersed with beautiful female winged figures. In all but one section, color still remains -- Green (4th style) and patches of green and red. At the northwest wall there is a very high window with a modern block, open to peristyle. At the southeast there is another rectangular window. The wall suggests it was made taller and more impressive.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 31 is to the southeast. Room 36 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Northwest of the lararium, and on the same wall, is a rectangular kitchen. The doorway is protected with Plexiglas. The floor slopes southwest. On the east wall, there is a round window and on a sloped roof is a shaped terracotta cooking vent. Room has a northwest-southeast axis. Doorway has a modern lintel and no discernible threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 is to the south. Room 19 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This very large rectangular room is entered by a southern doorway that opens to atrium 8. The room is on a north south axis and has a very large window opening on the west wall looking at peristyle 14. Painting and plaster remains on all walls to a degree. On the east wall is a protected painting of Hercules which gives the house its name. No other features are evident and the floor is lapilli and weeds. A marble threshold with indentations for door attachments is well-preserved. Close to window on west wall a brick column surrounded by masonry shows evidence of a previous room design. There is a slight straight wall indentation running from that column about two feet to the south at about six feet high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The dining room is to the south of atrium (8) and room 6 is to the southeast. Room 14 is to the west and the dining room abuts adjoining properties on the north and east.

DESCRIPTION: Floor is rubble and dirt. Vaulted ceiling. All walls are damaged, reconstructed, with traces of white plaster. Entrance is on the south.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous entrance to storeroom H is on the west wall to the side.
