DESCRIPTION: Enter from corridor with entrance on east wall. Enter from store room G on south wall. Floor is rubble and dirt. Vaulted ceiling. All walls, north, south, east and west are damaged, with traces of white plaster. Considerable debris present at south wall entrance.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Entrance from store room G on south.

DESCRIPTION: Entered from underground corridor. Entrance is on the east wall. A second door leads to another subterranean storage area (H) with a door on the north wall. This is a subterranean storage area with a pounded dirt floor, arched ceiling. The wall to the east is damaged badly, maybe some plaster. There is a large rectangular hole in the wall near the door and near corner with south wall. South wall is badly damaged, with a small rectangular opening at top center of vaulted ceiling and a round small hole at west side. Also a small opening exists in the ceiling. West wall is badly damaged. Trace of plaster. North wall has door into room H. Badly damaged, reconstructed, with a small rectangular hole at top.

This is a small rectangular storage room, in the eastern corner of the house. This is on a northeast/southwest axis. One enters from the western corner through a door on the northwest wall. The room is in poor condition. No floor is visible. The ceiling does not remain however 7 joist holes remain along the top of the southeast wall. There is rough rough plaster on all the walls. No painted surface exists. All walls are of greying colour.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is in the eastern most corner of the house. Room 13 is to the northwest. Room 15 is to the southwest and corridor 12 is to the northwest of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, north-south axis, opening south to peristyle (32). Southern doorway has marble threshold and placing for doors. At the south end of east wall there is a doorway with step threshold and modern lintel. Mosaic floor survives throughout, separated into two halves by border of geometric swastika in black and white tesserae. The southern half consists of opus signinum with pattern of flowers in black and white tesserae and white border. The northern half of the room is opus signinum with flowers in black and white tesserae, black border. In the center forming a rosette around which the couches were arranged is a square pattern of alternating black and white tesserae enclosed by borders of white and black. Extensive plaster survives on north, east and west walls, decorated in first style with alternating yellow, white and red panels. At the top of the walls in the north half of the room there are traces of plaster molded cornices and on the north wall plaster molded vaulted ceiling. The ceiling is modern restoration. At the north end of the east wall there is a rectangular window, modern lintel, looking into bedroom 35. This may be modern?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Room 34 is to the east.
Peristyle 32 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Facing the southwest wall to the right is a latrine. Few remains. Masonry projection which may have held a seat. Plaster on lower level and ground slopes downward to a drain below the wall. It is adjacent to the water feature and cooking platform on northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Water feature 6406 and preparation platform 6405 to southeast.
Cooking platform 6402 to northwest. 6401 and 6403 to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. On the west walkway we pass a large lararium with a large opening and an aedicula top, turn right. Then immediately left a a hallway that is mud, vegetation and stone. Note on the floor plan how the kitchen is not aligned with the main house. At the end we find a rectangular kitchen with a floor of vegetation and stones. At the south wall is a door which leads to a good sized room on the next street.
The kitchen is predominantly filled with a doubly large cooking platform. Two-thirds of this platform are two recessed storage areas of half-moon shape. Unfortunately, the platform surface looks like the floor. The platform is continued on the north side with a square platform addition. All of the walls have been resurfaced and built up. At this time they do not show any windows . A wall column divides the platform from the toilet and the toilet is also next to the door to the shop.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Next to latrine 4554

DESCRIPTION: Masonry and tile base forms a semi-circular water basin. The base of the basin is obscured by lapilli and debris but the upper course is visible revealing plaster lining that abuts directly on to the plaster of the adjoining east wall. Latrine 6387 abuts directly against the tile and masonry wall of the feature enclosing the plastered basin. Not enough of the exterior face of the wall survives to determine whether it was plastered or finished in any other way.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 6387 to the south, cooking platform 6386 to the west

DESCRIPTION: The platform abuts the north and east walls and is heavily reconstructed in modern times. The platform can be viewed directly from the street entrance. Wall plaster on the east wall predates the platform. Plaster runs contiguously between the wall and the platform. This condition is not evident on the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The platform is the only platform in the room; however Eschebach mentions, but does not locate, a latrine.

DESCRIPTION: The latrine is located in the kitchen, which is entered from the portico from the northeast. We note again the temperature in the barrel vaulted kitchen is cool. We turn to the southeast and we see a large area with a wall that is a bit higher than the cooking platform (approximately 1.30 meters). The latrine is bordered with a high northwest/southeast wall separating it from the cooking platform area. There is a ceiling height wall on the northeast side of the latrine that separates it from the storage area. The latrine floor is mud. On the northeast wall are two widely spaced struts that would have supported a wooden seat, that would have seated more than one individual. There is a skylight on the southeast wall opening which has been blocked in antiquity. The latrine is are is large and extends to the middle of the barrel vault in the room. The ceiling above the toilet area features an oval ceramic pipe abutting onto the northeast wall. The pipe in the ceiling aligns with the end of the toilet struts and was probably used for collecting water.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform area #20 - 3157 to the southwest storage room #3165 to the northeast.
Contiguous to rooms 14 to the southeast, room 12 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Raised preparation platform is approximately one meter high and approximately 2m long and runs along the northwest / southeast axis. The long arm about the northeast wall of room 9 and the short arm which runs along a northeast/ southwest axis about the northwest wall for approximately 50 cm. The counter is constructed of volcanic rock.

In the House of Obeillius Firmus, in the room identified as a kitchen (33), there is a pozzolana-coated round basin built into a masonry structure centered in the Southwest wall. The basin is partially destroyed by volcanic activity but three quarters of its radius remains. It is deep and still filled with other material, so actual depth cannot be determined. The Northeast side of the basin is attached to cooking platform 4422. The basin has a wide top, also of pozzolana, cement/plaster and it appears to have had masonry exteriors.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Escherbach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
To the Northwest of latrine 4420, and the Southeast of cooking platform 4422 and to the South-Southwest of latrine 4423.
Adjacent to corridor/passage 32 Southeast of Atrium 39

DESCRIPTION: Entrance to Dining room is at the south end of northeast wall. Dining room identification is based on location in house and size of room. Walls are stone with masonry door jams. Traces of stucco remain, particularly on southeast wall. Two layers of plaster remain at northeast wall. Floor is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room #4, which is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Garden area to the northeast of the insula. The perimeter of the garden has not been identified. Wall to the southeast. Eschebach says there is a cistern, dolium and open air triclinium under a vine pergola. Used for vine cultivation with olive and fig trees in the corners. Drain into unexcavated house to the southwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Relationship unknown - not excavated.

DESCRIPTION: Preparation platform is located to the west of the summus couch of the triclinium. As extant the couch has pretty much lost its form although in antiquity it was probably rectangular or square. Because of the deteriorated condition of the platform it is not possible to determine if it had been plastered and painted.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium (3049) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Standing in a central portion of the northwest wall of the space we see the top three rows of stone forming an outdoor masonry triclinium. There are two layers of stone forming a circular large inner table. The triclinium shows the usual slope. At the feet of the right couch arm there is evidence of a stone platform, square in shape it could have been used for food service or a space for eating for children or freed men. There is a possibility that future excavation would show further depth in the triclinium and the platform. In 2010 the outdoor triclinium was located in a cool tree studded area.
This dolium was located to the northwest of the other dolium, 2777. As extant the cavity is present but no remains of the dolium itself.
The missing dolium lay to the southeast of dolium 2776. Today its location is identified only through a depression in the ground.

We enter room 5 from the atrium which is to the southwest through an open space with a large modern lintel. There are 3 walls ( northwest, northeast, southeast). Each have remnants of plaster and some sort of border which is indiscernible today. High on the southeast wall is a window type opening to room 6. The floor is obscured with lapili and there is no ceiling extant. There appears to be a possible niche along the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 (atrium) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We are entering from a nice sidewalk. On the wall on the east there is a sign that says Taverna Q. Sallustius Inventus. We step up to an entrance to a large food shop. We look straight ahead to a north wall with a large opening to a preparation room (4) and another opening to a hall (2). The east wall is rubble, with a pipe on the southeast corner. There are little patches of plaster on this wall. There is a rectangular podium-shaped platform. It is made of concrete and roof times, with an unknown usage. On the west wall we see a vat (3818) with remains of opus signinum and connected to it is a long rectangular preparation platform (3817). The floor is pounded mud and lapilli. There is no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to a hallway (2) and a preparation room (4) and to a street.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small square preparation room. One steps up from the sales room (1) and enters this room through a doorway on the south half of the southeast wall. This room is in very poor condition. No flooring is visible. No ceiling remains. All walls preserve some plaster but no longer reveal any paint. Along the northwest wall two square cuttings pierce this wall to room 9 in bakery of Papirius Sabinus. A vertical cutting approximately 4 feet long is seen in the southwest wall near the south corner. The eastern door jamb has three pairs of deep drilled holes. According to Kevin Hill, the northwest wall may be mostly modern reconsruction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of room 1 and to the northeast of room 2. This room is southeast of room 9 from bakery of Papirius Sabinus.

DESCRIPTION: Small, quasi-rectangular vat is low and abuts the southeast and southwest walls of the room for approximately 3 feet on the southwest and to the doorway on the southeast. The northwest end is slightly irregular and angles toward the back of the room. Hydraulic plaster and opus signinum coat and form the vat. At its highest point it is approximately 2 feet up from the ground. Much volcanic debris fills the bottom of the vat.

At the west end of cooking platform 6501, cut into the south masonry wall is a semicircular niche for a latrine. Niche shows remnants of plaster and slots for a top lintel, as well as lower down for seat placement. Ground surface is obscured by soil and debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In room 2 (6503) west of cooking platform 6501.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room with an eat/west axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli. A doorway with modern lintel and fragments of a plastered threshold in the center of the west wall leads to garden 5. on the north face of the door jamb, there is undecorated plaster. At the west end of the north wall there is a doorway with modern lintel to latrine 4. At the east end of the north wall, a small window opens into the latrine. High in the center of the east wall there is a window with modern lintel that opens to the street. Traces of undecorated plaster are on the north, south, and west walls. There is a low masonry cooking platform, feature 6200, in the center of the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 4 is to the north. Room 5 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east/west axis. Floor obscured by lapilli. North wall survives with evidence of restoration but no visible plaster. Against the north wall extending from the west wall is cooking platform 6386. In the north west corner adjoining the platform and on the west wall are traces of plaster with a red or pink colour. The west and south walls survive only in the lower courses. In the centre of the south wall is a doorway to 6 with a stoned threshold and placing for a door. The southeast corner of the room is obscured by debris partially covering latrine 6387 and water feature 6388 in the centre of the east wall. At the north end of the east wall is a doorway to room 8 with a stone threshold and a placing for a door.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 to the east, room 6 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Masonry support for the face of a masonry triclinium. Only the lower course survives with no indication of the couch surface. The external face of the northern arm preserves traces of red plaster. Jashemski says that this triclinium came from an earlier phase prior to the earthquake of 62 CE after which debris filling the room was cleared and the remainder of the area turned over to horticultural use.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest corner of horticultural space

DESCRIPTION: In the fourth feature on the lower level, the ground is black in an arched rectangle. There is a serving tray with a brown casserole (?) surmounted by two pieces of food (?) and a pomegranate in the foreground.

Rectangular room north-south axis. Floor is obscured by lapilli. In the center of the west wall. There is a wide doorway with fragmentary stoned threshold opening to the street outside. At the southern end of the west wall there is a smaller doorway with stepped threshold which Eschebach says led to stairs. In the southern half of the east wall there is a doorway to to store room 3. At the northern end of the east wall there is a stone stop threshold to storeroom and there are 3 pierce-through holes along the east wall, possibly for a shelf. 2. High in the center of the east wall there is a window open to storeroom 2 . In center of north wall, there's doorway to mill/oven room 4.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 to North, 2 and 3 to the East.

DESCRIPTION:
This is an almost square room. The doorway is at the north end of the west wall and has a stone threshold with a placing for doors, opening inwards. The southern half of the west wall has a large, low window looking west to room 1.
The floor is obscured by lapilli. Fragments of plaster are found in the northeast, southwest, center of the north wall and high in the south wall. No extant decorations. Each wall shows signs of restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The mill is in the northeast corner of the room. The platform/base is reconstructed (modern). The meta is extant as is the catillus. There is no cracking or signs of repair in antiquity. The mill is one of four in the room and is closest to the easterly entrance.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill is one of four and is in the northeast corner of the room.

DESCRIPTION: The counter is basically 'L' shaped with a slight intrusion of a square edge into the west corner. The short arm of the counter,which runs parallel to the street along a northwest/southeast axis , is approximately 2m long. It provides a defining barrier for the south portion of the southeast side of the room. The longer arm which runs along the northwest / southeast axis is approximately 3m long and delineating the division of space in the middle of the room. The counter appears to have been reconstructed after 62 AD and the surface consists of black, gray, white and travertine pieces of marble and cement. The counter is approximately 1m high on the southeast wall. Abutting the counter is a pile of rubble, however a small fragment of counter plaster, painted red, appears at the bottom It cannot be discerned whether this rubble was a portion of the counter or not. The southwest face of the counter consists of rich colors (white, red, green and gray) where the marble is still present. There are 4 white marble slabs along the bottom. There are approximately 10 imprints for missing pieces. The face of the northwest outer wall of the counter contains only foundation material. Plaster appears on both arms of the interior side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dolia (negative feature 3220, 3209 and 3210 are to the south east.

DESCRIPTION:
This complete mill is in a good location with the exception that the kneading basin has been moved into the eastern corner. It sits along the southeast wall.
The basin does not show a sheath. The meta needs some repair. The catillus is missing two thirds of its top walls.
The height of he meta is taller than normal, specifically the distance between the bottom edge of the catillus and the top edge of the basin which is approximately 0.5m.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: kneading basin (3222) is to the east. A meta and basin (3227), catillus (3226) and meta and basin (3206) are to the southwest. Water basin (3225) and cistern (3216) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Square room with doorway south to corridor 5. No defined threshold. Modern lintel. To the east corner of the southeast wall adjoining the doorway is a small square window looking out to Room 10. Modern lintel. Traces of undecorated plaster survive on either side of the doorway. Plaster floor preserved in places. Southeast wall preserves extensive traces of lararium painting (3013). Upper half of the walls is modern restoration with modern roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms 5 and 10 to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: High on the northwest wall in the tympanium formed by the vaulting of the ceiling is a painting. In the center is a rectangular box on top of which sits a bronze tray, oval in shape. On the tray appears to be various food items.; on the right perhaps, a large fig. On the left my be a glass cup. The items in the center cannot be distinguished.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: floor below to southeast painting # 3077 to northeast.

DESCRIPTION: On northeast wall in the upper register is an Eros appearing to walk from left to right, balancing a second Eros on the right, the Erotes flanking a herm with a tragic mask. The Eros on the left carries a basket containing fruit.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: floor below southwest painting 3058 to northwest

DESCRIPTION: along northeast wall of portico was a storage chest, no longer existent. Its shape and size are unknown.
An upright storage chest, rectangular in shape, placed against the northeast wall. Present today is its plaster cast. It appears to have been made of wood.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Chests 3061, 3062, 3063 to northwest. paintings 3055, 3055, 3056 above on wall.

DESCRIPTION: An upright storage chest, rectangular in shape, placed on northwest-southeast axis against the northeast wall. Present today is a plaster cast. It appears to have been made of wood with a metal band around the center.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: chest 3062, 3061, 3060 tot eh southeast painting 3057, 3056, 3055 above.

DESCRIPTION: Vignette of two red fish to the north. 3 further fish are shown hanging in the background. The two red fish appear to be mullet, the 3 hanging fish are silver in color (perch?). The identification of all fish is uncertain.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: painting (3057) to the north, painting (3055) to the south, 3061, 3063, 3062, 3060 to the west (below)

DESCRIPTION: The masonry cooking platform lies in the west corner of the room abutting the northwest and southwest walls. The platform is in a southwest/northeast axis. The platform has two superimposed arched processes. The lower and taller one was probably for storage, the upper for cooking. Both recesses were stuccoed, but probably unpainted. The floor of the cooking platform was also stuccoed. Above the cooking platform had been inserted three tiles creating a slight lip on top of which is further masonry construction. The exterior of the cooking platform on its northeast/southeast sides were stuccoed but probably not painted. The entire cooking platform seems to have been inserted into the west corner after the garden painting had been done since the painting seems to continue behind the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium to the north, water feature to the northeast and southeast

DESCRIPTION: This small room lies along a northwest/ southeast axis, and lies under a steep flight of stairs to the southwest. The room is vaulted and is approximately three meters high and is plastered and evidence suggests some red paint. In the northwest wall on the west corner is a skewed rhomboidal shaped opening which is plastered and leads into the adjoining room which is now used for modern lawn or maintenance equipment. Above the window is a hole which corresponds to one in the north corner of this same wall (northwest) and underneath this level are other small holes which indicate perhaps the location of small nails or hooks. On the southwest and northeast walls are similar random holes both in the plaster and in the surface from which plaster has been vacated. The floor is covered in dirt and debris. The doorway which fills the southeast wall is not extremely high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 is to the south east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a low masonry platform. It has a poorly preserved cement surface with tile fragments. It stands against the north wall of the room with a window high on the east wall opening to the street to provide ventilation.

This is a large square room with a wide doorway to atrium 4 at the south. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Plaster survives extensively on the north and east walls and in places on the south and west walls. Fourth style painting with red and yellow panels is seen with a white upper register with architectural motifs. Molded plaster cornices survive on the north wall and in traces on the east wall. Above the cornice on the north wall is the placing for a floor joist. High on the east wall ate placings for 8 floor joists. Above these on the north and east walls are plaster from the floor above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 4 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular solid masonry platform with modern cement surface in the northeast corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: the latrine (6177 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The drain is in the southeast corner, but is filled with debris. Above the drain in the east wall. there is the placing for the seat. In the southeast corner a downpipe drains into the drain beneath.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (6176) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The peristyle garden is located to the north of atrium 8 and tablinum 13. This rectangular garden is on the east/west axis and contains a built lararium on the northeast corner. On the south and west sides of the garden are the remains of 3 columns with a low wall between. On the north wall is a pair of windows opening to storeroom 16. On the east wall is a large window opening to dining room 7, and although no longer present, a low wall in the tablinum 13 probably also contained a window. The walls in the lararium were plastered.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north is an adjacent property in addition to storeroom 16. Room 15 wraps the room on the south and west, and on the south is also located tablinum 13. Dining room 7 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This mill is in the southeast corner of the room. The stone base is of modern reconstruction with a concrete parged collection surface. Meta and catillus are intact. Top lip of (W) catillus is fractured and missing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill is south and east of the oven, kneading basin and masonry supports.

DESCRIPTION: One of 3 mills in the room. Base is of modern reconstruction/repair with a concrete parged material collection surface. Meta and catillus are extant. The top of the catillus is damaged. There is no evidence of repair in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: One of 3 mills and is closest to the oven face. Directly south of the preparation platform 6242.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room with a north/south axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Along the east wall are stairs to the floor above, beneath which is an arched cupboard space. The room opens to room 1 to the north with a low wall and the square platform of water feature 6295 at the junction of the two rooms. Undecorated plaster survives on the south wall. On the west wall there is white plaster with dark lower register with lararium 6298.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square masonry platform with modern cement pointing. There is a terracotta tile and brick surface into which is inserted a circular basin. The basin has modern cement restoration and no visible lining. Eschebach identifies this as a kettle. The base of the basin is obscured by debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 6298 and niche 6296 are to the south.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room to the northwest of the entryway opens off the garden area which is to the northeast. Room access is southeast corner of the east wall. In the northwest corner of the room is a plastered niche in the lower part of the wall. Niche is fully plastered but other walls show only slight evidence of plastering. There is a dirt floor and no windows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Entryway 1 to the southwest. Vicolo de Modesto to the west. Adjoining property 6.5.6 to the northeast. Room 4 and garden 2 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The feature is a large rectangular plastered water cistern. The plaster survives throughout and it is deep. In the center of the base of the south wall a square hole extends south. The cistern is not accessible as the basin is full of water. It has a stepped lip. Two terracotta lined channels run at the top of the south wall. The southeast channel drains to the cistern. To the west there is a rectangular feature of uncertain use. The cistern will originally have had to be covered as it blocks access to room 7 to the north
Mill is on the west side of the room. The platform and base are not extant. Catillus remains but it is not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: One of two mills in the room

DESCRIPTION: Circular volcanic stone machine with the base of the metal blade survives in the bottom. Four holes remain in the face of the face of the basin.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven 6191 to the north.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information for this feature sheet.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room with a north - south axis with doorway to the north end of the east wall. The north wall only survives in its lower course. The floor is obscured by lapilli and unexcavated volcanic debris. Plaster survives on the west wall with possible yellow color extending up the wall into the lower courses of a vaulted ceiling. Extensive plaster in south wall containing two circular plaster windows opening to room 6.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 7 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is on a north/south axis. At the west end of the north wall there is a doorway opening north to the atrium with a stone stepped threshold. The threshold preserves placing for a door. The floor is obscured by lapilli. There is undecorated plaster on the south wall and on the southwest corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The atrium is to the north. Room 8 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This water tower is on the Via del Vesuvio northwest of the intersection with the Via della Fortuna. This water tower is made of brick masonry. It has pipe recesses only on the northwestern and southeastern faces. It has extremely heavy calcium carbonate deposition in the southeastern pipe recess and on the southeast face, the entire northeastern face, and the southern half of the southwestern face. There is little calcium carbonate deposition in the northwestern pipe recess.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This water tower is between 6.14.17. It is northwest of the street shrine and public fountain 4826.

DESCRIPTION: House CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. This feature is a latrine. It is located at the north corner of the kitchen 19. There is a low partition which separates the latrine from the cooking platform to the southeast. No flooring is visible. The remains of a low L-shaped platform remains along the northeast and the northwest walls. The east portion of the northeast wall preserves yellow and red fresco above the low platform. The northeast wall has a rectangular window. The northeast wall has cuttings in the north corner for support of the seat. A drain is visible along the northwest wall. The walls are poorly preserved with only minor traces of stucco. The north wall is ashlar masonry. There is also one ashlar block on the northwest wall. The wall above the ashlar block is poorly preserved. The low L-shaped platform remains along the northwest and northeast wall preserves a section of its plastered surface on its southeast side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: northwest of the cooking platform 3139

DESCRIPTION: There is a square plastered vat inserted into the floor in the east corner of the room. The vat is filled with lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bench (3098) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The cooking platform takes up about 90% of the room. The platform abuts the southeast, northeast and southwest walls. The surface was made up of terracotta tiles. The northwest edge of the surface has a large lip across the entire width from northeast to southwest. In the south corner there is today a large hole through which one is able to see that the platform is not solid. The space underneath the platform is empty.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (11) to the north.

DESCRIPTION: On the western end of the northwest wall is a yellow panel with a winged figure. Above is a window scene with a female figure feeding a peacock. What is left of the next section shows a continuation of the architecture outside the window. A mask motif is at the top of the column and three dead ducks are suspended below.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Niche (3190) is below. A painting is to the northwest. Niche (3193) is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: On the northeast wall in the center of a large panel formed by two thin decorated columns, is a rectangular painting on a northwest to southeast axis showing a scene from a drinking party (Greek symposium?). Four individuals, two men and two women, lie on a couch. A servant stands to the upper right. In front of the couch is a tripod table with small drinking cups. On the left a man reclines holding in his left hand a drinking cup; his right hand reaches out to get a rhyton offered by the seminude female. To their left is a second couple, the male of which has already passed out from drinking.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Floor below; painting (3104) to the northwest; painting (3103) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: In the east corner, we see a fairly square pile of rubble. This is undoubtedly the remnants of a cooking platform. The window in the southwest wall supports this conclusion.
From atrium walk east into room past the lararium to the south.

This is a small dining room. This room is on a NE/SW axis. The room is in fair condition. The floor and walls are preserved. The ceiling is reconstructed. There is an entrance to the room in the northern corner of the NE wall. This doorway opens to the atrium and has a white marble threshold. Another door is located in the western corner of the NW wall. This door opens to the peristyle. A large window is located on the Northern half of the NW wall. The floor is a black overall pattern with a double band of white around the perimeter. In more patterning on this floor, it's not visible due to the accumulation of heavy dirt. The walls are in fair condition with a great deal of painting intact. These walls appear to be third style. There is a red dad with patterns containing figures and mythological creatures. The central zone is predominantly pale blue with fanciful architectural designs and garlands and putti. The upper zone reveals delicate architecture and birds, putti and a central goddess. The Southwest wall has a small window, located near the center; just below the ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 4 is situated to the East. Peristyle 26 is situated to the North.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room with an east west axis, arched ceiling. The floor is obscured throughout by earth and debris. The doorway in the west wall has a modern lintel. the doorway at the west end of the south wall has a has a modern lintel. The thresholds of both doors are obscured . Situated on the west wall is an opening, a collapse at the top of the roof? High in the east wall at the junction with the ceiling is an opening to the street level. This area is weak and close to collapse. In the center of the east wall there is a low plastered partition wall extending into the center of the room. Cooking platform 6373 is in the northwest corner. Lararium 6376 is in the northeast corner. There are remnants of plaster on the south wall with no visible decorations. Any sign of a latrine is obscured by debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: E is to the west and B is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: A long rectangular cooking platform, masonry, with no visible storage, extends along the north wall from the west wall. The western half of the top is obscured by earth and debris. The eastern half has collapsed, revealing fragments of a plastered or tile lip and surface. The eastern face is plastered, with no visible decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 6374 is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Square masonry altar with a plastered face. There is a plastered lip surface above, abutting the north wall of the room Above the altar on the wall is a poorly preserved lararium painting on a white background. From the west there is a partially preserved painting of a lare with cornucopia and with a yellow tunic. Legs of a smaller figure, a camillus; the arm, head and shoulders of a figure in a toga performing a sacrifice on an altar with indeterminate painted figures. The face and arms of a lare facing the scene, with a cornucopia forming a pair with the lare to the west. Above the scene are green garlands hanging above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Platform 6373 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Room 29 lies Northeast of the peristyle. It is a large rectangular room on a Northeast-Southwest axis. A white marble threshold borders the black and white tesserae, which makes up the mosaic floor. Just beyond the marble is the edge of the floor, which has a pattern of black and white lines enveloping white figures in groups of 4, which resemble arched white figures forming black arches in between. Approximately two feet between the geometric pattern of hexagonal mosaic, seen in black detail. Is is bordered by white tessearae on 4 sides. Plaster painted in second style occurs on all 4 walls, with most being on the Southeast and Northeast walls. On the lower register, in the Northern corner is a black panel which features a cloaked male, resting on the figure of a bull. This pattern of black is contiguous with the Northeast wall, which depicts other figures, 2 of which are reclining and one central figure, who is squatting and appears to be holding the doorway above him. At the Eastern corner of the Southeast wall, a figure, possibly representing Venus, appears to be resting on a dolphin. The only other shape that can be clearly seen onthe lower register is a large vessel. There is a slight outline of a figure onthe South end of the Southeast wall, however no details remain. On each of the panels that containlefelike figures, there are small framed flowers on the left and right sides. The upper register was painted red in panels, which were framed by painted columns extending through both registers. The center panel, at the Northeast wall appears to have had a square or rectangular painting, the outline of which is visible. The other fine panels of red have blue backgrounds and remnants winged figures. On the Northeast wall, above the left and right panels are white squares. The ceiling is modern, as is the high lintel.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To room 30, situated to the North and room 2840, to the Southeast. Southwest peristyle # 26.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room on north/south axis. Entered over stone threshold from atrium 7. No ceiling. Overgrown floor. Plaster remains on all 4 walls. On the north wall there is a white lower register with a red band across the top. The north west wall appears to be divided into two panels, with traces of red, yellow an blue paint. But style of decoration is impossible to tell. The north/east and east walls appear to have the same style of decoration, with the lowest register in red and the upper wall with no real defined color remaining on the plaster. The South wall continues the decoration with traces of bright red and white paint remaining over darker red in the lower register. The west wall shows evidence of more elaborate painting on the lower register which looks to be center frieze bordered by red lines that look like ribbons over black paint. A central panel bordered by architectural detail appears above, but designs is indistinguishable. I see no windows, only a large doorway for a view. Three gaps in the masonry that resemble post roles may have been original on the east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opening to north and off atrium 7

DESCRIPTION:
(Replaces sheet 21)
The lararium is rectangular and recessed into the middle of the north wall and adjacent to the north arm of the counter. The lararium is covered in white plaster with green bands in the corners. However, the rest of the wall painting is not discernible. The sill and the top of the lararium are not present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The lararium is contiguous to the counter in room 1 and the low opening/passthrough between rooms 1 and 4.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room on a NE/SW axis with main shop entry to the west and a large opening to the fauces on the south as well as a large opening onto the atrium to the east and a small opening onto the dining other to the east. Within the room is a large U-shaped counter with a small hearth; 6 dolia have been inserted into the counter. A preparation platform is situated in the middle of the room behind the counter. Both counter and preparation platform are covered in marble and have been reconstructed. The property was bombed in WW II and has been heavily reconstructed. No wall plaster survives. The west entry to the counter room contains a marble threshold (3 segments). The original floor is not visible and the ceiling has been reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 is contiguous to Room 4 (atrium) and room 5 (dining other) to the east. It is also contiguous to Room 1 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this dining garden from rooms 7 at the end of this commercial structure. The three walls of the garden are high and show evidence of being heavily reconstructed. The southwest wall has a large window to a tablinum which once allowed the tablinum to look at the garden. On the southeast wall we see signs of painted plastered and an opening to a latrine. Half of the northeast wall is taken by a dining triclinium. The dining area has a column that is plastered and introduces a wall that separates he dining room area from the garden. On the northwest wall we see holes that once could have held timber wood. There is a very large cement root of a big tree close to the northwest wall. there are 5 small trees lined up at the center of the garden and two trees to the south of the garden.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 7 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: When excavated forty-three amphorae of various types were found placed on and around the triclinium including dr.1 wine amphora, golbular oil amphora (will check type) as well a third broad-mouthed form with pointed handles (will check type) . Large quantities of amphorae are stored in the area of the atrium and tablinum of the property.

The latrine is inserted in kitchen (7) opposite the entrance into the room to the northwest, which today is blocked by a low rubble pile. In this very badly preserved space, the floor is covered with thick soil and stones. The walls show significant deterioration to the northeast and southeast.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the room from the southeast from the atrium. The room is along a northeast-southwest axis. On the northeast wall, east corner there is a large lararium with a recess above it. Original plaster exists on all 4 walls with traces of red, white and yellow paint. On the northwest and southwest wall approximately 2.5 meters high are traces of plaster molding. The walls are high, the height is indeterminate, but we see evidence of painting on the second story west corner with blue and gold paint. The floor is obscured with lapilli. The width of the entrance doors seems to have been narrowed in antiquity. There are seven beam holes on the northwest wall above the molding and plaster, and just over the door way on opposite sides of northeast and southwest walls are large holes possibly for floor joists.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is contiguous to the atrium (4) to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: On the far east end of the northeast wall is an arched deep recess to the floor. The back of the lararium has no discernible plaster. There is decoration on the top of the arch and curved to 1/3 to 1/2 down the east side. The decoration is third - fourth style, white plaster with yellow/green balls, tendrils, leaves. At the top of the arch is a square surrounding aqua frame. Within the frame is a red indiscernible scene/face. Three fourths of the way down on the east side are signs of a shelf support. Below this are signs of roughening of the plaster in preparation for repainting. There is modern graffiti on the upper east wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest of Room 4
VIDEO_COMMENTS: 012/013 indicated to be deleted on feature sheet.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room east-northeast/west-southwest. Opus signinum floor. Modern roof. Large areas of plaster survive on the southwest and southeast walls with red panels. Possible black panels, Xenia(?). Doorway in the northwest corner, no threshold, modern lintel, to Room 7. In the center of the northwest wall is a doorway to peristyle 5. Modern lintel. Preserved threshold with placings for doors. Red plaster survives on the internal face of the doorjamb. Modern roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 5 to the west. Room 7 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The design of the mosaic floor is simple, made up of beaten cement with fine terracotta fragments. A design is formed by small pieces of white marble. The entrance is a crosshatched band going in a northwest direction. The next section is wide, made up of marble fragments in columns. After a small band lacking any marble fragments, followed immediately by a band of the same width with marble fragments in squares with different designs. The rest of the floor to northwest wall has in the center a large square design made up of many squares of geometric design. This large square serves as the focal point, around which the dining couches would be arranged. Surrounding the central square, lined up in rows, are a series of 4 marble fragments, each forming flowers. The floor, where the benches would be placed, seems to sloped back towards the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
FN 3077, wall painting, to northeast
FN 3058, wall painting, to northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Vignette of red grapes spilling from an overturned basket. A bird (owl?) is shown flying above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Paintings (3056, 3057 ) to the north.
Chests (3060, 3061q, 3062, 3063) to the west, below.

DESCRIPTION: On the northeast wall, the semicircular lararium shows at least two plaster layers. the only indication of art work is at rear top. One phallus centrally positioned, tip of phallus on top layer. It is about halfway up the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: #3760 is to the south (directly underneath 3759).

DESCRIPTION: A wide terracotta shallow kneading basin with iron ties indicating repair in antiquity. The basin is embedded into a masonry plaster support. It is contiguous with terracotta basin 6412 to the south and abuts 6414 to the north.

We enter kitchen 9, at the rear of the house. We have a narrow low doorway to the kitchen. The floor is lapilli. There is one tiny patch of plaster in this L shaped kitchen. The ceiling posts are low, under 2 meters, in the long arm of the L and they are found on both long walls. The short arm of the L or the base of the L with the cooking platform seems to be unroofed. There is a good sized cooking platform in the Southwest with an arch for firewood or charcoal or pots and pans. There is some evidence for a latrine in the Southwest corner of the short arm of the L, at the end of the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (11), and a dining room (8), overlooking a garden (7), situated on the East wall.

DESCRIPTION:
This small rectangular room lies along a Northwest, Southeast axis. It is in complete disrepair. We enter from the Southern corridor (11) through a low doorway. To the Southeast in the corner, abutting the East and South walls, is a low piece of masonry. It appears that this room had been remodeled in antiquity due to the filling of a large space which was then surfaced with plaster and painted red and white with panels which were completed before the masonry was placed in the corner. There are traces of another column; celadon, and yellow remain within the filled space reaching to the peristyle centered in the East wall. There, is a small window whose bottom lip is broken. The walls are preserved to a first storey height and no ceiling is extant. The floor is obscured with lapilli and vegetation.
There is a hole on the North wall for an unknown purpose and this wall seems to have been plastered. 3 or 4 times in antiquity. he is about 1.5 meters above the floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor (11) is to the South; peristyle (7) is to the East

DESCRIPTION: Open to the west from space 1, room 7 is defined as a kitchen based upon a large masonry cooking platform in its southwest corner. Two identified dining rooms open off this space on the north and west. The east of the room is completely open to space 1. There do not appear to be any windows in the room. A couple holes at eye level on the south wall may have held shelf supports. No plaster remains on what appear to be heavily reconstructed walls. The floor is lapilli. The kitchen is divided from space 1 by pillars of opus vittatum and opus catercium. The rest of the walls are opus incertum. Eschebach recorded a lararium in this area but it is no longer present.
According to Eschebach a lararium was located in this area, but is no longer present.

The store room is a small rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis. We enter the store room from an opened doorway in the southwest. The three walls on the northwest, northeast and southeast each contain plaster with evidence of yellow and red painting. There are 6 support holes (3 each) to support two shelves on the northeast wall. The lowest row is approximately four feet (120 cm) above the ground. The higher is approximately two and a half to three feet ( 75 to 90 cm) above the lower.
On the northwest wall are two holes at the same height as the upper shelf holes, while there is only one on the southeast wall.
The walls are preserved to a second story height. There is no roof extant. The floor is obscured with lapilli and debris. The doorway of the northwest wall appears to be a plastered column which juts out into the room for about three inches ( 8 cm).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Atrium (2) to the southwest
Room 4 to the northwest
Room 6 to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: This is a small cubiculum. It is orientated on a southwest/northeast axis and is rectangular in plan. There is a door on the northwest wall through which one enters from the peristyle ( area 7). There is a window on the southeast wall towards the eastern half of the wall. The window is presently shuttered and the doorway has a locked, barred door. From the doorway we can see the southeast, southwest and northwest walls depict exotic scenes with pygmies thus giving the house its name. The northwest wall painting (3858) is a nilotic scene with pygmies and a crocodile surrounded by wildlife scenes, architecture with towers and pygmies carrying baskets of food. These are second style paintings. Above the paintings the southeast and northwest walls preserve their upper molding. No molding remains on the southwest wall which was arched for a vaulted ceiling. The room is in fair condition, the flooring is not visible, the original ceiling is not extant however is covered with a modern roof.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to the southwest of area 7 and to the southeast of the garden area

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room or a possible tablinum. It is a rectangular room on a northwest/southeast axis. There is a door on the southwest wall in the western corner. One enters the room from area 7 which surrounds the peristyle. There is a window on the southwest wall towards the middle of the room. This could be considered another doorway. This room is in very poor condition. The rubble walls have been heavily reconstructed. Plaster is preserved in parts of each of the four walls, however no paint survives. The floor is not visible and the ceiling no longer survives.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Southwest of area 7 surrounding the peristyle.
Southwest of room 5 and northwest of room 8 (the kitchen).

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. It has been identified that VII,2,20 is a domestic house. It has been determined that the last usage of this space is a domestic house. This determination is based on Eschebach 258-259.

This description is incomplete.

The storeroom is entered from the garden from the northwest. the room is rectangular in shape on a northwest/southeast axis. Neither the type of the floor nor the height of the floor is determinable. Approximately 40% of the southeast part of the floor has been raised. the surface of this portion is made of cement with stones embedded. This floor runs the entire width from the southwest to the northeast. The walls were stuccoed and painted of which little remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (15) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The masonry triclinium open northwest and takes up most of the dining room as extant. The surface is no longer extant but was probably plastered and painted as is implied by plaster on the exterior sides. The interior sides of each couch contains two storage niches for a total of six. In the center of the three couches appears to be the remnants of a table.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Platform 3003 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: In the west corner of the room is a rectangular masonry preparation platform on northwest/southeast axis. The surface was composed of pieces of terra cotta and marble and probably stuccoed as some stucco still survives on the northeast side.

In the corner of room (2) we see a large cooking platform. A large dolium was left next to the west end of the platform. There is a red bottom zone throughout the room with a black large border which continues over this platform. A lip is discernible on the south side (a small portion). There are two masonry struts probably to hold a grill.

In the large house attributed to Obellius Firmus, in the kitchen 33, this feature is a large platform immediately adjacent to the southwest and northwest walls in the west corner. To the northeast, it attaches to cooking platform 4421, and to the southeast it attaches to water basin 4424. The lower of the two platforms in this room, the tiled or cemented top surface is large and flat. The base is a solid masonry construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Continuous relationship to other features: To the northwest of latrine 4420 and water basin 4424, to the southwest of cooking platform 4421 and to the northwest of lararium 4423.

Continuous relationship with other rooms in structure: Adjacent corridor/passageway 32; southeast of Atrium 39.

DESCRIPTION: Along the west wall there is an elaborated garden triclinium. The masonry triclinium (1. medius 360m; 1 imus 285, 1 summus 230 - Jashemski). There is a rectangular table at the foot of the imus (.65 x .69m). There is a circular table between the benches (.50 m in diameter). There is a pergola abundantly displaying grapes. This triclinium back wall shows orange and red painting.

The counter room is located to the northwest of room (1). One enters the counter room from the southeast through a doorway. The smooth floor is slightly lower than that of room (1) and is made of plaster with terra cotta fragments. The walls were stuccoed and painted with remnants on all four walls. The ancient ceiling is not extant, but the height appears to be determined by the remnants in the northeast and northwest corner of a molding in plaster. In the southwest wall is a large doorway opening onto the sidewalk and street. The function of the room is defined by the L-shaped counter, one arm of which begins on the northwest wall and runs parallel to the street. Midway in the doorway, the counter turns at a 90 degree angle to the northeast and ends approximately two and a half feet from the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (1) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: An upright storage chest, rectangular in shape, placed on northwest-southeast axis against the northeast wall. Present today is its plaster cast. It appears to have been made of wood. Two decorative bronze pieces remain on the southwest side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: chest #3063 to northwest, chests 3061 and 3060 to southeast. Paintings 3056 and 3055 above.

DESCRIPTION: An upright storage chest, rectangular in shape , placed on northwest- southeast axis against northeast wall. Present today is its plaster cast. It appears to have been made of wood, but the corners of which seem to have had ivory bars running vertical. Today a bronze decorative piece and the remains of an iron locks appear on the southwest side. the lid appears to be in the open position. There also appears to be evidence of a shelf on the inside. ON the southwest side (front) is a vertical ivory bar which may have served as part of a doorway to gain access to the box under the shelf without opening the top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: chest 3062 and 3063 to northwest, chest 3060 to southeast. Paintings 3055, 3056, 3057 on wall above.

DESCRIPTION: The small niche lararium lies in the northwest wall at the level of and to the northeast of the upper portion of the cooking platform. The floor of the lararium is made from tiles and as extant protrudes slightly into the area of the room to the southeast. The interior of the lararium still contains a white stucco but no evidence of paint. The floor of the lararium that extends into the room is wider than the width of the lararium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform to southwest. Water feature to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Located to the north off entrance 15, this is a rectangular room on a north/south axis. Plaster remains on the walls. The doorway is wide, looking onto common area 1. Doorway has a tufa sill. High up on the west wall are two holes that may have been used for ceiling beams. Floor is lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The north and east walls are adjacent to the street and adjoining property. The south wall abuts latrine 2 and space 1. The west wall abuts dining room 4.

DESCRIPTION: This kitchen is a rectangular room with a north/south axis. The doorway is in the center of the west wall with a modern lintel. The floor is obscured by lapilli and structural debris. Plaster survives on the north, south, and west walls. High in the west end of the north wall is a window (or perhaps collapse?). In the center of the south wall is a rectangular plastered window tapering south to the street outside. In the southeast corner, the placement for a downpipe survives together for possible placing of a latrine seat. The area of the drain below is filled with debris. In the northeast corner there is a rectangular cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fauces 1 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room with a wide doorway in the south wall opening to atrium 2. The floor is obscured by lapilli. On the center of the north wall there is a square window with a modern lintel with traces of plaster on the base of the window. Plaster survives on the north, east, and the north end of the west wall with red decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular peristyle garden is aligned on a NE/SW axis. This is surrounded by 24 stucco covered columns between which Jashemski noted a wooden fence between the columns. The fluted columns are red on the bottom and white on the top (6 x 8). A narrow channel is enclosed by the columns. In the center, there is a large fountain pool. This is basically rectangular with alternating rectangles and semi-circular recesses. The walls of the pool are painted blue. The top surface is capped with white marble. In the center of the pool is a column supporting a column base which was part of a fountain. At the SW end of the pool water cascaded down from 7 marble steps, located adjacent to the S.E. side of the stepped fountain is a deep square tank which Jashemski suggested may hold fish while the pool was being cleaned or used to cool drinks. A similar yet smaller and more shallow tank is located just N.E. of the eastern corner of the peristyle garden. A puteo is located between the last columns at the Eastern end of the S.E. row.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is S.W. of the dining rooms (28) and (29). It is located N.W. of the atrium

DESCRIPTION: Retangular room on an east/west axis in heavily bombed out area. N and W walls are reconstructed, with traces of white and red plaster. Room is entered from wide doorway in southwall from atrium 7. East wall only exists partially. There is no ceiling and the floor is over grown. there are possible traces of red and yellow paint remaining in a very rustic condition. There is a very small remnant of a stone threshold in the doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 7 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The scavi sign reads: Taberna C. Catius Scithus. However, inside it appears to be a dining place. You can enter from the road via a privacy entrance situated at the South end of a Southeast wall. The floor is made up of lapilli and pounded dirt. There is no ceiling. The Southwest wall is made of stone and cement, with a portion of plaster. The South corner shows a tiny vertical slice of red paint. (In the high zone, there is a recess for a light source) There are 3 walls in the Northwest. The Western segment appears to be a prep and fish pond rooms. the middle wall contains a lararium. A close look at the interior back wall of the lararium, seems to indicate a graphite sketch. There is red paint, in evidence, on the back wall. Situated beneath, is a rectangular altar. A door to the North opens to a storeroom. The final third of the Northwest wall encloses the storeroom. The Northeast wall shows the 3 plaster layers of evidence. The bottom layer is grayish white in color. A 2nd thin layer is a red Pompei color. The top layer is a beige/light coral color. 3 beam holes are approximately 8 feet off the ground, and indicates some kind of covering. The S.W. shows no comparable beam holes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is contiguous to Room 5, to the N.W.. The room is contiguous to room 2, situated to the S.W..

DESCRIPTION: This is a storage room. There is a single entrance at the western end of the southeast wall. This room is square, on a northwest/southeast axis. It is in poor condition. The floor is not visible. There is no ceiling extant. The walls are preserved to between eight-twelve feet in height. The southwest wall has a low window at the south end. North of this window are two cupboards (3753 and 3752). The walls have some remaining plaster, particularly on the lower five feet of the wall. There is a horizontal etched line dividing the plaster from the wall above. On the northwest wall at about ten feet high is a horizontal groove shallowly out in the stone.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Room 1 is to the southeast.
Corridor (room 2) is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: In the southwest wall there is a cupboard located in the north corner. The cupboard is about 10 to 12 inches deep. Some plaster still remains within the cupboard. Two bracket holes remain with a bit of metal in the lower one. This in in poor condition with restoration at the top.

A rectangular room north / south axis. Floor obscured by lapilli. Undercoated plaster survives on east, west and south walls. Traces of 2 registers survives in northeast corners. At the west end of the south wall there is a blocked plastered doorway. In the center of the west wall, there is a high square window through to Room 1. At the north end of the west wall, there is a doorway with stone stepped threshold to salesroom 1. In the west wall there are 3 holes which pierce through to room 1. There are 3 holes piercing thru the wall completely and a 4th neither in line nor piercing thru on the north wall. There are 6 randomly placed holes in the east wall. These holes on the west and north walls may have supported shelves.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small rectangular room with a stone threshold with indentations for door pivots. The north and west walls were plastered and the floor is lapilli. The doorway is entered from a passageway (11) on the south side of the room. The room is on a northeast/southwest axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The southwest wall abuts a peristyle (2). The northeast wall abuts a storeroom (15). The southeast wall abuts a passageway (11) and the northwest wall abuts the adjoining property (6.5.9).

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular niche is cut out on the lower portion of the southwest wall immediately abutting the northwest wall. The niche is approximately one hundred fifty centimeters wide by fifty centimeters high. No decoration is present any longer.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The corner of the southwest wall it is immediately adjacent to the northwest wall of dining room 14.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a small detail located on the north side of the barrel vault. A small rectangular frame in red paint with a red line within it encloses a white panel. This small panel is painted green in the center and shows a small bird eating two cherries with their stems.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Painting (3262) to the east; mills (3265, 3266, 3267) below.

DESCRIPTION: Dining Room 16 is also off corridor 5 and has a partial door frame. Three rubble walls are extant but no plaster. The floor is mud. An improvised shower and a modern sink are present. This room is square and a similar size to dining rooms 14 and 15. This room, like dining rooms 14 and 15, has a view of the garden.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Stairway (with 10 steps and a landing) to the west; dining room (15-3258) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a L-shaped counter with a short arm facing the street to the east. Masonry body with rectangular plastered recess in the center of the long arm. Cement surface is extensively restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Niche 6205 is to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The niche is in the north wall of the counter room, in the northwest corner of said room. It is roughly 1.5 m. to the niche sill. Significant modern restoration and reconstruction is evident in the opus incertum wall. The niche has a modern wooden lintel. Plaster extant. Likely restoration and possibly not in situ. Plaster appears to have been red and white. Niche bisects the lower and upper plaster registers of the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The niche shares the room with the counter and is visible from the street.

DESCRIPTION: This is a large rectangular space opening to a garden (12) on the southeast. In the middle of the wall is a doorway to another dining room (13). A single couch niche is located on the northwest corner in the southwest wall. On the northwest section of the south wall no plaster remains; however, there are traces of a white mosaic floor. The axis of the room is northeast/southwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The open doorway, located to the southeast, opens to a garden (12). The southwest wall abuts a storeroom (15). The northeast wall opens to a dining room (13). The northwest wall abuts the adjoining property (6.5.9).

DESCRIPTION: This is a latrine with a drain across the southern end of the room. The drain is filled with earth. The floor of tiles and opus signinum slopes south to the drain. In the southwest corner there is a recess into the wall and against the floor level there is a terracotta down pipe draining through the west wall to the street beyond.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A cooking platform (6160) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular dining room lies along a northeast/southwest axis and is entered from the southern corner from dining room 10. In the west wall near the entrance is a low window which gives a view into the pseudoperistyle. The window is approximately one meter wide and 80 centimeters high. Plaster remains can be seen on all four walls, however these are only small fragments. High on the north wall are nine beam holes however these are not found on the corresponding south wall. In the north corner of the west wall is a slight right angle which juts into the space. The ceiling is not extant. The floor is obscured with vegetation and rubble.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Room (10-3256) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Entrance from large peristyle (32) and the room is located on the northwest side of the peristyle. Large entrance opening. Standing in the room one looks out on the peristyle garden. It is a very large room. Threshold is marble with one short step. The room is roofed with a reconstructed ceiling. The exterior of the entrance is plastered with traces of yellow paint. The upper walls are reconstructed. The floor has a geometric patterned mosaic in polychrome. Fragments of mosaic floor remain. Southwest wall has traces of plaster and painted in third style, very faint, with three registers in yellow and red and possibly white. Facing the wall, there is an entrance of the left side to room 33 to the southwest. There are three post holes above the doorway entrance and two post holes directly above two of them. Northwest wall has an entrance on far left to a cubiculum. There is plaster and traces of painting with three registers of red, yellow and white paint. The southeast wall is damaged and reconstructed, with plaster and painting with very faint traces of yellow, red, and white paint in three registers that are possibly third style. Facing that wall in lower right corner attached to southeast wall and entrance wall is a low rim, perhaps a water feature. Above, near the ceiling, is trace of molding. Southeast wall reconstructed with yellow and red plaster. There is a small cubicula that is entered from the northwest corner by an opening from this room. Above lintell centered at entrance way is a hole.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The entrance from portico 32 south. A side entrance from room 33 east. Room 35 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: On northeast wall, facing the entrance to the left to corridor 30, there is a cooking platform. Brick and stone with traces of plaster on both sides. It abuts northeast and southeast walls in the corner. No traces of tile surface, concrete only.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north of 6405, 6406, 6404, 6402. 6403 is on southeast wall above.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. It has been determined that this is a plastered recess for a latrine situated in the north corner of the kitchen. Plaster survives on the interior face of each of the three sides. The base of the latrine is obscured by earth and debris. The presence of a drain can be seen by the load-bearing arch in the wall to the north.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach 258-259
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Platform 4540 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. It has been identified that VII,2, 20 is a domestic house. It has been determined that the last usage of this space is a domestic house. This determination is based on Eschebach 258-259.

This description is incomplete.
Circular masonry support with poorly preserved surface and modern cement. Basalt meta in situ on the base.
Circular masonry base for mill. Plastered exterior survives in places. Modern restoration. Basalt catillus and meta survives in situ on the base.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
6412, 6413, 6414, 6415, 6416 and 6417 are to the north.
6411, 6421 are to the south.
6405 is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room on an east/west axis. The doorway in the center of the north wall opens from the peristyle (2). The floor is obscured by lapilli. No extant wall decoration remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle (2) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room. The floor is obscured by lapilli. The doorway in the northeast wall leads to the peristyle (2) and has a stone threshold. There is a possible blocked doorway from an earlier phase in the west wall. The north wall is a later addition as it lies against the yellow and red plaster of earlier phase at the junction of the north and east walls. Plaster with traces of yellow paint survives on the south and north walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle (2) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is on an east/west axis and has a doorway in the northwest corner leading to the peristyle (2). A matching door is in the eastern half of the north wall. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Plaster survives on the west and south walls with red trim. The east wall is an addition as it abuts the plaster in the south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The peristyle (2) is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular room is on a north/south axis. The doorway in the center of the north wall opens to a corridor (8). The floor is obscured by lapilli. Fragmentary plaster is on the south wall but has no visible decoration. There is a small plastered recess in the northeast corner, subsequently blocked.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A corridor (8) is to the north

DESCRIPTION: This is a square dining room opening to the northeast off of the peristyle (2). A secondary entrance is located in the southwest corner of the northwest wall. Another secondary entrance is located in the northeast corner of the southwest wall. The doorway opening to the peristyle has a stone threshold. The other two accesses have no evidence of thresholds remaining. The room was fully plastered with some remains of fresco paintings in shades of red and black. The floor is lapilli. No windows are evident.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The northeast wall abuts to the garden (12). The southeast wall abuts a corridor (8. The southwest wall abuts the peristyle (2). The northwest wall abuts a passage (11).

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis opens off the northeast wall of dining room 14. The doorway provides a view of the garden (12). The walls have some remains of plaster, but very little. There are no windows and no remains of flooring.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The southwest wall opens to dining room 14. The remaining three walls abut other structure addresses.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain 4828 is at the south east corner of 6.16.3 at the intersection of the via del Vesuvio and vicolo delle Nozze d' Argento. The fountain faces the latter. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. it has a subtle lining that rounds off the floor / wall junction. The lining in the floor is probably opus signinum although it is not observed. The interior dimensions of the basin are 1.28 m. by 0.90 m. and it is 0.70 m. deep. The pilaster is on the top centre of the north west slab and is decorated with the head of a feline (panther?) Worn hand placements are on either side of the pilaster and at the interior north west, east and south corners. The overflow is in the centre top of the north eastern slab and the drain is approximately 0.37 m. from the interior eastern corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: on the via del Vesuvio at the south west corner of 6.16.3

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 17 opens at the south end to secondary (other) atrium 18. Very little plaster remains in the walls. There are no windows. Room is almost square and is identified as a dining room because of the wide doorway that open almost across the entirety of the southern wall onto atrium 18. No floor remains. The entire structure was previously excavated pre-79AD levels. Threshold had clay tiles across the front.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: "Other" Atrium 18 lies to the south, room 12 is to the west, room 16 is to the east, and room 13 is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the long rectangular preparation room, which lies south of the kitchen, from the west. The room likes along a northeast/southwest axis. The walls are high and have been restored at some point. Only a small few fragments of plaster remain. On both long walls (north and south) we find nine beam holes for support. The floor is obscured with vegetation and marble slabs as well as random building materials in the back of the room. The ceiling in non extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen (3261) room 7 is to the north and dining room (3260) room 9 is south and room 5 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room. It is on the northwest/southeast axis. One enters the room from the west side through a very large arched opening. The ceiling is barrel vaulted. The flooring is not visible. There are opposing doorways at the west end of the north and south walls. Frescoes remain on the north, south, and east walls. The vault is also frescoed. Features 3262 and 3254 are paintings in the wall and vault. Features 3265, 3266, and 3267 sit along the north wall. About 50% of the frescoes remain. The west half of the vault has been conserved. The wall paintings are in the Fourth Style with plaster relief molding at the springing of the vault on the north and south walls and across the east wall. The door to room 11 is blocked with modern construction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The main entrance is contiguous to the corridor (5) to the west. Dining room (9-3260) is to the north. Room 11 is to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This room opens off the corridor (5). There is a marble threshold to the door. Masonry struts abut the window which seems the same size as that in dining room 14, but this window has a marble sill. This room is currently barricaded with a wooden slot door. Through this can be seen a room similar to 14 with red, black, and yellow paint. There is a sizable wooden shelf and a mound of tubs and buckets covered by plastic and a large pile of sand covering about one quarter of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor 5 to the south; dining room (14-3257) to the east; dining room (16-3259) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We enter room 7 which is a small kitchen with a large cooking platform from a door in the southeast end of a south wall from andron (5). The axis of the room is northwest/southeast. On the adjoining corner of the southeast of the room is the entrance to the latrine. The doorways to the kitchen and adjoining latrine are low. Occupying the entire east wall is a cooking platform which fits in between the north, east, and south walls and extends into the room approximately one meter in width, ending just before the entrance. There is a large stone structure abutting the east wall from the northeast corner and extending midway where it appears to have been broken. It is approximately one meter high and 20 centimeters deep. The walls of stone are preserved above first story high with reconstruction. No ceiling is extant. The floor is obscured with moss and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Latrine 6 to the west and andron 5 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: A very large cooking platform exists on northwest wall with a tile surface. Reconstructed, at least in part. Facing the platform there is no evidence of a rim. Facing the wall to the left is latrine 6404.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
6401, 6403 to the east.
6404, 6422 to the south.
6405 to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room - N/S axis. The floor is obscured by Lapilli. Traces of undecorated plaster on the south and west walls. In the center of the west wall there is a wide doorway with stepped stone threshold to the street to the west. In the northwest corner there is a masonry base with two proceeding steps for stairs to the floor above. Room 1 is contiguous with room 3 forming an L enclosing room 2 to the southeast. Room 2 is accessed through a doorway to the east. In the southeast corner is cooking a platform 6232. In the south wall behind the platform there is a terracotta drain from an upper floor above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 3 is to the northeast, Room 2 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular arched couch niche. The lower part of the niche is contiguous with the wall. At the base of the niche at the southern end there is a collapsed hole into the wall. Plastered decoration survives of yellow and red bands and red trim on a white background. It's in the southern end of the east wall. The brick courses at the base of the niche are inserted into an earlier recess as they rest against an earlier plaster layer. No decoration is visible on the earlier plaster.

The lararium is in the north wall, and would have been visible from the kitchen's primary entrance from the southeast corner of the room. It is roughly two meters from the floor to the sill of the lararium. north wall and lararium are of modern reconstruction. The surrounding plaster is extant. the color is not discernible due to the elements.
