CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium is in the kit hen containing two platforms

DESCRIPTION: The overall structure is oriented generally in N/S axis. The dining room is northeast of the primary structure entrance. The room is oriented with its entrance facing west toward the peristyle. there is a rectangular window high on the north wall. The window sill is roughly 3.2 meters high. Plaster remains on the north, south, east and west walls with white over red paint, likely 4th style. The floor is a black tesserae set into white stone In a diamond shaped geometric pattern. Extant at the west threshold entry to the room. There are no signs of doors in only the singular high - placed window, mentioned above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the west is the peristyle garden. To the north, east, and south is another structure /property.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular cooking platform is inserted against the plaster in the northwest corner of the room. It is a masonry platform with a tile surface and arched recess beneath. At the north end there is a masonry step against the north wall abutting directly to a plastered buttress in the northwest corner of the room. Against the south end a low square platform has been added with a modern (?) cement surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A latrine (6159) is located to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This rectangular room is on an east/west axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli. There is a plastered doorway with red paint in the north end of the west wall. In the center of the north wall a wide window looks out to the garden (12). Plaster decoration survives on all four walls with attending red, white and yellow panels, and white above - fourth style (?). High in the south wall parts of plaster cornice are visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The corridor (8) is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: At the far north end of the house (6.7.7) is located a rectangular kitchen that contains on its west wall a cooking platform (6282) with a built up hearth above. The walls were plastered plastered and there is the possibility of a high window in the southwest corner of the wall. The room is on an east/west axis. The floor is rubble.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The north and west walls abut adjacent property. The south wall abuts room 11. To the east is room 13 and corridor 10.

DESCRIPTION: In the open enclosure of the tomb of L. Barbidius are the the poorly preserved remains of an altar or platform constructed in opus incertum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature 4898 is to the east of the doorway and it lies along the wall to the northeast corner.

DESCRIPTION: This is tomb 15 by the Nocera Gate. It is the tomb of L. Barbidius. The facade is decorated with four engaged columns, two on each side with a shallow arched niche between each pair of engaged columns. A marble plaque remains above the entry commemorating the tomb owner L. Barbidius. The interior space, for funeral feasting, is enclosed by three walls of grey stone. Along the north west wall are the remains of an altar or platform (4898)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This tomb is situated between tombs 17 and 13 on the south side of the cemetery road.

DESCRIPTION: Two low masonry supports are bonded with the east wall. Supports and east wall have evidence of modern tuck-pointing.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Supports are directly south of the kneading basin and along the east side of the room.

DESCRIPTION: Large, shallow arched recess at the south end of the west wall. The base of the lararium is not preserved. Undecorated plaster with modern restoration survives throughout.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cistern 6247, mill 6240, 6241,6239, masonry support 6245. Kneading basin 6244, oven 6243, preparation platform 6242 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room faced west-east axis. Doorway in the southern end of the east wall with stepped threshold and modern lintel. Floor is obscured by lapilli . No extant wall decoration. two small holes in north wall of uncertain use. Third hole blocked. Cooking platform 6181 in northeast corner of room. Northwest corner of room w/ latrine 6182 is separated for the remainder of room by a partitioned wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 to east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a Catillus. It is broken along the rim. It is black basalt. It is not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to two other catilli (3266, 3267) along the north wall of room 10.

DESCRIPTION: This is a Catillus in poor condition with portions of both ends missing. It is black basalt. It is not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It sits between features 3265 and 3267. Two other catilli along the north wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular room on an east/ west axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli and extensive debris. All four wall show signs of restorations. At the north end of the west wall there is a small doorway with no visible threshold. In the center of the east wall there is a square window with a modern lintel looking into the street to the east. Above the window are facings for floor above or possible modern restoration. The north wall, east wall and east corner of south wall have white plaster with a red trim surviving at the east end of the north wall. Wall collapse at the north end of the east wall reveals a terracotta down pipe which drains out to the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This recessed space or niche is located in the northwest wall in the southern corner. The space is 1.5 meters wide, 1.5 meters tall and 20 centimeters deep. The vousoirs are visible on the northwest side of the arch. Wall plaster is preserved on the southern half of the arch, including the interior of the arch, otherwise the rough stone is visible.
PAH1 3, 26 remains a wine press CF Eschebach 162'

This house is not completed. We have determined that this is a dining room. This is a small, square room There is no apparent threshold. All the walls show the same restoration pattern, with brick and opus incertum and there is a high rectangular window in the northwest wall facing the street. Above this window we can see a second floor with another window facing the street. The floor is vegetation, debris, and stone. The west wall is restored with plaster and opus incertum. It shows a low doorway on the southwest corner filled with stone (modern restoration).

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to fauces and storeroom 4517 and opening onto atrium.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. We have determined that this large room is a dining room. There does not seem to be a threshold to the tall entrance door. The floor is vegetation with tiny spots of rocks and debris. The larger wall is northwest and it contains a rectangular window opening to the street. The east wall, the west wall, and one southeast wall are all of opus incertum and brick; the east wall and southeast wall have signs of plaster. There are definite signs of roofing, but no roof exists now. The walls show that there was a second floor.

BIBLIOGRAPHY: Eschebach.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fauces, atrium, and cubiculum are adjoining.

DESCRIPTION: Square sales room with wide open doorway to street to the east. Stone-stepped threshold, with placing for door. The northern half of the doorway is blocked by the base of a heavily restored L-shaped counter. Plaster survives on the north wall with red lower register, white upper. Along the wall extending from the east are seven holes, five of which are positioned to support two rows of shelves. At the west end of the north wall there is a square plastered niche with modern lintel. No decoration is visible. The west wall has a wide window through to room three and at the south end of the west wall is a wide doorway to three. Against the south wall there is a base for stairs to the floor above accessed from entrance 24. There is a doorway in the south wall to room 2. The floor is obscured by lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 to the south, Room 3 to the west .

DESCRIPTION: This feature is located in the south end of the southeast wall of dining room 5. It is in the small white rectangular field above the large white rectangular panel. Centered under ribbons, this image is badly faded; however, the ghost of a glass-footed bowl can be seen containing at least four round pieces of fruit. Slight traces of yellow paint remain on the bowl.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is to the southeast of feature 4578 on the opposite wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is a rectangular opening to a cistern with no cover evident. It is the north corner. It is heavily restored.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The water basin is to the north. Kneading basin (3222) and mills (3207, 3227,3226 and 3206) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The long axis of the room is generally east to west with a water trough running the entire length of the north rubble. The floor is of stone rubble. The east wall is of opus mixtum and contains an entrance from the street. That entrance has a stone threshold carved such that panels/doors could be used to secure the room. One steps down into the room from the threshold. The north wall is of opus incertum and opus mixture at the entrance opening. The north wall has evidence of repairs, both modern and from antiquity. The west wall is of opus incertum and is interrupted by a water basin/passthrough of modern reconstruction. Some opus signinum is extant. The south wall is of opus incertum with opus mixtum at the entrance to the mill room. This entrance has a stone threshold carved to indicate two pivot points such that one could secure the room. Plaster is not extant in the room. The room is a stable because of size, trough, and its proximity to the mill room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The street is to the east. The kitchen is to the west. The mill room is to the south. A differing property/structure is to the north.

DESCRIPTION: Feature 6366 is a large cooking platform attached to north wall. it is rectangular in shape with an arched recessed area underneath. Tile remains on top surface of cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Directly across from another cooking platform 6367 in the room. To the northwest of latrine 6368.

DESCRIPTION: This is an arched lararium niche with plaster surviving on the interior face. There is no visible decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cistern (6227) is directly in front of the lararium to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The preparation platform and surface is heavily reconstructed post antiquity. 2 basins exist with no terracotta vessels extant. Preparation platform is rectilinear with an easterly and westerly wing wall or bump-out. This form is atypical to what we commonly see in Pompeii. This form is likely a misinterpretation by modern restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation platform abuts the oven and its masonry banding is not contiguous with that of the oven.

DESCRIPTION:
Beehive oven is of opus latericium with opus incertum surround. Passthrough from the preparation room is west of the oven mouth. There is no post
baking passthrough to the east through the front face of the oven. Eschebach references a terracotta medallion above the oven mouth with phallic symbol and inscription which are not extant; only the niche remains. There is no high ventilation openings/vents evident. They were likely filled/covered post antiquity. Between the oven mouth and preparation room passthrough there is located a vertical opening through the top of the structure. This may be a chimney or flue.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The preparation platform is to the west of the oven mouth.

DESCRIPTION: Kneading basin is of black tufa, located in northeast corner of room in front of oven. It was damaged in antiquity with 3 iron repairs evident. The 3 pieces associated with this repair are not extant. Opus signinum is present. Distinctive wear is noted on the wedge and the inside of the basin lip.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Basin is directly east of the oven mouth and north of the masonry platform supports.

DESCRIPTION: Square tufa base for a circular cistern head. Cistern is filled with earth and a small cone shaped stone, not in situ, has been placed in the opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium 6246 to the southwest, mill 6241, 6240, 6239, masonry support 6245, kneading basin 6244, oven 6243, preparation platform 6242 to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular cooking platform against the east end of the north wall. The platform abuts directly against plastered wall to the east arched recessed storage beneath. tiled cooking surface partially preserved.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6182 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Two thirds of a catillus sits in the southwest entrance from room (1). It is not in situ.

This is a square stone constructed structure. Traces of fine plaster coating are visible on the interior of the southwest side and along the bottom of the northwest side. A large underground opening is visible at the northeast and southeast bottom. This stone feature abuts the earlier plastered and painted northwest wall which is visible along the northeast side of the cistern (interior). The northwest side of the cistern was probably lower then the other sides.

A latrine separated from remainder of room by a partitioned wall. the latrine is entered by a stepped threshold with tiled surface that slopes into the drain to the north. the drain is filled by debris. on the northeast and west sides are the masonry supports for a seat and in the east wall there is the placing for the wooden seat inserted into the face of the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6181 to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
Rectangular room, north south axis. Bombed out. Poorly preserved north, east and west walls. Pinkish hue on plaster on east and west wall with traces of a central rosette and architectural details in the east wall. Yellow trim and rosette in the west wall. Floor obscured by debris. According to Warscher the painting of Isis and Io referred to by Bonucci and now in the Naples museum (inv 9555) may have come from this room. Warscher suggests that the presence of a painting of Isis in a low status inn indicates that it was used by worshippers of isis.
The large quantities of cooking utensils found throughout the house supports its identification as an inn.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room east west axis. Bombed. Filled with earth, no visible floor, no south or west wall. According to Forelli the kitchen contained stairs to floor above, latrine 6339 and cooking platform 6338.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium 2 to the south

DESCRIPTION: No longer extant cooking platform against the north wall of the kitchen described by Warscher. Warscher's photograph shows arched storage recess beneath and tiled surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: north of room 37, room 35 to east, atrium 2 to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: No longer extant latrine described by Fiorelli.
Bombed out and filled with debris. Warscher identifies this as a possible dining room. Overlooking a garden according to Jashemski.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: South of Atrium 2

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east west axis, floor obscured by lapilli throughout. White plaster fragments survive on east wall, north east corner and north west corner. At the base of the north west corner there are traces of two layers of plaster of earlier decoration with red plaster and black overline. In the centre of the west wall there is a doorway with no visible threshold to atrium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 5 to the west

DESCRIPTION: Room has no ceiling or roof. Floor obscured by lapilli. Entrance is on south east all of House of the Labyrinth (6.11.10) off corridor 51. Whole house at 6.11.8 is in northwest side of the House of the Labyrinth, directly behind the bakery. On the northwest wall of room 2, on the right, there were stairs leading off the main corridor into atrium 5. The section of northwest wall is located under a stairwell. Damaged and some reconstruction with some plaster and traces of paint, very faded colour. In the wall under the stairwell there is a round post hole and a large recessed rectangular niche with traces of plaster. High up on wall there are traces of two post holes. Facing the wall to the left a wall projects north approximately one third into the room, behind which is a latrine (6425) On south west wall which is and has damaged no plaster or paint, there is a rectangular window above head level. Facing wall on left side, above cooking platform is a rectangular opening. Low on that wall is a round hole. Facing the south east wall in the lower right corner there are traces of a cooking platform (6426) On the wall is a trace of plaster but no paint. High up on the wall appears a row of post holes of uneven sizes. At the level of the doorway there are five post holes, possibly round. Other round holes appear in the wall. There is a large entrance along the north east wall. There are no remains.

We enter this dining room from the northwest over a lava stone threshold. There is a modern wooden lintel. The door is not extremely high but not too low. On the northeast portion of the doorway there is thick white plaster. On all walls we find evidence over lower register with golden yellow stenciling and a white upper register which had stencil work. High on the southeast and northwest walls there is patterned plaster and traces of red paint are faint on each fanlike flower. On the north corner of the northwest/southeast walls is an approximately two foot (60 cm) wide indentation which is where the original northeast wall stood. However there is now a southeast facing which juts out into the room about two foot (60 cm) forming the new face for a northeast wall. In other words, there is a small alcove in this corner. High in the center of the southeast wall is a small rectangular window which still contains plaster. High on the northwest wall above the doorway is a beam hole. The painting of a water plant low on the western side of the northwest wall indicates that the room was probably in the fourth style. The floor is covered with lapilli. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 33 to the southwest and hallway 7 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION:
(Replaces sheet 21)
The counter is u-shaped with 6 recessed dolia; a hearth is located at the east end with a support for cooking apparatus above, level with the counter surface. The counter has been heavily restored, with the marble segments repainted in their original positions. However, on the south arm of the counter, towards the east end, the marble segments do not survive. The hearth has also been heavily restored. The rim of only 1 dolium survives on the northeast arm of the wall, and the bodies of 2 dolia are visible in the interior of the counter shape. The bodies of the 6 dolia are still visible despite not having rims. The interiors of the dolia are filled with lapilli. The hearth located at the east end of the south arm of the counter is slightly offset in alignment. Because the hearth has been heavily restored it is difficult to be certain if this is the original slate. The base of the hearth survives with cocciopesto and broken tegula comprising the floor of the hearth. Signs of burning are present within the hearth. The marble segments on the top of the counter consist of giallo antico, cipollino, luna, black africanus, red porphey.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The counter room is contiguous to rooms 2 and 3 to the east of the property and south of room 4 within 6.2.2, accessed by the passthrough from room 1.

DESCRIPTION: Kitchen 19 is a square room oriented northeast by southwest. The larger entrance from porticos 18 to the northeast does not show any trace of the threshold. At the northern edge of the entrance (to the right) and aligned with the opening is the cooking platform. In the southwest corner of the room along the bottom of the southwest wall runs what looks like a rim, slightly raised above the floor. At the "rim" on the western wall seems to be a semicircular small opening which could have held a drain pipe. The whole corner may have been occupied by a latrine, but the evidence is too poor to support this suggestion. The room shows traces of a coarse earthen floor. The walls on the southwest, northwest and the southeast sides have been heavily reconstructed, along with the roof. On the southwest wall, at approximately 2.2 meters above the floor, are two square holes which could have supported the beams of a roof. On the north end of the northwest wall a section is framed by a semi-column. This section protrudes into the room and shows traces of red painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Porticos 18 to northeast, Dining room 17 to the southeast, and store room 20 to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the triclinium from room 5, through a door in the northeast wall. The triclinium is rectangular in shape on a northwest southeast axis. On the northeast wall is a large window opening into garden 10 The floor is beaten cement with fragments of white and bluish stones. The paintings on all 4 walls are 4th style. The lower register is a combination of plants, amphorae, and outdoor scenes of animals and humans. In the central register are a series of large rectangular frames around either square mythological scenes, floating winged figures (erates?) or small, rectangular frames around birds. The picture on the southeast wall is Venus fishing. On the southwest wall in Europa and the bull. The upper register has garlands and stylized architectural drawings. On the northwest wall, however are still extant 3 fish. The corresponding area of the southeast wall may also have been food-related but is too damaged to be sure. Although the ceiling is not extant, portions of plaster in the east corner indicate the ceiling was fairly low. In addition, the extant plaster from the northwest and southeast ends indicate the ceiling sloped from southwest to northeast.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 to the northeast. Room 5 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Large, U-shaped dining couch facing southwest finished with opus signinum and plaster. The surface of the couches has been extensively restored. There is a low wall restored at the end of lectus summus and imus. The exterior yellow-painted plaster, interior and front plaster blue background with wide red borders, possible traces of red figures. Similar coloring has been seen of Nilotic landscapes on other garden triclinia. Between the arms of the couches there is a plaster circular table with marble top. The floor between couches and in front is opus signinum with large marble inserts. In front of the northern arm there is a terracotta cistern head (3027) and in front of the southern arm a preparation platform (3028).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the west, cistern 3027, preparation platform 3028 and fish pond 3030. Cistern 3031 and water feature 3033.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this tiny square kitchen which lies at the northeast end of the shop from the southwest. There are a half/cooking platform, shelves and a latrine in the room, the former two on the southeast and northeast walls. Support holes fort he latrine are in the west corner along the northwest and southwest walls. The walls are plastered and painted red in the first register. High the southeast wall just over the shelves is a round opening and high on the northeast wall in the center is a window which is a light aperture as well as a vent for smoke. The walls on the northwest, northeast and southeast sides extend to the second story height and on the southwest wall above the door way the wall is lower, however it still extends above the first story level. The floor is obscured but seems to have been cement in antiquity. The threshold, which is still intact, is a step made of volcanic rock. Eschebach reports that in the kitchen there is a graffitto: "carmina communemne arma virumque ceno tro." The graffitto is not visible today. If this shop, as evidence suggested were bronze and iron workshop this passage from Virgil's Aeneid is befitting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 is to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: The store room is entered from the northeast from the peristyle through a very high linteled doorway. The door threshold indicates the door could have been locked. The floor has a small patch of cocciopesto in the north corner. The walls are plastered and painted white. The corners of the room all feature red paint. We identified this as a food and drink storage room because of the evidence of shelf support holes in all four walls. The support holes are at two levels. There are eight holes at the lower level and seven holes at the lower level. We have small oval shaped opening on the southwest wall located well above the top shelf support holes. The opening provides light and ventilation. The wall extends to the second story and has rafter strut holes on the northwest and southeast walls. The holes indicate there was a high ceiling but there is no other evidence of a ceiling. The shelving is evident in the indentations in the plaster above the shelf struts. On the northeast wall the width of the shelves is evident in the impression in the plaster (width approximately five centimeters). On the southwest wall there is a stain that runs from the opening on the southwest wall to the floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle to the northeast, stairway on the northwest, dining room 6-3160 on the south east.

DESCRIPTION: (We have the description and photograph from 2001, but the only drawing is an elevation.) (We also need a floor plan.) (The original feature is #143.) This rectangular room is on a north/south axis. The floor is obscured by lapilli. Extensive, undecorated plaster survives on the south wall. In the north wall there is a doorway with a modern lintel and stepped threshold opening north to an earlier tablinum. At the north end of the east wall there is a door with a stone threshold to the mill room (11). The threshold has multiple placings for a door. South of this doorway, in the east wall, there is a square opening for the passing through of bread to the oven room (room 11). Fragments of decorated plaster survives in the southeast corner with a black lower register and red above.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The tablinum is to the north. The mill room (11) is to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: To the north east of the north west corner of the ovens is a small stone basin, at one time encased in masonry, all abutting the oven. The interior has been cut in a cone shape and lined in plaster. On the interior west wall is a hole also lined with plaster. The use of the basin is unknown but may have been used for water.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Oven (3081) to the south west, mill (3086) to the north west, kneading basin (3085) to the north east, water basin (3083) to the south east, kneading machine (3084) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: From doorway 1 we walk through atrium 20 in a west direction to enter dining room 21. The dining room is a large rectangular room on an east/west axis. The north wall appears to have been divided into two rooms in a previous time by a jut in the center of the wall. Plaster remains in rough condition on all walls and in some places it is possible to see an earlier decorative scheme of red lines on white plaster. The AD 79 plaster is evident in two places on the south wall where it supersedes the previous plaster. It appears the room was painted orange-red in some areas in AD 79. The access to the room is by two doorways, one shorter on the southwest corner of the south wall and a taller doorway opening to atrium 20 on the west wall. A large almost floor height window opens on that same wall to the tetrastyle in the atrium giving the diners a view of that. There is another window above providing additional light. The south wall also shows previous room division by a recessed angle leading to the doorway. The floor is lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room opens to the west to atrium 20 and to the south to space 22. The north and east walls abut neighboring properties.

DESCRIPTION: Entering to the south of the peristyle garden, one enters a very large rectangular room with a north/south axis. The room is divided into two sections by juts in the wall midway down the long sides. A small doorway to an adjoining room is located on the northeast corner of the east wall. The larger opening is on the north wall and almost spans the width of the room. Marble door sills are evident on the two sides of the doorways with cutouts for door hardware. Painted plaster, although faded and ruined, appears on all walls. There are two very high windows on the south and east walls. There are shards of mosaic tiles on the floor amidst the rubble. Tile, along the east and west walls, appears in two places to have had a black border, that would have run around the walls, on white ground.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south is room 20 near entrance 6.7.1. To the west is corridor 19. To the east is dining room 16 as well as adjoining property.

DESCRIPTION: L-shaped room with north-south axis, facing oven 6417 to the north. In the southeast corner is a doorway with a stone threshold to a corridor (30) with placings for a door. In the center of the south wall is a doorway to stairs with modern lintel and a doorway with modern lintel to bath room 43. The west wall preserves signs of extensive restoration. The northwest corner encloses processing room 47, accessed through a doorway in the northwest corner with no visible threshold and modern lintel. South of the doorway is a small square window with modern lintel opening to processing room 47. Immediately southeast of the oven is water basin 6416. Along the east wall, extending north of the oven is a corridor (51). Along the east wall are four kneading basins 6412-6415. The floor of the northern half of the room is covered by lapilli. The floor of the southern half of the room is basalt paving slabs enclosing mills 6408-6410. In the southeastern corner a gap in the basalt paving reveals the presence of a fourth, no longer extant, mill. Undecorated plaster survives on the south, north and east walls. In the southeast corner is lararium painting 6411 and adjoining platform 6423 and water basin 6421. At the south end of the west wall, a wide block doorway basalt threshold. Against the base of the wall are two marble fragments and a section of a tufa column shaft.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Rooms 43 and 30 to the south. Room 47 to the northwest. Room 49 to the north.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the elegant dining room, rectangular with a northwest/southeast axis, via a large opening from the southeast. The shortest of the three dining room doors on the peristyle garden. There is a concrete threshold. In 2011, there is a 2X3 foot platform for dramatic presentations. there are speakers. There is a small door on the southwest leading to the next dining room (38). the floor is concrete at this time, any other decoration has disappeared. This is a dining room, has a barrel vault over two thirds of the room and a flat higher ceiling over the other third. Half of the barrel vault shows frescoes. This elegant dado stage with flowers and plants (and birds) is excellent fourth style, the second region continues with primarily black with columns , red and gold and cinnabar and continues to the third register. There is molding where the top wall zone meets the ceiling and where the barrel vault meets the ceiling.

The kitchen is defined as as an open-air garden located in the northwest part of the house in which hallway 5 leading to the garden to the northwest forms two sides. One enters the kitchen from hallway 5 through a small doorway in the north corner. The northeast and southeast is defined by a low wall separating the kitchen garden from hallway 5. In the southeast and northeast walls and in the east corner is a column. In the south corner is a rectangular pillar on a northeast-southwest axis. The columns and pillars support the modern, reconstructed roof covering hallway 5. Embedded in the southeast wall between the central column and rectangular pillar is a puteal covering the mouth of a cistern. In the west corner abutting the northwest and southwest walls is a tall cooking platform defined by superimposed arches. In the northwest wall to the northeast of the cooking platform is a small niche lararium. The floor is indeterminate. The low wall and columns were stuccoed and painted, the southwest walls still showing signs of a garden painting. In the east corner to the west of the gutter is a construction of unknown use that slopes slightly from west to east, opening toward the gutter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden 15 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: A large rectangular dining room runs on a northwest/southeast axis and we enter it from the southwest, which is northeast of the counter room (1). The southeast and northeast walls are preserved to a second story height, while the wall on the northwest slopes from the northeast to the southwest and is lower. Evidence on all walls suggest panels of red and yellow on the lower register and painted white plaster with evidence of some stenciling on the northeast, southeast, and northwest walls. The floor is obscured by lapilli and debris. There is a recess on the northeast wall which suggests a blocked window in antiquity which had been plastered for unknown use. The large doorway from the southwest contains a partial wall on the south side made of brick and covered with plaster painted red. We can see directly into the counter room and possibly into the street from this the doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Counter room (1) to the southwest; processing room (3) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We enter from the southwest and immediately to the northwest is a structure for cooking which consists of two U-shaped segments. This is an unusual structure in that on the southwest side we border the entrance and form the southwest and longer segment. Within this structure, we find a raised tufa stepped like portion which is approximately 20 centimeter high and 30 centimeter deep. On the western corner of the structure is a short pillar which may provide support for a grill. The northeast segment of the structure is a narrow pit/grill and consists of the middle partition to the extreme northeast end of the platform. Bottom of this second tufa segment is the same height and runs parallel to the step portion of the southwest segment. The innermost face of this structure on the northeast is thick and contains some pieces of terracotta tiles on the surface. The long arm which runs southwest/northeast also contains several terracotta tiles on the surface.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation 3172 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We walk into the dining hall in the north corner of the structure from the southwest. There are signs of a marble threshold at the entrance. The entrance is large, old ashlar blocks. The lintels are modern concrete as are the rest of the lintels in the shop-house. It is a dining hall based on its large size and placement. The entrance is very wide. The floor is partial mosaic, which is white tesserae with a black tesserae border. All walls are in place but reconstructed. It has a reconstructed concrete ceiling. The walls show minimal plaster with no color. The dining room views a reported altar which is nearly gone. We can see a portion of the external street corner arch from the dining room. The south side of the southeast wall shows a narrow but high doorway with a threshold which is blocked with a modern grate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The primary entrance to the shop-house is to the northwest. The kitchen is to the southwest. The garden is to the south. A blocked room to the south east is locked and contains modern equipment. The position suggests it is a cubiculum.

DESCRIPTION: The large cooking platform occupies the length of the east wall and abuts the north and south walls. It extends west into the room just short of the entrance. it is approximately 1m deep and 40 cm high. At the back of the structure is an upright stone structure which is approximately 1m high and 20 cm deep. It abuts the northeast wall for the northeast corner and extends midway across the back of the platform. it appears to have been broken. tiny fragments of plaster are visible at the broken portion. moss and debris cover both structures however, a few terracotta tiles remain on both upper and lower surfaces.

Evidence for a latrine is suggested in the east corner of the kitchen. The structure runs along a northeast / southwest axis and at its highest point, which is the northwest partition boundary, is approximately 50 centimeters high eroding to nothing at the west end. The structure abuts the northeast wall and in antiquity probably joined the southeast wall as well. Within this structure are two low parallel pilings of terracotta probably used to support a seat. A small fragment of plaster remains on the northwest face of the structure. The structure is in disrepair.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Cooking platform (3246) to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
The room has a large formal entrance to the Southwest, that is the width of the entire room. The entrance is made of thin marble, seen at ground level with a mosaic floor. The mosaic floor, situated at the entrance has a black geometric design, with a white background. The floor is white tesserae, in the dining area with a black border on 4 sides. The interior to the dining area contains ten individual columns. The two columns, seen at the entrance appear to be attached to large round pilasters.. The fluted columns hold an arch with pseudo ionic columns with traces of yellow paint. Each of the ten individual columns sits on a square base. The square bases are painted with traces of first style in yellow architectural design. At the top of the columns, there is a second level of continuous architrove. the columns define an interior dining area with separate corridors, situated on the North and South sides. the 2 columns situated at the back of the room are centered to the entrance.
There is a varying different geometric mosaic with a white and black pattern seen between the columns. When facing into the dining room, the wall is directly to the right. There are 3 registars. On the bottom register, there are 5 distinct patterns of red paint. The panels on the end are red painted in white is a laurel border possibly of marine life, with a matching panel situated on the other end of the wall.
Next, the two interior side panels are possibly of Dionysis. the statues are sitting on a painted raised platform. The center panel is sacro-idyllic landscape with traces of blue, yellow and white on the background.
The middle register is badly damaged and faded and mainly yellow; it consists of 3 large panels separated by painted architectural of 4th style. The center, damaged top register contains figures. On the left are birds and the center and side panels contain masks and flying figures.
The rear wall is badly damaged and the painting is identical to the wall located on the right sides. The large center panel is too badly damaged to be identified. The wall situated to the left, upon entering the dining room, it's badly damaged and appears to be decorated the same, as the wall situated to the right.
On the entrance, there are semi-attached columns painted the colors of red and yellow. The one situated on the left has a metal curtain hook. The ceiling is reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dining room opens to a significant spectacular view, looking on to the fish pond. The peristyle garden #26 is located to the West.

DESCRIPTION: This space is a kitchen. It is an L-shaped room. All generally on a northwest/southeast alignment. One enters this space through a doorway from the central courtyard (4), and enters the southeast section of the room towards the southern corner of the room. Looking into this space from the doorway one sees the L-shaped area to the right extending toward the northern corner of the house. From the doorway looking toward the right one sees three large blocks in situ which probably formed a cooking platform (3822). This room is in poor condition. The northwest wall preserves painted plaster (yellow) which extends across the northern corner slightly on to the northeast wall. This plaster is mostly at the bottom 4 feet of the wall. However, another patch of plaster is located about 6 to 9 feet above this and reveals a clear horizontal ridge. The partition wall to room 11 is preserved between 3 and 4 feet in height. The other interior walls are from 3 to 7 feet. A high window in the center of the northwest wall may have provided light to the space. No floors are visible. No ceiling exists. Although there is one joist hole in the northern corner of the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of space 9 (courtyard). It is northeast of the entranceway (1) fauces and to space 11.

DESCRIPTION: Sales room 1 is rectangular. It is on a north-south axis. The east wall consists of entrances 12 and 13, separated by a brick column. Both entrances have thresholds of stone and are a small step up from the sidewalk. The brick pillar shows evidence at its west midpoint that the room was apparently divided in two at some pint. The north wall is heavily reconstructed, but contains two holes that may have held a shelf at one point. The northwest corner of the room is open to kitchen 2. The quoining of the threshold consists of brick layers and continues into an all masonry opus concertum wall, again, reconstructed. In the center of the masonry portion of the west wall is a hole, roughly triangular in shape, that may have been a lamp niche or possibly a very small lararium. The south wall is identical to that of the west, but with a potential hole for a floor joist high up. There is no ceiling and the floor is obscured by dirt and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opening to street to the east. Kitchen 6502 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the dining room from the peristyle to the southeast. The room is rectangular in shape on a southeast-northwest axis. In the east corner there is a low doorway to room 39. In the south corner there is a doorway to room 37. The floor as extant slopes slightly on axis southeast to northwest. The floor is a beaten cement, simply decorated with small pieces of white marble. To the northwest the mosaic design is a large square, serving to define the location of the dining couches. The walls and ceilings are decorated in the 4th style. The southeast ceiling, taking up almost a fourth of the room, has three sections. The southwest and northeast sections are arched on a southeast-northwest axis. The center is rectangular in shape on a southeast-northwest axis. The center is rectangular in shape on southeast-northwest axis. The rest of the ceiling to the northwest is at a lower height, and is barrel-vaulted on a southwest-northeast axis. The doorway from the southeast is very wide, extending to almost entire width of room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Peristyle 31 southeast
Dining rooms E (39) , W (37)

DESCRIPTION: Water feature made up of gutter and fountain lies to the northeast of and parallel to the southwest wall of the house on a southeast northwest axis. The gutter is divided into 2 unequal parts by the doorway leading into room 5 to the southwest. The northwest portion, the longest in length, of the gutter has on its northwest end a rectangular basin of unknown function. The portion of the gutter lying to the southeast of the door has at its southeast end what appears to be a fountain with a lead pipe rising vertically in the center. Underneath the fountain lies a drain for the gutter. The interior of the gutter is faced with a waterproof stucco opus signinum.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Furrows to the northeast. Fish pond to the northeast. Triclinium to the northeast. Well to the north.

DESCRIPTION:
Two adjoining water structures lay at the back of masonry couch triclinium to the southwestern side of Space 2. The smaller water structure to the northeast is quasi-square and is delineated by about fifty centimeter high wall. In the eastern corner there are two small rectangular stone structures, the function of which is unclear. The floor is covered by vegetation but stone covering is visible in some parts (especially in the southern corner and by the eastern wall).

The bigger water structure lies to the southwest of the smaller tank (northeastern wall of larger water structure is the southwestern wall of the smaller tank). The water feature is rectangular with the northwestern wall, slightly running outward toward the northwestern corner (angled slightly). The floor is covered with vegetation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Masonry couch triclinium (2733) to the northeast. Cooking platform (2736) lo the northeast hearth (2734) to north water basin (2739) to northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This is a minority report. We enter the dining room from the southeast end of the peristyle portico. It is the final room along the portico in that direction. The threshold is marble. It has a red painted western door entrance in the lower section. We have the same black pavement with white tessera. This is a square room with a large window overlooking a peristyle garden. The window is on the southwest wall. All 4 walls show recent repainting. The lower zone is black with a plant motif. The room's second painted zone shows two pictures, one on the northeast wall, the other on the southeast wall. The northeast wall picture is faded while the southeast wall picture shows Venus and cupid and a male figure. The central zone is blue. On the southeast wall panel to the left we have amorini. The two blue central zone panels framing the window on the southwest wall show amorini. The dining room has a typical barrel vault. There is evidence of a top white zone with architectural features and a peacock.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle portico to the northwest (5). Dining room to north (7) -2862).

DESCRIPTION:
The western part of the room contains a floor of lava basalt blocks. The large mill room contains four mills of varying size and degrees of completeness. A pebble base is seen for all four mills. One mill has only a rubble foundation; two mills have a meta on top. The meta is solid and made of hard porous lava. One mill is complete. We see a lava catillus of hourglass shape with square sockets in place on top of the meta. This mill also has a circular metal fitting to catch the flour. On the North wall there is a door to a storage room. On the North oven wall, there is a deep niche. On the North wall of work area is a portion of plastered area painted white and deep red--27 turquoise tesserae survive- in the form of a snake (?). As in most bakeries there is very little space around the mills for the animals to move. Perhaps the horse in the stable was not used in this work area.
On the North wall close to the entrance to the storage room is a plastered niche. In both corners of the East wall are embedded amphorae making the access of the animal even more difficult.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: none listed.

DESCRIPTION: The dining room's primary axis runs primarily east to west. Its doorway is in the southeast corner which is northwest of the structure's primary entrance. Embedded in the south wall is an Etruscan column whose placement has no bearing on the dining room usage. One third of the column's drums, capital and echinus have been honed/removed so that the column would have been buried in the wall and not visible from this room in antiquity. High on the west wall are seven beam pockets with plaster evidence of a barrel-vaulted plaster ceiling or exedra. Plaster is extant on all the walls. The lower register is red and the upper register is white plaster. The upper register on the north wall is capped with a cornice relief. The room is entered from a raised black lava stone threshold. The floor is of stone rubble. The south wall, west end, contains a large couch niche. Modern restoration has divided the niche in two. The niche is painted in non-discernible red figuring on a yellow ochre background. The south wall contains a window with a sill three meters above the floor. The window was closed by modern restoration/stabilization effort. This is a dining room because of its size and niche. A meta is inside the entryway and is not in situ.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North and west are differing structures/properties. To the south is the atrium and likely a tablinum. To the east is a cubiculi.

DESCRIPTION: Dining room 4 is entered to the north of space 1 and is a fairly square large room. Paint and plaster remain on some of the walls. Doorway is on the south wall and is quite wide with a tufa door sill. Above the door is a small square window. On the east and west walls of the room are located two large holes on each which are paired across from each other and probably held a beam at ceiling height. In addition, ten smaller holes are located on the north wall where joists for an upper story would have been positioned. Lower down at eye height on the north and east walls today are two other indentations that may simply be fallen brick but may also be noteworthy. Floor is lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North wall abuts the adjoining property. The east wall abuts dining room 3 and the west wall abuts dining room 5. The south wall is contiguous to space 1.

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room, one enters through door at the southeast side of the room. The room is almost square. It is in fair condition, although none of the finished floor is preserved. The door jams are crumbling. The walls are preserved to a very high level with full style painting decoration. A large square tableaux has been removed from the center of the northwest wall. Although conserved and patched, two tunnel holes are evident on the northwest wall. The southeast wall on the east side of the door has a tall vertical cut through its center. The northeast wall bulges out above the dado and the dado is slightly concave forming a long couch niche (3893). This room has been conserved with a roof and the upper walls are also restored. Large tableaux are painted on the northeast and southwest walls. The southwest one seems to depict a female holding a helmet, seated with another figure holding a shield. Two putti holding a greave. On the northwest wall there is also a seated female and a warrior holding a large shield. These frescoes maybe Achilles themes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of peristyle area 10. It is southeast of room 7 and to the northeast to room 9.

DESCRIPTION:
The kitchen runs along a northwest/southeast axis and we enter from the fauces to the street (door 22) on the southwest. We enter this room from the northwest through a low partition wall on the southwest. Immediately on the northwest wall as we enter is a lararium which is painted in full style and contains a small altar. Today the lararium is covered with a protective awning. This kitchen is unusual because it contains an enormous archway adjoining the northeast and southwest walls, rising to a second story height at its apex. The facing of the arch as we enter forms the southeast portion of the lararium with painting and is plastered on the street side. Abutting the partition wall on the west corner of the northwest wall is a cooking platform which runs about half the length of this partitioning wall and includes the bottom of the arch. It continues for approximately 6 feet (180 cm) more along the southwest wall. Next to this cooking platform further southeast appears to be an arched drain into the street. The remainder of the room contains rubble on the east corner with roofing tiles and different rocks piled high.
On the southwest wall, high above the cooking platform, is a small light well to the street and another on the southeastern most portion of the wall at the same height. Under the latter are six large joist support holes. Other holes appear on this wall but could be from dislodged stones. The largest of these may have been for an oil lamp in the center of the southwest wall. There is no ceiling extant. Plaster is evident on all walls but there is no evidence of paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Hallway 19 to the west and dining room 15 to the east.

DESCRIPTION:
The peristyle lies in northwest part of the house. One enters the peristyle from andron (86) in the east corner. The peristyle is rectangular in shape on a northwest - southeast axis. On northwest side in the west corner is dining hall (35). To the northeast next to dining hall are rooms 36 and 37. To northeast of these rooms is triclinium 38. In north corner is dining room 39. In north corner of northeast wall is a door that has been closed up in antiquity. On southeast side in east corner is andron 26. To the southwest is room 25, followed by 32, then rooms 33 and 34 in the south corner. In the center is a rectangular open peristyle on a northeast - southwest axis and is defined by doric columns, 3 on the northwest side, 4 on northeast side, 2 on southeast side. The southwest wall has 5 engaged columns, for a total of 14 columns. The garden area in the center has, on northwest, northeast and southeast sides, a stone gutter. The southeast gutter has a drain hole in south corner of southwest wall. On southwest side, running northwest-southeast, is a walkway made up of 2 rows of flat stones running the width of the garden. Jashemski (1979) found evidence that the garden contained citron, fig and olive trees.
The columns support a roof, creating a covered portico on the northwest, northeast and southeast sides. High on walls of all 4 sides, covered by the portico, is a series of paintings of different subjects. Below on the second register is a series of large rectangular sections, with small vignettes in the center. The lowest register on all 4 sides bears paint but no figured representation. Around the portico at roof level on the northwest and northeast sides are gutters with lion head spouts. Those on the southeast side appear to be modern. Columns, with exception of 3 on southwest side, are painted gold on the lower half and white on the upper part.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Andron (26) to east, dining hall (35) to west, (25) to the southeast, (32) to the south , (33) to the south, (34) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: Room 7 is accessible from the Northeast from room #4. The entrance extends along the whole width of the room. The square room walls were painted: there are traces of red painting on the Northwest and Southwest walls along with plaster fragments on the same wall. The floor is covered with vegetation, debris, and heaps of soil. In the Northwest corner toward the entrance rests a 30 centimeter high block of stone which doesn't appear on the floor plan of the building. It probably doesn't belong to the room. The Northwest and Southwest walls are preserved to 2 meters. The Southeast wall is preserved to the four meters high roof which is difficult to discern if it is ancient or modern. The ceiling is not extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 is to the Northeast. Room 20 is to the Northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular garden containing an L-shaped masonry dining couch in northwest corner. According to Eschebach there is a storage niche under the north couch and a drain into a large pool in center of garden. A masonry table apparently stood next to the north couch; not visible due to cover of vegetation. A plaster-lined lararium niche is in the northwest corner above couch. Red background, blue plaster ceiling and traces of plaster molding found on the rear wall. No other decorative elements survive.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Corridor to west (room 5). Dining room to west (room 6). Kitchen to south (room 8). Unknown room to south (room 9). Corridor to west (room 5). Dining room to west (room 6). Kitchen to south (room 8). Unknown room to south (room 9). Features 1712, 1713.

DESCRIPTION: Small brick built altar with step in front. Built into undecorated recess. Plain plaster survives on north side of recess, top surface of altar and side of altar. No other decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: The masonry triclinium is room 17. It takes up the entire southern part of the room. The lectus sumus is along the eastern wall. The lectus medium is along the southern wall. The lectus imus is along the western wall. In the middle, among the three lectii, is a cylindrical shaped masonry table. On the inside of the lecti, surrounding the table, is a low platform. The northern ends of the lectus imus and sumus are defined by a bench that slopes toward the east and west walls respectively. To the north of these sloping walls are L-shaped benches. The branch of the benches, parallel and abutting the walls, are at the level of the back of the lecti. The benches that are perpendicular to the walls are at a level below that of the front of the lecti. At the northern end of the low bench on the western wall is a large preparation platform. The low bench parallel to the east wall has, at floor level, a drain opening leading to the garden (room 18). The floor of the room in this area seems to slope slightly toward the drain. The facades of the perpendicular platform, lecti, table and benches are elaborately painted in vegetation, birds and other shrubs. The walls on the east, south and west walls are likewise painted in red but without figural motifs. The red paint extends up 82 centimeters above the bench. Above that the paint seems to have been yellow or gold. As reconstructed the wall on the eastern side rises 134 centimeters from the top of the bench. There are two pillars rising higher to support the ceiling thereby creating two large rectangular windows along the eastern wall of the triclinium. The floor seems to be cocciopesto.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (room 18) is to the east. Garden (room 18) is to the east. None

DESCRIPTION: On the southwest wall in the center of a large panel formed by two thin decorated columns, is a rectangular painting on a northwest to southeast axis showing a scene from a drinking party (Greek symposium?). Four individuals, two men and two women, lie on couches. To the left of and behind the couch stands a woman with her head covered by a scarf, holding a cup in her right hand. She seems to be supported by a slave behind her. Behind appears to be a doorway. This woman may either be herself drunk and supported by a slave, or she may be a matron astonished by what she sees having just entered the room. The center couple recline on their left elbows; both gesture towards the veiled woman. The man, however, looks toward the couple to his left. The male member of this couple gestures with his right had towards the veiled woman. The female reaches out with her right hand and removes the lid from a glass cup on the table belonging to the other couple. Each couch has its separate tripod table. The table to the left is more delicate and appears to have feet shaped like deer hooves. The other table is shorter, thicker and heavier with feet shaped like lion paws. Both tables support cups and ladles.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Floor below. Painting (3105) to the northwest. Painting (3105) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room with a southwest/northeast axis. The main entrance is on the northeast side and is a wide opening with a view to the garden. there is a small door at the eastern end of the southeast wall. no flooring is visible. All walls preserve remains of frescoes in Pompeiian fourth style. A decorated black dado surrounds the room with a horizontal line of fruit and other decorative patterns. The frescoes on the side half of the southeast wall preserve a large yellow panel to the southern corner and with a large winged victory in the center and with a small cow above. Above this yellow panel is a square panel with a window view of the architecture beyond. The panels to the east of this have an architectural scene of a doorway below a panel of more architecture. Above the doorway are three shields. The frescoes on the southwest wall are best preserved along the bottom and sides. The side panels above the dado each show a large yellow panel with a concave edged blue rectangle. Within the rectangles portrait tondos are evident. On the northwest wall, the bottom and sides of the frescoes are preserved. A large central panel may have been removed. The western half of this wall preserves a painted niche (3190). Also on the western end of the wall is a yellow panel with a winged figure with three dead ducks suspended below (3192). At the northern end of the northwest wall the fresco includes fruit (possibly grapes) from a basket, a boar, and three dead ducks suspended with ribbon. A second niche is on the south end of the southeast wall (3193). The niches extend the room for couches. High on the northwest and southeast walls is a raised plaster molding. There is a lot of modern restoration along the edges of the frescoes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a garden (number?) to the northeast. There is an atrium (number?) to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: Entrance is off a walled garden (dining, 18) in the western wall. Doorway to small rectangular room with a painted storage room door on the western wall. Slightly barreled ceiling. Plastered walls and the plaster is cream colored. On the south wall are two great snakes arched above an altar with a pine cone burning on the altar. The larger snake is crested and bearded and is yellow with red scales and sharp forked tongue. The crest and beard are red. The female snake can be seen from head to tail. The burning sacrifice may include fruit, cakes and nuts. The snakes are surrounded by garlands and ribbons. There is a high window on the outside wall and a spherical stone that looks like an omphalos is on the top of a broken column on the floor. Below the window and in front of the storage room. Floor is mostly obscured by debris but parts show a polychrome marble chips.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (18) to the west. Garden (18) to the west. None

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis. A modern ceiling with an earth floor. The areas of the room are obscured by usage as storage for roof tiles. The upper courses of the walls are restored. Plaster survives at the base of the east, south and west walls. The plaster in the south and southwest corners shows white with a red trim. In the southeast corner there is a wide doorway with a plastered masonry threshold and a modern lintel leading to room #25. in the southwest corner, there is a blocked plastered cupboard niche. From earlier phase. The ceiling is modern reconstruction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room #25 to the east. Room #25 to the east. None

DESCRIPTION: Podium in rear with nearby stone water basin. Lararium on east wall in southeast corner. Staircase midway along west wall (stairs leading to south). Stone bases for arch that support stairs still in place to the south. Stone threshold is preserved all across front of shop. Door on west side. No indication of sales counter but this could have had wooden counter like the one depicted of the baker selling bread. A piece of a mill stone seems to be set in the northeast corner of shop.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room with plaster and paint visible on three walls. Opens to west. Couch niches on two walls are very evident (north and south). Wide entrance to west overlooks the garden area. Do the niches in the north and south walls represent where couches of the triclinium are inserted? If so, does that mean that this was necessary in order to get arrangement of three sofas into this room, (was the room too narrow? And was it necessary to add these niches? Does this represent a room a little less than standard size for a triclinium?
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Adjacent to rooms 4 and 7. Adjacent to rooms 4 and 7. None

DESCRIPTION: Room number identification is in plan by Lehman-Hartleben. Room is on lower level on south corner of the upper peristyle. It is down a half level below the kitchen and storerooms. The rear north wall and east is preserved and springing of the vaulting remains in place for almost the entire length of the east wall. Some painted plaster remains on the vault but it is badly faded. Has some indication of geometric borders. Wall on the west side is only partially preserved, not to the height of springing of the vault. No plaster on the west wall. Room is filled with debris and floor level cannot be seen. Room's southern outer limit has collapsed but it does have a brick pier. No clear indication of rear extent of room remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Level, fairly high above what had been a blank area inside city wall. Wall had to be used as fortification, at least as late as social war, the "impressive" thing is that so much fill had accumulated before the structure was built (3m). Garden - read Bradford with respect to amount of protective plastic around site would indicate excavations not complete and could be coming back this summer. The north corner of the triclinium is a an "opus signinum" lined channel runs to the west wall of room. Closer proximity of the triclinium to edge of the pool. Vann reports they are not contemporary uses. On north wall above triclinium on central axis are traces of a removed "painting".

DESCRIPTION: The room has two entrances. The one to the north is the largest and faces the garden (7). The other entrance is smaller and leads down on to the atrium (2) through two steps. Adjoining this entrance is a long rectangular window. There is small window high up on the west wall. Fragments of plaster remain on the wall but no traces of decoration remain. The floor mosaic remains. In the center is an emblem with a black and white square panel surrounded by geometric band of white tesserae. The central emblem is framed by one strand of guilloche and a band of vegetable motifs spreading out of a crater. The emblema contains a grid poised square in opus sectile. Around that is an octagonal pattern of interesting octagonals, forming oblong hexagonals. Irregular shaped squares of multicolored marble are inlaid in a geometric band. The door jams remain between which is a threshold mat of black and white geometric design. The garden (7)facing the dining room is decorated with a hunting scene among wild animals (boars, panther, bulls and gazelles) on the north wall. On the northeast wall is a landscape painting containing small human figures, but is too damaged to identify the scenes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (7) to north. Atrium (2) to south. Andron (10) to the east. Garden (7) to north. Atrium (2) to south. Andron (10) to the east. None

DESCRIPTION: Small rectangular room with a stone step underneath a single doorway which leads to a second portion of the room. This second portion consists of a large divided stone wall. The use of this area is uncertain. The planks on the bottom of this squared area is reasonably modern but older than the wooden and tile roofing atop it. Lindley believes that only the lower portion of the two flanking walls is ancient because there is modern mortar patching above it. This leads to an uncertainty as to how high the flanking walls actually were. The ancient mortar height goes against speculation that this is where the cooking platform was.* Lindley wants the ancient mortar sealing in southwest corner to be measured from ground up. The main portion of kitchen has a sealed window on the southern end of the west wall. There is also a horizontal array of post holes indicating a second story. There are a few remnants of plaster on eastern and western wall. There is another entrance, also with a step leading into the second portion of the room (with the alcove) which looks out onto open-air courtyard (11)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Located north of the latrine (15); west of room 13; northwest of open-air courtyard (11). Located north of the latrine (15); west of room 13; northwest of open-air courtyard (11). None

DESCRIPTION: The storage room, where carts could be brought in, was located on the second (lower) level on the southeast side of the house. The entrance from the street, which divides I.6 and I.7, is very wide. Someone entering the room would need to step up two steps but carts could be brought in with a ramp provided. Above the doorway is a large rectangular window to provide light. The room is oriented on a southeast/northwest axis. It is vaulted the entire length. On the southwest wall, near the northwest end, is a doorway leading into room 8L and the rest of the house. On the southwest wall, just to the left of the street entrance is a doorway leading into room 10L and two more rooms behind it. The walls were plastered in antiquity; but if it was decorated nothing remains. On the west wall to the back (rear) of the room, toward the southwest, appears to have been a quarter circle window. (This window may be modern.) In the ceiling, approximately 70% of the way back to the rear (west) end of the room is what appears to be a large light well though at present it is blocked to the floor above. In the west wall, in the southwest corner, at floor level, is a drain which seems to drain from the peristyle (room 14) above. A gutter, which runs the entire length of the southwest wall, appears to empty into the street but there is no evidence for it.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 8L to the northwest. 10L to the northwest. 8L to the northwest. 10L to the northwest. None

DESCRIPTION: The shop is to the west of the House of Stephanus entrance. The shop opens to the north into the Via del Abbondanza. At the front of the shop on the west side is an L shaped counter. The one side of the counter takes about 1/2 of the doorway, while the second half of the counter, although no longer present, would extend into the shop. At the rear on the east side of the shop is a tall doorway leading into the atrium of the house. This doorway also has slots in the threshold to close the shop off from the remainder of the house. On the south wall is a doorway leading into what may have been a storeroom for the shop. On the west wall, above the level of the counter and a little to the south, is a large lararium. The walls of the shop were painted, but very little remains today. The front entrance to the shop still retains its threshold with the slots used to close off the entire width of the entrance during the night. High on the west and east walls are holes that may have supported beams. In the middle of the east wall, accordingly to Eschebach, where were steps which may have lead to a loft supported by the beams. The floor appears to be a beaten floor. Inside the shop entrance approximately 40% into the shop seems to be a stone which appears to have a cutting to seat something such as a wooden pole, its function is unknown.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

There are three slabs of volcanic rock covering two thirds of the shelf. Behind the shelf is the square opening into the oven. There is brick facing on front of structure except for on top. There about one third is just rocky material. There is a small rectangular opening on the south side of the front wall. On the ground in front of the front of the south side is an L-shaped group of masonry rocks. On the north side there of the structure there is a large rectangular opening

DESCRIPTION: Room 3 is a large peristyle. The central courtyard of this peristyle may be divided into two unequally sized spaces by two larger pilasters which show a rarely decorative feature: two semicircular semi-columns enjoining two square semi-pillars. In the modern description of this open area these two pilasters are said to have supported a pergola shading the northeastern section of the courtyard. On the northwest wall there is evidence of plaster. The courtyard of the peristyle is framed by bricked columns resting on a low wall. The northeast section of the courtyard which is said to be covered by a pergola contains the altar for sacrifice. On the top of the northwest and southwest walls are rows of joist holes. The nine remaining holes on the northwestern wall are equidistant and could have supported the roof of the peristyle porticus. The eight remaining joist holes on the southwestern wall are more irregular in shape and distance between each other. (The southwestern section of room 3 has been recorded in a Minority Report as Room 15. See Minority Report for more detail.) The central open space of the peristyle is covered by vegetation (bushes, trees, and grass) while the surrounding porticus is covered with lapilli. The area containing the altar faces the main entrance to 2.1.12 (room 1).

DESCRIPTION: As the excavation has not been fully carried out, Room 6 will be described as a large single unit, although scattered traces of walls show that this space was divided into smaller spaces. In fact, on the northwestern side, opposite Room 4 (dining room), there is evidence of a low wall framed by five columns which seem to belong to the peristyle. A number of huge dolia have been found in this space; however, as they are mostly not embedded it is difficult to locate them to a specific space. Three medium sized dolia rest on the ground to the northwest. They are mostly well preserved. The rim of two dolia are half preserved. In the middle of what appears to be the central courtyard of the peristyle (close to the northwest colonnade wall) there is evidence of a huge embedded dolium but only the base of the dolium is preserved. In the southwestern corner six big dolia are mostly embedded in the construction of a modern wall above which are some casts of victims on display. For what is visible today they are in very good condition. Two dolia still show their huge rims. More dolia are visible in the eastern corner; however, as they are in a fragmented state it is difficult to ascertain if they were embedded (like the small fragments in the middle of this corner suggest) or resting against the wall (like two broken halves of dolia appear today). The northeastern wall of this corner shows traces of painting on the lower zone while a low wall in the eastern side suggests the perimeter of this space. This L-shaped space of this entire room is situated on a northwest/northeast axis. The two walls bounding this room to the northeast and southwest are preserved to first story height. The northeast wall is framed by supporting pillars and shows some traces of painting. Three of the dolia show signs of repair along the bodies of the containers. It is debatable if they are modern or ancient repairs.

DESCRIPTION:
One enters the dining room over a threshold constructed of volcanic rocks. The room is basically squre and is located around a NE/SW axis. Evidence of 4th style painting is apparent on all walls. Yellow, red, white and green colors survive. The panels are delineated with stenciling and 3-D views on the NW and SE walls and below the large window on the N.E. wall which looks into the garden ( ). In the East corner, the wall juts out slightly and receeds back into the S.E. wall at a smoothed right angle which looks like a faux column which has been decorated. The lower register of the walls was painted white with red borders and framing of sorts of various flowers. the Afore-mentioned middle panels contain both architectural and stenciled segments and vague facial cameos can be discerned with 5 circular outlines that are visible, and perhaps a 6th, at a 1.5m level on the 4 walls. the upper register of the walls were decorated in antiquity with both a lower plaster cornice and an upper highly decorative moulding. The portion between the 2 moulding sections were painted with red borders and evidence on the N.W. wall indicates a blue stripe as well. The ceiling was painted in antiquity as is evidenced with extant red paint in the S.W. corner. Above the upper cornice on the S.E. wall are 6 holes for support while only 2 can be seen on the N.W. wall. The ceiling has been restored above the ancient level. The floor appears to have been cement and contained chips of white marble and red rock. In the East corner, today, remains a portion of a column base or capital.
The lower register on the West and South of the S.W. wall may have been black in color.

DESCRIPTION: House of CC Cuspii Pansa and Proculus. The work area is called a kitchen but is unique because it includes a large enclosed oven with evidence of a large preparation room and a possible kneading area. The oven is good shape and shows no evidence of restoration. The attributes associated with the oven are the water basin, the preparation room and the possible kneading room. There are no mills, or though there is a catillus in the preparation room to the southwest of the oven and a catillus in the peristyle. The large enclosed oven has a projecting brick faced arch which accompanies a rectangular ash pit and a rectangular opening. There is no iron grill to cover the baking entrance. The interior of the beehive oven features a square shaped recess that currently does not go through to the southwest wall. There are basalt stones framing the oven opening and basalt stones supporting the arch over the oven entrance facade and a basalt floor in the entrance to the oven and inside the oven. To our surprise we see a small arched opening to the northeast of the oven with no floor at the base of the arch, but has a floor at the base of the oven. The small arched opening to the northeast of the oven opening requires additional study. In the oven there is a passage way to the preparation room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water basin feature 28-3148

You are struck by the coolness of the kitchen. The kitchen is of a good size but suitable for a house this size. The kitchen has an elaborate large cooking platform on the southwest wall abutting the southeast and southwest walls. Above the cooking platform is a smoke hole and a sky light opening. The sky light opening above the southeast wall. There is a mid height northwest southeast wall separating a latrine from the cooking platform area. Above the latrine is a sky light opening in the southeast wall at ceiling level that has been blocked in antiquity. The cooking are is very spacious. On the northwest wall near the entrance is a rectangular block of stone abutting the wall. The low block of stone may have served as a preparation platform.

DESCRIPTION: We enter dining room 3 from the southeast. The room, which is slightly rectangular, runs along a northwest/southeast axis. On the north, west, and south walls we find remains of painted plaster which was yellow and possibly white in antiquity. In the west corner of the room where the north and west walls converge, pieces of plaster cornice which have been molded and decorated with blue and red paint and ornate pattern, show a division of upper and lower wall space. In the same area we find evidence of red borders which run parallel and perpendicular to the cornice. The walls have been restored to first story height as have the ceiling and floor. Modern equipment and decoration fill the room. There is a hearth and sink on the south and east side. High in the west wall is a small tiny window and centered on the east wall is a modern window which looks into the garden in the pseudoperistyle. The entrance to the room has modern doors which can be locked and both windows have shutters and screens as well.
