There are eight beam pockets along the south wall for a second story that is not extant. There is a stair/platform in the southeast corner of the room. There is evidence of modern tuck pointing on the south wall. The east wall is of opus incertum with a two-stepped entrance to Room 3. The entrance to Room 3 is of opus mixtum. There is one beam pocket extant on the east wall. There is minimal plaster extant. There is a low register in red. The north wall is of opus mixtum and it has a door opening north to storeroom 6219. This is a salesroom because of street frontage, a wine press found in Room 3 and size.

DESCRIPTION: The U-shaped counter, located within the counter room contains 6 dolia of which 2 are inserted into the west arm opening to the street, and 4 on the south arm opening to the fauces 1, with a small hearth jutting out off the south arm. The counter is constructed of masonry with a marble top. On the west arm the exterior face of the counter is also covered with marble fragments. The counter as a whole has received extensive restoration efforts, but it is still possible to note that the marble has been reused here, possibly a sill. This consists of various types of marble. On the west arm, two dolia are present with rims missing, and the east side of the west arm has collapsed so that it is possible to see a roof tile (modern) inserted into the masonry. The four dolia located on the south arm are also missing rims, but within each hole fragments of terracotta dolia are visible. The small hearth located at the east arm's end is a small U-shaped insertion into the counter. A terracotta surface of the counter is visible inside the hearth.

DESCRIPTION:
One enters the triclinium from corridor (5) by way of a small doorway in the west corner. Most of the room is taken up by a masonry triclinium. There probably was not a ceiling to the room hence open-air. The floor is at a lower level than corridor (10), and is of beaten cement with fragments of terra cotta. The lower part of the southwest, southeast, and northeast walls have a lower register in red and on top a black band. the upper register is unknown because the plaster is no longer extant or the paint is gone. The northwest wall is defined by a low wall in the center of which is a tall painted rectangular column on a southwest/northeast axis. Its placement is slightly off-center to the northeast in relation to the triclinium.

In the west corner abutting the southwest wall is a rectangular platform on a northwest/southeast axis. In the middle of the southwest wall is a large window opening onto room (10). most likely into a cistern in Room (2). In the west corner to the southeast of the platform, there is a drain in a southwest direction that seems to lead under room (10). Along the base of the southwest wall is a gutter that leads from this drain towards the southeast where in the south corner a drain leads to the outside of the house. The floor southeast to the northeast such that rain water would flow southeast to northwest. The rectangular column in the northwest wall is pointed on all four sides. At the top on all four sides is a garland On the southeast side clearly visible to diners is a large human figure garlanded man with a right hand raised holding some sort of staff in his left hand and appearing to be walking. On the southwest side is another human figure seemingly standing on a pedestal. His dress is foreign (eastern), and he is holding up the lower portion of his tunic with both hands, displaying his erect phallus. On the northeast side just below the garland are two figures. Below the garland is a lyre. Below the lyre is a large black bird standing on a cage. On the northwest side below the garland are two cornucopia flanking what appears to be a caduceus.

The fountain stands in the middle of the masonry triclinium. The fountain, which is somewhat cylindrical, flares out to a wider base where it rests on a marble-covered floor. This floor, along with the fountain, is delineated by a marble band on all four sides. At the bottom of the southwest marble band, almost in the middle, is evidence of a drain pipe. The location of this pipe at the bottom of the marble recessed floor, along with the hole piercing the top center of the fountain, suggests that the whole central area of the masonry triclinium was decorated with a fountain in the middle of a rectangular pool. However, as it is not possible to verify the water system of this area, the high marble structure which has been described as a fountain might have been used as a support for a table instead.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Three couches to the southwest, northwest and northeast. Garden to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The triclinium is an elaborate masonry triclinium with pergola and two mosaic fountains. The triclinium is located in the northwest corner of the Dining Garden Peristyle. It faces east. The medius is 4.5m, immus 4.2 and summis 3.55 (Jashemski). At the end of the summus one can see a white painted stucco. The bottom part shows the typical painted garden fence and the top part is gone. There is a large rectangular center table with a pipe coming up out of the center. This triclinium shows 13 aedicular arched recesses. The triclinium shows the typical slopes. There is a wall surrounding the south, west, and north sides of the triclinium. Jashemski shows this wall as a low masonry wall with space for plants. There are four round columns, one at each corner, that would have supported a pergola. There is evidence of stucco on the west column. To the northeast and southeast in front of the triclinium are two large ornate fountains. The dominant tesserae colors are white, deep blue, light blue, coral, and green. At the back of each fountain are stairs that go to the top. Jashemski reports that Stephano DeCaro that the steps led to the reservoirs. The fountains are almost duplicates of each other. The north facade will be described. It has a large niche in a rectangular block that has a pediment at the top. There is a rectangular pool area in front of each fountain. The large arched niche contains a smaller niche with a protruding marble shelf. The north fountain still contains a center water pipe coming up through the bottom. The interior niche contains shells with outlining in green and red tesserae, Both fountains, beneath the small niche, show two ducks and two fish. At the top of the large niche is a flying swan, clearly 4th style. At the middle zone of the fountain are two green jumping dolphins. The shells are everywhere on the facade, probably modern restoration. The north water fountain contains a small circular marble table, which may or may not have been there originally. On the east facade of the north fountain we see remains of a garden painting with evidence of a garden fence done in pink and gold, and a large crater outlined above the fence. On the west side of the facade we see the fence again. The large crater outlined in yellow shows blue water within the crater. Remnants of the same garden painting are evident on the south fountain but are less visible. The fountains are covered by a plastic roof. The triclinium is uncovered.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous other features: Altar (3046) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular atrium is located along a north/south axis. From entrance 19 to the east Eschebach says there was a mosaic impluvium that is shown on the plan; however no trace remains (2012). In the southeast corner there is a rectangular preparation platform (6156). Traces of plaster floor survive in the southwest corner of the south wall, and in the center of the west wall against the entrance to room 19. Traces of plaster may survive in front of the preparation platform. Stone thresholds may survive for doorway (room 23), and fauces (room 25)on the kitchen side. In the northwest corner three masonry steps lead up to room 12. The remainder of the floor is obscured by lapilli. Undecorated plaster with upper and lower register survives on the south wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 23, 24, 25, 26 and 27 are to the east. Rooms 16, 17, and 12 are to the north and rooms 19, 20, and 21 are to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
The preparation room's long axis is venally west east.
The room is entered through the north wall at the northwest corner over a stone threshold. The threshold is carved to indicate door panels such that one could secure the room.
The west wall has a pass through of opus mixtum to the oven platform/mouth of oven. The west wall is prominently of opus incertum with very little white plaster extant at its southerly edge.
The south wall of opus incertum with some white plaster extant in a low red plaster register half a meter tall. On the eastern edge of the south wall are found four, possibly five, supports for two, possibly three, shelves.
Five pock hole sexist in the south wall that do not seem to be shelf supports or shrines but would seem to be a deteriorated wall construction.
The east wall has a window to the street with a sill two meters high. The wall is opus incertum with the upper third in opus mixtum, probably reconstructed in antiquity. There is some white plaster extant.
The north wall is of opus incertum with opus mixtum at the entrance opening. There is some white plaster extant.
The floor is stone marble with vegetation. On the west wall are what appear to be three beam pockets, possibly for stair supports. The special configuration of the room, does not support these being for
a staircase.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill room is to the north, the oven to the west, a different property to the south and the street is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a very large ceramic vessel. The lower wall rises almost vertically from the flat bottom. The shoulder is carinated. The rim flares and turns inward for a flat horizontal lip with a wide opening. The upper portion including the shoulder to the rim is broken and missing several pieces. Approximately one third of rim survives. No extant repairs are visible. The interior is filled with lapilli and not visible. The dolium is half embedded in the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is the third dolium from the southern corner. Dolia (3212 and 3211) to the southwest, dolia (3214 an 3215) to the northeast. Cistern 3217 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: Spanning the west wall of the kitchen (12) is a brick cooking platform with a cement top, probably reconstructed. On the north end of the top, spanning about one third of the total top distance is a built up hearth with arched wood storage underneath. The hearth is a a cube shape also made of terracotta brick with a cement top. The platform appears to have been heavily restored.

This is a dolium. It is a very large ceramic vessel. The lower wall slightly flares from the flat bottom. The shoulder is carinated. The rim flares and turns inward for a flat horizontal lip and wide opening. It is almost complete although it is cracked in pieces on the southern side and the rim is broken and missing several sections. This rim has undergone extensive repairs. At least seven cracks have been repaired with metal staples covered with a pink plaster. One section is replaced in concrete and is badly broken missing all of the lip. There is an inscription on the flat edge of the rim at the west side. This is not clearly legible although it appears to be a numeric designation for the capacity of the vessel. This dolium is half embedded in the southeast wall. The interior is filled with lapilli and not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is second from the south corner in the line of 5 dolia along the south east wall. (3214 and 3215 to the northeast, 3212 and 3211 to the southwest) Cistern 3217 to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: The room's primary axis is west to east and entered from the street over a raised stone threshold. Carving in the stone threshold is not evident. The north wall is opus incertum with the upper two-thirds of modern construction. The lower corner of the north wall has a passthrough slot to the property to the north and does not appear to be from antiquity. The west wall is of opus incertum. Tufa ashlar blocks are at the entrance and appear to be all modern reconstruction. The south wall is of opus incertum from antiquity with modern tuck pointing. The east wall is of opus incertum. The top two-thirds of the wall appears to be modern reconstruction. Minimal plaster is extant in the northeast corner of the room. The color is red. The floor is stone rubble. There is a heavily reconstructed platform (6234) is in the northeast corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: A differing structure/property is to the north and east. Rooms 2 and 3 (cubicula) are to the south and the street is to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular room. East west axis. Floor obscured by lapilli throughout. Doorway in the center of the south wall to 14. No visible threshold. Blocked doorway from earlier phase at the west end of the south wall. Fragments of plaster survive on the south wall. Extensive fragments of plaster on the north wall with pink hue. Plaster survives extensively on the east wall divided into two sections but with no discernible decorations. At the top of the east wall a painted plaster cornice with red trim survives along the entire edge of the east wall indicating that this had a high ceiling (no ceiling extant). At the east end of the south wall there are two holes into the wall. The function is unclear. Maybe collapsed and plastered over.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 14 is to the south

DESCRIPTION: The dining tablinum is oriented generally on a N/S axis. The room can be viewed directly from the structures primary south entrance and through the peristyle garden and from the street. North, east and west walls are of Opus Incertum with evidence of reconstruction and a 1976 reconstruction plaque is in the north wall. Some plaster is extant in the northeast and northwest corners or the room. Room's primary entrance is on the south wall with a secondary entrance in the southeast corner of the room. No sign of windows, jams or threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is contiguous to the peristyle garden on the south. To the east is the repositories and anti room. To the north is another structure / property, situated to the west is room 10.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the storage room from the northeast. This room runs along a northwest/southeast axis. It is located under the stairs and it is a irregular room in that there is a large threshold like step up and down to a lower level under the stairs. On the northwest side of this lower part the ceiling of this room angles at 45 degrees under modern stairs. There is a modern lintel which delineates the angled space. This portion of the room appears to have been plastered with cement and is obscured with ash on the floor. The upper and main portion of the store room contains four holes, two above two lower, probably for shelf support. This holes are in a plastered, nicely painted wall of orange and white with red vertical lines. There are red borders that form panels. The ceiling in this portion of the room is formed by modern stairs, forming a flat roof. On the south wall is a large window or light well which has a modern wooden lintel inserted and lined with lead. It is about 3 x 3 feet (100 x 100 cm approx.). There is a portion of a small partition on the west side of the northwest wall. Today large pieces of plaster and marble are on hte floor in a pile. Note, on the northwest wall, there is a gap in the plaster, which may have indicated an enclosure and another one above the partition on the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 7 to the north

DESCRIPTION:
We enter the kitchen from a door on the southeast wall. Abutting the southeast wall and north wall is a large cooking platform with two arched recesses underneath. The outer facing of the front (South) is made of brick which was faced with plaster painted red as evidenced on the lower southern corner. Also the northern face of the platform is still also entirely faced with red plaster. The cooking platform is in relatively good repair. The floor surrounding the cooking platform creates an "L" for the remaining space which would allow greater access to the platform surface. Underneath the moss covered floor seems to be beaten cement which continues under both recesses and covers most of the room.
All walls are preserved to a second story height. On the northern wall are two hole approximately 5 feet (150 cm) from the ground on either end of the wall, which probably provided shelf support. Traces of red painted plaster covers all the wall on the northeast and southwest. beam holes appear high, four on the northeast, eight on the southwest. On the northeast wall above these holes is one much larger hole. On southeast wall there is a square window with a wooden lintel and plastered sill. There is no ceiling extant. A modern wooden lintel is over the doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 8 to the southwest

DESCRIPTION: As part of the kitchen area, we see a beautiful lararium. We see two-thirds of a semicircular water holder. There is a red cinnabar border of approximately five foot by six foot. It is cream in color with an unknown rectangle in the center. We see gardens, lares (possible Augustus with a cornucopia). There are two sedate lares with their tunics, shawls, brown skin, black hair holding rhytons and situla (cups). There is indication of wine being poured from the rhyton to the situla on each lares figure. The northwest lar seems feminine in her features? In the center of the ground line, there is an offering on the altar which attracts the snake with some red flames and perhaps the outline of an egg. The snake's head is above the altar and it's tail is in the lower east corner. In the lower southwest, there are two figures. The figure nearest the altar wears a red palea, covering head and shoulders and blue underneath. She offers a patera with both hands. The figure on the southwest is taller and could be the ancestor, master of the house or Augustus holding a cornucopia with a conical object and two pieces of fruit. The central figures are approximately one half the size of the lares. On the ground line, knee level of the lar, we see a small figure with dual Pan pipes and on the other side there is probably a slave holding a platter in one hand and one or two fish in the other. Below the ground line, the features and details of the snake become more intricate. There are undulating plants beneath the altar, including a couple of irises. There are other leaves and iris plants in the cinnibar and lighter orange with much green foliage.

Entered from doorway 21 at rear end of house. The kitchen is on a northeast/southwest axis. In the center of the room, abutting the north wall to store room 12 are two masonry supports for a cooking platform. At the northeast end of the room adjacent to both storeroom 12 and the exterior door is a latrine which gives the room an "L" shape. There is a raised threshold in doorway 21, and a window above the latrine opening out into the street. Little plaster remains on the walls giving no evidence of decoration. Areas of the wall show signs of modern repair. Floor slopes to street outside door 21 but is rubble.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is at south east end of house directly entered off of street Via Della Fullonica. Storeroom 12 is completely within the room and the southwest doorway opens to pergola 9.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Cindy. Mosaic on wall in the latrine area approximately 3 1/2 meters above latrine. See comments for feature 6135

DESCRIPTION: This water basin is located in southwest wall immediately south of the entrance to room 4. It is embedded in a stone platform. The form of this platform is rounded on its northeast side. The embedded ceramic vessel appears to be a wide mouth jar with a side flaring to flat lip. This vessel is complete except for a small chip in the rim. Ancient repairs are seen on 4 large cracks. Two of these repairs have visible metal staples and all have buff colored fine plaster covering. Most of the vessel is not visible because it is filled with gravel. The platform is topped with plaster and stands almost a meter high.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Water basin 3219 and lararium 3233 to the northwest; oven 3197 to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: Square room, wide open doorway center of south wall with marble step threshold and placings for a door. In the east and west corner of the south wall are small doorways with same step threshold and placings for doors. Opening south to peristyle 32. At the south end of the east wall there is a doorway with marble threshold, with placings for door and modern lintel. At the north end of the east wall is a doorway to bedroom 39 with marble threshold, placing for doors and modern lintel. At the southern end of west wall a doorway with marble threshold, placing for doors and modern lintel. At the north end of the west wall, doorway to room 37, marble threshold, placing for door and modern lintel. White mosaic floor survives throughout with black border with black border with a marble central diamond-patterned rosette. Extending along the north, west and east walls are ten Corinthian columns constructed of brick and plaster contiguous with the columns and extending along the southern face of the room to form a border for the entire room is a mosaic pattern in white, yellow, red, green and black tesserae in a 3-D geometric pattern. Extensive plaster decoration survives on the north, east and west walls, with second, third style decoration of architectural elements and theatrical mask. Ceiling reconstructed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Rooms 40 and 39 to the east.
Rooms 37 and 36 to the west.
Room 32 to the south.

DESCRIPTION: On the floor on the southwest wall is a round opening in a square stone, raised shape, very low platform that perhaps goes to cistern or is deep basin for water. It is adjacent to a preparation platform and directly below niche that connects to a water pipe.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Preparation platform 6405 to the east. Water feature 6422 above. Cooking platform 6401 and lararium 6403 to the north. Cooking platform 6402 and latrine 6404 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: This is a storeroom. It is a rectangular shaped room on a northeast/southwest axis. One can enter this space from the dining garden 13 at the southwest wall or from the kitchen 10 at the south corner of the southeast wall. A tall deep cupboard 3851 is located to the west of the doorway 8. It is separated from the rest of the storeroom by a partition all the way to the ceiling. The storeroom itself is in very poor condition. Cement floors are visible in the north corner. Plaster remains on all four walls. No painting is discernible. No ceilings remain, however, four joist holes are preserved in the northeast wall and one in the partition wall to the southwest wall. There is a small high window in the northeast wall and a large square window in the northwest wall which may have been above the ceiling of this room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: kitchen 10 to the northwest, dining garden 13 to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: Room 4 is a processing room which is on a northwest-southeast axis, northwest of the structure's entrance. The room is irregular in shape due to features which complicate the space. An interesting room a vat feature 3759 fills the entire width of the back (northwest) wall and protrudes into the room in approximately one-third of the space. On the southwestern wall a preparation platform delineates the remaining portion of the room and is about 3 feet high. On the southeastern side of the vat on the south corner between the preparation platform and an indentation for enabling feet to get closer to the vat, lies a structure which probably held a dolium. The height of the room is indeterminate; however, all walls except the wall between the cooking platform and the vat in room 3 are preserved to an almost second story height. The floors are obscured with lapilli and devbris and no ceiling is extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is northwest of room 3754.

DESCRIPTION: The masonry couch in the open air triclinium is U shaped with the central area facing southeast. The 3 couches slope down outwards. In the northern corner between the eastern and northwestern couch is a high buttress that makes an incomplete triclinium couch. This structure does not show any trace of painting nor the usual ledge around the inner sides. The eastern corner of the northeastern couch adjoins triclinium 6 so close that one had to step over this couch in order to get to corridor 5.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: No video information on this Feature Sheet.

DESCRIPTION: This is a vat. It is about 6 ft long by 3 ft wide and is preserved to about 18 inches in height. There is some smooth plaster. Preserved on the southwest wall of the vat that which may be hydrolic plaster. the bottom surface of this is not visible and the walls are rough cut stone and mortar. This is in poor condition. This vat may have been a fish tank.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 4 is to the northwest. Room 2 is to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The horticultural space at the northeast end of the property is a large, square space on an east west axis with an opening to the room on the west wall. Within the room in the southwest corner are two masonry tanks with a dividing wall between them (Feature 2998) near to which is a small, masonry square structure and in the southeast corner is a latrine separated from the horticultural space by a low wall. There is a wide opening on the west wall to the horticultural space with the remains of a small threshold. On the north wall two beam holes, one at the northwest end and one at the northeast end; the remains of plaster can be found at the northeast end of the wall but the color doesn't remain. The east wall has a beam hole located in the northeast corner and the wall has been restored in recent years. The latrine is located in the southeast corner and is entered from the north. On the south wall is a single beam hole within the latrine space. No sign of the floor or surfaces within the garden remain and the room is in a poor state of preservation.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room number 10 is contiguous to room 9 to the west and the exterior of the property to the east of room 10 The feature 2998 is located in the southwest corner of room 10

DESCRIPTION: Circular plastered cistern filled with debris surmounted by a circular terra cotta well. Head with decorated lip consisting of incised lines and circular embossed elements. In front of the lectus imus of couch 3024.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Triclinium 3024 to the east. Fishpond 3030 to the west. Water feature (3033) to the west. Cistern (3031) to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the property from the southeastern entrance. This space is difficult to interpret due to an open channel running through the property on a northeast/southwest axis. This space would have been appropriate and abundant for outside dining. In this space there is evidence of a large masonry triclinium with a table. At the foot of the right triclinium platform there is evidence of a platform that could have been for serving food or used for children or freed men. The property (space) borders a house located on the southeastern side beyond the channel. The southeastern wall is interrupted by a low door on the street of the Palestra. The northwest part of the wall, surrounding the space, shows some evidence of plaster. This is an area where large trees grew based on ancient sources.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room ( ) to the southeast

DESCRIPTION: This is a dining room with two entrances flanking the east corner. The door on the southeast wall is low, with a marble threshold. The doorway on the northeast wall is tall and is missing a threshold. This rectangular room also has a window through the northeast wall. The view from this window overlooks the contiguous water feature and the peristyle beyond it. The interior of the room is decorated with frescos. The paint on the dado is the best preserved and reveals rectangular and diamond patterns. The flooring is not visible. Decorative plaster molding is preserved on three quarters of the walls, above the frescos. On the northwest and southeast walls there are arched pediments above the straight molding. These are the ends of a barrel-vaulted ceiling. The south corner above the arched molding on the southeast wall preserves a small section of fresco. This may predate the vaulted ceiling. The upper part of the existing northeast wall is cut with an unidentifiable small niche cutting into the ceiling vault. The upper remains of the southwest wall have eleven rectangular holes for ceiling/upper story support beams.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to Room 11 and Room 2. Room 2 is a step down from Room 12.
VIDEO_COMMENTS:
Keep both. Retake.
see LK's addition on retake, not in original script.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the dining room which lies off the peristyle(11) to the southwest. The room has a northeast /southwest axis. There is a large doorway with a volcanic threshold which allows a view to the garden. On either side of this threshold are white stones for placement of door posts. A small doorway just inside the room on the west side of the northwest wall provides access to stairs, an andron, and the peristyle. Red painted plaster survives on the lowest abutment of the door on the northwest and southeast facings and also on the west side of the southwest wall at the lowest portion. On the northwest wall there is evidence of yellow paint; traces of red over niche feature 3133. A larger a painted portion covers most of the extant northeast wall, primarily in white paint with traces of yellow and red pattern. The floor which is now obscured with dirt and overgrowth is cocciopesto, and bits of white tesserae. The southeast wall is volcanic. The height of the ceiling is indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: (11) to the southwest, west (17).

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that the House of the Small Fountain was a domestic property. Room #6 in that structure, we have identified as a store room. We have made this identification based upon the size and shape of the room; the narrowness of the doorway; and the presence of three series of post holes indicating wooden shelf placement along the walls. The room is entered from the south east by a very tall narrow bricked doorway with a marble sill with indentations that show door hardware attachment. The room is rectangular on a northwest southeast axis. Fresco is found on all walls with a red dado and white or perhaps yellow above. The northeast and northwest walls were constructed of opus incertum. The southwest wall appears appears to be constructed of masonry fill with brick courses. The door wall is reconstructed but shows traces of opus incertum above the door header. The north east,north west and south west walls have high post holes indicating the presence of an upper storey.
Today a reconstructed ceiling covers the room. Evenly spaced in three rows into the thick plaster are squared post holes. There is a series of three by three on the south west wall, a series of two by two on the north west wall, and a series of one row of three on the north west wall. We would assume there were three rows all the way around the room but the lack of plaster probably hides those on the adjacent walls. The floor today is packed dirt and probably originally contained some sort of pavement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room opens on the north west side of atrium 4.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. We are looking along the south eastern wall at a great cooking platform with a front lip, rear shelf, recessed storage pit. The top is of pebbles. Escheback said there were five cooking utensils on the cooking platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the south east wall. Enter from the atrium of slaves.

DESCRIPTION: A good sized rectangular lararium niche is on the prep room wall. No signs of color or figures. We can't move close as the roof slabs are stacked close to it. The walls in this room are bare of any plaster. The lararium is situated in the western corner of the northwest wall, half way up. Dimensions of the lararium as per drawing measurements.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Kitchen and hallway to stairs and garden area

DESCRIPTION: At the entrance to the kitchen there remains a circular opening to a cistern. The circular opening is about 15 feet deep. Today it is covered by a rectangular wooden cover. The proximity provided a useful water source for the kitchen and the latrine. The cistern is located in the doorway area located on the eastern end of the southeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Toilet and cooking platform. Narrow door leads to storeroom.

DESCRIPTION: In this niche tomb there are identical benches within the tomb. The bench runs the entire length of the interior, it is low, made of opus incertum and shows signs of plaster. The bench runs north-south (on the east side). This bench would have allowed for resting, eating and drinking.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: See feature sheet.

DESCRIPTION: Travertine altar with statue of herm of Mercury now lost.

This is the House of the Vettii. On the dado of the south-west wall closest to the west corner is found a painting of a female dressed in a purplish chiton holding what appears to be a patera in her hands. The painting has a black background and is delineated by thin red vertical bands with yellow edging and various leaf forms make up the background.

In this niche tomb there are identical benches within the tomb. This bench runs the entire length of the interior; it is low, made of opus incertum and shows signs of plaster. The bench runs north-south (on the west side of the niche tomb). This bench is made available for resting, eating and drinking.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: See feature sheet 6592 bench

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
We have identified the usage of room (28) as a dining hall. This identification is based on: the location of the room opening on to the peristyle with a view of the peristyle central fountain, as well as the nympheum; the main entrance to this room is a very high, very wide doorway on the north eastern wall with a white stone threshold; and the size of this large room. This room is generally in very poor condition. The floor is not visible in any part of the room, with only a cement layer visible in the north corner. Although the walls preserve some rough plaster, particularly in the north corner, there is no smooth stucco or fresco remaining. The walls are opus incertum and the north west wall has preserved plaster with ceramic embedded in the central part of the wall. The walls are preserved to various heights with no evidence of ceiling remaining. The only other features intact in this room are two doorways opening on to the corridor on the south east wall of the room, one in the south corner and one in the east corner. These doors are reconstructed lower than the doorway to the peristyle, while both doors have marble thresholds. The door near the east corner is wider than the door by the south corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the west of the peristyle and colonnade (29) and (30) and is adjacent to the corridor at its south east side.

DESCRIPTION:
Circular, plastered cistern with opus signinum surviving throughout. The base of the cistern is obscured by debris. The cistern has a masonry plastered cap inserted into the north east corner of the room and abutting directly against the doorway to garden 6, in the northeast corner.
The plaster exterior face of the cap is contiguous with the plaster on the north wall. The southern face of the cap is removed to facilitate access to the cistern. On the interior face of the cistern at ground level there is a lip.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northeast corner of kitchen 4 (4134). The room also contained negative features 4137 (lararium) and 4135 (hearth)

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
We have identified this area as a root cellar for food storage. This identifications is based on the location of this space at a lower level below the dining room (6787) and accessed through the kitchen preparation area (26).

This large rectangular space is on a south west / north east axis, the perimeter walls supporting the walls of the dining room above. It is uncertain how far down the original floor would have been as this has not been fully excavated.

Stone supports remain down the central sections, allowing for passage throughout the space. Holes cut along the south east and north east walls held floor joists above the stone supports. Traces of thick cement cover these joists providing support for the floor of the dining room above.

Near the center of the south east wall is an arch built into the stonework of that wall, but it is unclear whether this arch was originally an opening or whether it supported the structure of the wall.

The entrance to this cellar is at the south west end of the service corridor where one enters the doorway at the south east and crosses the preparation area (26) and continues down to a small landing and turns north east down a narrow passage to a doorway at the south corner of the south west wall of the cellar.

This passage may have been a stairway to the original floor level of the cellar.

Both sides of the stairway wall present preserved plaster, as does the north east wall at the top of the stairs.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is directly below dining room (25). It is north east of preparation area (26) an access stairway.

DESCRIPTION: In the north corner of room 9, we have identified a potential latrine based upon an indentation running along the northwest wall as well as a possible drain underneath the northeast end of cooking platform 4129 which may indicate a drain. The area is square and slopes slightly down.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
to the northeast of cooking platform 4129
to the west of cooking platform 4132
to the north of cooking platform 4131

DESCRIPTION:
Long, shallow, high, rectangular couch niche extending along the northwest wall from the north corner almost the entire way to the west corner.
The niche is carved directly out of the wall with a stone base. Red plaster survives with no visible decorative detail. The plaster is the same as that in couch niche (4154) and on the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Couch niche (4154) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. We have identified the House of the Vetti as a domestic space and room 16 as a dining room based upon its view towards the peristyle courtyard, its very large doorway and its rectangular shape. The room is on northeast-southwest axis and is entered from the southwest from a very high door covering most of that wall. To the southeast is a second doorway of average height entering to ala 17. The room is covered with fresco painting on the southeast, northeast and northwest walls. Much is in situ. The dado is a series of panels painted to look like expensive marble and cut stone. The central panels have red alternating with white backings and primarily deal with mythological scenes. The white backed panels contain two figures (male and female) whereas the red panels are full mythological scenes. The central panels are divided by architectural panels with four insets of nautical scenes on the long southeast and northwest walls and two food scenes topped with masks on the northeast wall. Above the central panels is an architectural setting with figures positioned in doorway settings. The central figure on the rear wall appears to hold a patera and rhyton. The ceiling is no longer extant and very high upon the wall are post holes that probably indicate there was an upper storey. The floor is covered with a wood walkway and no special flooring is visible underneath.

This is the House of the Vettii. In the central panel directly above a naval scene is a bearded head with brown curly hair leaning against a basket which appears to contain green vegetables and carrots. The basket is sleigh shaped, with the tall part of the sleigh abutting the head on the left as you face the painting. The painting is located directly to the east of the low door on the south-east wall.

We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
We walk along a corridor from the water garden, on the right passing two doors to room 28, and then past a corridor and on the left past a door to room 25 and a food prep area. We enter in the east end of the northeast wall. We identify this by location and by the presence of a bath furnace in the room. There is also an "L" shaped cooking platform. The walls show no sign of plaster. There is no evidence of a ceiling. The floors are rubble. There is no window above the cooking platform. The door opening is larger than other kitchen doors, with three steps down into the room.
The cooking platform has four storage areas below for wood or charcoal.

We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
This cooking platform is large and 'L' shaped. Its surface on the north west wall is interrupted by a large bath furnace. The south west wall of the platform shows a rear shelf. There are some storage areas: two under the south west portion of the platform, and two under the north west portion of the platform. On the north east wall, by the door, is an additional arched niche for storage that is not part of the platform.

We have determined that this structure V-1-20 is a shop-house based upon the description of Eschebach and we have identified Room 4 as a kitchen. The kitchen is rectangle sitting on a southeast northwest axis. There are 2 door ways entering from rooms 2 and 3 entering from the southwest and two door ways from rooms 5 and 6 to the northeast. The northern most of the northeast doorways coming from Room 6 is very high. Immediately abutting that in the north corner is a cistern going deep into the ground (4136). Some trace of red plaster remains near the cistern on the heavily reconstructed, opus incertum walls. Eschebach tells us that there was a hearth (4135) and a lararium (4137) that were originally in this room but are no longer in this room. There are two piles of rubble that could be their remains. There are no windows and no roof. The floor is rubble. Eschebach also tells us that part of this room was a garden.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southwest of rooms 5 and 6 is the northeast of room 2 and hallway 3.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the room as a dining room. This room is northeast of the dining hall. The doorway is one-third the size of the dining hall entry. To compensate there is a square window above the lintel. There is no threshold and the floor is mud. The walls show dado red with distinctive fourth style flowers. The remaining part of the walls are cream. At the top in several places we see a nice molding. There are three features that help identify this L-shaped room as a dining room. The protruding corner of this L-shaped room is on the northeast side, and has a couch niche on each wall (6843) and (6844). Couch niche (6843) faces southeast and couch niche (6844) faces southwest. On the southwest wall there is a large depression niche for a cupboard (6841). These walls which have been changed to provide more space for couches had been repainted in the fourth style. Besides the dining room features we have discussed, the door overlooks a beautiful garden.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
The cupboard niche (6841) is situated on the southwest wall. The dining couch niche (6844) is located on the northwest side of the corner protrusion. The couch niche on the other wall of the corner (6843) faces the southeast.
The dining room is to the northeast of the large dining hall (34).

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this space is a dining room within a residential structure. This identification is based on the location of the room directly off the atrium with its very tall door and also the decoration of this room. This is a rectangular space on a northeast-southwest axis, similar to the adjacent room to the southwest (18). This room is in fair condition. A white threshold is in place in the tall doorway in the southeast wall, and there is a low secondary doorway in the east corner of the northeastern wall. The doorway opens to the ala, and there is no threshold. No flooring is visible. All four walls preserve plaster and some paint. The decorative scheme includes a red dado with broad panels above, perhaps white, which are divided by thin red bands. Traces of stucco molding remain above these panels. This molding is particularly well-preserved near the south corner of the southeast wall. On the northwest wall in the west corner the plaster above the stucco molding has traces of painted decoration. No ceiling remains. On the north end of hte northeast wall is a slight curving surface suggesting a shallow couch niche.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of the atrium (19). It is to the southwest of the ala (16).

DESCRIPTION: In the northwest side of the atrium are the remnants of a semi-circular platform. It is low and one can see the top surface. It is stone and mortar.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is close to the lararium, which is just southwest of it.

DESCRIPTION: Large rectangular shaped dining room with a northeast-southwest axis. Floor is obscured by debris. Large dip is found at the base of the east and west walls perhaps indicating the original floor level. No plaster is found. In the center of the northeast wall 1/2 foot above the ground there is a terracotta lined drain through the wall to the street outside. At the west end of the southwest wall there is a unfinished opening through to room #12 perhaps providing common access to a small window in the northwest wall. At the south end of the southwest wall is a doorway with no visible threshold and restored lintel opening to the garden (15). Upper courses of all walls are extensively restored. No ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Garden (15) to the south. Garden (15) to the south. None

DESCRIPTION: This is a large ceramic dolium intact. It is embedded into the corner of the room. Immediately to the Northwest is the gutter for the must draining from the wine press. On the northern lip of the dolium is a potter's stamp.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to cistern 6897 and winepress 6894 which are to the east. Cistern 6896 and press 6895 are to the east, southeast.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified Room 15 as a store room based upon its location off of the atrium at the landward side of the house and proximity to the kitchen. The room is small
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: and would have had a low ceiling. Post holes are visible in the northeast and southwest ends and the southern end. It was plastered with red and white and yellow paint (colors are visible on walls). The southwest wall contained a small doorway
BW_ROLL: with a granite sill and a small rectangular window next to it. The walls are of opus incertum
COLOR_ROLL: and a room with an open cut-out is visible in the northwest. The room is rectangular and on a north-south axis. The floor is rough stone.
DIGITAL_IMAGE: The room is contiguous to the atrium's rectangular walkway.

DESCRIPTION: A good-sized altar engaged to the wall only at the bottom back with two lips on the side and a finished surface on the front or face of the altar and on the platform.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: There is a lararium above the altar.
PHOTOGRAPHER: Larry Ludwicki

DESCRIPTION: A recessed rectangular lararium
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: with no traces of paint
BW_ROLL: On the west wall above the cooking platform in the kitchen.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vetti. In the central panel directly above a naval scene is the head of an old man with a grey beard and moustache and head of scraggly grey hair. He is looking toward the central panel on the wall as you face the painting and the back of his head leans against a sleigh-shaped basket filled with food and fruit (perhaps an artichoke). The painting is located on the western end of the northwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The painting is located on the western end of the northwest wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. In the central panel directly above a naval scene is a beardless head with long brown curly hair, wide open brown eyes and a gaping mouth looking towards the major central panel in the room. The head leans against a sleigh-shaped woven basket with a handle containing two drinking rhytons and some other foodstuffs. The painting is located on the north end of the north-west wall.

This is the House of the Vettii. Abutting the south corner on the northeast wall is a small painting depicting a goat standing on the left side as you face the painting. It is looking to the right. The goat is in a structural space with a corner immediately to his right. Leaning against the wall at a right angle to the goat is a sheaf of wheat. A window follows to the right with two containers sitting on the window sill that appear to hold grain or some liquid or such similar food stuff. There is another similar container laying on its side below the window sill. This long rectangular is framed with a grey band with a red lining insert. Above in the center is a staring, horrified mask with high brown curly hair with a feather brush coming out to the left, from behind the head.

This is the House of the Vettii. Near the west corner of the northwest wall above the dado in the solid black band is a painting of putti figures travelling on what appears to be a road. Beginning on the right as we face the painting is a figure riding a tiger and holding a shield. Directly behind is a winged figure whose back is to us holding a long staff. To his left is a winged figure bowing, making an offering (probably of a drink) to two goats who are hitched to a cart. The cart is being driven by a putti with a crop in his hand. The cart appears to contain a reclining figure facing backwards being followed by hoofed satyr playing pan pipes. The final figure to his left is a putti with an amphora being carried on his shoulder and a wand in his hand.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The painting is to the northwest of figure 6604 and to the west of figure 6601.

DESCRIPTION: We have decided the structure number V-1-13 is a shop-house and room number 9 is a kitchen based upon Eschebach's description of a room with a very high platform and two preparation platforms. The room is almost square with a narrow doorway to the southwest opening up off the working area of a popina that also does metal work. The door is narrow with no threshold evident. Walls are opus incertum with the top of the street wall on the northwest side appearing to be reconstructed at the top. The room is currently open to the sky. The room contains an extremely high narrow platform of solid masonry, rectangular, long and narrow with no trace of a tiled surface remaining. The prep platform 4131 sits on the southwest wall next to the northwest of the open doorway, currently low to the floor. Prep platform 4132 appears to have stretched between two masonry ends (no counter service remains) and sits against the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: immediately to the northeast of room 8

DESCRIPTION: We have identified a long rectangular, tall masonry structure in the west corner of room 9 as a cooking platform. The short end of the platform sits on the southwest wall with the long end of the rectangle abutting the northwest wall. The platform is taller than most cooking platforms but has been identified as such by Eschebach. There is no window evident but the upper wall is partially reconstructed. We believe that a gap at the northeast end of the cooking platform may have been a drain, indicating the possibility of a latrine. No plaster is evident.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
to the northwest of feature 4131
to the southwest of feature 4130
to the west of feature 4132

DESCRIPTION: High, shallow, rectangular couch niche extending from the east corner along the southeast wall of the room. The base of the niche is no longer extant. The niche is plastered in red, identical to the plaster in couch niche (4152) and on the walls of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Couch niche (4152) to the north

DESCRIPTION: The U-shaped cooking platform covers the southeast end of kitchen 16. The platform is low and made of masonry. No trace of the top remains. The two arms of the U are narrow and protude to the northwest from the main surface of the platform. The southwest arm is considerably shorter than that on the northeast. The main portion of the platform sits against that southeast wall. Immediately to the northeast, at platform height, is oven (4149).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the northeast of platform height is oven (4149)

DESCRIPTION: There is a circular terracotta water basin. The basin is restored with plaster on the southeast and upper parts. The basin is embedded into the southeastern arm of counter 4124.

This famous lararium is in the west corner of the atrium. There are small stepped platforms in the northwest and southwest corners and a cream marble surface. There is a large marble sheath on the front surfaces and above that is a medium size section on the two front faces that has been removed and sent to the museum. These famous panels show the destruction of the 62-63 AD earthquake, showing statues falling down.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is close to the platform, which is just northeast of it.

DESCRIPTION: We identify this room as a preparation room. It opens to the kitchen and is next to another preparation room, this room lies on a northwest/southeast axis. This one rectangular room with a pod and pebbletton. With only the smallest portion of painted plaster on the walls. This pod is open to the sky. In the northeast wall there is a rectangular shallow opening with a partial opening into the adjoining preparation room (6836)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The preparation room opens to the kitchen (6832) to the northwest and another preparation room (6836) to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: We approach this latrine to see large floor tiles sloping down into the latrine and a large toilet hole that slopes northeast to the street. There is a terracotta pipe remaining along the side of this toilet hole an angle. This large latrine was possibly made for multiple people.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The latrine is located northeast of the water basin.

DESCRIPTION: Large square room overlooking garden area (9). Identified as a dining room by large doorway with lava stone threshold with view to garden to northeast. Little plaster remains to determine wall decoration. A small store room opens up on the northwest wall which utilizes the space under a stairway. Lapilli floor. Several stones remains in threshold. Door attachment recesses remains in door jamb.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 10 is located at back of house northwest of garden area (8 and 9). Store room 11 on north wall with stairs above it. Tablinum is to the south and atrium and room 12 are to the west.

DESCRIPTION: We see a rectangular lararium that slopes inward at the top. The back wall shows orange points and there is a plaster around the niche. There are no other paintings.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Close to the basin and niche cupboard

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this space as a space for public eating and drinking. Feature 4306 is a public water fountain of stone construction. It is on the edge of the sidewalk to the northwest of the shrine. The modern spigot is surrounded by a raised annulus with no decoration. There is a drain hole to the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the northwest of altar 4303 and to the west of wall painting 4305.

DESCRIPTION: This is a medium-sized dolium. It is in situ with about two-thirds imbedded in the ground. It is fully intact except for small chips in the rim. This dolium is straight-sided with carinated shoulders rising inward to a slightly flaring rim. It is made of terracotta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium (4991) is located to the southeast of 4990 and adjacent to the western corner of room 10.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is identified as a cooking platform. It is a vaulted space embedded in the west end of the southwest wall. The front opening has a rounded lip across the bottom, covered with a carved roof tile at the northwest end. The upper surface of the platform is not visible. Plaster remains are visible on the southeast edge of the vaulted opening, below the springing of the vault. The vaulted top is heavily restored. A round hole goes through the back wall, possibly a light or vent hole.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform is directly to the south of the doorway into Room #1 (4350).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified structure 1, 3, 9-10 as a shop house based upon the translation of Eschebach, who says that at the rear of the entrance 10, there is a kitchen with a latrine. The only existing evidence is a pile of rubble underneath a plethora of weeds at the back of this room (7). The room is rectangular and sits on a northwest/southeast axis, opening onto what was probably an atrium (9). Walls are opus incertum. The floor is covered with lapilli. No roof is present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south of room 9. To the southwest of room 8. Northeast of room 6.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a tiny painted vignette in the center of the northeast wall. It depicts a basin on a pedestal with a small jug on its side.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Painting 6955 is north of 6956.

DESCRIPTION: The rectangular cupboard niche workshelf is seen on the northwest wall and functions as a butler's pantry

Mostly ruined, the masonry base sits almost at floor level in the northern most corner of room 2, the kitchen. This has been defined as a cooking platform by Eschebach. It is rectangular in shape with its length along the NE wall in the North corner of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the NW of negative feature 4122.

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii. Abutting the north corner on the northeast wall is a small painting depicting two dead birds / one upside down, one feet down) laying on a flat surface with a fig to their left. There are two windows above the birds. The left window contain two figs. The right window contains a single fig. This long rectangular painting is framed with a grey band with a red lining insert. Above in the center is a staring, horrified mask with high brown curly hair with a feather brush coming out to the right from behind the head.
Two heavily resotred masonry supports for preparation platform. Surface does not survive. Abuts directly against south west wall of the room (1, 4118).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: On the south west wall of the room.

DESCRIPTION:
Rectangular room north-east/south-west axis. Wide doorway at the west end of the south-east wall, opening to the counter room (1). No visible threshold. floor obscured by lapilli throughout. Undecorated plaster survives in fragments on all four walls. Extensive restoration high on north-east and north-west walls. High along the length of the north-west wall are seven holes for floor joints - modern?
In the centre of the south-west wall there is a square window opening to room (2).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (4114) to the south-east.

DESCRIPTION: Long rectangular room northwest/southeast axis with wide open doorway south to peristyle 11, 12. Doorway has marble threshold with placings for door. Modern lintel. Coccio pesto floor partially obscured by debris. At the southern end of the west wall there is a doorway to dining room 19 (4139). Modern lintel, marble threshold with placing for door. The upper sections of all four walls are restored. In the center of the east wall there is a modern hole through to the adjoining corridor. Extensive third style painting survives on all four walls. Black lower register with alternating red and yellow panels above. Graffiti was found here CIL-4.4150.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle (11, 12) to the south and dining room 19 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: There is a shallow rectangular lararium niche (east end of the north wall) with plaster surviving on the rear and base. There is no visible decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Northeast corner of the room (4123).
Counter (4124) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
Rectangular room northeast/southwest axis with wide doorway opening southwest to atrium 28. Threshold does not survive. Fragments of opus signinum flooring survives throughout with intact segment in the north corner extending along the northeast wall. Pattern of diamonds surrounded by border of two lines of individual white tiles.
Northeast wall and the southeast wall preserve red painted plaster. No extant decorative detail.
There are two substantial couch niches (4152, 4154) on the north northwest and east southwest walls.
High in the center of the northeast wall, the base of a window survives tapering to the street outside.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (28) to the west.

DESCRIPTION:
This intersection is located at the junction of regions 6 and 7. This is a public space located at the intersection of vicolo di Foro and vicolo sopra Stanti/vicolo degli Augustali. It has been determined that this space was used for gathering. Marcus Tullius built the adjacent Temple of Fortuna Augusta (7.4.1) and enlarged the adjacent street. There is an honorary arch to the north which is piped for water. There are benches to the west on both sides of the street.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined VI-8-20 is a commercial fullery and that the room is a kitchen based upon the presence of a large cooking platform and an oven. The room was originally square but the addition of the oven made it more L-shaped. A series of post holes on the northwest wall indicate a low roof line and a window on the southwest wall would have allowed the smoke to escape. The kitchen is entered by a door on the northwest wall in the west corner. The cooking platform sits opposite the door frame with the oven immediately to the northeast opening at platform height level. The walls are opus incertum with traces of plaster on the northwest wall. The floor is rubble today.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southeast of corridor 17,to the northeast of room 16

DESCRIPTION: This room has been identified as a dining room within a residential structure. This identification is based on the fairly large size of the room; its location and wide doorway going out to the colonnade [33] and the enormous window on the southwest side opening into the ala [16]. This is a rectangular space on a northeast/southwest axis. The main entrance is almost the entire northeast side of the room. A secondary doorway is a small opening in the east corner of the southeast wall, going into the corridor [26]. A gray stone threshold is seen at the northeast doorway. The floor is small, white, stone, irregular tesserae in a cement matrix and it is very poorly preserved. Along he southeast wall there is also cocciopesto but it is impossible to determine the decorative scheme for this floor. The poor condition of this room, with extensive restoration of the upper wall, also makes it difficult to determine the decorative scheme for this floor. Small sections of plaster remain on the walls, revealing a red dado, but nothing above remains intact. In the south corner of the southeast wall there is a couch niche [6842]. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is southwest of colonnade 33 and corridor 26 runs along the southeast side.

DESCRIPTION: In the kitchen (room 7) adjacent to the masonry cooking platform is a much lower, square preparation platform. Made of masonry, this platform stands about 15 - 20 cm. high. The southeastern end of the platform is against the cooking platform (6536) and the southwest side runs along the southwest wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the northwest of cooking platform 6536

DESCRIPTION: We have identified structure Vi.10.14 as a house separate from VI.10.11 at the time of the eruption. We have determined that room 7 is a kitchen based upon the presence of a cooking platform. The room is rectangular and on a northwest - southeast axis. The cooking platform and preparation platform take up the southern half of the southwest wall. Entrance to the room was from a doorway in the north corner entering from room 8. The walls were plastered and painted with opus incertum beneath. The southeast wall appears to have two circular holes midway up as well as a large post hole near the top on its south corner. The southwest wall is today extensively reconstructed although patches of painted fresco remain. This wall also retains three post holes high up indicating the presence of an upper story and three post holes near its west corner midway up the wall. The northwest wall extends as far as the doorway with a small dividing wall coming off it heading toward the southwest. The southeast wall is largely reconstructed. The floor is rubble and the room is open to the sky.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the southeast of room 8.

DESCRIPTION: The wall on the northwest has a shallow, low entry into the kitchen. The wall is plastered and includes one large rough area for painting and a Pompeiian red slab underneath it. The feature is a rectangular lararium, with minimal evidence of bottom edge. Beneath the lararium niche is one great snake and the suggestion of the presence of a second. The interior of the lararium is painted with white plaster on top, bottom, two sides and rear and is painted with 38 red roses with green stems and leaves. To the north of the lararium on the wall we discerned blue, red and green figural elements. The snake below is burgundy and amber in color. This wall is outside of room 9 and is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this room as a food and drink preparation room. We have made this identification by the opening to the kitchen and a pass through to another preparation room (37) opening to many dinning rooms. This is a small rectangular room with a floor of mud and pebbles on a northwest/southeast axis. The walls shows small signs of painted plaster. In the northwest corner there is a sign of a half circle basin attached to the wall which shows small segments of painted plaster. There is a small floor level hole in the southwest wall going through to the adjoining preparation room (35).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to the kitchen to the northwest and a preparation room (37) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION: In the center of mill room 4, what was formerly in impluvium has been lined with pozzolano cement and turned into a water basin. The northeast side of the impluvium has been built up with masonry and clearly shows the pozzolano lining. The other three sides show the original cocciopesto, dotted with white marble pieces of the impluvium edge. The remains of the impluvium are now filled with sand. A cistern head [4186] sits on the immediate north corner of the impluvium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 4181 and 4188 are to the southeast. 4182, 4185, and 4183 are to the southwest. 4184 and 4187 are to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This structure has been determined to be a domestic room, in the House of the Faun. The room has been identified as a dining hall due to it's great size and open access to ambulatory 31. The large rectangular shape is aligned northwest by southeast axis with 2 small doors on the southwest and northwest corners. The present condition reveals a great deal of restoration with very few traces of the floor existing. The floor overlaid a maze of what appears to be a large system of tanks and a large cistern system. The walls are preserved and restored to full height with a modern roof. The upper portion of the southwest wall is restoration. The southwest, northeast and southeast walls have preserve holes mid-way up the wall with a little line of three holes across the upper portion of the southeast wall. No decoration is preserved in this room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is located to the southeast of ambulatory and directly to the northwest of the kitchen.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a painting. It is located on the central red register at the south end of the southeast wall. This large red panel depicts a pair of female figures, each located in the center of one half of the panel. They are mirror images of each other. The figures have one hand on a hip and one hand raised holding a jug on their head. These are done fresco secco.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is adjacent to 4253 in the southwest wall of dining room 4247.

DESCRIPTION: long L-shaped counter with marble. Stepped display counter connected to counter to the left. Storage space below display steps. Three dolia opening in long section of counter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: cooking platform. small rooms behind. cooking platform.

STRUCTURE_ID: Temple of the Genius of Augustus
DESCRIPTION:
It has been determined that this space is a rectangular area with north-west/south-east access within the Temple of the Genius of Augustus, across the front of the temple, separated by 2 interior partition walls from the sacred space to the east. This is identified as such due to: Traces of un-decorated plaster which survive; a wide open doorway in the centre of the west wall with marble threshold and modern lintel opening to the forum to the west;and placings for 4 sets of shelves in the east and west corners. The floor is obscured by lapilli.

Anything unusual: 2 interesting supporting items and rooms in the rear.

Eschebach (pp. 308-309) Check (cite?) Dobbins reference.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Sacred area to the east.

DESCRIPTION: In bakery V-3-8 we have determined that a large, square, elaborately decorated room, with a patterned coccio pesto floor was probably used as a dining tablinium. The room is entered from the south east by a large doorway, framed by two large windows looking out at the mill room and fauces to the street. Walls were made of opus incertum and were covered with plaster (today only a small section remain on all walls). The southwest wall however, near the south corner, has a good trace of 1st style block fresco. There are indications at the top center of that same wall of a very high window. An indentation in the wall running horizontally just below window level was probably in place for a stucco crown molding. Nice traces of a Greek key patter remains in the red coccio pesto floor with white marble insets. The room is currently open to the sky.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is entered to the northwest from mill room 4.

DESCRIPTION: Feature 4184 is a circular masonry base and mill with modern restoration. The catillus and meta are in situ but are now cemented together. The interior face has the ties from earlier restoration. The base is contiguous with the surrounding paving. On the northern face there is a grafitto of the letter "A" on the catillus.

DESCRIPTION: Feature 4185 is an arched, plastered lararium. Plaster survives on the rear and left-hand faces and on the base. Earlier plaster has been stippled to allow the adhesion of a second phase of decoration. There is a red lower register with white above. The earlier phase has a yellow lower register with red motifs and white above. The lararium is inserted into the west end of the north wall. To the west is the window into tablinum 5.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mills 4183 and 4182 are to the south. Prep table 4182, cistern 4186, water basin 4187, and oven 4188 are all varying degrees to the southeast. Mill 4184 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: The triclinium is located in the northeast side of the atrium, room two, on axis with the impluvium. One enters the triclinium from the southwest through a tall doorway. A modern ceiling is constructed in such a way that it pitches steeply from the southwest to the northeast with six modern openings. As reconstructed there appears to have been two large windows on each of three sides: the southeast, northeast, and northwest. The walls were plastered and decorated in the fourth style, much of which remains. The floor, though heavily damaged, seems to be decorated of a beaten cement and stones.

DESCRIPTION: House of the Vettii. It has been determined that this is a storage room, based on the accounts by Escherbach who notes that amphorae were stored in this room. The room is rectangular on a north-east/south-west axis. One enters a narrow, short doorway at the south-east side of the room from the peristyle. The floor seems to have been cocciopesto, remains of which can be seen at the north-west end of the room. The walls are plaster, without any traces of paint. There is a low doorway at the north-west side of the room leading out to areas (6). The south-west and north-east walls have three rows of three holes for shelving. The ceiling is modern metal covering. There are two high narrow windows on the north-east wall.

DESCRIPTION: This is the Houe of the Vettii. We have determined that this space is a dining room. This identification is based on the location of the room off the atrium, its large entrance way, and the decorative scheme (fourth style) of the wall paintings. The room is rectangular on a northwest / southeast axis. One enters at the northwest side of the room. There is a window centered at the upper section of the north east wall. The floor is cocciopesto with a large centrally placed round marble slab and other tiles of coloured marble placed on the north western area of the floor. The wall decoration has a low dark dado. The central panels are decorated with architectural elements in a mythological tableaux on a white background. The upper section is architectural, decorated with some figures, some holding bowls and fruit. The ceiling is a modern covering.

We have identified structure 4115 as a thermopolium based upon a large L-shaped counter and its large door openings to two cross streets. We decided that room 4 was a serving room based upon its proximity to the counter and its location to the NW of the counter room. The room is square with its large opening to the SE and a high window between it and room 3 (4116). At either side of the door opening are large stones that indicate a threshold was probably present in its past. The current floor is rubble. Wall construction is opus incertum interspersed with brick work. There are two structures / podium in the room which Escheback says were evidence of a staircase [western side of north west wall; western side of SE wall] . There is one other window on the SW wall opening to the street. Currently there is no covering overhead and there are slight remains of plaster on the walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Opens to the SE to room 1.

DESCRIPTION: Room 16 is entered from room 18 to the northwest. On the threshold is a rectangular stone. The small square room is delimited by a mostly collapsed wall to the northwest (wall that delimits the adjoining vat), two preserved walls to the north and northeast and a wall to the south which was probably pierced by a large window looking out onto space 15. Large sections of red plaster are visible on the north and northeastern walls. On the northeastern wall is a medium-sized rectangular window on the top and traces of another window are also visible on the top of the northern wall. The floor shows a few traces of mosaic decoration (white tesserae on a pinkish background) close to the doorway. The orientation of the room is northwest/southeast.

DESCRIPTION: The dining garden takes up most of the northeast part of the property. One enters the dining room from the southwest through the kitchen (1). The garden is essentially rectangular in shape on a northeast/southwest axis. In the south corner, the garden extends more to the southwest. High on the southwest wall is a narrow window opening onto the street. A staircase to the second floor abuts the southwest wall in the exterior of the east wall of room (1). To the east of the stairway, at the third step level, there is a small hearth. To the north there is a doorway to room (5). There are remains of eleven planting rows still visible along the northwest wall, running from the west end of the room (5) towards the north along the north wall. In the center of the garden a few meters northeast of room (1) was a well or cistern. The walls on all sides lack plaster except for a small amount on the southeast wall. It appears to have been painted. On the southeast wall, roughly on axis with room (5), there is a remnant of a wall extending into the garden. To the north of this wall and abutting it are the remains of a platform, the smooth surface of which is composed of plaster and fragments of terracotta. The function is unknown. Eschebach suggests that it was perhaps a latrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (1) to the southwest. Room (5) to the northwest.

The interior of the tank was cement with some large ceramic inclusions. It may have been completely plaster covered. This tank may have held fish.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
This is a semicircular platform in the north corner of the room. There is evidence of a tiled surface. There is a small rectangular niche at the floor level. There is some evidence of painted plaster.

We have identified this commercial structure as a food & drink shop, other. We have determined the usage of the room as an oven room. The feature in this room is an enclosed oven. There is an Eshcebach report of a second oven that is gone. The room is "L" shaped, with a rectangular garden in the north corner. The room opens to a preparation room to the east corner that has a water tank. The large oven is on the southeast wall. It is encased in walls of medium lava stones. It has an unusual opening, with no openings to side rooms, no storage space and no storage space for fuel. This oven room and this commercial property have no mills for grinding wheat. Wilhelmina Jashemski told Betty Jo Mayeske that Tatiana Warsher, author of the famous Pompeii Codex, told her of the common practice in Russia of designating a commercial oven for communal usage. People on designated times would bring their casseroles to the oven to bake them. This oven seems to be an example of this practice. The project people have noted an absence of baking ovens in private houses.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Door to preparation room is to the east of the oven at the northeast end of commercial space.
