DESCRIPTION: Eschebach identifies this as a caupona. The property is unexcavated. On either side of the shop entrance are benches (4156 and 4157). On the exterior face of the property traces of white and red plaster survived.

We have identified 18-6541 as a dining room. This identification is based on its location in the house with a magnificent view of a peristyle garden to the northwest. No traces remain of a ceiling but the walls are quite high and painted possibly in the Third Style. It is repaired with old but not ancient metal staples. The location and the characteristics of the room including the focus of the view, and research indicates this as a dining room. The floor is in a white mosaic with a black border partially in situ. The large entrance off the portico [19] and garden [20] has traces of a masonry threshold but no door jambs can be evidenced. The northwest wall has a large entrance with modern reconstruction on either side. Nothing else remains. The northeast wall is badly damaged and has modern reconstruction. There is an entrance on the north corner to corridor [16]. There is a marble threshold but no door jambs. There is no evidence of paint or plaster. The southeast wall is badly damaged and reconstructed in modern times. Traces of concrete and plaster with evidence of badly faded design on a black background remain. The design is possibly red and yellow. It is geometric and sits on the western side in the middle register. The southwest wall is the best preserved. It is very high with three registers. It was reconstructed at the original excavation. There is evidence of concrete and plaster in the middle and upper registers possibly in the Third Style, possibly five panels with three larger central panels and two smaller-width flanking panels. Traces of painting remain of possible architecture and scenes that are barely identifiable. Color palette includes yellow, red, back, blue and white. The best preserved area is the upper register in the south corner. On the west corner there is an entranceway to room 21 with a marble threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 18-6541 is contiguous to corridor 16 and to room 19 with a view and access to garden 20 via the northwest entrance. An entrance on the northeast side to corridor 16 and an entrance on the northwest side to room 21 remain.

DESCRIPTION: This public fountain is on the Via Stabia at the southeastern corner of the intersection with the Via della Abbondanza. It is in front of 1.4.15. The fountain is constructed of volcanic stone slabs. The interior measures 1.51 meters by 1.20 meters and it is 0.80 meters deep. It has an added lining to round the wall/floor junction. Only this lining and the floor is covered with opus signinum. The pilaster is situated in the center of the northeastern wall and is decorated with a comedy theater mask. This fountain has no modern plumbing. The overflow is at the top of the southwestern wall and the drainage hole is at the bottom of the southern corner. There are worn hand placements on either side of the pilaster, on the northeastern wall, about 0.45 meters from the interior east corner and about 0.15 meters from the interior north corner.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The fountain is located immediately southeast of/abutting the water tower 4722 and in front of 1.4.15.

DESCRIPTION: The room is large and rectangular, with the door opening to the NE facing a small garden. On the east corner of the south wall is a small doorway leading to the hallway. The threshold is stone and has evidence of circular representations which may be from a folding screen. Along the south wall, situated in the center is a drain (#2078). It is well preserved. The floor is heavily damaged with the remains of the non-patterned tesserae evident. The north and the west walls display third style paintings. The southern wall is severely damaged. On the north wall the decoration is black and framed with red. The western wall has a decoration framed with green contains red, yellow and gold. The picture is framed in the same red as is on the north wall. The picture contains water nymphs. On the top of the wall are white architectural elements and herm like figures that are standing in plinths. We can see a door to the left and an open window containing a faraway scene between the figures. Also present are garlands.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The hallway to the atrium is behind the south wall. South is garden, peristyle. The hallway to the atrium is behind the south wall. South is garden, peristyle. None

DESCRIPTION: Room 1 is rectangular on a northwest/southeast axis. Room 1 is entered through a large entrance as wide as the room to the northwest. Two pairs of semi-pilasters leaning against the northwestern and southwestern walls seem to divide this large room into three spaces. In the southeastern corner at the back, close to the entrance of processing room there is evidence of stairs leading up to a missing story. What is left today is a low step and a high platform which would have supported the stairs. In the western corner of the southwestern wall in the entrance into the vineyard (room 5) with the embedded dolia. On the same wall between the two pilasters there is what appears to have been a door. On the top is covered with a line of bricks supporting what looks like the opening but is difficult to discern the function. Because of the location of this room connecting the vineyard and processing room, the use of room 1 must be somehow associated with the production and processing of grapes. With comparison to all the traditions still surviving in Southern Italy, this space could be used for storing the agricultural tools. In some periods of the year the front part could be temporarily used for selling surplus wine and serving a glass of wine to the passersby. The ceiling is no longer extant but the walls are quite well preserved almost to full height of the first floor. The floor is now covered with lapilli. No plaster is extant. Along the southwestern wall, next to the last pilaster to the southern corner is a long, narrow indentation with a tiled bottom and stuccoed interior with an indeterminate function.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Vineyard (5) to the southwest; Processing room (2) to the southeast. Vineyard (5) to the southwest; Processing room (2) to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: This is a street shrine located on the south east side of the via dell' Abbondanza at the corner of the vicolo dell' Efebo. The shrine consists of a painting on both sides of a ramp alter. A celebrant would ascend the ramp from left to right, approaching the alter on the south east end of the ramp. The ramp has a base of opus incertum topped with larger stones. There is a thick layer of cement above the stones on the north west end. The ramp was originally plastered, with evidence of this still remaining close to the altar. There appears to be no sidewalk on this side of the street. There is a layer of concrete on the top. The altar is not well preserved. At the south east end of the ramp there is a large ancient down pipe. To the south east of the altar is a horizontal drain encased in stone, brick and roof tile.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 4922 Wall painting on each side of ramp altar 4921.

DESCRIPTION: This space is a dining room (11) in the House of Samellius Modesto This is a very large rectangular space on a northeast / southwest axis. The entrance to this space is in the southern end of the southeast wall. This space adjoins a serving room (12). The room is in poor condition. It is presently buttressed with wooden and metal supports. The ground is overgrown, no flooring is visible. The walls are opus incertum. The southwest wall of the southern end of the southeast wall, and the western end of the northwest wall are all preserved to a greater height than the rest of the walls. All walls preserved some plaster with some paint remaining. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
This space is to the northwest of room 12 (5128)
It is to the northwest of the atrium.

DESCRIPTION: In the northeast wall we see a tall niche suitable for a cupboard for kitchen equipment.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Close to the lararium and basin.

DESCRIPTION: There is a well defined niche cupboard in the southwest of this small dining room. There is a red dado and a cream top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is west of the entry to the room.

DESCRIPTION: The platform entrance to the passageway 11 on the east reflects the level of the parking area. Adjacent to the oven and off the passageway is a low door leading to a rectangular room used for food preparation. Probably this was a room where the kneading machine was used.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Passageway 11 on the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square mosaic, positioned to indicate the placement of triclinia. As one steps into this room, the mosaic is centered in the room above the step. There is a black and white patterned border. It is a double strand rope pattern within black and white borders. The central portion preserves three complete and one fragmentary triangle in an alternating black and white pattern. These fragments are the only remaining pieces of opus sectile.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This mosaic is to the southeast of the doorway and northwest of the painted feature 6973.

DESCRIPTION: To the south west from entrance 1 to the caupona sits a long, low bench along the sidewalk. The property is unexcavated and the identification of it as a caupona is based on Eschebach, and based upon that we are taking this as a dining bench. The bench is made from tufa stone. Just to note, immediately above the bench is frescoed plaster which shows evidence of painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the south west of bench 4156.

DESCRIPTION: In the east corner of horticultural space 14 is currently located a large dolium, broken across the top but with most of the body intact. Eschebach listed the dolium as embedded but it now sits on top of the ground. The bottom is flat and pieces of the rim indicate a large opening.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the north of cistern 4164.

DESCRIPTION: This space (9) is a kitchen in the Villa Arianna. This large square space is entered through a single doorway at the north end of the northeast wall. The room is currently a storage depot for excavated materials. No original flooring is visible. The walls are uncut stone. The upper portions are reconstructed as is the ceiling. There is a very large cooking platform (4711) with three arched openings. This platform is located along the southeast wall with the east corner containing a hearth *4712). There is a preparation platform (4713) along the northeast wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This kitchen is located to the southeast of a small cubiculum (4715). Outside the east end of the northeast wall is a fishpond (4714). There is a service courtyard to the northeast of the kitchen.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this feature in dining room 2 as a platform. It is a narrow platform running along the northwest wall, terminating in the west corner with a stepped shelf. The platform is stone construction, opus incertum, with the stepped shelf made of ceramic brick and tiles. While this identified as a preparation platform, we have also noted that this could have served as a bench, making the nature of the room suitable for dining.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This platform is to the northwest of platform 6849.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small rectangular room on an east/west axis. At the north end of the northeast wall is a low doorway to a fauces with a modern lintel and a stepped tufa threshold. The floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. Plaster survives on the northeast and west walls with a red lower register and white above. This is identified as a storeroom because of its utilitarian decoration and the function of the property as a whole.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Fauces 1 is to the east.

DESCRIPTION:
The L shaped counter occupies the S.W. part of room 1. The counter is about 1 meter in height and appears heavily reconstructed. The top surface is covered, predominantly, in white marble slabs. The counter is provided with a recess for a circular container. Situated towards the Northeast, seen at the bottom of the recess is a rectangular opening in the N.W. wall. On the West-
ern end of the Southwestern side of the counter, there are traces of (2) shelves protruding from the Northwestern wall. Both were used for a display of goods.

One enters the shop from the S.W. through the wide door. Approximately one-half of the door is blocked by the counter. The L shaped counter occupies most of the S.E. part of the room. The room is rectangular on the S.E./N.W. axis, seen in the North corner in the N.E. wall is a doorway to room #2. From the N.E. wall is a doorway to room #3. The original height of the building is unknown, but stairs situated in the East corner of the N.E. wall indicate the presence of a 2nd floor. The construction of the floor is indeterminate. Stucco,
present on the wall, indicates that rooms were stuccoed and probably painted, even though no decorations remain there.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to room #1 to the North and room #3, situated to the N.E..

DESCRIPTION: There are stones placed before the latrine which suggest steps. The latrine/toilet is built up with stone on three sides. Above the toilet is a very small rectangular window opening to the cooking platform. On the northwest wall is evidence of a square blocked up wndow.

DESCRIPTION: This is a square room with a plaster earth floor. There is an arched ceiling with traces of plaster. At the North end of the West wall, is a doorway with modern lintel and a threshold. At the East end of the North wall, a narrow doorway has been inserted with no threshold. Extensive restoration on all 4 walls, is apparent. The detail in the room, includes pieces of plastic.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 17, is located to the West and room 15 is situated to the North.

DESCRIPTION: The small rectangular room is situated on a North/South axis. The floor is obscured by earth and debris. At the West end of the North wall, is a doorway with modern lintel. No threshold is present. Situated high in the West wall, there is a plastered rectangular window, narrowing to the street, outside. Situated high in the East wall, there is a window or a collapse to room, #18. The ceiling is vaulted, with all 4 walls showing signs of restoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 17, is situated to the North.

DESCRIPTION: Situated on the West wall of Dining room #3, is a fairly long curved back couch niche. It is plastered, and begins 1 meter to the North of the doorway and is covered with red painted plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: In the N.W. corner of room #3.

DESCRIPTION: The extensive rectangular garden runs along the northwest/southeast axis. It is divided into halves by a long euripius which is decorated with an elegant fountain in the middle of the garden and a basin just southeast of the elegant fountain. The elegant fountain is covered by a pergola supported by four small brick columns. The basin is divided into four unequally sized parts which is decorated by a small temple structure: Four short columns support a vaulted arch finally decorated with white vegetable motifs on a red background. The northwestern portion of the euripius is ornamented with a semicircular vaulted niche supported by four little steps. In the middle of this painted niche is a hole for spouting water. The informative panel says that "The fruit trees... were there in antiquity. The root holes of these original trees were found... There was a double row of smaller trees, which scholars at the time identified as quince and pomegranate trees. The garden was restored again more recently, planting beds of iris and acanthus along the edges...". The walls are heavily restored to a first floor height. The garden is accessible from the house through stairs on either side of the porticus in Room 16. A street entrance (posticum 2.2.5) is situated at the opposite side of the space. This door gives easy access to the nearby amphitheater. This entrance into the garden is framed by a row of brink columns which support modern wooden beams. Excavation records mention the evidence for a masonry triclinium (2826) and amphorae (2827) which are no longer extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 16 to the northwest; Bounded on the remaining three sides by streets. Room 16 to the northwest; Bounded on the remaining three sides by streets. None

DESCRIPTION: The mill oven room is access from the southwest stress side entrance and is on a northwest east to southwest axis. The large rectangular room contains three mills and a single meta, and a large beehive oven and water feature - other. The west area of the room is entered through a wide entrance with a threshold containing a shutter channel and out of hours entry door typical of commercial properties. Immediately southeast of the threshold is an entry to room two (2) processing room with a volcanic stone threshold. The three mills are aligned to the northwest side of the room with the first mill closest to the west corner and the other two mills located northeast of the first. The third mills is located in the enter of the room. Surrounding each mills are paving stones used by animals for turning the mills. Small buttresses or short walls are located in the middle of the room with one on the northwest wall and one on the southwest wall. Southwest of this buttress on the southeast wall is located a meta, possibly not in its original position. In the east end of room one (1) is located the oven in the north corner along the northeast wall and a doorway on the northeast wall in the east corner. Partially obscuring the doorway on the north east wall is a masonry platform for stairs which includes a reused threshold stone at the base. The doorway on the northeast wall contains a segmented threshold in stone and a modern wooden lintel, immediately above which are three round beam holes and a window. The water feature is-other is located in the north corner in front of the oven. The ancient floors of the mill oven floor are obscured by lapilli with exception to the volcanic stones surrounding the mills. The property has received extensive restoration especially the pastry walls shared with the property 6-2-4 which was bombed in WW II. Trace of plaster survive in the northeast end of room one(1) on the the northeast wall and the southeast wall but the colors and decoration are not discernible. A small window is located at the top of the southeast wall, in the middle. There are four beam holes present on the southeast wall, one at the upper floor at the southeast end of the wall, one at the ground floor level of the south wall, the middle of the wall, two (2) at the southwest wall, one at ground level and one at upper floor level. There are three beam holes located on the northwest wall, one north of the most northeasterly mill, one in the middle of the wall between middle and most northeasterly mills, and one behind the middle mill.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room one (1) is contiguous to room four (4) in the east and room two (2) to the south.

DESCRIPTION:
Excavations in 1951-52 were unpublished but Jashemski refers to soil contours of rectangular planting beds. Maiuri suggests that cabbage was grown here. Jashemski also refers to four basins and a cistern.
Large rectangular garden area occupies the south and east of the insula enclosing the property. The baths are to the west and north. The walls are extensively restored. In the center of the southeast wall there is a gate to the amphitheater. The exterior wall of the atrium complex 18 has extensive traces of Pompeian first style. Two doorways open to the garden peristyle. The western door has a threshold with three steps and the eastern has two restored side walls of which only the lower course is preserved. Immediately south is a large, poorly preserved masonry platform. The eastern quarter of the platform contains an inserted rectangular basin. No traces of interior lining survive (one of the basins referred to by Jashemski?) Immediately NE is a modern cover of the Fontina aqueduct. Against the N wall to the S of the bath latrine, is a circular cistern surmounted by a lead water pipe. To the east of the latrine there is the rectangular masonry base of a water basin. Traces of plaster survive on the internal and external surfaces. The south external wall of the atrium complex 18 contains joist holes. Their purpose is unclear. Two ancient tree roots survive. The modern garden is planted with pear, apple and pomegranate trees.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle garden 3 to NW

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a painting. It is located at the upper portion of the southeast wall filling a painted, arched space. A large bird is in the center facing east. The bird is positioned on a shelf or ledge. Along the length of this ledge are four bunches of cherries.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The painting is located to the southeast of mosaic 6969 and also southeast of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small central floor mosaic. It was tagged as restored in 1996. The mosaic is a black and white pattern of squares and lozenge shapes comprising four octagons. The position of the central mosaic indicates the triclinia would have been placed along the northwest, northeast and southeast walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mosaic is east of the niche cupboard (6970), and east of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: This is a medium-sized dolium. It is imbedded in the ground in situ fully intact. This dolium is straight-sided with carinated shoulders rising inward to a slightly flaring rim. Approximately two thirds of the dolium is below ground. It is made of terracotta.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dolium is located directly southeast of 4989 and northwest of 4991. It is northeast of 4988.

DESCRIPTION: In the bakery V-3-8 we have identified room 12 as a storeroom due to its small size, utilitarian painting and position immediately off a mill room #4. The room is roughly square with its tall doorway opening to its southwest into the mill room. The northeast wall has a tiny square window opening to the street outside, high up on the wall. Construction is opus incertum with patches of red and yellow plaster near the bottoms of the walls. Floor is lapilla. A small part of a mill sits in the south corner of the room a puteal sits in the west corner of the room. Neither appears to be situ. There is no ceiling

DESCRIPTION:
Small rectangular room on northeast - southwest axis opening through two doorways with stepped threshold to garden 6. The two doorways are separated by a pillar. Both doorways have modern lintels. Traces of undecorated plaster survive on the northeast wall and southeast wall. Extensive modern restoration on all walls, especially in the upper registers, to modern ceiling. In the south corner there is a cupboard niche (6972). Identification of the kitchen is based on size, and proximity to dining rooms 8 and tablinum 9.

Bibliography: Eschebach, p.38

DESCRIPTION: In the eastern most corner of dining room 49, there is a square structure with a rectangular opening about 1 to 1 1/2 meter ih from the floor facing the south. The opening is about 2 meters deep and goes down below the opening-- close to floor level. The room is locked (and we are not able to go in and measure) but we can see some post hole openings inside the room. The outside of the cupboard is decorated in Architectural style (see room 6913) and acts as a divider for two triclinia.

DESCRIPTION:
This house is not completed. This structure is also known as "House of Theseus", "House of the Seven Skeletons", and "House of the American Admiral". It has been determined that this early house may have been used as a commercial property or solely as domestic. There is a very wide door on the south wall and it is very high. We immediately see a very large room. The floor is covered with debris of plastic molds, signs, broken stones and plastic sheeting. The floor is vegetation, debris, and lapilli. a threshold stone is discernible in some places. There is some sign of plaster on the two front walls. This is a rectangular room, oriented north, south, east, west. The back wall has a small rectangular window frame, covered with plastic. The wall is painted with red, orange, white, and yellow in non-discernible shapes. The roof slopes from the east to the west onto this wall, and it totally covered with modern materials. In the west wall is a small doorway to the atrium. The north and west walls repeat the colors of the back wall in about a fourth of the wall.The north east corner of the eastern wall shows an indentation. The front part of the wall juts out and the back part recedes.

Eschebach 257

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this as a house and identified the room as a kitchen. The conditions within the room: the walls are plastered, the floor is mud, and the ceiling is modern. Windows are placed appropriately to vent smoke. There is a rectangular window next to the lintel of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: This is a quarter round platform in the south east corner of the tomb enclosure. It is higher than the other platform in the north east corner (6581) of the enclosure. This has a fourth style dado painting with a black background, deep red Pompeiian border and green plants.

The vaulted triclinium is situated along the middle of the southwest side of the peristyle. One enters the triclinium from the northeast through the wide doorway that extends almost the width of the opening. A wide but shallow rectangular space precedes the triclinium whose dining couches take up the rest of the space within the room. In the middle of the southwest wall above the ten steps that rise up and back into the wall, the steps appear to descend through a large rectangular opening constructed as if to reflect a cave. At the top of the stairs is an opening that penetrates through the wall. The lower portion of the walls of the room, the floor and most of the triclinium couch is covered with marble. On the southwest wall on either side of the stairs is a semicircular niche. On the southeast and northwest walls is a rectangular niche. High on the southwest wall above the stairs is a large rectangular window on a vertical axis. The southwest wall still retains the marble facing from the level of the triclinium couch up to the level of the first step of the staircase. The southeast and northwest walls also had a similar marble facade only a little of which still remains. From the top level of the marble facade and upward, the walls were painted with various scenes. Still extant is the western corner of the northwest wall and the north corner of the northwest wall. A small portion also remains on the southeast wall. The interior of the northeast wall on either side of the entrance appears to have lacked the marble facade. As reconstructed, the ceiling has a barrel vault.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 2 to the northeast

DESCRIPTION: Space 2 is accessible from the southwestern side of entrance 1. This huge space includes a number of features. Stone stairs to the northwest leading up to a missing story, a masonry couch triclinium with two enjoined water structures at the back (to the west) a cooking platform opposite the masonry couch to the northeast, a cellar to the southeast along the perimeter wall of the structure. The remaining space to the south is today planted as a vineyard. Along the northwest wall a small entrance connects space two with the enjoined lamps workshop; however the two structures seem not to be related to the same building. The space between the entrance and the masonry couch triclinium to the southwest wall with the pathways running along the vines are paved with regularly shaped blocks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Processing rooms (3) to the east; Entrance to the north; cellar to the southeast. Processing rooms (3) to the east; Entrance to the north; cellar to the southeast.

DESCRIPTION: At the southeast end of the underground wine cellar running the entire width of the cellar is a wall approx. one half the height of the room that together with the walls create a deep vat. The walls of the vat are lined with opus signinum so as to prevent leakage. The vat is approx. square in shape.

We have identified V-1-18 as a house and have determined that room 19 is a dining room. We have based this determination on its very large front opening to the peristyle garden, on the presence of central rectangular mosaic panel in the mosaic tiled floor and its very elaborate colorful frescoed walls. The room is entered primarily from the peristyle, but also has an entrance to the NE from dining hall 13. The room is roughly square. The upper portion of the walls and roof are restored and the lower walls are frescoed and painted. The dado is black with red, green and yellow lines setting off what appears to be garden symbolism. The main panels are red and it is only on the NW wall does any trace of painting remain in the form of a centrally located primary panel. The panel appears mythological with a central couple, male and female surrounded by three winged cupids (Diana and Actaeon) (NW wall) and Judgement of Paris. The third scene is no longer present.

DESCRIPTION: This oven differs in many ways from typical baker's ovens. The beehive component of the oven is enclosed, and is typical in interior but the door is a rhomboid, not arched. There is no fuel storage area, and no water basin. On the east side of the oven door, there is a narrow recessed area behind the room wall. It does not give access to a preparation room and it is too narrow for moving loaves of bread (panis quadratus) outside of the oven door, to the south there is a platform. There is no passage way to the room for baked bread.

This is the Villa of Arianna. This space (10) has been identified as a cubiculum due to its size.

This is a partially preserved, rectangular space on a northwest/southeast axis; only the southwest portion of the space remains. The remaining walls are almost entirely reconstructed. There is white marble which would have been a threshold for a doorway at the west end of the southwest wall.

The bottom portion of the northeast, southeast and southwest walls preserves fresco with white backgrounds with red banding and reinserted decorative panels. There is one in the center of the southeast wall and one in the center of the southwest wall (4716). The floor only preserves the underbed for what is presumed to be a mosaic floor. The walls are brick at the lower level with greystone opus reticulatum above. The walls are reconstructed with post holes above a brick section. They support a reconstructed ceiling. The room is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is adjacent to the courtyard to its northeast and is directly northwest of the kitchen (9).

DESCRIPTION: There is a long, shallow, high couch niche extending along almost the entirety of the north wall. Traces of undecorated plaster survive. The base is obscured by earth and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North side of dining room from northeast corner.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
We have identified this room as a dining room. This identification is based on the location, as it opens on to the atrium (17) through a very tall doorway. One enters the room over a wide white stone threshold with cuttings for a door. A much shorter secondary doorway is in the western corner of the room, through the northwest wall. This door also has a stone threshold and one steps down to the level of the dining room floor, although at the time of this visit the room is undergoing restoration and the floor is mostly covered. We can see traces of a cocciopesto surface. The walls are well preserved in height with a small, high window centrally placed in the northeast wall. The painting decoration was first style with a dado supporting large panels, which may have been black separated by vertical red bands. Above this panel level is a section of plaster encrustation (rectangular forms imitating colored stone blocks). There are horizontal bands of plaster molding, one above and another below these rectangular blocks, best preserved on the northeast and southeast walls. On the northwest wall an arched molding springs from the north corner attesting to a vaulted ceiling on a northwest-southeast axis. The ceiling above is reconstructed. Overall the condition of this room is fair.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room opens up to the atrium (17). It is adjacent to the northwest side of (19)

DESCRIPTION: Two large ashlar blocks are on a raised portion of the floor.

DESCRIPTION:
A floor-to-ceiling covered niche is located on the North corner of the East wall.
The niche extends approximately half of the total wall distance beginning at the North corner to the door. The interior is covered with red and yellow plaster with remains of red paint. The niche appears to have extended from floor to ceiling. Cupboard niche designation was determined based upon recently work by P. Allison.
Minor metal repair 'wings' appear along mortar line repair on the lower right area.

Large rectangular room at northeast corner of the property. Axis of the room is north northwest by southeast. Little plaster remains on any of the walls. Four joists on the east wall and approximately ten holes, evidence of a second story. With opus quadratum above, incertum below (no wall). Three small high windows located directly below the joists in the northeast wall. Access to the room was provided by a small doorway on the south wall and the southwest corner. Room was identified as a dining room because of (1) the size, (2) view through small doorway led to a large open area, and (30) floor is lapilli and weed.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is in northeast corner of the whole structure. To the southwest is dining room 27, to the south east is dining room 29, and due south through the doorway is room 30, an open area for carts.

DESCRIPTION: Entering the dining room through large southwestern entrance with marble threshold with holes for a door. Rectangular room with a north/south axis. Room had high lintel and posts (as reconstructed). Floor is lower than threshold. The floor retains no mosaic work. Walls go to second floor. On the southeast wall there is a rectangular window opening to the street on the second floor. No ancient ceiling. Currently protected by modern cover. Walls show late plaster, apparently third style. From the center of the room the view to atrium impluvium is partially blocked by a pilaster of tufa block and brick alternating courses. The room overlooks atrium with impluvium, which is next to large entrance vestibule. There are no features.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room (6) to the south. Room (6) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: The L-shaped counter is located in the northeast part of the room, slightly inside. The short arm to the northwest runs parallel to the sidewalk on a northeast/southwest axis. On the northeast end of the short arm there is a step shelf, which has three steps. The top two steps extend to the northwest wall of the shop. The bottom step extends only to the exterior side of the short arm. All three steps extend into the exterior of the shop to the southeast, beyond the interior wall of the short arm. The long arm, perpendicular to the short arm, extends about 3/4 of the way into the interior of the shop on a northwest/southeast axis. Embedded in the long arm, just before it meets the short arm, is a small dolium. At the base on the exterior, (northwest and southwest) sides of the L-shaped counter appears to be a step on a higher level than the floor. At the southeast end of the long arm is a hearth, the width of which is wider than that of the long arm. The hearth is roughly rectangular in shape, on a northwest/southeast axis. The floor of the hearth is higher than that of the room. The cooking platform is defined by a U-shaped construction opening to the southeast. As extant, the cooking platform is on a slightly lower level than the long arm. The L-shaped counter was stuccoed and painted red. There is no evidence of color and decoration on the hearth. The step shelves are constructed of cement and brick, while the surface of the L-shaped counter employs fragments of tile and stone rubble. On the interior face of the short arm of the north corner, below the step shelves, is a recess that may have supported a dolium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Lararium (2804) to the south None Lararium (2804) to the south

DESCRIPTION: We enter from a small doorway from the oven room (12, 6804) on the north end of the north west wall. There is a remnant of a tufa threshold. This is a small rectangular room. The south west wall includes the beehive encasement of the oven in the adjacent room. In the south corner, we see the remains of a water tank. In the east corner, there are remains of a platform. There is no plaster or painting. The floor is littered with broken amphorae, chunks of plaster wall and chunks of marble. The floor itself is mud and stones.

This feature has been identified as a couch niche in the south corner of the southeast wall of dining room (27). It is a shallow recess which is fairly wide but short, and preserved some of its plaster and painted surface, which is red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature shows that a couch would lie along the southwest wall below large window.

DESCRIPTION: Dining niche (6843) is on the northeast wall of the new corner of the room. It is a slight slope to permit more room for a couch. There is a red dado and a cream top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is east of niche 4844.

DESCRIPTION: The dining niche (6844) is on the southwest wall of the new corner of the room. It is a slight slope to permit more room for a couch. There is a red dado and a cream top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is west of niche (6843).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this feature as a couch niche. It is a long indentation along the southeast wall. It is cut into the wall and is low and shallow. The length of this is uncommon. Frescoes can be seen along the back of the niche, preserving black paint.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This niche is located south of the doorway.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified structure V.3.8 as a bakery based upon a mill room with oven. Eschebach tells us that the large square area at the back of the building was a stable. The room is sitting on a southwest/northeast axis. There are no remains of plaster on any of the 4 opus incertum walls. There is no evidence of windows except a small vertical slit in the southwest wall. There are also 2 post holes in that same walls that appears to have had something attached, perhaps a shelf. The floor is rubble and overgrown with grass. The threshold is narrow and is the only access to the room. It is located in the east corner of the room. At the west end of the southwest wall there is an indentation in the wall that appears to be almost a perfect circle, although it simply, maybe missing stone. There is no lintel or wall above the threshold and no ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the west of garden 7.

DESCRIPTION:
large platform with two inlets for food/ drink storage
setup to one of dolia
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Bottom of grinder on floor in foreground. Side doorway to corridor; back doorway to back room. side doorway to corridor; back doorway to backroom bottom of grinder on floor in foreground
TIME_COUNT: not specified but in footage 29:39-32:08 LB RW

DESCRIPTION:
This is the Villa Arianna.

We have identified this space (12) as a dining room due to its size, location and decoration. The northwest portion of this space is no longer extant, the remaining space suggests a square room. much of the mosaic floor remains, which is white with a double black band defining the central area. There are no traces of the northwest wall. The northeast wall is preserved only in a very low wall of opus incertum rising to a small section of grey cut stone with rubble fill towards the north corner. The southeast and southwest walls are better preserved with fresco in fourth style preserving a high yellow dado punctuated by black panels with mythological sea creatures. Two panels near the south corner of the southeast wall have been cut away. In the center zone of the walls are large black panels with remains of a figurative scene on the southeast wall and a female figure depicted directly on the black panel on the south west wall. There is a black panel on both the south and east ends of the southeast wall. The black panels alternate with short red panels supporting windows painted above. There are paper copies of the frescoes painted near the south corner. On the southeast just below the painted window on the southwest wall the copy includes the window and vignette. The upper portion of the walls are reconstructed.

This room is under the covering above the large atrium. The remaining southwest wall has a cut stone portion preserved at the western end of the wall. To the south of this there is lower brickwork supporting opus reticulatum. This room is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northeast of the tablinum and to the southwest of the cliff face.

DESCRIPTION: In bakery V.3.8 the mill room is large, opens directly off of fauces 1, and was originally the atrium of a home. The room has been identified by the presence of an almost intact mill, two mill bases, a large beehive oven, and an impluvium turned into a water basin. The walls are opus incertum with a solid southwest wall abutting property V.3.7. The northwest wall contains a lararium. Also along this wall is dining tablinum 15, with its two windows and large doorway to the north. It is followed by a doorway to andron 15. The northeast of the room contains doorways to storerooms 10, 11, 12, and 14. The southeast wall of the room contains the oven to the east and an entrance to fauces 1 in the center. Platform 4181 takes up the remaining space to the south. The three mills create an "l" shape along the southwest and northwest walls of the room, with space around them paved for donkeys. The impluvium in the center of the room has been turned into a waterproof basin, with a cistern head on its north corner. It is only around the mill bases that any trace of floor pavement remains. The room is undecorated except for a trace of plaster by prep platform 4181.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The mill room is to the northwest of fauces 1, to the southwest of storerooms 10 and 11, to the west of storerooms 12 and 14, to the south of andron 15, and to the southeast of dining tablinum 5.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified house VI-10-11 a a house and at the back of the house is a colonnaded garden [Room 20], with the remains of a triclinium as its center. The three exterior garden walls to the northeast and northwest abut property VI-10-7, the House of the Anchor. The southwest wall abuts the street and the southeast wall faces Area 19. The garden had a portico on the southeast supported by two pillars and four columns. According to Jashemski these were joined by a low wall which had a space at the top for plants. In the middle of the garden was a masonry triclinium which Jashemski suggests was probably shaded by a pergola. The back wall of the garden to the northwest has two rows of postholes. The lower row of postholes continues along the northeast wall. A door to the street is located in the southwest wall and has two steps up leading to it. Directly behind the colonnade on the southeast is a drain with a drain hole at the southwest end leading to the street. It is lined with stone. The southwest wall has a window to the street on either side of the doorway.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the northwest of Area 19.

DESCRIPTION: Situated to the West of the entrance VI-1-2, was located an L shaped masonry bench. The long arm abuts and is parallel with the SW wall of VI-1-2, as seen in a SE/NW axis. The short arm is roughly perpendicular to the long arm. The axis is situated to the West of a NE/SW axis. As reconstructed, the top is made of fragments of roof tiles and cement. The masonry structure was , from the most I can tell, covered with stucco. No decoration remains, if any.

The square counter room is open to the S.W. of the street. The Northwestern section of the room is occupied by an L shaped counter. The threshold of the large entrance door is covered with marble slabs, divided by a channel for a sliding door which extends for the length of the threshold. The walls running NW/SE, are about 2m high and are preserved. Situated in the middle of the Northeastern side is large brick plaster, in a position of adjoining. It is a stone foundation, for the stairs. The floor is now covered with lapilli. No longer is there an existing roof or ceiling. There are traces of plaster, seen on the N.W. wall, behind the counter.
Situated to the South of the entrance, it is framed by (7) blocks of stone, forming a pillar, while to the West; only (3) remain
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous. is room 2; to the N.E.

DESCRIPTION: You enter the room from the SW, through a door situated to the NW of the counter. The room is roughly square in shape. The counter occupies the SE part of the room. Seen, opposite the N.E. end of the counter is a room situated to the NW, it is room #2. In the North corner is a doorway, leading to dining rooms, 3 and 4. Situated in the E corner, is a doorway leading to room #5. Seen, in the SE wall, behind the counter is a doorway that is leading to room #6. The height of the room is indeterminate. The walls are plastered, and no decoration remains. The floors of the room are indeterminate.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 6, situated to the S.E.. Room 5, is to the East and room 4 is to the North. Room 3, is situated to the North.

DESCRIPTION: One enters the room from the northwest through Room 8. The room is rectangular in shape on a northeast/southwest axis. The southeast side of the room is defined by a series of pillars, eight in number, on axis. The northeast end of the room is defined by the biclinium with fountain. The southwest end is delimited by the zoothecula (possible dining room). The northwest side is defined by a wall painted to represent three large windows looking on to an expanse containing wild animals (paradeisoi). On the northwest side abutting on the euripus is a series of columns supporting a roof, creating a covered colonnade. In the center is a long rectangular euripus on axis running from just in front of the zoothecula all the way to the biclinium between the two couches. The area between the pillars and the columns was probably unroofed in antiquity. Two small bridges cross the euripus, just in front of the doorway to the triclinium (2871). To the southeast of the second bridge is the platform forming the front part of a large fountain overlooking the sunken garden. The floor is of beaten cement.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining Room (2871) to the northwest; Dining Room (2824) to the southwest; Dining Garden (2825) to the southeast; Room 8 to the southwest. Dining Room (2871) to the northwest; Dining Room (2824) to the southwest; Dining Garden (2825) to the southeast; Room 8 to the southwest. None

DESCRIPTION: The high bench, approximately 50 centimeters high) runs along the northwest wall of the shop (2.1.1) off the street. The top of the bench is tiled. Because of it close proximity to the shop the bench was probably used by the customers of the same shop; however the bench continues along the northeastern wall of the fauces of the house (2.2.2). It is an L shaped bench overall. Another bench is situated on the opposite (northeast) wall. Both the L-shaped bench to the northeast were used by the clients awaiting to greet the master of the house during the morning ritual salutatio. Once the ritual was completed, the same benches may have been used by the customers of the adjoining shop.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: None None None

DESCRIPTION: Entered by a low doorway in the south wall from kitchen 7, dining room 6 is rectangular and is on an east/west axis. This room was identified as a dining room because of its larger size. Three upper story beam holes are seen in the north wall with one more possibility for a beam hole in the west wall at about the same height. The west wall appears to have had a doorway that was closed up and plastered over in antiquity. Remains of plaster are predominately found on that west wall. Floor is lapilli. There are no windows visible today in the room. In the northeast corner of the room where the two walls join together, currently there are, at ceiling height, three larger sized tufa blocks stacked one on top of the other with an indentation above. This could be either an upper floor beam support or simply fallen masonry.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: North and west walls abut the adjoining property. The east wall abuts dining room 5. The south wall abuts kitchen 7.

DESCRIPTION: This feature has been identified as a painting. It is a food and drink subject due to its depiction of Bacchus holding his wine cup. It is a mythological scene with the figure against a bluish background. Bacchus reclines against a tree with craggy rocks behind and a large trireme is seen in the water in the background to his right with faint architecture to his left.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This painting is directly below painting 4251 and to the east of painting 4254.

DESCRIPTION: In the Villa of the Mysteries we have four wide areas (31, Room 35, 42, 81) that are similar to porches that have dining rooms and other roms that are open and passageways that are open to them. We have suggested that the dining could take place in this area based upon its unusually wide width and formal flooring. The floor is of cut tesserae in white with colored stone inserts. It is bordered by a solid black band, with solid white tesserae on the outside. The walls are largely restored with some traces in small areas of plaster. This area is rectangular and is on a northwest/southeast axis. The ceiling is restored and a series of four columns and a low wall divide the area from the formal garden beyond to the west and northwest.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest of Rooms 46, 45, 48, 49. To the southwest of 80, northeast of 84, southeast of Garden 82, 83.

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a raised masonry base containing a circular terracotta wellhead, the lip of which does not survive. The base is obscured by earth and lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is due west of passageway 4259

DESCRIPTION: Eschebach 1993: 13.

This painting, presented as a square panel in the center of the south west wall in the upper yellow register, is one of four around the room each of which depicts food and drink. Although this painting is not well preserved, a series of what may be four cups can be identified based on a comparison with the cups on the northeast wall (4252).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The feature is above the painting of Andromeda. It is to the west of painting 4251, 4253 and 4254; south west of 4249 and directly across from 4252 on the north east wall.

DESCRIPTION: In bakery V.3.8, in the southern corner of room 4, two masonry ends are left which would designate a preparation platform. The platform would have abutted the southeast wall, and the spacing of the two ends as well as their width indicate quite a large platform top (probably originally of wood). The platform end in the southern corner of the room is just slightly higher than its partner, but there is no indication of what the original total height would have been.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the southwest of oven 4188 and to the south of all other features in the room.

DESCRIPTION: Large marble covered L-shaped counter bordering onto street; Has area for fire for keeping food/drink warm at end. One dolia visible in counter top.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Interior cooking platform. Storage area behind open area to left (from street). storage area behind open area to left (from street) interior cooking platform

DESCRIPTION: In bakery V.3.8's mill room 4 sits a base to a mill. It is constructed in a circular form of brick and stone. The interior of the circle is hollow. No other parts of the mill remain. Paving stones surround the mill on the ground, indicating the path around which the mill would have been turned.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Prep platform 4181 is to the southeast, oven 4188 is to the east, and mill 4183 is to the northwest. Basin 4187, cistern 4186, and mill 4184 can be found at varying degrees to the northeast.

DESCRIPTION: This is a small rectangular passageway joining the atrium (2) to the kitchen (4258), defined by the doorway to the kitchen to the north and contiguous with the atrium to the south. It has an earth floor. The western half of the space consists of well head (4255).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous with kitchen (4258) to the north and Atrium (2) to the south

DESCRIPTION: One enters the kitchen from a short doorway past the storeroom near the floor on the SW wall of the hallway. The entrance is on the South. In the SE corner just after entering the room is the preparation platform. In the North corner is an L-shaped cooking platform. The area along the NW wall has a built-up structure used as a drain that opens through a small hole into the garden. On the West corner of the SW wall, adjacent to the West end of the cooking platform, is the latrine. The floor seems to be of a simple beaten plaster. High on the NW wall is a window that opens onto the garden. The walls of the kitchen were at one time plastered and painted. Decorations indeterminate. On the East wall, above the preparation platform is a lararium painting that has almost completely disappeared. A portion of the floor below the lararium, between the preparation and cooking platforms, is missing today. On the NE wall, in the East corner, there seems to have been two post holes on line with the post holes that supported the roof of the storeroom. On the SW wall, just after you enter the room, is a small hole that may have served as a lamp niche. As reconstructed, there is no evidence of the height of the ceiling above the window on the NW wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Storeroom (5) to SE. (2) to SW. Storeroom (5) to SE. (2) to SW. None

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that the House of the Little Fountain is a domestic structure. We have identified room 20 as a store room. This identification is based on its location directly to the South East of the kitchen and the presence of post holds insets on which shelving would have been placed. The room is rectangular on a North East - South West axis with an entrance no longer in existence on the North East wall. Some trace of red plaster remains on the north end of the North West wall. Construction is opus reticulatum divided into three bands by coursed of flat rectangular brick. The ceiling is reconstructed and two ceiling height post holes on the North West and South East walls indicate there was probably an upper storey in antiquity. Shelving post holes are located on the South East and South West walls. A fairly high small windown is located on the North West wall that probably provided venting for the kitchen beyond In addition, directly above the window are the remains of a fairly large round terracotta pipe. The floor appears to be of concrete.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to the South East of kitchen 18 and to the South West of stairway 21.

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that the room is a dining room within a residential structure. This identification is based on the room location within the structure, on the presence of designated food and drink features, which are paintings, and on the structure of the room with a prominent window, vaulted ceiling and high doorway.
The entrance to this room comes from the atrium (22) and is a tall doorway in the west end of the north west wall. There is no threshold and the mosaic flooring no longer remains.
The frescoes remain on all four walls, going to various heights, and are in fair condition.
The vaulted ceiling remains, and has been conserved. There is a large window in the upper arched section of the north east wall. This has been conserved and is glazed.
Generally the wall decoration consists of a red dado and white sections above. These are in the fourth style. Each wall has a central tableau (designated features 6551-6554).
The north east wall is in the best preservation, with the frescoes preserved in part to the ceiling and with the wall and ceiling moldings intact.
Atrium (22) is to the west and the room 25 is north west of it.

This is the House of the Vettii.

This is an upper centre panel above the black framed panels. There are two figures in the centre, one reclining man with his head turned towards a standing figure of a woman in the act of pouring fluid into his mouth. This is a Dionystic figure with a faun left - behind it is a Thrysas holding figure of Dionysus. Upper register located on northern end of the north-west wall.

In the western leg of the u-shaped tomb enclosure on its northernmost wall there is a large painting of a pomegranate tree on a black or blue background. The painting is faded except for the pomegranates which you can make out clearly. Fifteen pomegranates are visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: All other paintings in the room are on the south or east legs of the u.

DESCRIPTION: We enter this elegant dining room from the south corner of the peristyle. There is an engaged column in the south wall. We can also enter the dining room from the northeastern end of the biclinium room, From the vantage of the door to the biclinium room (long passage biclinium with water feature). We see an intact wall with concrete. We see 4th style decorations on all walls. The ceiling is in place and we see nine coffers and four of them are framed recesses bordered on red. Besides the two doorways, which have lovely views, we can see on the east wall a low rectangular window overlooking the garden. There is a platform before the garden. The bottom zone of the paintings are black with green stencils with gryphons. The next zone has a central panel on the southwestern wall that has been removed. On either side of all the panels are elongated, painted Vitruvian style columns. The top zone has a variety of immortals with attributes evident.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Peristyle to the north; cubiculum to the northwest; biclinium room to the northeast; garden to the southeast. Peristyle to the north; cubiculum to the northwest; biclinium room to the northeast; garden to the southeast. None

DESCRIPTION: Minority Report: We enter this long space for religious banquets from the southwest. It is currently a roofed area. Floor is lapilli. There are high walls on the northwest side. The northeast opens to an altar and a dining room, The southeast wall has a door to the large dining hall. There is also a rectangular lararium niche. In the west corner of the space we find dining room (Room 2). The space is bordered by two rounded and rectangular columns. Four columns also were within the space; two on either side (south and north) and was part of a colonnade.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Sacred Space (2841) to the northeast; Dining Hall (2843) to the southeast; Dining Room (2832) to the west. Sacred Space (2841) to the northeast; Dining Hall (2843) to the southeast; Dining Room (2832) to the west. None

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that 5-1-18 is a domestic house and that number 4 is a kitchen, based upon the presence of a large cooking platform topped with an oven. The kitchen is on a southeast-northwest axis and is accessed by a door in the south corner. Walls are opus incertum with some reconstruction present. Large post holes close to the top indicate that this was roofed with a second floor. The walls were plastered. The NE wall contains two windows providing ventilation and light from the street as well as an arched lararium with a shelf. The SE wall has what appears to be a large looters hole above the cooking platform. And high up (where the second story would be) is a second arched lararium. The NW wall is missing but appears to have divided the room off from another space along the street wall. The oven and cooking platform sit along the NE wall. The floor is rubble with a pile of dirt that appears to be from modern excavation from the room adjacent.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is to the NE of corridor 3 and storage room 15, to the NW of storage room 5

DESCRIPTION: On the north west wall of room 4 (kitchen), directly above cooking platform 4143 sits a rather small oven with an arched opening, tiled on the inside with a slight bee hive roof. The oven is made of opus incertum and has a tiled, cemented base.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Directly above and on the north west wall of cooking platform 4143, and to the north of lararium 4144.

DESCRIPTION: Square room, floor obscured by lapilli and debris throughout. At the southern end of the east wall there is a poorly preserved doorway with fragmentary tufa threshold, opening to posticum (1). Plaster survives on the north east and north west walls, with no visible decoration. High in the north wall there is a narrow rectangular window tapering to the street outside. Identification as a storeroom is based on its proximity to the kitchen.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Posticum (1) to the east.

DESCRIPTION: This is the Villa Arianna. This feature (4716) is in room (10) a cubiculum. It is a fresco painting in situ, although it appears to have been reinserted in the centre of the southwest wall. It has a red background bordered by a rectangular yellow band. Depicted in the center is a footed two-handled vessel with a wide lip 9footed karter). This is yellow with white highlights depicting fluted and banded decoration.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is to the south of the entrance of the room.

DESCRIPTION: Southwest wall are the remains of the latrine. Only the two bases remain - as reconstructed. The base on the NW wall abuts the wall and partially blocks an arched opening into the SW wall. The use of this archway is unknown.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: cooking platform to the North east and dolium to the east None cooking platform to the North east and dolium to the east

DESCRIPTION: This feature is a painting in the atrium of the House of the Vettii. It is a small detail in the wall directly south of the entrance to room 2, at the south corner of the southeast wall. This a small vignette at the bottom of a narrow section of wall. This is a red field on a yellow panel. Against this red background is a figure depicted feeding a pheasant out of a footed bowl. It is in poor condition.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This painting is directly to the south of room 2 and to the east of room 3.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with 3 entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, Entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and Entrance 9 is the back entrance.
We have identified this room as a large dining hall. We base this on its location, over looking water garden and nymphaeum. As we look at this garden we see "above a podium decorated with three large mosaic panels were niches each in the form of aedicula from the bottom of which water jetted down into a large pool with three shallow divisions. In each niche above the jet there was a small base for a statuette. In front of this ornate facade in the middle of the garden there was a shallow pool which had a jet in the center". (Jashemski II 107). There are nine columns surrounding the garden; two engaged and seven that show cement covering fluted doric columns and 1 with brick. Two of the columns are connected to pillars that hold aquaduct pipes. Water jetted out from these pipes into two fountain basins. The alter base portion of the aedicula show mosaic patterns of squares and triangles with white, cobalt and Egyptian blue tesserae. On the north east wall of the portico there is an arched lararium niche . The threshold of the dining hall is open almost the full width of the room on the north west side. The pattern of the mosaic floor show eleven double overlapping Greek keys across the threshold. Beyond this there is a double black border around the whole floor of white background. Most of the center of the floor is missing. The two side walls show minimal evidence of plaster. The south east wall show more plaster.

Floor was restored in 1996.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Portico and colonaded water garden to the north west. dining room 25 to the west.

DESCRIPTION: Surrounding the podium of altar tomb 6576 is a walled u-shaped space. The long arms of the u run in a north-south direction and the short arm of the u is on the south side of the tomb podium (the north side of the tomb podium abuts an exterior wall). Beginning with the east arm of the u, the axis runs north to south and the northern most end contains platform 6581. The southeastern corner contains platform 6582. The entire walkway is enclosed by a high wall and on both the wall and the podium there is a series of fresco paintings. The walls are of varying heights and the corners are topped with pyramidal merlins. The access to the tomb is located on the exterior west wall. Access is over a stone threshold and the door is very small. Over the door is a frescoed bump.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It surrounds the tomb structure to the southwest and east.

DESCRIPTION: We see on the southeast wall above the platform (6582) a beautiful blue feathered peacock. On the northwest wall above the platform there is a table with possibly eggs and beneath the table is another peacock with a splendid tail.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Above the platform (6582)

DESCRIPTION:
This feature is a wall painting on the north side of the eastern exterior wall of the tomb structure (1). Located over the platform (#6581), it is adjacent to wall painting #6580.
Like 6580, it has a decorative vessel which is probably silver. This is a high pedestal, ovoid jar with a tall narrow neck and high strap handle.
Two bunches of green grapes are suspended against this jar.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
This is contiguous to platform 6581, which is below painting 6579 to the eastern side.
This is on the north side of the eastern wall of the tomb structure.

DESCRIPTION: Enter the Dining room from the Counter room(1), situated in the South corner of the S.W. Wall. The axis is South/North. The floor is covered with lapilli. This is rectangular room, in shape. The walls have no plaster. There is evidence of Opus mixtum and Roman brick work. There is no ceiling. There would be enough room for 3 Dining benches.

Dining Room #2 is entered from the Shop Counter seen to the Southeast. It is the 1st of several Dining rooms in this Hotel/Inn. The room is square, it shows scattered plaster fragments on all walls. The floor is currently covered by soil. The ceiling is no longer extant. The Southwestern wall is pierced by joist holes whose purpose is uncertain.

A masonry cooking platform sits in the south corner of room 7. It is rectangular in shape with a flat surface and stands about 50 cm. high today. DESCRIPTION: The square counter room is entered from the street, (through a large entrance to the northwest) over a step which is now approximately 30 cm high. The stone threshold shows the door guide. The room has one more entrance to the southeast. The smaller door connects the shop with the atrium of the house (2.2.2). On the southwestern wall is a large rectangular window which looks out onto a side street. To the south of this window is a storeroom (17). To the southwest of the entrance into the atrium is a flight of stairs which leads up to a missing second floor. Four stone steps are extant. On the northeastern wall is a lararium (2816). On the opposite side, in the western corner of the room, is the L-shaped counter (2815). On the western corner of the shop are traces of red painting. More evidence of painting is visible on the northwestern wall near the entrance door. The northern sections of the northwestern and northeastern walls are preserved to the second story. There is evidence of two joist holes and plaster in the northern corner of the northeastern wall. The southeastern and southwestern walls have been restored to the first story level. The ceiling is no longer extant and the floor is covered with lapilli.

DESCRIPTION: Room 2 is entered from Room 1 (fauces) and Room 9 (shop) both of which are to the northwest. The main axis of this irregularly rectangular room is southwest/northeast. The walls were painted as traces of plaster and red painting shows on the walls. On the northeastern wall there are five rectangular joist holes running above five rows of bricks that run the length of the wall. On the top of the same wall is a rectangular window which lies about one third of a meter above the joist holes. Today the floor is covered by lapilli. The large room contains, in the northern corner, four stone stairs leading up to a missing floor. On the eastern corner is an irregularly shaped pile of stones leaning against the wall, the function of which is unknown. The room also contains a hearth (2788) on the northwestern side. This feature leads us to define this space as a preparation room though the big size suggests that this space could have been used for purposes other than cooking. The ceiling is non-extant. There appears to be a blocked door and a blocked window (above the door) on the southwestern wall. The walls exist to the first floor height.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this space as a sales room, entrance 16 and associated with structure 15. It is commercial. This identification is based on its location opening to the street. In addition to the street entrance there is a fairly wide open doorway in the northern half of the northeast wall which opens into the atrium (4). The condition of this space is very poor, the upper section of the doorway to the street is reconstructed; only traces of plaster remain along the base of the northwest and southeast walls and on the brick pillars flanking the street doorway on the southwest wall. There are also no visible remains of the floor or ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is contiguous to the street on its southwest side and entrance 15 (1) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this space as a prep room within a commercial structure. This identification is based on the location of this space directly northeast of sales room (17) with a pass-through window (6796) located in the south end of the southwest wall. This is an almost square room which is entered from a doorway at the center of the southeast wall. This doorway goes out to the atrium (4). This space is in very poor condition. Although plaster remains on all the walls, this is cracking and falling apart. Paint is preserved only in hte south, east, and north corners of the room, where red vertical stripes can be seen, and small traces of horizontal bands very low on the wall, suggesting a small dado. No flooring is visible; no ceiling remains.

DESCRIPTION: This is the Kitchen in the House of the Vettii. We enter this room from the atrium of the servants. The floor is concrete and mud. The room includes a water basin, elaborate cooking platform. On the north west wall there is an iron door opening to an interesting pornographic display. There is no ceiling to the room. DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vetti. We are looking at a huge aedicular lararium, which is topped with a pediment and supported by two fluted columns in this servants lararium. The pediment contains stucco sacrifice instrument - a knife, patera, and bucranes. Beneath the signs of sacrifice are two dancing lars. They hold elaborate rhytons and small buckets. Between them stands a male figure. He is probably a priest because his head is covered. He holds a small cachet. The colours are still brilliant. Beneath the figures is a huge crested snake. Comment: We were allowed two hours in this great house by Director Grete Stefani who stayed with us the entire time out. Thanks to her.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Main atrium, kitchen, storerooms.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that the House of the Small Fountain is a domestic structure. We have identified room #10 as an ambulatory. We have made this identification based upon its large area which includes a peristyle colonnade surrounding an elaborate mosaic and shell fountain and its location at the rear of the house visible through the atrium and tablinum. The room is rectangular and is on a southeast/northwest axis. The space is elaborately frescoed showing mythological or sacred themes on a series of four panels. The panel on the southeast wall contains images of food being offered, carried, and fish being caught. Painting is described on feature sheet 6566. The fountain and the remaining three panels sit on the southwest wall. A series of three columns bisect the space with a fourth column dividing off the fountain from the northwest wall. A water channel runs along the floor to the northwest of the columns. The ambulatory walking area runs to the northeast of the columns in an L-shape culminating in the northwest corner of the room. The ambulatory walking area is roofed. Into the northeast of the water channel, the area is currently covered in gravel surrounding the fountain except for a square area immediately to the northeast of the fountain which is currently excavated showing water pipes connecting the fountain to the water channels. The fountain itself is shaped like a small house protruding to northeast from southwest wall. The fountain is covered with mosaic and shell with patterns of nature gods and water animals. The area inside the colonnade had no roof but had a series of rain spouts that would have channeled water into the area (indicating that this was perhaps a garden). The current floor of the ambulatory walkway is dirt and the original floor is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of passageway 9, tablinum 8, dining 11, dining 12, and is to the southwest of cubculi 13 and 14 and stairway 15.

A rectangular podium is covered with fresco with a garland decoration at the top in stucco and elaborate cornice work above the garland. The frescoes consist of a scene with a man sitting on a bisellium surrounded by other men, the banquet scene described on Feature sheet 6577 and a fresco of possibly two fountains on tables. On the top of the podium in a central position sits the burial altar. Three sides carry scenes of of Dionysios holding holding a rhyton on the west side of the altar with maenads on the north and south ends. The east side of the altar contains the inscription with two human figures (it is suggested they may be hermaphridic) standing on an umbrella-like structure with a similar structure above their heads. The top of the altar contains the standard rolled pillow forms. To the north and south of the altar, still on top of the podium, are paired ballustrades, each consisting of squared blocks topped by snakes coiled around omphaloi. Paintings of assorted putti are on the exterior side of the blocks.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Centered within the tomb enclosure and attached to the north exterior wall.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this feature may be a hold for a libation tube. it is an intentionally drilled hole. It has a round opening, visibly drilled deeply through to the center of the block. The hole is located in the third block from the north end of the bench. The hole is on the back of the seat, where it begins to curve for the lower part of the seat bottom. The depth of the hole was measured to be 14cm until blocked by earth and debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is located south of feature 6586, on the third block from the north corner of the bench.
