This space is identified as a storeroom located in the kitchen area of the Villa of the Mosaic Columns. This small rectangular space on a northwest/southeast axis. At the center of the southeast side, squared pillars flank the entrance-way. There is a brick column in both the southern and eastern corners. The southeast and northeast walls no longer exist. The remaining opus walls are opus incertum. Some plaster remains on the southwest and northwest walls as well as on the columns. The robbers hole comes through the southwest wall. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This is located to the northeast of room 14 and to the southwest of area 16.

DESCRIPTION: This space in the northern corner of the kitchen 5072 is identified as a latrine in the house of M.L.Fronto. The space is in very poor condition and overgrown with vegetation. It is separated from the cooking platform and the rest of the kitchen by partition walls in opus incertum. The walls in the latrine have remains of heavy plaster with graffiti incised in the south west wall. Along with other scratches, we can make out a large animal. The simplicity of this design suggests the artist was a child.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This latrine is to the north east of the cooking patform 5073 and in the north corner of the kitchen 5072.

DESCRIPTION: L. Eschebach reports a compitum at this location, behind the fountain. The fountain is here but no altar or painting is extant. There is a thick mortar layer on the sidewalk between 1.10.1 and the wall recess.

This niche is located on the inside of the northwest corner of the forum, immediately next to the capitolium. The sill is almost parallel to the height of the temple base. Niche apears to be made of cot sarno stones or is almost completely filled with rubble. The visible part of the niche shows a plaster lining. The niche is immediately northeast of the vertical reconstruction line in the wall.

The top of the sill is approximately 1.94m above the current ground level. The width of the niche is .33m; height from the sill is .37m, depth is at least .27m although undoubtedly deeper (filled).

(There is a possible altar stone behind, but not in situ and turned the wrong direction. Any other association is unknown and thus not recorded with the street shrines).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Niche 4932 is almost directly backing onto this niche, on either side of the wall.

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that this is a crossroad altar due to its location on the northwestern corner of insula 8. It faces to the northwest along the southeast wall of the structure at 9-8-1. It is identified as an altar due to its form and location. It's form is basically a rectangular platform. It is opus incertum with cut stone facing. The central area of the front projects out with the southeast central portion preserving some plaster. The top surface rises at the sides. These rises flank a rectangular surface which has a rectangular depression cutting its corners. This has been heavily conserved with modern plaster and mortar across the top.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Pompeii in pictures 9-8-1 Della Corte p. 134
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This fronts the Via Nola at the western corner of 9-8 and across the small road from 9-5.

DESCRIPTION:
The tomb of the Stronnii is an altar tomb. The altar is made entirely of tufa with molded profiles of tufa at the base. There are four courses of large tufa blocks and a projecting cornice decorated with egg and dart. The altar is topped with a pair of lions, symmetrically placed, each with a paw on the head of a goat. Directly below the cornice is an inscription CIL I. 3134. The probable date of the tomb is 70 - 30 BCE based o the lettering of the inscription and the construction. Campbell PNc 55

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Campbell pp 274-275
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: south of the pathway to the Nocera gate between unexcavated space and the tomb of Annedia and Lucius Caesius (PNc 54)

DESCRIPTION:
This is an aedicula tomb constructed of tufa and brick. The core is of opus incertum with brick quoins. Two inscriptions remain, one is embedded in the pedestal the other was added later. The tomb is dedicated to Publius Vestorius Phileros. The aedicula above the pedestal is of brick with opus incertum. A shallow niche topped with a pediment contains three headless tufa statues. The small burial chamber is entered through a low arch in the rear. Little remains of the stucco covering. There were sixteen columellae associated with the tomb according to Campbell (PNc 50) but only two remain.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Campbell pp 268 - 270
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: south of the pathway to the Nocera gate, between tombs 21 and 25.

DESCRIPTION: This is a cooking platform. In the east corner of kitchen 7 with its long end against the SE wall. It is a rectangular masonry structure. The platform is in a ruined state, but some of its brick arch over the storage below is still intact.

In the north corner on the north east side of the entire area of the tomb sits an altar attached to the wall enclosing the tomb of Eumachia next door. The altar is constructed of masonry with a rectangular base at ground level topped with a perfect rectangular concrete box that appears to be reconstructed. It is topped again by an original masonry piece shaped like a couch. Details remain on the ancient top and include a frieze of geometric stripes as a decorative element. The top surface is bookended by a volute at each end. Overall any other decoration cannot be clearly identified. The altar sits at a right angle from its tomb and is on a north west / south east axis.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This altar is located north of the tomb structure.

DESCRIPTION: This is the atrium (14) of the House of M Lucretius Fronto. It is located immediately off the fauces (12). It is a large room with an impluvium and compluvium defining the space as the atrium. The reconstructed compluvium has rain spouts to channel water into the impluvium below. The walls are opus incertum and are fully painted. Painted frescoes appear on all walls and we note in particular, the small animals, such as a deer and dog and some other four-footed beast as well as a winged animal centrally located, on the solid black panel wild animal's faces are interspersed with human faces on the yellow stripe dividing the black panels into sections. The register above these panels appears to show various birds. These are only truly identifiable on the northwest and a little on the northeast walls where we see some sort of animal centered above the tablinum door. Numerous doorways open to many areas of the house (see floor plan). The floor is cement with embedded tesserae and larger pieces of colored stone. At the entrance from the fauces a geometric pattern of white stones provides a "welcome mat." The impluvium in the center contained a fountain, a cistern and an elaborate offering table (5084). Around the impluvium is a mosaic border in a chain link pattern with a white border and a black background. There is presently a metal brace placed high above the door threshold.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the southwest is a door to stairs rising to a room above cubiculum 3 and the fauces. Dining hall 10 is to the southeast. The tablinum is northeast of the atrium.

DESCRIPTION: F
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space (room 3) is identified as a horticultural space within the food and drink shop/food processing establishment. This is a rectangular space on a southeast/northwest axis. The entrance is a wide opening at the southwest side of the space. The opening is flanked by two rectangular pillars. The tops of these two pillars slant downward towards the entranceway. This suggests that the space was unroofed. The identification as an unroofed garden space is further supported by the presence of a waster channel (gutter 5021) along the northwest
BW_ROLL: and southeast walls. Hydraulic cement creates a curved outer edge of these channels. There is a dolium (5022) buried near the south corner of the space. The walls of opus incertum with remains of of plaster on all walls. A rectangular window is located on the northwest wall. A rectangular niche (5023) is located at the center of the southeast wall.
COLOR_ROLL: This space is to the northeast of passageway (4). It is southeast of storage areas 5 and 6.
PHOTOGRAPHER: northeast

DESCRIPTION: We have identified House of the Ship B as a house. We have determined that the last usage of this room [3-6534] is as a dining room. This identification is based on location within the house with an entrance to the atrium. The room is on the southeast side of the house and atrium. There is no evidence of food and drink in this room. Characteristics of the room are that it is mid sized with traces of painting. There is a window to the street on the northeast side of the room. It is a mid sized rectangle in the center of the wall about two meters from the floor. The room is entered from the northwest corner with no evidence of a threshold. No traces of flooring remain today. It is entirely rubble and debris. There is no trace of a ceiling. The northwest wall is damaged with some modern reconstruction. Traces of stucco remain. It appears to be at least 2.5 meters high but we cannot determine the height. The wall to the northeast is damaged but was reconstructed in modern times. Evidence of concrete and plaster remains but no painting is discernible. Midway up the wall and in the center is a medium sized window to the street. The southeast wall again is badly damaged and reconstructed in modern times with traces of concrete and stucco with no discernible painting. It is so badly damaged that it is not certain if there were any windows. The southwest wall is badly damaged; it has modern reconstruction. There is evidence of concrete amid plaster but no discernible painting. In the lower west side of the southwest there is a low platform that is 70 cm by 47 cm deep. The plaster of the southwest wall appears to go behind this podium which has undergone major modern reconstruction.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The opening on the northwest side is tot he atrium [2].

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that shop 'V-I-1' is a food shop based upon the counter prominent in the front room and the reports given by Eschebach. We have identified Room (1) as the counter room based upon the presence of a masonry counter and its location open to the sidewalk at the juncture of two streets. The room is rectangular and is on a south-west/north-east axis. The long end of the L-shaped counter faces the street to the south-east, with its other arm facing the street to the south-west. The room has doorways on the north-west leading to rooms (2) and (3), and on the north-east to room (4). Walls are of mixed opus incertum and brick construction. The floor is rubble and there is a step up from the sidewalk on both street sides. The counter appears to take up two thirds of the space in the shop. No ceiling/roof is present. The walls around the room show trace of plaster decoration but no painted colour remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to the south-east of rooms (2) and (3) and to the south-west of room (4).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this structure as commercial. We have identified this space as a food production (preserving) area. Architecturally, this space is an atrium. The identification as a food production area is based on the presence of two features: a platform (6808) and a fish tank (6798). This working area is in the atrium of the structure, with an impluvium in the center (not centered in the entrance way (1)). Both sales rooms (2) and (17) open to this space at the southwest side. Entrance space (1) from door 15 also opens to this space between the two sales rooms (16) and (15). (14) and (16) also open onto this space. This large open space provides a passage from the front at the southwest to the back through space (14) to the oven in space (12). This space is in very poor condition, as is the rest of the structure. The dark stone impluvium is in situ, but no floor or wall surfaces are preserved or visible, except for some plaster in the western corner. No ceiling remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This processing room is to the northeast of entrance area (1), and southwest of prep room (16).

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this room is a dining room. This is a rectangular space on a southeast-northwest axis. The entrance to this room is a wide opening in the southeast wall. This room opens to the atrium (space two) at the southeast. On the northwest wall there is a large central window opening to a light well with a well-head adjacent to the southwest wall of the light well. There may have been a decorative fountain in this small space. A door leading into space six is located in the eastern corner of the northeast wall. The room was highly decorative. The condition is poor. The walls are opus incertum in the central areas, while on the southeast wall, the northwest wall, and the eastern end in the northeast wall, there are alternating courses of brick and cut stone. On the western corner of the southwest wall, there is a cut niche (3-3983). Preserved paint reveals a low dado. the walls were decorated with large panels of alternating colors, including red and yellow. On the northwest wall, the corners preserve a border of green paint. In the upper northern corner there are remains of decorative molding. This border may have slightly arched across the northwest wall although there are eleven beam holes cross this wall just above the height of the molding. There is no visible flooring surface. There is no ceiling preserved. There is some conservation and restoration of walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space s northwest of the atrium (space 2). It is southwest of spaces 5 and 6.

DESCRIPTION: One enters dining room 17 from corridor 10 to the SE or the tablinum 19 to the NE. The large entrance to the SE contains broken marble threshold fragments which indicate placements at the door or pivot. This opening provides a focal point intto the large impluvium in the atrium where there was a fountain. There is a large section which is indented into the stone on the NE wall of the threshold. Tough badly preserved, the floor was caccio pesto with white tesserae running diagonally forming diamonds with little black centered four petalled white flowers in the center of each. The painting on the walls is faint, but traces of red white and yellow can be seen on all four walls and faint outlines of green and red stenciling can be seen in at least 2 of the corners. One the SE and NW walls, faint columns garlanded in red can be seen above the the red dado and on the NW wall white impressions outline small birds holding garlands in their beaks decorating the red and white column. This room was probably decorated in 3rd or 4th style. Poorly preserved molding at the SW end of the room where the three walls meet provide an indication of the ceiling above which there was a vault on the SW and 7 beam holes above the arch. There is no ceiling extant but the western corner indicates 2 storeys. The floor is obscured with rubble and debris.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous with corridor 10 to the SE and tablinum 19 to the NE.

DESCRIPTION:
One enters the room from the north end at east wall. Room axis is east west. The threshold is of marble. There are door jambs on either side. One then ascends to marble steps to a raised floor that is obscured by lapilli. On the north wall there are remnants of painted plaster. There is a lower register with very faint traces; above which there is a narrow red border. Then a mid register carrying 3 panels painted in yellow and red. The style cannot be discerned. Above this there are traces of paint that may be an upper register. The western wall has a large formal entrance that looks out looks out on to the garden and peristyle. On either side of the entrance there is red and yellow painted plaster. The threshold is raised and appears to be of marble. Cuttings in the surface of the threshold are present for door jambs. On the south wall there are traces of painted plaster similar to those on the north wall but better preserved. There are three panels visible in a middle register that may be third style. Above the painted area there are fragments of a plaster ceiling molding. The east wall shows traces of painted plaster similar to elsewhere but poorly preserved.
A nice view of the impressive household shrine.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Atrium 5 to the east.
Portico 14 and garden 15 to the west

DESCRIPTION: This small nearly square preparation room runs along a northwest/southeast axis and has two doorways with marble thresholds and modern wooden and lead lintels. The thresholds have placements for small door pivots. The doorway on the northwest wall adjoins dining room 26 and the doorway on the southwest leads to the peristyle corridor (11). The common area of the two doors is formed by a column of brick between them at the western corner. The floor was of mixed pavement cement. Today there are two pieces of a column in the east corner, and in the south corner, some broken drain tiles. The floor is obscured with vegetation and debris. The northeast wall contains a large window into the next room, which is roofed. All walls, except the northwest, are high. There is no ceiling extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to dining room 26 to the northwest and corridor 11 to the southwesst.

DESCRIPTION: Room axis is North/South. One enters the room from the North side of the portico (14) to the south. The entrance is large and formal with a marble threshold. The floor is obscured by lapilli. The east wall is poorly preserved. A few traces of yellow paint remain. There may be a post hole high at the northern end. The North wall is poorly preserved. No traces of paint are visible. There is a large opening waist high on axis with the entrance that may be reconstructed. The West wall is badly damaged. Little plaster and no painting is visible. The South wall on either side of the entrance is poorly preserved. There are patches of adherent plaster at the lower extremes.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
Portico (14) and garden (15) to the South.
Room (25) to the North.

DESCRIPTION: This tenuously defined room in a heavily bombed out area of the workshop is on the south side of the house. There is only a roughly reconstruct east and reconstructed south wall to the room. South wall has remnants of red plaster in the southeast corner of the room. There is a clay pipe descending in the wall from the upper story which suggests the presence of a latrine. there is also in the southeast corner a fixed pile of rubble that suggests a cooking platform (6433). Boyce tells us that there was a lararium painting near the cooking platform. No ceiling, no floor. On the south wall to the west of the drain pipe are three low holes that may represent shelf placements and three higher holes that would hold joists for an upper level. In the southwest corner of the south wall is another hole that appears to go quite some distance into the wall at head height.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Plan shows opening to room 12 workroom to the north.

DESCRIPTION: On the west end of the north wall in room 10,the kitchen, lies a low platform. The remains of this platform lie along a northeast/southwest axis. This platform abuts the north and west walls and a south delineation which runs parallel to the entrance and walk space in the kitchen. This delineation appears to be the south end of the cooking platform. The south wall is approximately 20 cm high and 1 m long. The east wall is not extant, there is no surface remaining however lapilli and broken tiles obscure the space.

A very large masonry counter with a tiled top takes up about two-thirds of counter room (1). The counter is L-shaped with three openings for dolia facing the street to the south-east and one more dolia opening next to a hearth cut out on a south-west side. The dolia appear to be of different sizes with large dolia located on the north-east end of the counter adjacent to the building and its opposite counter on the south-west end. One of the smaller dolia is located between the two larger dolia and one is located to the north-west just before the hearth. The lips on three dolia to the south-east of the counter are missing, but the small dolia next to the hearth has a conciele lip that appears to be restored. The hearth is on the north-west end and is square in shape with some tiles sticking out indicating that the cooking surface was raised slightly above floor level. The south-east face of the counter has a marble fronted step above the threshold level which would access the large dolia to the north-east. There is masonry fill between the front of the counter and the street threshold at the north-east corner.

This is a large kitchen. It is a rectangular space on a northwest - southeast axis. On the northwest wall at the west corner is entrance 7 from the street. On the southwest wall in the west corner there is a door to the peristyle (9). To the northeast of the room is a latrine in the north corner of the house and to the southeast of the latrine is a storage room (3972). This kitchen has a cooking platform in the north corner of the room along the northwest wall (3970). Near the corner of the northeast wall is a long rectangular vat (3971). In the east corner along the southeast wall is a doorway into room 14. In the south corer along the southeast wall is walled in brick archway.
The condition of this space is poor. A stone threshold at entrance 7 is visible but no other floor surface is exposed. There is no roofing present. The walls are preserved at about 4 meters. The southwest wall preserves plaster with a projecting dado at about 1 1/2 meters height. This dado is of an orange and pinkish color. One small low window and a small niche are in the south corner of this wall and the window looks into the peristyle.
The brick arch in the southeast wall is set back from the surface of the wall. The arch way is filled except for a window at the apex of the arch. This wall was also plastered and has remains of the pink dado. The doorway in the east corner along the southeast wall is in very poor condition and is braced with modern scaffolding. Except for the brickwork arch the rest of the room is opus incertum. Two joist holes are visible on the southwest wall and two are visible in the east corner of the northeast wall. These holes are not aligned to each other across the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is northeast of the peristyle, and is southeast of the street.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified VI.10.2 as a domestic structure. We have determined that the last usage of this room 14 (6513) is as a dining room. This identification is based on the room location within the structure, with a clear view of a garden, as well as previous research. This dining room is located on the southeast corner of the house in the rear. The focus of the room is on a garden to the southwest. There is no longer any evidence of the entrance to this room, but it presumably opened to the garden. There is no evidence of a floor which today is rubble. On the southeast and northeast wall there appear to be post holes for a possible second floor. There is no evidence of a ceiling or roof today. On the northwest wall only a portion remains. This house was extensively bombed in 1942. On the portion that remains there appears to be ancient stucco, with some modern reconstruction in the top section. The northeast wall is better preserved with some modern reconstruction on the upper part. There are three post holes approximately 2.5 m from ground level. It appears that the lower part of the wall is partially concreted with no evidence of plaster or painting. On the southeast wall at the same level there are two rows of what appear to be post holes. There are four post holes at 2.5 m. At about .5 m. centered above these is a row of eight square openings that go straight through the wall and are possible post holes for an upper floor.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room (6513) looks out to a garden on the southwest. The northeast wall was next to a rear entrance to the property at VI.10.19.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this space as a Processing Room within the House of the Working Painters due to the finds within the room. It is a rectangular room on a northwest-southeast axis. This room opens to the peristyle though a doorway on the southeast wall. This is a high doorway. The condition of the room is poor with piles of excavation debris in the south and east corners. The northwest corner contains a pile of partially excavated amphorae still in lapili. These amphorae are [Feature Number 9-4059] visible. A moratarium and fragments of roof tile are also visible with the amphorae. Toward the north corner of the room there are remains on the floor indicating the position of some processing equipment. These are formed in rough cement. The floor in this room seems to have been just plaster, but it is hardly visible. The walls are preserved quite high. There is no evidence of plaster.
The south corner of the southeast wall preserves a square window which is still filled with volcanic debris, but preserves the original iron grid visible from the exterior of the room. No ceiling remains. There area several holes in the southwest wall, perhaps for shelving.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The room is contiguous to the peristyle locates south of the processing room.

DESCRIPTION: A rectangular atrium- North South axis. Along the east side from the North there is a doorway to a small room - cubiculum (11), fauces and small room - cubiculum (9). The South wall survives with extensive plaster; pink upper register and white lower register. The West wall plaster survives in fragments with pink color. The wall is divided into two by a corridor leading to the rear of the property. In the southern half there is a locked doorway with signs of modern restoration or that the doorway has been blocked in the modern era. High at the North wall there is a low stone step, perhaps for stairs extending along the north wall. Fragments of plaster on the North wall, pink lower register and white above. In the north east corner of the room there are fragments of plaster from earlier phases with red plaster overlaid by black plaster. In the north west corner of the room there is a cooking platorm (6392). Floor is obscured by lapilli throughout.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP:
(9),(10) and (11) to the East.
(7) and (12) to the West.

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room east/west axis. Wide doorway in the centre of the west wall overlooking the garden peristyle. Marble threshold with placings for the door. Modern lintel and ceiling.Mosaic paving survives throughout with white tesserae, black border and square central rosette consisting of geometric patterns and circles with images of ducks and marine life. Extensive decoration survives on all four walls. Third style decoration throughout with black lower register with architectural details, gardens and birds. Red panel above with architectural details, animals and seahorses. Yellow panels above divided by architectural borders with inserted figures and images. The centre of the south wall the (?) of cherubs. In the centre of the east wall are Theseus and Ariadne watched by Athena. In the centre of the north wall are Artemis and Callisto. On the north wall the upper register survives with further mythic scenes depicting Venus and Adonis, cupids, Leda and Tyndareus. In the northeast corner is a painting 6456.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: peristyle 8 to the east

DESCRIPTION: We enter this food and drink shop - other over an ashlar threshold from the sidewalk. An interesting metal remnant is left in the threshold. The room is a good sized serving room. The major identifiable feature is a large cooking platform in the west wall. There is some plaster remaining on the north wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 2 to the south

DESCRIPTION: In the centre of the west wall are three square holes to support three layers of shelves. At the end of the north wall there are four holes and at the west end of the north wall there are two surviving holes that would have originally supported four tiers of shelves. No shelves are visible on the south and east walls.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: 6419 to the south

DESCRIPTION: There is a small arched recessed niche on the north west wall, directly above a water feature on the floor. Facing the niche, from the corner of the walls, to the right a pipe comes in that terminates in the niche. The pipe runs to the next room from the arched niche to the northwest wall. We speculate that running water came into the niche which had a spout and water fell into the circular opening of the water feature 6406 below, thereby providing running water to the kitchen. No trace of the pipe remains.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: above the circular basin or cistern 6406 on floor and next to long cylindrical opening where pipe may have been. To west of 6404, 6402, 6401

DESCRIPTION: This is a small dining room. It is n a northwest/southeast axis. There are two entrances. One can enter through a narrow door from the fauces at the southeast corner of the room or through a wider door on the west wall from the atrium. There is a window in the west wall. The surface of the floor is not visible. Two small slit windows are on the upper east wall. A couch niche 3285 is adjacent to the small door in the south wall. Traces of plaster remain on the walls and decorative first style mouded panels are preserved n the north and east walls. There are three levels of cornice moulding at the upper portion of the wall.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 to the west

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room with a north/south axis. Originally a single room with 17 to the east separated by poorly preserved and extensively restored partition wall containing a doorway into the room. No visible threshold. Floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. Plaster survives on the northwest walls, pink in colour. Plaster moulding survives at the base of the north wall at the junction with the east wall. In the centre of the north wall, between rooms 17 and 18 there is a window into the garden with a modern lintel. Above the window in the western half of the north wall are four holes for floor joists for the second storey. Above the window is a possible window in the second storey. In the southwest corner, extending from the corner to the middle of the room is a latrine consisting of two stone supports between which the floor slopes to a central drain. The drain is filled with lapilli, no trace of the seat survives. In front of the east support is a square basalt block containing a square hole to support a no longer extant feature.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 17 to the east

DESCRIPTION: We have identified room 41 as a dining room because of its location and because there is a large window opening to the portico and a door opening to an unexcavated area which was probably a garden. The primary entrance to this room is a wide doorway to the south, with a marble threshold with cutouts for door attachments on both sides. The room is L-shaped, with two ends of the L forming rectangular niches on the north and west sides. The west wall has a small door in its southwest corner leading to room 38. The east wall has a large square window in its southeast corner leading to colonnaded garden 40/59. The black and which mosaic on the floor delineates the two niches via a rectangle with double black lines in the southeast bottom corner of the L. The walls are highly decorated with fourth style decoration, with small birds and winged creatures scattered throughout. The dado is a dark red with central pictures delineated by yellow bands. Beginning at the south wall west of the door and circling the rooms and the niches, the decorative scheme is of two white panels followed by a red panel repeating four times. Above that is a register with a solid background with red, gold and black typical fourth style divisions. Above that register is a plastered cornice, simply decorated in brown. The ceiling would have been above that. Currently the modern reconstruction is being held up by a mesh wire superstructure. Where is painting does not remain, the walls are a mix of simple masonry, stonework and opus reticulatum. On the niche to the east, one can see some remains of the triple black line with some unusual patterning setting off the niche itself.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: To the north of portico 24. To the west of portico 40.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 21-6542 as a dining room because of its location in the house with a large entrance on the northwest side to corridor 19 and a view of and access to garden 20. The room is large with very high ceilings and wall paintings. Research by Eschebach suggests that the room was used for dining. The ceiling is nonexistent. All of the walls have been reconstructed in modern times. The floor is lapilli and rubble today. The wall to the northwest side has a high and large entrance to corridor 19 and garden 20 with a marble threshold and evidence of door jambs. There is no evidence of ancient stucco or painting. The wall to the northeast is badly damaged and heavily reconstructed in modern times. There are traces of ancient plaster with possibly very faded yellow paint in the middle register. High in the reconstruction section are two square post holes. On the north side on the lower level is an entrance to room 18 with a marble threshold. The southeast wall, heavily reconstructed, has a large entrance to corridor 22. There is no evidence of plaster or painting remaining. The southwest wall is damaged and reconstructed in modern times. In the upper level it is reconstructed with three post holes, again from modern times. There is plaster and painting that is very faded. There are three discernible patterns with a middle and upper register, with a very faded possibly male figure in the center of the central upper register. The colors are faded yellow and red.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to corridor 19 with access to garden 20 on the northwest side. On the northern side of the northeast wall there is an entrance to room 18. On the southeast wall there is a large entrance to corridor 22.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified 6547 as a house and Room 13 as a preparation room off the kitchen. We have based this determination on the location between the kitchen and several identified dining rooms, and the presence of a masonry preparation platform. The room is small and undecorated, and is entered from Area 12 on its southwest and kitchen 14 on its northeast. The southeast wall is composed of the remains of a staircase to an upper floor and most likely a latrine under the stairs. The latrine and the low doorway to the kitchen are to the northeast. Two niches in the wall above the suggested latrine have an arched shape and plaster inside. We suggest the one directly above the latrine in the east corner as a lamp holder, the other may be a lararium. The northwest wall contains remains of a rectangular platform on the north end. The platform is of masonry construction and appears to have had a brick front, and is rubble today. The floor is rubble and the room is open to the sky.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is to the northeast of hallway 12 and to the southwest of kitchen 14.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this room (12 - 6538) as a dining room based upon the room's location within the structure as it appears to open on to room 13, a possible garden area. Research suggests the presence of a triclinium (Eschebach). No entrance remains, but the entrance to the room appears to be off room 10 to the southwest. This dining and possible garden complex is on the northeast side of the house. The floor is rubble and there is no evidence of a ceiling. It is entirely open today on the southwest side, which is presumed to be the entrance but there is no evidence of a threshold today. The wall on the northwest side is nearly nonexistent except for blocks delineating separation from room 13. The northeast wall is heavily damaged and reconstructed. There is a medium sized window centered on the wall mid way up looking out to the street. There are small traces of plaster but no evidence of paint. The southwest wall is damaged and reconstructed. There is no evidence of plaster or painting.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Dining room 12 is contiguous to room 13 (a possible garden) to the northwest and to room 10 (hall) to the southwest.

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that the structure located immediately to the southwest of the Herculanean Gate is a vaulted niche tomb belonging to Marcus Cerrinius Restitutus whose epitaph says he is a member of the Augustalis. This identification has been made based upon the location of the tomb immediately outside the city gates on the street of tombs. The tomb was heavily restored in 1977. Today the tomb consists of two low walls with benches to the southeast and southwest of a vaulted niche opening (features 6595 and 6591). The opening is arched and the interior runs on a north-south axis. Running on each wall on the east and west sides are low benches preceding (feature sheets 6593 and 6592). The chamber is entered via the south over a stone threshold. The south wall of the tomb shows slight traces of painted plaster and a rectangular niche in the center of the wall. A dirt floor is all that remains.

The tomb identification comes from an epitaph recorded in CIL but no longer present. The epitaph text reads M(arcus) Cerrinius / Restitutus / Augustalis Loc(vs) d(atus) d(ecreto) d(ecurionum). [Marcus Cerrinius Restitutus, Augustalis place given by decree of the decuriones.]

We walk into this good sized dining room from the west from the atrium 2 which is separated from the street by the vestibule. We see another short doorway to this room obviously for slaves. Today we see an added concrete block to frame the doorway with modern wood. This is laid upon the ancient threshold. As we enter the room we see three layers of plaster, the last painted white with red touches. Traces of original floor cementicum (?) are inlaid with marble pieces. Today this room has a huge ugly modern table covered with a tarp and unusable boxes. Underneath this is a rectangular marble tiled floor design mostly greyish white marble. The central coloured marble feature in the floor (which would not have been covered by dining benches) contains feature tiles of red and white marble. Two windows are present in the room. Protective wood awnings well above eye level are present over painted areas on three walls. All that can now be seen on the west covered picture may be a deer. A large chunk has been randomly cut out near signs of a dark turquoise sky (?) with a red frame. The lower dado is black and shows green plant forms as in fourth style. The protective awning on the north wall has no painting evident though the dado and its plants remain. We wish to note that Eschebach reported that this painting was of Bellerophon or Theseus, fighting Amazons, but they were depicted wearing Roman armour. The east wall contains the two high windows either side of the protective awning. The red frame of the painting and some blue can be seen but the picture has been randomly removed. Yellow and white squares can be seen in this wall. There is a modern ceiling.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: atrium 2 is to the west, room 15 to the south

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room, east/west axis. Doorway with stone stepped threshold and modern lintel in the centre of the north wall to rooms 17 and 18. At the south end of the east wall there is a doorway with stone threshold and modern lintel to room 20 to the east. Plaster survives in the north corner of the east wall adjoining lararium 6326 in the north wall, pink in colour. The upper corner of all four walls are modern restorations. High on the east wall there is a blocked doorway or window. Above the lararium in the east wall there is a recess for a sloping roof (modern?) Plaster survives in fragments along the north wall; ink lower register, white above. In the centre of the north wall there is a low partition wall with modern restoration. In the northwest corner there is latrine 6328. To the south of the latrine there is a partition wall that separates the latrine from cooking platform 6327 inthe southwest corner. Undecorated plaster fragments survive in the west wall. A window high in the centre of the west wall partially survives. Plaster survives in the south wall with pink lower register. In the centre of the south wall there is a small recess - for a candle or similar? Floor is obscured by lapilli although beaten earth/masonry floor survives in the west half of the room.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: room 17to the north; room 20 to the east

DESCRIPTION: This is the Villa Arianna. This space (1) is identified as a dining hall. This is a very large rectangular space on a northwest/southeast axis. It is a summer dining area which is open on all sides. The entrance is almost the full width of the northwest wall. This opens directly to the walkway which was presumably covered. The floor is entirely mosaic. Principally white fields with a black band perimeter and a double black line defining a large rectangular space. The threshold is defined by black triangles on a white ground which form a star-like pattern. The threshold has a grey stone embedded at each side with one large square cutting in each. The northeast, southeast, and southwest sides of the room are on walls with three large rectangular windows on each side. The lower walls are brick and fresco, although no painting remains, and the open window spaces are divided by rectangular brick pillars. Although heavily reconstructed these would have also been frescoed. The tops of the walls are restored with large, white, marble sills. All upper parts of this room are reconstructed. This arrangement creates a fully open space with a view to the sea and to the southwest, a view to dining room space, and out to the villa from the southeast and northeast.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This dining hall is contiguous to the walkway at the northwest side. This lies to the northeast of room 7.

DESCRIPTION:
This public fountain is on the north side of the Vicoli degli Augstali at the intersection of the Vicolo Storto. It is in front of 7.4.32. The fountain is constructed from six limestone slabs, and unlike most other fountains in the city, it has a semi-circular basin rather than a square one. The interior dimensions of the basin are 0.80 meters (maximum) by 1.24 meters (maximum). The floor of the basin slopes to the southeast. The basin is 0.66 meters deep on the northwest and 0.73 meters deep on the southeast. Plaster is modern with no decoration and it has modern plumbing. The overflow is at the center of the southeast slab. The drainage hole is below. A deeply worn hand recess is on the northwest side of the pilaster. Other worn hand recesses are on the northeast side of the pilaster and at the interior west and north corners. The floor of basin is probably covered with opus signitum.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This public fountain is located on the north side of the Vicolo degli Augustali and in front of 7.4.32.

DESCRIPTION: Square shaped dining room with a wide doorway opening to the south to sales room #1. Doorway partially blocked by a low wall in later phase. Plaster survives on all four walls. White background with red trim. Floor is obscured by Lapilli.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 1 to the south Room 1 to the south None

DESCRIPTION: This is the House of the Vettii (room 19). This room is identified as a cubiculum/small reception space. It is a small room decorated in fresco. This feature is one of a group of seven and is a small vignette located at the eastern end of the northeast wall. It ha a red border on a white background. There is a blue ground with a gray and white bird facing to the left. The bird is flanked by branches with leaves and cherries (preserved only on the left side). The painting is in poor condition, with sections missing at the upper left corner, lower right corner, and in two narrow sections across the middle. theEdit (http://162.243.72.220/features/4692/edit)View (http://162.243.72.220/features/4692)
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature (4696) is directly east of painting feature 4695 and north of feature 4697, which is on the southeast wall.

DESCRIPTION:
This is the so called House of Championnet. It is also known as the House of the Geometric Mosaic. This is identified as a double house (entrances 14 and 16), and part of the complex of L. Aelius Magnus, which includes entrances 14 to 20. This area was under reconstruction in 79 CE. The area has since had modern reconstruction including the insertion of conserved and reconstructed mosaics. The small rectangular room (26) in the house of the Geometric Mosaics has been identified as a serving room (7020) due to its position near dining room (25). We enter via a wide doorway from the atrium (17). A threshold of marble cut with round holes for posts, a square hole, and two small holes for bolts and door fittings are present. There is a further door on the southwest wall that leads to dining room (25). It has another door present in the southeast wall leading to a further room ( ). No threshold is preserved. The floor is almost entirely covered in plain white mosaic. The walls are brick and opus incertum and heavily reconstructed. Modern lintels are on all three north doors. Holes at shelf hold height are preserved on the west wall (2) and on the southwest wall (3). No ceiling remains.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Picturesâ€ƒ
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This serving room is to the southwest of atrium (17) and ala (29).

DESCRIPTION:
This is the so-called House of Championnet, also known as the House of the Geometric Mosaics. We have identified this section as a separate entity which one enters through entrance (13). This room (7) is identified as a dining room. This identification is based on location, size, decoration and feature (couch niche 7002). This is a rectangular space on a northeast, southwest axis. The entrance is located at the northern end of the northwest wall. There is no threshold other than a low course of opus incertum. No flooring is visible and gravel covers the entire space. The walls are opus incertum with masonry flanking the doorway. The northwest and northeast walls preserve plaster and fresco with trances of a dark dado and white panels above (perhaps missing their color). To the west of the doorway is feature #7002, a couch niche. The small wall section between the doorway and north corner is seen to also have a low niche of unidentifiable character. Post holes are cut through the southwest and southeast walls. No ceiling remains. This space is in very poor condition.

BIBLIOGRAPHY:
Pompeii in Pictures.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the southeast of the atrium (2) and to the southwest of room (6).

DESCRIPTION:
Enclosure tomb 42 on north-east side of street of tombs at the Nocera Gate. It is triangular in shape, sitting on a north-west - south-east axis, made of opus incertum. The north-west side of the tomb is open on it's upper half. The tomb extends below ground on all 4 sides and was probably originally enclosed. The 4 walls of the tomb below ground today are plastered, although no trace of colour remains. Campbell tells us that a hole on the south-east floor was most likely where the urn was buried. However, exploration reveals three more potential burials, as well as a terracotta pipe in the north west corner at floor level. We hypothesize three explanations for the pipe: 1) a libation tube? 2) drainage? 3) modern conservation or ... To the east of that hole are the remains of a platform (feature 4896). The exterior walls of the tomb were also plastered. The south-east wall was decorated with a house shaped with an overhanging roof with a central niche made to look like a window. White and red plaster remains. The south-east and north-west exterior walls also show plaster remains.

BIBLIOGRAPHY
Campbell P.N.C. 23
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Immediately to the north-east ramp to the amphitheatre gate. Maps show tomb 40 and 40a where today's ramp is located.
DIGITAL_IMAGE: 108-0382A & 108-0383B & 108-0834C & 108-0836D Comments: 4 pictures. A is north facing, B is west facing. C is south facing and D is east facing.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified a commercial structure and have determined the use of this room as a sales room. This identification is based on the location of this space along the street and the large open store front. This sales room is designated entrance (14). Access to this room from the street is a step up from the sidewalk onto the line of four grey stone blocks with a channel for a shutter. At the south corner of the space these blocks do not continue all the way to the south east wall where Eschebach notes a wall or cistern on this plan. This well is no longer visible. This is a rectangular space on a south east/north west axis. While the main entrance is along the street, there is another entrance to the atrium (4) at the eastern end of the north east wall. The room is in very poor condition; no flooring is visible; the walls are very poorly preserved, although some painted plaster is still intact on each wall except for the western corner of the small section of the south west wall. The north west wall has the most plaster, and a red panel can be seen. On the north east wall, near the middle, there is a niche cut down to the floor. The small, rectangular recess space of this niche had been plastered and painted. Directly above this recess niche is the bottom section of a low window directly into the prep room behind (16). Because of the poor condition of this area, perhaps bombed, no upper walls of ceilings remain. Although nothing is visible in the room, Eschebach noted platforms.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This sales room is contiguous to entrance 15, space(1) and is south west of atrium (4).

DESCRIPTION: We have determined the usage of this room is a preparation room. Some food prepared here for baking could include casseroles brought from private houses by slaves and servants. We enter this room from the old atrium which is being used as a processing room. We see a tufa threshold and tall doorway on the southwest wall. The northeast wall includes part of the oven encasement (12, 6801) which is in adjacent room (12, 6803). The floor is pebbles and mud. There is a smaller door on the northwest wall in the western corner that can lead to the room with the oven (12, 6803). There is clear but minimal evidence of plaster with cream and red paint in the north corner of the northwest wall and at the base of the north corner of the northeast wall. This indicates customer usage and slave and servant usage, by virtue of the small door.

southeast We have verified this room as a dining hall. It is situated on a northwest-axis. This large rectangular room is located so that it may overlook a beautiful garden area. Its location is next to a preparation room and a small dining room. The entrance door is located on the southeast wall and is high and extremely wide. We cross a marble threshold and then five black and white mosaic borders. There are two large post holes for a big door. In the center is a large rectangular emblem with ten squares on the long rectangular side and six on the shorter side. Some of the squares show a diamond form. This is perfect for observing while lying on a triclinium. There are three bands of mosaic that border in this decorative rectangle. The wall once displayed brilliant red and yellow paint, most likely third style. We see in situ a red dado on all four sides. There is no picture totally intact on the middle yellow ground: several were removed. There is a totally reconstructed ceiling over the entire dining hall. There are no windows.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is northeast of the preparation room (32) and northwest of the garden, and it is southwest of dining room (38).

DESCRIPTION: We have identified this space as a small dining room, or diaeta, in a domestic structure. This identification is based on the location of this space overlooking the peristyle garden (30). The passage opens through the space from the colonnade area (33) out to a central open space (40) and onto a matching diaeta in the eastern corner of the house (41). This suite of three spaces is in the northeast border of the peristyle garden. In addition to the two doorways in room 39 there is a large central window on the southwest wall. The windowsill preserves cuttings for a shutter. The condition of this room is fair to poor. The upper section is reconstruction going up the walls with a modern ceiling. The floor surface is not visible. All walls preserve painted plaster except the southeast wall, which has plaster but no traces of paint remain. The other walls reveal a red dado with decoration, and a scheme of white panels above which appear to be in third or fourth style. No distinct decorative images can be discerned at this time. Clearly the orientation of this small dining space was positioned to enjoy the peristyle garden. One entered through the doorway on the northwest wall. The low door on the southeast side has clearly shifted downward and originally mirrored the door to room (41).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This space is to the northeast of the peristyle garden (30), and southeast of the colonnade area (33).

DESCRIPTION:
We have determined that structure 6.12.2 is a villa urbana and room 31 is an ambulatory, which we define as a space surrounding a peristyle in which literary sources suggest Romans would walk, drink, eat and contemplate philosophy. This area is at the back of the house in what would have been a private area and surrounds a very large garden. The peristyle is entered from the southeast and can be accessed from rooms and spaces 22, 19, 21, 20, 23 and 24. The northeast and southwest walls have no rooms along them but they show width of the house from street to street. The peristyle courtyard is framed by eleven pillars on the southeast and northwest ends, and thirteen pillars on the northeast and southwest sides. The pillars are large, plastered and with a fluted pattern. No paint remains to tell what color they were. The northwest wall of the ambulatory consists of a series of small openings (rooms 26-30 on the floor plan) with back door 7 towards the north end. The walls of the ambulatory are made of opus incertum. Space 27 is open to the ambulatory and is at an appropriate 2 meter height. The facing of the opening is different from the other walls with a diamond shaped pattern (opus reticulatum), a protruding lip and a decorative dedo. The area is probably as deep as it is tall and currently contains three masonry pieces that appear to be tops, which may or may not be in-situ (this may have been a display area for statuary, which would have enhanced the ambulatory behaviors). The walls of the ambulatory have slight remaining evidence of painted plaster in first style decoration. In several spots we see remains of a cocciopesto style floor in the ambulatory. Space 26 contains an access to the cellars on the north end and is decorated in first style in red and yellow paint still remaining below. Immediately to it's west are two high rectangular shaped niches, (statuary?), with a triangular pediment remaining on the western most niche. They are about about a meter deep and the insides are painted red.

Bibliography: Jashemski 276, Escheback 201-203
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Surrounding garden 25 on all four sides to the south east of rooms 26, 30 and entrance 7 and to the northwest of rooms 19-24.

DESCRIPTION: In bakery V-3-8 we have identified room number 11 as a storeroom based upon its location directly off the millroom and its utilitarian decoration. The room is almost square with a southeast/northwest axis and a door opening to the southwest. The door is fairly large with hardware indentations near the top. Walls are all opus incertum with traces of plaster on all walls. A window to the street high up and square is the located in the northeast wall. A series of post holes above the window indicate an upper story. There are faint traces of 7 post on the northwest wall that show that the room may have had an arched ceiling. Plaster work shows a red dado with cream or white above. Floor is Lappeli. No trace of a door jamb, or a door threshold remains. The northwest wall has some plaster towards the bottom with a series of scratch marks which may indicate that the room was being redecorated at the time of the eruption.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room is located to the northeast of millroom number 4, to the southeast of room 10, and to the northwest of room 12.

DESCRIPTION: In mill room 4 one finds a large beehive oven with bricked surround, underneath storage, tiled stone surface, and large beehive shaped interior cavity. Openings to both the oven and the storage are square. The oven itself is built up with opus incertum, with the inside stone and brick. The front of the oven (the brick surround) originally would have been completely arched. Workspace exists between the brick surround and the oven body, with a pass-through in the west corner leading at an oblique angle to the east to prep room 13. Inside the oven to the east is a circular hole about one meter above floor level that probably provided ventilation. It is worth nothing that the storage below appears to be slightly off-center from the oven opening above, although both appear to be roughly the same size. The remains of the curved brick arch extend approximately halfway up to each side of the oven.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: The oven is to the northeast of platform 4181 and to the east or southeast of all other features in the room.

DESCRIPTION: A large space surrounding the altar where public officials or wealthy patrons would periodically feed the common man. We enter the crossroads shrine public space area from the north-west corner of Via Nola and Via Vesuvio. At the tip of the corner are two steps leading to a public water fountain decorated with a satyr with a beard and a fat tummy. Entrance is confined to this space. We are interested in the Crossroad Altar structure, sacred space around the shrine and the public space. On the west corner is the shrine. Directly north of the shrine is a water tower.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Parallel to the altar situated to the south west.

DESCRIPTION:
This room has a marvelous floor of rectangles done in dark yellow, red and black. We see 2 barrel vaults and 3 doorways. The southeast doorway is to the Dionysus dining room, the second doorway is close to the kitchen and the third doorway is next to the room decorated in Egyptian paintings.

There is a large rectangular structure on the northwest wall which functions as a dumbwaiter.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Northwest of Dionysus dining room 34

DESCRIPTION: We have identiied this building 1-3-5,6 as a large food and drink shop. We have determine that this room (4239) is a counter room. This counter is inside the shop and does not abut the entrance. Made of rubble with indications of a slight L-shaped return to the south on the eastern end. There is no extant evidence of the top of the counter.

Use map number 5. WE have identified the structure as a food and drink shop, large. We have determined that the usage of this structure is a food and drink shop based on the following criteria. The location is almost opposite to a large entrance to the Odeon. The food and drink features that we see are a counter (4240), a dining room (4241) and kitchen (4244).

We enter this structure through two wide doorways that have stone thresholds that have grooves. In the south front room number 1 (4239), we see evidence of a counter (4240).

There is a doorway to the east where we enter a dining room number 2 (4241). The far northeast end has a barrel vault. There is small evidence of beige plaster with one red flower on the northeast wall which is possibly a niche. There are also small areas of plaster on the southeast wall.

In the north end of the west side of this double structure, there is a second barrel vault on the east wall. WE believe that the kitchen (room 3, 4244) was under this barrel vault. There is no floor. It is now dirt and weeds. We can see a square in the northeast corner that may have had a toilet (room 3, 4245). There is evidence of a basin (4246) centered on the northeast wall where we see an indentation in the wall with a drainage area. Southwest of this area seems to be room 5. We see slight evidence of walls on the northern side of the space. There was a corridor running from front to back of the structure along the north wall of the structure. The room (7) to the west in front of this structure may have been a serving room connected to the counter room (1) by a wide passage wa. There is another room (4243, room 8) which may have been a storeroom. It has a low barrel vaulted ceiling. The floor is of rubble and weeds. There is minimal remaining beige plaster on the west wall.

This feature is a mosaic placed in the room center. According to the floor design, it would have been located between couches on the southwest, northwest, and northeast walls. The central mosaic has bands of white tesserae with a band of florettes and a central circle is outlined with bands of white and black tesserae and a band of white mosaic. The center of the circle is opus sectili with four marble pieces also placed at the corners in the field outside the circle.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This feature is located in the center of the floor. Southeast of wall painting 4269.

DESCRIPTION: It has been determined that this is a commercial and residential structure known as the Villa of the Mysteries. This space (72) has been identified as a passage for the channel carrying the liquid from the press (69) to the fermentation dolia in space 79. This is a small square space with a vaulted ceiling. There is a doorway from room 69 at the eastern end of the southeast wall. There is another doorway in the center of the northwest wall leading to space 79. The raised channel runs along the northeast wall. There is an opening in the north corner of the northwest wall through which this channel runs. Remains of plaster can be seen on the channel, on all walls, and on the ceiling. However, no paint remains. The floor is not visible, There is some modern restoration, particularly both door lintels.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Room 69 is located to the east. Space 79 is located to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION:
We have identified this structure as a residential house with three entrances. Entrance 7 is the main entrance, entrance 3 is the secondary entrance and entrance 9 is the back entrance. We have determined room number 9 as a dining room based on the following criteria-Located next to an atrium and also overlooks a water feature. There are two doorways in the North corner of the Atrium; on the North East corner, a door opens to the dinning room. We enter and we see a 'rectangularish' room that is wider on the Northwest end. The floor is mud and pebbles. The Northwest wall has a small dividing wall that overlooks an impressive garden with a water feature. The central part of the garden is a water feature (large rectangular) of a hydrolic cement. On three sides there is a wall, the top of which is plastered, allowing for people passing around and potted plants. The floor of this walkway was covered in cement. At the entrance from the atrium there is a square block of cement with a circular cistern opening. Close to the cistern there is a few inches of pipe, coming out from under the raised walkway. We are speculating that there is more than one entrance area for the water.
In the dining room the East and West walls show plaster. There are post holes that suggests a second floor above garden dinning room.
In the dining room, the East and West walls show plaster. There are post holes that suggest a second floor above the garden and dining room. In the dining room, there is minimal evidence of plaster on all three walls. In the East corner of the North East wall, there is a couch niche, which shows plaster.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium and water garden.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a dining room within a residential structure. This identification is based on: the location of this room, which opens directly on to the peristyle colonnade [29]; the form of this room, with its very wide doorway and very tall window to the atrium to the southwest; the great height of this room. This rectangular space is on an northeast/southwest axis. The room is in fair condition. The walls are all preserved painted plaster. The decoration is made up of a fairly tall dado and on each of the long walls there are three printed panels, with central panels painted red. The center of the red panel on the northwest wall reveals a large, filled tunneling hole. Large white bands are above the central panels going up the wall. Very faint traces of decoration suggest architectural features. Above this white panel, one can still see that preserved on the northwest wall is a horizontal stucco molding. There is rough plaster above this. The highest portion of the walls is reconstructed. No ceiling remains. The flood is not visible.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the southeast of the tablinum [25] and southwest of the colonnade [29].

DESCRIPTION: We have identified a domestic structure and determined that his space is a small dining room. This determination is based on the location of this room adjacent to the atrium and the evidence of decoration. This space is a rectangular room on a northeast/southwest axis. The room is in poor to fair condition. One enters from the atrium over a white stone threshold. This doorway is very tall. This room has no windows. The floor surface is not visible. The walls preserve some plaster with traces of paint. The tops of the walls have had restoration; no ceiling survives. This dining room may be the reason for the cooking platform just to the northeast of the doorway, out in the atrium.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northwest of the atrium (19). This dining room may be the reason for the cooking platform in the atrium.

DESCRIPTION: We have identified the structure of V.1.26 as a house. We enter a fauces, step up, and are greeted by a mosaic of a baby deer in repose. We have determined that the usage of the room is an atrium based on the following criteria. There is a very large impluvium surrounded by a black and white border. We look beyond this to a huge tablinum, second style paintings on the wall in red and yellow. A mosaic with a decorative emblema is on the floor. On either side of the office are the remains of a herm and vital parts of the herm have been removed to the museum. On the west side are two small dining rooms. Located on the Northwest wall is a cooking platform [6826]. In the west corner of the atrium is the lararium of the Host. There is a doorway to the atrium and a very large entrance to the street. On the other side of the main entrance is a wide door [27]. Down the steps is a large shop (no food or drink).
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Two dining rooms (to the west), a tablinum (to the northeast), two front shops, and the main entrance are all contiguous to this room.

DESCRIPTION: We have determined that this is a commercial and residential establishment known as the Villa of the Mysteries. Room 64 has been identified as a processing room due to its location and feature. This is a rectangular space on a southwest/northeast axis. The eastern end of the southeast wall is broken through and there is a small space behind the wall, but it appears that this was a partition wall across the entire southeast width of the room. One enters through a doorway at the west end of the southwest wall. This doorway opens to the covered colonnade of peristyle 26. The room is in fair condition. The floors are white uncut stone mosaic. The threshold is white marble. The walls are simple vertical red panels over a black dado. The low ceiling is a modern reconstruction, but according to beam holes this seems to be placed close to the original position. There are two small windows in the northeast wall. Water basin feature 64-6918 is located in the north corner of the wall and suggests the processing of some sort of liquid product.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is to the northeast of peristyle 26 and it is southeast of room 65.

DESCRIPTION: This is an opus signinum floor with a central rosette and decorated entrance around which three dining couches would be placed. In the center of the room between the couches there is a square mosaic rosette with black and white tesserae depicting vegetation in a black border around a marble centerpiece. Between the rosette and the doorway to the southeast as you enter the room, the floor is decorated with a grid of white tesserae and marble inserts.
We have determined that 6.12.2 is a villa urbana and room 48 is a kitchen based upon the presence of features: prep platform 6860
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: water basin 6862 and this lararium. The lararium is located on the northwest wall. Close to the second floor height is a large masonry structure
BW_ROLL:
an arched opening and plasters on either side of the opening. The inside of the lararium contains no existing figurative decorations but does have cornice molding as you find in a full sized room. The plaster work on the outside was painted red with traces of that color still remaining. Note: This lararium is extremely elaborate for a kitchen location.

Bibliography: Jashemski 276; Escheback 201/203
COLOR_ROLL: Preparation platform 6860 to the southeast water basin 6862 to the southwest.
PHOTOGRAPHER: temple shaped with a triangular cap on the top

DESCRIPTION: There are two entrances to dining hall (3917), one on the south west wall. At the western end is a smaller passageway from the atrium. There is a broken marble threshold with a door pivot hole and a wall which separates the corridor to the peristyle and the atrium. The second opening is 10-12 feet wide and is to the south west. It provides a vista of the peristyle garden. This entrance has a small broken white marble threshold which delineates the room and the western side of the wall is broken, while the southern door facing rises approximately 13 feet. No traces of painted plaster survive, however on the north east wall, approximately 10 feet from the ground are two holes which may have been for some kind of support, and on the south east wall there are three holes, approximately five feet from the ground. White tesserae are scattered among vegetation and ash, and there appears to have been some which may have been stained black.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to corridor 11 to the south west and to dining room 26 to the south east and atrium 13 to the north west.

DESCRIPTION: The counter room sits on an E/W axis, with the South end opening directly to via DeFortuna. 2 large counters, one rectangular, one v shaped are located on two short ends of the room. There is a t shaped brick column like small wall dividing the room from entrances 6-8-7 and 6-8-8. There is no ceiling, the floor is lapilli. The North end of the room is delineated by another short brick L shaped columnar structure. Attached to the end of counter 6460. The West wall is masonry with only a fragment of plaster remaining. At the South end of counter 6460, is a narrow concrete bench attached just inside entrance door 6-8-7. At entrance 6-8-8, there is a threshold for a door to close off the counter room from the street.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Contiguous to counter room 2 and store room 3 to the North and a street situated to the South

DESCRIPTION: The room is entered from the southwest and is oriented primarily north/south. All four walls have plaster extant, likely fourth style. The lowest register is primarily red. The middle register is yellow ochre in color. These are panelised with painted frames, topped with a plaster sigma relief with some garland/ribbon painted detail extant. The yop register is a yellow ochre topped by a plaster cornice with floral relief. East wall has a window - sill, situated 2 m above the stone rubble floor. This is a dining room because of the size, decor and view south to the atrium. Modern reconstruction is evident on the west wall. Walls are partially capped with modern terracotta tiles. The north, south and west walls are opus mixtum. Doorway shows no threshold or evidence of a door having been in place.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: to the south are ala 10 and atrium 9, to the east is the vicolo, to the north is the kitchen 14, to the west is the tablinum 12

DESCRIPTION: Rectangular room. East-west axis. Wide doorway in the east wall to atrium (5). No visible threshold. Floor is obscured by lapilli throughout. On the north wall there is extensive first style plaster with plain plaster beneath. On the west wall there is extensive first style plaster with yellow base. High in the center of the wall there is a square plastered window. On the south wall there is plaster decorated red borders going down. The difference in styles between the north, west and south walls suggests that it was redecorated. At the west end of the south wall there is a blocked plastered couch niche. At the west end of the north wall there is a second plastered couch niche (6435). At the top of the north wall there is a plastered cornice for the ceiling. On the southeast corner there is a red painted wave pattern and yellow trim.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Atrium (5) is to the east.

DESCRIPTION: A square sales room located on the corner of Via delle Terme and Vicolo della Fullonica. The room has two large entrances from the sidewalk, one facing each street. At the northeast end of the room restored remains of a staircase are located. On the west wall, we can see holes that imply shelving was present. There are approximately four slots in the wall for shelving. In addition on the large granite corner blocks, evidence remains of two holes at the top which may have supported wood beams for a second storey and lower down at door level either a shelf or door attachment are also present on both sides. There are two holes which appear to have supported square beams and two which appear to have supported wood shelving on the east wall. There is no plaster remaining o walls which are of opus reticulatum. No floor remains, although the bakery appears to e a step up from the street. No windows are present.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: oven room 2 to north, property VI.6.3 to the west, Via delle Terme to south, Vicolo della Fullonica to the east.

DESCRIPTION: Base 3864 is quite complete and surrounded by lava stones.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: Mill base (3863) to the west, mill base (3865) to the south.

DESCRIPTION: We enter the oven room from the northwest. The oven room runs along a northeast/southwest axis with the oven filling two thirds of the room and this includes the oven surround. the room is vaulted over the oven until it is bisected by passageways on the northwest and southeast. In the southwest corner of the room is a large water pipe which flows into a large dolium basin that abuts northwest and southwest walls. On the southeast side of this well preserved basin appears to have been a second basin in the same mounting. Plaster painted red is evident along the pipe on the southwest wall and behind the second basin. A pile of rubble is in the southeast corner of the room next to the northeast/southeast walls. On the northwest wall is a passthrough from the preparation room to the northwest. The opening is the width of a large terra cotta drain tile and is approximately as high as the length of a drain tile. The oven abuts a wall in this vaulted room which was painted in antiquity on both the northwest and southeast walls which suggests that the room was repurposed in antiquity.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This room is contiguous to room (8) on the southeast and the preparation room (3) to the north and room (5) to the northwest.

DESCRIPTION: This basin is a re used catillus which is placed upside down in the western corner of the room. It may have held a ceramic basin. There is also the remains of a large ceramic basin which may have been placed in the catillus. This catillus seems to be leveled with a large stone beneath it. The western corner behind the basin is not excavated.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: This basin is in the western corner of the room, and is just to the south of the doorway from the mill room (2).

DESCRIPTION: We enter the large Tuscan style atrium from the northeast fauces to the street. Just off centre from this entrance are the remains of an impluvium made of opus signinum which appears to have been square. The room is in disrepair. It runs along a northeast/southwest axis. On the eastern corner of the impluvium is a large, ancient cistern cover and to the east of this cistern cover, abutting the eastern portion of the east wall is a square hearth which is approximately one metre square and 3o cm high. The placement of the hearth is between the entrance to room 7 and the corner of the atrium. Evidence of plaster painted red remains on aspects of all the walls. In the south wall are doorways with the tablinum in the middle formed by ashlar blocks of sarno stone covered with plaster. The height of the walls, in most places is above the first storey level. On the western end of the north wall are two lararia the smaller one lower, the larger being more visible and higher. There is a window and a doorway on the north corner of the west wall to room 8. The floor is obscured with lapilli and vegetation. The ceiling is not extant.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: dining room 3276 to the northeast

DESCRIPTION:
This large rectangular dining room runs along a N.W.-S.E. axis. We enter from the doorway in the N.E. wall over a marble threshold and through a doorway that was plastered and painted red on the N.W. wall and as we enter the room, most of the wall is open to the garden on the N.W. side. The N.E. wall is approximately 3 feet high at the entrance and rises to an indeterminate height on thence S.E.. Evidence of plaster exists on all walls. The floor is poorly preserved but evidence shows a patterned mosaic floor of black and white tesserae. However, the design in the middle, does not exist.

High on the S.W. wall are 2 beam holes, one situated above the other. There are traces of red and yellow paint scattered about. On the N.W. floor, there appears to be inlay that mimics the threshold. There is no extant ceiling, however, there are tiles on the N.W. wall, seen at the North end.
CONTIGUOUS_RELATIONSHIP: It is contiguous to room 24, situated to the West.
VIDEO_COMMENTS: Done by Fran Capo and Lisa Wernicki

DESCRIPTION: This water feature which is located along the southwest wall of the oven room is a rubble and mortar structure which apparently held two basins.
